<details><summary>Fills from triggered stop orders are dropped (never settled)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** When a trigger order fires, the resulting market/limit order's fills settle positions, margin and fees exactly like any other order.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1301-1327: trigger_stops() calls self.place_order(params, stop.trader, stop.timestamp) and only inspects result.status (warn on Rejected); result.fills and result.self_trade_cancels are discarded. No fills log exists in OrderBook (grep for take_fills/fill_log/pending_fills returns nothing). The executor settles only the outer PlaceResult.fills of the order that caused the trigger (native_executor.rs:4124-4160, 4616-4640).
- **Suggestion:** Make trigger_stops return Vec<PlaceResult> (or push fills/self_trade_cancels into the outer PlaceResult with the triggered trader as taker) and have the Phase-3/4 settle path in native_executor.rs iterate them: update positions, release the stop's reservation, charge fees. Add a test: resting ask, buy fill crosses stop trigger, assert the stop trader's position changes. Alternatively, move trigger evaluation to the executor (see mark-price gap) so triggered orders flow through the normal place path.

</details>

<details><summary>exec_modify_order has no sender ownership check</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** modify/batchModify only affect orders owned by the signing user (or an approved agent for that user).
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3250-3254 dispatches ModifyOrder as Self::exec_modify_order(ctx, *order_id, *new_price, *new_qty) with no sender; exec_modify_order signature (ctx, order_id, new_price, new_qty) iterates every book and calls book.modify_order(order_id, ...) unconditionally. Contrast exec_cancel_order which checks order.trader != *sender. order_book.rs:702-706 modify_order takes no trader either.
- **Suggestion:** Pass sender into exec_modify_order; before modify, book.get_order(order_id) and reject if order.trader != sender (mirror the cancel_order check). Margin delta is already applied to modified.trader, so a griefer today can also force another user's order_margin up. Add a negative test in cancel_batch_exec_tests.rs style.

</details>

<details><summary>Stop/trigger orders fire on last trade price, not mark/oracle price</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Trigger orders (SL/TP) are evaluated against the mark price (configurable to last/oracle per order via tpsl trigger type); mark is derived from oracle + book, resistant to single-print manipulation.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1272-1290 trigger_stops() reads self.last_trade_price and fires only when a fill occurs in that same place_order call (order_book.rs:572-575). No executor/oracle path ever invokes trigger evaluation (grep trigger_stops\|pending_stops in torus-bridge returns only OrderStatus::PendingTrigger status matches at native_executor.rs:4129,4621,4777,4982). Oracle/mark lives in crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs but is not consulted.
- **Suggestion:** Add OrderBook::trigger_stops_at(mark: FixedPoint) -> Vec<PlaceResult> and call it from the executor once per block after oracle/mark update (and after fills), using the per-market mark price. Store a trigger_source enum (Mark\|Last\|Oracle) on StopOrder (wire-format change). Fixes thin-book/manipulation risk and lets stops fire with no trade in the market.

</details>

<details><summary>reduce_only is stored but never enforced</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Reduce-only orders can only decrease \|position\|; size is clipped to the current position, resting reduce-only orders are cancelled/clipped when position shrinks, and they cannot open or flip a position.
- **Torus evidence:** reduce_only exists on PlaceOrderParams (torus-types/src/lib.rs:1067), Order/StopOrder (order_book.rs:46,106) and is serialised (order_book.rs:2278) and shown in RPC (types.rs:336), but grep reduce_only across crates/torus-bridge/src and torus-core position.rs/margin.rs/order_book.rs yields no read of the flag except construction in a proposer test (proposer.rs:431). Phase-2 reserve (native_executor.rs:3753-3781) and settle do not branch on it.
- **Suggestion:** In the Phase-2 prep path of native_executor.rs: if params.reduce_only, load the sender's position for market_id; reject if side would increase/flip it; clip quantity to \|position\|; skip order-margin reservation (reduce-only needs none). On position change (settle Phase 4 / liquidation), re-clip or cancel resting reduce-only orders of that trader. Add tests before implementing.

</details>

<details><summary>Pending stop orders cannot be cancelled individually</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** A trigger order has an oid and can be cancelled by oid or cloid like any open order; it appears in openOrders/frontendOpenOrders.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:589-640 cancel_order() looks up self.order_index only (resting orders) and returns OrderNotFound otherwise; pending_stops is only drained in cancel_all (order_book.rs:651,695) and on trigger (1284). exec_cancel_order relies on book.get_order which is order_index-based.
- **Suggestion:** In cancel_order, on order_index miss, search pending_stops by id (owner check via stop.trader) and remove it, returning a synthesized Order (or a new CancelledStop variant) so the executor can release any reservation. Keep the id-ascending invariant (order_book.rs:1377). Also expose pending stops in RPC getOpenOrders.

</details>

<details><summary>Market (and StopMarket) orders reserve zero margin and have no slippage bound</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL market orders are IOC limit orders with a slippage cap (default 3%?) and are margin-checked against worst-case fill before matching; TWAP chunks are capped at 3% slippage.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3753-3761 and 4001-4008: order_margin_required = ZERO when is_market; comment at native_executor.rs:414 'Margin reserved (possibly ZERO for market orders)'. order_book.rs:509-523 only checks that the opposite side is non-empty; execute_match walks every level for is_market (no price bound). StopMarket converts to Market with price ZERO at order_book.rs:1303-1306.
- **Suggestion:** Represent market orders as IOC limits with a computed limit (best opposite ± slippage bps from market params) and reserve margin at that bound; or run a pre-match margin check against worst-case fill (the unused check_margin_at_match helper from the prior audit may be reusable, verify it still exists in margin.rs).

</details>

<details><summary>Take-profit orders and positionTpsl/normalTpsl grouping absent</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL supports TP (take-market/take-limit, triggered when price moves favourably) in addition to SL, and the 'positionTpsl' grouping ties TP/SL to the whole position (size follows position, OCO-cancel each other, reduce-only), vs 'normalTpsl' attached to a specific order.
- **Torus evidence:** OrderType enum has only Limit/Market/StopMarket/StopLimit (torus-types/src/lib.rs:1072-1083); trigger-direction validation at order_book.rs:421-436 explicitly REJECTS a buy whose trigger is below last price (which is exactly a take-profit for a short), so TP cannot even be emulated. No grouping field on PlaceOrderParams (lib.rs:1059-1069). grep tpsl/take_profit/TakeProfit over torus-types/core/bridge/rpc returns nothing.
- **Suggestion:** Add OrderType::TakeMarket{trigger}/TakeLimit{trigger,limit} (or a trigger: {price, is_tp: bool} struct) with inverted direction validation; add grouping: Option<TpslGroup{Position\|Normal}> and an OCO link id so filling/cancelling one cancels the sibling; position-tpsl orders are reduce-only with size tracking the position (depends on reduce_only enforcement gap).

</details>

<details><summary>Cancel-by-cloid, batchModify and cloid uniqueness absent</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** cancelByCloid action; modify/batchModify accept oid or cloid; cloid is a 128-bit hex and HL rejects duplicate open cloids per user.
- **Torus evidence:** NativeAction has only CancelOrder{order_id}, CancelAllOrders{market_id}, ModifyOrder{order_id,...} (torus-types/src/lib.rs:588-600). client_order_id is Option<u64> (lib.rs:1067), never indexed in OrderBook (no cloid map; order_book.rs:240-350 fields), no uniqueness check in place_order (order_book.rs:367-420). RPC only echoes it (torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1916).
- **Suggestion:** Add a per-book HashMap<(Address,u64),OrderId> cloid index (maintained on insert/cancel/fill-complete, included in Borsh/row persistence), reject duplicate open cloids, add NativeAction::CancelByCloid{market_id,cloid} and ModifyOrderBatch(Vec<ModifyParams>) with canonical-bytes + EIP-712 encodings.

</details>

<details><summary>Order expiry (expiresAfter) and dead-man switch (scheduleCancel) absent</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Actions carry optional expiresAfter (ms) and are rejected if included after that time; scheduleCancel sets a time after which all the user's open orders are cancelled (dead-man switch).
- **Torus evidence:** The only 'expiry' in the action path is session-key expiry (torus-types/src/lib.rs:346,664; native_executor.rs:5595-5612). PlaceOrderParams has no expiry field (lib.rs:1059-1069); no ScheduleCancel variant in NativeAction (lib.rs:580-660); Order struct has no expiry (order_book.rs:36-48).
- **Suggestion:** Add expires_after_ms: Option<u64> to SignedNativeAction (checked against block timestamp in resolve/validate) and NativeAction::ScheduleCancel{at_ms: Option<u64>} stored per account; executor runs a per-block sweep (cheap BTreeMap<at_ms, Address>) that calls cancel_all for due accounts.

</details>

<details><summary>Min-notional rule absent (only lot_size dust check)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Orders must be >= $10 notional (except reduce-only closing remainder); price/size precision rules via szDecimals and 5 significant figures.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:376-384 only rejects quantity < lot_size; no price*qty threshold anywhere (grep min_notional/MIN_NOTIONAL over torus-core, torus-bridge, torus-types: no hits). Tick check applies only to Limit (order_book.rs:397), so StopLimit limit prices bypass tick validation.
- **Suggestion:** Add min_notional to market params / OrderBook::new; in place_order reject if price*qty < min_notional for non-reduce-only orders; apply tick check to StopLimit.limit and StopMarket/StopLimit.trigger.

</details>

<details><summary>Scale and TWAP orders absent</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Scale orders fan out N limit orders across a price range (frontend/API helper); TWAP is a native order type executed in 30-second sub-orders with 3% max slippage per chunk, tracked as a twap state on-chain.
- **Torus evidence:** No Scale/TWAP in OrderType (torus-types/src/lib.rs:1072-1083) or NativeAction (lib.rs:580-660); grep -il twap/scale over rpc/types/bridge gives only unrelated hits (scale = exec-scaleup perf naming). PlaceOrderBatch (lib.rs:587) is a viable substrate for scale orders client-side.
- **Suggestion:** Scale: document as a client-side helper over PlaceOrderBatch (no chain change). TWAP: add NativeAction::TwapOrder{market,side,total_qty,duration_ms,reduce_only} with per-block scheduler in the executor emitting IOC limit chunks bounded by slippage; needs the market-order slippage bound first.

</details>

<details><summary>Trading fees still never charged on fills</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Maker/taker fees per fill with volume tiers, referral/staking discounts; fees fund HLP/AF.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1374 total_native_fees declared, 1853 initialised to 0, 5995 read at epoch boundary; grep taker_fee\|maker_fee\|fee_bps in native_executor.rs returns nothing else. (Confirms prior-audit claim; fee design belongs to the fees area, noted here because fills are settled in the order path.)
- **Suggestion:** In the Phase-4 settle path where fills adjust balances (native_executor.rs:4124-4160/4616-4640), deduct maker/taker bps from the fill notional and accumulate into total_native_fees; defer tiers to the fees area.

</details>

*Confidence notes:* Verified by reading: order_book.rs place_order/cancel/modify/trigger_stops/match_at_level, NativeAction enum, exec dispatch and exec_modify_order/exec_cancel_order signatures, Phase-2 reserve path. Not verified: whether exec_cancel_order's get_order could ever find a pending stop (assumed order_index-based from name/usage); whether market_workers.rs parallel path has any extra reduce_only or fill handling for triggered stops (grep shows none, but I did not read it fully); whether check_margin_at_match still exists in margin.rs. HL facts I am less sure of: the default market-order slippage cap (I believe 3% on the UI/TWAP chunks, API market orders are IOC limits with caller-chosen slippage); HL's STP default behaviour (I believe the resting order is cancelled, i.e. 'expire maker', matching Torus); the exact min-notional ($10) and whether trigger price may be chosen between mark/last/oracle per order (HL triggers on mark price; per-order trigger-source selection I am not certain of). TWAP interval (30s) and 3% per-chunk slippage are from research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md:333.

### funding-mark

#### funding-mark — opus

Torus has only part of an oracle layer and none of the rest of HL's funding and mark-price stack. Validators can submit prices: a signed SubmitOraclePrices action is checked for an active validator and written as raw per-block submissions. OracleManager has a stake-weighted median with MAD outlier rejection and staleness detection. But nothing in production calls the block-level aggregate_oracle_prices or run_liquidation_checks, and no validator process publishes prices. So the aggregated price row is never written, the price RPC and precompile return nothing or zero, and submissions pile up with no pruning. There is no funding engine at all: Position has no funding accumulator and max_funding_rate_bps is just an unused field. There is no mark price apart from the oracle, no impact prices, no price bands or oracle-deviation checks on orders, and no open-interest caps. Margin is reserved from the order's own limit price at a default 20x, because margin_configs is never filled outside tests.

**Already present:**
- Signed SubmitOraclePrices native action exists and is EIP-712 hashed: crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:643 (enum variant), lib.rs:1145-1149 (OracleSubmission {prices, timestamp}), crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:218,470
- Executor handler checks the sender is an Active, registered validator, then stores the raw per-validator submissions: crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3276 (dispatch), 5685-5726 (exec_submit_oracle_prices)
- OracleManager with a stake-weighted median, outlier rejection at 3x mean absolute deviation, a min-3-reporter fallback to the last valid price, and a 10% bound on a single reporter versus the last price: crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:200-271, 379-420
- Staleness detection: DEFAULT_MAX_ORACLE_AGE=100 blocks, aggregation_window=10 blocks, also applied in get_last_valid_price: crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:21-22, 117-131, 274-295, 341-358
- Oracle prices readable from the EVM via precompile (oracle_reader/read_oracle_price/read_all_oracle_prices): crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:573-660
- RPC torus_getMarkPrice (returns the oracle price as both mark and index, plus the last trade price) and torus_getOpenInterest (full scan of the positions column family, summing long/short size): crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1557-1642
- Tiered leverage tables (50/20/10/5x by notional) and cross/isolated maintenance-margin maths taking oracle prices: crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:16-50, 101-250
- Liquidation engine with an ADL fallback that takes oracle prices (library code, see gaps for wiring): crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:76-160; native_executor.rs:5923-5985
- Tick-size, lot-size, positive-price and per-trader order-count checks on placement: crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:376-416
- Stop-trigger direction check against the last trade price: order_book.rs:420-470, trigger_stops 1272-1295

| Gap | Status | Impact | Effort | Lockstep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Funding engine entirely absent (no premium sampling, no interest component, no hourly settlement, no funding accumulator) | absent | critical | L | yes |
| Oracle aggregation never runs in production, so the aggregated price is never written | unwired | critical | S | yes |
| No validator oracle publisher (no sidecar or daemon that fetches external CEX prices and submits them) | absent | critical | M | no |
| Raw oracle submissions grow without bound (pruning only runs inside the never-called aggregation) | buggy | high | S | yes |
| No separate mark price (HL median of oracle-plus-EMA basis, book mid and external perp prices) | absent | high | M | yes |
| Liquidation and margin health checks against the oracle never run in production | unwired | critical | M | yes |
| No order price bands or deviation check against oracle/mark (no 'price too far from oracle' rejection) | absent | high | M | yes |
| No open-interest caps (per-market OI limit, per-user cap, or reduce-only mode when the cap is hit) | absent | high | M | yes |
| No impact bid/ask prices (needed for the premium index) | absent | medium | S | yes |
| Oracle weighting and staleness are block-based and only partly stake-weighted | partial | medium | S | yes |
| Margin reservation ignores the market's leverage config and oracle/mark price | buggy | high | M | yes |

<details><summary>Funding engine entirely absent (no premium sampling, no interest component, no hourly settlement, no funding accumulator)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL samples a premium index every 5s, roughly (impact price - oracle) / oracle. Each hour it settles F = avg premium + clamp(interest - premium, +/-0.05%), where the interest rate is 0.01% per 8h paid hourly as 1/8. The rate is capped at 4% per hour, and the payment is size * oracle * F between longs and shorts.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1155-1161: MarketParams.max_funding_rate_bps is the only funding concept. Its other occurrences are hash encoding only (lib.rs:828,906; eip712.rs:620). A grep for 'funding\|premium' across crates/*/src finds no engine. Position (crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:52-61) has trader/market/is_long/size/entry_price/realized_pnl/isolated_margin/margin_type and no cumulative-funding or last-funding-index field.
- **Suggestion:** Add a torus-core/src/funding.rs. Per market, store a FundingState {premium_sum, samples, last_settle_ts, cumulative_funding_index} in a new CF_NATIVE_FUNDING column family. Each block in NativeExecutor's end-of-block hook (next to the fee distribution near native_executor.rs:5990), sample the premium from impact bid/ask (see the impact-price gap) and the oracle. On an hour boundary (block timestamp), compute F with the HL formula, clamp it by max_funding_rate_bps, and advance cumulative_funding_index. Add a funding_index_snapshot to Position, a Borsh migration, and settle lazily on touch or eagerly for all positions. This needs a state-layout migration and lockstep upgrade.

</details>

<details><summary>Oracle aggregation never runs in production, so the aggregated price is never written</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Validators publish oracle prices about every 3s. The protocol takes a stake-weighted median each round and it is immediately the index used for funding, margin and liquidation.
- **Torus evidence:** native_executor.rs:5904 `pub fn aggregate_oracle_prices` has no callers outside tests. A grep for aggregate_oracle_prices in crates/ (excluding tests) matches only its definition. The consensus app (crates/torus-consensus/src) has no 'oracle' references. OracleManager::aggregate_price (oracle.rs:200-271) is the only writer of the 'agg' key (oracle.rs:263-266), so get_price (oracle.rs:274) returns NoOraclePrice on any live chain. As a result RPC get_mark_price (torus.rs:1609-1612) reports 0, and the precompile oracle reads find nothing.
- **Suggestion:** Call NativeExecutor::aggregate_oracle_prices once per block from the block-execution pipeline, after user actions and before liquidation/funding. Pass the listed market ids and a deterministic snapshot of active-validator stakes from ctx.staking. Gate it at an activation height. The validator_stakes list must be sorted and deterministic.

</details>

<details><summary>No validator oracle publisher (no sidecar or daemon that fetches external CEX prices and submits them)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Every HL validator runs a price publisher that pulls weighted CEX spot prices (Binance 3, OKX 2, Bybit 2, Kraken/KuCoin/Gate/MEXC/HL 1) and submits them about every 3s.
- **Torus evidence:** Grepping crates/ for SubmitOraclePrices/OracleSubmission finds only torus-types, the executor dispatch (native_executor.rs:3276), oracle.rs, error.rs and tests (native_bridge_tests.rs, chaos.rs). There is nothing in crates/torus-node/src (its only 'mark' matches are 'all_market_trades' at main.rs:935-944).
- **Suggestion:** Add a torus-node oracle_publisher task, enabled only when the validator key is present. It polls configurable CEX REST/WS feeds and computes a weighted median of the per-venue prices. On a timer (for example every N blocks), it signs and gossips NativeAction::SubmitOraclePrices through the existing mempool forward path. This is off-chain only and not consensus-breaking.

</details>

<details><summary>Raw oracle submissions grow without bound (pruning only runs inside the never-called aggregation)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL keeps only the current round's validator submissions.
- **Torus evidence:** oracle.rs:186-188 writes a new key per (market, validator, block): submission_key = 'sub'+market+validator+block (oracle.rs:137-145). Pruning of old submissions happens only in collect_submissions (oracle.rs:303-336), which is reached only from aggregate_price, and that is unwired in production (see the previous gap). Even when it runs it deletes at most 100 keys per call (prune_limit, oracle.rs:331-334). The submission action charges a flat 1000 gas (native_executor.rs:5725) whatever the number of prices.
- **Suggestion:** Key submissions by (market, validator) only and overwrite in place, keeping block_number in the value, so state is bounded at markets*validators. Alternatively, prune in a dedicated per-block pass. Also cap prices.len() per submission and charge gas per price.

</details>

<details><summary>No separate mark price (HL median of oracle-plus-EMA basis, book mid and external perp prices)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL's mark price is the median of three values: (a) the oracle plus a 150s EMA of (book mid - oracle), (b) the median of best bid, best ask and last trade, and (c) a weighted median of CEX perp mids. It is used for margining, liquidations, TP/SL triggers and unrealized PnL.
- **Torus evidence:** RPC get_mark_price sets mark = index = oracle (torus.rs:1609-1612: `Ok(op) => (op.price, op.price, op.block_number)`). There is no mark computation in torus-core. Margin and liquidation helpers take a raw `oracle_prices` slice as the mark (margin.rs:194,215,253; liquidation.rs:153-160).
- **Suggestion:** Add mark.rs in torus-core. Keep a per-market EMA of (mid - oracle) in state, updated each block in the end-of-block hook from best_bid/best_ask (order_book.rs:798+) and last_trade_price. Compute mark = median(oracle+ema_basis, median(bid, ask, ltp), external_perp_mid). The external perp median would come from an optional second field in OracleSubmission, which changes the action's wire format. Store mark next to 'agg' in CF_NATIVE_ORACLE. Feed it to the liquidation, margin and stop triggers.

</details>

<details><summary>Liquidation and margin health checks against the oracle never run in production</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL checks every account against mark price each block and liquidates when equity is below maintenance margin.
- **Torus evidence:** native_executor.rs:5923 `pub fn run_liquidation_checks` has no non-test callers (grep matches only its definition). It also iterates ctx.margin_configs (native_executor.rs:5929-5934). That map is created empty (native_executor.rs:1842 `margin_configs: HashMap::new()`) and nothing outside tests inserts into it, so even if it were wired it would loop over zero markets.
- **Suggestion:** Load MarketMarginConfig per market from the stored market listing at executor init and on ListMarket. Call run_liquidation_checks each block after aggregation, using mark prices and a deterministic trader set: maintain a per-market index of traders with open positions rather than taking a caller-supplied slice.

</details>

<details><summary>No order price bands or deviation check against oracle/mark (no 'price too far from oracle' rejection)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL rejects limit orders priced more than about 95% away from the reference price (configurable for HIP-3). Market and IOC orders are bounded by slippage (default 8-10%) from mark. Prices are limited to 5 significant figures.
- **Torus evidence:** OrderBook::place_order checks only lot size, positive limit price, tick alignment, a per-trader count limit, and stop-trigger direction against last_trade_price (order_book.rs:376-470). There is no oracle or mark reference. The pre-match executor path reserves margin and passes market orders through with no reserve and no slippage bound (native_executor.rs:3755-3760, 4913-4917). Unknown markets get a default OrderBook with tick=lot=1 (native_executor.rs:4994-4997).
- **Suggestion:** In the executor's prep phase (native_executor.rs ~3745 and exec_place_order ~4911), look up the market's mark or oracle and reject a limit order when \|price - ref\|/ref exceeds a per-market max_price_deviation_bps. Clamp a market order to a synthetic limit at ref*(1 +/- max_slippage) so it sweeps no further. Add these fields to MarketParams (torus-types lib.rs:1155). Reject orders for unlisted markets instead of creating a default book.

</details>

<details><summary>No open-interest caps (per-market OI limit, per-user cap, or reduce-only mode when the cap is hit)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** After JELLY, HL enforces per-asset OI caps, both notional and as a multiple of oracle, plus per-user OI limits on small caps. At the cap only reduce-only flow is allowed, and order prices are also constrained when near the cap.
- **Torus evidence:** No OI state is kept in consensus. OI is computed only on demand in RPC by a full scan of the positions column family (torus.rs:1557-1600). MarketParams (lib.rs:1155-1161) and MarketListing (lib.rs:1164-1171) have no OI field, and grepping 'open_interest\|oi_cap' in torus-core/bridge src finds nothing.
- **Suggestion:** Keep a per-market OpenInterest {long, short} row updated in settlement (settle_market_results_sequential/parallel, native_executor.rs:4081/4328) whenever position size changes. Add max_oi_notional to MarketParams. In order prep, reject an order that would raise OI above the cap unless it reduces the trader's position.

</details>

<details><summary>No impact bid/ask prices (needed for the premium index)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL computes impact bid and ask as the average fill price for a fixed notional (impact notional = 20000 USDC divided by initial margin fraction, so it depends on leverage) and uses them in the premium index.
- **Torus evidence:** OrderBook exposes only best_bid/best_ask and level rows (order_book.rs:798+). A grep for 'impact' in crates/*/src finds nothing.
- **Suggestion:** Add OrderBook::impact_price(side, notional) -> Option<FixedPoint> that walks levels until the notional is filled, returning None if depth is insufficient. Call it from the funding sampler.

</details>

<details><summary>Oracle weighting and staleness are block-based and only partly stake-weighted</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL takes a stake-weighted median of validator prices, with time-based freshness and roughly 3s cadence.
- **Torus evidence:** reject_outliers uses an unweighted simple median and mean absolute deviation (oracle.rs:396-420), while the final price uses weighted_median (oracle.rs:257). Staleness is block-count based: max_oracle_age 100 blocks and window 10 blocks (oracle.rs:21, 126-128). It ignores the submission timestamp; the executor even discards it (`_submission_timestamp`, native_executor.rs:5689) and stores ctx.timestamp. min_oracle_reporters is a fixed 3 rather than a stake fraction (oracle.rs:22).
- **Suggestion:** Express staleness in block-timestamp seconds, and require reporters to cover at least 2/3 of stake rather than a count of 3. Use the stake-weighted median for the outlier centre. Reject submissions whose timestamp is too far from the block time.

</details>

<details><summary>Margin reservation ignores the market's leverage config and oracle/mark price</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL computes initial margin from the user's chosen leverage (at most the asset max) on the order's notional, and checks account health using mark price.
- **Torus evidence:** reserve_for_qty_cfg uses the order's limit price and falls back to 20x when there is no config (native_executor.rs:4805-4817 `.unwrap_or(20)`). margin_configs is always empty in production (native_executor.rs:1842, never inserted). Market orders reserve zero (native_executor.rs:3757-3761, 4913-4917), so MarketParams.max_leverage is never applied.
- **Suggestion:** Fill margin_configs from the stored market listing at init (the genesis market layout is at torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:432). For a market order, reserve against mark*(1+slippage) notional. Add a per-user leverage setting (HL updateLeverage).

</details>

*Confidence notes:* Not verified because of the time box: (1) Whether settlement or withdraw paths call OracleManager::get_price indirectly. I grepped torus-bridge/consensus/node for 'oracle' and found only the executor init and the dispatch, so this is unlikely. (2) Whether weighted_median (oracle.rs ~420+) is correct; I did not read it. (3) Whether tests reach aggregation through a harness that hides a production caller; I grepped all non-test src and found none. (4) Whether genesis writes margin config somewhere the executor reads under another name; I found only a HashMap::new() init. HL facts I am less sure of: the exact mark-price formula (150s EMA basis and the CEX perp median weights); the limit-order price band (I believe about 95% from reference for standard perps, with stricter HIP-3 settings); the size of OI caps and the per-user OI limits added after JELLY; impact notional = 20000 USDC divided by initial margin fraction. The deep-dive doc (research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md:343,61,68,533) confirms the funding formula, the 4%/h cap, the validator-weighted median feed weights, and that OI limits were added after JELLY.

#### funding-mark — fable

Torus has a real validator oracle module (stake-weighted median with MAD outlier rejection, staleness, single-reporter 10% clamp) and a SubmitOraclePrices action gated to active validators, but nothing drives it: no node-side price publisher exists, and `aggregate_oracle_prices` / `run_liquidation_checks` have zero callers outside their own file, so in production the aggregated price is never written and margin/liquidation never run against a live price. There is no funding engine at all (the only trace is `max_funding_rate_bps` in MarketParams, which is itself a no-op because UpdateMarketParams/ListMarket/DelistMarket are stubs). Mark price is just oracle price echoed into both `mark_price` and `index_price` in RPC; there is no median-of-(oracle, book mid, external) construction, no impact prices, no premium index, no interest rate. Order placement validates only positive price, tick size, and per-trader order count: no price bands vs oracle/mark, no open-interest caps, and `margin_configs` is never populated so every market reserves at a hardcoded 20x default.

**Already present:**
- Oracle submission + stake-weighted median aggregation with MAD-based outlier rejection: crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:178-271 (submit_price, aggregate_price), :361-420 (simple_median, mean_abs_deviation, reject_outliers, weighted_median)
- Oracle staleness detection (max age 100 blocks) and min-reporters fallback to last valid price: crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:21-22, :231-233, :274-295, :338-355
- Single-reporter manipulation clamp (10% max move vs last valid price): crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:235-256
- SubmitOraclePrices action restricted to Active registered validators: crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5685-5721; EIP-712 typed hash for it: crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:218,470
- Oracle price used as the mark for unrealized PnL / maintenance margin / liquidation math (library level): crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:182-250, crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:153-163,192-207; zero/negative oracle rejected
- RPC get_mark_price returns oracle price, index (=oracle), and last trade price: crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1604-1641, types.rs:351-357; EVM OracleReader precompile 0x0802: crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:32,315
- Tick-size and positive-price validation on limit orders: crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:387-407
- Leverage-tier-based initial margin reserve (effective_max_leverage over tiers): crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4806-4818, crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:61-68
- MarketParams.max_funding_rate_bps exists in the type/encoding layer only: crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156-1161, :828, :906

| Gap | Status | Impact | Effort | Lockstep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hourly funding engine entirely absent (no premium index, interest rate, cap, settlement, or position accumulator) | absent | critical | L | yes |
| Oracle aggregation and liquidation sweep are implemented but never invoked (no end-of-block driver) | unwired | critical | M | yes |
| No node-side validator oracle publisher (cadence, source weighting, external feeds) | absent | critical | L | no |
| Mark price is just the oracle price; no median-of-(oracle, book, external) construction and no impact prices | partial | high | M | yes |
| No price bands / max-deviation checks on orders relative to oracle or mark | absent | high | S | yes |
| No open-interest tracking or OI caps | absent | medium | M | yes |
| Market parameter governance is a no-op, so per-market funding cap / leverage / margin config never reaches the executor | stub | high | M | yes |
| Oracle aggregation defaults are weak for a production feed (3 reporters, 10-block window, no per-source weighting, pruning capped at 100 keys) | partial | medium | S | yes |

<details><summary>Hourly funding engine entirely absent (no premium index, interest rate, cap, settlement, or position accumulator)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Every hour HL pays funding = avg premium index (sampled from impact bid/ask vs oracle over the hour) + clamp(interest 0.01%/8h - premium, -0.05%, +0.05%), capped at 4%/hr, settled peer-to-peer on oracle-price notional; positions carry a cumulative funding accumulator so settlement is O(1) per position at touch time.
- **Torus evidence:** grep for 'funding' across crates/torus-core/src, crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs, crates/torus-rpc/src returns nothing; only hits are crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:828,906,1161 (max_funding_rate_bps field + its hash encoding). Position struct has no funding field: crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:33-41. Liquidation/margin equity never deducts funding: crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:182-250.
- **Suggestion:** Add `cum_funding_long/short: FixedPoint` per market in a new CF (or in OrderBook meta row) and `funding_entry: FixedPoint` on Position (crates/torus-core/src/position.rs, bump borsh layout). In native_executor end-of-block hook (where aggregate_oracle_prices should be called, see gap 2), every N blocks (~1h) compute premium = (impact_bid - oracle)/oracle if impact_bid>oracle etc., accumulate per-block samples, at hour boundary set rate = avg_premium + clamp(0.0000125 - avg_premium, -0.0005, 0.0005), clamp by MarketParams.max_funding_rate_bps, bump cum_funding. Settle lazily: in position touch paths (fill apply, liquidation check, cross_margin_equity) subtract size*(cum_funding - funding_entry). Expose via RPC get_funding_rate + funding history.

</details>

<details><summary>Oracle aggregation and liquidation sweep are implemented but never invoked (no end-of-block driver)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Validators publish oracle prices roughly every 3 seconds; the weighted-median oracle price is updated in-state each block and immediately used for margin, liquidation, and funding.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5904-5920 (aggregate_oracle_prices) and :5923-5965 (run_liquidation_checks) are `pub fn` with no callers: workspace grep for 'aggregate_oracle_prices(' and 'run_liquidation_checks(' returns only their definitions; the only SubmitOraclePrices producers are tests (crates/torus-bridge/tests/native_bridge_tests.rs:137, crates/torus-integration-tests/tests/chaos.rs:71). Consequently the 'agg' key read by get_price (oracle.rs:274-295) is never written in prod, so RPC get_mark_price (torus.rs:1609-1612) and precompile 0x0802 return 0.
- **Suggestion:** In the block-finalize path of the native executor (the function that drains the post-EVM action phases, around native_executor.rs:6159-6210 category ordering), after the Oracle phase call `aggregate_oracle_prices(ctx, &listed_markets, &validator_stakes)` with stakes pulled from ctx.staking, then collect `(market, price)` and call `run_liquidation_checks`. Deterministic: same block, same submissions. Trader list for liquidation should come from a per-market position index rather than a passed slice.

</details>

<details><summary>No node-side validator oracle publisher (cadence, source weighting, external feeds)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Each HL validator runs a price-fetcher pulling spot prices from Binance, OKX, Bybit, Kraken, Kucoin, Gate, MEXC, Hyperliquid spot (weighted 3,2,2,1,1,1,1,1 — exact weights from memory, verify) and signs a submission every ~3s; the oracle is the stake-weighted median of these.
- **Torus evidence:** grep -i 'oracle\|SubmitOraclePrices\|price_feed\|binance' in crates/torus-node/src and crates/torus-consensus/src returns only a comment at crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:8331 (unrelated). No task/service produces NativeAction::SubmitOraclePrices outside tests.
- **Suggestion:** Add an `oracle_publisher` task in crates/torus-node (tokio interval ~ every k blocks) that fetches configured CEX spot feeds (per-market source list + weights in node config), computes a local weighted median, signs a SubmitOraclePrices action with the validator key, and injects it into the mempool. Keep the on-chain side unchanged (already validates active validator). Off-chain only, so not consensus-breaking.

</details>

<details><summary>Mark price is just the oracle price; no median-of-(oracle, book, external) construction and no impact prices</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL mark price = median of (1) oracle price + 150s EMA of (mid - oracle), (2) median of best bid, best ask, last trade on HL, (3) median of Binance/OKX/Bybit/Gate/MEXC perp mid prices; if only two inputs exist use their average. Impact bid/ask = execution price for a fixed notional (e.g. 20000 USDC / N) walking the book, used for premium index and liquidation mark.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1609-1612 assigns oracle price to both mark_price and index_price; crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:155-163 and margin.rs:194,215 use raw oracle_prices as 'mark'. No impact-price computation anywhere in crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs or book_reader.rs (grep 'impact' returns nothing). Last-trade-price exists (torus.rs:1618-1636) but is not blended into the mark.
- **Suggestion:** Add `mark_price.rs` in torus-core: `fn compute_mark(oracle, book_best_bid, book_best_ask, last_trade, ema_basis) -> FixedPoint` taking median of available components; add `fn impact_prices(book, notional) -> (bid, ask)` walking levels via book_reader. Store the computed mark alongside the aggregated oracle in CF_NATIVE_ORACLE under a 'mark'+market key each block, and have margin/liquidation read mark instead of raw oracle. Use the same mark in RPC.

</details>

<details><summary>No price bands / max-deviation checks on orders relative to oracle or mark</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL rejects limit orders whose price is more than 95% away from the reference (mark/oracle) price, applies 80%-ish bands on resting orders for some assets, and market orders are IOC limits with a default 1%-slippage band (exact band percentages: verify). Liquidations and ADL also use mark not last trade to resist book manipulation.
- **Torus evidence:** Order validation in crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:387-418 checks only price>0, tick alignment, and MAX_ORDERS_PER_TRADER_PER_MARKET; crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4906-5010 (exec_place_order) contains no oracle/mark reference (grep for 'oracle\|band\|deviation' in that range: none). CoreError has InvalidPrice (error.rs:15) but no band error.
- **Suggestion:** In exec_place_order before reserve_for_qty (native_executor.rs ~4915), read `ctx.oracle.get_price(market_id, ctx.block_height)`; if non-stale and price>0, reject limit orders with \|price - mark\|/mark > band_bps (new MarketParams field, default e.g. 9500 bps) and clamp market orders to mark*(1±slippage_bps). Add CoreError::PriceOutOfBand. Skip the check when no oracle price exists so devnet/bench without oracle keeps working.

</details>

<details><summary>No open-interest tracking or OI caps</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL enforces per-asset open interest caps (new orders that would increase OI beyond the cap are rejected, reduce-only still allowed) and tracks OI per market for the info API.
- **Torus evidence:** grep -i 'open_interest\|oi_cap\|max_oi\|total_long\|total_short' across crates/torus-core/src, crates/torus-bridge/src, crates/torus-types/src returns no hits. MarketParams (torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156-1161) has only max_leverage and max_funding_rate_bps.
- **Suggestion:** Maintain `open_interest: FixedPoint` per market (sum of long sizes) updated in the position-apply path (where Position size changes after fills, native_executor.rs settle plan) and liquidation reduce path (liquidation.rs:312). Add `max_open_interest` to MarketParams; in exec_place_order reject position-increasing orders whose worst-case fill would exceed the cap (allow reduce_only). Expose via RPC market info.

</details>

<details><summary>Market parameter governance is a no-op, so per-market funding cap / leverage / margin config never reaches the executor</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Per-asset max leverage, margin tiers, funding caps, OI caps and listing/delisting are live parameters updated by the core team (and HIP-3 deployers) and take effect immediately in the matching/margin engine.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3328-3336: UpdateMarketParams/ListMarket/DelistMarket return ok(…,0) with an explicit 'Intentional stubs' comment. ctx.margin_configs is initialised empty at :1842 and grep for 'margin_configs.insert' finds nothing, so reserve_for_qty_cfg falls back to the hardcoded 20x at :4813-4815 for every market. Governance ListMarket builds ExecutionPayload::MarketListing at :5744 but nothing consumes it into executor state.
- **Suggestion:** Implement a market registry CF (market_id -> MarketParams + MarketMarginConfig + tick/lot); make exec for ListMarket/UpdateMarketParams/DelistMarket write it, load it into ctx.margin_configs on executor construction (native_executor.rs:1740-1842), and have the funding engine and band/OI checks read from it. Allocate market_id from a registry counter rather than hardcoding.

</details>

<details><summary>Oracle aggregation defaults are weak for a production feed (3 reporters, 10-block window, no per-source weighting, pruning capped at 100 keys)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL oracle requires contributions from a supermajority of stake, is refreshed every ~3s, and weights multiple external sources per validator before the on-chain stake-weighted median.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:21-22,123-131 (DEFAULT_MAX_ORACLE_AGE=100, min reporters=3, window=10); :327-330 prunes at most 100 stale keys per aggregate call; collect_submissions does a full prefix iteration per market per block (:305-325). OracleConfig::default() is hardcoded at native_executor.rs:1740 and torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1608 with no genesis/config override.
- **Suggestion:** Make OracleConfig part of genesis/chain params; require submitted stake >= 2/3 of active stake (not just a count) before accepting a new aggregate; index submissions by block prefix so pruning and collection are O(window) rather than a full market scan.

</details>

*Confidence notes:* Verified by direct read: oracle.rs full logic, exec_submit_oracle_prices, aggregate_oracle_prices/run_liquidation_checks and their lack of callers (workspace grep), market stubs at 3328-3336, empty margin_configs with no insert, order_book validation block, RPC get_mark_price, absence of any 'funding'/'open_interest'/'impact' symbols in core/bridge/rpc. Not verified: whether some out-of-tree binary (devnet/tools scripts) submits oracle prices, and whether the consensus app has an end-of-block hook that could cheaply host the aggregation call (I did not read app.rs beyond grep). HL facts I am less sure of: exact CEX source weights for the oracle (3/2/2/1/1/1/1/1 is from memory), the 150s EMA term in mark price component 1, exact order price band percentages (95% / 80%) and the default market-order slippage band, and whether the interest-rate component is 0.01%/8h vs 0.01%/hr (deep-dive says 0.01% per 8h; the funding cap of 4%/hr and the ±0.05% clamp are consistent with the deep-dive section 5.3).

### fees

#### fees — opus

Torus has no trading-fee engine at all. Fills settle realized PnL and margin only. Nothing in the fill path, the Fill struct, order params or market params refers to a fee, and `ctx.total_native_fees` is declared, set to 0 and read, but never incremented on current main (the prior audit claim still holds). The only fee flow that exists is EVM gas: the block's `gas_used*effective_gas_price` sum is passed to `distribute_fees`, which splits it by hard-coded constants that change linearly over 1825 epochs (`lerp_bps`) into burn, validator, treasury and dev pool. Those credits appear to mint new balance on top of what revm already burned or paid to the proposer, so they look like supply inflation rather than a redistribution. The genesis `ChainConfig` fee-split fields are loaded but nothing reads them. Everything Hyperliquid builds on trading fees is absent: maker/taker schedules, 14-day volume tiers, maker rebates, HYPE-staking discounts, referrals, builder codes (approveBuilderFee and the per-order builder fee), spot-vs-perp schedules, fee routing to HLP and the Assistance Fund, and the flat withdrawal fee.

**Already present:**
- Block-level fee distribution hook is wired into the commit path: crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1939 calls NativeExecutor::distribute_fees(&mut ctx, computed_fee_revenue) every native block (after process_governance, before process_epoch_boundary)
- distribute_fees implementation: crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5991-6014 sums ctx.total_native_fees + EVM fees and calls RewardDistributor::distribute_block_fees
- Fee split engine with linear interpolation start->end over TRANSITION_EPOCHS=1825: crates/torus-economics/src/rewards.rs:24-75 (burn/validator/treasury/dev_pool), constants at crates/torus-economics/src/types.rs:337-349 (start 10/0/45/45%, end 25/25/25/25%)
- Validator fee share goes to the proposer's delegators pro-rata after commission: crates/torus-economics/src/rewards.rs:78-110 (distribute_validator_share)
- EVM fee revenue computation: crates/torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs:389-394 compute_fee_revenue = sum(gas_used*effective_gas_price) over receipts; invoked at crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1588
- EIP-1559 base-fee floor in the EVM mempool: crates/torus-mempool/src/validate.rs:81-84 (base fee frozen at 1 gwei per the comment)
- Treasury and dev pool addresses are in ChainConfig: crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1235-1240
- userFills/newTrades WS streams exist (crates/torus-rpc/src/streams.rs:227-258) and carry closedPnl/startPosition/dir. They have no fee field, but they are the natural place to add one

| Gap | Status | Impact | Effort | Lockstep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Perp trading fees are never charged (total_native_fees never incremented) | absent | critical | L | yes |
| EVM gas fees appear to be re-minted by distribute_fees (double count / inflation) | buggy | high | M | yes |
| Genesis fee-split config is ignored; split is hard-coded constants | unwired | medium | S | yes |
| No 14-day volume tracking or tiered fee schedule | absent | high | M | yes |
| No maker rebates | absent | medium | S | yes |
| No staking-based fee discount | absent | medium | S | yes |
| No builder codes (approveBuilderFee / per-order builder fee) | absent | high | M | yes |
| No referral system | absent | low | M | yes |
| No spot fee schedule (and no spot book) | absent | medium | XL | yes |
| No flat withdrawal fee | absent | low | S | yes |
| Fee data missing from user-facing APIs (userFills, userFees) | absent | medium | S | no |

<details><summary>Perp trading fees are never charged (total_native_fees never incremented)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Every perp fill charges the taker a fee (base 0.045%) and the maker a fee (base 0.015%, falling to 0 or a rebate at higher tiers), debited in USDC from the trader's margin at fill time and reported per fill (fee, feeToken) in userFills.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1374 declares total_native_fees, :1853 sets it to 0, :5995 reads it. No write exists anywhere (grep for total_native_fees over crates/ finds only these lines plus the doc comment at :4307, which says 'NO fees are touched in Phase 4'). apply_fill_via_caches at native_executor.rs:4713-4737 credits only closed_pnl to bal.available and debits no fee. The Fill struct at crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:52-61 has no fee field. torus-core/src has no fee references at all.
- **Suggestion:** Add maker_fee_bps/taker_fee_bps (signed, so a maker rebate can be negative) to the per-market config (MarketParams in torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156 and the margin_configs map in ctx). In apply_fill_via_caches, or in pass B of settle_market_results_{sequential,parallel} (native_executor.rs:4081/4328), compute fee = notional*bps for the taker and the maker, debit bal.available, and accumulate into ctx.total_native_fees in canonical fill order (taker then maker), so the parallel path stays byte-identical. The determinism comment at :4305-4308 must be updated. Add fee_raw to BlockFills extras so the userFills stream (streams.rs) can report fee. Needs a lockstep upgrade at a fork height.

</details>

<details><summary>EVM gas fees appear to be re-minted by distribute_fees (double count / inflation)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** On HyperEVM, both the base fee and the priority fee are burned. Validators receive nothing from gas, and nothing is re-credited anywhere.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs:389-394 computes revenue as gas_used*effective_gas_price (the full amount the sender paid). The EVM env sets beneficiary to the proposer (crates/torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:146, proposer.rs:93), so revm already pays the tip to the proposer and burns the base fee. Then crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1939 passes the same total into distribute_fees, and rewards.rs:57-72 credits 90% of it (burn is a no-op) through staking.credit_balance (crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:836-840, which does account.balance += amount via put_account). Nothing debits these credits, so it looks like a mint of roughly 0.9x the gas volume per block, plus the proposer collects the tip twice.
- **Suggestion:** Choose one model. (a) HL parity: burn all gas by setting beneficiary to Address::ZERO or a burn sink, and drop EVM fees from distribute_fees (pass 0). (b) If the protocol wants to share gas revenue, set the EVM beneficiary to a protocol fee-sink account, then have distribute_fees debit that sink by exactly the amount it credits out. Add an integration test asserting that total supply is conserved across a block containing EVM txs (crates/torus-integration-tests/tests/fee_flow.rs is the right home).

</details>

<details><summary>Genesis fee-split config is ignored; split is hard-coded constants</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL routes trading fees to HLP, to the Assistance Fund (USDC→HYPE buyback, then burn), and to market deployers (up to 50% for HIP-3 and spot deployers). Validators get no fee share.
- **Torus evidence:** ChainConfig.fee_burn_bps/fee_validator_bps/fee_treasury_bps/fee_dev_pool_bps (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1231-1234) are populated from genesis (crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:502-505) but read only in tests and construction sites (app.rs:3716, main.rs:309). distribute_block_fees uses constants instead: lerp_bps(FEE_START_*, FEE_END_*) at rewards.rs:37-55, with constants at torus-economics/src/types.rs:340-349. Governance ParameterChange (native_executor.rs:5738-5743) passes key and value through, and nothing showed it mapping to fee parameters.
- **Suggestion:** Either delete the dead ChainConfig fields, or thread them into NativeExecContext and use them in distribute_block_fees, with governance-updatable overrides stored in state (for example a CF_PARAMS key 'fee_split'). Add destinations matching HL: an assistance-fund or buyback account and an LP-vault (HLP-equivalent) share, plus a deployer share once permissionless listing exists.

</details>

<details><summary>No 14-day volume tracking or tiered fee schedule</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Fee tier is set by 14-day weighted volume, (perp volume) + 2x(spot volume), across 7 tiers, from 0.045%/0.015% at base down to 0.024%/0.000% for perps. Tiers are recomputed daily per user, and subaccounts aggregate to the master account.
- **Torus evidence:** grep -i volume over crates/torus-core/src and crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs (excluding comments and tests) returns nothing. No per-user volume state exists, and MarketParams (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156-1162) has no fee or tier fields.
- **Suggestion:** Add a per-user rolling volume ledger (for example a CF_USER_VOLUME row of 14 daily buckets keyed by day index from the block timestamp), updated in fill settlement pass B. Add a global FeeSchedule {tiers: [(min_volume, taker_bps, maker_bps)]} in state, editable by governance. Look up the tier per fill from the bucket sum. Keep the lookup O(1) by caching each user's tier for the day.

</details>

<details><summary>No maker rebates</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Makers whose share of total maker volume exceeds 0.5%, 1.5% or 3.0% earn rebates of -0.001%, -0.002% or -0.003%, paid continuously per fill. Aligned-quote and stable pairs get further rebate boosts.
- **Torus evidence:** No fee or rebate field in Fill (order_book.rs:52-61), PlaceOrderParams (torus-types/src/lib.rs:1060-1069) or MarketParams (lib.rs:1156-1162). A grep for 'rebate' over crates/ returns no hits.
- **Suggestion:** Make maker_fee_bps signed in the fee schedule. When it is negative, credit the maker from the fee pool collected in the same block, never by minting. The rebate must be bounded by the taker fee on the same fill so the protocol stays net non-negative per fill. Compute maker share from the volume ledger above.

</details>

<details><summary>No staking-based fee discount</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Staked HYPE gives a discount stacked on the volume tier: 5% for >10 staked, 10% for >100, 15% for >1k, 20% for >10k, 30% for >100k, 40% for >500k. The account's delegated stake is what counts.
- **Torus evidence:** The staking module exists (crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs, e.g. the delegations_for_validator helper used at rewards.rs:106), but no fee path consults it, because no trading fee path exists (see the first gap). Grepping the fill path for 'discount' or 'staked' finds nothing.
- **Suggestion:** When computing the fee per fill, look up the trader's total delegation (cache it per block or per epoch from StakingManager, since delegations only change at epoch boundaries or through explicit actions), map it to a discount tier, and multiply the tier's fee by (1 - discount). Keep the tier table in governance-editable state.

</details>

<details><summary>No builder codes (approveBuilderFee / per-order builder fee)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** A user signs ApproveBuilderFee{builder, maxFeeRate}, capped at 0.1% for perps and 1% for spot. Orders may then carry builder:{b, f} with f no larger than the approved max. The builder fee is charged on top of the exchange fee and credited to the builder, whose account needs at least 100 USDC in perps equity. userFills reports builderFee.
- **Torus evidence:** The NativeAction enum (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:582-679) has no ApproveBuilderFee variant. PlaceOrderParams (lib.rs:1060-1069) has no builder field. SessionScope::Trading (lib.rs:264-271) lists only order actions. A grep for 'builder' finds only BundleState and config builders, nothing fee-related.
- **Suggestion:** Add NativeAction::ApproveBuilderFee{builder: Address, max_fee_bps: u16}, stored at CF_BUILDER_APPROVALS[(user, builder)], plus EIP-712 typing and an exclusion from Trading-scoped sessions. Add Option<BuilderFee{builder, fee_tenth_bps}> to PlaceOrderParams, appended as an optional tail so existing hashes keep their encoding, and validate it against the approval at placement. At fill settlement, debit the taker (or the order owner) and credit the builder in pass B order. Also extend CoreWriterAction::PlaceOrder (lib.rs:1182).

</details>

<details><summary>No referral system</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** A user can set a referral code (setReferrer) and gets a 4% fee discount on their first $25M of volume. The referrer earns a share (10%) of the referee's fees. Codes are registered by users who have traded enough volume.
- **Torus evidence:** The NativeAction enum (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:582-679) has no SetReferrer or RegisterReferrer variant. Grepping 'referr' over crates/ returns no hits.
- **Suggestion:** Once fees exist: add RegisterReferralCode{code} and SetReferrer{code} actions, a CF_REFERRALS map, and per-referee cumulative volume (from the volume ledger). Apply the discount in fee computation, and in pass B credit the referrer's share out of the collected fee rather than minting it.

</details>

<details><summary>No spot fee schedule (and no spot book)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Spot has its own schedule (base 0.070% taker / 0.040% maker, top tier 0.025%/0.000%). Spot volume counts double toward tier volume, stable pairs are 80% cheaper for takers, and spot deployers can keep up to 50% of fees.
- **Torus evidence:** TransferToSpot/TransferToPerp exist as actions (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:602-609), but searching crates/ for spot_book, SpotMarket or 'spot order' returns nothing. MarketListing (lib.rs:1165-1172) has no market-kind field to tell spot from perp.
- **Suggestion:** This depends on a spot CLOB, which is out of scope for the fees area. When markets are added, add a market_kind {Perp, Spot} to the market config, give the FeeSchedule two tier tables, and weight spot volume 2x in the volume ledger.

</details>

<details><summary>No flat withdrawal fee</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Withdrawing from HyperCore to the Arbitrum bridge costs a flat 1 USDC, which covers the validators' gas for the bridge transaction.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3300-3302 routes Withdraw to exec_withdraw_to. That handler (around :5844-5860) converts the amount and calls Lockbox::withdraw_from_native_to with the full amount, and deducts no fee.
- **Suggestion:** Add a governance parameter withdraw_fee (FixedPoint). In exec_withdraw_to, require amount > fee, debit amount + fee (or net it out), and accumulate the fee into ctx.total_native_fees so it reaches distribute_fees.

</details>

<details><summary>Fee data missing from user-facing APIs (userFills, userFees)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** userFills rows include fee, feeToken and builderFee. The info endpoint 'userFees' returns the user's daily volumes, active tier, staking discount, referral discount and current maker/taker rates. The fee schedule is queryable.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-rpc/src/streams.rs:227-258 (fills_for_user) builds rows with orderId, startPosition, closedPnl and dir from block.extras, and has no fee field (see the test row at streams.rs:436). grep for '"fee"' across crates/torus-rpc/src finds only eth.rs:160 (base_fee).
- **Suggestion:** After fees are charged: add maker_fee_raw/taker_fee_raw (and builder_fee) to the BlockFills extras and emit fee/feeToken/builderFee in RpcUserFill. Add a torus_userFees RPC that reads the volume ledger, staking tier and referral state. The RPC part does not affect consensus, but the extras format is written at exec.

</details>

*Confidence notes:* Read-only check against current main. `total_native_fees` is still never incremented: a grep of all crates/ found only the declaration (native_executor.rs:1374), the initializer (:1853), the read (:5995) and a doc comment (:4307). The EVM double-mint finding is my inference from the code and was not run. revm normally burns the base fee and pays the tip to `beneficiary`, and here the beneficiary is the proposer. `distribute_fees` then credits 90% of the full gas_used*effective_gas_price through `StakingManager::credit_balance`, which does put_account on the state backend. I did not confirm that this is the same account ledger the EVM debits from, or whether some settlement step elsewhere offsets it. Treat it as PLAUSIBLE and verify with a supply-conservation test. I also did not read `exec_withdraw_to` in full, only the lines around 5844-5860. HL facts I am unsure of: the exact middle-tier rates and thresholds; the referral numbers (4% discount, referrer share near 10%, $25M cap from the research doc); the builder-fee caps (0.1% perps, 1% spot) and the 100 USDC builder minimum; whether the flat withdrawal fee is still exactly 1 USDC; and the current routing between the Assistance Fund and HLP after the late-2025 governance changes. The research doc gives the staking discount tiers, maker-rebate thresholds and spot base rates; I did not check them against live HL docs.

#### fees — fable

Torus has a complete block-level fee *distribution* pipeline (4-way burn/validator/treasury/dev_pool split with BPS interpolation, proposer commission + delegator pro-rata, wired at end of every block) but no trading-fee *collection* at all: `total_native_fees` is initialised to 0 and never incremented, `Fill` carries no fee, and fill settlement only moves realized PnL. There is no fee schedule (no maker/taker bps on MarketParams, no 14d-volume tiers, no maker rebates, no staking discount, no referral, no builder codes) and no spot book, so HL's spot schedule has nothing to attach to. The only fees that flow today are EVM gas fees, and those appear to be counted twice: revm pays the priority fee to the proposer (beneficiary = proposer) and burns the base fee, then `distribute_fees` re-credits the full gas_used x effective_gas_price to treasury/dev_pool/validators via a mint-style `credit_balance` with no debit, and the "burn" bucket is a no-op. Genesis fee-split bps are parsed into ChainConfig but RewardDistributor reads hard-coded constants instead. The prior audit's "trading fees never charged" claim is confirmed on current main.

**Already present:**
- Block fee split schedule (burn/validator/treasury/dev_pool, lerp from epoch 0 to 1825): crates/torus-economics/src/rewards.rs:24-73, constants crates/torus-economics/src/types.rs:337-349
- Fee distribution wired in the prod exec path every block: crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1939 -> crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5991-6013 (distribute_fees)
- Validator fee share -> proposer commission + delegators pro-rata: crates/torus-economics/src/rewards.rs:76-110 (distribute_validator_share)
- EVM gas fee revenue computed per block and cross-checked in header validation: crates/torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs:389-394 (compute_fee_revenue), crates/torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:165-168, header field crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:459-460
- Genesis fee-split config parsed (start/end/transition_epochs) and mapped to ChainConfig fee_*_bps: crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:138-150, 502-505, 607-611; crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1230-1234
- Maker/taker attribution per fill (needed for any maker/taker schedule): crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:52-61 (Fill{maker,taker,maker_side}); userFills stream exposes role/startPosition/closedPnl/dir: crates/torus-rpc/src/streams.rs:433-437
- Fill settlement path where a fee debit would slot in: crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4713-4738 (apply_fill_via_caches credits closed_pnl to bal.available)
- Burn supply tracker (cumulative_burned) exists for inflation accounting: crates/torus-economics/src/rewards.rs:380-383
- StakingManager with per-address stake/delegation (prerequisite for staking-based fee discounts): crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs (credit_balance at 836-841)
