<details><summary>Trading fees are never charged or accumulated</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Every perp fill charges taker 4.5 bps / maker 1.5 bps at base tier (spot 7/4 bps), deducted from the account's USDC margin at fill time and routed to HLP / assistance fund / deployer.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1374 (field `total_native_fees: u64`), :1853 (only write: `total_native_fees: 0`), :5995 (only read, in distribute_fees); grep over crates/ shows no other reference. crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:52-61 Fill has no fee field. crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4713-4738 apply_fill_via_caches only credits closed_pnl, no fee debit.
- **Suggestion:** In native_executor.rs PlaceOrder settlement (around the apply_fill calls at ~5042/5062 and apply_fill_via_caches 4713), compute fee = notional * fee_bps(role, trader) / 10_000, debit `bal.available` for taker and maker via BalanceCache, add to `ctx.total_native_fees` (widen to u128/U256; it is u64 today), and extend `Fill`/packed fill rows with `fee`. distribute_fees then already routes it. Must be deterministic and included in the native state root.

</details>

<details><summary>No fee schedule parameters (maker/taker bps, tiers by 14d volume)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Tiered schedule keyed on 14d weighted volume (perps + 2x spot): taker 0.045%->0.024%, maker 0.015%->0.000% across 7 tiers; per-user rolling volume tracked in state.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156-1162 MarketParams = {tick_size, lot_size, max_leverage, maintenance_margin_bps, max_funding_rate_bps} -- no fee fields. No volume tracking: grep for volume_14d/fee_tier/taker_fee/maker_fee returns nothing outside unrelated matches.
- **Suggestion:** Add a FeeSchedule (vector of {min_14d_volume, taker_bps, maker_bps}) to ChainConfig (types/lib.rs ~1226) with governance update via UpdateMarketParams/new action; add a per-user rolling-volume CF (daily buckets, 14 entries) updated on each fill in native_executor.rs; look up tier at fill time. Keep bps as u16/u32 integer math on FixedPoint notional.

</details>

<details><summary>Maker rebates absent</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Makers supplying >0.5%/1.5%/3.0% of total 14d maker volume receive -0.001%/-0.002%/-0.003% (paid out of taker fees); top tier maker fee is 0.
- **Torus evidence:** Depends on gap 1; crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:52-61 and native_executor.rs:4713-4738 have no maker-side credit path; no rebate symbol anywhere in crates/.
- **Suggestion:** Once fees exist, allow signed maker_bps (negative = rebate) in FeeSchedule; credit maker from the taker fee before routing the remainder to total_native_fees. Needs global 14d maker-volume counter to compute share-of-maker-volume tiers.

</details>

<details><summary>Staking-based fee discounts absent</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Staked HYPE tiers (Wood >10 ... Diamond >500k) give 5%-40% discount stacked on volume tier.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs exposes stakes/delegations (e.g. get_validator, credit_balance :836) but nothing in the order path reads them; no discount symbol in crates/torus-bridge or crates/torus-core.
- **Suggestion:** After fee lookup in native_executor.rs, read the trader's permanent stake / delegated total from StakingManager (cache per block) and apply a discount table from ChainConfig. Torus's permanent-staking model is a natural fit (stake is irreversible, so discount tier cannot be gamed by unstaking).

</details>

<details><summary>Referral discounts/rewards absent</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Referred users get a 4% discount on first $25M volume; referrers earn 10% of referees' fees; set via setReferrer action, queried via referral info endpoint.
- **Torus evidence:** grep -rn referr crates/ returns no hits; crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs NativeAction enum (around :600-620, Withdraw at :610) has no SetReferrer variant.
- **Suggestion:** Add NativeAction::SetReferrer{code} + referral CF; at fee time split referee discount / referrer reward before routing to total_native_fees. Low priority until fees exist.

</details>

<details><summary>Builder codes (approveBuilderFee, per-order builder fee) absent</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** User signs ApproveBuilderFee{builder, maxFeeRate}; orders may carry {b: builder, f: fee_tenths_bps}; builder fee is charged on top of the protocol fee and credited to the builder; exposed in userFills as builderFee.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:36-48 Order has no builder field; crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1182-1189 CoreWriterAction::PlaceOrder has no builder field; no ApproveBuilderFee in NativeAction (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs ~:600-620); grep -i builder in crates/ hits only revm BundleState::builder.
- **Suggestion:** Add NativeAction::ApproveBuilderFee{builder, max_fee_tenth_bps} with a per-(user,builder) CF; add optional {builder, fee_tenth_bps} to NativeAction::PlaceOrder and the EIP-712 encoder (types/lib.rs ~:792-906); at taker fill, debit builder fee from taker and credit builder balance; surface builderFee in userFills (streams.rs ~:433). This is HL's main front-end distribution lever and is cheap once gap 1 lands.

</details>

<details><summary>EVM gas fees appear to be paid twice (priority fee to proposer by revm, then full revenue re-minted by distribute_fees)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HyperEVM burns both base and priority fees; no re-crediting, no inflation from gas.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs:93 and crates/torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:146 set `beneficiary: proposer`; crates/torus-evm/src/executor.rs:184-191 uses Context::mainnet() + SpecId::CANCUN with no beneficiary-reward disable (disable_base_fee only in call_mode :188-189). crates/torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs:389-394 compute_fee_revenue = sum(gas_used*effective_gas_price) which is then passed to distribute_fees (native_executor.rs:5995) and credited via crates/torus-economics/src/rewards.rs:57-70 using StakingManager::credit_balance (crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:836-841: `account.balance += amount`, no debit from anywhere). rewards.rs:21 documents 'Burn portion is destroyed (no-op)'.
- **Suggestion:** Decide one model. Either (a) set beneficiary to a dedicated fee-sink address (or zero) and have distribute_fees debit that sink before crediting buckets, so no net mint; or (b) keep revm's native handling (priority -> proposer, base burned) and pass only the amounts that were actually collected into a sink. Also make the burn bucket actually reduce supply (debit sink + bump cumulative_burned at rewards.rs:380). Add a supply-conservation test: sum(balances) + burned is invariant across a block with EVM txs.

</details>

<details><summary>Genesis/ChainConfig fee split bps are ignored; schedule is hard-coded</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** N/A (HL has fixed destinations) -- but Torus's own design says ratios are governance-configurable.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:502-505 populates ChainConfig.fee_burn_bps/..; crates/torus-economics/src/rewards.rs:38-55 uses FEE_START_*/FEE_END_*/TRANSITION_EPOCHS constants from crates/torus-economics/src/types.rs:337-349; grep for fee_burn_bps outside torus-genesis/torus-types hits only test fixtures (app.rs:3716-3719, integration test :66-69).
- **Suggestion:** Pass the ChainConfig (or a FeeSplitConfig) into NativeExecContext and have distribute_block_fees take start/end/transition from it instead of constants; governance proposal type to update it. Keep constants only as genesis defaults.

</details>

<details><summary>Fee destinations differ from HL: no HLP vault, no assistance-fund buyback, no deployer share</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Fees go to HLP (per vault share), the Assistance Fund (auto-buys HYPE, burned), and up to 50% to HIP-3/spot deployers. Nothing to validators.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-economics/src/rewards.rs:57-70 routes only to burn(no-op)/validator/treasury/dev_pool; crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3329-3337 ListMarket/UpdateMarketParams/DelistMarket are ok-stubs (ECON-PF-07), so there is no deployer identity to pay. No vault module in crates/.
- **Suggestion:** This is a deliberate Torus economic design choice (4-way split), not necessarily a gap to close. If HL parity is wanted: add a per-market `deployer` + `deployer_fee_bps` to MarketListing when the market registry lands, split before the 4-way split; HLP/assistance-fund equivalents require vault + buyback modules (separate area).

</details>

<details><summary>No spot fee schedule / spot trading</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Spot book with its own schedule (0.070%/0.040% base, down to 0.025%/0), 2x weighting of spot volume in the 14d tier, stable-pair and aligned-quote modifiers.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3296-3297 TransferToSpot just calls exec_withdraw_from_native (moves funds to EVM); no spot order book in crates/torus-core/src (order_book.rs is perp-only, fills go through PositionManager).
- **Suggestion:** Out of scope for fees alone; note that the FeeSchedule type should carry separate perp/spot tables and a spot-volume multiplier so a later spot book plugs in without a second schema change.

</details>

<details><summary>No fee visibility in RPC: userFills lacks fee/feeToken/builderFee, no userFees endpoint</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** userFills includes fee, feeToken, builderFee per fill; info type userFees returns the user's current taker/maker rates, 14d volume, active referral discount and staking discount.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-rpc/src/streams.rs:433-437 and :450-454 userFills row keys = tradeId, marketId, side, price, quantity, role, orderId, startPosition, closedPnl, dir, blockNumber, timestamp (no fee). RPC method list in crates/torus-rpc/src/lib.rs (torus_getTradeHistory :2439, torus_getUserTrades :2528, torus_getOrderBook :2613) has no fee query.
- **Suggestion:** After gap 1: add `fee` to the packed fill row and the userFills/newTrades JSON (streams.rs builders), and a torus_getUserFees RPC that returns effective rates from the FeeSchedule + volume CF + stake tier. Row-format change is state/DA-visible only if fills are in the native root; RPC shape is not consensus.

</details>

<details><summary>Withdrawal fee absent</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Flat 1 USDC fee on L1 withdrawals (to Arbitrum); deposits free; HyperCore actions gasless.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5848-5854 exec_withdraw_to passes the full amount to Lockbox::withdraw_from_native_to with no fee deduction; TransferToSpot :3296 likewise.
- **Suggestion:** Torus's Withdraw moves TRS native->EVM on the same chain (no external bridge), so a withdrawal fee is arguably unnecessary; if anti-spam is wanted, deduct a flat ChainConfig.withdraw_fee into total_native_fees in exec_withdraw_to. Torus native actions are already gasless like HL (no gas symbol in the native path).

</details>

*Confidence notes:* Verified by reading: total_native_fees has exactly three references (decl, init 0, read) on current main; Fill/Order/MarketParams/PlaceOrder have no fee or builder fields; distribute_fees is wired at app.rs:1939; credit_balance is a pure balance increment; RewardDistributor uses constants not ChainConfig. Not verified (read-only, no build/test run): whether revm's Cancun mainnet handler actually credits the priority fee to `beneficiary` in this executor configuration -- I believe revm's default post-execution does reward the beneficiary and that Torus has not disabled it, which would make the EVM double-count gap CONFIRMED; treat it as PLAUSIBLE until a supply-conservation test is run. I did not inspect how `evm_fee_revenue` is reconciled against EVM account balances in the state root. HL facts I am confident in: base perp 4.5/1.5 bps, spot 7/4 bps, 14d weighted volume with 2x spot, staking discounts 5-40%, builder codes via approveBuilderFee with fee in tenths of a bp, EIP-1559 burn on HyperEVM, 1 USDC withdrawal fee. Less sure: exact referral numbers (4% discount / 10% reward, $25M cap -- the deep-dive only states the $25M cap), exact maker-rebate thresholds (taken from research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md:274), and the current precise split of fees between HLP and the Assistance Fund (the deep-dive gives direction, not ratios; in practice most non-HLP fees go to the Assistance Fund). The 'TransferToSpot is a withdraw' claim is from the dispatch arm only; I did not read exec_withdraw_from_native.

### margin-liq

#### margin-liq — opus

Torus has library-level margin and liquidation code in crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs and liquidation.rs: a cross/isolated MarginType, notional-based leverage tiers, maintenance margin set at 50% of initial at tier max leverage, force close, ADL and socialized loss. Almost none of it runs in production. MarginEngine::check_initial_margin and check_margin_at_match have no non-test callers, and run_liquidation_checks (native_executor.rs:5923) has no caller at all, so liquidations never happen on a live chain. margin_configs starts empty and nothing in production adds to it. In practice the margin model is: reserve notional/20 for a resting limit order, then give that reservation back to `available` when the order fills. Positions therefore open with zero locked collateral, every fill is hard-coded to Cross, market orders reserve nothing, and withdrawals only check `available`. Leverage is unbounded, and losses can drive balances negative with nothing to absorb them. There are no updateLeverage or updateIsolatedMargin actions, no mark price, no partial or backstop liquidation and no liquidator vault. The dormant liquidation code also has correctness bugs that would surface the moment it is wired in.

**Already present:**
- MarginType {Cross, Isolated} enum, and a Position.isolated_margin field persisted in Borsh (crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:45-66, 87-140)
- Notional-based margin tiers 50x/20x/10x/5x and effective_max_leverage lookup (crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:18-53); MarketMarginConfig with maintenance_factor_bps=5000, i.e. maintenance = 50% of initial at max leverage, the same ratio HL uses (margin.rs:61-79)
- MarginEngine::check_initial_margin (cross free margin = equity - maintenance; isolated = available >= IM), check_margin_at_match, cross_margin_equity, total_maintenance_margin, check_isolated_maintenance (margin.rs:91-250). Library only, unwired (see gaps)
- LiquidationEngine: check_liquidations (cross account-level plus isolated per position), execute_liquidation at oracle price with a 2.5% penalty sent to the insurance fund, auto_deleverage, socialize_loss (insurance fund first, then pro-rata across eligible traders) (crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:72-450). Library only
- Insurance fund balance stored as a raw i128 under key b"insurance_fund" in CF_NATIVE_BALANCES (liquidation.rs:59, 432-450)
- Order-margin reservation for resting limit orders, with telescoping release on fill, cancel and maker consumption (A5), so order_margin does not leak (native_executor.rs:3755-3781, 4123-4160, 4781-4818, 4836+); the parallel Phase-2 prepare is equivalent (native_executor.rs:3980-4040)
- Position open/increase/reduce/close/flip transitions with weighted-average entry and realized-PnL credit (position.rs:434-540), plus a PositionCache batch path
- Oracle-price rejection of zero or negative prices in liquidation (liquidation.rs:160-164, 199-203)
- RPC get_position with unrealized PnL from the oracle price, and a balances endpoint with total_margin_used = order_margin + sum(isolated_margin) (crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:772-821, 849-875)
- Metrics counter liquidations_triggered (crates/torus-telemetry/src/lib.rs:61)

| Gap | Status | Impact | Effort | Lockstep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Liquidation engine never runs in production | unwired | critical | M | yes |
| Positions hold zero collateral: order margin goes back to `available` on fill | buggy | critical | L | yes |
| No per-market margin configs in production (margin_configs always empty) | unwired | high | M | yes |
| No updateLeverage / updateIsolatedMargin actions; every fill is hard-coded to Cross | absent | high | M | yes |
| Market orders reserve no margin and are not margin-checked | buggy | critical | S | yes |
| Withdrawals and transfers ignore open positions (no withdrawable computation) | absent | critical | S | yes |
| Cross liquidation executes all of an account's positions at one market's oracle price | buggy | high | S | yes |
| Liquidation is an off-book force close at oracle; no market liquidation, partial liquidation, or liquidator-vault backstop | partial | critical | XL | yes |
| ADL is not ranked or side-aware, pays winners instead of closing at the bankruptcy price, and its result is discarded | buggy | high | M | yes |
| No mark price; margin and liquidation use raw oracle, and tiers are discontinuous step functions | absent | medium | M | yes |
| reduce_only not enforced; liquidations and risk-reducing orders cannot rely on it | unwired | medium | S | yes |
| No portfolio margin and no spot-collateral unification | absent | low | XL | yes |

<details><summary>Liquidation engine never runs in production</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HyperCore checks every account against maintenance margin continuously, using mark price, as part of block execution. Undercollateralized accounts are liquidated in the same block.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5923 defines pub fn run_liquidation_checks. A repo-wide grep for run_liquidation_checks returns only that definition, with no caller in torus-consensus, torus-node or the block pipeline. LiquidationEngine is used only inside it (native_executor.rs:13, 5938, 5965, 5972).
- **Suggestion:** Call run_liquidation_checks once per block from the exec pipeline (crates/torus-consensus/src/exec_pipeline.rs or the end-of-block hook that already calls aggregate_oracle_prices and distribute_fees). Run it after oracle aggregation and before fee distribution, with a deterministic trader set: an index of traders with open positions kept in state (a CF keyed by market then trader), not a caller-provided slice. Emit liquidation events to the trade stream. All nodes must upgrade together.

</details>

<details><summary>Positions hold zero collateral: order margin goes back to `available` on fill</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** When an order fills, its margin becomes position margin. For cross, account value must stay >= the initial margin of all positions (free collateral). For isolated, the margin is locked in the position. Users cannot open more than equity times leverage.
- **Torus evidence:** native_executor.rs:4615-4639 sets margin_release = the full reserved amount for filled quantity, returning it to available (4517-4520, 4155-4160). fill_transition always creates positions with isolated_margin: ZERO (crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:443-454, 520-529). Nothing in the executor counts open-position margin in `available`, so a trader can place, fill, and place again to build unbounded notional on the same collateral.
- **Suggestion:** Make account-level free collateral the gate. At Phase 2, require account_value (available + order_margin + sum of cross uPnL at mark) - sum(position IM at the user's leverage) - order IM >= new order IM. Call MarginEngine::check_initial_margin, and check_margin_at_match in Phase 4 per fill, cancelling the remainder if it fails. On fill, move the released order margin into position margin: for isolated, add it to pos.isolated_margin; for cross, keep a per-account cross_margin_used, or recompute it. Note that cross_margin_equity already subtracts order_margin even though the reserve also subtracts from available (margin.rs:190 vs native_executor.rs:3780). That double deduction has to be resolved when this is wired in.

</details>

<details><summary>No per-market margin configs in production (margin_configs always empty)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Each asset has its own maxLeverage and a margin table (tiers with maintenance deductions), set at listing and changeable by governance or the deployer (HIP-3).
- **Torus evidence:** native_executor.rs:1356 declares pub margin_configs: HashMap<MarketId, MarketMarginConfig>, initialised to HashMap::new() at 1842. The only inserts are in crates/torus-bridge/tests/maker_margin_release_tests.rs:500,503,664. reserve_for_qty_cfg therefore falls back to .unwrap_or(20) (native_executor.rs:4815-4816), and run_liquidation_checks iterates an empty map (5930-5936), so it would be a no-op even if it were called.
- **Suggestion:** Store MarketMarginConfig (max_leverage, tiers, maintenance) in a state CF populated from genesis markets and from ListMarket/UpdateMarketParams, which are currently no-op stubs at native_executor.rs:3332-3336. Load it into ctx.margin_configs at block start. Enforce config.max_leverage as a cap; it is never read in margin.rs today, only the tiers are.

</details>

<details><summary>No updateLeverage / updateIsolatedMargin actions; every fill is hard-coded to Cross</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** updateLeverage {asset, isCross, leverage} sets per-asset leverage and margin mode. A user may not switch an open position from cross to isolated, and lowering leverage is allowed only if margin suffices. updateIsolatedMargin (and topUpIsolatedOnlyMargin) adds or removes isolated margin. Isolated positions are margined separately from the cross account.
- **Torus evidence:** Grep for UpdateLeverage\|UpdateIsolatedMargin\|update_leverage over crates/ returns nothing. PlaceOrderParams has no leverage or margin-mode field (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1060-1069). Settlement passes MarginType::Cross for every fill (native_executor.rs:4663, 4730), so Position.isolated_margin is never non-zero outside tests.
- **Suggestion:** Add NativeAction::UpdateLeverage{market_id,is_cross,leverage} and UpdateIsolatedMargin{market_id,delta}, and store a per-(trader, market) leverage setting in a CF next to positions. Pass that setting to fill application instead of the MarginType::Cross literal, and use it for reserve_for_qty in place of tier max leverage. Validate leverage <= tier max for the resulting position notional. Add an EIP-712 type in torus-types/src/eip712.rs and an RPC/exchange endpoint.

</details>

<details><summary>Market orders reserve no margin and are not margin-checked</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Market orders, which are IOC limits with slippage, are checked against margin like any order. Fills that would breach initial margin are rejected.
- **Torus evidence:** native_executor.rs:3757 `let order_margin_required = if !is_market {...}`. The parallel prepare does the same at 3998-4007 (else FixedPoint::ZERO), and so does exec_place_order at 4914-4917 (comment: 'For market orders, margin is settled at fill time'). Nothing settles margin at fill time (see the zero-collateral gap).
- **Suggestion:** For market orders, compute a reservation from a worst-case price (oracle times (1 ± slippage cap), or the price limit HL takes as part of a market order). Alternatively, run check_margin_at_match per fill in Phase 4 and stop matching when free collateral is exhausted. Both need the zero-collateral fix first.

</details>

<details><summary>Withdrawals and transfers ignore open positions (no withdrawable computation)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** withdrawable = max(0, accountValue - total initial margin used by cross positions), computed with unrealized PnL at mark (only realized gains are withdrawable beyond margin). Withdraw and class transfers are bounded by it.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:89 and :140 check only `native_bal.available < amount`. exec_withdraw_to and exec_withdraw_from_native (native_executor.rs:5826-5857) apply no margin check. RPC balances report available_balance = native_bal.available with no withdrawable field (torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:867-875).
- **Suggestion:** Add MarginEngine::withdrawable(positions, trader, configs, mark_prices) = max(0, equity - sum(IM of cross positions) - order_margin). Gate Lockbox::withdraw_from_native, withdraw_from_native_to and TransferToSpot with it inside the executor, where oracle prices are available. Expose marginSummary{accountValue,totalNtlPos,totalMarginUsed} and withdrawable in RPC in the shape of HL's clearinghouseState.

</details>

<details><summary>Cross liquidation executes all of an account's positions at one market's oracle price</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Each position is closed at its own market price through the book. Cross liquidation is account-level but per-asset in execution.
- **Torus evidence:** run_liquidation_checks loops per market config (native_executor.rs:5937), but check_cross_liquidation flags every cross position of the trader in every market (crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:131-143). The loop then calls execute_liquidation(&ctx.positions, liq, oracle_price) with the oracle price of the loop's market_id (native_executor.rs:5952-5965), so a BTC-loop pass closes the trader's ETH position at the BTC price. total_maintenance_margin also applies one market's config to every market (margin.rs:202-229).
- **Suggestion:** Check cross accounts once per trader, outside the per-market loop. Close each flagged position at oracle_prices[liq.market_id]. Change total_maintenance_margin to take &HashMap<MarketId, MarketMarginConfig> and look up each position's own market config.

</details>

<details><summary>Liquidation is an off-book force close at oracle; no market liquidation, partial liquidation, or liquidator-vault backstop</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL first sends market orders to the book at mark price. Positions over about $100k (or ~20% at a time with a cooldown) are liquidated partially. If account equity drops below 2/3 of maintenance, the backstop liquidator (an HLP sub-vault) takes over the position and remaining collateral. Liquidated users keep remaining margin on market liquidations, and HL charges no separate penalty.
- **Torus evidence:** execute_liquidation (liquidation.rs:193-252) deletes the position via positions.delete_position at the oracle price, with no counterparty. Open interest becomes one-sided: the other traders' positions stay open and are now matched by nobody, so the system has net exposure. It charges a fixed 2.5% penalty (DEFAULT_LIQUIDATION_PENALTY_BPS liquidation.rs:62) and credits it to the insurance fund before checking solvency (219-222). When the trader is bankrupt, the fund is credited money that does not exist, and the deficit is clamped to zero on the trader (234-240). No vault or backstop account exists.
- **Suggestion:** Model liquidation as reduce-only IOC market orders the executor submits into the book for the liquidated account during the per-block liquidation phase, with partial sizing for large notional. If equity < 2/3 MM or the book cannot absorb the order, transfer the position at mark to a protocol backstop account (a liquidator vault address with its own NativeBalance). Penalize only from available equity, capped at that equity, never out of thin air.

</details>

<details><summary>ADL is not ranked or side-aware, pays winners instead of closing at the bankruptcy price, and its result is discarded</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** ADL runs only when the backstop vault cannot absorb the position. Counterparties on the opposite side are ranked by (uPnL% times effective leverage) and closed against the liquidated position at its bankruptcy price, which preserves OI symmetry. The loss is absorbed by the closed price, not paid out.
- **Torus evidence:** auto_deleverage (liquidation.rs:255-341) takes every profitable trader in the market on either side (no is_long filter, 263-270) and sorts by absolute uPnL (273). It credits their realized PnL at oracle to available (330-332), which increases protocol liability instead of covering the deficit. It never creates a reverse position. The caller ignores its return value and any shortfall: `let _ = LiquidationEngine::auto_deleverage(...)` (native_executor.rs:5972). socialize_loss has no non-test caller.
- **Suggestion:** Rewrite ADL to select opposite-side positions only, rank by pnl_pct * leverage, and close them against the bankrupt position at the bankruptcy price. That is a paired fill through fill_transition, so the liquidated and ADL'd sides cancel and OI stays balanced. Order the waterfall: market liquidation, then backstop vault, then insurance fund, then ADL. Decide whether socialize_loss is kept at all (HL has no socialized loss) and propagate the errors.

</details>

<details><summary>No mark price; margin and liquidation use raw oracle, and tiers are discontinuous step functions</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Margining and liquidation use mark price = median(oracle-based price, book-derived prices such as impact or mid with EMA, and CEX perp prices). Margin tables give a maintenance rate per tier with a maintenance deduction, so margin is continuous in notional. Maintenance is half of the tier's initial margin at max leverage.
- **Torus evidence:** No mark_price function in crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs (grep for mark_price\|impact returned nothing). LiquidationEngine and RPC use the oracle price directly (liquidation.rs:155-158, torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:795-802). Margin tiers use the whole position's notional against step thresholds (margin.rs:46-53, 214-226), so crossing $100k notional jumps the maintenance requirement from 1% to 2.5% of the entire position. check_initial_margin checks the order notional, not the resulting position notional (margin.rs:103-111).
- **Suggestion:** Add OracleManager::mark_price(market_id) = median(oracle, book mid EMA, impact price) from order_book book_reader, and use it in margin and liquidation. Change MarginTier to carry a maintenance deduction, so MM = notional * mmr_tier - deduction_tier. Evaluate tiers on post-fill position notional.

</details>

<details><summary>reduce_only not enforced; liquidations and risk-reducing orders cannot rely on it</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Reduce-only orders are clamped or rejected so that they only decrease an existing position. They are also exempt from margin checks, which lets an underwater user still close.
- **Torus evidence:** reduce_only is only stored and serialized in crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:46,106,448,484,535,2278,2354. There are no references in crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs (a grep for reduce_only there returned nothing).
- **Suggestion:** In Phase 2 prepare, load the sender's position. Reject reduce_only orders that are on the same side or would flip, and clamp quantity to the position size. Skip the margin reservation for reduce-only orders. Liquidation market orders need this too.

</details>

<details><summary>No portfolio margin and no spot-collateral unification</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL portfolio margin (pre-alpha/alpha) unifies spot balances and perp positions in one margin account with offsets between them. Spot assets such as HYPE and BTC count as collateral, and an earn-borrowing component is included.
- **Torus evidence:** Perp margin is the single NativeBalance {available, order_margin} (position.rs:147-200, used in margin.rs:121,188). There is no spot book and no multi-asset collateral; TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot only move the single native asset (native_executor.rs:3293-3298).
- **Suggestion:** Defer until a spot book and multi-collateral balances exist. Then generalise equity to sum(collateral_i * price_i * haircut_i) + uPnL in a PortfolioMarginEngine.

</details>

*Confidence notes:* Torus findings come from code I actually read: margin.rs (all of it), liquidation.rs 1-455, position.rs 300-545, and native_executor.rs at 3755-3781, 3970-4040, 4610-4690, 4720-4735, 4778-4818, 5350-5357 and 5811-5990. Wiring claims (run_liquidation_checks and MarginEngine having no production callers, margin_configs never populated) rest on repo-wide greps over crates/*.rs. An indirect caller through a macro or a non-Rust path is unlikely but not ruled out. I did not read app.rs or exec_pipeline.rs in full, but grep found no run_liquidation_checks reference in them. I did not trace exec_place_order 4940-5000 line by line; I assumed it mirrors the batch path, as its comments say. I did not check whether TransferToSpot checks margin, beyond lockbox.rs testing only `available`. Prior-audit claims now confirmed on current main: check_margin_at_match unused, market orders reserve zero margin, reduce_only not enforced, List/Delist/UpdateMarketParams are no-op stubs (native_executor.rs:3332-3336). HL facts I am less sure of: the exact partial-liquidation threshold and cooldown (I recall partial liquidation for positions over $100k, 20% at a time, with a 30s cooldown); the backstop trigger at equity < 2/3 maintenance margin; the exact ADL ranking formula (roughly (mark/entry) * (notional/account value), i.e. PnL% times leverage); the current mark-price formula, which has changed over time (median of oracle+EMA, book mid/impact, and CEX perp mids); maintenance deductions in margin tables; and the status of portfolio margin and HIP-3 margin tables in late 2026. HL also restricts some assets to isolated-only or strict-isolated; I did not list that as a separate gap.

#### margin-liq — fable

Torus has a reasonably complete margin/liquidation library in crates/torus-core (margin.rs, liquidation.rs: tiered leverage, cross/isolated maintenance checks, force-close at oracle, ADL, socialized loss, insurance-fund key), but almost none of it is wired into the production block path. The consensus app's post-batch tail (crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1937-1940) calls drain_core_writer, process_governance, distribute_fees and process_epoch_boundary only; NativeExecutor::run_liquidation_checks has zero callers, so no position is ever liquidated on mainnet paths. Every fill is applied with MarginType::Cross hardcoded, there is no leverage field on orders and no UpdateLeverage/UpdateIsolatedMargin action, ctx.margin_configs is never populated in prod (defaults to a flat 20x reserve), market orders reserve zero margin and check_margin_at_match / check_initial_margin are never called by the executor, and Withdraw only checks `available >= amount` with no maintenance-margin-aware withdrawable computation. Versus Hyperliquid (user-settable leverage per asset with cross/isolated/strict-isolated, notional-based margin tiers, continuous liquidation through the book then liquidator-vault backstop below 2/3 maintenance, ADL last resort, withdrawable = account value minus initial margin of positions and open orders), Torus is missing the entire enforcement layer and the HL liquidation waterfall; what exists is unwired library code with several correctness bugs in the one call site that does exist.

**Already present:**
- Margin tiers by notional with effective_max_leverage lookup (crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:18-53) and used in prod by the limit-order reserve formula reserve_for_qty_cfg (crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4805-4818) - notional / tier max leverage, default 20x when no config
- Limit-order margin reservation on placement with available->order_margin move and insufficient-margin rejection (native_executor.rs:3757-3781 batch path, 4917-4940 single path); telescoping release on fill/cancel so total released == total reserved (native_executor.rs:4978-5012, 4826-4898); modify-order delta reservation (native_executor.rs:5377-5399)
- Cross-margin equity and total maintenance margin computations (margin.rs:179-229) with order_margin deducted from equity; isolated maintenance check (margin.rs:232-249); maintenance = initial-at-tier-max-leverage * maintenance_factor_bps (default 50%)
- LiquidationEngine library: check_liquidations cross+isolated (liquidation.rs:72-190), execute_liquidation force-close at oracle with 2.5% penalty credited to an insurance_fund key in CF_NATIVE_BALANCES (liquidation.rs:193-252, 432-449), auto_deleverage ranked by unrealized PnL (liquidation.rs:255-342), socialize_loss insurance-fund-first then pro-rata (liquidation.rs:345-429) - all unit/integration tested in crates/torus-core/tests/{margin,liquidation}_tests.rs
- Position model carries margin_type and isolated_margin fields with borsh encoding (crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:52-62); realized PnL is credited/debited to available at fill (position.rs:385-390)
- RPC exposes margin_mode, isolated margin and a simplified liquidation_price per position plus total_margin_used = order_margin + sum(isolated_margin) (crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:790-872)
- Governance parameter allowlist validates maintenance_margin_bps (25..=5000) and max_leverage (1..=200) (crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:557-585); ListMarket proposal carries maintenance_margin_bps (native_executor.rs:5744-5752)

| Gap | Status | Impact | Effort | Lockstep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Liquidation engine never runs in the block pipeline | unwired | critical | M | yes |
| run_liquidation_checks liquidates cross positions at the wrong market's oracle price and with the wrong config | buggy | critical | S | yes |
| No per-user leverage or margin-mode selection (updateLeverage / updateIsolatedMargin absent); all fills forced to Cross | absent | high | L | yes |
| Market orders reserve zero margin and no margin check happens at match | unwired | critical | M | yes |
| Withdrawable ignores open positions (no account-value / initial-margin based withdrawable) | absent | critical | M | yes |
| No market liquidation through the order book, no liquidator/backstop vault; force-close at oracle only | partial | high | XL | yes |
| ADL does not cover the deficit: profit is paid to the deleveraged trader and closed at oracle, not bankruptcy price | buggy | high | M | yes |
| Per-market margin configs never populated; governance max_leverage / maintenance_margin_bps are validated but not applied | stub | high | M | yes |
| Insurance fund is a raw key in the balances CF, only ever credited, never spent or exposed | partial | medium | S | yes |
| RPC liquidation price and margin figures are placeholders | partial | medium | S | no |

<details><summary>Liquidation engine never runs in the block pipeline</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HyperCore checks every account against maintenance margin continuously (each block, on every mark-price update) and liquidates underwater positions automatically; liquidation is part of the state transition.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5923 defines run_liquidation_checks; the only prod block tail is crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1937-1940 (drain_core_writer, process_governance, distribute_fees, process_epoch_boundary) - no liquidation call; grep for run_liquidation_checks across crates/ finds only the definition. app.rs contains no 'liquidat' or 'oracle_prices' token at all.
- **Suggestion:** In crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs after process_governance (line ~1938), build oracle_prices from ctx.oracle (aggregate_oracle_prices is also uncalled - wire it first) and a trader set (positions_for_trader needs an index: add a CF or in-memory set of addresses with open positions, maintained in apply_fill_cached_effect/flush), then call NativeExecutor::run_liquidation_checks(&mut ctx, &traders, &oracle_prices). Include the resulting balance/position mutations in the state root. Also fix run_liquidation_checks itself before wiring (see next gap).

</details>

<details><summary>run_liquidation_checks liquidates cross positions at the wrong market's oracle price and with the wrong config</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Each position is marked and closed at its own asset's mark/oracle price; the cross account check uses each asset's own maintenance rate.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5937-5985: loops over (market_id, config); check_liquidations (liquidation.rs:115-147) flags ALL cross positions of the trader regardless of market; then execute_liquidation(&ctx.positions, liq, oracle_price) at 5965 passes the loop market's oracle_price (5952-5957), not liq.market_id's. total_maintenance_margin (margin.rs:202-229) applies a single config's tiers/maintenance factor to every market's position. ADL result at 5972 is discarded with `let _ =` and socialize_loss is never called (grep shows only tests call it).
- **Suggestion:** In run_liquidation_checks, look up oracle price per liq.market_id (not the loop market); dedupe cross liquidations per trader (run the cross check once per trader with per-market configs, i.e. pass the margin_configs map into total_maintenance_margin). Chain deficits: execute_liquidation -> auto_deleverage -> socialize_loss, and propagate ADL errors instead of `let _`.

</details>

<details><summary>No per-user leverage or margin-mode selection (updateLeverage / updateIsolatedMargin absent); all fills forced to Cross</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Users set leverage per asset (updateLeverage action, 1x..asset max; BTC 40x, ETH 25x, others up to 50x) and choose cross, isolated or strict-isolated; updateIsolatedMargin adds/removes collateral on an isolated position. Initial margin = notional / user leverage.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-678 NativeAction enum has no UpdateLeverage/UpdateIsolatedMargin/SetMarginMode variant; PlaceOrderParams (lib.rs:1060-1069) has no leverage or margin_type field. native_executor.rs:4663, 4730, 5048, 5068 pass MarginType::Cross hardcoded to apply_fill; position.rs:453 and 505 create positions with isolated_margin: FixedPoint::ZERO. Isolated code paths in margin.rs/liquidation.rs are therefore dead in prod.
- **Suggestion:** Add NativeAction::UpdateLeverage{market_id, leverage, cross: bool} and UpdateIsolatedMargin{market_id, delta} (plus EIP-712 types in torus-types/src/eip712.rs); persist per-(trader,market) leverage/mode in a new CF; have reserve_for_qty_cfg use min(user leverage, tier max) instead of tier max; pass the stored margin_type into apply_fill and move isolated collateral available->isolated_margin on open / back on close. Add session-key scope for the new actions.

</details>

<details><summary>Market orders reserve zero margin and no margin check happens at match</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Market (IOC at aggressive limit) orders are margin-checked against the account's withdrawable/initial margin before and at match; an order that would leave the account below initial margin is rejected.
- **Torus evidence:** native_executor.rs:4912-4920 and 3757-3762: `order_margin_required = if !is_market { reserve_for_qty(...) } else { FixedPoint::ZERO }`. MarginEngine::check_initial_margin / check_margin_at_match (margin.rs:91-176) have no callers outside crates/torus-core/tests/margin_tests.rs. Fills apply unconditionally (native_executor.rs:5042-5080) and realized loss debits available with no floor (position.rs:385-390), so a zero-balance account can open an unbounded market-order position.
- **Suggestion:** For market orders, reserve against a worst-case price (best opposite level * (1 + slippage cap) or last mark) in the Phase-2 prep (native_executor.rs:3757) and release the difference after fills; additionally gate each taker fill with a cheap post-fill check: available - order_margin + upnl >= initial margin of resulting positions (reuse cross_margin_equity/total_maintenance_margin, margin.rs:179-229) and reject/undo the order when it fails. Prior-audit claim verified still true on current main.

</details>

<details><summary>Withdrawable ignores open positions (no account-value / initial-margin based withdrawable)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** withdrawable = account value - (initial margin of positions + margin of open orders); withdrawals and transfers out of perp are capped at withdrawable so an account cannot withdraw collateral backing a position. Transfers also require the account to stay above initial margin.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:78-98 withdraw_from_native checks only `native_bal.available < amount`; exec_withdraw_from_native / exec_withdraw_to (native_executor.rs:5826-5858) delegate directly. Cross positions lock no collateral at all: filled-portion margin is released (native_executor.rs:4978-4999), so a trader can withdraw their entire available balance while holding an open cross position. RPC total_margin_used (torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:849-872) likewise counts only order_margin + isolated_margin.
- **Suggestion:** Add MarginEngine::withdrawable(positions, trader, configs, oracle_prices) = available - order_margin + sum(upnl) - sum(initial margin at position leverage); call it in exec_withdraw_* and TransferToSpot before Lockbox, rejecting amount > withdrawable. Expose it in the RPC account summary.

</details>

<details><summary>No market liquidation through the order book, no liquidator/backstop vault; force-close at oracle only</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** When account value < maintenance, HL first sends market orders to close the position on the book (partial liquidations allowed, maintenance margin tiers). If after that the account is still below ~2/3 of maintenance, the liquidator vault (HLP backstop) takes over the position and remaining collateral at mark price; the liquidator vault keeps any surplus. ADL only if the backstop cannot absorb.
- **Torus evidence:** liquidation.rs:193-252 execute_liquidation deletes the position and settles PnL at oracle price with a flat 2.5% penalty to the insurance fund (DEFAULT_LIQUIDATION_PENALTY_BPS, liquidation.rs:62); it never touches the order book (no OrderBook import in liquidation.rs) and there is no vault/backstop account. The counterparty exposure simply vanishes, so the open-interest books are left unbalanced (longs != shorts).
- **Suggestion:** Implement a two-stage flow in run_liquidation_checks: (1) submit a reduce-only IOC order on the book via the executor's fill path for the liquidated size at a price band around mark; (2) if remaining size or account value < 2/3 maintenance, transfer the position + remaining collateral to a protocol liquidator account (a vault once vaults exist) at mark price. Keep the insurance fund crediting as the penalty sink. This restores OI conservation that the current delete_position breaks.

</details>

<details><summary>ADL does not cover the deficit: profit is paid to the deleveraged trader and closed at oracle, not bankruptcy price</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** ADL closes profitable opposite-side positions at the bankrupt trader's bankruptcy price (so their profit above that price covers the shortfall), ranked by profit-and-leverage score, only after the backstop fails.
- **Torus evidence:** liquidation.rs:312-331: realized_pnl is computed at oracle_price, credited to the counterparty (`bal.available += realized_pnl`, line 328) AND subtracted from loss_amount (line 331) - nobody absorbs the loss, so the protocol stays short while reporting the loss as covered. Ranking (line 278) is by absolute uPnL, not HL's PnL%/leverage queue. Counterparty side is not checked (line 269-274). Insurance fund is never drawn (socialize_loss uncalled in prod).
- **Suggestion:** Close ADL counterparties at the bankruptcy price (entry +/- isolated_or_cross margin per unit) and route the price difference to the deficit, i.e. credit the counterparty pnl_at_bankruptcy and reduce loss_amount by (pnl_at_oracle - pnl_at_bankruptcy). Filter to opposite side, rank by (pnl% * effective leverage). Call socialize_loss for any residual.

</details>

<details><summary>Per-market margin configs never populated; governance max_leverage / maintenance_margin_bps are validated but not applied</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Each asset has its own max leverage, margin tiers (e.g. BTC: 40x <= $150M? notional; tiers reduce leverage above thresholds) and maintenance = half initial at max leverage; changes are operator-set per asset.
- **Torus evidence:** native_executor.rs:1842 `margin_configs: HashMap::new()` and grep for margin_configs.insert finds only tests (crates/torus-bridge/tests/maker_margin_release_tests.rs:500,503,664). reserve_for_qty_cfg falls back to 20x (native_executor.rs:4815-4816) for every market. governance.rs:557-585 only validates the strings; no code outside governance.rs reads max_leverage/maintenance_margin_bps into a MarketMarginConfig. ListMarket stores maintenance_margin_bps as 'initial_margin' with market_id 0 (native_executor.rs:5744-5752) and the prior audit's note that List/UpdateMarketParams are no-ops is consistent with UpdateMarketParams mapping to None at 5753-5755. MarketMarginConfig.max_leverage field (margin.rs:63) is never read by any check.
- **Suggestion:** Persist MarketMarginConfig (tiers, max_leverage, maintenance_factor_bps) per market in state at genesis/ListMarket and load into ctx.margin_configs when NativeExecContext is built; apply ParameterChange executions for max_leverage/maintenance_margin_bps to that state. Use config.max_leverage as the cap in effective_max_leverage.

</details>

<details><summary>Insurance fund is a raw key in the balances CF, only ever credited, never spent or exposed</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Liquidation surplus and backstop profits accrue to the liquidator vault / HLP (not a separate insurance fund in the classic sense); losses beyond the backstop trigger ADL. HL does not socialize losses across all traders.
- **Torus evidence:** liquidation.rs:59 INSURANCE_FUND_KEY stored under CF_NATIVE_BALANCES (liquidation.rs:432-449); credited at liquidation.rs:214-218; the only debit path socialize_loss (liquidation.rs:345-366) has no prod callers. No RPC endpoint reports it (no 'insurance' in torus-rpc/src/torus.rs). Socialized loss (liquidation.rs:372-427) debits all open-position holders pro-rata to size, which HL does not do.
- **Suggestion:** Give the fund a proper address/account (or lockbox entry) so it appears in supply accounting and the state root is auditable, wire socialize_loss (insurance step) after ADL in run_liquidation_checks, and either remove the pro-rata trader haircut or gate it behind a governance flag. Add an RPC getter.

</details>

<details><summary>RPC liquidation price and margin figures are placeholders</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** clearinghouseState returns per-position liquidationPx computed from maintenance margin, leverage, cross account value, plus marginUsed, withdrawable, accountValue, and maintenance margin requirements.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:804-812 computes liquidation_price = entry -/+ isolated_margin/size, which is ZERO-margin-based for every prod position (isolated_margin always 0 per position.rs:453,505), so it returns entry price for longs/shorts; torus.rs:849-872 total_margin_used ignores cross position initial margin and no withdrawable or maintenance figure is returned.
- **Suggestion:** Once per-user leverage exists, compute liquidation price from maintenance rate: long liq = entry - (equity - maint_notional_rate*notional)/size (cross uses account equity); add withdrawable, maintenance_margin and account_value fields using the MarginEngine helpers.

</details>

*Confidence notes:* Verified by reading current main: no caller of run_liquidation_checks (app.rs tail at 1937-1940), MarginType::Cross hardcoded at four fill sites, market orders reserve ZERO (4917-4920), check_initial_margin/check_margin_at_match called only from crates/torus-core/tests, margin_configs inserted only in tests, lockbox withdraw checks available only. I did not execute any code or tests (read-only sprint). I did not read the full execute_batch Phase-2 path to confirm whether any other balance check gates market-order fills (grep for 'bal.available <' shows only reserve/modify sites, so I believe none). I did not verify whether TransferToSpot has its own margin gating (likely same Lockbox-style check). Hyperliquid facts I am reasonably confident about: user-settable leverage per asset with cross/isolated modes, margin tiers by notional, maintenance = half of initial at max leverage, book liquidation first then liquidator-vault backstop when below ~2/3 maintenance, ADL last resort, withdrawable = account value minus initial margin of positions and open orders. Less sure of: exact backstop threshold fraction (2/3), the exact ADL ranking formula (profit-and-leverage based), whether strict-isolated mode is live, and current per-asset max-leverage numbers (the deep-dive doc says BTC 40x / ETH 25x). HL does not socialize losses across traders - fairly confident but not verified against primary docs in this sprint.

### vaults-accounts

#### vaults-accounts — opus

Torus has one account model: a single EOA (secp256k1 EIP-712) with an ed25519 session-key layer. Sessions are scoped (Trading/TransfersOnly/Full), last at most 24h, and each owner can hold at most 5. Replay protection is a permanent (sender, nonce) set, plus a ±60s millisecond-timestamp window that only the mempool checks. There are no vaults (no HLP, no user vaults), no subaccounts, no named agent wallets, no dead-man switch (scheduleCancel) and no multi-sig accounts: the NativeAction enum (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-680) has none of these variants, and grep finds no vault, subaccount or multisig code in any crate. On the security side, I found two consensus-level bugs. On-chain execution compares a seconds-based block timestamp with a millisecond session expiry, so sessions never expire after admission. ModifyOrder has no ownership check, so any signer can reprice or resize anyone's resting order.

**Already present:**
- Ed25519 session keys as a substitute for HL agent wallets: NativeAction::CreateSession/RevokeSession (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:654-662), executed in exec_create_session/exec_revoke_session (crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5591-5680). Expiry is checked against now_ms at creation (5606-5612), there is a 5-per-owner cap (5615-5626), and revoke is owner-only (5660-5666)
- Session scopes Trading / TransfersOnly / Full. Full excludes CreateSession, RevokeSession, Withdraw, Delegate, Undelegate, PermanentStake and ClaimRewards (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:244-288). Scope is enforced on the consensus path in batch_verify_impl (crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:1149) and in resolve_sender (eip712.rs:820-838)
- Sessions are verified with a batched ed25519 verify_batch fast path (crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:1169-1170). Session-signed actions resolve to the owner address, so they share the owner's nonce space (eip712.rs:838)
- Persistent replay protection: CF_NATIVE_NONCES is keyed sender++nonce (crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:83-98). It is checked on the live commit path with in-block dedup (crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1752-1780), in catchup/sync (crates/torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:379-389) and by the proposer (crates/torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs:218)
- Time-based nonces (ms timestamps) with NONCE_WINDOW_MS=60_000 (crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:27), enforced at mempool admission (crates/torus-mempool/src/lib.rs:467-476, 596-605; native_pool.rs:449-465 prunes stale entries)
- Owner-checked CancelOrder (crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5164-5176) and CancelAllOrders with an optional market filter (native_executor.rs:3247-3249, 5209)
- Spot<->perp transfers (TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot) and Withdraw{to}, which sends to an arbitrary address and is roughly HL's usdSend/withdraw3 (native_executor.rs:3290-3298, 5826-5860)
- A batched order action under one signature and nonce, PlaceOrderBatch (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:584-590), which plays the role of HL's multi-order 'order' action for market makers

| Gap | Status | Impact | Effort | Lockstep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Session-key expiry is never enforced at execution because block timestamps are in seconds and expiries are in milliseconds | buggy | critical | S | yes |
| ModifyOrder has no sender/ownership check, so anyone can modify any order | buggy | critical | S | yes |
| No vaults (no HLP protocol vault, no user/strategy vaults) | absent | high | XL | yes |
| No subaccounts | absent | high | L | yes |
| No dead-man switch (scheduleCancel) | absent | high | M | yes |
| No named agent wallets (approveAgent): sessions are ed25519-only, capped at 24h and limited to 5 | partial | medium | M | yes |
| Nonce model: the consumed-nonce set grows forever, and the time window is checked only in the mempool, not in consensus | partial | medium | M | yes |
| No multi-sig accounts (convertToMultiSigUser / multiSig action) | absent | low | L | yes |

<details><summary>Session-key expiry is never enforced at execution because block timestamps are in seconds and expiries are in milliseconds</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL agent wallets stay valid until the user replaces or deregisters them. Validity is checked against consistent ms time, and a pruned agent's nonce state goes with it. An expired credential is never accepted.
- **Torus evidence:** build_proposal sets the header timestamp in SECONDS (crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:4734-4737 `.as_secs()`). exec_create_session documents this and converts it with `ctx.timestamp.saturating_mul(1000)` (native_executor.rs:5600-5606), and SessionData.expiry is stored in ms. The live exec path passes `torus_block.header.timestamp` (seconds) to batch_verify_native_actions_cached (app.rs:1678-1680), which then checks `timestamp <= session.expiry` (crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:1149). Catchup does the same through resolve_sender(block.header.timestamp, ...) (crates/torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:370-372), and eip712.rs:832 compares `current_timestamp > session.expiry`. A seconds value (~1.7e9) is always below a ms expiry (~1.7e12), so on-chain the 24h limit is never enforced.
- **Suggestion:** Normalize at one place: pass `header.timestamp.saturating_mul(1000)` into batch_verify_native_actions_cached (app.rs:1680), resolve_sender in validator.rs:371 and proposer.rs:210. A safer option is a typed `BlockTimeMs` newtype for the verify APIs. Add a test that creates a session, advances the block timestamp past expiry and asserts the action resolves to None. Ship it as a height-gated fork (activation height) because it changes which actions execute. Also prune expired sessions (see the session-cap gap).

</details>

<details><summary>ModifyOrder has no sender/ownership check, so anyone can modify any order</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL `modify` / `batchModify` only act on orders owned by the signer, or by the master account an approved agent acts for. Other users' oids/cloids are rejected.
- **Torus evidence:** The dispatch drops the sender: `NativeAction::ModifyOrder { order_id, new_price, new_qty } => Self::exec_modify_order(ctx, *order_id, *new_price, *new_qty)` (crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3250-3254). exec_modify_order has no sender parameter. It searches every book and calls book.modify_order, then debits or credits `modified.trader`'s balance (native_executor.rs:5359-5421). OrderBook::modify_order does no owner check either (crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:702-730). CancelOrder, by contrast, does check `order.trader != *sender` (native_executor.rs:5170).
- **Suggestion:** Pass `sender` into exec_modify_order. Before mutating, look up `book.get_order(order_id)` and return Err if `order.trader != *sender`, the same way exec_cancel_order does. Check whether execute_batch Phase 1 routes ModifyOrder through the same function (native_executor.rs:6192 categorizes it as NonGtcOrder). Add a negative test where a different signer tries to modify. Gate it at a fork height.

</details>

<details><summary>No vaults (no HLP protocol vault, no user/strategy vaults)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HLP is a protocol vault that market-makes, backstops liquidations and earns a share of fees/funding, with a 4-day deposit lockup. User vaults: a leader keeps >=5% ownership and earns a 10% profit share, with a 1-day lockup for depositors. Actions include createVault, vaultTransfer (deposit/withdraw with lockup) and vaultModify (allowDeposits, alwaysCloseOnWithdraw). A vault trades as its own address, which the leader controls through vaultAddress on actions. Withdrawals are pro-rata NAV and may force-close positions.
- **Torus evidence:** The NativeAction enum (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-680) has no vault variant. `grep -rniE 'vault' crates --include=*.rs` returns no source files (only session-key matches in eip712.rs/app.rs). The executor dispatch (native_executor.rs:3210-3343) has no vault handlers. The research doc describes HLP and user vaults (research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md:354-370), but nothing in the code implements them.
- **Suggestion:** Add a torus-core `vault` module: VaultState {leader, total_shares, allow_deposits, profit_share_bps, lockup_ms, min_leader_bps} and VaultShare {owner, shares, entry_nav, locked_until}, in new CFs (CF_VAULTS, CF_VAULT_SHARES). A vault is just an Address whose NativeBalance and positions already exist, so trading reuses the existing perp path. Add NativeAction::CreateVault, VaultDeposit, VaultWithdraw and VaultModify, plus an optional `vault: Option<Address>` on order/cancel actions that requires sender == leader. NAV = balance + unrealized PnL from mark prices. Withdraw pays pro-rata NAV, takes the 10% leader profit share above the depositor's high-water mark, and enforces the lockup and the leader's 5% minimum. For HLP, seed a genesis protocol vault and route liquidation backstop and part of the fees to it. That requires the fee/liquidation paths to credit it, so check the prior audit's 'fees never charged' finding first.

</details>

<details><summary>No subaccounts</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** A master account creates subaccounts (createSubAccount with a name, gated by volume). Each subaccount has its own margin, positions and orders but no private key; the master signs for it with `vaultAddress`=subaccount. subAccountTransfer / subAccountSpotTransfer move USDC and spot between master and sub. A master can have up to about 10 subaccounts.
- **Torus evidence:** No SubAccount variant in NativeAction (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-680). grep for subaccount/sub_account finds nothing. Every action executes as the recovered `sender` (native_executor.rs:3210-3215), and no action has an 'act on behalf of' field.
- **Suggestion:** Derive subaccount addresses deterministically (keccak(master\|\|index)[12..]), store them in CF_SUBACCOUNTS (sub -> master, name) plus a master -> Vec<sub> index, and add NativeAction::CreateSubAccount{name} and SubAccountTransfer{sub, is_deposit, amount}. Add an optional `on_behalf_of: Option<Address>` to SignedNativeAction or the order actions, resolved in execute_action: if set, require registry[sub] == sender, then execute with the sub as the effective account. This shares the plumbing with vault leaders acting for vaults. Margin, positions and orders already key on Address, so isolation comes for free.

</details>

<details><summary>No dead-man switch (scheduleCancel)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** `scheduleCancel{time}` sets a timestamp (at least 5s in the future) at which all of the user's open orders are cancelled. It can be re-armed and cleared with time=null, and there is a daily trigger limit. Market makers rely on it for safety when they lose connectivity.
- **Torus evidence:** The NativeAction enum has no ScheduleCancel (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-680). grep for schedule_?cancel/dead.?man finds nothing in crates. CancelAllOrders exists (native_executor.rs:3247-3249, exec_cancel_all at 5209), but the user has to submit it, so it is not a timer.
- **Suggestion:** Add NativeAction::ScheduleCancel{time_ms: Option<u64>} (Trading-scope allowed) that writes CF_SCHEDULED_CANCELS keyed by deadline_ms(8 BE)++addr, so it can be range-scanned, plus a per-user trigger counter. In the begin-block or end-block hook of the native executor, range-scan entries with deadline <= block_ts_ms and call the existing exec_cancel_all_run(ctx, addr, None) for each, then delete the entries. Use ms block time (see the timestamp-unit gap). Require time >= now+5s and cap triggers per day.

</details>

<details><summary>No named agent wallets (approveAgent): sessions are ed25519-only, capped at 24h and limited to 5</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** approveAgent{agentAddress, agentName, nonce} is signed by the master's EIP-712 key. An agent is a normal secp256k1 address, so standard wallet and SDK tooling can sign. The user has one unnamed agent plus up to 3 named ones (more for subaccounts), with no fixed 24h expiry (validUntil is optional). Agents can trade and cancel but cannot withdraw or transfer. Approving a new agent under the same name replaces the old one, and its nonce state is pruned.
- **Torus evidence:** Sessions require an ed25519 key (ActionSignature::Session at crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:332-341), MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS = 24h (eip712.rs:742) and MAX_SESSIONS_PER_ADDRESS = 5 (eip712.rs:745). SessionData has no name (lib.rs:344-349). count_sessions_for_owner counts every stored session, including expired ones (crates/torus-state/src/db.rs:715-730), and the only deletion is the explicit RevokeSession (native_executor.rs:5675). So expired sessions keep using the 5-slot cap until the user revokes them, and a bot must re-create its session at least every 24h.
- **Suggestion:** Add `name: Option<String>` (bounded) to SessionData and let CreateSession replace the existing session with the same name. Skip expired sessions in count_sessions_for_owner (and/or prune them lazily on create), and keep an owner -> sessions index instead of the full-CF scan at db.rs:719-728, which is O(all sessions) per create. Consider a secp256k1 agent variant (ActionSignature::Agent{agent_addr, sig}) recovered through ecrecover and mapped to its owner, for EVM-wallet tooling compatibility. Consider raising or removing the 24h cap for Trading scope.

</details>

<details><summary>Nonce model: the consumed-nonce set grows forever, and the time window is checked only in the mempool, not in consensus</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL keeps the 100 highest nonces per signer. A new nonce must be greater than the smallest of those 100, not already used, and within (T - 2 days, T + 1 day) of block time. So per-signer state is bounded, concurrent bots can use out-of-order nonces, and the window is part of the state machine.
- **Torus evidence:** CF_NATIVE_NONCES stores every (sender, nonce) forever (crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:83-98). The only writes come from the consumed_nonces loop (app.rs:2041), and no pruning or delete of this CF exists anywhere (grep for prune.*nonce only hits evm_pool). The ±60s NONCE_WINDOW_MS (eip712.rs:27) is enforced only at mempool admission (crates/torus-mempool/src/lib.rs:467-476, 596-605). The consensus exec path checks just 'already consumed' and in-block dedup (app.rs:1766-1780), as does validator.rs:379-389. A proposer can therefore include a never-submitted signed action of any age, and state grows by one row per action forever.
- **Suggestion:** Replace the unbounded set with a per-signer bounded structure: CF_NONCE_SET keyed by sender, holding a sorted Vec<u64> of the top 100. On consumption, reject if nonce <= min (when full) or already present, insert it, and evict the minimum. Enforce `block_ts_ms - 2d < nonce < block_ts_ms + 1d` (or Torus's chosen window) inside the consensus exec path, next to app.rs:1766. Migrate by building the top-100 from the existing CF at a fork height, then drop the old CF in batches.

</details>

<details><summary>No multi-sig accounts (convertToMultiSigUser / multiSig action)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** convertToMultiSigUser{authorizedUsers, threshold} turns an account into an on-chain k-of-n multisig. After that, actions are wrapped in a `multiSig` action carrying signatures from the authorized users (payloadMultiSigUser + outerSigner). This is native, not a contract.
- **Torus evidence:** grep for multi_?sig finds nothing in crates. ActionSignature has only Eip712 and Session variants (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:332-341), and resolve_sender recovers exactly one signer (crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:801-841).
- **Suggestion:** Add CF_MULTISIG (account -> {signers: Vec<Address>, threshold}) and NativeAction::ConvertToMultiSig{signers, threshold} (EIP-712 only), plus ActionSignature::MultiSig{account, sigs: Vec<Signature>}. In resolve_sender, ecrecover each signature over the shared signing hash, dedup, check membership and the threshold, and return `account`. Once converted, reject plain Eip712 signatures from the account's own key. Teams can work around this with a HyperEVM Safe until it lands.

</details>

*Confidence notes:* I verified everything from current main source. I did not run builds or tests.  Verified bugs: - The seconds/ms session-expiry mismatch rests on build_proposal's `.as_secs()` (app.rs:4737) together with the comment and conversion in exec_create_session (native_executor.rs:5600-5606). I did not trace whether the RPC/mempool session-admission path checks expiry in ms. If it does, expired sessions are rejected at admission but still execute when a proposer includes them, or when they are already in flight. Either way, the on-chain check is ineffective. - ModifyOrder ownership: I confirmed the single-action dispatch path (native_executor.rs:3250-3254) and the body of exec_modify_order. I did not read execute_batch's Phase 1 to confirm it routes ModifyOrder through the same function, though line 6192 suggests it does.  HL facts I am unsure of: - Agent limits: 1 unnamed + 3 named per account, plus 2 per subaccount. - Nonce window: exactly (T-2d, T+1d). - scheduleCancel: the 5s minimum and the daily trigger cap of 10. - Subaccount count and volume gate: ~10 subaccounts, gated at $100k volume. - Vault lockups: 4 days for HLP and 1 day for user vaults. The research doc says 24h for user vaults. - Leader minimums: 5% minimum and 10% profit share. These match the research doc. - convertToMultiSigUser field names. - Whether HL agents have an optional validUntil.  Not covered in this area: HyperEVM ERC-4626 vaults and CoreWriter.

#### vaults-accounts — fable

Torus has no vault layer at all: no HLP/protocol vault, no user strategy vaults, no leader profit share, no withdrawal lockups, and no subaccounts; a grep of every crate and docs/ for vault/subaccount/multisig/schedule_cancel returns zero files, and all perp state is keyed by a single Address with no notion of a sub-identity. The one account-abstraction feature that exists and is wired end to end is ed25519 session keys (CreateSession/RevokeSession with Trading/TransfersOnly/Full scopes, 24h max expiry, 5 per owner), which is the analogue of HL's approveAgent but with a different key type, no agent naming, no per-agent nonce space, and a Full scope that lets a session key submit governance/validator actions. The nonce model is a 60-second timestamp window plus a persistent, never-pruned (sender,nonce) set in CF_NATIVE_NONCES, which is replay-safe but grows unboundedly and is far stricter than HL's (T-2d, T+1d) window with 100 highest nonces per signer. Dead-man switch (scheduleCancel) and multi-sig users (convertToMultiSigUser) are entirely absent; CancelAllOrders exists and would be the building block for scheduleCancel.

**Already present:**
- Session keys (HL agent-wallet analogue): NativeAction::CreateSession/RevokeSession at crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:662-670, SessionScope {Trading, TransfersOnly, Full} with allows() at crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:244-262, SessionData {owner, expiry, scope, created_at} at crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:344-349, executor at crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5591-5680 (24h max expiry via MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS, 5-per-owner via MAX_SESSIONS_PER_ADDRESS at eip712.rs:742-745, owner-only revoke), resolution on both RPC (crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:307) and consensus exec path (crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1753-1766, crates/torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:368-372); 11 integration tests in crates/torus-bridge/tests/session_key_tests.rs:93-384
- Privileged-action fence: requires_eip712() at crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:748-759 forbids session keys from CreateSession/RevokeSession/Withdraw/Delegate/Undelegate/PermanentStake/ClaimRewards; recover_sender rejects session sigs for those at eip712.rs:764-773
- Nonce replay protection, wired: time-window check (NONCE_WINDOW_MS=60_000, eip712.rs:27, enforced at eip712.rs:860-865 and 887-892 and in mempool at crates/torus-mempool/src/lib.rs:467-471, 596-602); persistent (sender,nonce) set CF_NATIVE_NONCES (crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:85-93), checked and consumed on the live commit path at app.rs:1766-1780 and written at app.rs:2038-2044, and rejected as InvalidBlock on the catch-up validator path at validator.rs:379-389; in-block dedup via seen_in_block at app.rs:1752,1775
- CancelAllOrders (per-market or all) with margin release: crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5209-5284 -- usable as the primitive for a future scheduleCancel
- Native withdraw to bridge lockbox: native_executor.rs:5837-5854 (Lockbox::withdraw_from_native[_to]) -- no lockup, immediate

| Gap | Status | Impact | Effort | Lockstep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No protocol vault (HLP) -- no liquidation backstop pool, no community LP of exchange PnL | absent | critical | XL | yes |
| No user (strategy) vaults -- no leader/follower copy-trading with profit share | absent | high | XL | yes |
| No subaccounts | absent | medium | L | yes |

| No multi-sig accounts (convertToMultiSigUser / multiSig wrapper) | absent | medium | L | yes |
