<details><summary>No protocol vault (HLP) -- no liquidation backstop pool, no community LP of exchange PnL</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HLP is a protocol-owned vault that market-makes, backstops liquidations (positions below maintenance that cannot be closed on-book are handed to HLP), and receives taker fees, funding, and liquidation proceeds; depositors share PnL with a 4-day withdrawal lock; HLP is split into sub-pools with one sub-pool taking each liquidation.
- **Torus evidence:** grep -rli 'vault' crates docs --include=*.rs --include=*.md returns no files. Liquidation lives in crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs (no backstop-pool handoff). Withdraw path native_executor.rs:5837-5854 goes straight to Lockbox with no lock or vault accounting.
- **Suggestion:** Add a VaultAccount state object in torus-types (id, owner=protocol, total_shares, nav, per-depositor shares + unlock_at) stored under a new CF in torus-state/cf.rs and included in the native trie root. Add NativeAction::{VaultDeposit, VaultWithdraw} executed in native_executor.rs; VaultWithdraw checks unlock_at >= deposit_ts + 4d. Wire liquidation.rs so that when on-book liquidation leaves residual position below maintenance, the position is transferred to the vault's margin account (vault is an Address-keyed account so existing position/margin code works). Route liquidation fees and the taker-fee share into the vault balance. This is a state-transition change: lockstep upgrade.

</details>

<details><summary>No user (strategy) vaults -- no leader/follower copy-trading with profit share</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Any user can create a vault; followers deposit USDC and share proportional PnL; leader keeps >=5% ownership and takes 10% of follower profits (none on losses); 24-hour withdrawal lock after deposit; vault trades under the leader's signature.
- **Torus evidence:** No vault types anywhere (see grep above). All perp state is keyed by a plain Address (SessionData.owner: Address at torus-types/src/lib.rs:345; cancel_all keyed by *sender at native_executor.rs:5220). No notion of shares, NAV, or profit share in crates/torus-economics/src (grep 'profit_share\|leader' hits only unrelated consensus comments).
- **Suggestion:** Same VaultAccount primitive as HLP but with owner=leader: NativeAction::CreateVault{name, min_leader_frac}, VaultDeposit, VaultWithdraw (24h lock), CloseVault. Vault trades: extend SessionScope/allows() or add a 'TradeOnBehalfOf(vault_id)' dispatch in native_executor so the leader's EIP-712/session signature can place orders whose margin account is the vault's address. Profit share computed on withdrawal as high-water-mark of follower share price; enforce leader_shares/total_shares >= 5% on leader withdraw.

</details>

<details><summary>No subaccounts</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** A master account can create named subaccounts (createSubAccount) with isolated margin/positions, transfer USDC between them (subAccountTransfer), and trade on them with the master's signature; API wallets approved on the master also work on subaccounts.
- **Torus evidence:** grep for subaccount/sub_account across crates returns nothing. NativeAction enum (torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-680) has no sub-account variants; sender resolution returns a single Address (eip712.rs:870-895) that is used directly as the margin/position key.
- **Suggestion:** Cheapest design: derive a subaccount Address deterministically (keccak(master\|\|index)) and store a CF_SUBACCOUNTS map sub->master. Add NativeAction::{CreateSubAccount{name}, SubAccountTransfer{sub, to_sub: bool, amount}} and an optional `on_behalf_of: Option<Address>` on PlaceOrderParams/Cancel that the executor validates against the map before swapping the effective account. Because subaccounts are real Addresses, position/margin/liquidation code needs no change.

</details>

<details><summary>Agent/API wallets differ from HL: ed25519-only, unnamed, owner-shared nonce space, 24h cap, Full scope too broad</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** approveAgent authorizes a secp256k1 agent wallet (so any EVM signer/SDK works) with an optional name (one unnamed + several named agents), validity up to a long horizon (configurable expiry, default long-lived); each agent keeps its own nonce set; agents can only sign exchange actions (orders, cancels, modify, TWAP, leverage) and never withdrawals, transfers out, or agent approval.
- **Torus evidence:** ActionSignature::Session is ed25519 only (eip712.rs:711-716, 772); MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS=24h (eip712.rs:742) enforced at native_executor.rs:5607-5609; no name field in SessionData (lib.rs:344-349); nonce key is native_nonce_key(&owner, nonce) on both paths (app.rs:1766, validator.rs:379) so two session bots for the same owner collide on identical-ms nonces; SessionScope::Full permits every action not in requires_eip712 (lib.rs:248-251, eip712.rs:748-759) -- i.e. a session key can SubmitProposal/Vote/RegisterValidator/UpdateCommission/RotateValidatorKey/TransferToSpot/TransferToPerp/ListMarket.
- **Suggestion:** (a) Add ActionSignature::AgentEcdsa variant resolved via secp256k1 recover -> CF session lookup by recovered agent address (reuse SessionData with owner), keeping ed25519 as-is. (b) Add optional `name: Option<String>` to CreateSession and index by (owner,name) to allow replace-by-name. (c) Key CF_NATIVE_NONCES by the *signing* key (agent pubkey) rather than owner so each agent has an independent nonce space. (d) Narrow SessionScope::Full to exchange actions only (drop governance/validator/ListMarket variants from allows()). (e) Raise MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS or make it a governance param. All of (a)(c)(d) change sender resolution on the exec path, which is explicitly lockstep per the comment at lib.rs:256-262.

</details>

<details><summary>No dead-man switch (scheduleCancel)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** scheduleCancel{time} registers a time after which all of the user's open orders are cancelled by the protocol if not refreshed; calling without time clears it; HL rate-limits it and (I believe) gates it behind a minimum traded-volume threshold.
- **Torus evidence:** grep -rli 'schedule_cancel\|dead.man' crates docs is empty; NativeAction enum at torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-680 has no ScheduleCancel. Block-level helpers in native_executor.rs:5861-5873 (drain CoreWriter queue) show the pattern for per-block processing but nothing scans a cancel schedule. CancelAllOrders exists (native_executor.rs:5209-5284) but only on explicit submission.
- **Suggestion:** Add NativeAction::ScheduleCancel{time_ms: Option<u64>} and a CF_SCHEDULED_CANCELS keyed (time_be, addr). In the per-block pipeline (next to CoreWriterQueue::drain at native_executor.rs:5873) iterate keys with time <= block_ts and call exec_cancel_all(ctx, &addr, None), then delete the key. Allow SessionScope::Trading to submit it. Add trie inclusion so state root covers the schedule.

</details>

<details><summary>No multi-sig accounts (convertToMultiSigUser / multiSig wrapper)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** A user can convert to a multi-sig user with a set of authorized signers and threshold; subsequent actions are submitted via a multiSig envelope carrying N signatures over the inner action, verified against the stored signer set; conversion back requires the threshold too.
- **Torus evidence:** grep -rli 'multisig\|multi_sig' crates docs empty. ActionSignature has exactly two variants, Eip712 and Session (eip712.rs:764-773); resolve_sender returns a single Address (eip712.rs:870-895).
- **Suggestion:** Add ActionSignature::MultiSig{account: Address, sigs: Vec<Eip712Sig>} and CF_MULTISIG_USERS {account -> (signers, threshold)}. resolve_sender recovers each sig over the same struct hash, dedups, checks >= threshold are in the signer set, and returns `account`. Add NativeAction::ConvertToMultiSigUser{signers, threshold} (None to revert) gated by requires_eip712 or by the existing threshold if already multisig. Batch verify path in eip712.rs needs a slow-path branch for this variant.

</details>

<details><summary>Nonce model: 60s window and unbounded nonce set vs HL's (T-2d,T+1d) window with 100-highest-per-signer</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Nonces are ms timestamps; a nonce is valid if it is within roughly (T - 2 days, T + 1 day) of block time and greater than the smallest of the 100 highest nonces already used by that signer and not among them; each signer (user or agent) keeps its own 100-slot set, so state is bounded per signer and pre-signed orders stay valid for a long time.
- **Torus evidence:** NONCE_WINDOW_MS = 60_000 at eip712.rs:27 enforced at eip712.rs:860-865 (and mempool lib.rs:467-471); every consumed (sender,nonce) is written to CF_NATIVE_NONCES at app.rs:2038-2044 and never deleted -- grep for CF_NATIVE_NONCES outside tests shows only put/get (cf.rs:85-93, app.rs:1766,2041, validator.rs:379); crates/torus-state/src/pruner.rs has no nonce handling (grep 'nonce' empty). Note: window check uses `current_time_ms` while block timestamp is seconds (see conversion comment at native_executor.rs:5600-5606) -- verify the exec path passes ms consistently.
- **Suggestion:** Replace the grow-forever set with a per-signer bounded structure: CF_NATIVE_NONCES value = sorted Vec<u64> of the 100 highest nonces (one key per signer). Accept iff nonce > min(set) \|\| set.len()<100, and nonce not in set; insert and truncate. Widen NONCE_WINDOW to asymmetric past/future bounds (e.g. 2d back, 1d forward) so pre-signed/queued orders survive network hiccups. Alternatively keep the set but add a pruner pass deleting keys older than the window (nonce < block_ms - window) since the window already makes them unreplayable; that is the smaller non-lockstep-safe-ish change but still touches a CF read on the exec path.

</details>

<details><summary>No RPC surface to list an account's session keys / agents</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** info endpoints (e.g. extraAgents, userRole, subAccounts, userVaultEquities, vaultDetails) let a client enumerate agents, subaccounts and vault positions for an address.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs references sessions only for signature validation (torus.rs:307-309) and in tests (torus.rs:1954-2010); no handler enumerates sessions. count_sessions_for_owner exists on the state side (used at native_executor.rs:5615) so an index by owner is available.
- **Suggestion:** Add torus_getSessions(address) in torus-rpc using the owner index behind count_sessions_for_owner; return pubkey, expiry, scope, created_at. Node-local, no state change.

</details>

*Confidence notes:* Could not verify (read-only, no build): whether the exec-path nonce window check is fed ms or seconds (the create_session comment at native_executor.rs:5600 documents a seconds/ms mismatch that was fixed for sessions; I did not trace current_time_ms for the nonce check on app.rs's path). Did not inspect the full RPC method table (my grep pattern returned empty) so the 'no session listing endpoint' gap is based on a grep for 'session\|agent' in torus-rpc/src showing only validation and test usage. HL facts I am unsure of: the exact nonce window bounds (I recall (T-2 days, T+1 day) and 100 highest nonces per signer, but the past bound may have changed); whether scheduleCancel still requires a minimum traded volume (I recall a $1M-volume gate) and its exact rate limit; the number of named agents allowed per user and agent max validity (I recall up to ~180 days default); HLP sub-pool mechanics beyond what research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md section 5.5 states. HL vault facts (4-day HLP lock, 24h user-vault lock, 10% leader profit share, 5% min leader ownership) are taken from research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md:354-370.

### spot-listing

#### spot-listing — opus

Torus has no spot venue or token layer at all: there is one collateral asset (TRS). The NativeBalance model holds only {available, order_margin}, and "TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot" just moves TRS between the EVM account record and the native perp balance through the Lockbox. There is no token registry, no HIP-1 deploy/auction/genesis, no HIP-2 Hyperliquidity, no HIP-3 deployer markets, and no spotSend/sendAsset. Perp listing is partly in place. Genesis seeds metadata into CF_NATIVE_MARKETS, and a governance ListMarket proposal writes a metadata row there. The matching engine ignores that metadata, though: every book is created lazily with tick=1.0/lot=1.0 for any market_id, and per-market margin configs are never populated. The direct ListMarket/DelistMarket/UpdateMarketParams actions are no-op stubs that return success, governance listing always writes market_id 0, and UpdateMarketParams/Delist proposals are text-only. In practice the "market registry" serves only RPC display.

**Already present:**
- Spot<->perp transfer of the single native asset (TRS): NativeAction::TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:602-609) go to Lockbox::deposit_to_native / withdraw_from_native (crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3293-3298, 5811-5841; crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:31-126). These debit/credit the CF_ACCOUNTS EVM balance atomically against NativeBalance.available.
- Withdraw from native balance to an arbitrary EVM address (NativeAction::Withdraw, native_executor.rs:3300-3302, 5844-5858, Lockbox::withdraw_from_native_to lockbox.rs:128). This is the closest thing to an HL send, but it is single-asset and native to EVM only.
- Genesis perp-market seeding into CF_NATIVE_MARKETS with base/quote/lot/tick/initial_margin (crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:424-452). The genesis test set seeds 100 markets (lib.rs:667-681).
- Governance proposal pipeline with a MarketListing ExecutionPayload. It is executed by process_pending_proposals, called from native_executor.rs:6110, which writes the borsh market row to CF_NATIVE_MARKETS (crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:1080-1107).
- RPC reads market metadata from CF_NATIVE_MARKETS (crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:55-63, 916). The EVM precompile getMarkets iterates the same CF (crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:549-565).
- OrderBook enforces lot-size minimum and tick alignment once tick/lot are set (crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:376-400), and tick/lot are persisted in book meta (order_book.rs:2503-2504).
- Oracle price submission per market_id, restricted to active non-jailed validators (native_executor.rs:5691-5713).
- Type-level variants for ListMarket/DelistMarket/UpdateMarketParams in both NativeAction and ProposalAction, with EIP-712 encodings (lib.rs:672-680, 1115-1123, 899-925).

| Gap | Status | Impact | Effort | Lockstep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No spot order book / spot clearinghouse (multi-asset balances) | absent | critical | XL | yes |
| Order books ignore listed tick/lot; every market_id auto-creates a book with tick=1.0, lot=1.0 | buggy | critical | M | yes |
| Per-market margin configs never populated (listing does not create risk params) | unwired | critical | S | yes |
| Direct ListMarket / DelistMarket / UpdateMarketParams actions are no-op stubs that report success | stub | high | M | yes |
| Governance ListMarket always writes market_id 0, overwriting itself; UpdateMarketParams/Delist proposals are text-only | buggy | high | S | yes |
| getMarkets precompile reports the wrong 'active' flag | buggy | medium | S | no |
| HIP-1 native token deployment (Dutch ticker auction, genesis distribution, deploy steps) | absent | high | XL | yes |
| HIP-2 Hyperliquidity (protocol market-making on new spot pairs) | absent | medium | L | yes |
| HIP-3 builder-deployed perps (stake bond, deployer oracle, deployer controls, fee share) | absent | medium | XL | yes |
| spotSend / sendAsset / usdSend between users (multi-asset, cross-dex) | partial | medium | M | yes |

<details><summary>No spot order book / spot clearinghouse (multi-asset balances)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HyperCore runs a separate spot clearinghouse with per-token balances (USDC, HYPE, every HIP-1 token) and a CLOB per spot pair on the same matching engine. Spot fills settle by transferring base/quote tokens, with no margin or positions.
- **Torus evidence:** NativeBalance holds only available/order_margin, a single asset (crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:146-150). No TokenId/AssetId/spot types exist anywhere: grep for TokenId\|token_id\|AssetId\|SpotMarket\|is_spot across torus-types/core/bridge/state returns nothing. Every PlaceOrder goes through the perp margin path (reserve_for_qty, native_executor.rs:4911-4918). MarketListing has only base/quote strings plus perp fields (lib.rs:1165-1172).
- **Suggestion:** Add a token registry CF (token_index -> {name, sz_decimals, wei_decimals, deployer, evm_contract}) and a CF_SPOT_BALANCES keyed (addr, token) -> {total, hold}. Add a MarketKind {Perp, Spot{base_token, quote_token}} on market metadata. In exec_place_order branch on kind: for spot, place a hold of quote (buy) or base (sell) instead of margin, and in settle swap balances with no PositionManager. Reuse the existing OrderBook and matching unchanged. Include the new CFs in the native state root.

</details>

<details><summary>Order books ignore listed tick/lot; every market_id auto-creates a book with tick=1.0, lot=1.0</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Each asset has szDecimals and a price-precision rule (5 significant figures, max decimals = 6 - szDecimals for perps, 8 - szDecimals for spot). Orders on unknown assets are rejected.
- **Torus evidence:** exec_place_order: `.entry(market_id).or_insert_with(\|\| OrderBook::new(market_id, FixedPoint::ONE, FixedPoint::ONE))` (native_executor.rs:4959-4964). The same fallback appears in the parallel path at native_executor.rs:3825-3828. CoreError::MarketNotFound is defined (crates/torus-core/src/error.rs:88-89) but is never constructed. Nothing in bridge/core reads base_asset/lot/tick back from CF_NATIVE_MARKETS. The genesis comment says the CF 'drives ... order/margin validation' (torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:424-426), but no consumer exists.
- **Suggestion:** At executor load (next to load_order_books), parse CF_NATIVE_MARKETS rows (8-byte keys, StoredMarket layout) into a MarketRegistry on NativeExecContext. In exec_place_order and the batch path, reject unknown or delisted market_id with MarketNotFound, and create new books with the registry tick/lot. Also enforce lot-multiple (not just lot-min) in order_book.rs:376.

</details>

<details><summary>Per-market margin configs never populated (listing does not create risk params)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Each perp listing carries maxLeverage and margin tables; the clearinghouse uses them for initial/maintenance margin and liquidation.
- **Torus evidence:** ctx.margin_configs is initialised as HashMap::new() (native_executor.rs:1842), and no prod code inserts into it; the only inserts are in crates/torus-bridge/tests/maker_margin_release_tests.rs:500,503,664. As a result reserve_for_qty_cfg falls back to 20x for every market (native_executor.rs:4805-4817). The liquidation sweep iterates margin_configs (native_executor.rs:5931-5937) and so iterates nothing in prod. The governance listing converter drops max_leverage and maps maintenance_margin_bps into initial_margin (native_executor.rs:5744-5752).
- **Suggestion:** When building the MarketRegistry, also build a MarketMarginConfig per market (max_leverage, maintenance factor, tiers) and insert it into ctx.margin_configs. Carry max_leverage and maintenance_margin_bps through ExecutionPayload::MarketListing, adding the fields to the borsh layout in genesis, governance and the RPC StoredMarket together. Verify liquidation then covers all listed markets.

</details>

<details><summary>Direct ListMarket / DelistMarket / UpdateMarketParams actions are no-op stubs that report success</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Perp listing, delisting and param changes happen through validator governance (and for HIP-3, through the deployer's perpDeploy actions such as setOracle and haltTrading). Delisting halts the book, cancels orders and settles positions at a final price.
- **Torus evidence:** native_executor.rs:3327-3336: `NativeAction::UpdateMarketParams { .. } => NativeActionResult::ok("update_market_params", 0)`, `ListMarket(_) => ok("list_market", 0)`, `DelistMarket { .. } => ok("delist_market", 0)`. The comment AUDIT ECON-PF-07 marks these as intentional stubs. The handlers have no sender check, so any user gets a success receipt.
- **Suggestion:** Return an err ('use governance proposal') until a real implementation exists, so receipts are honest. Then route these actions only through governance execution: implement handlers that mutate the MarketRegistry, update OrderBook tick/lot when no resting orders conflict, and, on delist, set status=Delisted, cancel all resting orders (reuse the CancelAllOrders path), and settle open positions at the oracle price.

</details>

<details><summary>Governance ListMarket always writes market_id 0, overwriting itself; UpdateMarketParams/Delist proposals are text-only</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Every new asset gets the next asset index; the universe is append-only and delisted assets keep their index.
- **Torus evidence:** exec_submit_proposal: `ExecutionPayload::MarketListing { market_id: 0, // auto-assigned` (native_executor.rs:5744-5745), but nothing assigns it. governance.rs:1080-1100 writes key `market_id.to_be_bytes()`, which is 0 for every listing. `ProposalAction::UpdateMarketParams { .. } \| ProposalAction::DelistMarket { .. } => None // text-only for now` (native_executor.rs:5754-5756).
- **Suggestion:** In execute_payload, allocate the id at execution time: keep a NEXT_MARKET_ID counter row (max existing 8-byte key + 1), and reject a listing whose base/quote pair already exists. Add ExecutionPayload::UpdateMarketParams and ::DelistMarket variants (bump the ProposalType discriminants at governance.rs:81-110) that call the registry mutators above.

</details>

<details><summary>getMarkets precompile reports the wrong 'active' flag</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Spot and perp meta queries return each asset's real status (isDelisted, onlyIsolated, and similar).
- **Torus evidence:** precompiles.rs:557-561 reads `value.first()` as is_active, but the row is borsh base_asset String, so byte 0 is the low byte of the string length. Any non-empty, non-256-char symbol reads as active, and a delisted state cannot be represented at all.
- **Suggestion:** Decode the StoredMarket layout (shared with RPC: move StoredMarket into torus-types or torus-core) and add an explicit status field (Active/Halted/Delisted) set by the delist path.

</details>

<details><summary>HIP-1 native token deployment (Dutch ticker auction, genesis distribution, deploy steps)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** spotDeploy is a multi-step flow: registerToken2 (wins the ticker via a 31-hour Dutch auction in HYPE; it starts at 2x the last price, floor 500 HYPE), userGenesis/genesis balances, registerSpot (pairs with a quote token), registerHyperliquidity, then optional setDeployerTradingFeeShare. Tokens can be linked to an ERC20 on HyperEVM (requestEvmContract/finalizeEvmContract) for 1:1 core<->EVM transfers.
- **Torus evidence:** The NativeAction enum (lib.rs:580-680) has no deploy/token variants. CoreWriterAction has only PlaceOrder/CancelOrder/Delegate/PermanentStake (lib.rs:1181-1200). Lockbox moves only the EVM native balance (lockbox.rs:181-186 reads the CF_ACCOUNTS balance), with no ERC20 linkage.
- **Suggestion:** After the spot clearinghouse exists, add NativeAction::SpotDeploy(SpotDeployAction) with sub-steps stored in a CF_SPOT_DEPLOY_STATE keyed by deployer. Keep the auction state (last_price, auction_start_block, gas floor) in CF_FEE_CONFIG. Charge in TRS, linear-decaying over N blocks, and burn or send to treasury. Add an evm_contract field on the token record plus lockbox handling for system-address transfers.

</details>

<details><summary>HIP-2 Hyperliquidity (protocol market-making on new spot pairs)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Deployer seeds a price range (startPx, nOrders, orderSz, nSeededLevels). The protocol keeps a ladder of resting orders each block (strategy refreshed every ~3s, 0.3% spacing), funded from deployer genesis allocation, and needs no external keeper.
- **Torus evidence:** There are no references to hyperliquidity, ladder or protocol-owned orders in the crates. The only spot-related matches are TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot (types lib.rs:247-274, 601-609).
- **Suggestion:** Add a per-spot-market HyperliquidityState {start_px, n_orders, order_sz, filled_levels} owned by a reserved system address. In the end-of-block hook (next to process_pending_proposals at native_executor.rs:6110), deterministically re-place missing ladder orders through the normal OrderBook::place_order with a system sender.

</details>

<details><summary>HIP-3 builder-deployed perps (stake bond, deployer oracle, deployer controls, fee share)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Permissionless perp DEXs: the deployer must keep a large HYPE stake (500k on mainnet), slashable by validators for malicious operation. Each deployer runs its own dex namespace with its own collateral, sets oracle and mark prices via perpDeploy setOracle, sets margin tables, OI caps and funding multipliers, can halt trading, and earns up to 50% of fees. Listing slots are won by auction; growth mode cuts fees by 90%.
- **Torus evidence:** Oracle submission is validator-only (native_executor.rs:5691-5713). The listing path is governance-only (native_executor.rs:5744; governance.rs:1080). MarketListing has no deployer, collateral or oracle-source fields (lib.rs:1165-1172). No fee accrual exists at all (the earlier audit's finding that total_native_fees is never incremented was not re-verified here).
- **Suggestion:** Add a deployer: Option<Address> and oracle_source {Validators \| Deployer(addr)} to the market record. Add NativeAction::PerpDeploy{RegisterAsset, SetOracle, HaltTrading, SetOiCap}, gated on a minimum self-bond in a new staking bucket. Let exec_submit_oracle_prices accept prices from the market's deployer for Deployer-sourced markets, and wire slashing of the bond through governance.

</details>

<details><summary>spotSend / sendAsset / usdSend between users (multi-asset, cross-dex)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** usdSend and spotSend move USDC or any token between L1 users. sendAsset moves any token between spot, perp dexes, subaccounts and users. usdClassTransfer moves USDC between spot and perp of the same user, with no EVM hop.
- **Torus evidence:** Withdraw{amount,to} debits the sender's native balance and credits the recipient's EVM balance (native_executor.rs:3300-3302, 5844-5858; lockbox.rs:128). It is TRS-only, and there is no native-to-native transfer. TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot use the EVM account as the 'spot' side (lockbox.rs:31-126), so 'spot' here means the EVM balance, not an L1 spot ledger.
- **Suggestion:** Add NativeAction::SendAsset {token, amount, destination, source_dex, dest_dex} operating on CF_SPOT_BALANCES and the perp NativeBalance. As an interim step, add a NativeTransfer {to, amount} that moves NativeBalance.available between users, checking order_margin. Add a SessionScope::TransfersOnly mapping (lib.rs:244-274).

</details>

*Confidence notes:* Torus claims were verified by reading the cited lines on current main (2026-10-01). There is one inference I did not fully trace. I did not find a production writer of ctx.margin_configs (grep across crates shows only HashMap::new() at native_executor.rs:1842 and test inserts), but a write via a get_mut/entry pattern in an unexpected crate could have been missed. Lines 5189/5323/5377 read margin_configs and do not insert. I did not verify whether CF_NATIVE_MARKETS is in the consensus state root; the genesis comment says it is not. I did not re-check the prior audit's fee-accrual claim. HL facts I am less sure of: the exact HIP-1 auction parameters (31h, 2x/500 HYPE floor, which the research doc confirms) and the current HIP-1 action names (registerToken2, userGenesis, registerSpot, registerHyperliquidity, setDeployerTradingFeeShare). On the HIP-3 stake, 500k HYPE is my recollection for mainnet and may have changed. The deployer fee share (up to 50%) comes from the research doc. The HIP-2 refresh cadence (~3s) and 0.3% spacing are also my recollection. The sendAsset action semantics across dexes reflect 2025-era docs.

#### spot-listing — fable

Torus has no spot layer at all: the only asset is TRS, `NativeBalance` is a single-collateral {available, order_margin} record, and the actions named `TransferToSpot`/`TransferToPerp` are really the EVM<->native lockbox (so "spot" means the EVM balance, not a token clearinghouse). There is no HIP-1 token standard, no ticker auction, no HIP-2 Hyperliquidity, no HIP-3 builder-deployed perps, and no spotSend/sendAsset. Perp listing exists only as a weak registry: genesis seeds `CF_NATIVE_MARKETS` and governance can write a row there (always market_id 0), but the matching engine never consults that registry — `exec_place_order` auto-creates an `OrderBook` with tick=lot=1.0 for any market_id, so markets are effectively self-listed by the first order and governance rows are decorative. `UpdateMarketParams`/`ListMarket`/`DelistMarket` native actions remain intentional no-op stubs (ECON-PF-07), confirming the 2026-09-29 audit on this area.

**Already present:**
- Perp market registry rows (base/quote/lot/tick/initial_margin, borsh) in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS, seeded at genesis: crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:189-215 and :424-438; read by RPC get_markets: crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:880-930
- Governance proposal pipeline with ListMarket/UpdateMarketParams/DelistMarket variants + EIP-712 hashing: crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1113-1172, crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:228-232,532-553,596-603; executed MarketListing payload writes a registry row: crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:1080-1107
- EVM<->native collateral transfer (the 'usdClassTransfer'-like primitive, single asset TRS): NativeAction::TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot -> Lockbox::deposit_to_native/withdraw_from_native, atomic WriteBatch: crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3293-3298, 5811-5835; crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:1-40; lockbox precompile at 0x0820: crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:36
- Native Withdraw to a different EVM address (debit sender, credit `to`), the closest analog to spotSend for the native coin: crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3300-3302
- Per-book tick/lot persisted in book meta and restored at boot: crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:2054
- Oracle price submission restricted to active, non-jailed validators (not deployer-pushed): crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5691-5705

| Gap | Status | Impact | Effort | Lockstep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No native spot order book / spot clearinghouse / multi-token balances | absent | critical | XL | yes |
| Matching engine ignores the market registry: any market_id self-lists on first order with tick=lot=1.0 | buggy | critical | M | yes |
| ListMarket / DelistMarket / UpdateMarketParams native actions are no-op stubs; governance path always lists market_id 0 and drops delist/param updates | stub | high | M | yes |
| No HIP-1 native token standard or ticker Dutch auction | absent | high | XL | yes |
| No HIP-2 Hyperliquidity (protocol-native block-transition liquidity) | absent | medium | L | yes |
| No HIP-3 builder-deployed perps (deployer stake, deployer oracle, fee share, slashing) | absent | medium | XL | yes |
| No spotSend / sendAsset: native-balance transfer to another address only exists as Withdraw-to-EVM | partial | medium | S | yes |
| RPC market listing always reports status 'active' and has no spot/token metadata endpoints | partial | low | S | no |

<details><summary>No native spot order book / spot clearinghouse / multi-token balances</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HyperCore keeps a separate spot clearinghouse with per-token balances (USDC + every HIP-1 token), spot pairs on the same CLOB engine, USDC freely movable between spot and perp wallets, and portfolio-margin unification in progress.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:147-150 (NativeBalance = {available, order_margin}, single asset); crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:600-612 (TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot doc says 'Spot -> Perp balance' but they dispatch to the lockbox); crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3293-3298 (TransferToSpot => exec_withdraw_from_native, i.e. native->EVM); crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:1-8; no RPC spot endpoints (grep spotMeta/token in crates/torus-rpc/src returned nothing)
- **Suggestion:** Introduce a token id (u32) and a per-(address, token) balance CF (e.g. CF_SPOT_BALANCES keyed addr\|\|token_id) in torus-state; add a SpotBalance type in torus-core/position.rs; give OrderBook/market meta a `kind: Perp\|Spot{base_token, quote_token}` so spot fills settle by moving token balances instead of opening positions (new settle path beside the position/margin settle in native_executor apply pass ~4085-4100). Rename TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot to EvmDeposit/EvmWithdraw (or keep names but add a real UsdClassTransfer between spot-quote balance and perp collateral).

</details>

<details><summary>Matching engine ignores the market registry: any market_id self-lists on first order with tick=lot=1.0</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Orders on an unlisted asset index are rejected; tick/lot (szDecimals, price precision) and margin params come from the listed asset's metadata and are enforced on every order.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4959-4964 (`order_books.entry(market_id).or_insert_with(\|\| OrderBook::new(market_id, FixedPoint::ONE, FixedPoint::ONE))` in exec_place_order); registry only read by RPC crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:893-930 and by genesis seeding crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:424-438 ('drives RPC market listings and order/margin validation' comment is not true for the engine); margin tiers are hard-coded, not per-market: crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:16-40
- **Suggestion:** At NativeExecutor boot, load CF_NATIVE_MARKETS into an in-memory `markets: HashMap<MarketId, MarketMeta>`; in exec_place_order (and batch pre-validation ~4911) reject with a MarketNotFound error when absent, and create the book with the registry's tick/lot. Have governance MarketListing execution also insert into the live map (requires the economics executor to signal the native executor, or have the native executor re-read the CF after governance execution each block). Note genesis comment says CF_NATIVE_MARKETS is OFF the consensus state root (lib.rs:193) — if the engine starts reading it, it must be moved onto the root or validators can diverge.

</details>

<details><summary>ListMarket / DelistMarket / UpdateMarketParams native actions are no-op stubs; governance path always lists market_id 0 and drops delist/param updates</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Perp listing/delisting and parameter updates (leverage caps, margin tables, isolated-only, oracle config) are validator-governed on HyperCore and take effect in the state machine; HIP-3 deployers call perpDeploy/updateMarketParams for their own DEX.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3328-3336 (AUDIT ECON-PF-07 'Intentional stubs', all three return ok with 0 gas); :5744-5756 (ProposalAction::ListMarket -> ExecutionPayload::MarketListing { market_id: 0 // auto-assigned }, UpdateMarketParams\|DelistMarket => None 'text-only for now'); crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:1080-1107 writes row at key 0, overwriting any genesis market 0; MarketListing.max_leverage is dropped and maintenance_margin_bps is stored as initial_margin (5745-5752)
- **Suggestion:** Add a durable `__next_market_id__` counter row in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS (same pattern as NEXT_GLOBAL_ORDER_ID_KEY at native_executor.rs:2549-2560); in exec_submit_proposal allocate from it instead of 0. Extend the stored market row with max_leverage, maintenance_margin_bps, max_funding_rate_bps and a status byte; implement ExecutionPayload::UpdateMarketParams and ::DelistMarket (delist = cancel all resting orders, set status, block new orders, allow reduce-only until positions are flat). Either remove the direct NativeAction::{List,Delist,UpdateMarketParams} variants or gate them behind a governance/admin check instead of silently succeeding.

</details>

<details><summary>No HIP-1 native token standard or ticker Dutch auction</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HIP-1 tokens are protocol-level (name<=6, weiDecimals, szDecimals, maxSupply, genesis allocations, anchor-token distribution), with a 31-hour Dutch auction in HYPE for the ticker (start 2x last price or 500 HYPE floor), a multi-step deploy flow (registerToken2 -> userGenesis -> genesis -> registerSpot -> registerHyperliquidity), an auto-provisioned USDC pair, and a lockbox/system-address mapping to an ERC20 on HyperEVM.
- **Torus evidence:** No token/asset types anywhere in crates/torus-types/src (grep token_id/TokenId/asset_id empty); NativeAction enum has no deploy/genesis variants: crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:579-680; lockbox is TRS-only: crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:26-40; HL section research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md:401-409
- **Suggestion:** Depends on the spot-balance gap. Add a TokenRegistry CF (token_id -> {name, wei_decimals, sz_decimals, max_supply, deployer, deploy_state}) and NativeAction::SpotDeploy{RegisterToken, UserGenesis, Genesis, RegisterSpot} executed in native_executor with deployer-only checks. Dutch auction: a single state row {last_winning_price, window_end}; price(t) linear decay from max(2*last, floor) to floor over 31h using block timestamp; winner pays in TRS (burned or to treasury). Defer anchor-token distribution and EVM ERC20 linking to a later phase.

</details>

<details><summary>No HIP-2 Hyperliquidity (protocol-native block-transition liquidity)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Deployer-locked liquidity placed as a 0.3% geometric grid of orders, refreshed every block by the state transition itself (no operator, no contract); fills on one side automatically place the opposite side.
- **Torus evidence:** No per-block order-placement hook in the executor beyond user actions; block-level steps are oracle/governance/funding-adjacent only (NativeAction categories crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6185-6200); no 'hyperliquidity' symbol in repo; HL: research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md:411-418
- **Suggestion:** After spot books exist, add a deterministic end-of-block pass in the native executor (next to save_order_books_deferred, ~2838) that, for each market with a registered Hyperliquidity config {start_px, n_orders, n_seeded_levels, locked_base, locked_quote}, cancels the protocol's prior grid orders and re-places them from a protocol-owned pseudo-address whose balances cannot be withdrawn. Must be deterministic across validators, so it must run inside the state transition, not in a sidecar.

</details>

<details><summary>No HIP-3 builder-deployed perps (deployer stake, deployer oracle, fee share, slashing)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Anyone staking 500k HYPE can deploy a perp DEX; the deployer pushes oracle prices for its markets (setOracle), sets margin tables/leverage, collects up to 50% of fees, and validators can slash the deployer bond up to 100%.
- **Torus evidence:** Oracle submission is validator-only: crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5691-5705; ListMarket has no deployer/stake fields: crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1165-1172; staking has PermanentStake/Delegate only, no deployer-bond primitive: crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:~617-633; HL: research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md:420-427
- **Suggestion:** Phase after market registry fix: add `deployer: Option<Address>` and `oracle_source: Validators \| Deployer` to the market row; add NativeAction::PerpDeploy { bond via a new locked-stake record, markets: Vec<MarketListing> } that requires a configurable bond in TRS; allow SubmitOraclePrices from the deployer only for its own market_ids (branch in exec_submit_oracle_prices on market oracle_source); route a fee share to the deployer once the fee engine exists (prior audit: fees never charged). Slashing of deployer bond via a governance ProposalAction.

</details>

<details><summary>No spotSend / sendAsset: native-balance transfer to another address only exists as Withdraw-to-EVM</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** spotSend moves any token between Core addresses (and to the EVM system address for bridging); sendAsset (2025) is the generalized transfer across spot/perp/sub-account/vault/HIP-3 DEX destinations in one action.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3299-3302 (Withdraw { amount, to } debits native, credits EVM balance of `to`); no native->native transfer action in NativeAction enum crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:579-680; CoreWriter only exposes PlaceOrder/CancelOrder/Delegate/PermanentStake: crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1181-1200
- **Suggestion:** Add NativeAction::NativeTransfer { to, amount } (later `token_id`) executed with the same WriteBatch pattern as Lockbox::deposit_to_native in crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs, plus an EIP-712 type hash in eip712.rs and an ActionCategory::Lockbox mapping at native_executor.rs:6193. Expose it through CoreWriter and the RPC action submit path.

</details>

<details><summary>RPC market listing always reports status 'active' and has no spot/token metadata endpoints</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** info `meta`/`spotMeta`/`spotMetaAndAssetCtxs`/`perpDexs` expose universe, szDecimals, token metadata, deployer, and delisted/isolated-only flags.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:920-926 (`status: "active".to_string()` hard-coded); no token/spot RPC methods (grep in crates/torus-rpc/src empty)
- **Suggestion:** Once the market row carries a status byte and leverage fields, surface them in RpcMarketInfo; add torus_getTokens / torus_getSpotMarkets when the token registry lands.

</details>

*Confidence notes:* Verified by reading: ECON-PF-07 stubs (native_executor.rs:3328-3336), governance ListMarket market_id 0 (5744-5756), on-demand OrderBook creation with tick=lot=1 (4959-4964), single-asset NativeBalance (position.rs:147-150), TransferToSpot/Perp == lockbox (3293-3298, 5811-5835), validator-only oracle (5691-5705). Not verified: whether any other code path reads CF_NATIVE_MARKETS for order validation (grep in native_executor shows only the order-id counter / book-mode marker / save paths at 2541-2884, so I believe none, but the batch pre-reserve path around 4911 could use book.tick_size from a previously loaded book meta); whether margin.rs hard-coded tiers are the only leverage source in prod (margin.rs:16-40 read, but callers not traced). HL facts I am less sure of: exact current HIP-3 bond amount (deep-dive says 500k HYPE; HL has discussed lowering it), the exact deploy step names (registerToken2/userGenesis/genesis/registerSpot/registerHyperliquidity from memory of HL docs), sendAsset semantics (introduced 2025, details from memory), and the 31-hour auction starting price rule (deep-dive says 2x last or 500 HYPE floor). Could not run the `idx` tool (not on PATH); used grep/sed instead.

### hyperevm

#### hyperevm — opus

Torus has a working HyperEVM-style interop core. A revm Cancun EVM runs with custom precompiles at 0x0800-0x0820: four readers (book/position/open orders, balances/markets, oracle, staking), two delayed writers (CoreWriter orders, CoreWriterStaking) and an immediate Lockbox. Writer side effects are checkpointed per call frame, so a revert also rolls back native writes. A one-block-delayed queue is drained in the live commit path. Compared with Hyperliquid it is missing several pieces: the dual small/large block architecture (there is one 30M-gas block), token linking between Core spot tokens and ERC20s through 0x20.. system addresses (the Lockbox moves only the single native balance), and most HL read precompiles (mark/spot px, BBO, spot balances, vault equity, account margin summary, L1 block number, token/perp info). CoreWriter covers only place/cancel/cancelAll and staking, with no cloid, reduce-only, transfers, vault or API-wallet actions. There are also real bugs: the order ID CoreWriter returns does not match the ID actually assigned, stop order types are silently downgraded to Limit, Lockbox EVM-balance writes probably get overwritten by revm's account cache, and EVM gas fees are not burned (they go to validators and may be counted twice). JSON-RPC is a minimal subset with no historical state, no debug/trace and none of HL's big-block or system-tx methods.

**Already present:**
- Cross-VM precompile address map 0x0800-0x0803 readers, 0x0810/0x0811 writers, 0x0820 lockbox: crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:30-36, dispatch at :312-323
- OrderBookReader getOrderBook/getPosition(with uPnL at oracle px)/getOpenOrders: precompiles.rs:330-345, read_position :425-450
- BalanceReader getBalances/getMarkets: precompiles.rs:505-563
- OracleReader getPrice (with staleness flag)/getAllPrices: precompiles.rs:573-644
- StakingReader getStakingInfo/getValidators: precompiles.rs:671-760
- CoreWriter placeOrder/cancelOrder/cancelAll queued for block+1: precompiles.rs:779-863, CoreWriterQueue::enqueue :999-1015
- CoreWriterStaking delegate/undelegate/claimRewards/lockPermanent: precompiles.rs:869-947
- CoreWriter queue drained and executed in the live commit path with a delay guard: crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1937 -> crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5870-5900, conversion :6266-6304
- Writer-precompile side effects journaled per call frame and per tx (a revert also reverts native writes): crates/torus-evm/src/executor.rs:21-70, 268-327; precompile_provider.rs:22-35
- eth_call/estimateGas deny writer precompiles (read-only mode): precompiles.rs:270-306
- Lockbox depositToNative/withdrawFromNative (atomic, immediate) and native withdraw_to action: crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:31-128, native_executor.rs:5850-5857
- EIP-1559 base fee computed from parent header: crates/torus-evm/src/eip1559.rs:15, crates/torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs:71-75
- Precompile addresses pre-warmed (EIP-2929): precompile_provider.rs:142-145
- Core eth_* RPC set (chainId, blockNumber, getBalance/Code/StorageAt/TransactionCount, gasPrice, maxPriorityFeePerGas, sendRawTransaction, getTransactionByHash/Receipt, getBlockByNumber/Hash, call, estimateGas, getLogs, feeHistory) plus eth_subscribe newHeads/logs/newPendingTransactions: crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:31-77, 1081-1148; net_*/web3_*: net.rs, web3.rs
- Native torus_* RPC namespace (getOrderBook, getPosition, getMarkPrice, getOpenInterest, submitNativeAction, etc.): crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:100-213

<details><summary>The order ID CoreWriter.placeOrder returns does not match the ID the order actually gets</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL CoreWriter is fire-and-forget: sendRawAction returns nothing. Contracts track orders by cloid and cancel by cloid or oid, where the oid is read back through precompiles/events.
- **Torus evidence:** precompiles.rs:836-838 returns `((current_block + 1) << 64) \| seq` as the order_id. The real ID comes from the global book counter `ctx.next_global_order_id` (native_executor.rs:4103-4104, 4967 `book.set_next_order_id(ctx.next_global_order_id)`). A contract that later calls cancelOrder(bytes32) with the returned ID (precompiles.rs:839-848) will cancel nothing, or the wrong order if the IDs ever collide.
- **Suggestion:** Stop returning a synthetic oid. Either return 0 or a bytes32 cloid, and add cloid to QueuedActionKind::PlaceOrder (it is hard-coded `client_order_id: None` at native_executor.rs:6282) plus a cancelByCloid selector. Alternatively, reserve the oid at enqueue time from a deterministic per-block CoreWriter oid space that the executor honors.

</details>

<details><summary>CoreWriter accepts StopMarket/StopLimit order types but executes them as plain Limit orders</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** The HL CoreWriter limit-order action encodes tif (Alo/Gtc/Ioc). Trigger orders go through the order action with an explicit trigger price and tpsl type.
- **Torus evidence:** precompiles.rs:802-807 accepts order_type 0..=3 (2=StopMarket, 3=StopLimit), but decode_order_type (native_executor.rs:6306-6311) maps `_ => OrderType::Limit`. No trigger price is carried in the ABI (precompiles.rs:787-793), so a stop becomes a resting or immediately crossing limit order. reduce_only is hard-coded false (native_executor.rs:6281).
- **Suggestion:** Reject order_type > 1 in core_writer until trigger orders exist, or extend the selector with triggerPx, reduceOnly and cloid (versioned encoding like HL's `sendRawAction(bytes)` with a version byte + action id) and map them into PlaceOrderParams.

</details>

<details><summary>Lockbox EVM-balance writes probably get overwritten by revm's account cache (fund mint/burn)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL EVM<->Core transfers move tokens through system addresses: an ERC20/native transfer to 0x2222../0x20.. is picked up after the EVM block and credited on Core, so EVM accounting stays inside the EVM state machine.
- **Torus evidence:** The Lockbox writes CF_ACCOUNTS directly through the native journal (lockbox.rs:31-75; journal commit_tx at executor.rs:321-324). The EVM uses `State::builder().with_database_ref(state_db).with_bundle_update()` (executor.rs:250-253), and the caller's account (already loaded and gas-debited by revm) ends up in the bundle taken at executor.rs:367-371, which is applied after the journal writes. The EVM debit (deposit) or credit (withdraw) therefore looks likely to be overwritten. No EVM-level test calls depositToNative: it is used only in torus-core/tests/precompile_tests.rs:706,790, which call the precompile function directly.
- **Suggestion:** Make the EVM side of the transfer go through revm. Either (a) follow HL: treat a value transfer to a system address as the deposit, then credit native in a post-EVM system step from receipts/logs, or (b) have the precompile adjust the balance through the revm journal (context.journal().transfer / balance_incr) instead of CF_ACCOUNTS. Add an integration test that runs depositToNative inside an EVM tx and checks the EVM and native balances add up.

</details>

<details><summary>No dual-block architecture (small fast blocks + large slow blocks)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HyperEVM produces small blocks (~1s, 2M gas) and large blocks (~1 min, 30M gas) as interleaved chains with separate mempools. Users opt into big blocks through the evmUserModify {usingBigBlocks} action, and RPC exposes eth_usingBigBlocks and eth_bigBlockGasPrice.
- **Torus evidence:** There is a single DEFAULT_BLOCK_GAS_LIMIT = 30_000_000 (executor.rs:73), carried from the parent header (proposer.rs:77-81). BlockEnvCfg has a single gas_limit (executor.rs:76-83). Grepping for big/small/dual block finds nothing.
- **Suggestion:** Add a block_kind to the header and a per-sender big-block flag in state. In the proposer, include EVM txs from a small mempool every block and from a big mempool every N blocks with a higher gas_limit. Keep separate EIP-1559 base-fee tracks for each. Add a usingBigBlocks native action and RPC methods.

</details>

<details><summary>No Core spot token <-> ERC20 linking or system addresses (0x20.. / 0x2222..)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Each HIP-1 spot token can be linked to an ERC20. Transfers to 0x2000...{token_index} move the token to Core, and Core spotSend to that system address moves it to the EVM. HYPE uses 0x2222..2222. Linking is done with a deployer requestEvmContract/finalizeEvmContract flow, and there are no wrapped IOUs.
- **Torus evidence:** The Lockbox handles only the native NativeBalance.available against the EVM native balance (lockbox.rs:1-8, 31-75; the precompile takes only an amount at precompiles.rs:953-990). No token index, system-address or ERC20 linking code exists anywhere in crates/ (grep for system_address/0x2000/token_index finds nothing). There is no spot token registry to link to.
- **Suggestion:** This depends on spot tokens existing first. Then add a token registry CF (token_index -> {evm_contract, decimals, extra_wei_decimals}), a link action pair (request/finalize, nonce- or storage-slot-verified as HL does), and system address 0x20<index> handling: after EVM execution, scan Transfer logs to system addresses and credit Core spot balances, and let Core spotSend to the system address mint/transfer the ERC20 from the system contract balance.

</details>

<details><summary>Read precompiles cover a fraction of HL's L1Read surface</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** L1Read precompiles (0x...0800 onward) expose position, spotBalance, userVaultEquity, withdrawable, delegations, delegatorSummary, markPx, oraclePx, spotPx, l1BlockNumber, perpAssetInfo, spotInfo, tokenInfo, accountMarginSummary, coreUserExists and bbo, each at its own address with gas that scales with input.
- **Torus evidence:** The readers are getOrderBook/getPosition/getOpenOrders (precompiles.rs:333-345), getBalances/getMarkets (:508-515), getPrice/getAllPrices oracle only (:580-588) and getStakingInfo/getValidators (:674-680). There is no mark-price or BBO reader, even though torus_getMarkPrice exists in RPC (torus.rs:210). There is no account margin summary, withdrawable, vault equity, L1 block number or market/asset info (max leverage, sz decimals). read_balances returns `available` twice and labels slot 3 'total_margin_used' but fills it with order_margin (precompiles.rs:539-544). getMarkets returns only the id and an active byte (:549-563).
- **Suggestion:** Add selectors (or HL-style per-address readers) for markPx (reuse the mark-price code behind torus_getMarkPrice), bbo(market) (top-of-book from book rows), accountMarginSummary(user) (equity, margin used, notional, withdrawable from the margin engine), perpAssetInfo(market) (leverage tiers, tick and lot size from market config), and l1BlockNumber. Fix read_balances so it returns the real margin used and withdrawable values. Bound getOrderBook to top-N with metered gas, as the comment at precompiles.rs:369-372 already notes.

</details>

<details><summary>CoreWriter action set is narrow (no transfers, vaults, API wallets, cloid cancel, builder fee)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** CoreWriter (0x3333..3333, `sendRawAction(bytes)` with a version byte and a 3-byte action id) supports limit order (with reduceOnly, cloid), vault transfer, token delegate, staking deposit/withdraw, spotSend, usdClassTransfer, finalizeEvmContract, addApiWallet, cancelByOid, cancelByCloid, approveBuilderFee, sendAsset and borrow/lend. It burns ~25k gas and emits a RawAction log.
- **Torus evidence:** QueuedActionKind has only PlaceOrder/CancelOrder/CancelAll/Delegate/Undelegate/ClaimRewards/LockPermanent (precompiles.rs:1100-1126). The core_writer selectors are at precompiles.rs:787-863. No log is emitted by the precompile (precompile_provider.rs:126-137 returns only output). Results of drained actions are discarded: `let _ = NativeExecutor::drain_core_writer(&mut ctx);` (app.rs:1937).
- **Suggestion:** Add QueuedActionKind variants that map onto existing NativeActions (transfer/withdraw_to, cancel by cloid once it exists, add agent wallet if present). Adopt a single versioned `sendRawAction(bytes)` entrypoint so new actions don't need new selectors. Emit an EVM log per queued action, and persist the drained-action results (success/err) so contracts and indexers can tell a CoreWriter action failed.

</details>

<details><summary>EVM gas fees go to validators, possibly counted twice, instead of being burned</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** On HyperEVM both the EIP-1559 base fee and the priority fee are burned (research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md:234). HYPE is the gas token.
- **Torus evidence:** The block beneficiary is set to the proposer (proposer.rs:88-93, validator.rs:405-411, executor.rs:534), so revm's mainnet handler credits the priority fee to the proposer. compute_fee_revenue then sums gas_used * effective_gas_price, which includes base fee and priority fee (proposer.rs:389-394), and distribute_fees passes that total to RewardDistributor::distribute_block_fees (native_executor.rs:5991-6013, called at app.rs:1939). The base fee revm burned and the priority fee already paid to the proposer are distributed again as staking rewards.
- **Suggestion:** Decide on a policy. For HL parity, set beneficiary to Address::ZERO (or a burn address) and stop passing EVM fee revenue to distribute_fees. If fees should fund validators, keep only one path: either the revm beneficiary credit or the RewardDistributor, never both. Add a supply-invariant test (sum of EVM and native balances before and after a block with EVM txs).

</details>

<details><summary>JSON-RPC: no historical state and many standard or HL-specific methods missing</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** The HyperEVM RPC (rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm) serves standard eth_* methods, including eth_getBlockReceipts, eth_syncing and block-tagged state queries (archive nodes for history). It also adds eth_bigBlockGasPrice, eth_usingBigBlocks and eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber/Hash, which expose the system txs that mirror Core->EVM transfers.
- **Torus evidence:** The EthApi trait lists 19 methods (eth.rs:31-75). There is no eth_getBlockReceipts, eth_getTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex, eth_getBlockTransactionCountBy*, eth_syncing, eth_accounts, eth_newFilter/getFilterChanges, eth_getProof, eth_createAccessList, debug_trace* or txpool_*. eth_call rejects any block other than latest (eth.rs:818-825, HistoricalStateUnavailable). There are no system-tx or big-block methods.
- **Suggestion:** Add eth_getBlockReceipts and the by-index/count methods first (they read from the existing receipt/body stores), then eth_syncing, filter APIs and eth_createAccessList. Add debug_traceTransaction by re-executing with a revm tracer inspector. Expose CoreWriter/Lockbox side effects as system txs once token linking exists. Historical eth_call needs state snapshots or the reverts retained in BundleRetention::Reverts.

</details>

<details><summary>CoreWriter delay is exactly one block, not HL's time-based delay</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL delays CoreWriter order and vault-transfer actions on-chain by a few seconds to stop latency arbitrage, which lets EVM contracts beat direct L1 users. Actions run after the EVM block, and the EVM reads Core state one Core block old.
- **Torus evidence:** enqueue targets `block_queued + 1` (precompiles.rs:1000). The drain asserts block_queued < block_height (native_executor.rs:5879-5893). The delay is one consensus block, whose duration is set by HotStuff block time, and it is not configurable.
- **Suggestion:** Make the delay a governance parameter (in blocks, or in ms translated using the header timestamp), and apply it to order actions only (staking can stay at +1), as HL does.

</details>

*Confidence notes:* Verified by reading code: the precompile map and selectors, CoreWriter enqueue/drain wiring (app.rs:1937), the order-ID mismatch (the synthetic block<<64\|seq ID vs the global counter), the decode_order_type downgrade, frame-level journal revert handling, the single 30M gas limit, the RPC method list and the latest-only eth_call. PLAUSIBLE, not proven by running anything: (1) Lockbox EVM-balance overwrite. This rests on reading revm State/bundle semantics with the direct CF_ACCOUNTS journal commit, and on the absence of an EVM-level lockbox test. I did not trace how BlockCommitter applies the bundle against the already-committed journal writes, or confirm whether revm's cached caller account is re-read. (2) Double counting of EVM fees. This assumes revm's mainnet handler credits the priority fee to the beneficiary, and I did not read RewardDistributor::distribute_block_fees to see whether it mints or moves existing funds. EVM wei vs 8-decimal FixedPoint unit consistency in the Lockbox (lockbox.rs:229-247) was not checked. HL facts I am less sure of: exact small/large block parameters (1s/2M gas, 60s/30M gas), the full CoreWriter action list and versioned encoding, the ~25k gas burn, the exact L1Read precompile address assignments (0x0800+ per function), and the names of the eth_getSystemTxsByBlock*/eth_usingBigBlocks/eth_bigBlockGasPrice RPC methods. The prior audit's non-EVM claims (funding, fees, etc.) were out of scope and not re-verified here.

#### hyperevm — fable

Torus has a real, wired Core<->EVM interop layer: four read precompiles (0x0800-0x0803: book/position/open orders, balances/markets, oracle prices, staking), two delayed writer precompiles (0x0810 CoreWriter orders, 0x0811 staking) backed by a per-tx-journaled queue drained one block later in the production exec path, an immediate atomic Lockbox (0x0820), a read-only precompile mode for eth_call/estimateGas, EIP-1559 base fee, CANCUN spec, and a modest eth_*/torus_* JSON-RPC surface with two WS stream kinds. What is missing versus HyperEVM: the dual small/big block architecture, any spot-token/ERC20 linking (there are no spot tokens at all; the lockbox only moves the single native unit, which the EVM treats as 8-decimal), most of HL's read-precompile surface (l1BlockNumber, markPx, bbo, margin summary/withdrawable, vault equity, spot balances, leverage/isolated flags), most CoreWriter actions (cloid, reduce-only, cancel-by-cloid, vault/spot/usd-class transfers, builder fee), a bounded/metered gas for the unbounded getOrderBook read, and a large slice of standard Ethereum RPC (filters, eth_subscribe newHeads/logs, eth_syncing, by-index getters, debug/txpool). Fee economics also differ: HL burns all EVM gas, Torus pays the proposer as coinbase and additionally routes the full gas_used*effective_gas_price into the native fee distributor, which looks like a possible double credit of priority fees (unverified).

**Already present:**
- Read precompiles 0x0800 OrderBookReader (getOrderBook/getPosition/getOpenOrders), 0x0801 BalanceReader (getBalances/getMarkets), 0x0802 OracleReader (getPrice/getAllPrices with staleness flag), 0x0803 StakingReader (getStakingInfo/getValidators) — crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:30-36, 330-347, 505-516, 573-588, 671-679
- CoreWriter 0x0810 (placeOrder/cancelOrder/cancelAll) and CoreWriterStaking 0x0811 (delegate/undelegate/claimRewards/lockPermanent) enqueue into CF_CORE_WRITER_QUEUE keyed by target block = queued+1 — precompiles.rs:779-863, 869-895, 999-1014
- Delayed-execution drain is wired in the production exec path: NativeExecutor::drain_core_writer (crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5870-5900, with a queued<current guard) is called from crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1937 after both native batches and before governance/fee distribution; queued actions mapped to NativeAction at native_executor.rs:6268-6300
- Enqueue goes through the StateBackend (per-tx journaled overlay) so reverted EVM txs do not leave queued actions; read-your-writes sequence numbering — precompiles.rs:997-999, 1066-1085
- Lockbox 0x0820 depositToNative/withdrawFromNative, immediate and atomic via WriteBatch — crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:1-60, precompiles.rs:953-985
- Read-only precompile mode for eth_call/eth_estimateGas denies writer precompiles — precompiles.rs:84-87, 272-278; crates/torus-evm/src/precompile_provider.rs:44-56, 105-106; crates/torus-evm/src/executor.rs:208
- EIP-1559 base fee computed per block from parent (calc_next_block_base_fee) with 1 gwei genesis base fee; mempool tracks base fee — crates/torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs:72-95, 336; app.rs:5646; crates/torus-evm/src/eip1559.rs
- CANCUN spec with mainnet gas params — crates/torus-evm/src/executor.rs:186, 259, 402; per-block EVM gas limit carried in the header (evm_gas_limit, default 30M) — app.rs:4739-4742, crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:304
- EVM fee revenue (gas_used*effective_gas_price) summed from receipts and fed into the native RewardDistributor with a burn_bps split — proposer.rs:389-394, app.rs:1588-1589 and 1939, native_executor.rs:5991-5995, crates/torus-economics/src/rewards.rs:26-38
- JSON-RPC: eth_ blockNumber/call/chainId/estimateGas/feeHistory/gasPrice/getBalance/getBlockByHash/getBlockByNumber/getCode/getLogs/getStorageAt/getTransactionByHash/getTransactionCount/getTransactionReceipt/maxPriorityFeePerGas/sendRawTransaction, net_ listening/peerCount/version, web3_ clientVersion/sha3, plus torus_ trading/staking/governance methods incl. getOrderBook and getMarkPrice — crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:64-66, crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:100, 210
- WebSocket torus_subscribe with newTrades(marketId) and userFills(user) stream kinds — crates/torus-rpc/src/streams.rs:52-66
- Native action ordering around the EVM: cancels and non-GTC orders run pre-EVM-visible, rest post — native_executor.rs:6216-6235; block order is EVM validate/commit (app.rs:1509-1585) then native batches (app.rs:1902-1903) then CoreWriter drain (app.rs:1937)

| Gap | Status | Impact | Effort | Lockstep |

| Dual block architecture (small fast + big slow blocks) absent | absent | medium | L | yes |

| EVM gas economics differ: fees not burned, proposer credited as coinbase AND full effective price fed to fee distributor (possible double credit) | partial | high | S | yes |

| Standard Ethereum JSON-RPC surface incomplete (filters, eth_subscribe, eth_syncing, by-index getters, debug/txpool, HL big-block RPCs) | partial | medium | M | no |
