<details><summary>Dual block architecture (small fast + big slow blocks) absent</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HyperEVM produces two interleaved block streams on the same chain: small blocks every ~1s with a 2M gas limit for normal txs, and big blocks every ~1min with 30M gas for deployments/heavy compute; users opt in per-address via eth_usingBigBlocks and query eth_bigBlockGasPrice.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:4739-4747 (single evm_gas_limit from parent header drives select_block_payload), crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:304 (evm_gas_limit: 30_000_000 single value), crates/torus-rpc registered method list has no usingBigBlocks/bigBlockGasPrice (grep of #[method(name=...)] across crates/torus-rpc/src/*.rs)
- **Suggestion:** Add a block-class field to the Torus header (or derive from height % N) with a second gas limit and a second EIP-1559 base-fee lane (eip1559.rs already takes parent gas target/used as inputs). In app.rs select_block_payload, pick the lane's gas limit and have mempool.drain_evm filter txs by sender's big-block flag (store flag in a native CF, set via a torus_/eth_usingBigBlocks RPC that submits a signed native action). Keep the native CLOB cadence unchanged; only the EVM gas budget per block alternates.

</details>

<details><summary>Spot token <-> ERC20 linking and per-token lockbox system addresses absent</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Every HIP-1 spot token has a system address 0x2000...{token_index}; sending ERC20 to it (or Core spot send to it) moves balances between the Core spot ledger and the linked ERC20 contract with no wrapped IOU. HYPE itself links to the EVM native balance at 0x222...2. Token linking is a two-step deploy/link flow with a finalizeEvmContract CoreWriter action.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:30-36 and 65 (ALL_PRECOMPILE_ADDRESSES is exactly 7 fixed addresses, none in 0x2000.. range), crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:1-12 and 228-247 (single-asset lockbox moving the native margin unit only; no token index), no spot/token types found under crates/torus-core/src or crates/torus-types/src (grep SpotToken\|TokenId\|token_index returned nothing)
- **Suggestion:** Blocked on a Core spot ledger existing (spot area). Once a token registry CF exists, add is_precompile handling for the 0x2000_0000_..._{index} range in precompiles.rs (precompile_address helper already builds addresses from u16 ids; widen to a token-index scheme), implement transfer-in via EVM ERC20 Transfer events observed in the executor's receipt loop (executor.rs:287-350) crediting the Core spot balance, and transfer-out via a QueuedActionKind::SpotSend drained in drain_core_writer that calls the linked ERC20 through a system tx. Add a torus_ RPC to query linked tokens.

</details>

<details><summary>Read precompile coverage much narrower than HL (no l1BlockNumber, markPx, bbo, margin summary, withdrawable, vault equity, spot balances, leverage/isolation)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL read precompiles at 0x0800..0x080f expose position (szi, entryNtl, isolatedRawUsd, leverage, isIsolated), spotBalance, vaultEquity, withdrawable, delegations, delegatorSummary, markPx, oraclePx, spotPx, l1BlockNumber, perpAssetInfo, spotInfo, tokenInfo, bbo, accountMarginSummary, coreUserExists.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:333-343 (only getOrderBook/getPosition/getOpenOrders), 424-446 (getPosition returns size/entry/upnl/rpnl/margin; no leverage, isolated flag or mark px), 508-512 (getBalances/getMarkets only), 518-545 (getBalances 'available' is just native available and 'total_margin_used' is only order_margin; position margin ignored), 580-584 (oracle agg price only; no mark price even though RPC exposes torus_getMarkPrice at crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:210), full selector list grep shows 18 selectors total with no l1BlockNumber/bbo/markPx
- **Suggestion:** Add selectors (new selectors are additive, but any change to existing outputs is a hard fork): getMarkPrice(bytes32) reusing whatever torus_getMarkPrice reads; getBbo(bytes32) from book_reader::read_book_depth top level; getL1BlockNumber() returning current_block already threaded into oracle_reader; getAccountMarginSummary(address) computing equity/maintenance from CF_NATIVE_POSITIONS + oracle; extend getPosition with leverage/isolated once those fields exist in Position. Gate behind a spec/height flag so already-deployed chains keep old outputs (same pattern as the classic-layout note at precompiles.rs:362-367).

</details>

<details><summary>CoreWriter action set is a small subset of HL's (no cloid, reduce-only, cancel-by-cloid, vault/spot/usd-class transfers, builder fee, api wallet)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL CoreWriter (0x3333...3333, sendRawAction(bytes) with action-id-prefixed ABI payloads, ~25k gas) supports limit order with cloid/tif/reduceOnly, vaultTransfer, tokenDelegate, stakingDeposit/Withdraw, spotSend, usdClassTransfer, finalizeEvmContract, addApiWallet, cancelOrderByOid, cancelOrderByCloid, approveBuilderFee. Actions are delayed a few seconds before Core executes them.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:787-860 (placeOrder(market,side,type,price,qty,tif) with no cloid/reduce_only/trigger; cancelOrder(oid); cancelAll(market)), 1102-1129 (QueuedActionKind has 7 variants only), 837 (returned order id is a synthetic block+1<<64\|seq packed value — consistency with the executor-assigned OrderId not verified), crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6268-6300 (mapping to NativeAction, no reduce_only/cloid passed)
- **Suggestion:** Extend QueuedActionKind::PlaceOrder with cloid, reduce_only and trigger price once the native NativeAction::PlaceOrder carries/enforces them (reduce_only is reportedly stored-but-unenforced in the executor, verify there). Add CancelByCloid. Consider replacing the fixed-selector ABI with an HL-style versioned sendRawAction(bytes) dispatcher so new actions don't require new selectors. Verify that the order id returned at precompiles.rs:837 equals the id the native executor assigns when the queued action runs; if not, return a cloid instead.

</details>

<details><summary>EVM gas economics differ: fees not burned, proposer credited as coinbase AND full effective price fed to fee distributor (possible double credit)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** On HyperEVM EIP-1559 base fee and priority fee are both burned; validators are paid from staking emissions, not gas. HYPE is the 18-decimal gas token.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs:93 and crates/torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:146, 248, 409 (beneficiary = proposer; revm credits priority fees to coinbase, no disable_beneficiary flag found in crates/torus-evm/src), crates/torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs:389-394 (compute_fee_revenue = sum gas_used*effective_gas_price including base fee), crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1588-1589 and 1939 (routed into NativeExecutor::distribute_fees), crates/torus-economics/src/rewards.rs:26-38 (RewardDistributor splits with burn_bps to proposer/treasury/etc.); crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:228-229 ('Both use the same 8-decimal scale' — EVM native balance is interpreted as 8-decimal units, not 18-decimal wei)
- **Suggestion:** Decide the policy explicitly. If matching HL: set beneficiary to a burn/zero address in proposer.rs/validator.rs and drop the EVM component from distribute_fees (or route only base fee to burn). If keeping validator rewards: check whether revm's coinbase credit (priority fee) overlaps with compute_fee_revenue's total; if so subtract priority or set beneficiary to Address::ZERO and let RewardDistributor be the single payer. Document the 8-decimal EVM unit (gas token != 18 decimals) in RPC docs or add a scaling layer, since Foundry/ethers tooling assumes 18 decimals for the native coin.

</details>

<details><summary>getOrderBook precompile has flat 2600 gas for unbounded output (DoS vector) and reverts on classic production book layout</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL read precompiles are fixed-cost and return bounded data (bbo returns top of book only; there is no full-book read precompile).
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:40, 47-50 (GAS_PRECOMPILE_READ 2600 flat for 0x0800-0x0803), 369-372 (doc comment: 'returned level count is unbounded ... That bound must land before mode 1/2 chains expose this selector to untrusted EVM traffic'), 362-367 (classic layout still decodes only legacy OrderBookSnapshot so a production whole-book blob makes the precompile revert), crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:373-422 (no depth cap)
- **Suggestion:** Add a depth argument (getOrderBook(bytes32,uint8 n)) capped at e.g. 20 levels and meter gas as base + per-level cost in TorusPrecompiles::run (precompile_provider.rs:69) instead of the const precompile_gas table; add a getBbo selector that costs GAS_PRECOMPILE_READ. Fix the classic arm to decode the production whole-book blob (or return empty + stale flag) behind a height-gated flag.

</details>

<details><summary>Standard Ethereum JSON-RPC surface incomplete (filters, eth_subscribe, eth_syncing, by-index getters, debug/txpool, HL big-block RPCs)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HyperEVM exposes the standard Ethereum JSON-RPC that Foundry/Hardhat/ethers/viem expect (eth_syncing, eth_getBlockTransactionCountBy*, eth_getTransactionByBlock*AndIndex, eth_newFilter/getFilterChanges/getFilterLogs/uninstallFilter, eth_subscribe newHeads/logs on WS, eth_getProof on some providers), plus eth_usingBigBlocks and eth_bigBlockGasPrice.
- **Torus evidence:** Registered #[method(name=...)] set across crates/torus-rpc/src/{eth,net,web3,torus,streams}.rs: eth has only blockNumber, call, chainId, estimateGas, feeHistory, gasPrice, getBalance, getBlockByHash, getBlockByNumber, getCode, getLogs, getStorageAt, getTransactionByHash, getTransactionCount, getTransactionReceipt, maxPriorityFeePerGas, sendRawTransaction; crates/torus-rpc/src/streams.rs:52-66 only newTrades/userFills (no newHeads/logs/eth_subscribe); no debug_/txpool_ namespace files in crates/torus-rpc/src
- **Suggestion:** In crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs add eth_syncing (from consensus height vs peer height), eth_accounts (empty), eth_getBlockTransactionCountByHash/Number and eth_getTransactionByBlock{Hash,Number}AndIndex (reuse the getBlockBy* block-body path), and a filter manager (newFilter/newBlockFilter/getFilterChanges/uninstallFilter) backed by the same log index getLogs uses. Extend streams.rs StreamKind with NewHeads and Logs(filter) and register eth_subscribe/eth_unsubscribe aliases over the existing torus_subscribe plumbing.

</details>

<details><summary>Block processing order differs from HL (EVM executes before Core; CoreWriter actions run after next block's native batch)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL: HyperCore block executes first, then the EVM block (reading Core state one block old), then EVM->Core transfers, then CoreWriter actions, with CoreWriter actions delayed a few seconds.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1509-1585 (EVM validation/commit happens first), 1812 and 1902-1903 (native pre_evm/post_evm batches after EVM — the split at crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6216-6235 is by action category, not by EVM position), 1937 (drain_core_writer runs after both native batches of block N+1), crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:1000 (target_block = queued+1)
- **Suggestion:** Not necessarily a defect, but document the guarantee contracts get: precompile reads see end-of-previous-block Core state and EVM-originated orders land after all user actions of the next block (worst-case ~2 block delay). If HL parity is wanted, move the EVM section after the native batches in app.rs and run drain_core_writer immediately after the EVM section so CoreWriter orders execute at the tail of the same block (keeping the anti-frontrun property only if the delay is kept). Either choice is a hard fork.

</details>

*Confidence notes:* Could not verify (read-only, no build): (1) whether revm with beneficiary=proposer actually credits priority fees on top of compute_fee_revenue being distributed — grep found no disable_beneficiary/reward handling in crates/torus-evm, so the double-credit is a hypothesis, not a confirmed bug; (2) whether the synthetic order id returned by CoreWriter placeOrder (precompiles.rs:837) matches the OrderId the native executor assigns at drain time; (3) exact body of crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs methods (only method names were enumerated); (4) whether reduce_only is enforced in the native executor (prior audit claim, not re-verified here). HL facts I am unsure of: exact HL read-precompile address list and ABI (0x0800-0x080f, including bbo, accountMarginSummary, coreUserExists which were added in 2025 and may have shifted), CoreWriter gas cost (~25k) and exact delay semantics, eth_usingBigBlocks/eth_bigBlockGasPrice method names, and the statement that priority fees as well as base fees are burned (research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md:84 asserts both are burned; I did not independently confirm). HL small/big block parameters (1s/2M, 1min/30M) are taken from research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md:76-82.

### api-data

#### api-data — opus

Torus exposes its DEX data through one JSON-RPC namespace (torus_*, 24 methods, crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:97-227) plus standard eth_* and an explorer REST service, all over HTTP and WS through jsonrpsee. It does not offer anything like HL's single info/exchange schema. Reads cover the basics: book snapshot, per-market position, balances, markets, trades, open orders, OI, mark price and user trades. Several HL info types are missing or thin: clearinghouseState (all positions with margin summary), metaAndAssetCtxs, frontendOpenOrders with trigger orders, orderStatus, historicalOrders, userFillsByTime, fundingHistory/userFunding, portfolio and candleSnapshot on the node. WebSocket streaming has only two DEX streams, newTrades and userFills (streams.rs:27-32). HL's l2Book, bbo, allMids, candle, orderUpdates, userEvents, userFundings and webData streams are all missing. EIP-712 signing and session (agent) keys are implemented. Rate limiting is per-sender per-block mempool caps plus node admission shedding. The HL-style weight budget per IP, and address-based limits that scale with traded volume, do not exist. Order lifecycle events (placed, canceled, rejected) only feed metrics counters. They are never stored or streamed, so an equivalent of HL's node_order_statuses or book-diff feeds cannot be built.

**Already present:**
- EIP-712 typed-data signing of native L1 actions. Domain is name=Torus, version=1, chainId=TORUS_CHAIN_ID, verifyingContract=0 (crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:163-174, signing hash at :181). A fixture generator and CI gate exist (crates/torus-types/tests/eip712_vectors.rs). SignedNativeAction uses a millisecond-timestamp nonce and supports an ed25519 session-key alternative (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:951-957).
- Agent-wallet equivalent: CreateSession/RevokeSession with SessionScope Trading/TransfersOnly/Full (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:244-252, NativeAction variants around :650-660).
- Action submission over JSON-RPC, usable over HTTP and WS: torus_submitNativeAction, a batched submitNativeActions (max 100) and a bincode-encoded submitNativeActionsBin (crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:142-162; SUBMIT_BATCH_MAX in lib.rs:33). Because these are ordinary JSON-RPC methods on the WS transport, they roughly cover HL's ws 'post'.
- l2Book snapshot: torus_getOrderBook returns all aggregated price levels with orderCount, reading every book layout (torus.rs:741-770).
- torus_getMarkets with pagination (torus.rs:880-936). It is a thin version of HL meta: asset names, lot and tick size only.
- torus_getOpenOrders, filterable by market, covering every book layout (torus.rs:1468-1500; crates/torus-core/src/book_reader.rs:448).
- torus_getPosition for one market with uPnL at the oracle price (torus.rs:772-829), and torus_getBalances (torus.rs:831-876).
- torus_getOpenInterest and torus_getMarkPrice (torus.rs:207-211, 1604-1643).
- Trade history: torus_getTradeHistory, getTradeHistoryRange (block range), getBlockTrades, and getUserTrades capped at 1000 (torus.rs:121-219, 1645).
- WS stream newTrades {marketId?}, serialized once per (block, filter). The all-markets variant is restricted on validators via TORUS_ALL_MARKET_TRADES (streams.rs:36-101; torus.rs:1723-1810).
- WS stream userFills {user} with HL-style dir (Open Long/Close Short/Long > Short), startPosition, closedPnl and oid (streams.rs:104-120, 228; types.rs:385-399).
- eth_subscribe newHeads, logs and newPendingTransactions for HyperEVM-equivalent streaming (crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:1081-1141).
- Explorer REST: OHLCV candles at 1m/5m/15m/1h built by indexing torus_getBlockTrades (crates/torus-explorer/src/api.rs:37; db.rs:397-411; indexer.rs:338-356).
- Non-validator node: --rpc-only mode with an ephemeral identity (crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:162, 448-462).
- Node protection: 1000-subscription cap (torus.rs:1813-1830), 512 max connections and a 10MB response cap (lib.rs:41-79), 64 submit permits with a 250ms queue timeout (lib.rs:24-29), a per-sender eth_sendRawTransaction limiter (eth.rs:625-629; lib.rs:193), and mempool per-sender caps of 64 per block and 512 pending, plus admission shedding (crates/torus-mempool/src/rate_limit.rs:58, 125-180).

| Gap | Status | Impact | Effort | Lockstep |

| No order book / BBO / allMids WebSocket subscriptions | absent | critical | M | no |
| Order lifecycle (orderUpdates / userEvents / orderStatus / historicalOrders) not recorded or exposed | absent | critical | L | no |
| No clearinghouseState equivalent (all positions + margin summary + withdrawable) | partial | high | M | no |
| No metaAndAssetCtxs: market metadata and per-asset context missing | partial | high | M | no |

<details><summary>No order book / BBO / allMids WebSocket subscriptions</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL WS offers l2Book {coin, nSigFigs, mantissa}, sending a snapshot on every block change; bbo, sent on change; and allMids, all mids pushed each block. These are the main market-data feeds used by market makers and frontends.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-rpc/src/streams.rs:27-32: StreamKind has only NewTrades and UserFills. streams.rs:63-65 rejects any other kind ('expected "newTrades" or "userFills"'). torus.rs:1765 subscribes only to notifier.new_trades.
- **Suggestion:** Add StreamKind::L2Book(market, depth), Bbo(market) and AllMids. Publish one post-commit book-delta signal per block from the execution thread, next to the BlockFills FillSink (crates/torus-state/src/trade_rows.rs:83-90), carrying the touched markets. In the notifier, build each touched market's snapshot once per block via book_reader::read_book_depth (already used at torus.rs:752) and share it as Arc<RawValue>, the same way new_trades_payload works. Truncate to N levels and add a block height/time field. The send could be skipped when the book is unchanged.

</details>

<details><summary>Order lifecycle (orderUpdates / userEvents / orderStatus / historicalOrders) not recorded or exposed</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL info provides orderStatus by oid or cloid, and historicalOrders returning up to 2000 recent orders with status (open/filled/canceled/triggered/rejected/marginCanceled) and statusTimestamp. WS provides orderUpdates and userEvents (fills, funding, liquidation, nonUserCancel). The exchange response returns resting:{oid} or filled:{totalSz,avgPx,oid} per order. Non-validator nodes can write node_order_statuses.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4750-4775: per-order OrderStatus (Filled/Resting/Rejected/Cancelled) only increments telemetry counters. crates/torus-state/src/trade_rows.rs:44-79: BlockFills/TradeFill carry fills only, with no place/cancel/reject events. crates/torus-rpc/src/types.rs:431-436: RpcSubmitResult is {hash, error} only, with no oid or fill status. There is no getOrder, orderStatus or historical-orders method in the trait (torus.rs:97-227).
- **Suggestion:** Extend the existing exec-thread sink with a per-block Vec<OrderEvent {oid, cloid, trader, market, status, filled_qty, remaining, reason, ts}>, emitted where record_order_status_funnel is called (native_executor.rs:4248/4574/5102) and on cancel paths. Persist the events node-locally in a CF keyed (trader, height, idx), pruned like CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES. Expose torus_getOrderStatus(oid\|cloid) and torus_getHistoricalOrders(trader, limit), plus WS orderUpdates {user}. Return per-order status in submit results via an action-hash to outcome lookup, so a submit-then-query pattern works. This is node-local and not consensus state.

</details>

<details><summary>No clearinghouseState equivalent (all positions + margin summary + withdrawable)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** clearinghouseState returns assetPositions[] (szi, entryPx, positionValue, unrealizedPnl, returnOnEquity, liquidationPx, leverage {type, value}, marginUsed, maxLeverage, cumFunding), marginSummary and crossMarginSummary (accountValue, totalNtlPos, totalRawUsd, totalMarginUsed), crossMaintenanceMarginUsed and withdrawable, all in one call.
- **Torus evidence:** torus.rs:103-108: getPosition takes a single market. torus.rs:799-809: liquidationPrice is a 'simplified estimate' using only isolated_margin, and is 0 for cross positions. types.rs:276-296: RpcPosition has no leverage, positionValue or cumFunding. RpcBalances has no accountValue, withdrawable or maintenance margin. torus.rs:851-855: total margin is order_margin plus summed isolated_margin, with no cross maintenance requirement.
- **Suggestion:** Add torus_getClearinghouseState(trader). Iterate pm.positions_for_trader (already called at torus.rs:847). Compute equity, maintenance margin and liquidation price with the same torus-core margin functions the liquidation engine uses, rather than the RPC-local estimate. Return the HL-shaped struct and fix getPosition's liquidation price to share that code.

</details>

<details><summary>No metaAndAssetCtxs: market metadata and per-asset context missing</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** meta gives universe[] {name, szDecimals, maxLeverage, onlyIsolated, isDelisted}. metaAndAssetCtxs adds per asset: funding, openInterest, oraclePx, markPx, midPx, impactPxs, premium, prevDayPx and dayNtlVlm.
- **Torus evidence:** types.rs:300-307: RpcMarketInfo is {marketId, baseAsset, quoteAsset, lotSize, tickSize, status}. torus.rs:926: status is hardcoded "active", so delisted or halted markets are never reported. torus.rs:1608-1611: getMarkPrice returns mark_price == index_price == oracle price. OI and mark are separate per-market calls (torus.rs:207-211). No 24h volume or prevDayPx exists anywhere in the RPC.
- **Suggestion:** Extend get_markets to decode StoredMarket's real status and leverage/margin params and return them. Add torus_getMetaAndAssetCtxs to batch oracle price, mark, book mid (from read_book_depth top of book), long/short OI and funding, once funding exists. Maintain node-local rolling 24h volume and prevDayPx from the BlockFills stream so the call does not scan history.

</details>

<details><summary>No fundingHistory / userFunding endpoints or userFundings stream (funding engine absent)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** fundingHistory {coin, startTime} returns hourly funding rates and premiums. userFunding / userNonFundingLedgerUpdates return per-user funding payments. WS has userFundings. Funding is paid hourly.
- **Torus evidence:** grep -i 'funding' over crates/torus-core/src, crates/torus-bridge/src and crates/torus-state/src returns no matches, so there is no funding engine and no data to serve. The trait has no funding method (torus.rs:97-227).
- **Suggestion:** API work is blocked on a consensus-side funding engine. After it lands, record per-market funding (rate, premium, time) and per-user payments as node-local rows written from the exec sink. Expose torus_getFundingHistory(market, startTime, endTime), torus_getUserFunding(user, startTime, endTime) and WS userFundings. Add a cumFunding field to positions.

</details>

<details><summary>Fills lack fee/hash/liquidation fields; no time-range user fills</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL fills include coin, px, sz, side, time, startPosition, dir, closedPnl, hash (tx hash), oid, crossed (taker flag), fee, feeToken, tid, builderFee and liquidation info. userFillsByTime {user, startTime, endTime} pages up to 2000 fills, and up to 10000 most recent are queryable.
- **Torus evidence:** types.rs:385-399: RpcUserFill has no fee, feeToken, tx hash or liquidation flag. Role stands in for crossed. types.rs:361-370: RpcUserTrade lacks oid, startPosition and closedPnl, which the stream has. torus.rs:213-219 and 1645-1652: getUserTrades takes only (trader, market, limit≤1000) with no time or block range. native_executor.rs:1374 and 1853: total_native_fees is initialised to 0, and no maker/taker fee code exists in torus-core or torus-bridge, so there is no fee to report.
- **Suggestion:** Make the backfill RPC and the stream share one schema: add oid, startPosition, closedPnl and dir to RpcUserTrade, which FillExtras already carries (trade_rows.rs:58-63). Add the action hash and a liquidation flag to FillExtras. Add a fee field once fees are charged. Add torus_getUserFillsByTime(user, startMs, endMs, limit) over CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES using a time-seeked key prefix.

</details>

<details><summary>Open-orders endpoint omits trigger (stop) orders; no frontendOpenOrders</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** frontendOpenOrders returns resting and trigger orders with isTrigger, triggerPx, triggerCondition, isPositionTpsl, reduceOnly, orderType and origSz. openOrders returns resting orders.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/book_reader.rs:487-498: read_open_orders keeps only KeyShape::OrderRow and skips StopRow, although stop rows exist (book_reader.rs:9-10, 147). The classic path uses book.orders_for_trader (book_reader.rs:470), while pending_stops are stored separately (crates/torus-core/src/order_book/cancel_batch.rs:477). As a result, a user's queued StopMarket/StopLimit orders are invisible through the RPC.
- **Suggestion:** In book_reader::read_open_orders, also decode StopRow entries and classic book.pending_stops for the trader. Add trigger fields (isTrigger, triggerPx, kind) to RpcOpenOrder (types.rs:327-339), optionally behind torus_getFrontendOpenOrders.

</details>

<details><summary>No node-served candles (candleSnapshot) or candle WS stream</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** The info candleSnapshot {coin, interval, startTime, endTime} supports intervals from 1m to 1M, with up to 5000 candles available. WS candle {coin, interval} pushes live candle updates.
- **Torus evidence:** Candles exist only in the separate torus-explorer SQLite indexer (crates/torus-explorer/src/db.rs:397-411, intervals 1m/5m/15m/1h only) and are served via REST /api/candles/{market_id} (api.rs:37). The node RPC has no candle method or stream (torus.rs:97-227; streams.rs:27-32).
- **Suggestion:** Either add a node-local candle aggregator fed by the BlockFills stream (it can share the newTrades notifier), with torus_getCandles plus a WS candle {market, interval} stream, or extend the explorer with more intervals (3m, 30m, 2h, 4h, 8h, 12h, 1d, 3d, 1w, 1M) and a WS push. The node-local route avoids the indexer's polling lag.

</details>

<details><summary>No weighted per-IP request budget or volume-based per-address action limits</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** REST/WS is limited per IP with a weight budget (about 1200 weight per minute; info calls weigh 2 to 20, exchange calls 1 plus floor(batch/40)) and a cap on WS connections and subscriptions per IP. Per address, the action budget is 1 request per 1 USDC of cumulative traded volume plus an initial 10k buffer. When throttled, 1 request is allowed every 10s. There is also a 1000 open-order cap per user, raised with volume.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-mempool/src/rate_limit.rs:58 and 180: per-sender caps are 64 per block and 512 pending, static and not tied to traded volume. rate_limit.rs:125-176: admission shedding is node-global, pool-size based. crates/torus-rpc/src/lib.rs:24-79: global permits, max connections and response size, but no per-IP or weighted limiter for reads. lib.rs:193 and eth.rs:625-629: TxSubmitLimiter covers EVM raw transactions only. torus.rs:1813-1830: the subscription cap is global (1000) rather than per connection or per IP. The research doc notes HL's 1200 weight/min (research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md:484).
- **Suggestion:** Add jsonrpsee RPC middleware (set_rpc_middleware) holding a per-IP token bucket weighted by method: heavy scans such as getOpenOrders without a market, getMarkets or getTradeHistoryRange cost more. Add per-connection and per-IP subscription caps. For address limits, keep a node-local cumulative-volume counter per address fed by BlockFills. At ingress in torus.rs, around the validate_batch_size calls at :304 and :1951, apply a budget of 10k + volume_usd per address with a 1-per-10s floor. This is ingress policy only, so no consensus change is needed. Any open-order cap enforced in matching would be consensus-breaking.

</details>

<details><summary>No L1 data streaming files / book-diff feed for non-validator nodes</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL non-validator nodes can be run with --write-trades, --write-fills, --write-order-statuses, --write-raw-book-diffs and --write-misc-events, appending node_trades, node_fills_by_block, node_order_statuses and node_raw_book_diffs to hourly files under ~/hl/data. Indexers and market makers consume these locally.
- **Torus evidence:** An --rpc-only mode exists (crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:162, 448-462). The only exec-thread data hook is FillSink with Arc<BlockFills> (crates/torus-state/src/trade_rows.rs:83-90), which carries fills only. grep for book_diff, order_status writers and node_fills finds only the metrics funnel (native_executor.rs:4750). No disk-stream writer exists.
- **Suggestion:** Generalise FillSink into a BlockEventsSink carrying fills, order events and book diffs (level price, size, side per touched market). Add an optional --write-events <dir> flag on rpc-only nodes that appends block-ordered NDJSON, rotated hourly. The same event bus would feed the l2Book and orderUpdates WS streams above, so one producer serves all three consumers.

</details>

#### api-data — fable

Torus exposes a jsonrpsee `torus_*` namespace (25 methods + one `torus_subscribe`) plus a standard `eth_*` namespace, rather than Hyperliquid's `/info`, `/exchange` and `/ws` surfaces. Reads cover book, position, balances, markets, trades (market/block/range/user), open orders, OI, mark price, staking and governance; streaming covers only `newTrades` and `userFills` (plus eth newHeads/logs/newPendingTransactions). Missing entirely vs HL: funding history (no funding engine, so nothing to serve), candleSnapshot on-node (candles live only in the off-chain torus-explorer), orderStatus/historicalOrders (no closed-order index), user-portfolio/clearinghouse aggregate, allMids/bbo/l2Book/candle/orderUpdates/userFundings/webData subscriptions, ws post actions, synchronous order-placement results (submit returns only an action hash), and any address-based or volume-based rate limit on native-action ingress (only a global admission limit, a per-sender pool cap, and an EVM-only 50-tx/10s TxSubmitLimiter). Signing is genuinely EIP-712 with an ed25519 session-key extension, which is at parity or better than HL's agent-wallet scheme. A non-validator `--rpc-only` node mode exists but there is no HL-style file-based L1 data streaming (node_trades/fills/order_statuses); the only out-of-process feed is the websocket.

**Already present:**

<details><summary>No funding engine, so fundingHistory / userFundings / predictedFundings cannot exist</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL computes an hourly funding rate per perp from premium vs oracle, settles payments each hour, and serves `fundingHistory`, `userFunding`, `predictedFundings` via /info and a `userFundings` ws subscription; metaAndAssetCtxs carries the current `funding` and `premium`.
- **Torus evidence:** The only 'funding' token in the whole non-test tree is the MarketParams field max_funding_rate_bps (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1161, serialized at :828,:906); grep of crates/torus-core/src, crates/torus-state/src and crates/torus-rpc/src for 'funding' returns nothing else; no CF for funding in crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:4-140; no RPC method in torus.rs:97-228.
- **Suggestion:** This is primarily a core-engine gap (see the perps/funding area), but the API part is: add CF_NATIVE_FUNDING keyed (market_id, settle_height) storing rate/premium/oracle, plus a per-user ledger CF (user, height, market) written in the settlement step; expose torus_getFundingHistory(market, from, to), torus_getUserFunding(user), and include `funding`/`premium`/`nextFundingTime` in RpcMarketInfo (types.rs:300). Add a `userFundings` StreamKind in streams.rs:27 fed from the same BlockFills-like notifier (lib.rs:103 StreamBlock).

</details>

<details><summary>No metaAndAssetCtxs equivalent: market info lacks mark/oracle/funding/OI/24h volume in one call</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** `meta` returns universe (szDecimals, maxLeverage, onlyIsolated) and `metaAndAssetCtxs` returns per-asset ctx (funding, openInterest, prevDayPx, dayNtlVlm, premium, oraclePx, markPx, midPx, impactPxs); `allMids` ws pushes all mid prices.
- **Torus evidence:** RpcMarketInfo has only market_id, base_asset, quote_asset, lot_size, tick_size, status (crates/torus-rpc/src/types.rs:300-309). Mark/index/last price is a separate per-market call getMarkPrice (torus.rs:210, types.rs:351-358) and OI another (torus.rs:207, types.rs:343-348). No max-leverage, maintenance-margin, 24h volume, prevDayPx, or mid fields anywhere in types.rs:260-405.
- **Suggestion:** Add torus_getMarketsAndContexts returning Vec<(RpcMarketInfo, RpcAssetCtx)> where RpcAssetCtx = {markPrice, indexPrice, midPrice, openInterest, funding (once present), dayVolume, prevDayPx, maxLeverage, mmBps}. 24h volume/prevDayPx need a rolling aggregate maintained on the execution thread from BlockFills (lib.rs:103-186 notifier) or a node-local RocksDB rollup keyed by (market, hour). Extend RpcMarketInfo with leverage/margin params from MarketParams (torus-types lib.rs:~1150).

</details>

<details><summary>No orderStatus / historicalOrders: closed, cancelled and rejected orders are not queryable</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** `orderStatus` (by oid or cloid) returns the order plus status (open/filled/canceled/triggered/rejected/marginCanceled…) and `historicalOrders` returns the last 2000 orders for a user; `orderUpdates` ws pushes every status transition.
- **Torus evidence:** OrderStatus enum exists only inside the matching engine (crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:67,78) and is never persisted: no closed-order CF in crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:4-140 (only CF_NATIVE_ORDERS/CF_BOOK_ORDER_ROWS for live orders). No RPC method takes an order id or client_order_id (torus.rs:97-228). submitNativeAction returns only the keccak action hash (torus.rs:143,1154), so a client cannot learn whether an order rested, filled, or was rejected except by polling getOpenOrders/getUserTrades.
- **Suggestion:** Node-local (non-consensus) order-event log: in the execution result path that already builds BlockFills/extras (lib.rs:103-186), also emit per-order status transitions (placed/resting/partial/filled/cancelled/rejected with reason) and persist them to a node-local CF keyed (user, seq) and (order_id) plus a cloid→order_id index. Serve torus_getOrderStatus(id\|cloid) and torus_getHistoricalOrders(user, limit) and add StreamKind::OrderUpdates(user) in streams.rs:27. Keep it node-local so it stays non-consensus-breaking.

</details>

<details><summary>WebSocket subscription coverage: no l2Book, bbo, allMids, candle, orderUpdates, webData, userEvents</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL ws offers allMids, l2Book (with nSigFigs/mantissa aggregation), trades, bbo, candle, userEvents, userFills, orderUpdates, userFundings, userNonFundingLedgerUpdates, webData2, activeAssetCtx, notification.
- **Torus evidence:** StreamKind has exactly two variants: NewTrades(Option<market>) and UserFills(user) (crates/torus-rpc/src/streams.rs:27-32; dispatch torus.rs:1786-1799). Order book is pull-only via getOrderBook (torus.rs:100). The BlockNotifier only carries new_heads and fills (lib.rs:103-186, `notify_fills`).
- **Suggestion:** Extend BlockNotifier (lib.rs ~103-186) with a per-block book-delta/BBO snapshot computed by the exec thread for touched markets (the mode-2 row store already knows which rows changed), then add StreamKind::L2Book(market, depth), Bbo(market), AllMids. Reuse the StreamBlock once-per-filter serialization pattern (streams.rs:158-213). Candle streams can be derived from newTrades on the node with a small in-memory OHLCV rollup.

</details>

<details><summary>No candleSnapshot on the node; candles only in the separate explorer service</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** `candleSnapshot {coin, interval, startTime, endTime}` is served by the API node itself (intervals 1m…1M, up to 5000 candles) and `candle` ws streams live updates.
- **Torus evidence:** Only candle code is crates/torus-explorer/src/api.rs:37,213-233 (GET /api/candles/{market_id}, separate axum service with its own DB via indexer.rs/db.rs); nothing candle-related in crates/torus-rpc, torus-state or torus-core (grep -rni candle lists only torus-explorer files).
- **Suggestion:** Either document the explorer as the official candle source and give it the HL interval set, or move the OHLCV rollup into torus-rpc as a node-local RocksDB CF (market, interval, bucket_ts) updated from the fills notifier (lib.rs:186 notify_fills), served by torus_getCandles and a `candle` StreamKind.

</details>

<details><summary>No address-based or volume-based rate limit on native-action ingress; limits are global or EVM-only</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL enforces IP limits (1200 weight/min REST), per-address limits of 1 request per 1 USDC traded cumulatively (10k buffer), 10 open-order cancel grace, and ws limits (100 inflight posts, 1000 subscriptions, 10 unique users per IP). Rate-limited addresses can still cancel.
- **Torus evidence:** TxSubmitLimiter (50 tx / 10 s per sender) is only consulted in eth_sendRawTransaction (crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:627; lib.rs:190-227,309). Native submit path (torus.rs:1101-1154, verify_one_action_with :287-320) applies validate_batch_size and the global admission_limit (torus-mempool/src/rate_limit.rs:164-176) plus per-sender pending cap NATIVE_PER_SENDER_CAP=512 (rate_limit.rs:180); nothing is keyed by IP or by traded volume, and there is no per-connection subscription cap (active_subscriptions is a single node-wide counter, torus.rs:1751, eth.rs:1064).
- **Suggestion:** Add a jsonrpsee middleware layer (tower) in RpcServer::start (lib.rs:284+) keyed by peer IP with token-bucket weights per method; reuse TxSubmitLimiter for native senders in verify_one_action_with (torus.rs:306 after sender recovery), seeded with a volume-derived allowance read from CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES. Preserve the existing 'cancels never shed' rule (lib.rs:1535-1544). Add per-connection subscription cap in the subscribe handlers.

</details>

<details><summary>No synchronous order placement response (resting / filled / rejected per order)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** /exchange `order` returns per-order statuses immediately: {resting:{oid}}, {filled:{totalSz, avgPx, oid}}, or {error}. Clients get oid and fill info without polling.
- **Torus evidence:** submit_native_action returns RpcResult<String> = hex action hash (torus.rs:143,1101-1154); submitNativeActions returns RpcSubmitResult per item (types.rs:431) which is admission-level only (accepted/rejected by the mempool), not execution outcome. Execution happens later on the leader after forwarding (lib.rs:269-278).
- **Suggestion:** Cannot be synchronous under BFT ordering, but can emulate: assign deterministic order ids at ingress (hash-derived, already keccak(canonical JSON) torus.rs:318) and return them, then expose torus_getOrderStatus (gap above) and an `orderUpdates` stream so clients subscribe before submitting. Document the async model explicitly in the API docs.

</details>

<details><summary>No clearinghouseState / portfolio aggregate (all positions + margin summary in one call)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** `clearinghouseState` returns all assetPositions (szi, entryPx, leverage, liquidationPx, unrealizedPnl, marginUsed, cumFunding, returnOnEquity), marginSummary (accountValue, totalNtlPos, totalRawUsd, totalMarginUsed), withdrawable; `portfolio` returns PnL/accountValue history.
- **Torus evidence:** getPosition requires a market_id and returns one RpcPosition (torus.rs:103-108, types.rs:276-288); getBalances gives total_margin_used/available_balance (types.rs:290-298) but no account value, no per-position leverage or ROE, no cumFunding; there is no all-positions call and no PnL history store (cf.rs:4-140).
- **Suggestion:** Add torus_getAccountState(trader) that iterates CF_NATIVE_POSITIONS by address prefix (cf.rs:42) and returns positions + margin summary computed with the same mark price used by getMarkPrice (torus.rs:210), and a node-local daily snapshot of accountValue for a `portfolio` history.

</details>

<details><summary>No HL-style non-validator L1 data streaming (node_trades / node_fills / order_statuses files)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** A non-validator hl-node run with --write-trades / --write-fills / --write-order-statuses / --write-misc-events writes hourly JSONL files under ~/hl/data/ (node_trades, node_fills, node_order_statuses, replica_cmds, periodic_abci_states) that indexers tail; this is the canonical bulk data path, independent of the ws.
- **Torus evidence:** --rpc-only mode exists (torus-node/src/main.rs:162,288-289,448-463) but the only data egress is RPC/ws: no file writer for trades/fills in crates/torus-node/src (grep for BufWriter/fs::write shows only keystore.rs:95). Trade bulk access is via getBlockTrades/getTradeHistoryRange paging (torus.rs:186-197).
- **Suggestion:** Add a `--write-trades/--write-fills DIR` option in torus-node main.rs that subscribes to the existing BlockNotifier fills channel (lib.rs:103-186) and appends hourly-rotated JSONL using the RpcStreamTrade/RpcUserFill row formats already in types.rs:375-400, so file rows and ws rows are byte-identical.

</details>

<details><summary>No ws 'post' (requests/actions over the websocket) and no per-connection subscription limit</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL ws supports {method:'post', request:{type:'info'\|'action', payload}} so clients submit orders over the same socket, with 100 inflight posts per IP and 1000 subscriptions per IP.
- **Torus evidence:** jsonrpsee serves all `torus_*` methods over both HTTP and ws transports, so method calls over ws work implicitly (lib.rs:284+ RpcServer); but there is no inflight-per-connection accounting: active_subscriptions is one node-wide AtomicUsize (lib.rs:254, torus.rs:1751, eth.rs:1064-1075), and submit permits are global (SUBMIT_PERMITS=64, lib.rs:24).
- **Suggestion:** Treat as mostly present via jsonrpsee ws; add a per-connection counter in a jsonrpsee RpcServiceBuilder middleware for subscriptions and inflight submits, and document that submitNativeActions over ws is the 'post' equivalent.

</details>
