HL facts I am less sure of: exact current rate-limit numbers (1200 weight/min, 1 req per 1 USDC traded with 10k buffer, 1000 subs / 100 inflight posts per IP, 10 users per IP) are from memory of docs as of early 2026 and may have changed; the exact list of hl-node --write-* flags and the file names (node_trades, node_fills, node_order_statuses) are from the hyperliquid-dex/node README as I recall it; candleSnapshot's 5000-candle cap and historicalOrders' 2000-order cap are from memory. The research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md section 7.3 only confirms the three endpoints and the 1200 weight/min figure.

### validators-staking

#### validators-staking — opus

Torus has most of the staking parts in torus-economics: register, delegate, undelegate, permanent stake, claim rewards, commission changes, jail votes, unjail, key rotation, epoch rotation with a rotation cap and a minimum-set floor, and a stake-weighted oracle. Most of them are dispatched from NativeAction in crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs; the core/native_executor.rs path in the brief does not exist. The lifecycle is still broken in several places. Unbonding is never processed, so undelegated tokens are locked forever. Validator inflation hands the self-stake share of rewards to outside delegators. Equivocation slashing comes from each node's own local view instead of consensus-ordered evidence, which is a state-divergence risk. Joining as a validator needs a governance whitelist, not permissionless self-stake as on Hyperliquid. Jailing only takes effect in consensus at the next epoch (100k blocks), DowntimeTracker and DoubleSignDetector are still unused, governance ParameterChange writes keys nothing reads, and ListMarket always writes market key 0.

**Already present:**
- Validator registration with a minimum self-stake of 10k TRS: crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:42-81 and types.rs:303. Dispatched at crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3304 (exec_register_validator at :5506), gated by a governance whitelist.
- Delegate: native_executor.rs:3257 calls exec_delegate (:5428), which calls staking.rs:90. It rejects Jailed and Tombstoned validators.
- Undelegate creates a 7-day UnbondingEntry: native_executor.rs:3260 and :5440, staking.rs:130-186, UNBONDING_PERIOD at types.rs:313. Entries are capped at 100 per delegation (staking.rs:163).
- Permanent stake (irreversible; unlock needs an 80% governance vote): staking.rs:233, native_executor.rs:3263. It earns 5% APY through rewards.rs:131-163.
- Validator inflation reward of a flat 5% APY on active stake, split by commission and accrued to pending rewards, with ClaimRewards: rewards.rs:167-240, staking.rs:327, native_executor.rs:3266 and :5468.
- Commission changes capped at 100 bps per change with a 2-day cooldown, max 50%: types.rs:316-319, :589, staking.rs:350.
- Epoch-boundary processing (rewards, then set rotation with safe_rotation_cap and enforce_minimum_floor) runs in the prod exec tail: native_executor.rs:6025-6103, called at crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1940.
- Consensus validator-set updates (ValidatorSetUpdates) at the epoch boundary, including applying pending key rotations: app.rs:4074-4160. Top-N by stake with N = max_validators = 21: crates/torus-economics/src/epoch.rs:35-70, crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:307.
- JailVote: an Active validator votes, with stake weighting, a >2/3 threshold and 1-day vote expiry; reaching the threshold slashes 0.1% and jails for 2 days. staking.rs:518-612, native_executor.rs:3311 and :5479.
- UnjailSelf: cooldown plus a minimum self-stake check, then back to Candidate: staking.rs:637-680, native_executor.rs:3312 and :5496. TopUpSelfStake: native_executor.rs:3268.
- Slash function that cuts self_stake and all delegations proportionally, burns the slashed amount and auto-jails below the minimum: staking.rs:392-475. Tombstoning: staking.rs:503.
- Equivocation (leader double-proposal) detection in hotstuff that feeds on_speculative_rollback, which buffers a 5% slash plus tombstone applied at the next commit: hotstuff_rs/src/hotstuff/implementation.rs:1209-1235, torus-consensus/src/app.rs:5119-5160 and :1532-1561.
- Stake-weighted-median oracle with outlier rejection; only Active validators may submit: crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:199-258 and :424, native_executor.rs:5685-5721.
- Stake-weighted governance: SubmitProposal and Vote (including Abstain), quorum on total staked, process_pending_proposals every block, TreasurySpend, ValidatorRegistration whitelist, PermanentUnlock: crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:786, :923, :961-1130, native_executor.rs:3284-3290 and :6106, app.rs:1938.
- Validator key rotation applied at the epoch: staking.rs:906-996, app.rs:4088.

| Gap | Status | Impact | Effort | Lockstep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unbonding never processed: undelegated tokens are locked forever | unwired | critical | S | yes |
| Validator inflation hands the self-stake share of rewards to delegators | buggy | high | S | yes |
| Equivocation slashing comes from each node's own local view, not consensus-ordered evidence | buggy | critical | M | yes |
| Validator entry is permissioned by governance whitelist, not permissionless | partial | high | S | yes |
| No self-stake withdrawal or validator exit, no delegation lockup, no redelegation | absent | medium | M | yes |
| Jailing only takes effect in consensus at the next epoch; downtime and latency jailing not automated | partial | high | M | yes |
| Two staking writers at the epoch boundary: consensus-thread status writes alongside exec writes | buggy | high | M | yes |
| Reward model: flat 5% APY snapshot at the epoch, no time weighting | partial | medium | M | yes |
| Governance ParameterChange is a dead write, and ListMarket overwrites market key 0 | stub | high | M | yes |
| No on-chain protocol-upgrade mechanism | absent | low | M | yes |
| Slashing misses unbonding stake, and jail votes slash where HL does not | partial | low | S | yes |

<details><summary>Unbonding never processed: undelegated tokens are locked forever</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** On HL, undelegated stake returns to the user's staking balance after the 1-day delegation lockup. A staking-to-spot withdrawal goes through a 7-day unstaking queue and is credited to spot automatically when it matures.
- **Torus evidence:** staking.rs:189-226 defines process_unbonding, which credits matured entries. The only callers are tests: torus-integration-tests/tests/staking_lifecycle.rs:357, :363, :420 and staking.rs:1203. There is no NativeAction to claim unbonded tokens (the dispatch at native_executor.rs:3256-3273 has Delegate, Undelegate, PermanentStake, ClaimRewards and TopUpSelfStake only), and process_epoch_boundary (native_executor.rs:6025-6103) never sweeps unbonding entries. exec_undelegate (native_executor.rs:5440-5453) debits the delegation and pushes an entry that nothing ever releases.
- **Suggestion:** Pick one of two fixes. (a) Add NativeAction::ClaimUnbonded { validator } that calls ctx.staking.process_unbonding(sender, validator, ctx.block_height). (b) Keep an index CF of release_block -> (delegator, validator) and drain matured entries deterministically in process_epoch_boundary or every block, before reward distribution. Also expose pending unbonding entries over RPC (torus-rpc/src/torus.rs get_staking_info).

</details>

<details><summary>Validator inflation hands the self-stake share of rewards to delegators</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** On HL, rewards accrue pro-rata to each stake. The validator earns its self-delegation rewards plus commission on delegator rewards.
- **Torus evidence:** rewards.rs:202-206 computes val_emission from total_stake() = self_stake + total_delegated (types.rs:93). rewards.rs:214-215 sets delegator_pool = val_emission - commission over that whole amount. The delegator loop (rewards.rs:230-240) then splits delegator_pool only among delegation records, normalised by val.total_delegated. Registration sets total_delegated = 0 and keeps self_stake separate (staking.rs:67-74), so the self-stake share goes to outside delegators. Example: self 10k, one delegator with 1k, 10% commission. The delegator gets 90% of the emission while holding 9% of the stake. distribute_validator_share (rewards.rs:78-125, the fee share) has the same flaw.
- **Suggestion:** Split val_emission into self_part = val_emission * self_stake / total_stake, which goes to the validator, and del_part = the remainder. Take commission only from del_part and distribute del_part - commission across delegations. Apply the same fix in distribute_validator_share.

</details>

<details><summary>Equivocation slashing comes from each node's own local view, not consensus-ordered evidence</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL does not slash automatically today; misbehaviour is handled by jailing through validator votes. Any slashing that does change state has to be deterministic across replicas.
- **Torus evidence:** Each replica detects equivocation from proposals it personally received: hotstuff_rs/src/hotstuff/implementation.rs:1209-1235 and :2150-2160 (seen_proposals). The app buffers the result in node-local self.pending_slashes (torus-consensus/src/app.rs:5147-5152). That buffer is drained into the next committed block's execution (app.rs:5109) and applied as direct DB writes (app.rs:1532-1561). The evidence is never put in a block. A node that saw both conflicting proposals slashes and tombstones; a node that saw only one does not, so the staking state and validator set diverge. The slash also passes current_block = 0 (app.rs:1535), so the SlashRecord key (staking.rs:1054) is always height 0, which overwrites the previous record, and the auto-jail jailed_until is near zero.
- **Suggestion:** Make the evidence a transaction. Add NativeAction::SubmitEquivocationEvidence carrying both signed proposals. The leader includes it, every replica verifies the signatures in exec, and staking.slash and tombstone_validator run with the real block_height. Drop the local pending_slashes path, or keep it only to generate that transaction. Reuse DoubleSignDetector (torus-consensus/src/slashing.rs:126) for vote double-signs.

</details>

<details><summary>Validator entry is permissioned by governance whitelist, not permissionless</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Anyone can register a validator on HL by self-delegating 10k HYPE. The active set is the top validators by stake (I am not sure of the exact cap), recomputed each epoch.
- **Torus evidence:** exec_register_validator (native_executor.rs:5512-5522) rejects senders without a governance whitelist entry. Whitelisting only happens through an ExecutionPayload::ValidatorRegistration proposal that passes (governance.rs:1109-1121), and it expires after 7 days (types.rs:592). Registration also uses the sender's entire balance as self-stake (native_executor.rs:5524-5526) instead of a chosen amount.
- **Suggestion:** Make the whitelist check optional, behind a governance param (for example permissionless_validators = true), and add a self_stake amount to RegisterValidator. Epoch top-N selection (epoch.rs:35-70) already does stake-ranked admission.

</details>

<details><summary>No self-stake withdrawal or validator exit, no delegation lockup, no redelegation</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** On HL, a validator can unstake its self-delegation, subject to keeping the minimum while active. Delegations have a 1-day lockup, after which they can be undelegated or moved to another validator. Staking-to-spot withdrawals go through a 7-day queue.
- **Torus evidence:** NativeAction has only Delegate, Undelegate and TopUpSelfStake for stake movement (torus-types/src/lib.rs:616-620, native_executor.rs:3256-3273). grep finds no deregister, withdraw_self or redelegate in torus-economics/src or torus-types/src. delegate (staking.rs:90-126) records no lock time, so stake can be undelegated in the same block. Self-stake can only go up (staking.rs:683 top_up_self_stake).
- **Suggestion:** Add UnstakeSelf { amount }, which enforces self_stake >= MIN_SELF_DELEGATION unless the status is Candidate/Inactive and goes through the unbonding queue. Add Redelegate { from, to, amount }, which moves stake without the queue but keeps a lockup. Record last_delegated_block on Delegation and reject an undelegate before last_delegated_block + DELEGATION_LOCKUP_BLOCKS (1 day).

</details>

<details><summary>Jailing only takes effect in consensus at the next epoch; downtime and latency jailing not automated</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** On HL, validators vote to jail peers that are unresponsive or have high latency. Jailed validators stop taking part in consensus and stop earning rewards until they unjail. HL epochs are short (about 90 minutes), so set changes land quickly.
- **Torus evidence:** record_jail_vote (staking.rs:518-574) only flips the status. ValidatorSetUpdates are produced only when EpochManager::is_epoch_boundary(height) holds (app.rs:4082-4085), and epoch_length = 100_000 blocks (main.rs:306), about 55 hours at the 2s TARGET_BLOCK_TIME_SECS (types.rs:310). Until then a jailed validator keeps its consensus power. DowntimeTracker and DoubleSignDetector (torus-consensus/src/slashing.rs:126, :235) are only constructed in tests (slashing.rs:344-482, torus-integration-tests/tests/slashing_jailing.rs:120, :287); lib.rs:22 re-exports them without using them. DOWNTIME_WINDOW_BLOCKS and DOWNTIME_THRESHOLD_PCT (types.rs:365-368) are unused.
- **Suggestion:** Emit a ValidatorSetUpdates delete (power 0) in the block where a jail or tombstone happens, not only at the epoch: hook app.rs epoch_validator_set_updates, or use a per-block 'pending removals' list. Feed QC signer bitmaps from committed blocks into DowntimeTracker. That data is deterministic because it lives in the justify QC, so the tracker can auto-jail at threshold during exec. Optionally shorten epoch_length to roughly HL's cadence.

</details>

<details><summary>Two staking writers at the epoch boundary: consensus-thread status writes alongside exec writes</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** On HL, validator-set and staking state transitions all happen inside deterministic block execution.
- **Torus evidence:** epoch_validator_set_updates runs during propose/validate on the consensus thread (app.rs:4716, :4839). It calls staking.apply_pending_rotations (app.rs:4088) and EpochManager::update_validator_statuses(&self.staking, ...) (app.rs:4131) against the live staking DB. process_epoch_boundary (native_executor.rs:6067) writes statuses again in exec. The two paths compute from possibly different snapshots: the consensus thread uses self.last_validator_set and the current staking state, while exec builds the old set from staking (native_executor.rs:6122-6145). They can disagree, for example when the cap > 0 branch differs (app.rs:4110-4114 vs native_executor.rs:6053-6054).
- **Suggestion:** Make exec (process_epoch_boundary) the only writer. Have it persist the computed new_set and diff to a CF. Change epoch_validator_set_updates to read that persisted result, read-only, and turn it into ValidatorSetUpdates. Remove the staking writes from the consensus thread.

</details>

<details><summary>Reward model: flat 5% APY snapshot at the epoch, no time weighting</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** On HL, the staking reward rate is inversely proportional to the square root of total HYPE staked (about 2.37% at 400M staked). Rewards accrue every minute on the current stake and are compounded and distributed daily, and they come from the future emissions reserve.
- **Torus evidence:** rewards.rs:187-192 mints total_active_staked * 500 bps * epoch_length / BLOCKS_PER_YEAR once per epoch, using the delegation snapshot at the boundary (rewards.rs:230). Someone who delegates one block before the boundary gets a full epoch's reward. The rate does not respond to the staking ratio. BLOCKS_PER_YEAR assumes 2s blocks (types.rs:310, :322); if real block time is faster, emissions and the 7-day UNBONDING_PERIOD and 2-day JAIL_DURATION_BLOCKS (types.rs:313, :371) all scale wrongly in wall-clock terms.
- **Suggestion:** Track a per-validator cumulative reward-per-stake index, updated every block (or every N blocks) using the block timestamp delta instead of block counts, and settle delegators lazily on delegate/undelegate/claim (F1-style). Use rate = k / sqrt(total_staked) to match HL. Derive the time-based constants from the timestamp, not from TARGET_BLOCK_TIME_SECS.

</details>

<details><summary>Governance ParameterChange is a dead write, and ListMarket overwrites market key 0</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** On HL, validator votes change live protocol state: oracle and bridge actions, and governance of perp listings and parameters through validator stake votes and deploy auctions. Parameters take effect when they are applied.
- **Torus evidence:** execute ParameterChange writes CF_FEE_CONFIG[param_key] (governance.rs:1043-1051). The only readers of keys such as max_leverage and maintenance_margin_bps are tests (torus-economics/tests/governance_tests.rs:370, torus-integration-tests/tests/staking_lifecycle.rs:207); no prod code reads them. exec_submit_proposal hard-codes market_id: 0 (native_executor.rs:5744-5745). MarketListing execution writes CF_NATIVE_MARKETS[0u64.to_be_bytes()] (governance.rs:1080-1101), the same CF the executor uses for book-mode and order-id rows (native_executor.rs:2541, :2558), so a second listing overwrites the first. UpdateMarketParams and DelistMarket map to None, so the proposal is text only (native_executor.rs:5754-5756).
- **Suggestion:** Allocate market_id from a durable counter at execution time and call the same market-creation path the executor uses (OrderBook, MarketMarginConfig, OracleConfig). Make the margin/leverage engine read a governance param overlay (CF_FEE_CONFIG) on block start, or have ParameterChange mutate MarketMarginConfig directly. Add payloads for UpdateMarketParams and DelistMarket.

</details>

<details><summary>No on-chain protocol-upgrade mechanism</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** As far as I know, HL coordinates node software upgrades off-chain (validators run new binaries at a set time) rather than through on-chain upgrade proposals.
- **Torus evidence:** grep for SoftwareUpgrade, upgrade_height or ProtocolUpgrade across crates/*.rs returns nothing. ExecutionPayload has no upgrade variant (governance.rs:176-198).
- **Suggestion:** Add ExecutionPayload::ScheduleUpgrade { name, height, binary_hash }. Exec stores it, and the node halts at that height unless it runs the matching version. This gives lockstep upgrades without an emergency coordinated restart.

</details>

<details><summary>Slashing misses unbonding stake, and jail votes slash where HL does not</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL currently has no automatic slashing; jailing only stops rewards. If slashing is kept, the standard design also slashes stake that is still unbonding from when the infraction happened.
- **Torus evidence:** slash (staking.rs:411-426) reduces only del.amount and leaves the del.unbonding entries alone. A delegator who undelegates right after an infraction keeps 100% of that stake. record_jail_vote applies DOWNTIME_SLASH_BPS (0.1%) on top of jailing (staking.rs:563-568).
- **Suggestion:** In slash, also scale unbonding entries whose release_block - UNBONDING_PERIOD is greater than or equal to the infraction height. Decide whether jail votes should slash at all, to match HL's no-slash jailing.

</details>

*Confidence notes:* Corrections to the prior audit. The executor is crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs; crates/torus-core/src/native_executor.rs does not exist. 'process_unbonding never called' is confirmed: only tests call it. 'DowntimeTracker/DoubleSignDetector unused' is confirmed, but there is a separate equivocation-slash path through hotstuff on_speculative_rollback, and that path is wired. 'governance ListMarket always market_id 0' is confirmed (native_executor.rs:5745, governance.rs:1080-1101). I did not trace whether the executor's market loader actually decodes the governance-written CF_NATIVE_MARKETS[0] row (precompiles.rs:550 iterates that CF), so whether it corrupts market 0 is plausible but unverified. The dual-writer finding (consensus-thread update_validator_statuses at app.rs:4131 alongside exec at native_executor.rs:6067) is plausible. I did not confirm that the two writes actually diverge in practice or that the consensus-thread staking handle writes the same DB that is state-rooted. I did not check whether ValidatorSetDiff.inserts carries power changes for validators that stay in the set. I did not inspect the torus-bridge validator.rs/proposer.rs validator voting on bridge deposits or withdrawals in depth (only that it uses epoch_for_block). Hyperliquid facts I am unsure of: the exact active-set cap; whether jailing removes a validator from consensus immediately or at the next epoch; the exact reward formula constant (about 2.37% at 400M staked, inverse-sqrt); and how protocol upgrades are coordinated. I did not read research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md because of the time box. Actual block time versus TARGET_BLOCK_TIME_SECS = 2 is unverified; recent perf work suggests blocks may be faster, which would shorten the time-based constants in wall-clock terms.

#### validators-staking — fable

Torus has a substantially more built-out staking/validator stack than the 2026-09-29 audit implied: DPoS delegate/undelegate with a 7-day unbonding queue, stake-weighted top-N validator rotation at epoch boundaries (max_validators=21, min 4, rotation cap + BFT floor), 5% APY validator inflation split by commission to delegators, stake-weighted (>2/3) peer JailVote with 2-day jail + unjailSelf, double-sign slashing (5% + tombstone) wired from hotstuff's equivocation callback, commission-change limits, key rotation, and a governance module with whitelisted validator registration. The main gaps vs Hyperliquid are (a) unbonding never matures in prod (process_unbonding has zero non-test callers, so undelegated funds are locked forever), (b) no automatic downtime/latency detection (DowntimeTracker/DoubleSignDetector still unwired; jailing is purely manual votes), (c) validator registration is governance-whitelisted, so the set is not permissionless and registration locks the sender's entire balance with no exit path, (d) no delegation lockup / withdrawal-cap semantics, flat-APY rewards instead of HL's 1/sqrt(staked) curve, no auto-compounding, and (e) no protocol-upgrade/hl-visor-style mechanism. Note HL itself does not slash today, so Torus's slashing is strictly ahead of HL there.

**Already present:**
- DPoS delegate/undelegate with UNBONDING_PERIOD = 7 days of blocks and max 100 pending entries: crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:90-185, types.rs:313; wired in native executor crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5428-5453 (NativeAction::Delegate/Undelegate at :3257-3260)
- Stake-weighted top-N validator set rotation at epoch boundary with rotation cap, MIN_ACTIVE_VALIDATORS=4 floor, status updates, key-rotation apply: crates/torus-economics/src/epoch.rs:35-70, crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:4074-4182 (consensus side) and crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6025-6104 (exec side, called at app.rs:1940); max_validators=21 default in crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:307 and torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:618; hotstuff set synced with stake power at app.rs:471-479
- Validator inflation rewards (5% APY on active stake, commission split, pro-rata to delegators) + permanent-stake rewards at epoch boundary: crates/torus-economics/src/rewards.rs:166-263, native_executor.rs:6034-6044; claim via ClaimRewards -> staking.rs:327-342 / native_executor.rs:5469-5477
- Block fee distribution to proposer/treasury/dev-pool/burn with epoch-lerped split: native_executor.rs:5991-6014, rewards.rs:24, types.rs:340-349
- Peer jail voting, stake-weighted >2/3 of active stake, 1-day vote expiry, auto 0.1% slash + 2-day jail; unjailSelf after cooldown with min-stake and tombstone checks; delegation to jailed rejected: staking.rs:518-613, :637, :90-105; types.rs:359-374; NativeAction::JailVote/UnjailSelf wired at native_executor.rs:3311, :5479-5504
- Double-sign (leader equivocation) slashing 5% + tombstone, buffered from hotstuff's on_speculative_rollback callback and applied at block execution: crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:5118-5162, :1532-1560; hotstuff_rs/src/hotstuff/implementation.rs:1247,1263,2179
- Validator registration with MIN_SELF_DELEGATION 10,000 TRS, commission cap 50%, +1% max change with 2-day cooldown, key rotation applied at epoch: staking.rs:42-83, :350, :906-996; types.rs:303-319, :589; native_executor.rs:5506-5554
- Governance: proposals (ParameterChange/TreasurySpend/MarketListing/ValidatorRegistration/PermanentUnlock/Text), stake voting, timelock, per-block processing: crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:176-198, :698-999, :1036-1080; called every block at app.rs:1938
- Validator oracle voting with stake-weighted median + MAD outlier rejection (HL-like): crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:1, :199-258; NativeAction::SubmitOraclePrices at native_executor.rs:3276
- RPC exposure of staking state (getStakingInfo/getValidators/getEpoch/getDelegations/getProposals incl. unbonding entries): crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:129-167, :1013-1026

| Gap | Status | Impact | Effort | Lockstep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unbonding queue never matures in production (undelegated funds locked forever) | unwired | critical | S | yes |
| No automatic downtime / latency jailing; DowntimeTracker and DoubleSignDetector unwired | unwired | high | M | no |
| Validator set is governance-whitelisted, not permissionless | partial | medium | S | yes |
| Validator registration locks the sender's entire balance and there is no exit/withdraw-self-stake path | partial | medium | M | yes |
| No delegation lockup and unbounded undelegation semantics differ from HL | partial | medium | S | yes |
| Staking reward curve is flat 5% APY, not HL's inverse-sqrt-of-stake schedule, and rewards are not auto-compounded | partial | low | S | yes |
| No protocol upgrade / coordinated hard-fork mechanism (hl-visor equivalent) | absent | medium | L | yes |
| Validator-set rotation computed twice on different threads (consensus-side and exec-side) with status writes from both | partial | medium | M | yes |
| Equivocation slash is buffered node-locally rather than carried as on-chain evidence | partial | high | M | yes |

<details><summary>Unbonding queue never matures in production (undelegated funds locked forever)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** After undelegating, HYPE enters a 7-day unstaking queue and is automatically returned to the spot/staking balance when the queue entry matures (max 5 pending withdrawals per address).
- **Torus evidence:** StakingManager::process_unbonding exists at crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:189-225 and is correct, but grep across all crates (excluding tests) finds no caller: not in crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs (staking handlers :5428-5504, epoch boundary :6025-6104) nor crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs. Undelegate at staking.rs:172-181 pushes an UnbondingEntry with release_block = now + UNBONDING_PERIOD, and nothing ever credits it back. RPC shows the entries (torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1013-1026) but they never release. The 2026-09-29 audit claim is still true on current main.
- **Suggestion:** Add a deterministic sweep in NativeExecutor::process_epoch_boundary (native_executor.rs:~6032, before Phase A) or per-block in the exec tail (app.rs:1937-1940): iterate CF delegations (staking.delegations_for_* exists) and call process_unbonding(delegator, validator, ctx.block_height) for entries with release_block <= height. For O(1) per block, additionally index unbonding entries by release_block (new CF key release_block\|\|delegator\|\|validator written in undelegate) and drain only matured keys. Alternatively add a user-triggered NativeAction::WithdrawUnbonded that calls process_unbonding (cheaper, HL-unlike but safe). Any choice changes state transition -> lockstep upgrade.

</details>

<details><summary>No automatic downtime / latency jailing; DowntimeTracker and DoubleSignDetector unwired</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Validators continuously measure peer liveness/latency (target 200ms two-way to >=1/3 of stake) and automatically cast jail votes; a jailed validator stops participating and earning until unjailSelf after the jailed-until time, which is rate-limited.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-consensus/src/slashing.rs:126-222 (DoubleSignDetector) and :235-300 (DowntimeTracker with record_signer/detect_downtime) are only re-exported at crates/torus-consensus/src/lib.rs:22; no call sites in app.rs or torus-node (grep for DowntimeTracker\|record_signer\|JailVote in crates/torus-node/src returns nothing). DOWNTIME_WINDOW_BLOCKS/DOWNTIME_THRESHOLD_PCT (types.rs:365-368) have no non-test readers. JailVote is a purely manual NativeAction (native_executor.rs:5479-5494); nothing in the node submits it automatically. Double-sign detection works only for leader equivocation via hotstuff's on_speculative_rollback (app.rs:5118), not for conflicting votes by non-leaders.
- **Suggestion:** Node-side (non-consensus) automation: in torus-node, instantiate DowntimeTracker, feed it from QC signer bitmaps on each committed block (hotstuff QC exposes signatures per validator), run detect_downtime every DOWNTIME_WINDOW_BLOCKS, and have the local validator sign and submit NativeAction::JailVote{target} through the normal mempool path for any peer under DOWNTIME_THRESHOLD_PCT (rate-limit one vote per target per JAIL_VOTE_EXPIRY_BLOCKS). Since jailing still requires >2/3 stake-weighted votes on-chain, this is not consensus-breaking. Optionally wire DoubleSignDetector to observed PhaseVote gossip and emit a SubmitEvidence action later (that part would be consensus-breaking).

</details>

<details><summary>Validator set is governance-whitelisted, not permissionless</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Since April 2025 the validator set is permissionless: any account with >=10,000 HYPE self-delegated can register; the active set is the top 21 by stake, recomputed each epoch.
- **Torus evidence:** exec_register_validator at crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5512-5522 rejects registration unless ctx.governance.is_whitelisted(sender) (governance.rs:1213) via a ValidatorRegistration proposal (governance.rs:195) that must pass a stake vote and timelock; the whitelist slot expires after WHITELIST_EXPIRY_BLOCKS (types.rs:592). Top-21-by-stake rotation itself is present (epoch.rs:35-70).
- **Suggestion:** Make the whitelist a genesis/governance-togglable parameter (e.g. GovernanceParams.permissionless_validators: bool, governance.rs:445) and skip the is_whitelisted check in exec_register_validator when set; keep MIN_SELF_DELEGATION as the only barrier. If the whitelist is an intentional bootstrap control, document it and add a ParameterChange key to flip it so the switch to permissionless does not need a binary upgrade.

</details>

<details><summary>Validator registration locks the sender's entire balance and there is no exit/withdraw-self-stake path</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Validator self-delegates exactly 10,000+ HYPE (locked 1 year), can later undelegate self-stake like any delegator, and can retire; delegations persist independently.
- **Torus evidence:** native_executor.rs:5524-5538 uses the sender account's full balance as self_stake (comment: 'sender's full balance is used as self-stake'), so a validator must empty its wallet into stake. staking.rs pub fn list (lines 29-1033) has top_up_self_stake (:683) but no withdraw_self_stake/unregister/deregister; grep for Unregister\|Deregister\|WithdrawSelfStake in torus-types/src/lib.rs returns nothing. Self-stake can only leave via slashing.
- **Suggestion:** Add an explicit self_stake amount to NativeAction::RegisterValidator (torus-types/src/lib.rs:646) and validate >= MIN_SELF_DELEGATION. Add NativeAction::UndelegateSelfStake{amount} that reduces self_stake into an unbonding entry (reuse Delegation/UnbondingEntry keyed delegator==validator) with the floor that remaining self_stake >= MIN_SELF_DELEGATION while status is Active/Candidate, otherwise auto-transition to Inactive so epoch rotation drops the validator. Optionally enforce HL's 1-year lock on the initial self-stake via a registered_at_block field in ValidatorState (types.rs:80-90).

</details>

<details><summary>No delegation lockup and unbounded undelegation semantics differ from HL</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Each delegation event locks the delegated amount for 1 day before it can be undelegated; max 5 pending unstaking withdrawals per address; undelegation 7-day queue.
- **Torus evidence:** staking.rs:90-127 delegate() records only amount (Delegation struct types.rs:143-148 has no lock/last_delegated_block field); undelegate() at :130-185 has no lockup check and allows up to 100 unbonding entries per (delegator,validator) pair rather than 5 per address. This lets a delegator instantly flip stake between validators to swing jail-vote weight or epoch ranking inside one epoch.
- **Suggestion:** Add last_delegation_block: u64 to Delegation (bump borsh encoding with a versioned prefix), set it in delegate(), and reject undelegate() while current_block < last_delegation_block + DELEGATION_LOCKUP_BLOCKS (1 day = 43_200 blocks at 2s). Lower MAX_UNBONDING_ENTRIES to a per-address cap if you want HL parity.

</details>

<details><summary>Staking reward curve is flat 5% APY, not HL's inverse-sqrt-of-stake schedule, and rewards are not auto-compounded</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Reward rate is inversely proportional to sqrt(total HYPE staked) (~2.1-2.4% APY at ~400M staked), rewards are distributed each epoch and auto-compounded (re-delegated to the same validator); jailed validators earn nothing.
- **Torus evidence:** rewards.rs:188-193 computes emission = active_stake * VALIDATOR_INFLATION_APY_BPS(500) * epoch_blocks / BLOCKS_PER_YEAR regardless of total staked (types.rs:328). Rewards are credited to a pending-rewards bucket (staking.rs:798 credit_rewards) and only reach balance via explicit ClaimRewards (staking.rs:327-342); no re-delegation. Jailed exclusion is present (rewards.rs:171-174 filters Active).
- **Suggestion:** If HL parity is wanted: in distribute_validator_inflation compute apy_bps = BASE_BPS * sqrt(REF_STAKE) / sqrt(total_active_staked) using an integer isqrt on U256 (alloy U256 has root()), and in the delegator loop call delegate-equivalent credit (delegation.amount += share; val.total_delegated += share) instead of credit_rewards for an auto-compound flag. Both are economics-policy decisions; keep flat APY if intentional, but document it.

</details>

<details><summary>No protocol upgrade / coordinated hard-fork mechanism (hl-visor equivalent)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** hl-visor supervises hl-node, GPG-verifies new binaries and performs coordinated upgrades; governance (VoteGlobalAction, ~89 variants) lets validators vote on protocol-level actions (e.g. the JELLY delisting, assistance-fund burn).
- **Torus evidence:** grep for protocol_version\|hard_fork\|activation_height\|upgrade across crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs and crates/torus-node/src/*.rs finds only an unrelated comment (lib.rs:1365). ExecutionPayload (governance.rs:176-198) has no Upgrade/ProtocolVersion variant; ParameterChange only writes string keys into CF_FEE_CONFIG (governance.rs:1043-1052). ChainConfig has no activation-height table.
- **Suggestion:** Add a ChainConfig.protocol_version plus an activation-height map (torus-types ChainConfig ~lib.rs:1228) checked at block validation (reject blocks whose header.protocol_version != expected for height). Add ExecutionPayload::ProtocolUpgrade{version, activation_height, binary_hash} executed by governance that writes the schedule to state; have torus-node refuse to produce/validate past activation_height when its compiled version is older (fail-stop with a clear log). A supervisor binary with signed-release verification can come later; the on-chain schedule is the consensus-critical piece.

</details>

<details><summary>Validator-set rotation computed twice on different threads (consensus-side and exec-side) with status writes from both</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Validator set and stakes are static within an epoch and recomputed once at the epoch boundary from committed state.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:4074-4182 (epoch_validator_set_updates, called from block production/validation at :4716 and :4839) calls apply_pending_rotations and update_validator_statuses on the consensus thread, while NativeExecutor::process_epoch_boundary (native_executor.rs:6025-6104, called at app.rs:1940) recomputes the set and calls update_validator_statuses again on the exec thread. The exec fast-path comment at app.rs:1516-1517 acknowledges 'consensus-thread staking writes' at epoch boundaries as a reason to barrier. Both read StakingManager over the same DB; ordering relative to the epoch block's own Delegate/Undelegate actions (executed at :1902-1903) may differ between the two computations.
- **Suggestion:** Make one path authoritative: have process_epoch_boundary (exec, post-state of the epoch block) write the new ValidatorSet + hash into state, and have epoch_validator_set_updates on the consensus side read that committed set (or the header.validator_set_hash of the executed epoch block) rather than recomputing from live staking state. Add a test that applies a Delegate action in the epoch-boundary block and asserts both paths agree on the set.

</details>

<details><summary>Equivocation slash is buffered node-locally rather than carried as on-chain evidence</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL has no automatic slashing today; its spec says double-sign penalties would be set by stake-weighted validator vote, i.e. an on-chain, replicated decision.
- **Torus evidence:** app.rs:5147-5156 pushes PendingSlash into self.pending_slashes on the node that observed equivocation; :5109-5114 attaches them to the next committed block locally; :1532-1560 applies slash + tombstone with direct DB writes. A node that did not observe the equivocating proposals (e.g. syncing, or received only one of the two) never buffers the slash, so staking state can diverge across nodes unless staking CFs are excluded from the state root (not verified).
- **Suggestion:** Turn the evidence into a replicated action: add NativeAction::SubmitDoubleSignEvidence(DoubleSignEvidence) (slashing.rs:51-124 already has a self-verifying evidence type with verify()), have on_speculative_rollback build evidence and submit it to the mempool instead of pending_slashes, and execute the slash in NativeExecutor with a slash_record_key dedup (staking.rs:1054). Keep the local path only as a fallback metric.

</details>

*Confidence notes:* Verified by reading code: process_unbonding has no non-test caller (grep across crates excluding tests/ and _tests.rs); DowntimeTracker/DoubleSignDetector only re-exported; registration whitelist gate; full-balance self-stake; no self-stake withdrawal fn; flat 5% APY; double-sign slash wired via hotstuff callback. Not verified: whether staking column families (validators/delegations/rewards) feed the state root — grep for CF_VALIDATORS in crates/torus-state returned nothing, so the divergence risk in the equivocation-slash gap may be mitigated or may be hidden; also did not confirm whether the two epoch-rotation paths can actually disagree (flagged as design smell, not a reproduced bug). Did not inspect torus-node for any out-of-band validator health automation beyond grep. HL facts: the 21-validator top-by-stake set, 10k HYPE min self-delegation (1-year lock), 1-day delegation lockup, 7-day unstaking queue with max 5 pending withdrawals, inverse-sqrt reward formula, jail-vote mechanism, 200ms latency target, 'no automatic slashing' and hl-visor upgrade model are taken from research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md sections 3.1-3.4 and 1.x; the exact HL jail-vote quorum threshold, unjail rate-limit, and whether HL validators cast jail votes automatically vs. by operator are not spelled out in that doc and are from memory (medium confidence). I am unsure whether HL's auto-compounding re-delegates every epoch or daily.

### bridge-transfers

#### bridge-transfers — opus

Torus has no external-chain bridge. "Deposit" and "withdraw" only move value between a user's EVM account balance (CF_ACCOUNTS) and their native perp balance (CF_NATIVE_BALANCES), through Lockbox. That path is reachable from signed NativeActions and from the 0x0820 EVM precompile. HL's other pieces are all missing: validator-signed bridge withdrawals with a dispute period, deposit crediting from an external chain, withdraw fees, usdSend/spotSend between users, multi-asset spot balances and a ledger-update history. Two problems are worse than missing features. First, Lockbox converts 1:1 between 8-decimal native raw units and 18-decimal EVM wei, so value moves across at a 1e10 mismatch. Second, a withdrawal checks only `available` and ignores open cross positions, so traders can pull collateral out from under them. For new nodes, restoring from a snapshot is wired as a CLI flag, but snapshots are never created in production. P2P sync only replays blocks, and the snapshot verification only checks the root the snapshot itself recorded.

**Already present:**
- Lockbox moves value between a user's EVM and native balances, both directions, in one atomic RocksDB WriteBatch: crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:31 deposit_to_native, :78 withdraw_from_native, :128 withdraw_from_native_to (debits the sender's native balance, credits another address's EVM balance)
- NativeAction transfer variants TransferToPerp / TransferToSpot / Withdraw{amount,to}: crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:602-613, with EIP-712 typed hashing at crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:206-208,387
- Executor routes them to Lockbox: crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3293-3302 -> exec_deposit_to_native/exec_withdraw_from_native/exec_withdraw_to at :5812-5860; ActionCategory::Lockbox at :6193-6195
- EVM lockbox precompile 0x0820 with depositToNative(uint128)/withdrawFromNative(uint128): crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:36,319,953-985. Its writes are kept in a per-tx NativeStateOverlay journal, committed only if the tx succeeds and blocked under eth_call: crates/torus-evm/src/executor.rs:202-225, precompiles.rs:305-309
- Session-key scopes keep Withdraw out of Full and allow TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot under TransfersOnly: crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:246-290
- Genesis can pre-fund native balances (CF_NATIVE_BALANCES): crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:76-80,208-218; testnet/genesis-weighted-base.json:1292
- Margin engine has cross and isolated models, and cross equity includes unrealized PnL: crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:131-132,179-195,232-247 (it is just not used on the withdraw path)
- Snapshot primitives: RocksDB checkpoint create, verify (recomputes the composite EVM+native root), restore with an atomic dir swap, plus a SnapshotManager with interval and prune: crates/torus-state/src/snapshot.rs:78,111,165,224-260
- Restore from a snapshot is wired as a node CLI flag: crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:120,471-476
- P2P block sync (headers/bodies) for catch-up by replay: crates/torus-network/src/sync.rs:7-17
- Lockbox integration tests call Lockbox directly (conservation, atomicity, no rounding loss): crates/torus-integration-tests/tests/lockbox_e2e.rs:37-231

| Gap | Status | Impact | Effort | Lockstep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lockbox moves value 1:1 between 8-decimal native and 18-decimal EVM units (1e10 inflation) | buggy | critical | S | yes |
| Withdraw and TransferToSpot ignore open cross positions (collateral can be pulled from under a position) | buggy | critical | M | yes |
| EVM lockbox precompile writes may be overwritten by revm's account bundle (double-spend or mint risk) | buggy | critical | M | yes |
| No external-chain bridge (validator-signed withdrawals, dispute period, deposit crediting) | absent | high | XL | yes |
| No user-to-user native transfers (usdSend / spotSend) and no transfer between perp and spot sub-ledgers | absent | high | S | yes |
| Single collateral and no spot token balances (no multi-asset ledger, no spot token transfers) | absent | high | XL | yes |
| No ledger-update history (deposits, withdrawals, transfers) via RPC | absent | medium | M | no |
| No withdrawal fee, rate limit or lock (withdrawals are instant and free) | absent | medium | M | yes |
| Snapshot creation is never wired into block commit, and there is no P2P state sync | unwired | high | L | no |
| Snapshot verification only checks the root the snapshot itself records, not a certified root | partial | medium | M | no |

<details><summary>Lockbox moves value 1:1 between 8-decimal native and 18-decimal EVM units (1e10 inflation)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Spot<->EVM transfers in HL keep value: a token's HyperCore weiDecimals and its ERC20 decimals are linked when the token is deployed, and the system contract scales between them. 1 HYPE on Core is 1 HYPE on the EVM.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:227-247: fp_to_u256 and u256_to_fp copy the raw i128 unchanged ('Both use the same 8-decimal scale'). EVM balances are in 18-decimal wei: crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:295-298 (stake_to_power divides by 10^18), testnet/genesis-weighted-base.json:77 (treasury balance 1e27 wei). Native balances are 8-decimal FixedPoint: genesis-weighted-base.json:1295 'available': '1000000000000.0'. Result: deposit_to_native (lockbox.rs:40) debits only fp.raw wei, so 1 EVM TRS (1e18 wei) becomes 1e10 native TRS, and withdraw credits 1e-10 of the intended EVM value.
- **Suggestion:** Add a SCALE = 10^10 in lockbox.rs. Use evm_wei = fp.raw * 1e10 in fp_to_u256, and in u256_to_fp reject a wei amount that is not a multiple of 1e10, or truncate it and refund the dust. Apply the same scale in precompiles.rs:960-980 (or have the ABI take wei). Decide whether NativeAction::TransferToPerp.amount is wei or fp raw and document it in eip712.rs. Add a test that deposits 1e18 wei and asserts native = 1.0. This changes balances, so all validators must upgrade together.

</details>

<details><summary>Withdraw and TransferToSpot ignore open cross positions (collateral can be pulled from under a position)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL only lets a user withdraw or transfer out the 'withdrawable' amount: account value minus the margin required by open positions (a transfer margin requirement based on initial margin). Unrealized PnL counts against it, which blocks suicide-liquidation withdrawals (the HL deep dive notes this was partially patched).
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:86-92 and :136-142 check only native_bal.available >= amount. Cross positions hold no separate margin: crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:59-61 (isolated_margin is 0 for cross), and NativeBalance is just {available, order_margin} at position.rs:147-150. MarginEngine::cross_margin_equity (margin.rs:179) exists but neither the executor handlers (native_executor.rs:5812-5860) nor Lockbox call it.
- **Suggestion:** In exec_withdraw_from_native and exec_withdraw_to, before calling Lockbox, compute equity_after = cross_margin_equity(...) - amount. Reject when equity_after < sum(initial margin of cross positions) + order_margin, using oracle/mark prices from ctx. Also cap withdrawals at available minus max(0, -sum(uPnL)). Apply the same check in the 0x0820 precompile path. Add a test: open a cross position at 10x, try to withdraw all available, expect an error.

</details>

<details><summary>EVM lockbox precompile writes may be overwritten by revm's account bundle (double-spend or mint risk)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL's EVM<->Core transfers go through system addresses and are applied in Core's own state transition, so the ERC20/native balance accounting stays consistent.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:57-70 writes the caller's CF_ACCOUNTS balance record (raw 72 bytes) through the precompile journal. crates/torus-evm/src/executor.rs:218-225 commits that journal to state_db. Then executor.rs:229-233 runs merge_transitions/take_bundle on revm's own cached account state, which never saw the precompile's balance change. Persisting the bundle afterwards can overwrite the debit or credit. lockbox_e2e.rs:37-231 calls Lockbox directly and never runs it through an EVM tx.
- **Suggestion:** Unverified: I did not trace where the bundle is persisted. Either apply the EVM-side balance change through revm's journal (for example ctx.journal().balance_incr/transfer to or from a lockbox system address inside the precompile) instead of raw CF_ACCOUNTS writes, or apply journal writes after the bundle commit. Add an e2e test that sends an EVM tx calling 0x0820 depositToNative and checks EVM balance + native balance before and after.

</details>

<details><summary>No external-chain bridge (validator-signed withdrawals, dispute period, deposit crediting)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL's Bridge2 contract on Arbitrum takes USDC deposits, which validators observe and credit on HyperCore. A withdrawal is a signed withdraw3 action; validators sign it and submit it to the bridge, and after a 200 second dispute period it is finalized. invalidateWithdrawals and validator-set update requests are handled with 2/3 validator signatures. There is a flat 1 USDC withdraw fee.
- **Torus evidence:** No Solidity bridge contract in the repo (find *.sol returns only devnet/uniswap/*). A grep for dispute\|arbitrum\|bridge2\|withdraw_?fee\|usdc across crates/*.rs finds nothing outside tests. NativeAction::Withdraw (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:609-613) only credits an EVM address on the same chain (lockbox.rs:128). crates/torus-bridge is the consensus<->execution glue, not a cross-chain bridge.
- **Suggestion:** Add NativeAction::BridgeWithdraw{amount,dest} that locks the funds and records a pending withdrawal (new CF_BRIDGE_WITHDRAWALS keyed by nonce). Validators sign the withdrawal message with their own keys as a vote extension, and once a 2/3-stake signature set exists it is exposed over RPC for a relayer. Add a deposit-observer action (validator oracle-style attestations of external deposit events, credited at 2/3 stake) and a fee parameter in governance. Write the external contract (or reuse CCTP/IBC, as research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md:650-691 recommends).

</details>

<details><summary>No user-to-user native transfers (usdSend / spotSend) and no transfer between perp and spot sub-ledgers</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** usdSend moves perp USDC to another user's account. spotSend moves any spot token to another user. usdClassTransfer moves value between a user's own spot and perp balances. sendAsset moves value between dexes and subaccounts. All are EIP-712 user-signed actions with no gas.
- **Torus evidence:** The NativeAction enum (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-680) only has TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot (EVM<->native for the same user) and Withdraw (native -> any EVM address). There is no native->native recipient transfer. The names TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot are misleading: they call Lockbox EVM<->native (native_executor.rs:3293-3298), not a spot ledger.
- **Suggestion:** Add NativeAction::UsdSend{to, amount} with an EIP-712 hash in eip712.rs. Execute it in native_executor.rs as an atomic debit of sender.available (with the withdrawable margin check above) and a credit of to.available in CF_NATIVE_BALANCES. Keep it out of Trading-scoped sessions, as SessionScope already does for Withdraw at lib.rs:277-286.

</details>

<details><summary>Single collateral and no spot token balances (no multi-asset ledger, no spot token transfers)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HyperCore keeps per-user spot balances for many tokens (HIP-1), each with a linked ERC20, and transfers them between Core and EVM through system addresses. Perps use USDC collateral; unified/portfolio margin also lets spot assets back positions.
- **Torus evidence:** NativeBalance has one asset: {available, order_margin} at crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:147-150. Transfer and Withdraw actions carry no token or asset id: crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:602-613. The lockbox only moves the native gas token's balance from the CF_ACCOUNTS record: lockbox.rs:181-205.
- **Suggestion:** Add a token registry and a CF_SPOT_BALANCES keyed by (address, token_id). Extend the transfer actions with token_id. Link each token to an ERC20 system contract so the lockbox mints and burns ERC20s instead of writing the native balance field. Leave multi-collateral margin for later.

</details>

<details><summary>No ledger-update history (deposits, withdrawals, transfers) via RPC</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL's info endpoint has userNonFundingLedgerUpdates (deposits, withdrawals, internal transfers, spot transfers, liquidations, vault flows) with time ranges, and a websocket userNonFundingLedgerUpdates feed.
- **Torus evidence:** The torus_* RPC methods in crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:100-213 cover order book, position, balances, markets, trade history, staking and governance; there is no ledger or transfer history method. A grep for ledger\|transfer\|deposit\|withdraw in crates/torus-rpc/src finds only an eth_call test (lib.rs:2250). The lockbox handlers return a bare NativeActionResult::ok and record no event (native_executor.rs:5821,5838,5855).
- **Suggestion:** In the executor, append a LedgerEvent{height, user, kind, amount, counterparty} to an off-root CF (the same pattern as the trade-history CF used by getTradeHistoryRange). Expose torus_getLedgerUpdates(user, from, to) and a streams.rs subscription for it.

</details>

<details><summary>No withdrawal fee, rate limit or lock (withdrawals are instant and free)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Bridge withdrawals cost a flat 1 USDC. They become final after the dispute period, and there is a pause/invalidate path, so they can be stopped (used in incidents). Vault deposits have 1-day or 4-day lockups.
- **Torus evidence:** Lockbox describes its transfers as 'IMMEDIATE (not queued like CoreWriter)' (crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:3-4). There is no fee in exec_withdraw_to (native_executor.rs:5846-5860), and no pause flag or pending queue.
- **Suggestion:** Add governance params withdraw_fee and withdraw_paused. Charge the fee to the treasury in exec_withdraw_to. For the external bridge, keep pending withdrawals with an unlock height (dispute window) and a governance InvalidateWithdrawals action.

</details>

<details><summary>Snapshot creation is never wired into block commit, and there is no P2P state sync</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HL non-validator nodes start from state snapshots (abci_state files written periodically by nodes; `hl-node` can load a snapshot and replay from there) instead of replaying from genesis. Exact distribution method not verified.
- **Torus evidence:** SnapshotManager::should_snapshot/create_and_prune (crates/torus-state/src/snapshot.rs:233-251) are only called from crates/torus-integration-tests/tests/snapshot_dos_keys.rs:77-176, never from torus-node or torus-consensus. SnapshotConfig defaults to snapshot_interval: 0 (snapshot.rs:61-66). Restore is wired only as a manual CLI flag (crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:120,471-476). P2P sync is block headers and bodies only (crates/torus-network/src/sync.rs:7-17), with no state-chunk messages.
- **Suggestion:** Add --snapshot-interval/--snapshot-dir node flags. Run SnapshotManager on the post-commit path in app.rs once state_root is final, in a background thread so the checkpoint's hard links do not stall commit. Add SyncRequest::GetSnapshotManifest/GetSnapshotChunk to sync.rs so a new node can fetch the checkpoint files, then catch up with the existing block sync.

</details>

<details><summary>Snapshot verification only checks the root the snapshot itself records, not a certified root</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** A node that joins from a snapshot should anchor it to the state root in a block finalized by consensus (a QC-signed header). Otherwise a malicious snapshot provider controls the state.
- **Torus evidence:** crates/torus-state/src/snapshot.rs:111-147 recomputes the composite root and compares it to metadata.state_root, which is read from snapshot_metadata.json inside the same snapshot directory (snapshot.rs:113-116). restore_from_snapshot (snapshot.rs:165-174) accepts it on that basis. Nothing checks the root against a quorum-certified header.
- **Suggestion:** Pass a trusted (height, block_hash) into restore, from a CLI trust anchor or from a QC fetched from peers. Fetch that header over sync, check its QC against the validator set, and require header.state_root == computed_root before swapping the data dir.

</details>

*Confidence notes:* Confirmed against code: - The 1e10 decimal mismatch. The EVM side is clearly in wei (genesis divides stake by 1e18, the treasury holds 1e27), and the native side is 8-decimal. #### bridge-transfers — fable

Torus has no external-chain bridge at all: "deposit"/"withdraw" mean moving TRS between the EVM account balance and the single native perp balance via an atomic Lockbox (precompile 0x0820 or NativeAction TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot/Withdraw{to}). That path is solid (atomic WriteBatch, EVM-tx journal reverts native side effects, EIP-712, session-scope exclusion), but it is immediate, fee-less, unlimited, and crucially does not check open positions: cross and isolated position margin is never reserved out of `available`, so a trader with an open position can withdraw all collateral to the EVM. There is no usdSend-style user-to-user native transfer, no spot wallet or token layer (TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot are misnomers), no ledger-update history endpoint, and SnapshotManager exists but is never instantiated by the node (periodic snapshots and network state-sync are absent; new nodes replay from genesis, restore only from a local CLI path). Versus Hyperliquid (Arbitrum USDC bridge with 2/3-stake validator signatures, ~200s dispute period, $1 withdraw fee, withdrawable = free collateral, usdSend/spotSend/usdClassTransfer, userNonFundingLedgerUpdates, snapshot-based node bootstrap), the collateral-lock bug is the one that matters most.

**Already present:**
- Atomic EVM<->native Lockbox (deposit_to_native, withdraw_from_native, withdraw_from_native_to) using a single WriteBatch: /home/oz/projects/torus-economy/Torus-hyperBFT/crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:31-180
- Lockbox precompile 0x0820 with depositToNative(uint128)/withdrawFromNative(uint128), i128 overflow guard: /home/oz/projects/torus-economy/Torus-hyperBFT/crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:953-985; writer precompiles denied in eth_call/estimateGas: precompiles.rs:85-86

<details><summary>Withdraw / TransferToSpot does not lock collateral backing open positions</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Hyperliquid computes a per-user withdrawable amount = account value minus margin required for open positions and open orders (free collateral); withdraw/usdSend/usdClassTransfer requests above that are rejected, so a position can never be left uncollateralised by a transfer.
- **Torus evidence:** lockbox.rs:85-93 and :137-145 only check `native_bal.available < amount`; NativeBalance has only {available, order_margin} (/home/oz/projects/torus-economy/Torus-hyperBFT/crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:147-150); new positions are created with isolated_margin: ZERO and nothing is debited from `available` (position.rs:444-456; `grep isolated_margin native_executor.rs` returns nothing); cross equity is computed as `available - order_margin + uPnL` with no reservation (/home/oz/projects/torus-economy/Torus-hyperBFT/crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:179-199). exec_withdraw_to / exec_withdraw_from_native (native_executor.rs:5826-5858) call Lockbox directly with no position check. No test in lockbox_e2e.rs covers withdraw with an open position.
- **Suggestion:** In NativeExecutor::exec_withdraw_from_native / exec_withdraw_to (native_executor.rs:5826-5858) and in lockbox_precompile withdrawFromNative (precompiles.rs:971-981), compute withdrawable = cross_margin_equity(...) - total_maintenance_margin(...) (or initial margin, HL-style) using ctx.positions + current oracle prices, and reject if amount > withdrawable. Longer term, actually reserve position margin: debit `available` into a new `position_margin` field (or set pos.isolated_margin) at fill time so `available` alone is safe. Add a failing test first: open cross position, attempt full withdraw, expect InsufficientMargin.

</details>

<details><summary>No external-chain bridge (validator-signed withdrawals, dispute period, deposit observation)</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** USDC deposits land in an Arbitrum bridge contract; validators observe and credit after L2 finality (~1 min, min 5 USDC). Withdrawals are signed by validators representing 2/3 of stake, posted to Arbitrum, subject to a ~200 s dispute period (deep-dive 8.1, verified) during which withdrawals can be invalidated, then finalized.
- **Torus evidence:** grep for arbitrum\|bridge_contract\|signed_withdraw\|finalize_withdraw\|dispute_period\|withdrawal_queue across crates/ returns no hits. The only 'bridge' is crates/torus-bridge (consensus<->executor glue) and the Lockbox (lockbox.rs:1-8 header: 'bidirectional asset transfer between EVM and native balance'). NativeAction::Withdraw's `to` is an EVM Address on the same chain (torus-types/src/lib.rs:609-613).
- **Suggestion:** This is partly a design choice (TRS is the native asset, so no USDC rail is needed for day-one trading). If external collateral is wanted: add NativeAction::BridgeWithdrawRequest{amount, dest_chain_addr} that moves funds to a CF_BRIDGE_PENDING queue with block height; validators produce BLS/ECDSA signatures over (nonce, to, amount) after N blocks (dispute window) via a new consensus-side hook in torus-consensus/src/app.rs commit path; an external relayer submits to an L1/L2 contract requiring >=2/3 stake-weighted signatures; deposits are observed by validators and injected as a system action (like SubmitOraclePrices) that credits CF_NATIVE_BALANCES. Reuse staking validator set + validator_set_hash already written into SnapshotMetadata (snapshot.rs:26).

</details>

<details><summary>No user-to-user native transfer (usdSend) — only EVM-side crediting</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** usdSend transfers USDC between two users' perp accounts instantly and fee-free; spotSend does the same for spot tokens; both are first-class actions with EIP-712 types and appear in ledger history.
- **Torus evidence:** NativeAction::Withdraw{amount,to} debits sender native and credits `to`'s EVM balance (lockbox.rs:128-180, native_executor.rs:5843-5858) — the recipient must then TransferToPerp themselves. No variant credits another user's CF_NATIVE_BALANCES (torus-types/src/lib.rs:596-613 lists only TransferToPerp, TransferToSpot, Withdraw).
- **Suggestion:** Add NativeAction::NativeSend{to: Address, amount: U256} to torus-types lib.rs, an EIP-712 type in eip712.rs, include it in SessionScope::TransfersOnly, and implement Lockbox::transfer_native(state, from, to, amount) as a two-Put atomic_write on CF_NATIVE_BALANCES (same shape as withdraw_from_native_to). Apply the same withdrawable guard as gap 1.

</details>

<details><summary>No spot wallet / multi-token collateral layer; TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot are misnomers</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** HyperCore keeps separate perp and spot balances per user, with HIP-1 spot tokens (USDC, HYPE, ...) and usdClassTransfer moving USDC between perp and spot wallets; spot tokens map 1:1 to ERC20s on HyperEVM via system-address transfers; perp collateral is USDC (single-collateral cross margin).
- **Torus evidence:** NativeBalance = {available, order_margin} only (position.rs:147-150). TransferToPerp -> Lockbox::deposit_to_native (EVM->native) and TransferToSpot -> Lockbox::withdraw_from_native (native->EVM) (native_executor.rs:3293-3298); there is no spot balance CF (cf.rs:41-45 lists only orders/positions/balances/order_books/markets). grep for erc20\|hip1\|spot_token\|TokenId\|collateral_token in torus-core/torus-types/torus-bridge returns nothing.
- **Suggestion:** Either rename the variants to DepositToNative/WithdrawToEvm (cheap, honest) or introduce a CF_NATIVE_SPOT_BALANCES keyed (trader, token_id) with a TokenId registry (genesis-seeded TRS = token 0), make TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot move between spot and perp wallets, and route EVM<->native through the spot wallet. Single-collateral (TRS) cross margin can stay; HL is also single-collateral for perps.

</details>

<details><summary>Withdrawals are immediate: no fee, no delay/queue, no rate limit</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Withdrawals cost a flat 1 USDC (deep-dive 4.1), take ~5 minutes including the ~200 s dispute window, and are the natural hook for freezing an address in incident response; deposits are free.
- **Torus evidence:** exec_withdraw_* return NativeActionResult::ok(_, 1500) immediately with no fee deduction (native_executor.rs:5821, 5838, 5855); Lockbox has no fee or delay parameters (lockbox.rs:78-180); no CF for pending withdrawals (cf.rs). CF_FEE_CONFIG exists (cf.rs:69) but is not consulted on the lockbox path.
- **Suggestion:** Only meaningful once an external bridge exists (gap 2). For same-chain EVM<->native moves, HL's equivalent (system-address transfer) is also fee-less, so leave as is; if a fee is wanted, read CF_FEE_CONFIG in exec_withdraw_to and credit CF_TREASURY in the same atomic_write.

</details>

<details><summary>No ledger-update history (deposits, withdrawals, transfers, liquidations) in RPC or state</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** info endpoint userNonFundingLedgerUpdates returns a per-user time-ordered list of deposits, withdrawals, internal transfers, vault flows and liquidations; ws subscription userNonFundingLedgerUpdates streams them live.
- **Torus evidence:** Only trade history is persisted (CF_NATIVE_TRADES, CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES at cf.rs:76-77) and exposed (torus_getTradeHistory/torus_getUserTrades at torus-rpc/src/lib.rs:2439-2528; streams.rs:59-60 only has userFills). grep ledger\|userNonFunding\|transfer_history in torus-rpc returns nothing. The explorer reconstructs transfer amounts from block actions (indexer.rs:319-331) but not success/failure or resulting balances.
- **Suggestion:** Mirror the user-trades design: add CF_NATIVE_USER_LEDGER (key = trader ++ block_height ++ seq) written by the committer alongside CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES for Lockbox actions, liquidation deductions (liquidation.rs:424) and realized-PnL credits; add torus_getUserLedgerUpdates RPC and a userLedgerUpdates stream in streams.rs. Keep it out of the state root (same as trade history) so it is not consensus-breaking.

</details>

<details><summary>SnapshotManager unwired; no periodic snapshots or network state-sync for new nodes</summary>

- **Hyperliquid:** Hyperliquid nodes bootstrap from periodically published state snapshots (hl-visor fetches them) and then replay recent blocks; a new node does not replay from genesis.
- **Torus evidence:** SnapshotManager::new is only called in its own unit test (snapshot.rs:477) and in crates/torus-integration-tests/tests/snapshot_dos_keys.rs:163; grep SnapshotConfig\|snapshot_interval across torus-node, torus-consensus, torus-bridge and configs/ returns nothing. torus-consensus/src/app.rs has no snapshot hook (matches at 2715/3208/3681/4302 are unrelated uses of the word). Restore is CLI-only from a local path (main.rs:470-478); no snapshot message type in torus-network (grep snapshot\|StateSync in torus-network/src hits only peer_scoring/body_send_trace). main.rs:771 confirms archive nodes 'remain the genesis-sync source', i.e. new nodes replay from genesis via hotstuff block_sync.
- **Suggestion:** (a) Add `snapshot_interval`/`max_snapshots`/`snapshot_dir` CLI/genesis knobs in torus-node main.rs, build a SnapshotManager, and in the commit path (torus-consensus app.rs commit handler, or the committer in torus-bridge/src/committer.rs) call should_snapshot(height) then create_and_prune on a blocking thread with SnapshotMetadata{validator_set_hash from staking}. (b) Serve snapshots over HTTP from RPC (torus_listSnapshots / static file) or S3 and extend --restore-from-snapshot to accept a URL, verifying state_root against a trusted committed header before resuming hotstuff block_sync from meta.block_height.

</details>
