### reduce-only

**opus** — unwired, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

In Torus, `reduce_only` is decoded, signed, hashed, stored, persisted and shown over RPC, but nothing ever checks it. It is not checked when the order is placed, when it matches, when a stop order triggers, or when a fill updates the position. A grep over all of crates/ for reads of `.reduce_only` finds only these: copying it into Order/StopOrder, serializing it, the EIP-712 and action hash, the RPC open-order view, and one test assert. No code compares it with the trader's position. So a reduce-only order acts as a normal order: it can open, grow or flip a position, and it reserves margin like any other order. On current Hyperliquid, a reduce-only order is rejected at placement if it would increase the position. Its size is capped to the open position (so it cannot flip), and it is cancelled or cut back when the position shrinks.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1067 PlaceOrderParams.reduce_only: bool, the field in the order action
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:711 and crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:264,272 the field is only hashed and signed
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:46 Order.reduce_only and :106 StopOrder.reduce_only, the field is only stored
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:448,484 stop and stop-limit orders copy params.reduce_only into pending_stops with no check against position
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:493-536 place_order checks are PostOnly cross, market liquidity, then builds Order {reduce_only: params.reduce_only}; there is no reduce-only branch
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1314 a triggered stop passes stop.reduce_only back into place_order, still unchecked
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4906-5033 exec_place_order: reserves margin for the full quantity (reserve_for_qty, line ~4918), calls book.place_order(params.clone()) (~4968), then applies fills; it never reads params.reduce_only
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:2278,2354,2407,2472 the field is only serialized and deserialized
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1915 the field is only shown in RpcOpenOrder
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:300 the fill-update path handles open/increase/reduce/close/flip with no reduce-only context
- Grep across all crates/*.rs for `.reduce_only`, `is_reduce` and `would_flip` returns no enforcement site

**Risk:** Users and bots that rely on reduce-only take-profit and stop-loss orders, or reduce-only market closes, can end up with the position flipped or enlarged. Example: long 1, a reduce-only sell of 2 fills fully and leaves short 1. Another example: a reduce-only stop sits in the book after the position was closed by hand; it later triggers and opens a new position. Both expose the user to liquidation they never meant to take. Because reduce-only orders reserve margin, an under-margined user cannot place a closing order (Hyperliquid lets those through), which blocks de-risking. The liquidation and ADL paths (liquidation.rs) do not go through this flag, so the protocol itself is not exploited directly. Clients that copy Hyperliquid semantics will act wrongly without any error.

**Fix:** 1) At placement, in crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs exec_place_order and the batched Phase-2 place path: if params.reduce_only, load the sender's position for market_id. Reject if there is no position, or if the side would increase it (buy when long or flat, sell when short or flat). Otherwise cap the quantity to |pos.size| minus the size of the sender's other resting reduce-only orders on the same side, and skip or zero the margin reservation. 2) At match, in crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs place_order and the taker match loop: because the book does not know positions, pass a `max_reduce_qty: Option<FixedPoint>` (or a position snapshot) into place_order and clamp taker fills to it. For resting reduce-only makers, after each fill re-check the maker's position and cancel or trim their reduce-only orders that would now flip (this matches Hyperliquid's auto-cancel). 3) At stop trigger (order_book.rs:1314), apply the same check again with the live position. 4) Add tests for these cases: long 1 with reduce-only sell 2 fills only 1; reduce-only buy while long is rejected; a reduce-only stop that triggers after the position is closed is rejected. This changes execution results, so it needs a coordinated upgrade.

**Unsure:** I did not read the batched Phase-2/Phase-3 PlaceOrder path in native_executor.rs (around lines 213-411 and 3343) line by line. The grep found no `.reduce_only` read there or anywhere else, so it is unlikely to hold a check. I did not check whether torus-evm precompiles or the mempool or RPC validation layer reject reduce-only orders; the grep shows only struct literals with `reduce_only: false` in those crates. The Hyperliquid behavior described comes from public documentation, not from checking it in this session.

</details>

**fable** — unwired, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

Torus carries `reduce_only` end to end as data only: it is a field on `PlaceOrderParams` (torus-types/src/lib.rs:1067), it is signed/hashed (eip712.rs:264, lib.rs:711), copied into `Order`/`StopOrder` in the book (order_book.rs:448, 484, 535, 1314), serialized (2278/2407), and echoed back over RPC (torus.rs:1915). But nothing reads it: `exec_place_order` (native_executor.rs:4906-4990) only does margin reservation and calls `book.place_order`, with no position lookup; the native executor's sole other mention is hardcoding `reduce_only: false` for EVM-precompile-queued orders (6282); `execute_match` (order_book.rs:961) and `fill_transition` (position.rs:434) never consult it, and `fill_transition` explicitly performs "Flip: close + open opposite" (position.rs:489). Hyperliquid rejects a reduce-only order at placement if it would not reduce the current position (including against the trader's other open reduce-only orders) and caps fill size at match time so it can never flip or grow; Torus does neither. The repo's own Astra round-2 audit (docs/audits/astra-round2-2026-09-24.md:32, finding 5) already records this gap and it remains open on main.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1067 — `pub reduce_only: bool` on PlaceOrderParams (decoded/signed field)
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:264,272 — reduce_only is part of the EIP-712 struct hash (`bool reduceOnly`)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3217 — `NativeAction::PlaceOrder(params) => Self::exec_place_order(...)`
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4906-4990 — exec_place_order: margin reserve then `book.place_order(params.clone(), *sender, ctx.timestamp)`; no position read, no reduce_only reference
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6282 — only reduce_only mention in the executor: `reduce_only: false` when converting QueuedActionKind::PlaceOrder (EVM precompile path drops the flag entirely)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:448,484,535,1314 — reduce_only copied verbatim into StopOrder/Order and re-passed on stop trigger; grep shows no other read in the module
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:961 — `fn execute_match(&mut self, taker: &mut Order, is_market: bool)`; no reduce_only usage in the file outside struct copies/serde/tests
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:300,434,489 — apply_fill/fill_transition 'Handles open/increase/reduce/close/flip'; line 489 `// Flip: close + open opposite`; no reduce_only parameter
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1915 — RpcOpenOrder echoes `reduce_only: order.reduce_only` (display only)
- docs/audits/astra-round2-2026-09-24.md:32 — audit finding 5: 'matching and settlement do not enforce it. Closing orders can open or reverse exposure.'

**Risk:** A trader (or a client/UI that relies on reduce-only semantics as a safety rail, e.g. take-profit/stop-loss close orders) can have a reduce_only=true order open a new position, grow an existing one, or flip it to the opposite side: if the position is already closed by another fill before the resting reduce-only order matches, the order still executes in full and creates fresh exposure, consuming margin the user did not intend to risk. The flag also appears in the signed payload and RPC output, so clients see a guarantee the chain does not provide. Not a direct theft vector, but a silent integrity/safety mismatch vs Hyperliquid and a liquidation-risk amplifier for stop orders flagged reduce-only.

**Fix:** 1) Placement: in `exec_place_order` (native_executor.rs ~4906, and the batch/FlatAction::Place path ~3513) when `params.reduce_only`, read `ctx.positions.get_position(sender, market_id)`; reject if no position or if `params.is_buy` matches the position's side; clamp quantity to `pos.size` minus the sum of the sender's other resting reduce-only orders on that market in the same closing direction (or reject if that exceeds). 2) Match: thread a per-trader position-size cap into `OrderBook::place_order`/`execute_match` (order_book.rs:367/961) or, simpler, enforce in `apply_fill_via_caches`/`fill_transition` (native_executor.rs:4713, position.rs:434) by truncating a reduce-only taker fill at the remaining position size and cancelling the remainder; also do the placement check again when a stop re-places (order_book.rs:1307). 3) Resting reduce-only orders: on any fill that shrinks the position, cancel/shrink the trader's resting reduce-only orders that would now exceed it (same hook as the maker-side settlement). Add tests under crates/torus-bridge/tests (placement reject, partial clamp, no flip) and extend precompile queued-order decoding (native_executor.rs:6282) to carry the flag.

**Unsure:** Did not read the full body of `execute_match` (order_book.rs:961+) or `apply_fill_via_caches` (native_executor.rs:4713) line by line; the conclusion that neither checks reduce_only rests on a crate-wide grep showing zero reads of the field outside struct construction/serde/tests, plus the audit's matching finding. Did not verify the batch (`FlatAction::Place`) settlement path separately, nor whether any newer branch/worktree has a fix in progress.

</details>

### cloid-modify

**opus** — buggy, impact critical, effort M, lockstep yes

Torus stores a client_order_id: Option<u64> on each Order and carries it through place, stop and serialization, but nothing indexes it. There is no cloid-to-order map, no cancel-by-cloid action and no modify-by-cloid. Hyperliquid uses a 128-bit hex cloid with cancelByCloid and modify/batchModify that accept oid or cloid. Torus has only a single NativeAction::ModifyOrder{order_id,new_price,new_qty} and no batchModify. Its core modify keeps queue priority on a qty decrease and otherwise does cancel+insert_order without re-matching, so a price change that crosses the spread rests as a crossed book; Hyperliquid re-processes a modify as a new order that can take liquidity. Most serious: exec_modify_order takes no sender and does no ownership check, unlike exec_cancel_order, so any signer can reprice or resize any trader's resting order.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:47 Order.client_order_id: Option<u64> is stored but only copied around (lines 449,485,536,1315 and serialization at 2280-2495); grep found no index or lookup by client_order_id
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:594-598 NativeAction::ModifyOrder{order_id, new_price, new_qty} identifies the order by order_id only; the CancelOrder{order_id} enum has no cloid variant
- grep for cloid/batchModify/CancelByCloid across crates/*.rs found nothing
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:700-777 modify_order: a qty decrease is done in place and keeps its seq; any other change does cancel_order then insert_order (lines 762-775), losing priority
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1185-1210 insert_order only appends to the price level and never calls the matching engine, so a crossing reprice is not matched
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3250-3254 dispatch calls exec_modify_order(ctx, *order_id, *new_price, *new_qty) and does not pass sender
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5359-5418 exec_modify_order loops over all books and calls book.modify_order with no check of order.trader against the sender; margin deltas are charged to modified.trader (the victim)
- native_executor.rs exec_cancel_order (around line 5300) does check order.trader != *sender, which shows modify lacks the same guard
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:269 ModifyOrder is allowed under the Trading session scope

**Risk:** Exploit: any account, or a Trading-scoped session key, submits ModifyOrder{order_id: <victim oid>, new_price: Some(far off-market), new_qty: Some(large)}. The victim's resting order is repriced or resized, and margin up to the victim's available balance is locked against them. The attacker can then trade against the repriced order and steal value, or grief makers by repricing their orders so they lose queue priority. A crossing reprice also leaves the book crossed (best bid >= best ask) with no fill, which breaks the market-data invariants and the price logic built on them. Without cloid indexing, HL-style clients and bots that track orders by cloid cannot cancel or modify by cloid. A u64 cloid is also not wire-compatible with HL's 16-byte cloid.

**Fix:** 1) Security (urgent): pass sender into exec_modify_order (native_executor.rs:3250) and add the same ownership pre-check exec_cancel_order uses, returning err when order.trader != sender. Add a test where another account's modify is rejected. 2) Crossing reprice: in OrderBook::modify_order, when the price changes, run the replacement through the normal match path (or reject a post-only order that would cross) instead of insert_order. 3) Cloid: widen client_order_id to [u8;16] (needs a migration), and add an index HashMap<(Address, Cloid), OrderId> to OrderBook that is maintained in insert_order, cancel and fill-removal and rejects duplicate live cloids per trader. Add NativeAction::CancelByCloid{market_id, cloid} and let ModifyOrder/BatchModify take an OrderRef enum {Oid, Cloid}. 4) BatchModify(Vec<Modify>), executed in order with per-item results, following the PlaceOrderBatch pattern. Add new EIP-712 type encodings in torus-types lib.rs:762.

**Unsure:** Not verified: whether a pre-execution validator (mempool, or the signature or session layer) enforces ownership for ModifyOrder before the executor runs. Grep found ModifyOrder in native_executor only at dispatch and categorization, which suggests it does not. Also not verified: whether removal on fill keeps trader_orders consistent after a modify re-insert, and the exact line of exec_cancel_order (read via sed offset, around 5300). I did not run tests to show the exploit.

</details>

**fable** — partial, impact critical, effort M, lockstep yes

Torus stores a client order id as `Order.client_order_id: Option<u64>` (carried from PlaceOrderParams, EIP-712 hashed, serialized in book rows, and echoed in RPC order responses as hex), but there is no cloid index: the book's only lookup is `order_index: order_id -> OrderLocation`, and no `CancelByCloid` / cloid-keyed cancel, no cloid uniqueness check in the mempool/RPC, and no query-by-cloid exist. Modify exists as a single `NativeAction::ModifyOrder { order_id, new_price, new_qty }` (no market_id, no cloid, no batch variant; `PlaceOrderBatch` is the only batch action and there is no `CancelOrderBatch`/`BatchModify`). `OrderBook::modify_order` does in-place qty-decrease (keeps priority) and otherwise cancel + re-insert with the same order_id but a fresh queue seq (loses priority), which matches Hyperliquid's modify semantics for priority; however the re-insert goes through `insert_order` without matching, so a price modify that crosses the book rests crossed, and `exec_modify_order` performs NO sender-ownership check (unlike `exec_cancel_order`), scanning every book for the id. Hyperliquid by contrast indexes cloid (128-bit hex), supports `cancelByCloid`, `modify`/`batchModify` (oid or cloid as target, replacement order fully re-validated/matched), and rejects duplicate cloids among open orders.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:47 — `pub client_order_id: Option<u64>` on Order (stored, not indexed)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:590-594 — cancel_order looks up only `self.order_index.remove(&order_id)`; no cloid path
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:700-787 — modify_order: qty-decrease in place keeps seq; else `cancel_order` + `replacement.id = order_id; self.insert_order(replacement)` (no matching, priority lost)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1185-1197 — insert_order does push_back + order_index insert only; no cross/match
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-598 — NativeAction has PlaceOrder, PlaceOrderBatch, CancelOrder{order_id}, CancelAllOrders{market_id}, ModifyOrder{order_id,new_price,new_qty}; no cloid cancel, no batch modify/cancel
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:325,351 — EIP-712 type strings CancelOrder(uint128 orderId,...) and ModifyOrder(uint128 orderId,...) — oid-only
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3250-3254 — dispatch calls `exec_modify_order(ctx, *order_id, *new_price, *new_qty)` without sender
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5359-5421 — exec_modify_order iterates all books, no `order.trader != *sender` check (grep count of 'sender' in fn body = 0); margin delta adjusted
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5162-5175 — exec_cancel_order DOES check `order.trader != *sender`
- crates/torus-rpc/src/types.rs:337 and crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1916 — client_order_id exposed as Option<String> hex in RPC order view only
- grep across crates: no `CancelByCloid`, `batch_modify`, `BatchModify`, cloid-keyed map, or duplicate-cloid rejection found (only rate_limit.rs:263 comment mention)

**Risk:** Exploit: any signer can submit ModifyOrder for another trader's order_id (ids are sequential/guessable) and change its price/qty — exec_modify_order has no ownership check; the margin delta is then charged/released on the victim's balance. Secondary: a price modify that crosses the opposite side is re-inserted without matching, leaving a crossed book (and a non-matched order that should have filled). Feature gap: market makers cannot cancel/modify by cloid or batch-modify, so they must track Torus oids and send N separate modify actions (each a full signature/nonce), unlike Hyperliquid.

**Fix:** 1) native_executor.rs: add `sender: &Address` to exec_modify_order and reject when `old_order.trader != *sender` (mirror exec_cancel_order:5170). 2) order_book.rs modify_order fallthrough: after cancel, run the replacement through the matching path (same as place_order) instead of raw insert_order, or reject crossing modifies. 3) Cloid: add `cloid_index: HashMap<(Address,u64), OrderId>` to OrderBook maintained in insert_order/cancel_order/fills; reject duplicate (trader,cloid) in place; add `NativeAction::CancelByCloid { market_id, cloid }` and an `OrderRef { Oid(u128) | Cloid(u64) }` target for ModifyOrder; add `ModifyOrderBatch(Vec<ModifyOrderParams>)` alongside PlaceOrderBatch with EIP-712 hash + encode arms in eip712.rs/lib.rs and executor dispatch. 4) RPC: expose open-order lookup by cloid and accept cloid in cancel/modify JSON.

**Unsure:** Did not verify whether an upstream layer (mempool/RPC ingress or action validation in app.rs) rejects ModifyOrder whose order_id belongs to another sender — grep for 'sender' inside exec_modify_order body returned 0, but a pre-check elsewhere is possible though none was seen. Did not read whether order_seq is re-stamped on insert_order (test comments in book_rows_tests.rs:22 say it is). Did not check EVM CoreWriter path for a cloid/modify precompile. Hyperliquid comparison is from recall of its API docs, not fetched live.

</details>

### trigger-tpsl

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes

There is a basic stop-order mechanism: OrderType has only Limit, Market, StopMarket{trigger} and StopLimit{trigger,limit}. Stop orders go into a per-book `pending_stops` Vec. They fire only on the order book's last trade price, and only inside place_order after a fill happens (synchronously, in the same tx, at most 10 cascade rounds). Nothing evaluates triggers against mark/oracle price each block: `check_stops()` has no callers outside order_book.rs. There is also no take-profit semantics. The trigger direction is fixed: a buy fires when price >= trigger, and a sell is rejected if trigger >= price. There is no isMarket/tpsl flag and no normalTpsl/positionTpsl grouping, unlike Hyperliquid, which supports TP and SL on either side, triggers on mark price, offers positionTpsl sized to the position, and links child orders with OCO.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1071-1082 OrderType enum = Limit \| Market \| StopMarket{trigger} \| StopLimit{trigger,limit}; no tpsl kind/grouping field
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:93-108 StopOrder struct (trigger_price, limit_price, reduce_only), no tp/sl tag or parent/OCO link
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:420-456 StopMarket validated against self.last_trade_price (Buy: trigger<=ltp rejected; Sell: trigger>=ltp rejected) then pushed to pending_stops with status PendingTrigger; so a sell take-profit above market is rejected
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:576-579 trigger_stops() is called only when the current place_order produced fills
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1271-1336 trigger_stops uses last_trade_price only (not mark/oracle), at most 10 cascade iterations, and the triggered order reuses the original stop.timestamp
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:778-781 pub check_stops() exists, but grep finds no caller in crates/ outside order_book.rs (so no per-block or oracle-update sweep)
- grep for tpsl\|positionTpsl\|normalTpsl\|take_profit\|stop_loss\|grouping across crates: no TP/SL-related hits
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6182 StopMarket classified as NonGtcOrder for rate-limit category only

**Risk:** Stops fire on the last trade price, so anyone who can print a single trade on a thin book can trigger stop cascades (stop-hunting), up to 10 rounds inside one tx. Without a mark-price sweep, a stop also never fires when the oracle or mark price moves but nobody trades. Users cannot place a real take-profit (a sell stop above market is rejected), so they cannot protect positions the way they would on Hyperliquid. A stop with no position-linked sizing or OCO can open a reverse position if reduce_only is not set. A triggered order keeps its original timestamp, which may give it stale priority. Liquidation then becomes the only backstop.

**Fix:** 1) In crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs, add a trigger order type matching Hyperliquid: Trigger{trigger_px, is_market, tpsl: Tp|Sl} and an order-level grouping na|normalTpsl|positionTpsl. Update the EIP-712 encoding in torus-types/src/eip712.rs and in precompiles.rs:800; this is consensus-breaking. 2) In order_book.rs, change the trigger direction to use (tpsl, side) instead of a fixed stop direction, and store parent/OCO links in StopOrder (with persistence via stop_rows and restore_stop_row). 3) Replace the last-trade-price trigger with a mark-price sweep. In the native executor's per-block end-of-block hook (crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs, wherever mark and oracle prices are updated), call a new `book.trigger_on_mark(mark_px, block_ts)` for each market, in deterministic order. Stop calling trigger_stops from inside place_order. 4) positionTpsl: size the order to the live position at trigger time and force reduce_only; cancel the sibling when one leg fills, and cancel both when the position closes. 5) Add tests: a mark-only move with no trades fires the trigger, a TP above market is accepted, and OCO cancels the sibling.

**Unsure:** I did not read StopLimit lines 458-500 in full, but they mirror StopMarket. I did not check whether the native executor has its own mark-price stop sweep under different names (a grep for check_stops and pending_stops outside torus-core found none, and I did not grep for something like 'mark' plus 'stop'). I did not check whether the triggered order's margin is re-checked by the executor when a stop fires inside the order book (a margin bypass is possible), or whether the RPC exposes trigger fields beyond the order-type label at torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1896-1897.

</details>

**fable** — partial, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes

Torus has StopMarket{trigger} and StopLimit{trigger,limit} order types (torus-types) stored per-market in `OrderBook.pending_stops` and evaluated ONLY against `last_trade_price` of that book, and ONLY as a side effect of a fill in the same book (`place_order` -> `trigger_stops` when fills non-empty). There is no per-block sweep: `check_stops()` (the manual trigger entry) has zero callers outside order_book.rs, and nothing in torus-bridge/native_executor evaluates stops against the oracle/mark price (oracle prices are used only by liquidation/margin). Hyperliquid triggers stop/TP orders on mark price each block, supports take-profit (TP) as a distinct direction-aware trigger, and has TP/SL attached to positions (positionTpsl grouping, auto-sized to position, cancelled with the position). Torus has no take-profit semantics (a Buy stop only fires on price >= trigger, Sell on price <= trigger — stop-loss direction only; TP direction is rejected at placement via the ECON-FIND-12 check), no tpsl grouping/OCO, no position-attached TP/SL, and no RPC exposure of pending stops.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1072-1081 — OrderType enum: Limit, Market, StopMarket{trigger}, StopLimit{trigger,limit}; no TakeProfit, no tpsl grouping field in PlaceOrderParams (1060-1069)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:96-107 — StopOrder struct (trigger_price, limit_price, reduce_only); no position link / OCO sibling
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:420-490 — place_order stores stops in pending_stops; direction check rejects Buy trigger<=last_trade_price / Sell trigger>=last_trade_price (so take-profit direction is impossible)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:576-578 — trigger_stops() called only when !fills.is_empty() after a place_order in this book
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1272-1335 — trigger_stops uses self.last_trade_price (not mark/oracle), loops up to 10 cascades, re-places as Market/Limit
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:778-781 — pub fn check_stops() exists; grep shows no callers in any other crate (no per-block sweep)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5903-5960 — aggregate_oracle_prices / run_liquidation_checks use oracle prices for liquidation only; no stop evaluation; grep for run_liquidation_checks callers in bridge/src returned none
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1896-1897 — RPC only stringifies order type names; no pending-stop query endpoint found
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:234-235 — pending stops not journaled; persisted via row store (book_reader.rs:651-657), so stops do survive restarts

**Risk:** Stops never fire in a market with no trades even if mark/oracle price blows through the trigger (e.g. thin market gapping via funding/oracle) — users' stop-losses silently do nothing until someone else trades. Triggering on last_trade_price instead of mark is manipulable: a single small self-trade or wash print at a crafted price fires all resting stops in a cascade (up to 10 rounds inside one place_order), enabling stop-hunting far cheaper than on Hyperliquid. No take-profit at all, so users cannot bracket positions; no position-attached TP/SL means stops with reduce_only remain after a position is closed/liquidated by other paths and can open unintended exposure (reduce_only semantics on the re-placed order mitigate only if enforced in executor). Margin reserve for stop orders at placement (native_executor.rs:3753-3760 reserves on params.price for non-Market types) may reserve zero for StopMarket (price=0), so triggered market orders can fail margin at fire time (logged as warn, order dropped: order_book.rs:1319-1327).

**Fix:** 1) Add an end-of-block hook in torus-bridge native_executor (next to aggregate_oracle_prices / liquidation step in validator.rs step 7) that for each market loads the book and calls a new `OrderBook::trigger_stops_at(mark_price)` using the aggregated oracle/mark price (refactor trigger_stops to take a price param; keep last-trade path or drop it). 2) Extend OrderType with TakeProfitMarket/TakeProfitLimit (or a `trigger_direction` / `is_tp` flag) and relax the ECON-FIND-12 direction check accordingly; fire condition becomes direction-aware. 3) Add a `tpsl: Option<TpslGroup>` to PlaceOrderParams (normal vs position), store OCO sibling id on StopOrder, cancel sibling on fire; for position-tpsl, size from current position at fire time and cancel on position close in the executor position-update path. 4) Expose pending stops in RPC open-orders (torus-rpc/src/torus.rs) and in `orders_for_trader`. 5) Fix margin reservation for stop orders at placement (reserve on trigger price for StopMarket).

**Unsure:** Did not confirm whether validator.rs block pipeline (step 7 oracle aggregation) calls run_liquidation_checks under a different name — grep in torus-bridge/src found no callers, so a per-block liquidation sweep may also be unwired; did not read reduce_only enforcement for triggered orders in the executor; did not verify exact margin reservation behaviour for StopMarket (price=0) beyond the lines cited.

</details>

### twap-scale

**opus** — absent, impact medium, effort L, lockstep yes

Torus has no TWAP or scale orders. A case-insensitive grep for twap, scale_order and ScaleOrder across crates/*.rs finds nothing. NativeAction (torus-types/src/lib.rs:580) has PlaceOrder, PlaceOrderBatch, Cancel, CancelAll and Modify, but no TwapOrder, TwapCancel or scale action. OrderType (lib.rs:1072) is only Limit, Market, StopMarket and StopLimit. Hyperliquid has native TWAP orders (a sub-order every 30s, 3% max slippage per slice, with twapOrder/twapCancel actions) and scale orders (a range of limit orders spread across prices, built on the frontend/SDK and sent as one batch). The scale-order case is only "partial-by-proxy": PlaceOrderBatch can carry a client-built price ladder, but there is no native action for it. The block-level hook a TWAP scheduler needs already exists: the post-engine tail in torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1936-1940 runs once per native block with the block height and timestamp.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- grep -rniE 'twap\|scale.?order' crates --include=*.rs -> 0 hits
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-680 NativeAction variants: PlaceOrder, PlaceOrderBatch(Vec<PlaceOrderParams>), CancelOrder, CancelAllOrders, ModifyOrder, transfers/staking/governance/oracle/session/market admin; no TWAP or scale variant
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1072-1094 OrderType {Limit, Market, StopMarket, StopLimit}; TimeInForce {GTC, IOC, FOK, PostOnly}
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1853-1878 NativeExecContext built with header.height and header.timestamp (the deterministic clock a 30s slicer would use)
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1901-1903 execute_batch(pre_evm) then execute_batch(post_evm), the per-block user-action path
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1936-1940 per-block tail: drain_core_writer, process_governance, distribute_fees, process_epoch_boundary (this is the natural hook site)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3352 execute_batch(ctx, &[(Address, NativeAction)]) is the entry a scheduler can call with synthesized child orders
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1272-1300 trigger_stops(), a conditional-order precedent but driven by last trade price inside the book, not by time
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5923 run_liquidation_checks has no non-test caller in crates (grep), so there is no per-block liquidation sweep wired in either

**Risk:** This is a missing feature, not a safety bug. Users and integrators who expect Hyperliquid parity cannot run TWAP execution on chain. They would have to run off-chain bots that send IOC slices, which carries liveness and censorship risk and leaves no on-chain view of TWAP state or fills. If TWAP is added later, it must use header.timestamp/height (not wall clock) and a deterministic iteration order, or validators will diverge. Separately, run_liquidation_checks appears to have no production caller, so there is no per-block liquidation sweep. That should be checked independently.

**Fix:** 1) torus-types/src/lib.rs: add NativeAction::TwapOrder {market, side, total_size, duration_secs, reduce_only, randomize:false} and NativeAction::TwapCancel {twap_id}. Optionally add ScaleOrder {market, side, total_size, start_px, end_px, n_orders, skew}, which expands deterministically into a Vec<PlaceOrderParams> and reuses the PlaceOrderBatch path. 2) native_executor.rs Phase 1 (non-PlaceOrder actions): persist a TwapState {id, owner, remaining, next_slice_ts, end_ts, max_slippage_bps=300} in a new state prefix keyed by (next_slice_ts, id). 3) Add NativeExecutor::process_twaps(&mut ctx), called in app.rs between the post_evm execute_batch (line 1903) and drain_core_writer (line 1936), or just before process_governance. It scans due TWAPs ordered by (next_slice_ts, id), synthesizes IOC limit slices priced at the oracle or mid price ±3%, runs them through execute_batch so margin, matching and settlement are reused, then updates remaining/next_slice_ts (+30s) and emits events. 4) Expose TWAP status and history through torus-rpc. 5) Add determinism tests (replay parity) and slicing/cancel tests.

**Unsure:** I did not check whether an off-chain bot, SDK or frontend already has a TWAP or scale helper (only crates/*.rs was searched). I did not read execute_batch_inner, so I have not confirmed it can be safely re-entered a third time per block (execute_batch is already called twice, which suggests yes). I did not confirm the oracle or mark price accessor a slippage bound would use. I did not verify whether liquidations run per block through some path other than run_liquidation_checks.

</details>

**fable** — absent, impact medium, effort L, lockstep yes

Torus has no TWAP or scale order support anywhere in the protocol: `OrderType` is only Limit/Market/StopMarket/StopLimit and `NativeAction` has only PlaceOrder/PlaceOrderBatch/Cancel/CancelAll/Modify for the book; no parent/child order linkage, no slice scheduler, no per-slice slippage cap exists in crates/ (grep for twap|scale_order|sub_order|child_order|slippage returns zero hits in torus-core/bridge/rpc/node). The only mentions are design docs: research/PRD-trading-app.md 4.10 sketches `OrderType::TWAP { total_qty, duration_blocks, num_slices }` as "Phase 3, requires protocol work", and research/hyperliquid-deep-dive.md:333 records Hyperliquid's behaviour (30-second sub-orders, 3% max slippage per chunk). Hyperliquid additionally supports scale orders purely client-side (the frontend fans out N limit orders); Torus already has `PlaceOrderBatch` so a scale order is a frontend-only feature today, whereas TWAP needs a native per-block scheduler. The natural hook is the post-engine tail of `execute_committed_block_with` in crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs, where `process_governance`/`distribute_fees`/`process_epoch_boundary` already run per block with `ctx.block_height`/`ctx.timestamp` available.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1072-1083 — `pub enum OrderType { Limit, Market, StopMarket{trigger}, StopLimit{trigger,limit} }`; no TWAP/Scale variant
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1085-1095 — `TimeInForce { GTC, IOC, FOK, PostOnly }`; nothing time-sliced
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-600 — `NativeAction` book variants: PlaceOrder, PlaceOrderBatch(Vec<PlaceOrderParams>), CancelOrder, CancelAllOrders, ModifyOrder — no TWAP/CancelTwap

**Risk:** Feature gap, not a safety bug: users cannot submit TWAP orders, so large fills must be manual or client-side (a bot sending IOC slices every N blocks), which leaks intent and breaks if the client disconnects. Scale orders are achievable today via PlaceOrderBatch with no protocol risk. If TWAP is added naively (child orders injected without the per-slice slippage cap or without deterministic ordering relative to user actions), it could produce non-deterministic state roots across validators or let slices run through thin books; HL's 3% per-chunk cap is a specific safeguard that must be mirrored.

Scale orders: no protocol change; frontend fans out N limit orders via `PlaceOrderBatch` (one signature/nonce).

**Unsure:** Did not read `execute_batch_phases` fully nor the margin-reservation path, so whether a TWAP's unfilled remainder should reserve margin up front (HL does not) vs. per-slice is unverified. Did not check whether any RPC or torus-web frontend already does client-side scale/TWAP fan-out; the `idx` command was unavailable so searches were grep-only, though repo-wide grep for twap/scale found only research docs. Did not confirm chain block time, so the exact block count for a 30s interval is unverified.

### tif-stp

**opus** — present, impact low, effort S, lockstep no

GTC, IOC and post-only are all implemented in `OrderBook::place_order`, and so is self-trade prevention. It cancels the resting (maker) order, matching Hyperliquid's documented maker-expiring behaviour. Post-only is rejected outright (`OrderStatus::Rejected`, nothing changes) if it would cross the opposite best price, the same as Hyperliquid's ALO rejection. IOC cancels whatever is left after matching, and GTC rests it on the book. Torus also has FOK, which Hyperliquid's API does not offer; its pre-check skips the trader's own orders, so it stays consistent with self-trade prevention.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:497-505 - a PostOnly order is rejected before matching when would_cross(side, price) is true; no fills and no book change
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1217-1222 - would_cross: a buy crosses when price >= best_ask, a sell when price <= best_bid (same price counts as crossing, as in HL ALO)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:539-549 - FOK pre-check with can_fill_completely; rejected if it cannot fill completely
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:558-575 - Filled when nothing is left; Market/IOC/FOK leftover becomes Cancelled; GTC/PostOnly leftover is inserted into the book (Resting or PartiallyFilled)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1072-1086 - self-trade prevention in match_at_level: if maker.trader == taker.trader, the maker is popped from the queue, removed from the indexes, recorded in the journal, pushed to self_trade_cancels, and matching continues to the next maker
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1236-1265 - can_fill_completely skips orders where order.trader == trader, so the FOK check matches the self-trade behaviour
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:3299-3331 - tests self_trade_prevention_cancel_resting (maker cancelled, GTC taker rests) and self_trade_skips_to_next_maker
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4861-4873 - the executor collects self_trade_cancels (trader, price, remaining) for maker-side settlement and margin accounting; telemetry counter at 4119/4511/4974
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1900-1903 - RPC exposes the TIF as gtc/ioc/post_only

**Risk:** No exploit path found. Small gaps compared with Hyperliquid: (1) A post-only rejection returns only the bare Rejected status. Hyperliquid's error text says the order 'would have immediately matched', so Torus clients cannot tell an ALO rejection from other rejection reasons. (2) Self-trade prevention has one fixed mode (cancel maker). There is no per-order choice of mode, which Hyperliquid also lacks, so this matches. (3) An IOC/market taker that only hits its own orders cancels those makers and is then itself Cancelled. That is the intended behaviour, but a user can use it to wipe their own resting orders.

**Fix:** No change to consensus is needed. Optional: add a rejection-reason enum to PlaceResult (for example PostOnlyWouldCross, FokUnfillable, NoLiquidity) and pass it through the RPC layer, so clients see Hyperliquid-style error strings.

**Unsure:** Not checked: (1) whether the native executor's order-margin release for self-trade-cancelled makers is complete (only the collection code at native_executor.rs:4861-4873 was read, not the release path); (2) whether stop orders that convert to PostOnly when triggered go through the same would_cross check; (3) the batch/cancel_batch matching paths (cancel_batch.rs:730 uses IOC). Hyperliquid's self-trade prevention mode is cited from memory, not checked against its current docs.

</details>

**fable** — present, impact low, effort S, lockstep no

Torus implements all four semantics in the order book and they match Hyperliquid. GTC/PostOnly remainders rest; IOC (and FOK/Market) remainders are Cancelled; PostOnly (= HL ALO) is Rejected pre-match when `would_cross` (buy price >= best ask, sell price <= best bid), identical to HL's "post-only would immediately match" rejection; self-trade prevention cancels the RESTING maker order (popped from the queue, index/trader_orders/seq cleaned, returned whole in `self_trade_cancels`) and the taker continues to the next maker, matching HL's cancel-resting behaviour. The executor consumes `self_trade_cancels` to release the cancelled maker's margin reservation and counts them in telemetry; RPC exposes tif as gtc/ioc/fok/post_only; precompile validates tif code <= 3.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:497-505 — PostOnly rejected (OrderStatus::Rejected) when would_cross before any matching
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1217-1222 — would_cross: Buy price >= best_ask, Sell price <= best_bid (inclusive, so touching the opposite side is a cross)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:552-575 — after execute_match: Filled if remaining==0; Cancelled for Market/IOC/FOK remainder; GTC/PostOnly rest via insert_order (Resting or PartiallyFilled)

- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:3299-3328 — tests self_trade_prevention_cancel_resting and self_trade_skips_to_next_maker (taker rests / fills vs other maker)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:3019-3040 — tests post_only_rejected_when_crosses / sell variant
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4860-4900 — executor computes margin release for STP-cancelled makers from self_trade_cancels (price, remaining_qty at cancel)

Optional hardening: make `decode_time_in_force`/`decode_order_type` (native_executor.rs:6306-6321) return Result and reject unknown codes instead of defaulting, or assert the precompile validation is the only ingress. Optionally add a test that a PostOnly reject releases any taker-side margin reservation (not verified here).

**Unsure:** Did not verify that a PostOnly/FOK Rejected taker order has its own margin reservation released (native_executor.rs:417 comment says 'Rejected pre-book' is handled, not read in full). Did not verify whether the RPC/user-facing response distinguishes a PostOnly-cross rejection reason from other Rejected causes (HL returns an explicit error string). Did not check whether all CoreWriter ingress paths pass through the precompile tif<=3 validation before decode_time_in_force's GTC fallback.

### funding-engine

**opus** — absent, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes

Torus has no funding engine. Nothing samples a premium index, there is no hourly or per-block funding accrual, no funding-index or cumulative-funding state, and no funding payment is ever applied to positions. `max_funding_rate_bps` appears only as a field on `MarketParams`: it gets serialized for action hashing and EIP-712, and the wallet CLI parses it. The executor handles `UpdateMarketParams` as a no-op stub, so the cap is never stored or enforced anywhere. Hyperliquid, by contrast, samples the premium (impact bid/ask vs oracle) every 5 seconds, adds a fixed interest component (0.01% per 8h), and pays funding every hour at 1/8 of the computed 8h rate. That hourly rate is capped at 4% and settled peer-to-peer against each position's notional at the oracle price.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156-1162 MarketParams { tick_size, lot_size, max_leverage, maintenance_margin_bps, max_funding_rate_bps: u32 } (the only definition; MarketListing at 1164-1172 has no funding field)
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:828 max_funding_rate_bps serialized into the ProposalAction::UpdateMarketParams action hash
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:906 max_funding_rate_bps serialized into the NativeAction::UpdateMarketParams action hash
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:620 encode_u64(p.max_funding_rate_bps) in EIP-712 struct encoding; eip712.rs:1430 test vector value 100
- tools/wallet/src/commands/governance.rs:40,96,180-186 CLI parses max_funding_rate_bps from JSON (with a note that MarketListing lacks it)
- Other files that reference max_funding_rate_bps: crates/torus-types/src/action_hash_scratch_tests.rs and crates/torus-types/tests/eip712_vectors.rs (hash/encoding tests only)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3327-3334 comment 'AUDIT: ECON-PF-07 -- Intentional stubs'; NativeAction::UpdateMarketParams { .. } => NativeActionResult::ok("update_market_params", 0), params discarded
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5754-5755 ProposalAction::UpdateMarketParams => None // text-only for now (governance proposal has no execution payload)
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:52-62 Position has trader, market_id, is_long, size, entry_price, realized_pnl, isolated_margin, margin_type and no funding/entry-funding-index field
- grep over crates/*.rs for premium\|cumulative_funding\|funding_index\|entry_funding\|settle_funding found no non-test hits; every 'funding' hit in crates/torus-bridge/tests means account deposit balance, not perp funding
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:101-253 margin uses caller-supplied oracle_prices as the mark; no funding term in equity

**Risk:** Perp prices are not tied to the index. Without funding, nothing pushes the book price back toward the oracle, so a perp can trade at a lasting premium or discount at no cost to either side. For example, a whale can hold a large one-sided position for free while the mark/oracle gap grows. If marks track the oracle, a growing gap leaves liquidations misaligned with the book, and the insurance fund or ADL ends up absorbing the cost. Governance can also 'set' max_funding_rate_bps today, the action returns ok and nothing changes. That misleads operators and users into thinking a cap is in force. Funding PnL is missing from equity, so margin and liquidation math leaves out a cash flow that Hyperliquid users expect.

**Fix:** 1) Add per-market funding state in torus-core (new funding.rs): premium samples accumulator, cumulative_funding_index (FixedPoint, signed), last_funding_time. Store it in StateDb under a market key. 2) Add Position.entry_funding_index (with a state migration) and set it on open/increase/flip in position.rs. 3) Sample the premium in the block pipeline in native_executor.rs: once per sample interval, after matching, compute the premium from impact bid/ask (or mid) against the oracle price. 4) At each hourly boundary, compute rate = clamp(avg_premium + clamp(interest - premium, ±0.05%), ±max_funding_rate_bps) and update the cumulative index. Settle lazily per position on touch, or eagerly by iterating open positions: debit or credit pos.size * oracle * (index_now - entry_index) to the account or isolated margin. 5) Include unsettled funding in cross_margin_equity in margin.rs. 6) Implement the UpdateMarketParams stub (native_executor.rs:3332, 5754) so the market registry actually stores max_funding_rate_bps. 7) Expose funding history and predicted rate via torus-rpc (fundingHistory, predictedFundings). Write determinism tests first, including fixed-point rounding and the sign convention.

**Unsure:** I did not check torus-evm precompiles or torus-rpc for a funding endpoint; the grep covered crates/*.rs, so any 'funding' RPC naming would have shown up only if it used those words. I did not trace where oracle_prices come from or whether any mark-price smoothing exists. The Hyperliquid parameters (5s sampling, hourly payment, 4%/h cap, 0.01%/8h interest) are from my own knowledge of current Hyperliquid docs and were not checked in this session.

</details>

**fable** — absent, impact critical, effort L, lockstep yes

Torus-hyperBFT has no funding engine at all: no premium-index sampling, no funding-rate computation, no periodic (hourly) funding settlement into positions, and no cumulative funding index on Position or Market. A case-insensitive grep for "funding"/"premium" across all non-test code in every crate (torus-core, torus-bridge, torus-rpc, torus-economics, torus-state, torus-node) returns nothing except the single field `MarketParams.max_funding_rate_bps`. That field exists only as a governance payload: it is hashed into EIP-712/action bytes and parsed by the wallet CLI, but the only executor handlers for `UpdateMarketParams` are explicit stubs that return ok(0) without reading params, and the governance proposal path maps it to `None // text-only for now`. Hyperliquid, by contrast, samples a premium index (impact bid/ask vs oracle) every few seconds, computes an 8h-interest + premium rate clamped to +/-4%/hr, and pays funding hourly between longs and shorts on every open position.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**

- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:828 and :906 — max_funding_rate_bps only serialized into ProposalAction/NativeAction hash bytes
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:620 — encoded into EIP-712 struct hash; :1430 test vector
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3327-3336 — `// AUDIT: ECON-PF-07 -- Intentional stubs.` `NativeAction::UpdateMarketParams { .. } => NativeActionResult::ok("update_market_params", 0)` — params never read

### mark-oracle

**opus** — unwired, impact critical, effort L, lockstep yes

Torus has an oracle library: active validators submit prices through the `SubmitOraclePrices` action. Aggregation drops outliers more than 3x the mean absolute deviation (MAD) from the median, then takes a stake-weighted median over a 10-block window. It needs at least 3 reporters, otherwise it falls back to the last price, caps a single reporter at 10% movement, and marks the price stale after 100 blocks. That aggregation (`aggregate_oracle_prices`) and the liquidation sweep (`run_liquidation_checks`) are defined in `native_executor.rs` but nothing in the repo calls them outside tests. So no aggregated price is ever written to state, and liquidation never runs. There is no separate mark price either: margin, liquidation, PnL and the RPC `get_mark_price` all treat the raw oracle price as mark (the RPC returns mark = index = the same oracle value, or 0). Hyperliquid instead publishes a validator stake-weighted median of CEX spot prices roughly every 3 seconds, and sets mark = median(oracle + EMA of the book-vs-oracle basis, book bid/ask/last median, CEX perp mids). That mark drives margin, liquidations, TP/SL and unrealized PnL, and funding uses oracle vs impact prices.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:1 module doc: validator-submitted prices, stake-weighted median
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:21-22 DEFAULT_MAX_ORACLE_AGE=100 blocks, DEFAULT_MIN_ORACLE_REPORTERS=3; :127 aggregation_window=10
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:200-271 aggregate_price: collect window submissions, stake lookup, reject_outliers, <3 reporters -> get_last_valid_price, single-reporter 10% cap (:236-256), weighted_median, store agg row
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:274-296 get_price sets stale flag but still returns the price
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:338-355 get_last_valid_price errors StaleOraclePrice past max age
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:394-450 reject_outliers (3*MAD from simple median), weighted_median (cumulative stake >= 50%)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5685-5722 exec_submit_oracle_prices: active-validator check, then submit_price only (no aggregation)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5904-5920 aggregate_oracle_prices and :5923 run_liquidation_checks: repo-wide grep shows no callers besides definitions
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:150-164 isolated liquidation mark = oracle_prices entry; missing/zero price -> skip (Ok(None))
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:194,215 cross equity and maintenance only include positions that have an oracle price; missing price silently drops the position from both
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:446-449 position reader uPnL uses oracle agg price, Err -> 0, no staleness check; :654-665 get_oracle_price_fp ignores block age
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1608-1612 get_mark_price returns (oracle, oracle) as (mark, index), ZERO on error; last_trade_price read separately but not blended
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs: grep for MarginEngine::/funding found no margin or funding calls in the executor

**Risk:** On a live chain the aggregated oracle row is never written, because `aggregate_oracle_prices` has no caller. As a result: (1) the RPC mark price returns 0 and precompile uPnL returns 0; (2) margin and liquidation code treats positions with no price as invisible. Even with the sweep wired, a missing or stale price makes the engine skip liquidation (`Ok(None)`) rather than act on it, so bad debt can build up during an oracle outage. (3) With the sweep unwired, underwater accounts are never liquidated at all. Mark is oracle-only, with no book-mid or external-perp blend. Whoever controls more than 50% of reporting stake sets the mark directly, and the only check is the 3x MAD filter. The single-reporter 10% cap applies per aggregation, so a lone reporter can still walk the price 10% per call. The precompile and RPC paths never check staleness, so EVM contracts can read an old price without knowing it is old.

**Fix:** 1) In the block pipeline (wherever end-of-block hooks run in torus-bridge / the node commit path), call `NativeExecutor::aggregate_oracle_prices(ctx, listed_markets, active_validator_stakes)` after each block's oracle submissions. Then build `oracle_prices` from `OracleManager::get_price`, keeping only non-stale entries, and call `run_liquidation_checks`. 2) Add `mark.rs` in torus-core: mark = median(oracle + EMA150s(book_mid - oracle), median(best_bid, best_ask, last_trade)), with an optional external perp mid. Store the mark per block and pass it, instead of the raw oracle price, to margin.rs, liquidation.rs, position uPnL and RPC get_mark_price. 3) In margin.rs:194/215, treat a missing or stale price as an error, or freeze the account, instead of skipping the position. 4) In precompiles.rs:654, check the block age (or reuse `OracleManager::get_price`). 5) Add a validator sidecar that submits CEX-median prices on a fixed cadence (about every 3s, or every N blocks).

**Unsure:** My callers check was a text grep over *.rs. A macro or trait dispatch could call `aggregate_oracle_prices` / `run_liquidation_checks` under another name, though nothing turned up. I did not look for an off-chain validator sidecar that sends `SubmitOraclePrices` on a schedule, or for any non-Rust process. Funding-rate code was not found in torus-core/torus-bridge by function-name grep and may live in another crate (e.g. torus-economics). I did not check whether an order-placement margin check exists in another module that uses entry price or last trade price.

</details>

**fable** — unwired, impact critical, effort L, lockstep yes

Torus has no separate mark price: the "mark" used for PnL, margin and liquidation is simply the stake-weighted-median oracle price from `OracleManager` (crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs), with 3*MAD outlier rejection, a min-3-reporters fallback to the last stored price, a 10% single-reporter deviation cap, and a 100-block staleness flag. The RPC `get_mark_price` returns the aggregated oracle price as both mark and index (0 if none) and does not blend book mid, last trade, or external perp prices. Critically, `aggregate_oracle_prices` and `run_liquidation_checks` exist in native_executor.rs but are not called from the block pipeline in torus-consensus app.rs (which calls only execute_batch, drain_core_writer, process_governance, distribute_fees, process_epoch_boundary), and no validator-side oracle submitter exists in node/consensus crates, so in a live chain the aggregated price is never produced and liquidations never run. Hyperliquid, by contrast, has validators publish a stake-weighted median of CEX spot prices every ~3s (oracle price, used for funding) and computes a separate mark price as the median of (oracle + 150s EMA of mid-oracle basis), (median of best bid/ask/last trade on HL book), and (median of external perp mids), with mark driving liquidations and unrealized PnL.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:19-22 — DEFAULT_MAX_ORACLE_AGE=100 blocks, DEFAULT_MIN_ORACLE_REPORTERS=3; :128 aggregation_window=10 blocks
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:200-271 — aggregate_price: collects latest submission per validator in window, keeps only validators with known stake, reject_outliers (3*MAD, :393-400), falls back to get_last_valid_price if <3 reporters, caps single reporter at 10% deviation, then weighted_median; stores StoredAggregatedPrice under 'agg'+market key
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:274-295 — get_price: stale = current_block - stored.block_number > max_oracle_age (flag only, price still returned)
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:338-355 — get_last_valid_price errors StaleOraclePrice when older than max_oracle_age
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5684-5721 — exec_submit_oracle_prices: sender must be registered Active validator; submission timestamp ignored (_submission_timestamp), uses ctx.block_height/ctx.timestamp
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5902-5920 — aggregate_oracle_prices(ctx, markets, validator_stakes) wrapper
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5923-5965 — run_liquidation_checks takes external oracle_prices slice, skips market if price <= 0; no staleness check on the slice
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1902-1940 — block pipeline calls execute_batch, drain_core_writer, process_governance, distribute_fees, process_epoch_boundary; grep across crates finds no caller of aggregate_oracle_prices or run_liquidation_checks (only definition + torus-core/tests/oracle_tests.rs for aggregate_price)
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:152-172 — isolated liquidation check uses oracle_prices entry as `mark`; :192-203 execute_liquidation force-closes at oracle_price, rejects <=0
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:194,215,253 — cross-margin equity and maintenance margin use oracle_price_for(oracle_prices, market_id) as mark
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:66-77 — unrealized_pnl/notional parameterised on mark_price (whatever caller passes)
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:445-446, 590-609 — PositionReader PnL and OracleReader.getPrice read the 'agg' key directly and compute stale with DEFAULT_MAX_ORACLE_AGE
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1604-1642 — get_mark_price: mark_price = index_price = OracleManager.get_price(...).price, FixedPoint::ZERO on error; last_trade_price read separately from book; no mid/EMA blend
- grep for funding_rate in crates/*/src hits only torus-types (action/EIP-712 definitions), no funding engine in torus-core

**Risk:** Because aggregation and liquidation checks are never invoked from block execution and no node-side submitter exists, positions can never be liquidated on a live chain and PositionReader/RPC report zero or NoOraclePrice: undercollateralised accounts accrue bad debt with no backstop. Even once wired, using the raw oracle as mark (no book-mid/EMA component) means mark cannot track Torus's own book during dislocations, and a price that is stale but still returned by get_price (stale is only a flag; run_liquidation_checks takes a bare slice with no staleness check) could liquidate users at a 100-block-old price. Submission timestamp is ignored, and the 10-block aggregation window with 'latest per validator' means a validator's stale submission from up to 10 blocks ago still votes.

**Fix:** 1) Wire the pipeline: in crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs around :1937, after drain_core_writer call NativeExecutor::aggregate_oracle_prices(&mut ctx, &listed_markets, &validator_stakes) (stakes from ctx.staking), then build oracle_prices from ctx.oracle.get_price(m, height) filtering `stale==true`, and call NativeExecutor::run_liquidation_checks(&mut ctx, &traders_with_positions, &oracle_prices). 2) Add a validator-side oracle submitter task in torus-node that signs NativeAction::SubmitOraclePrices from configured external feeds each block/N blocks. 3) Introduce a mark price in torus-core (new fn in oracle.rs or a mark.rs): median of {oracle, book mid from book_reader best bid/ask + EMA basis, last trade}, persisted per block alongside 'agg'; make liquidation.rs/margin.rs take mark prices and reserve the oracle price for funding (which also needs implementing). 4) In run_liquidation_checks reject stale prices explicitly rather than relying on callers.

**Unsure:** Did not read app.rs around line 12926 (second execute path) or the full torus-node crate to be certain no alternate pipeline invokes aggregate_oracle_prices/run_liquidation_checks; grep across all crates found no callers, but a differently named wrapper is possible. Did not verify weighted_median semantics (lines 400+ of oracle.rs) or whether validator_stakes passed anywhere would be non-empty. Hyperliquid details are from my training knowledge (as of mid-2026), not re-verified against current docs within the time box.

</details>

### bands-oi

**opus** — absent, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

Torus has none of Hyperliquid's three order-size and price guards. There is no price band (HL rejects limit prices more than about 80% away from the reference price and caps market-order slippage), no per-asset open-interest cap (HL rejects orders that would add OI past an asset's cap), and no maximum order size or notional. OrderBook::place_order only checks four things: qty >= lot_size, limit price > 0, the tick multiple and 200 orders per trader per market. exec_place_order only reserves margin for limit orders. Market orders reserve no margin and have no price bound at all. Open interest is only reported through RPC (get_open_interest) and is never checked. The only size-related limit is leverage tiering: past the top tier, effective_max_leverage falls back to 1x. That is a leverage limit, not a hard cap on notional.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:376-416 place_order validation: lot_size dust, price>0, tick multiple, MAX_ORDERS_PER_TRADER_PER_MARKET; no oracle/mark distance or size check
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:28 MAX_ORDERS_PER_TRADER_PER_MARKET = 200 (only count cap)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4905-4919 exec_place_order: margin reserve only for non-market orders; market orders reserve ZERO, no slippage/price bound
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4959-4962 book auto-created via or_insert_with(OrderBook::new(market_id, ONE, ONE)) for any market_id: no listed-market or per-market limit config
- crates/torus-core/src/error.rs:7-80 CoreError has no PriceBand/OI-cap/MaxOrderSize variant (only MaxOrdersExceeded, MaxLeverageExceeded, DustOrder, InvalidTickSize)
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:46-53 effective_max_leverage tiers by notional, fallback 1x beyond top tier (implicit, not a hard notional cap)
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:247-253 10% per-block deviation clamp applies to oracle aggregation only, not to order prices
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:208,1557 get_open_interest is read-only RPC; grep found no OI enforcement anywhere in crates/

**Risk:** 1) A fat-finger or malicious market order can sweep the whole book with nothing bounding the price. With a thin book that can push last_trade_price to an extreme and trigger stop orders, and if mark or liquidation reads book prices it can cause cascading liquidations (oracle manipulation via the book, as in the HL JELLY / POPCAT incidents). 2) A limit order far from the oracle can rest or cross at an absurd price, so a counterparty taking it gets an off-market fill. 3) Without an OI cap, a whale can build unbounded OI in an illiquid asset, leaving the insurance fund or HLP-equivalent with tail risk that cannot be liquidated in an orderly way. 4) There is no absolute maximum order size, so one order can be as large as the margin allows, at up to 1x leverage past the top tier.

**Fix:** Add per-market risk params to the market config that governance registers next to tick_size and lot_size in crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs: price_band_bps (for example 8000 for a 0.2x to 5x band, plus a tighter cap for market-order slippage), max_oi_notional and max_order_notional. In NativeExecutor::exec_place_order (native_executor.rs around line 4905), before the margin reserve: (a) load the oracle or mark price and reject a limit price outside the band; (b) turn market orders into IOC orders with a limit of oracle*(1 +/- slippage_bps), as HL does; (c) reject an order whose qty*px exceeds max_order_notional; (d) compute the market's current OI from position state (the RPC get_open_interest already has the logic) and reject a non-reduce-only order that would raise OI above max_oi_notional. Add CoreError variants PriceOutOfBand, OpenInterestCapExceeded and MaxOrderNotionalExceeded. Mirror the same checks in torus-bridge/src/market_workers.rs:315, the parallel path. Stop auto-creating books for unknown market_ids.

**Unsure:** I did not read market_workers.rs:315 to see whether that path adds checks before place_order. I did not check whether there is a reduce-only flag in PlaceOrderParams. I did not trace whether mark price or liquidation uses last_trade_price, which affects how severe the manipulation path is. I did not check the RPC or EIP-712 ingress for size limits. Hyperliquid's exact numbers (the 80% band, OI cap behaviour) come from my knowledge of HL, not from this repo.

</details>

**fable** — absent, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

Torus has no order price bands (no check of limit price vs oracle/mark), no per-asset open-interest cap, and no max order size/notional check anywhere in the order path. Pre-book validation in the native executor (serial exec_place_order and the parallel phase2 prepare) checks only margin reservation (available >= price*qty/leverage); OrderBook::place_order then checks only qty >= lot_size, limit price > 0, tick alignment, and a 200-resting-orders-per-trader-per-market cap. Market orders have no slippage/price protection at all (no "slippage" symbol in core or bridge). The only notional-related logic is margin tiers (effective_max_leverage), which lowers leverage for larger positions but never rejects. Open interest exists only as an RPC read-side full-scan aggregate (get_open_interest), not as consensus state, so an OI cap cannot even be enforced without adding tracking. Hyperliquid by contrast rejects limit orders outside a band around mark/oracle (e.g. ~95% away / 1% for post-only-ish rules), caps market-order slippage (default 8%), enforces per-asset OI caps, and has per-order and per-position notional limits.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:375-410 — place_order rejects only qty < lot_size, limit price <= 0, price % tick_size != 0, and trader_order_count >= MAX_ORDERS_PER_TRADER_PER_MARKET (const = 200 at line 28); no oracle/mark comparison, no max qty/notional.
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4004-4050 — phase2_parallel_prepare: the only PrepOutcome::Reject reasons are 'insufficient margin' or a balance-load error; comment says 'Same formula as the serial loop / exec_place_order'.
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4906-4960 — exec_place_order: computes reserve_for_qty, errors only on margin/balance failure, then creates book with OrderBook::new(market_id, FixedPoint::ONE, FixedPoint::ONE) if missing; no price-band/OI/size check.
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:16-52 — MarginTier{max_notional,max_leverage} and effective_max_leverage(): a leverage ladder with an unlimited last tier (i128::MAX), returns 1x fallback — never rejects.
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1557-1585 — get_open_interest is an RPC-side full RocksDB scan of CF_NATIVE_POSITIONS summing long/short; OI is not tracked in executor state.
- grep over crates/torus-core/src and crates/torus-bridge/src for slippage\|price_protection\|max_slippage\|price_band\|oi_cap\|max_order_size\|max_notional (non-tier) — no hits.

**Risk:** Fat-finger or malicious limit orders at absurd prices (e.g. sell BTC-PERP at 1) rest or fill instantly against the book, printing wild trades that feed mark/last-price-derived logic and can trigger cascading liquidations of otherwise healthy accounts. Market orders can sweep the entire book with unbounded slippage. Without OI caps a single whale or coordinated group can build arbitrarily large positions in thin markets (bounded only by their collateral via margin tiers), making liquidation unwinds exceed book depth and pushing losses onto the insurance fund / ADL. No max order size means one order can be sized to exhaust matching-engine CPU in a block (DoS vector amplified by the 200-orders-per-trader cap being per market, not per order size).

**Fix:** 1) Add to market metadata / MarketMarginConfig (crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs or the listing struct used at native_executor.rs:5740-5750): `max_order_notional: FixedPoint`, `oi_cap: FixedPoint`, `price_band_bps: u32`, `market_slippage_bps: u32`. 2) In native_executor.rs exec_place_order (and mirror in phase2_parallel_prepare so outcomes stay a pure fn of config+params+sender balance): before reserve_for_qty, fetch the latest aggregated oracle price for params.market_id (same source exec_submit_oracle_prices/aggregate_oracle_prices write, ~5685/5904) and reject with NativeActionResult::err("place_order", "price outside band") if |price - oracle|/oracle > band; reject if price*qty > max_order_notional. 3) For market orders, pass a derived limit price = oracle*(1±slippage) into OrderBook::place_order so matching stops at that level (order_book.rs ~370). 4) Track per-market long/short OI in PositionManager state (increment/decrement where positions are opened/closed in the fill-settlement path) and reject position-increasing fills when long_oi+qty > oi_cap; expose that counter from get_open_interest (torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1557) instead of the full scan. 5) Tests in crates/torus-core/src/order_book tests + native_executor tests covering each rejection.

**Unsure:** Did not read the full exec_place_order body past the first ~85 lines or the fill-settlement path, so a post-match check (e.g. leverage-tier enforcement at fill) that indirectly bounds position size was not verified; also did not confirm whether the RPC/mempool layer (torus-rpc lib.rs) applies any pre-consensus size filter — grep found none. Exact current Hyperliquid band/slippage percentages are from memory, not verified live.

</details>

### fee-charging

**opus** — absent, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

Fills on the native CLOB charge no trading fees. `NativeExecContext.total_native_fees` is set to 0 when the context is built and nothing ever adds to it. Across all crates it shows up only at its declaration, its 0 init, a doc comment and the single read in `distribute_fees`. torus-core (order_book/, margin.rs, position.rs) has no maker or taker fee field, fee rate or fee debit. The only revenue `distribute_fees` passes on is EVM gas fees (`compute_fee_revenue(receipts)`). `RewardDistributor` then splits that by an epoch-interpolated schedule: burn (only computed, never debited or credited anywhere), validator share (commission plus pro-rata to delegators), treasury, and dev_pool as the remainder. Hyperliquid charges tiered taker and maker fees on every fill, debited from the user's USDC margin, with maker rebates for top tiers, and sends the fees to HLP and the Assistance Fund (which buys HYPE). Torus has none of this.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1373-1374 `/// Accumulated native fees during this block. pub total_native_fees: u64` (declared but never added to)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1853 `total_native_fees: 0,` set when the context is built; a grep across all crates finds no `+=` or other write
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4306-4307 doc comment: 'NO fees are touched in Phase 4 (`total_native_fees` is only read at the epoch boundary)'
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5991-6013 distribute_fees: total = total_native_fees (always 0) + total_evm_fees, then RewardDistributor::distribute_block_fees
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1580-1589 computed_fee_revenue comes only from torus_bridge::proposer::compute_fee_revenue(&validated.receipts), i.e. EVM receipts, and is 0 when there is no EVM
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1939 NativeExecutor::distribute_fees(&mut ctx, computed_fee_revenue)
- crates/torus-economics/src/rewards.rs:24-75 split is burn/validator/treasury/dev_pool by lerp_bps; burn is computed and never debited or credited ('Burn portion is destroyed (no-op)'); treasury and dev_pool go through staking.credit_balance
- grep -i 'fee' over crates/torus-core/src/order_book/, margin.rs and position.rs: zero hits; grep for taker_fee\|maker_fee\|fee_rate\|fee_bps\|TRADING_FEE across crates: no non-test hits

**Risk:** 1. Trading on the perps CLOB is free, so the chain earns no protocol revenue from its main product, and validators, treasury and dev_pool get nothing from trading.
2. With no fees, wash trading and spam orders cost nothing (only margin is locked). That fakes volume, leaderboards and any volume-based incentives, and loads the matcher for free.
3. No insurance fund or HLP-style vault is built up from fees to absorb liquidation shortfalls.
4. On the EVM side the 'burn' is never subtracted from any account. Fees are only credited, never debited from payers in this function (EVM gas is presumably already taken from the sender by revm). So the burn share simply vanishes from accounting, and that should be checked for supply consistency.

**Fix:** 1. Add maker and taker fee rates (in bps, possibly per-market or tiered) to market config in torus-core.
2. In the native executor's fill settlement (Phase 4 pass B, where balance credits are applied in sequential order), debit `notional * taker_bps` from the taker's balance and `notional * maker_bps` from the maker's (or credit a maker rebate). Add the net amount to `ctx.total_native_fees`, and make the field u128 or U256 to avoid overflow. Keep the debits in pass B's sequential order so results stay deterministic.
3. Optionally send part of the fees to an insurance or HLP-style vault address before `distribute_fees`, and make the burn share explicit, for example by crediting a burn sink address or tracking total supply.
4. Update the C3 doc comment at native_executor.rs:4306 and add tests for fee debits on fills.

**Unsure:** 1. I did not read the fill settlement code line by line (pass B credits / settle_fill). The claim that no fee is charged rests on the grep finding zero 'fee' matches in torus-core matching/margin/position and no writes to total_native_fees. A fee hidden under a name without 'fee' in it (e.g. 'commission' or 'rebate' in the bridge settle path) has not been ruled out.
2. I did not check whether EVM gas fees are debited from senders through revm, nor how the burn share affects total supply.
3. The Hyperliquid comparison comes from my own knowledge (tiered fees of about 0.045% taker and 0.015% maker at base tier, rebates, fees going to HLP and the Assistance Fund), not from a source I checked.

</details>

**fable** — absent, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

Torus charges no taker/maker trading fees on CLOB fills. `Fill` (crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:52) carries only price/qty/maker/taker; the fill-settlement paths (`apply_fill_via_caches` at native_executor.rs:4180/4200, `apply_fill` at 5042/5062) touch position and realized PnL only, with no fee debit, and there is no fee-rate constant, fee tier, or fee field anywhere in torus-core/torus-types. `ExecutionContext.total_native_fees` (native_executor.rs:1374) is initialized to 0 (line 1853) and never incremented anywhere in the repo; it is read only in `distribute_fees` (line 5995), so the end-of-block distribution (`RewardDistributor::distribute_block_fees`, rewards.rs:24, split burn/validator/treasury/dev-pool with burn as a no-op) only ever sees EVM gas fee revenue (`compute_fee_revenue` over receipts, app.rs:1588). Hyperliquid, by contrast, charges volume-tiered taker (~3.5 bps base) and maker (~1 bps, with rebates) fees on every perp fill, deducted from the account's USDC margin, with a referral/builder cut and the remainder routed to the Assistance Fund (HYPE buyback) and HLP. The project's own plan docs explicitly scope trading fees out (docs/plans/trade-streams.md:148, trade-streams-impl.md:28).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4306-4307 — comment: 'NO fees are touched in Phase 4 (`total_native_fees` is only read at the epoch boundary)'
