### fee-tiers-builder

**opus** — absent, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes

Torus-hyperBFT has no trading-fee system at all on its native CLOB. There are no maker or taker fees, no 14-day volume tiers, no maker rebates, no staking fee discounts, no referral codes and no builder codes (approveBuilderFee or a per-order builder fee). The accumulator `total_native_fees` is declared and set to 0, but nothing ever adds to it. The only fee revenue that exists is EVM gas (EIP-1559), which `distribute_fees` splits among validators, treasury, dev pool and burn. Hyperliquid, by contrast, charges taker and maker fees per fill, tiered by 14-day weighted volume. Its maker fee turns into a rebate at high maker share, HYPE staking gives a 5-40% discount, referral codes give a discount plus a kickback, and builders can charge a fee (up to 0.1% on perps) on each order once the user approves it with ApproveBuilderFee.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1373-1374 `/// Accumulated native fees during this block. pub total_native_fees: u64` — grep finds only the declaration, the init `total_native_fees: 0` (1853), a doc comment (4307) and one read (5995); there is no `+=` anywhere in crates/
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4306-4307 doc says 'NO fees are touched in Phase 4 (total_native_fees is only read at the epoch boundary)'
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5991-6014 distribute_fees adds total_native_fees (always 0) to total_evm_fees and passes the sum to RewardDistributor::distribute_block_fees
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1060-1069 PlaceOrderParams has market_id/is_buy/price/quantity/order_type/tif/reduce_only/client_order_id, with no builder field or fee field
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-680 NativeAction variants (PlaceOrder..DelistMarket) include no ApproveBuilderFee, SetReferrer or RegisterReferral action
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156-1172 MarketParams/MarketListing have no maker or taker fee fields
- grep -rniE 'builder_fee\|approveBuilderFee\|referral\|fee_tier\|rebate\|14d' over crates/*.rs: no relevant hits (the only match is a hex hash in order_book.rs:4374)
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1230-1232 the only fee config is the gas-fee split bps (fee_burn_bps, fee_validator_bps)

**Risk:** Native trading is free. The protocol earns nothing from CLOB volume, so validators, stakers and the treasury get no trading revenue. Without fees or rebates the venue cannot pay market makers to provide liquidity. Placing and cancelling orders costs nothing, so spam and wash trading are cheap; the only limits are rate limits and margin. Front ends cannot earn builder fees, so there is no reason for third parties to integrate. The staking token has no fee-discount utility. Any fee-related tokenomics in the docs or economics model (fee splits to burn and validators) only applies to EVM gas. A hidden bug: `total_native_fees` looks like it is wired up but is always 0, so anyone reading the code could think native fees already exist.

**Fix:** 1) In torus-types, add `taker_fee_bps` and `maker_fee_bps` (signed, so a negative value is a rebate) to MarketParams and MarketListing, or as a global FeeSchedule in genesis params next to fee_burn_bps. 2) In the fill path in native_executor (where each trade_id fill is credited, in pass B so ordering stays deterministic), charge the taker notional*taker_bps, credit or charge the maker, and do `ctx.total_native_fees += net`. 3) Add per-user rolling 14-day volume state: daily buckets in a ring keyed by block-time day, updated on each fill. Add a tier table that maps (volume, maker share) to bps, plus a staking-discount lookup that reads the staking module's delegated stake. 4) Builder codes: add NativeAction::ApproveBuilderFee{builder, max_fee_bps} stored per user, and an optional `builder: Option<(Address,u16)>` field on PlaceOrderParams. On fill, check it against the approved max and credit the builder. 5) Referrals: add NativeAction::SetReferrer{code} and a RegisterReferralCode action, apply a taker discount, and give the referrer a share. 6) Add RPC info endpoints: userFees, referral, maxBuilderFee. Greps for 'fee' in torus-core/src and the order_book dir found nothing relevant, which makes this unlikely. I did not check docs/ or specs for planned fee designs, or crates/torus-economics beyond the rewards.rs fee split.

**fable** — absent, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes

Torus has no trading-fee layer at all on the native CLOB: no maker/taker fee rate, no fee field in MarketParams or PlaceOrderParams, no fee deduction on fills, and the executor's `total_native_fees` counter is initialized to 0 and never incremented, so only EVM gas fees ever flow into the FeeSplitter (burn/validators/treasury/dev_pool). Consequently none of the Hyperliquid features exist: no 14d-volume fee tiers, no maker rebates, no staking-based fee discounts, no referral codes, no approveBuilderFee / per-order builder fee. The only trace is a product PRD in research/ that lists referrals as a Phase-2 wish (proposing NativeAction::SetReferralCode, CF_REFERRALS, torus_getReferralInfo). Hyperliquid, by contrast, has 14d rolling-volume tiers with maker rebates for top tiers, HYPE-staking discounts, 4%/10% referral rebates, and builder codes (approveBuilderFee action + builder:{b,f} on each order, fee capped at the approved max).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1060-1068 PlaceOrderParams has market_id,is_buy,price,quantity,order_type,time_in_force,reduce_only,client_order_id — no builder/fee field
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156-1172 MarketParams/MarketListing: tick_size,lot_size,max_leverage,maintenance_margin_bps,max_funding_rate_bps — no maker/taker fee bps

- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1231-1234 only fee params are fee_burn_bps/fee_validator_bps/fee_treasury_bps/fee_dev_pool_bps (chain-level split)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1374,1853 total_native_fees declared and set to 0; grep shows no `+=`/assignment anywhere in crates/

- grep -rniE 'fee_tier\|builder_fee\|approveBuilderFee\|referral\|rebate\|staking.*discount' --include=*.rs crates/ → 0 hits
- research/PRD-trading-app.md:560-580,849 referrals described as unbuilt Phase-2 proposal (SetReferralCode, CF_REFERRALS, torus_getReferralInfo)

**Risk:** Perp trading generates zero protocol revenue today, so validator/treasury economics rest solely on EVM gas; no builder-code mechanism means frontends/aggregators cannot be paid on-chain, and no tiers/rebates means no maker-liquidity incentive. No exploit path (nothing to abuse), but any later addition of fees changes balance arithmetic on every fill and the fee-distribution path, i.e. it is a consensus-affecting state change that needs a coordinated upgrade.

EIP-712 typed-data hashes for the new/changed actions must be versioned (eip712.rs).

Did not check torus-evm precompiles or torus-rpc for an unwired fee-quote endpoint. Hyperliquid comparison is from training knowledge, not re-verified against current docs.

### isolated-leverage

**opus** — unwired, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes

The torus-core library has a `MarginType {Cross, Isolated}` enum, an `isolated_margin` field on Position, a `MarginEngine::check_initial_margin` with separate cross and isolated branches, an isolated maintenance check and an isolated liquidation path. The native executor uses none of it. It hard-codes `MarginType::Cross` on every fill. `NativeAction` has no UpdateLeverage, UpdateIsolatedMargin or margin-mode action, `PlaceOrderParams` has no leverage field, and `check_initial_margin` is called only from margin.rs itself and from tests. Per-market `max_leverage` exists in MarketParams/MarketListing and has a governance bound of 1..=200. But `ctx.margin_configs` starts as an empty HashMap and is only filled in tests, so every market falls back to a flat 20x reserve. Hyperliquid, by contrast, lets each user choose cross or isolated per asset, set leverage per asset (`updateLeverage`), add or remove isolated margin (`updateIsolatedMargin`), and caps leverage per market (e.g. 40x/50x on BTC, lower on alts).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:45-61 MarginType {Cross=0, Isolated=1}; Position.isolated_margin and margin_type fields
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:24-52 default_margin_tiers (50/20/10/5x) and effective_max_leverage with a 1x fallback
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:60-79 MarketMarginConfig.max_leverage field (only tiers are used in lookups)
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:91-140 check_initial_margin takes a user leverage plus margin_type and has isolated and cross branches; grep finds callers only at margin.rs:164, 299 and in tests/margin_tests.rs
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4656-4663 and 4723-4730 apply_fill_cached_effect is always passed MarginType::Cross (also at :5048 and :5068)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4799-4817 order margin reserve = notional / tier max leverage, default 20 when no config; there is no user-chosen leverage
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1842 margin_configs: HashMap::new(); inserts appear only in tests/maker_margin_release_tests.rs
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-680 NativeAction variants: PlaceOrder, Cancel, Modify, transfers, staking, governance, UpdateMarketParams, ListMarket, DelistMarket. There is no UpdateLeverage or UpdateIsolatedMargin
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1060-1068 PlaceOrderParams has no leverage or margin-mode field
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1155-1171 MarketParams.max_leverage / MarketListing.max_leverage exist
- crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:571-583 max_leverage param validated as 1..=200
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:100-188 isolated liquidation path exists but can never fire because no position is Isolated
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:791-823 RPC reports cross/isolated and an isolated liq price, but isolated is unreachable

**Risk:** Users cannot isolate risk: every position is cross-margined, so one losing market can liquidate the whole account. Users cannot lower their leverage either, since reserves are always at tier max (20x by default). Leverage caps set by governance or market listing are dead config. A market listed with max_leverage=3 still trades at 20x reserve because margin_configs is empty, which risks under-collateralization on illiquid or volatile listings. The isolated liquidation and RPC code is unreachable and untested end to end, so it is likely to rot. Clients written for Hyperliquid that send updateLeverage or updateIsolatedMargin have no counterpart action.

**Fix:** 1) Populate ctx.margin_configs from MarketParams on genesis, ListMarket and UpdateMarketParams in native_executor.rs. Clamp tiers to MarketParams.max_leverage, and use `min(tier, config.max_leverage)` inside effective_max_leverage or reserve_for_qty_cfg. 2) Add per-(trader, market) user settings `{leverage:u32, margin_type}` to PositionManager state, with borsh persistence. 3) Add `NativeAction::UpdateLeverage {market_id, is_cross, leverage}`, which rejects a value above the market max and re-checks margin when a position is open. Add `NativeAction::UpdateIsolatedMargin {market_id, delta: signed FixedPoint}`, which moves funds between bal.available and pos.isolated_margin and rejects a withdrawal below initial margin. Add both to the action hash/encoding in torus-types (lib.rs ~826-916) and the RPC/EIP-712 signing paths. 4) In the executor, replace the hard-coded MarginType::Cross in the apply_fill paths (4663, 4730, 5048, 5068) with the user setting. Compute reserves with the user leverage instead of the tier max, and route the isolated initial margin into pos.isolated_margin. 5) Add tests for an isolated liquidation that does not touch cross equity, and for a leverage cap set through governance.

**Unsure:** I did not read the full apply_fill_cached_effect in position.rs to see whether it handles Isolated (e.g. allocating isolated_margin). I did not check whether genesis or node startup fills margin_configs somewhere outside native_executor.rs; grep for "margin_configs" non-get uses outside tests found only the HashMap::new() at :1842. I did not check whether an EVM precompile or CoreWriter path (precompiles.rs, CoreWriterAction) exposes leverage or margin-mode changes. I did not verify the UpdateMarketParams handler body.

</details>

**fable** — unwired, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes

Torus-core has the data model and math for cross vs isolated margin (MarginType enum, Position.isolated_margin, MarginEngine::check_initial_margin branching on margin_type, check_isolated_maintenance, isolated liquidation path in liquidation.rs), and per-market max_leverage exists in MarketParams/MarketListing and MarketMarginConfig with notional-based tiers (50/20/10/5x). But nothing reaches users: NativeAction has no UpdateLeverage or UpdateIsolatedMargin variant, PlaceOrderParams carries no leverage or margin-mode field, the native executor hard-codes MarginType::Cross on every fill, and fill_transition always writes isolated_margin = ZERO. Margin reserved per order is always notional / effective_max_leverage(notional), i.e. every trader is implicitly at tier-max leverage in cross mode with no way to choose lower leverage or isolate a position. Hyperliquid by contrast exposes updateLeverage (per asset, cross/isolated flag) and updateIsolatedMargin (add/remove USDC to an isolated position) and enforces per-asset max leverage with user-selected leverage determining initial margin.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-677 NativeAction enum: PlaceOrder, CancelOrder, ModifyOrder, transfers, staking, governance, oracle, sessions, market listing — no UpdateLeverage/UpdateIsolatedMargin variant
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1060-1069 PlaceOrderParams has market_id,is_buy,price,quantity,order_type,time_in_force,reduce_only,client_order_id — no leverage or margin_type
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156-1172 MarketParams/MarketListing carry max_leverage and maintenance_margin_bps per market
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3210-3336 execute_action dispatch: no leverage/margin arm
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4663 and :4730 apply_fill_cached_effect called with hard-coded MarginType::Cross
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4808-4818 reserve_for_qty_cfg: margin = notional / effective_max_leverage(tiers, notional), default 20x — no user leverage
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:44-62 MarginType {Cross, Isolated}; Position.isolated_margin documented '>0 for isolated, 0 for cross'
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:434-506 fill_transition always sets isolated_margin: FixedPoint::ZERO on open and flip
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:16-52 MarginTier + default tiers 50/20/10/5x, effective_max_leverage by notional
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:60-77 MarketMarginConfig {max_leverage, maintenance_factor_bps, tiers}; note max_leverage field is never used in checks read (tiers used instead)
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:92-140 check_initial_margin takes leverage + margin_type, branches Isolated (available >= initial) vs Cross (equity - maint >= initial)
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:231-249 check_isolated_maintenance uses pos.isolated_margin + uPnL vs maintenance at tier max leverage
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:100-103,149-173,224-226 isolated positions liquidated individually; isolated_margin returned to balance
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:790-792 RPC reports margin_mode cross/isolated from position.margin_type

**Risk:** Users cannot reduce leverage or isolate risk: every position is cross-margined at the tier maximum (up to 50x on small notional), so a single adverse move in one market can liquidate a trader's whole account, and there is no way to cap loss to a per-position margin allocation. Isolated code paths in margin.rs/liquidation.rs are dead code at runtime (isolated_margin always 0), so if MarginType::Isolated were ever reachable, check_isolated_maintenance would immediately report under-maintenance (equity = 0 + uPnL). No direct exploit, but a Hyperliquid-parity gap and an API/UX blocker for perps trading.

**Fix:** 1) crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs: add NativeAction::UpdateLeverage { market_id, leverage: u32, is_cross: bool } and NativeAction::UpdateIsolatedMargin { market_id, delta: FixedPoint } (plus EIP-712 hashing in eip712.rs/action_hash). 2) Add per-(trader,market) leverage/margin-mode setting stored via PositionManager (new state key) with default = tier max, cross. 3) crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs: dispatch arms in execute_action (~3210); exec_update_leverage validates leverage <= min(MarketParams.max_leverage, effective_max_leverage(tiers, current notional)) and rejects if open position would fall under initial margin; exec_update_isolated_margin moves delta between bal.available and pos.isolated_margin with maintenance check. 4) reserve_for_qty_cfg (~4808) and settle paths (~5191-5384): use user leverage instead of tier max; pass stored MarginType into apply_fill_cached_effect at 4663/4730 instead of hard-coded Cross; on isolated open, debit available into pos.isolated_margin in fill_transition/settlement. 5) margin.rs: have MarketMarginConfig.max_leverage actually cap tiers (currently unused). Tests: margin_tests.rs, position_cache_exec_tests.rs.

**Unsure:** Did not read exec_place_order body or margin_configs population (native_executor.rs ~1842, 3684, 3980-4006) to confirm MarketMarginConfig.max_leverage from MarketParams is ever enforced rather than only tiers; did not check torus-economics/governance.rs UpdateMarketParams for max_leverage changes; did not verify whether MarginEngine::check_initial_margin is called at all by the executor (grep showed only effective_max_leverage imported from margin.rs, suggesting check_initial_margin may itself be unused in the executor path). No cargo build run (read-only).

</details>

### liquidation-adl

**opus** — unwired, impact critical, effort L, lockstep yes

Torus has a LiquidationEngine in crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs with four pieces: a margin check (cross and isolated), a full force-close at the oracle price with a fixed 2.5% penalty paid to the insurance fund, an ADL that ranks traders by raw unrealized PnL, and socialize_loss (insurance fund first, then spread pro-rata by size). Its only executor entry point is NativeExecutor::run_liquidation_checks (native_executor.rs:5923), and nothing in the repo calls it, so liquidation never runs during block execution. socialize_loss is called only from tests, and the ADL result is dropped with `let _`. Compared with Hyperliquid: there is no market liquidation through the order book, no partial liquidation (the whole position is closed at the oracle price), no backstop liquidator vault (HLP), and ADL ranks by PnL alone instead of by leverage and PnL. Liquidation is not part of the per-block state transition.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5923 pub fn run_liquidation_checks: the only caller of check_liquidations, execute_liquidation and auto_deleverage. A repo-wide grep finds no other reference to run_liquidation_checks, so it has no callers.
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5964-5966 execute_liquidation(&ctx.positions, liq, oracle_price) uses the price of the market currently being looped over, not liq.market_id. check_liquidations (liquidation.rs:80-108) returns liquidations for all of a trader's markets, so on the first market's pass positions in other markets would be closed at the wrong price.
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5972 `let _ = LiquidationEngine::auto_deleverage(...)`: the ADL Result is thrown away, and if ADL does not cover the deficit nothing calls socialize_loss.
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:193-251 execute_liquidation: deletes the whole position at the oracle price (LiquidationMethod::ForceClose). There is no book order and no partial step.
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:62 the penalty is the constant DEFAULT_LIQUIDATION_PENALTY_BPS=250. The governance parameter liquidation_penalty_bps (torus-economics/src/governance.rs:641) is validated but this engine never reads it.
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:258-276 ADL ranking sorts only by unrealized PnL descending. It does not weight by leverage or margin as Hyperliquid does. There is no counterparty-side filter: any profitable position in the market is eligible.
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:314-330 ADL credits realized PnL to the deleveraged trader but never debits it from the bankrupt side or the counterparty pool, and the oracle-price close does not offset any opposite-side position.
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:344-428 socialize_loss: insurance fund first, then pro-rata by size, skipping traders with less than 2x their share. Called only from tests (liquidation.rs:644, tests/liquidation_tests.rs:150, 372).
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:59 the insurance fund is a raw key b"insurance_fund" in CF_NATIVE_BALANCES. There is no vault or backstop-liquidator account (grep for backstop/HLP/liquidator_vault finds only DA code).

**Risk:** Because no liquidation sweep runs in block execution, underwater positions are never closed. Losses can grow without limit until the clearinghouse is insolvent and losing accounts keep their exposure. An attacker can open highly leveraged opposing positions across two accounts, let one go deeply negative, and withdraw the profit from the other, leaving the deficit unbacked. If the function is wired up as it is today: positions in other markets would be closed at the wrong market's price (a direct loss of funds and something an attacker could exploit), ADL would mint PnL to winners without a matching debit (it creates value from nothing), and leftover deficits would be silently dropped because ADL errors are discarded and socialize_loss is never called.

**Fix:** 1) Call run_liquidation_checks from the per-block execution path, after oracle aggregation and before fee distribution. Use the deterministic set of traders with open positions (from a position index, not a list the caller passes in). Its results must feed into the state root. 2) In run_liquidation_checks, look up the price by liq.market_id instead of the loop's market. Better, have check_liquidations take a single market, or call it once per trader. 3) Handle the ADL result: if any deficit remains, call socialize_loss, and propagate errors instead of ignoring them. 4) Toward Hyperliquid parity: first send a reduce-only IOC market order into the CLOB, and partially liquidate in steps while the account is above a backstop threshold. If that fails, move the position and its margin to a backstop liquidator vault account at the oracle price. Run ADL as a matched close against the bankrupt position, with counterparties ranked by leverage times PnL. 5) Read liquidation_penalty_bps from governance parameters. The main files are crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs and crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs (around line 5923), plus the block-execution entry in torus-consensus/app.rs.

**Unsure:** I did not read the block-execution entry point in torus-consensus/src/app.rs to rule out a separate inline liquidation sweep. A grep for liquidat/LiquidationEngine across crates found no other path. I did not check whether ctx.margin_configs gets populated at runtime, or whether the CLOB order path does a pre-trade margin check that partly reduces the risk. My grep for callers of aggregate_oracle_prices in consensus/bridge returned nothing, so oracle aggregation may also be unwired; that is unverified. A raw 'adl' grep may have missed differently named code.

</details>

**fable** — unwired, impact critical, effort L, lockstep yes

Torus has a LiquidationEngine (crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs) with check_liquidations (cross + isolated maintenance check vs oracle price), execute_liquidation (full force-close at oracle price with a 2.5% penalty credited to an insurance fund stored under a raw key in CF_NATIVE_BALANCES), auto_deleverage (ranks counterparties by absolute unrealized PnL only, reduces most profitable first), and socialize_loss (insurance fund first, then pro-rata haircut on all positions in the market). A per-block driver exists, NativeExecutor::run_liquidation_checks (native_executor.rs:5923), but it has zero callers: the consensus block tail (torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1937-1940) runs drain_core_writer, process_governance, distribute_fees, process_epoch_boundary and never invokes liquidation or oracle aggregation; socialize_loss is called only from tests. Compared to Hyperliquid there is no market (book) liquidation, no partial liquidation / maintenance-target close, no backstop liquidator vault (HLP) takeover at 2/3 maintenance margin, no ADL ranking by PnL-and-leverage with position-size proportionality, and no oracle/mark-price distinction (liquidation uses raw oracle price). Positions are force-closed at oracle price with no counterparty, so the force-close path is settlement-only, not a market liquidation.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:72-112 check_liquidations scans traders list given by caller; cross flags all cross positions, isolated per-position
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:193-252 execute_liquidation: full close at oracle price, 250 bps penalty to insurance fund, deficit returned as remaining_deficit; no partial close, no book interaction, no liquidator counterparty
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:255-342 auto_deleverage: ranks by unrealized PnL descending only (no leverage factor), closes/partially reduces counterparties and credits them realized PnL
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:345-429 socialize_loss: insurance fund first, then pro-rata by size, skipping traders with <2x share balance; unrecoverable deficit only logged (tracing::warn)
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:59,432-449 insurance fund is a raw 16-byte value under key b"insurance_fund" in CF_NATIVE_BALANCES
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5923-5988 run_liquidation_checks: calls check_liquidations, execute_liquidation, auto_deleverage (result ignored via let _), never calls socialize_loss
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1902-1940 block execution runs execute_batch, drain_core_writer, process_governance, distribute_fees, process_epoch_boundary — no run_liquidation_checks / aggregate_oracle_prices call
- grep of repo: run_liquidation_checks appears only at its definition (native_executor.rs:5923); socialize_loss only called in crates/torus-core/tests/liquidation_tests.rs:150,372
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1842 margin_configs initialised as HashMap::new() in context construction
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:804-809 RPC liquidation_price is a 'simplified' entry_price - isolated_margin/size estimate
- docs/Torus-hyperBFT-review.md:317,319 prior audit already flagged oracle/liquidation never called and maintenance-margin formula bug

**Risk:** Undercollateralised positions are never liquidated in production blocks: a trader can hold a position whose losses exceed margin indefinitely, leaving the protocol with unbounded bad debt, while profitable counterparties' PnL is backed by nothing. Exploit path: open max-leverage long and short from two accounts, let price move, withdraw/realise the winning side's PnL (via any close-position path) while the losing side's negative equity is never force-closed or socialised. Even if run_liquidation_checks were called, the ADL result is discarded (let _) and socialize_loss is never reached, so any deficit beyond ADL coverage is silently lost; force-close at oracle price with no counterparty also means position-side open interest becomes inconsistent (closed positions have no offsetting fill).

**Fix:** 1) Wire into the block tail in crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs after execute_batch/drain_core_writer (~line 1937): gather oracle prices for listed markets (NativeExecutor::aggregate_oracle_prices, native_executor.rs:5904, also uncalled) and a trader set (positions CF iteration or a maintained index of accounts with open positions), then call NativeExecutor::run_liquidation_checks(&mut ctx, &traders, &oracle_prices); populate ctx.margin_configs from market listings (native_executor.rs:1842 currently empty, listing params at ~5751). 2) In run_liquidation_checks (native_executor.rs:5964-5985): capture auto_deleverage's result, compute remaining deficit, and call LiquidationEngine::socialize_loss for the remainder; surface errors as NativeActionResult::err. 3) Hyperliquid parity (bigger, separate): replace oracle-price force-close with a book market order (reduce-only IOC via the matching engine) first, fall back to backstop/insurance-fund takeover below ~2/3 maintenance, add partial liquidation that closes only enough to restore margin above maintenance for large positions, and rank ADL by PnL-and-leverage (profit% x leverage) rather than absolute uPnL. 4) Add an integration test in crates/torus-integration-tests that executes a block with an underwater position and asserts the position is closed and the insurance fund credited.

**Unsure:** Did not verify whether any other path (e.g. a native action variant or precompile, or the 12926 batch path in app.rs) indirectly triggers liquidation — the grep for Liquidat in torus-types and the executor found only the engine imports, and run_liquidation_checks has no callers, but I did not read the full native action enum. Did not verify whether the maintenance-margin scaling bug flagged in docs/Torus-hyperBFT-review.md:319 is fixed in margin.rs. ### margin-at-match

**opus** — unwired, impact critical, effort L, lockstep yes

MarginEngine::check_margin_at_match (margin.rs:151) and check_initial_margin (margin.rs:91) are only called from crates/torus-core/tests/margin_tests.rs; nothing on the live order path calls them. Live code paths (exec_place_order at native_executor.rs:4912-4940, batch serial path at 3753-3781, parallel prep at 4001-4030) only reserve price*qty/max_lev against `available` for non-market orders. Market orders reserve ZERO and get no margin check. The reserve is released as soon as the order fills (4970-5015), and apply_fill (position.rs:309-333) locks no collateral for the new cross position. So there is no post-fill initial or maintenance check, and the user's chosen leverage is ignored. Hyperliquid works differently: it checks initial margin for the order's new position at placement, and a fill cannot leave an account below initial margin, except for reduce-only orders and liquidations.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:151-176 check_margin_at_match just delegates to check_initial_margin; grep of crates/ shows its only callers are tests/margin_tests.rs:169-290
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4912-4919 `order_margin_required = if !is_market { reserve_for_qty(..) } else { FixedPoint::ZERO }`: market orders skip the margin check completely
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3753-3761 and 4001-4012 same zero-reserve logic for market orders in execute_batch serial and parallel prep
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4805-4818 reserve_for_qty_cfg uses the LIMIT price and tier max leverage, never the user's leverage or the cross equity/maintenance of existing positions
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4975-5015 the filled portion's reservation is released back to `available` BEFORE apply_fill; no margin check afterwards
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5025-5060 apply_fill for taker and maker with MarginType::Cross; an error only aborts on storage failure
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:309-333 apply_fill updates the position and credits realized PnL with no margin or collateral check; position.rs:386-390 credit_realized_pnl can drive `available` negative with no floor
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:507-522 the market-order guard only checks that liquidity exists
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:180-189 cross_margin_equity computes `available - order_margin`, but placement already moved the reservation out of `available` into `order_margin` (native_executor.rs:4939-4940), so resting-order margin is subtracted twice in liquidation equity (liquidation.rs:122)

**Risk:** 1) Market order with no collateral: an account with 0 balance sends a Market order of any size (up to book depth). It reserves 0, fills, and opens an unbacked cross position. If price moves in its favor it withdraws the profit. If not, the loss is socialized: the counterparty, insurance fund or ADL absorbs the negative equity, because `available` simply goes negative. 2) Cheap limit order that crosses the book: an IOC/limit SELL at a 1-tick price reserves about 1*qty/lev (near zero) but fills against bids at market price, so it gives the same unbacked short. 3) Even an honest limit order releases its reservation on fill, so an open cross position holds no margin. One account can open positions in many markets with the same `available`, as long as it keeps no resting orders. A fill can leave the account below maintenance immediately, and only the liquidation scan catches it, after the fact. 4) The user's leverage and existing cross losses or maintenance are never considered, so an account that is already under water can keep adding exposure. 5) Side bug: order_margin is subtracted twice in cross equity, so accounts with resting orders can be liquidated falsely.

**Fix:** Add one pre-match and one post-fill check in crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs (exec_place_order, the execute_batch serial path at ~3753, and the parallel prep at ~4001). (a) For Market and crossing orders, compute the reserve from a bounded worst-case price: the oracle/mark price times a slippage cap, or the book's walk price, never the user's limit price for sells. Reject when it exceeds free cross margin, computed as MarginEngine::cross_margin_equity minus total_maintenance_margin. (b) After apply_fill for the taker, call MarginEngine::check_margin_at_match with the actual fill price and the user's leverage. On failure, stop matching or revert that fill: run the check inside the matching loop per fill, or pre-size qty against free margin. Reduce-only orders and liquidations are exempt. (c) Keep initial margin locked for open cross positions, or compute it each time from position notional, so the reservation released on fill does not reappear as free `available`. (d) Fix cross_margin_equity to use `available` (or available + order_margin), not `available - order_margin`. Add tests: a 0-balance market order is rejected; a 1-tick sell limit with qty far beyond equity is rejected; a fill that would cross maintenance is blocked.

**Unsure:** Not checked: an RPC or mempool layer above the executor might pre-validate market orders against margin. I grepped only bridge/core for MarginEngine, and only tests use it there. Not read: the full apply_fill_via_caches batch settle path (native_executor.rs:4713) and fill_transition (position.rs ~430-520). Neither showed a margin check in the grep, but I did not read them in full. Not verified: whether liquidation (liquidation.rs:122-166) runs every block, which bounds how long an unbacked position lives. Not confirmed: whether withdrawals check cross equity rather than raw `available`. If they check raw `available`, positive available plus negative uPnL would allow a further drain. The double-subtraction claim rests on reading margin.rs:180-189 together with native_executor.rs:4939-4940.

</details>

**fable** — unwired, impact critical, effort L, lockstep yes

MarginEngine::check_margin_at_match (and check_initial_margin, which it wraps) exist in crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs but their only callers are crates/torus-core/tests/margin_tests.rs; no executor or settlement path invokes them. The live executor (crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs) does its own Phase-2 "reserve": limit orders lock notional/effective_max_leverage into order_margin (user leverage, cross equity, unrealized PnL and maintenance margin are all ignored), and market orders reserve exactly ZERO with no balance check at all. At settlement the entire reservation is released back to `available` as soon as the order stops resting (filled or IOC-cancelled), fills are applied via apply_fill_cached_effect which only mutates the position row, and realized PnL is added to `available` unbounded (can go negative). Hyperliquid, by contrast, checks initial margin against account value at order placement, re-checks at match for position-increasing fills (order is cancelled if it would breach), treats market orders as IOC limit orders subject to the same check, and holds initial margin against the open position.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:151-178 — check_margin_at_match defined; delegates to check_initial_margin (margin.rs:91-144)
- grep over crates/ for check_margin_at_match\|check_initial_margin\|MarginEngine:: — hits only in crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs, liquidation.rs (total_maintenance_margin) and crates/torus-core/tests/margin_tests.rs:169-290; zero hits in torus-bridge/native_executor.rs or market_workers.rs
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:414-416 — PrepOutcome::Pass doc: 'Margin reserved (possibly ZERO for market orders)'
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3999-4045 — phase2_parallel_prepare: `required = if !is_market { reserve_for_qty_cfg(..) } else { FixedPoint::ZERO }`; balance checked only `if required > ZERO`, market orders always Pass
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4914-4940 (exec_place_order, serial path) — same: 'For market orders, margin is settled at fill time (no resting order)' but nothing settles it later
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4805-4818 — reserve_for_qty_cfg: notional / effective_max_leverage(tiers, notional), default 20x; user-selected leverage, existing positions, unrealized PnL never consulted
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4614-4639 — compute_market_settle_plan: `margin_release = if !order_rests { prep.margin_reserved }` i.e. a fully filled limit order gets 100% of its reservation returned to available; no position collateral retained
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4649-4672 — fills applied with apply_fill_cached_effect(.., MarginType::Cross) only; no margin check before/after the fill
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:309-345,385-391 — apply_fill/credit_realized_pnl: position row updated, `bal.available += pnl` with no floor; no margin accounting
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4539,4734 — settlement credits realized PnL straight into available
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:507-525,552 — place_order: market order only rejected if book side empty; no margin concept in the book

**Risk:** Exploit 1 (zero-collateral market order): an address with 0 native balance submits NativeAction::PlaceOrder{order_type: Market} on any market with resting liquidity; Phase 2 passes with required=0, the book fills it, apply_fill opens a position backed by nothing. Exploit 2 (infinite leverage via limit): deposit dust, place a limit order sized to notional/max_lev <= dust; on fill the full reservation is released, so the trader holds a 20x+ position with available restored to the pre-order amount, then repeats to stack unbounded notional. In both cases adverse moves are realized as `available += pnl` going negative, i.e. bad debt socialized to counterparties/insurance; the maintenance-margin logic in liquidation.rs cannot recover collateral that was never held. Also, there is no at-match re-check, so even a correctly margined limit order filled after the account's equity has decayed (other positions' losses in the same block) goes through.

**Fix:** In crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs: (1) Phase 2 (phase2_parallel_prepare ~L3999 and exec_place_order ~L4914, plus the serial loop ~L3770): for market orders compute a reservation from a reference price (best opposite level or oracle/mark) × quantity / leverage and reject when `available < required`, instead of ZERO. (2) In compute_market_settle_plan (~L4614) and the sequential settle equivalents (~L4520, L5012): for each fill, before apply_fill_cached_effect, call MarginEngine::check_margin_at_match(positions, trader, market_id, is_buy, fill.price, fill.quantity, leverage, margin_type, cfg, oracle_prices) for the taker (and maker when position-increasing); on Err, mark the order's fill_error and void the fill (or cancel remaining) as Hyperliquid does. (3) Stop releasing the reservation on fill: move the filled portion's margin from order_margin into a per-position `isolated_margin`/locked field (position.rs:60 already has isolated_margin) rather than back to available, and only release on close/reduce. (4) Pass the oracle prices already held by the executor (ctx has margin_configs; add oracle snapshot) so cross_margin_equity is meaningful.

**Unsure:** Did not read crates/torus-rpc or torus-mempool margin references — an RPC-side pre-check could reject obviously unfunded orders before consensus, but it would not be a consensus guarantee. Did not verify reduce_only enforcement or whether the liquidation engine is wired into block execution. Did not read exec_place_order L4906-4990 in full (only grep lines) nor the serial Phase-2 loop at ~L3770; both mirror the parallel path per their comments. Did not confirm the exact current Hyperliquid at-match semantics from docs (stated from knowledge).

</details>

### vaults

**opus** — absent, impact medium, effort L, lockstep yes

Vaults are not implemented anywhere in Torus. A case-insensitive grep for vault, hlp, profit share and subaccount found nothing in any .rs file under crates/ or in specs/PRPs/docs. The NativeAction enum covers orders, transfers, staking, governance, oracle, validator, session and market actions, with no vault actions such as create, deposit, withdraw, distribute or set leader. CoreWriterAction, the EVM-to-core bridge, likewise has no vaultTransfer. Hyperliquid has a protocol HLP vault (market making plus a liquidator sub-strategy) and user vaults, each with a leader who must hold at least 5% and takes a 10% profit share. Deposits are share-accounted and there is a lockup (4 days for HLP, 1 day for user vaults). The closest thing in Torus is a single scalar insurance fund (CF_NATIVE_BALANCES key "insurance_fund"). Liquidation penalties are credited to it and losses are socialized out of it. It has no depositors, no shares, no equity accounting and no strategy.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-700 NativeAction variants: PlaceOrder, PlaceOrderBatch, CancelOrder, CancelAllOrders, ModifyOrder, TransferToPerp, TransferToSpot, Withdraw, Delegate, Undelegate, PermanentStake, ClaimRewards, TopUpSelfStake, SubmitProposal, Vote, SubmitOraclePrices, RegisterValidator, UpdateCommission, JailVote, UnjailSelf, RotateValidatorKey, CreateSession, RevokeSession, UpdateMarketParams, ListMarket, DelistMarket; no vault actions
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1181+ CoreWriterAction: only PlaceOrder, CancelOrder, Delegate, PermanentStake; no vaultTransfer
- grep -rniE 'vault\|hlp\|profit.?share' across all crates/*.rs: zero hits
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:59 INSURANCE_FUND_KEY = b"insurance_fund" stored in CF_NATIVE_BALANCES
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:209-218 liquidation penalty (DEFAULT_LIQUIDATION_PENALTY_BPS of notional) credited to the insurance fund
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:350-366 socialize_loss draws down the insurance fund first, then continues to the next loss-absorption step

**Risk:** No protocol market maker means no baseline liquidity on new or thin markets, so spreads will be wide and slippage high. Liquidations rely only on order-book takers plus the insurance fund. Hyperliquid routes liquidations through HLP's liquidator vault as a backstop. Without one, once the insurance fund is empty losses go straight to socialization or ADL, which makes Torus more prone to bad debt. Users cannot share in market-making or liquidation PnL, and nobody can run a copy-trading or managed vault. There is no direct exploit, because the feature does not exist to attack. The gap is in liquidity and solvency, not in security.

**Fix:** 1) Add a Vault state type in crates/torus-state with these fields: address (a derived pseudo-account that holds its own native balance and positions), leader, total_shares, per-depositor {shares, last_deposit_ts}, lockup_secs, profit_share_bps, leader_min_fraction_bps and is_protocol. Keep it in a new CF_VAULTS column family. 2) Add NativeAction variants: CreateVault, VaultDeposit{vault, amount}, VaultWithdraw{vault, shares}, and VaultLeaderAction{vault, inner}, so the leader trades as the vault address. CloseVault is optional. 3) In the native executor (crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs), price shares at vault equity divided by total_shares, where equity is cash plus unrealized PnL at the oracle price, using the existing position helpers. On withdrawal, enforce the lockup and the leader's minimum share, and pay the profit share on gains above the depositor's cost basis. 4) Optionally make the liquidation engine (crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs) hand failed book liquidations to a protocol HLP vault's address before socialize_loss, and seed that vault, or migrate the insurance fund into it, at genesis. 5) Add a CoreWriterAction::VaultTransfer and read-only RPC endpoints for vault details and user vault equity. All of this changes the state schema and action encoding.

**Unsure:** I only skimmed variant names and did not read every NativeAction variant body; the lines from about 700 to the end of the enum were checked only through a grep for capitalized names. I did not check the EVM precompiles (crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs) for vault-like contract logic beyond the zero-hit grep. I also did not check whether off-chain or EVM Solidity contracts in other directories (for example tools/ and research/ beyond the grep scope) sketch a vault design. The insurance-fund behavior beyond lines 209-218 and 350-366, including what socialize_loss does after the fund runs out, was not read in full.

</details>

**fable** — absent, impact medium, effort XL, lockstep yes

Torus-hyperBFT has no vault concept at all: no HLP-style protocol market-making vault, no user vaults, no deposit/withdraw-lockup/leader-profit-share/vault-equity state, and no vault actions. The word "vault" does not appear anywhere in crates/ (only in research/*.md docs, where it is explicitly listed as out of scope). The full native action surface is `NativeAction` in crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580 (orders, spot/perp transfers, withdraw, staking, governance, oracle, validator, session keys, market admin) with nothing resembling Hyperliquid's vaultTransfer / createVault / vaultModify. The only adjacent mechanism is a passive protocol-owned insurance fund in the liquidation engine (crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:59, keyed `b"insurance_fund"`) that accumulates liquidation penalties and backs socialized loss; it is not user-depositable, does not trade/market-make, has no shares/equity accounting, and has no RPC exposure.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-676 — `pub enum NativeAction` enumerates every native action (PlaceOrder/Batch, Cancel*, ModifyOrder, TransferToPerp/Spot, Withdraw, Delegate/Undelegate/PermanentStake/ClaimRewards/TopUpSelfStake, SubmitProposal/Vote, SubmitOraclePrices, validator ops, CreateSession/RevokeSession, UpdateMarketParams/ListMarket/DelistMarket); no vault variant exists

**Risk:** No safety exploit (nothing exists to exploit). Did not verify whether the insurance fund balance is seeded at genesis (crates/torus-genesis unread).

### subaccounts-agents

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes

Torus has no subaccounts, no HL-style approveAgent/API wallets, and no scheduleCancel dead-man switch. A grep for subaccount, sub_account, schedule_cancel, scheduleCancel, dead_man, approve_agent and approveAgent across crates/*.rs found nothing. What it has instead is ed25519 session keys. The owner registers one with an EIP-712-signed CreateSession{pubkey, expiry ≤ 24h, scope} and removes it with RevokeSession. There are three scopes (Trading, TransfersOnly, Full), a limit of 5 sessions per owner, and the session signs actions for the owner. The closest HL equivalent is an agent wallet, but HL agents can only trade (no transfers or withdrawals), last up to about 180 days, are named (1 unnamed + 3 named per account, plus 2 per subaccount), and are pruned when they expire. Torus's Full scope is much wider than an HL agent: it allows everything except session management, Withdraw, Delegate, Undelegate, PermanentStake and ClaimRewards.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:244-252 defines the SessionScope enum {Trading, TransfersOnly, Full}
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:264-270 Trading allows PlaceOrder, PlaceOrderBatch, CancelOrder, ModifyOrder and CancelAllOrders only (same reach as an HL agent)
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:276-285 Full is a deny-list: it blocks only CreateSession, RevokeSession, Withdraw, Delegate, Undelegate, PermanentStake and ClaimRewards. That leaves SubmitProposal, Vote, RegisterValidator, UpdateCommission, RotateValidatorKey, TopUpSelfStake, ListMarket, DelistMarket, UpdateMarketParams and SubmitOraclePrices allowed (variants at lib.rs ~582-677)
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:344-349 SessionData{owner, expiry, scope, created_at}; there is no name/label field
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:742-745 MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS = 24h and MAX_SESSIONS_PER_ADDRESS = 5
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:747-752 CreateSession and RevokeSession must use an EIP-712 signature
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:816-838 resolve_sender checks the ed25519 signature, looks up the session, then checks expiry and scope.allows, and returns session.owner
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:1137-1162 consensus batch-verify path enforces the same expiry and scope
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5598-5652 exec_create_session converts block seconds to ms, checks the 24h limit, max 5 sessions and duplicate pubkey, then calls put_session
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5655-5679 exec_revoke_session checks the owner, then calls delete_session
- crates/torus-state/src/db.rs:715-730 and crates/torus-state/src/backend.rs:85-96 count_sessions_for_owner scans the whole CF_SESSIONS column family and does NOT filter out expired sessions
- grep for prune/expired session code: the only delete_session caller is exec_revoke_session (native_executor.rs:5675), so expired sessions are never garbage-collected
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:307-308 RPC ingress uses validate_with_sessions with a state_db.get_session lookup

**Risk:** (1) Safety: a leaked Full-scope session key can do privileged things HL never lets an agent do. It can call RotateValidatorKey (take over a validator), call RegisterValidator or UpdateCommission, vote and propose in governance, list or delist markets, change market params, and submit oracle prices if the owner is an oracle or validator. TransferToPerp and TransferToSpot are also allowed. Anything that moves value or holds validator authority should need the owner's EIP-712 key. (2) Liveness/UX bug: expired sessions still count toward the limit of 5 and are never pruned. Once 5 sessions have expired, the owner cannot create a new one ("max 5 active sessions exceeded") until they send an EIP-712 RevokeSession for each old key. A bot that rotates daily sessions breaks after 5 days. (3) DoS/perf: every CreateSession does a full scan of CF_SESSIONS on the single exec thread, so cost is O(all sessions globally). Old sessions are never removed, so the scan grows without limit. (4) Missing features compared with HL: there is no dead-man switch. If a market-making bot crashes, its resting orders stay live until someone cancels them, with no scheduleCancel deadline. There are no subaccounts for isolating margin or strategies, and no named agents or per-vault/per-subaccount agents. The 24h session limit means clients must re-register with EIP-712 every day, where an HL agent lasts up to about 180 days.

**Fix:** (a) Change SessionScope::Full in crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:276 from a deny-list to an allow-list, or at least add RotateValidatorKey, RegisterValidator, UpdateCommission, TopUpSelfStake, UnjailSelf, SubmitProposal, Vote, ListMarket, DelistMarket, UpdateMarketParams and SubmitOraclePrices to the deny-list. This is a lockstep deploy, because the scope is also enforced on the consensus path (eip712.rs:1149). (b) In count_sessions_for_owner (db.rs:715, backend.rs:85), pass now_ms and skip sessions with expiry <= now. Better still, add an owner-to-sessions index key (CF_SESSIONS prefix by owner) so lookups do not scan everything, and have exec_create_session delete the owner's expired sessions before counting. (c) Add NativeAction::ScheduleCancel{time: Option<u64>}: store a per-owner deadline (allowed for Trading scope; HL requires it to be at least 5s in the future and limits the number of triggers per day), and in the block-begin hook of native_executor cancel all resting orders for owners whose deadline has passed, then clear the deadline. (d) Subaccounts: add CreateSubAccount{name}, which derives an address from (master, index), and SubAccountTransfer{sub, amount, is_deposit}, both requiring the master's EIP-712 signature. Let the session owner act for a subaccount by adding a vault_address/sub_account field to the signed envelope, then check that the sender is the master. (e) Optionally raise MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS for Trading-scope sessions and add a name to SessionData. All of these change consensus.

**Unsure:** I did not check whether the executor separately requires a validator-only signer path for RotateValidatorKey, RegisterValidator or SubmitOraclePrices. If that path rejects session-resolved senders, risk (1) is smaller; I only read SessionScope::allows. I did not check whether the RPC or an SDK exposes CreateSession to users, or whether vault-style delegation exists under another name. The HL figures (about 180-day agent validity, 1 unnamed + 3 named agents, 2 per subaccount, scheduleCancel minimum 5s and 10 triggers/day) come from my own knowledge of HL docs and were not re-checked against live HL docs in this session.

</details>

**fable** — partial, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes

Torus has a working ed25519 session-key system that is the rough analogue of Hyperliquid agent/API wallets: the owner signs an EIP-712 `CreateSession { session_pubkey, expiry, scope }` (max 24h expiry, max 5 sessions/address), the session key then signs actions with the same EIP-712 struct hash over ed25519, and `resolve_sender` checks signature, existence, expiry and a 3-value scope (Trading / TransfersOnly / Full-minus-withdraw-stake-session-ops) before mapping to the owner address; `RevokeSession` deletes it. Compared with HL, Torus scopes are finer (HL agents are all-or-nothing trading agents, cannot withdraw) but its expiry cap is far tighter (24h vs HL's up-to-180-day agent validity and named persistent agents), and there is no agent naming/listing. Subaccounts (HL `createSubAccount`/`subAccountTransfer`, trading on behalf of a sub-account via `vaultAddress`) are entirely absent, and the dead-man switch `scheduleCancel` is absent: only a synchronous `CancelAllOrders { market_id: Option }` exists, with no block-time-triggered scheduled cancel.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:244-288 — `enum SessionScope { Trading, TransfersOnly, Full }` and `allows()`: Trading = PlaceOrder/PlaceOrderBatch/CancelOrder/ModifyOrder/CancelAllOrders; Full excludes CreateSession/RevokeSession/Withdraw/Delegate/Undelegate/PermanentStake/ClaimRewards
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:344-349 — `struct SessionData { owner, expiry, scope, created_at }` persisted in state DB
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:742-745 — `MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS = 24h`, `MAX_SESSIONS_PER_ADDRESS = 5`
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:801-840 — `resolve_sender`: for `ActionSignature::Session` rejects `requires_eip712` actions, verifies ed25519 over EIP-712 signing hash, looks up session, checks expiry and `scope.allows`, returns `session.owner`
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3318-3324 — dispatch of CreateSession/RevokeSession to exec_create_session/exec_revoke_session
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5598-5675 — exec_create_session enforces expiry <= now+24h, not already expired, per-address count cap, no pubkey collision; exec_revoke_session checks ownership then delete_session
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:591 — `NativeAction::CancelAllOrders { market_id }` is the only cancel-all primitive; grep across crates/ for scheduleCancel/schedule_cancel/dead-man returned zero hits
- grep across crates/ for subaccount/sub_account/SubAccount returned zero non-test hits (only files matching were app.rs/eip712.rs session tests and bridge session_key_tests.rs)
- crates/torus-bridge/tests/session_key_tests.rs:1-60 — dedicated lifecycle/authorization test suite exists for session keys

**Risk:** Without scheduleCancel, a market maker whose bot/connection dies keeps resting quotes live until manual intervention — the exact scenario HL's dead-man switch exists for; on a volatile L1 this is the main user-facing safety gap. Without subaccounts, users cannot isolate margin/strategies under one master key, so a compromised or over-scoped session key exposes the whole account. The 24h session expiry forces daily re-signing by the master key, which pushes integrators to keep the master key hot (worse security than HL's long-lived agents). No exploit path identified in the session logic itself: scope and expiry are checked on the consensus/exec path, and session keys cannot create sessions, withdraw or stake.

**Fix:** 1) scheduleCancel: add `NativeAction::ScheduleCancel { time_ms: Option<u64> }` in crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs (+ hash in eip712.rs, allow in SessionScope::Trading), store `scheduled_cancel_at` per address in state, and in the per-block hook in crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs (where funding/liquidation sweeps run) iterate due entries and reuse the existing CancelAllOrders path (line ~3247); mirror HL rules (min +5s in future, clear when None, rate-limit). 2) Subaccounts: add `CreateSubAccount { name }` / `SubAccountTransfer` actions and an optional `on_behalf_of: Option<Address>` on the signed action envelope resolved in `resolve_sender` (eip712.rs:801) via a `subaccount -> master` map; keep margin/positions keyed by the sub address. 3) Agent parity: raise MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS (or make it a config constant) toward HL's 180d and add an optional `name` to SessionData plus an RPC query to list an address's sessions.

**Unsure:** Did not read the per-block executor hook to confirm where a scheduled-cancel sweep would best attach; did not verify whether any RPC method exposes session listing (grep of crates/torus-rpc for 'session' hit only test code); did not check the roadmap doc contents for planned subaccount/scheduleCancel work (grep returned no hits). HL comparison figures (agent validity up to 180 days, scheduleCancel semantics) are from memory, not fetched.

</details>

### listing-governance

**opus** — stub, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes

Torus has no working market lifecycle. The native ListMarket, DelistMarket and UpdateMarketParams actions in the executor are explicit no-op stubs that return ok with no state change (marked AUDIT ECON-PF-07). The only path that writes a market at runtime is a governance ListMarket proposal. It hardcodes market_id 0 ("auto-assigned", but nothing assigns it), so every listing writes to the same CF_NATIVE_MARKETS key 0 and overwrites the previous one. It also fills initial_margin from maintenance_margin_bps. Governance Delist and UpdateMarketParams map to None and are text-only. In practice, markets exist only if seeded at genesis into CF_NATIVE_MARKETS, which is off the consensus root. Hyperliquid, by contrast, has validator-voted listing and delisting, a margin-table and leverage update path, and HIP-3 permissionless builder-deployed perps through a Dutch gas auction with a staking requirement. None of these exist in Torus: there is no deploy, auction or HIP-3 code.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3327-3336 - comment 'Admin (governance-gated, stubs)... AUDIT: ECON-PF-07 -- Intentional stubs'. UpdateMarketParams, ListMarket and DelistMarket each return NativeActionResult::ok(..., 0) with no state change
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5744-5752 - ProposalAction::ListMarket becomes ExecutionPayload::MarketListing { market_id: 0, // auto-assigned ... initial_margin: from listing.maintenance_margin_bps }
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5754-5756 - ProposalAction::UpdateMarketParams \| DelistMarket => None // text-only for now
- crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:1080-1107 - the MarketListing execute writes key = market_id.to_be_bytes() straight into CF_NATIVE_MARKETS with no id allocation, no existence or collision check, and no order-book or risk-param initialisation
- crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:424-452 - genesis seeds markets into CF_NATIVE_MARKETS, which the comment says is 'OFF the consensus native state root' and drives RPC listings and order validation
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:250-266 - validate_known_markets rejects orders for ids with no CF_NATIVE_MARKETS row at the RPC layer only. The comment notes the exec-side phantom-book fix (native_executor.rs:656) is a separate consensus item
- grep for HIP-3/hip3/DeployAuction/PerpDeploy across crates and docs returned no matches

**Risk:** (1) Any passed governance ListMarket proposal writes to market 0 and silently overwrites the existing market 0 row, changing its base/quote, tick and lot sizes, and margin. That can corrupt a live market, and a second listing proposal replaces the first. (2) initial_margin is taken from maintenance_margin_bps, which understates the initial margin and allows more leverage than intended. (3) CF_NATIVE_MARKETS is off the consensus state root, so a governance listing is applied without being committed to the root. Validators that diverge on it (for example a node restored from a snapshot) are not detected. (4) No market can be delisted or have its params changed: signed native admin actions report success but do nothing, which misleads clients and explorers. (5) Order validation against the market registry is RPC-only, so orders that bypass RPC can still create phantom books at execution. (6) There is no permissioned or permissionless path, like HIP-3, to add a market in production short of a new genesis.

**Fix:** 1. Add a deterministic market-id allocator: a NEXT_MARKET_ID counter row, or max(existing)+1. Use it in governance.rs execute (the MarketListing arm at line 1080), and reject listings whose id already exists. Drop the hardcoded market_id: 0 at native_executor.rs:5745.
2. Carry initial_margin_bps and maintenance_margin_bps separately in the MarketListing payload. This needs MarketListing in torus-types/src/lib.rs:1165 plus a migration of the payload borsh.
3. Implement ExecutionPayload::MarketDelist (set a status flag and run a cancel-all and settle path) and ExecutionPayload::UpdateMarketParams in governance.rs, and map them at native_executor.rs:5754.
4. Make the native admin actions at native_executor.rs:3332-3336 return an error ("governance-only") instead of a fake ok, or route them through governance authority.
5. Move the market registry onto the consensus state root, or hash it into the root.
6. Add an exec-side MarketNotFound check (torus-core error.rs:89 already defines the variant).
7. Optional: a HIP-3-style deployer path with a stake bond and a gas auction, as a new NativeAction.

**Unsure:** I did not check who may submit or vote on ListMarket proposals (quorum or stake thresholds), or whether a proposal can actually reach execution end to end. I did not read the exec-side phantom-book path at native_executor.rs:656. I did not confirm whether the RPC StoredMarket reader treats key 0 specially. I did not check the tests in torus-integration-tests for a governance-listing scenario.

</details>

**fable** — stub, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

The three native market-lifecycle actions (ListMarket, DelistMarket, UpdateMarketParams) are explicit no-op stubs in the executor: they return ok with zero gas and touch no state (native_executor.rs:3327-3336, marked "AUDIT: ECON-PF-07 -- Intentional stubs"). The only prod path that adds a market is governance: ProposalAction::ListMarket becomes ExecutionPayload::MarketListing with a hardcoded `market_id: 0 // auto-assigned` (native_executor.rs:5744-5745), but governance.rs:1080-1098 never auto-assigns -- it writes the Borsh row directly under key 0u64 in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS, so every governance listing collides on market_id 0 and overwrites the previous one; UpdateMarketParams/DelistMarket proposals carry no execution payload at all ("text-only for now", native_executor.rs:5754-5756). Markets are otherwise seeded only at genesis (torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:424-446). There is no HIP-3 style perp-deploy auction, no deployer-stake/permissionless listing path, and no executor-side market-existence check on PlaceOrder (margin_configs is an in-memory map; MarketNotFound exists in torus-core/src/error.rs:89 but is not raised by the executor). Hyperliquid, by contrast, lists perps via the HIP-3 deployer auction (stake-gated, Dutch-auction fee, deployer sets oracle/params and can delist) plus core-team listings, and delisting/param changes actually mutate state.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3327-3336 — NativeAction::UpdateMarketParams/ListMarket/DelistMarket all return NativeActionResult::ok(..., 0) with no state change; comment says intentional stubs pending a market registry
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5744-5756 — exec_submit_proposal maps ProposalAction::ListMarket to ExecutionPayload::MarketListing{market_id: 0 /*auto-assigned*/, ...}; UpdateMarketParams/DelistMarket map to None (text-only); max_leverage from the listing is dropped and initial_margin is derived from maintenance_margin_bps
- crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:1080-1098 — execute_proposal MarketListing arm: key = market_id.to_be_bytes() then put_cf_raw(CF_NATIVE_MARKETS, &key, &data); no next-id counter, so id 0 is written verbatim
- crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:1010-1030 — process_pending_proposals finalizes/executes passed proposals after timelock; called from native_executor.rs:6107-6110 process_governance (wired)
- crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:189-200,424-446 — GenesisMarket seeded into CF_NATIVE_MARKETS with explicit market_id; comment says CF is off the consensus state root
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:549-563 — getMarkets precompile derives `active` from value.first() byte, which is the first byte of the Borsh base_asset String length prefix, not an active flag
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:52,251-262 — RPC validates market ids against CF_NATIVE_MARKETS rows (only RPC-side check found)
- grep over crates: no occurrences of auction/Auction, HIP3, DeployPerp, next_market_id

**Risk:** In prod there is no working way to add, delist, or re-parameterize a market after genesis: native List/Delist/UpdateMarketParams silently succeed (signed, nonce-consuming, zero-fee no-ops that look successful to clients), and governance ListMarket writes every new market to id 0, clobbering any genesis market 0 (or a prior listing) with new tick/lot/margin values -- a passed proposal can therefore silently change BTC-PERP's lot/tick sizes rather than list a new market. No delist means a market with a dead oracle or exploit cannot be halted on-chain. Because CF_NATIVE_MARKETS is off the state root, a governance listing is also not consensus-attested. The getMarkets precompile's `active` flag is garbage (reads a Borsh length byte), so EVM contracts cannot rely on it.

**Fix:** 1) Add a durable next-market-id counter row in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS (pattern already exists for the global-order-id counter at native_executor.rs:2549) and use it in governance.rs execute_proposal MarketListing arm instead of trusting payload.market_id; reject if key exists. 2) Give UpdateMarketParams/DelistMarket real ExecutionPayload variants (governance.rs:186 enum + 221/281 ser/de) that rewrite/flag the CF_NATIVE_MARKETS row and, on delist, cancel resting orders and block new PlaceOrder for that id. 3) Either delete the three NativeAction stubs (native_executor.rs:3327-3336, lib.rs:672-679, eip712.rs:228-232) or gate them behind a governance/admin-key check that returns err instead of ok. 4) Add an executor-side market-existence check in exec_place_order (native_executor.rs:~4911) returning MarketNotFound. 5) Fix precompiles.rs:558 active flag to read a real status byte once one exists. HIP-3 style permissionless deploy auction is a separate larger feature.

**Unsure:** Did not read the full exec_place_order body to confirm there is no market-existence check beyond margin_configs lookup; did not verify how the executor's in-memory margin_configs/order books are initialised from CF_NATIVE_MARKETS at startup (so whether a governance-listed market becomes tradable without restart is unverified); did not confirm whether any genesis config in use actually assigns market_id 0 (collision severity depends on that); Hyperliquid HIP-3 details are from general knowledge, not re-verified against current docs.

</details>

### spot

**opus** — absent, impact high, effort XL, lockstep yes

Torus has no native spot layer. There is no spot order book, no spot token registry or HIP-1 deploy flow, no per-token spot balances, and no spotSend. The only spot-related things are two NativeAction variants, TransferToPerp and TransferToSpot. Despite the names, they move the single native token (TRS) between the EVM account balance (CF_ACCOUNTS) and the native perp balance (CF_NATIVE_BALANCES) through Lockbox. In other words, "spot" here means the EVM balance, not a HyperCore spot clearinghouse. Hyperliquid, by contrast, has a spot clearinghouse with multi-token balances, HIP-1 token deploy with gas auctions, HIP-2 hyperliquidity, spot pair order books (@N), usdClassTransfer for USDC between spot and perp, spotSend, and spot↔EVM linking via system addresses.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:600-608: the only transfer variants are TransferToPerp{amount: U256}, with the doc 'Spot -> Perp balance', and TransferToSpot{amount}. Neither has a token or asset field.
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:582-677: the NativeAction variant list has no SpotSend, SpotDeploy, token register, or spot order variants. PlaceOrder only targets perp markets.
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3293-3298: TransferToPerp maps to exec_deposit_to_native and TransferToSpot maps to exec_withdraw_from_native.
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5811-5840: both functions call Lockbox::deposit_to_native / withdraw_from_native and pass only the amount.
- crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:1-72: the module doc says 'bidirectional asset transfer between EVM and native balance'. It debits the EVM balance in CF_ACCOUNTS and credits NativeBalance in CF_NATIVE_BALANCES, so there is one asset with no token dimension.
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:147-150: NativeBalance holds only {available, order_margin}, a single collateral balance with no per-token map.
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1165-1172: MarketListing has base/quote strings but also perp-only fields (max_leverage, maintenance_margin_bps). There is no spot market kind.
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3328-3336: ListMarket, DelistMarket and UpdateMarketParams are intentional no-op stubs (ECON-PF-07), so even perp market registration is not implemented.
- crates/torus-core/src/ has only perp modules (order_book, margin, liquidation, position, oracle, lockbox, precompiles). It has no spot module.
- grep for spot, usd_class, spot_send, hip1 and token_deploy across torus-core, torus-types, native_executor, torus-rpc and torus-state found only the TransferToPerp and TransferToSpot hits.

**Risk:** Torus cannot offer what Hyperliquid's spot side does: no token launches (HIP-1), no spot trading, no multi-asset collateral, and no user-to-user native transfer (spotSend). The only way to move value between users is an EVM transfer after withdrawing. The variant names TransferToSpot/TransferToPerp are misleading, because they suggest a Hyperliquid-style usdClassTransfer when they are really an EVM↔native lockbox. Integrators and SDKs that port Hyperliquid semantics could mis-model balances. I found no exploit path in this area, since the lockbox writes are atomic (ECON-PF-04).

**Fix:** 1) In torus-types, add a TokenId and a SpotToken registry type, plus new NativeAction variants SpotSend{to, token, amount}, SpotDeploy (register token, genesis balances, register pair) and spot order placement (or a market-kind flag on PlaceOrder). Keep the new variants in step with the EIP-712 encoding in crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs.
2) In torus-state, add CF_SPOT_BALANCES keyed by (addr, token_id) and CF_SPOT_TOKENS / CF_SPOT_PAIRS.
3) In torus-core, add a spot.rs clearinghouse: balance holds on order placement and settlement on fill with no margin. Reuse order_book.rs matching with a spot settlement callback.
4) In native_executor.rs, wire exec_spot_send / exec_spot_deploy / spot order exec, and either rename TransferToPerp/ToSpot to EvmToNative/NativeToEvm or redefine them as usdClassTransfer between the spot quote-token balance and the perp NativeBalance.
5) In torus-rpc, add spotMeta and spotClearinghouseState info endpoints.
6) Implement ListMarket, which is currently a stub, as the prerequisite registry.

**Unsure:** I did not open torus-rpc handlers or torus-evm precompiles beyond the grep, which found no spot hits there. I did not check whether the EVM side has ERC-20 linking that could act as a substitute token layer, or whether the order_book module carries a market-type field outside the grep terms I used. Hyperliquid's current HIP-1 and HIP-3 details are from my own knowledge, not from code.

</details>

**fable** — absent, impact high, effort XL, lockstep yes

Torus has no native spot subsystem. The only "spot" in core is a naming convention: `NativeAction::TransferToPerp`/`TransferToSpot` (torus-types/src/lib.rs:601-608) dispatch to `exec_deposit_to_native`/`exec_withdraw_from_native` (native_executor.rs:3293-3298, 5811-5838), which call `Lockbox::deposit_to_native`/`withdraw_from_native` (torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:30-60) — a single-asset TRS move between the EVM account balance and `NativeBalance{available, order_margin}` (position.rs:147-150). That is an EVM<->perp-margin lockbox (closer to Hyperliquid's EVM deposit/withdraw path), not usdClassTransfer between a spot ledger and a perp ledger. There is no spot order book (MarketListing at lib.rs:1165-1172 has no market type; order_book has zero spot/token references), no token registry or HIP-1 deploy action (NativeAction list lib.rs:582-677 contains only perp order ops, transfers, staking, governance, oracle, validator, session, ListMarket/DelistMarket of perp markets), no per-token spot balances (only CF_NATIVE_BALANCES, a single TRS balance; precompiles.rs:518-525), and no spotSend (the only P2P transfer is `Withdraw{amount,to}` TRS to an EVM address, lib.rs:610-613). Hyperliquid has a full spot CLOB, HIP-1 token deploy with spot pairs, per-token spot balances, usdClassTransfer, spotSend, and HIP-1 token<->ERC20 linking via system addresses.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:582-677 — full NativeAction enum: no token deploy/registry, spot order, spotSend, or usdClassTransfer variants; only TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot/Withdraw
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:601-608 — TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot documented as 'Spot -> Perp balance' / 'Perp -> Spot balance' but carry only a U256 amount (single asset TRS)

Any UI/wallet labeling TransferToSpot as a "spot balance" is misleading: it is the EVM account balance. No exploit path — functionality simply does not exist. Feature-parity gap vs Hyperliquid is large (spot is a major HL revenue/volume line and the on-ramp for HIP-1 tokens and ERC20 linking).

**Fix:** Minimal path: (1) add a `TokenId`/token registry in torus-types + torus-core (new CF e.g. CF_TOKENS, CF_SPOT_BALANCES keyed (addr, token_id)) with a `DeployToken` NativeAction (or ProposalAction) carrying name/decimals/supply (HIP-1 analogue); (2) add `MarketKind{Perp,Spot{base_token,quote_token}}` to MarketListing (lib.rs:1165) and branch settlement in the matching path (torus-core order_book + margin.rs) so spot fills move token balances instead of margin/positions; (3) add `SpotSend{token_id,to,amount}` NativeAction + executor handler; (4) rename or re-define TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot as true UsdClassTransfer between CF_SPOT_BALANCES[quote token] and NativeBalance, keeping the existing EVM lockbox as a separate Deposit/Withdraw action; (5) extend BalanceReader precompile (precompiles.rs:505) with getSpotBalance(address,tokenId). Did not check torus-evm for any ERC20<->native linking precompile beyond torus-core/src/precompiles.rs.
