### withdraw-vs-positions

**opus** — confirmed-bug, impact critical, effort M, lockstep yes

Neither TransferToSpot nor Withdraw computes a "withdrawable" amount. In native_executor.rs, exec_withdraw_from_native (and exec_withdraw_to) only convert the amount and call Lockbox::withdraw_from_native / withdraw_from_native_to. Those functions check just `native_bal.available >= amount`. Nothing looks at open positions, unrealized PnL, initial or maintenance margin, or oracle prices. Cross positions don't lock any collateral (isolated_margin is 0 for cross), and the order margin reserved at placement goes back to `available` when the order fills. So a trader with open cross positions, including ones in unrealized loss, can withdraw their whole `available` balance and leave the positions with no collateral. Hyperliquid instead caps withdrawals at withdrawable = accountValue - max(initial margin used, ...), with unrealized PnL counted in accountValue.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3296-3302 — TransferToSpot routes to exec_withdraw_from_native; Withdraw routes to exec_withdraw_to; neither passes positions or prices
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5826-5858 — exec_withdraw_from_native and exec_withdraw_to only call Lockbox; there is no margin or equity check
- crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:78-98 — withdraw_from_native: the only guard is `native_bal.available < amount`, then it debits available
- crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:128-149 — withdraw_from_native_to: the same check, `available` only
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:59-60 — isolated_margin is '>0 for isolated, 0 for cross', so cross collateral is not locked anywhere
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:147-150 — NativeBalance has only available and order_margin, with no position-margin bucket
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3780-3781, 4029-4030 — placing an order moves the reserve from available to order_margin
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4155-4160, 4517-4522 — on fill, the reserve goes from order_margin back to available, so the collateral behind a filled position can be withdrawn
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:179-199 — MarginEngine::cross_margin_equity exists (available - order_margin + cross uPnL); its only callers are check_initial_margin (margin.rs:132) and liquidation.rs:122, not lockbox or withdraw
- grep for 'withdrawable' across torus-core, torus-bridge and torus-consensus src: no hits

**Risk:** 1. Open a leveraged cross position. Because the reserve goes back to `available` on fill, that collateral can then be moved out with TransferToSpot (to EVM) or Withdraw (to any address). The position is left with no backing, or negative equity if it is already losing, and bad debt goes to the insurance fund / ADL / other traders. 2. A trader in unrealized loss can withdraw ahead of liquidation and push the loss onto the system. 3. A partial version of the same thing: a withdrawal can push an account below maintenance margin in one step. This breaks Hyperliquid's guarantee that a withdrawal never takes an account below its initial-margin requirement.

**Fix:** 1. In native_executor.rs, add a `withdrawable(ctx, sender)` helper next to exec_withdraw_from_native, built from MarginEngine::cross_margin_equity(&ctx.positions, sender, &oracle_prices) and the initial margin across all cross positions. Use per-market config from ctx.margin_configs and the oracle/mark prices the executor already has. Computing initial margin needs a per-position loop, because total_maintenance_margin takes one config. 2. withdrawable = max(0, min(available, cross_equity - cross_initial_margin_used)). Optionally, like HL, count only negative uPnL (no withdrawing unrealized gains). 3. Reject when amount > withdrawable, before calling Lockbox, in both exec_withdraw_from_native and exec_withdraw_to. Alternatively, move the check into Lockbox, which would need a PositionManager and prices. 4. If any position lacks a valid oracle price, block the withdrawal (fail closed). 5. Add tests: open a cross position at 10x, then (a) withdrawing the full available balance is rejected; (b) with a uPnL loss, withdrawable shrinks; (c) with no positions, the full balance can be withdrawn. The withdraw result changes, so this is a consensus-affecting change and needs a coordinated upgrade.

**Unsure:** 1. I did not check whether app.rs or the RPC layer has a pre-check before NativeAction dispatch. Both checks inside the executor are missing either way, so a precheck outside consensus would not be enough. 2. Isolated positions: I did not confirm whether isolated_margin is taken out of `available` when an isolated position opens. If it is, isolated collateral is protected and only cross is exposed. 3. A possible second bug: cross_margin_equity computes `available - order_margin`, but placing an order already moves the reserve out of available, so order margin may be subtracted twice. I didn't verify this here. 4. I did not trace the CoreWriter path (core_writer_to_native). It uses the same executor and so presumably has the same gap.

</details>

**fable** — confirmed-bug, impact critical, effort M, lockstep yes

There is no withdrawable computation. `exec_withdraw_from_native` (and `exec_withdraw_to`, used by `Withdraw`/`TransferToSpot`) converts the amount and calls `Lockbox::withdraw_from_native[_to]`, whose only guard is `native_bal.available < amount`. Cross positions do not lock margin: the executor reserves order margin into `order_margin` at submission (3780-3781) but releases it back to `available` on fill (4157-4159, 4266-4268), and `cross_margin_equity` treats `available - order_margin + uPnL` as the full equity base. So a trader with open cross positions and unrealized losses can withdraw their entire `available` balance, leaving positions backed by nothing (negative equity) until liquidation.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3296-3297 — TransferToSpot dispatches straight to exec_withdraw_from_native with no margin check
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5826-5841 — exec_withdraw_from_native: u256_to_fp then Lockbox::withdraw_from_native; no position/equity lookup
- crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:78-98 — withdraw_from_native: only check is `native_bal.available < amount`, then `available -= amount`
- crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:128-149 — withdraw_from_native_to: identical check (used by Withdraw{to})
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:147-150 — NativeBalance has only `available` and `order_margin`; no position-margin field for cross
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:178-198 — cross_margin_equity = available - order_margin + sum(unrealized_pnl of cross positions): confirms cross margin lives in `available`
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3766-3781 — order placement moves funds available -> order_margin
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4155-4159, 4263-4268 — on fill, reserved order_margin is released back to `available` (taker and maker)
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:424 — bad-debt deduction `bal.available -= deduction` is the only post-hoc recovery path

**Risk:** Exploit: deposit, open max-leverage cross position (margin reserved then released to available on fill), immediately TransferToSpot/Withdraw the full available balance. Position now has zero collateral; any adverse move is bad debt borne by the insurance fund / counterparties, and unrealized losses are never clawed back from the withdrawn funds. Hyperliquid computes withdrawable = accountValue - (initial margin of cross positions + order margin) - max(0, -uPnL) and rejects beyond that; this is a hard parity gap and a solvency hole.

**Fix:** Add `MarginEngine::withdrawable(positions, trader, config, oracle_prices) -> FixedPoint` in crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs: equity = cross_margin_equity(...); im = sum over cross positions of notional(mark)/leverage (reuse the initial-margin math from total_maintenance_margin, using initial not maintenance); withdrawable = max(0, equity - im) (order_margin is already excluded via cross_margin_equity). In native_executor.rs exec_withdraw_from_native and exec_withdraw_to, before calling Lockbox: fetch oracle prices for the trader's markets (ctx.oracle), compute withdrawable, and return NativeActionResult::err("withdraw_from_native", "exceeds withdrawable") if fp_amount > withdrawable. Add tests: open cross position then withdraw full balance -> rejected; withdraw up to equity-IM -> ok; with unrealized loss withdrawable shrinks.

**Unsure:** Did not read fill_transition (position.rs:434) to confirm isolated_margin handling for isolated positions; isolated margin is held in pos.isolated_margin (liquidation.rs:226 returns it to available on close), so isolated positions appear protected and the hole is specific to cross. Did not check whether the EVM precompile / RPC path has a separate withdraw entry that bypasses native_executor.

</details>

### nonce-consensus

**opus** — confirmed-bug, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

The 60s NONCE_WINDOW_MS check runs only at mempool ingress (torus-mempool lib.rs, plus SignedNativeAction::validate / validate_with_sessions). The execution and consensus paths never check it. app.rs live execution calls batch_verify_native_actions_cached, the catchup validator and proposer call resolve_sender, and none of these look at the nonce against block timestamp; the only nonce check there is the (sender, nonce) replay lookup in CF_NATIVE_NONCES. CF_NATIVE_NONCES is written once per executed action, keyed sender(20)++nonce(8) with the block height as value, and no code anywhere deletes or prunes it, so it grows without bound. So a proposer (or a node replaying the mempool after restart) can include a validly signed action whose nonce is hours or days old or far in the future, and every validator will execute it, provided that exact (sender, nonce) was never consumed.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:27 NONCE_WINDOW_MS = 60_000
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:859-865 and 887-892: the window check exists only in validate()/validate_with_sessions()
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:801-841 resolve_sender: verifies the signature and session expiry against current_timestamp, with no nonce-window check
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:1098+ batch_verify_impl: the only use of .nonce is struct_hash at relative line 57; no NonceTooOld/NONCE_WINDOW
- crates/torus-mempool/src/lib.rs:467-471, 596-602: the window is enforced at mempool admission
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1677-1700: exec resolves senders via batch_verify_native_actions_cached(header.timestamp), with no window
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1766-1781: the only exec-time nonce gate is the CF_NATIVE_NONCES replay lookup plus the seen_in_block dedup
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:2038-2045: put_cf_raw(CF_NATIVE_NONCES, key, height) for every consumed nonce
- crates/torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:367-391: the catchup validator calls resolve_sender plus the replay check only
- crates/torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs:208-223: the proposer calls resolve_sender, and the replayed-nonce branch only does tracing::warn (it does not skip or reject)
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:84-85: CF_NATIVE_NONCES has value block_height; grep finds no delete/delete_range/prune on CF_NATIVE_NONCES anywhere in crates/
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:103: the comment says NONCE_WINDOW_MS 'gates mempool admission', which confirms the window is ingress-only by design

**Risk:** (1) A Byzantine or buggy proposer can include a stale signed action. Examples: one the user signed but that expired from the mempool, a body kept in CF_NATIVE_PENDING (which is deliberately decoupled from the window), or a far-future-nonce action. All honest nodes will execute it deterministically, so a user's 'expired' intent can be executed long afterwards. Hyperliquid instead rejects nonces outside (T-2d, T+1d) and requires nonce > min(100 highest seen) as a state-machine rule, not a mempool rule. (2) Because the replay guard is only 'exact (sender, nonce) never seen', reordering and old nonces are fine at consensus level, so there is no monotonic or bounded-set semantics. (3) CF_NATIVE_NONCES grows by one row per executed native action forever. At HL-like throughput (tens of thousands of actions per second) that is unbounded disk and RocksDB compaction growth, and it slows the replay lookup on every action. Pruning is unsafe today, because without a consensus-level window an old pruned nonce could be replayed, so the two problems are coupled. (4) Minor: the proposer.rs replay branch only warns, which is harmless because exec dedups, but it is misleading.

**Fix:** Make the window a deterministic execution rule keyed to header.timestamp, not wall clock. In app.rs, in the exec loop at about 1757-1781, and in torus-bridge validator.rs at about 369-391, drop (do not slash) any action where nonce + W < header.timestamp or nonce > header.timestamp + W_future, reusing the NonceTooOld/NonceTooFuture logic from eip712.rs:859-865 as a shared helper, e.g. SignedNativeAction::check_nonce_window(ts). Make the proposer skip such actions too. Once that is enforced, prune CF_NATIVE_NONCES deterministically. Option A: a per-sender bounded set (HL-style: keep the 100 highest nonces, require nonce > min of them), stored in one row per sender. Option B: a time-bucketed key prefix (bucket(nonce) ++ sender ++ nonce), with DeleteRange of buckets older than header.timestamp - W at commit. Either way, gate it behind an activation height, since it changes execution results.

**Unsure:** I did not read the full mempool selection path (native_pool.rs:449-470 evict-stale) or how the sync/DA path re-injects CF_NATIVE_PENDING bodies, so whether honest proposers can actually emit stale actions in practice (as opposed to Byzantine ones) is unverified. I also did not check whether some compaction filter or snapshot-pruning code outside the grep patterns (delete_cf/delete_range with 'nonce') clears CF_NATIVE_NONCES, for example a generic CF wipe in state sync. app.rs:10427-10458 mentions CF_NATIVE_NONCES in a test about state transfer and was not read.

</details>

**fable** — confirmed-bug, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

The ±60s nonce window (NONCE_WINDOW_MS, torus-types eip712.rs:27) is enforced only at mempool ingress against the local wall clock (torus-mempool lib.rs:462-475) plus lazy pool eviction (native_pool.rs:454-470). The consensus exec path (app.rs:1677 batch_verify_native_actions_cached with block timestamp -> resolve_sender) and the bridge validator (validator.rs:367-391) only verify the signature/session and check CF_NATIVE_NONCES for replay; resolve_sender (eip712.rs) contains no nonce-range check, only session expiry. The window-checking functions `validate`/`validate_with_sessions` (eip712.rs:860-891) are not called on the block path. CF_NATIVE_NONCES is written per consumed action (app.rs:2038-2044, 36 bytes/entry) and no delete/prune/range-delete of it exists anywhere in torus-state/consensus/bridge, so it grows unboundedly. Consequently a proposer can include an arbitrarily old (or far-future) nonce and the block validates; correctness then rests solely on the permanent nonce set, which is exactly what prevents pruning it.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-mempool/src/lib.rs:462-475 — admission uses SystemTime::now() and rejects nonce outside ±NONCE_WINDOW_MS; the only window gate
- crates/torus-mempool/src/native_pool.rs:454-470 — evict_expired drops pool entries older than window; comment claims they 'can never pass validation again' (not true: validation has no window check)
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:27 — NONCE_WINDOW_MS = 60_000
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:860-891 — window check lives only in validate()/validate_with_sessions(); resolve_sender (read in full) has no nonce-range check, only session.expiry
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1677-1693 — exec resolves senders via batch_verify_native_actions_cached(block.header.timestamp, session lookup); no window
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1752-1780 — replay guard: skip if (sender,nonce) in CF_NATIVE_NONCES or duplicated in block; no staleness check
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:2038-2044 — every consumed nonce written to CF_NATIVE_NONCES with value=height; never removed
- crates/torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:367-391 — validate_block_with_native_inner: signature + replay check only, no window
- crates/torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs:207-224 — proposer replay check only logs 'skipping' but does not actually skip the action (minor: app.rs guard covers it)
- grep delete_cf\|delete_range\|prune\|compact x nonce in torus-state/src, torus-consensus/src, torus-bridge/src — zero hits
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:103-107 — doc confirms the window is a mempool-admission gate only

**Risk:** (1) A byzantine or buggy proposer can include actions whose nonce is years old or far in the future; validators accept them. Combined with the DA store (CF_NATIVE_PENDING) keeping stale bodies, a leader can resurrect any never-executed signed action a user ever broadcast, long after the user assumed it expired — HL semantics guarantee expiry. (2) CF_NATIVE_NONCES grows ~36B per action forever (at HL-like 100k+ actions/s that is multi-GB/day) and cannot be pruned safely because pruning an entry makes that nonce replayable given (1). Hyperliquid bounds this: nonce must be within ±1 day of block time AND above the 100th-highest used nonce per address, enforced in consensus, so per-address state is O(100).

**Fix:** 1) Enforce the window deterministically in consensus: in app.rs replay-guard loop (~1762) and validator.rs (~378) drop/reject actions where signed.nonce + NONCE_WINDOW_MS < block.header.timestamp or signed.nonce > block.header.timestamp + NONCE_WINDOW_MS (consider widening W toward HL's 1 day, or keep 60s but note block-ts vs wall-clock skew for in-flight actions). Add a test in app.rs tests (near 10324) that a stale-nonce action in a block is not executed and not recorded. 2) With the window enforced, prune CF_NATIVE_NONCES: entries with nonce < block_ts - W can never be replayed. Key is sender||nonce_be so a nonce-range delete needs either a secondary CF keyed nonce_be||sender (range-delete at each commit) or HL-style per-sender bounded set (keep 100 highest nonces per address, reject nonce <= min). 3) Fix proposer.rs:218 to actually `continue`/filter the action it logs as skipped. Files: torus-consensus/src/app.rs, torus-bridge/src/validator.rs, torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs, torus-state/src/cf.rs.

**Unsure:** Did not read batch_verify_native_actions_cached body to confirm it has no window check, but it calls into resolve_sender semantics and NONCE_WINDOW_MS appears nowhere in eip712.rs outside validate/validate_with_sessions and tests, so a check there is ruled out by grep. Did not verify whether the proposer re-runs evict_expired before select_for_block (callers list shows only tests calling evict_expired directly; the 'selection/drain wrappers' in lib.rs were not read). Did not inspect whether Hyperliquid's current rule is still 'within 1 day, above 100th-highest nonce' — stated from recollection.

</details>

### gov-param-change

**opus** — confirmed-bug, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

Both suspicions hold. When a ParameterChange proposal executes, it checks the key against a whitelist (maintenance_margin_bps, max_leverage, voting_period_blocks, quorum_bps, permanent_weight_multiplier_num/den) and then writes the raw UTF-8 value to CF_FEE_CONFIG under that key string. Nothing reads those rows back. The executor, matching engine and margin code never look up these keys, and governance itself loads its own params (voting period, quorum, multipliers) from a single borsh blob at GOVERNANCE_PARAMS_KEY, not from the per-key rows, so even governance-about-governance changes have no effect. The governance ListMarket conversion hardcodes market_id: 0 ("auto-assigned", but nothing assigns it). So every listing overwrites the same CF_NATIVE_MARKETS row at key 0u64. It also stores maintenance_margin_bps in the initial_margin field, and the direct NativeAction::ListMarket is a no-op stub.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:1043-1051 execute_payload ParameterChange: validate_param_change then state.put_cf_raw(CF_FEE_CONFIG, param_key.as_bytes(), new_value.as_bytes()); only a tracing::info follows
- crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:555-640 validate_param_change whitelist: maintenance_margin_bps, max_leverage, voting_period_blocks, quorum_bps, permanent_weight_multiplier_num/den
- grep across crates/ for the string literals "maintenance_margin_bps"/"max_leverage"/"voting_period_blocks" (excluding tests) hits only governance.rs:557/571/585, the validator itself, so there are no runtime readers
- grep CF_FEE_CONFIG across crates: the only reads are governance.rs:1001/1193/1438 (PROPOSAL_COUNTER_KEY and GOVERNANCE_PARAMS_KEY), never the per-param keys
- crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:1190-1205 get/set_governance_params use the single borsh blob GOVERNANCE_PARAMS_KEY, so a voting_period_blocks/quorum_bps ParameterChange does not change GovernanceParams
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5744-5753 ListMarket -> ExecutionPayload::MarketListing { market_id: 0, // auto-assigned ... initial_margin: from maintenance_margin_bps }
- crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:1080-1100 MarketListing execution: key = market_id.to_be_bytes(); put_cf_raw(CF_NATIVE_MARKETS, &key, &data), with no id allocation
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5754-5756 UpdateMarketParams/DelistMarket -> None (text-only)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3328-3337 direct NativeAction::ListMarket/UpdateMarketParams/DelistMarket are no-op ok() stubs (ECON-PF-07)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6110 process_pending_proposals is called from the executor, so execution does run; the writes themselves are dead
- crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:193,424-426 CF_NATIVE_MARKETS is OFF the consensus native state root

**Risk:** Governance looks like it works: a proposal passes, executes and logs "governance parameter updated", but margin, leverage, quorum and voting-period settings never change. Token holders and the UI will think risk params were changed when they were not. Each governance market listing overwrites row 0, so a second listing silently replaces the first. Row 0 also holds whatever genesis seeded at id 0, if anything. Listings store the maintenance margin as the initial margin. Because CF_NATIVE_MARKETS is outside the state root, this writes non-root state from a consensus path. That makes it hard to audit, and it does not give HL-parity on-chain market deployment (HIP-3-like) or parameter governance.

**Fix:** (1) ParameterChange: route keys to typed state the runtime actually reads. For governance keys, load GovernanceParams, mutate the field and call set_governance_params. For risk keys (maintenance_margin_bps, max_leverage), write them into the per-market or global risk config that the margin and liquidation code in torus-core reads, and have the executor read it (or apply it to the engine at the end of the block). Reject any key that has no consumer. (2) ListMarket: allocate an id inside execute_payload, e.g. a monotonic NEXT_MARKET_ID counter in a root-tracked CF, or max(existing ids)+1 by iterating CF_NATIVE_MARKETS. Refuse to overwrite an existing key. Carry initial and maintenance margin as separate fields. Create the order book or register the market with the engine so it can trade. Ideally keep market metadata in a CF that is included in the state root. (3) Implement UpdateMarketParams/DelistMarket payloads, which currently become None. Add tests asserting that a passed ParameterChange changes behaviour, e.g. a liquidation threshold or voting period, and that two listings get distinct ids.

**Unsure:** I did not check whether the matching engine or executor loads markets dynamically from CF_NATIVE_MARKETS at runtime (books may be created lazily), so I can't say whether a governance-listed market at id 0 is actually tradable. I did not check whether genesis configs use market_id 0. I did not check whether CF_FEE_CONFIG is part of the consensus state root. The no-reader conclusion rests on a grep for the string literals; a key built dynamically (format!) somewhere would have been missed, but none was seen.

</details>

**fable** — confirmed-bug, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

An executed ParameterChange writes `CF_FEE_CONFIG[param_key] = new_value` as a raw UTF-8 string (governance.rs:1043-1051). No runtime code reads those keys: the only CF_FEE_CONFIG readers in non-test code are governance.rs itself, and they read the borsh-encoded `gov_params` struct and the `gov_next_id` counter, not "max_leverage"/"maintenance_margin_bps"/"voting_period_blocks"/"quorum_bps". So even governance's own params (voting_period_blocks, quorum_bps) are not changed by a passed proposal, and the executor's leverage comes from `ctx.margin_configs` (a HashMap seeded empty at construction), so it is a dead write. Governance ListMarket: the executor converts every `ProposalAction::ListMarket` to `ExecutionPayload::MarketListing { market_id: 0 }` (native_executor.rs:5744-5745, comment "auto-assigned" but nothing assigns it), and execute_payload stores it under key `0u64.to_be_bytes()` (governance.rs:1088-1097), so every listed market overwrites the same key 0; the direct `NativeAction::ListMarket` is an explicit no-op stub (native_executor.rs:3335).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:1043-1051 — ExecutionPayload::ParameterChange executes as put_cf_raw(CF_FEE_CONFIG, param_key.as_bytes(), new_value.as_bytes())
- crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:43,46,1001,1193,1438 — only non-test CF_FEE_CONFIG readers: GOVERNANCE_PARAMS_KEY=b"gov_params" (borsh GovernanceParams struct) and PROPOSAL_COUNTER_KEY=b"gov_next_id"; neither matches the string keys written by ParameterChange
- crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:555-640 — validate_param_change accepts keys maintenance_margin_bps, max_leverage, voting_period_blocks, quorum_bps, permanent_weight_multiplier_num/den
- grep of crates/ for CF_FEE_CONFIG outside governance.rs: only torus-state/cf.rs (const), pruner.rs (doc comment), and tests (governance_tests.rs:370, staking_lifecycle.rs:207 assert the raw write exists) — no executor reader
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:15,1356,1842,4815 — executor leverage comes from ctx.margin_configs: HashMap<MarketId, MarketMarginConfig>, initialized HashMap::new(), used via effective_max_leverage; not derived from CF_FEE_CONFIG
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5738-5753 — ProposalAction::ListMarket -> ExecutionPayload::MarketListing { market_id: 0, // auto-assigned ... }
- crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:1080-1097 — MarketListing writes CF_NATIVE_MARKETS under key market_id.to_be_bytes() with no counter/auto-assignment
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3327-3336 — NativeAction::ListMarket/UpdateMarketParams/DelistMarket are intentional stubs (AUDIT ECON-PF-07) returning ok with no state change
- crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:189-197,446,911 — genesis seeds CF_NATIVE_MARKETS keyed by market_id (sample uses market_id 1); CF_NATIVE_MARKETS is off the consensus state root

**Risk:** Governance is decorative: a proposal to change max_leverage/maintenance margin/quorum/voting period passes, emits "governance parameter updated", and changes no executor or governance behavior; operators and users would believe risk parameters changed when they did not. Governance market listing always writes slot 0 so a second listing silently overwrites the first, and because the executor's matching/margin paths never consult CF_NATIVE_MARKETS for market config (precompile getMarkets only enumerates it), a "listed" market is still not tradable. Hyperliquid parity requires live-updating margin tiers / listing via governance, so this is a parity gap, not just a cosmetic one.

**Fix:** 1) governance.rs execute_payload ParameterChange: for voting_period_blocks/quorum_bps/permanent_weight_multiplier_*, load GovernanceParams via get_governance_params(), mutate the field, re-put under GOVERNANCE_PARAMS_KEY (borsh). 2) For max_leverage/maintenance_margin_bps: either scope the key per market (e.g. "max_leverage:<market_id>") and have the executor rebuild ctx.margin_configs from CF_FEE_CONFIG at block start (native_executor.rs near line 1842 / process_governance at 6107), or reject these keys in validate_param_change until a reader exists. 3) ListMarket: in native_executor.rs:5744 replace market_id: 0 with an id from a persisted counter (e.g. CF_NATIVE_MARKETS b"next_market_id" alongside NEXT_GLOBAL_ORDER_ID_KEY), or pass the listing's requested id; add a duplicate-key check in execute_payload MarketListing. Add tests asserting GovernanceParams changes after execution and that two ListMarket proposals produce distinct keys.

**Unsure:** Did not read how ctx.margin_configs is populated outside the constructor (only saw HashMap::new() at 1842 and reads at 4362/4815); if some node-startup path fills it from CF_FEE_CONFIG I missed it, but grep for CF_FEE_CONFIG across crates found no such reader. Did not verify whether torus_types::MarketListing carries a market_id field that the executor could have forwarded. Fixing ParameterChange semantics changes state transitions, hence consensus_breaking=true for a live chain.

</details>

### unknown-market-reach

**opus** — confirmed-bug, impact high, effort S, lockstep yes

The only check for unknown market ids is `validate_known_markets`, an RPC-only ingress guard in torus.rs:257, called at torus.rs:305 and :1952. Its own doc comment calls it "non-consensus" and says the exec-side fix is a separate item. The executor has no registry check. `exec_place_order` reserves margin with `cfg=None`, which falls back to 20x leverage, then calls `order_books.entry(market_id).or_insert_with(|| OrderBook::new(market_id, ONE, ONE))`, creating a tick=lot=1 book. The batched matching path does the same through `unwrap_or_else`. The CoreWriter EVM path has no market check at the precompile enqueue, at `core_writer_to_native`, or at `drain_core_writer`, so unknown market ids from that path reach this same code and create a book.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:249-257 doc comment: 'RPC-only ingress guard (non-consensus ...) ... phantom-book trap ... exec-side fix is a separate consensus item'
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:261-266 point-get on CF_NATIVE_MARKETS; this is the only 'unknown market_id' rejection site (grep found none in torus-bridge, torus-core or torus-consensus apart from the unused-here CoreError::MarketNotFound at torus-core/src/error.rs:89)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4906-4921 exec_place_order: no market existence check before reserving margin
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4805-4817 reserve_for_qty_cfg: cfg None -> unwrap_or(20) leverage (no rejection)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4960-4964 '// Get or create order book' entry().or_insert_with(OrderBook::new(market_id, FixedPoint::ONE, FixedPoint::ONE)) and dirty_books.insert, so it gets persisted
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3824-3828 batched Phase 3 matching: order_books.remove(&market_id).unwrap_or_else(\|\| OrderBook::new(market_id, ONE, ONE))
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:815-837 CoreWriter placeOrder: checks only quantity overflow, then enqueues market_id as-is
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5870-5899 drain_core_writer: only a block-delay guard, then core_writer_to_native + Self::execute
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6266-6276 core_writer_to_native maps market_id straight into NativeAction::PlaceOrder
- grep of validator.rs, proposer.rs and consensus app.rs for market_id / CF_NATIVE_MARKETS: test fixtures only, no registry validation

**Risk:** Any EVM contract or EOA can call CoreWriter.placeOrder with an arbitrary market_id. One block later this deterministically creates and persists a phantom tick=1/lot=1 book. Every node does the same thing, so there is no fork, but it bloats state permanently: one book per id with no listing fee. The order reserves margin at a default 20x with no oracle or mark price, and two colluding accounts can match each other there and open positions in a market with no margin config, mark price or funding. Liquidation and funding logic may then hit those positions. A Byzantine proposer that includes signed native actions directly, skipping RPC, gets the same result. On Hyperliquid, orders for a nonexistent asset index are rejected during consensus execution, so this is a parity gap.

**Fix:** Add a check in the consensus executor. In `exec_place_order` (native_executor.rs:~4911) and in the batched prepare phase (before line ~3800, where `market_batches` is filled), reject the action when `market_id` has no row in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS. Use a per-block cached set or the loaded market registry, and return `NativeActionResult::err("place_order", "unknown market_id")` or `CoreError::MarketNotFound`. Replace both `OrderBook::new(market_id, ONE, ONE)` fallbacks (lines 3828 and 4964) with a load from market meta, or make them unreachable. Optionally also reject at the CoreWriter precompile enqueue (precompiles.rs:~822) for early feedback, but the executor check is the one consensus depends on. This changes execution results for blocks that contain such actions, so it needs a coordinated upgrade or activation height.

**Unsure:** Not verified: whether the P2P gossip/mempool admission path calls validate_known_markets (torus.rs:1952 is a second RPC-side caller and I did not trace its context). Either way the guard is not a consensus rule, so a proposer can bypass it. I did not confirm whether margin_configs is populated for every listed market, and I did not trace what happens downstream to positions opened in a phantom market (mark price, funding, liquidation). CancelOrder and other actions with a market_id were not audited.

</details>

**fable** — confirmed-bug, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

The only market-registry check is the RPC-side, non-consensus `validate_known_markets` (torus.rs:257-281), called from the RPC submit path (torus.rs:305). No equivalent check exists at consensus or exec level: gossip ingest (`add_native_action_from_gossip`, mempool lib.rs:502+) only verifies signatures/session ownership; `validate_block` (app.rs:4915-4952) has zero market references; the CoreWriter EVM path enqueues raw actions (`CoreWriterQueue::enqueue`, precompiles.rs:999) and `drain_core_writer` converts them via `core_writer_to_native` and calls `execute` directly (native_executor.rs:5873-5899). All three exec paths then conjure a tick=lot=1 book on miss: serial `exec_place_order` (`.entry(market_id).or_insert_with(|| OrderBook::new(market_id, ONE, ONE))`, native_executor.rs:4961-4964) and the parallel matcher (`remove(&market_id).unwrap_or_else(|| OrderBook::new(.., ONE, ONE))`, native_executor.rs:3825-3828), with margin falling back to a default via `ctx.margin_configs.get(&market_id)...unwrap_or(20)` (native_executor.rs:4799-4816). The source itself documents this: the RPC guard's doc comment says "exec-side fix is a separate consensus item" (torus.rs:252-254).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:249-281 — validate_known_markets is explicitly 'RPC-only ingress guard (non-consensus)'; doc comment notes exec-side fix is a separate consensus item
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:305 — the only call site of validate_known_markets (RPC submit path)
- crates/torus-mempool/src/lib.rs:502-550 — add_native_action_from_gossip verifies session signature/owner only; no market lookup (grep for 'market' in that range: none)
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:4915-4952 — validate_block contains no market references
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5873-5899 — drain_core_writer: CoreWriterQueue::drain -> core_writer_to_native -> Self::execute, no market registry check
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:993-1020 — CoreWriterQueue::enqueue borsh-serializes the action and stores it; no CF_NATIVE_MARKETS lookup
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4959-4964 — serial exec_place_order: ctx.order_books.entry(market_id).or_insert_with(\|\| OrderBook::new(market_id, FixedPoint::ONE, FixedPoint::ONE))
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3824-3828 — parallel matching phase: remove(&market_id).unwrap_or_else(\|\| OrderBook::new(market_id, ONE, ONE))
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4795-4816 — reserve_for_qty uses ctx.margin_configs.get(&market_id) with unwrap_or(20) default, so unknown markets get a default leverage instead of rejection
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:2054 — rebuild_book uses real meta.tick_size/lot_size only for books already persisted; new phantom books get ONE/ONE

**Risk:** Any path that bypasses the single RPC node's guard reaches the book with an unregistered market_id: (1) a CoreWriter call from an EVM contract with an arbitrary market id; (2) a gossiped SignedNativeAction from a peer node (or a node running a modified RPC); (3) a proposer including such an action in a block, which every validator will execute identically. Result: a phantom tick=1/lot=1 book with default 20x margin, no oracle/market config, persisted into state and dirtied each block. This is state bloat/griefing and a divergence from Hyperliquid, where orders on nonexistent assets are rejected at the consensus action layer, never creating state. It also means the RPC guard gives a false sense of safety since the invariant is not consensus-enforced.

**Fix:** Add a consensus-level registry check in the executor, shared by all three paths. In crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs: (a) in exec_place_order (~4909) and the parallel prep phase (~3660-3790, where margin is checked before market_batches insertion), look up market existence (e.g. ctx.margin_configs.contains_key(&market_id) or a cached CF_NATIVE_MARKETS set loaded into NativeExecContext at block start) and return NativeActionResult::err("place_order", "unknown market_id") before any book access; (b) replace the two or_insert_with/unwrap_or_else book conjuring sites (3828, 4964) with a hard error or a construct that reads tick/lot from CF_NATIVE_MARKETS meta (like rebuild_book at 2054). Optionally add the same check in core_writer_to_native/drain_core_writer (5897) and in mempool add_native_action_from_gossip for early shedding. Add exec tests: unknown market via CoreWriter and via direct execute must not create a book entry.

**Unsure:** Did not read core_writer_to_native's body or the EVM-side CoreWriter precompile input validation (torus-evm) to confirm it does not reject unknown market ids before enqueue; grep of precompiles.rs showed no CF_NATIVE_MARKETS lookup outside the read-only getMarkets precompile, but torus-evm was not inspected. Did not confirm whether margin_configs is populated only from registered markets (if it is, a contains_key check there would be the cheapest registry gate).

</details>

### pending-stops-dos

**opus** — confirmed-bug, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

Stop orders bypass the 200-per-trader-per-market cap. The check reads only `trader_orders` (order_book.rs:410-411), and StopMarket/StopLimit are pushed into `pending_stops` and returned before `insert_order` runs (order_book.rs:438-455, 474-491). So stops are never counted, and placing more stops never trips the cap. Stops also cannot be cancelled by id: `cancel_order` looks up only `order_index` and returns OrderNotFound for a stop (order_book.rs:590-594). The only way to remove them is `cancel_all` for that trader (order_book.rs:651, 695; cancel_batch.rs:477, 960). `pending_stops` is an unbounded, unindexed `Vec` (order_book.rs:251). Every `place_order` that produces fills calls `trigger_stops` (order_book.rs:577-578), which runs `retain` over the whole Vec, up to 10 passes while the price keeps moving (order_book.rs:1271-1336). The whole-book serializer also writes every stop (order_book.rs:2536-2539).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:28 MAX_ORDERS_PER_TRADER_PER_MARKET = 200
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:410-411 the cap counts only trader_orders.get(&trader).len()
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:438-455 and 474-491 StopMarket/StopLimit are pushed to pending_stops and return PendingTrigger before insert_order, so trader_orders and order_index are never updated
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:251 pending_stops: Vec<StopOrder> (no per-trader index, no cap)
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:590-594 cancel_order uses only order_index and returns OrderNotFound for a stop id
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:651,695 and cancel_batch.rs:477,960 stops are removed only through cancel_all (a retain by trader)
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:577-578 every place_order with non-empty fills calls trigger_stops()
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1271-1336 trigger_stops runs up to 10 iterations, each a full pending_stops.retain plus a clone of the triggered stops
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:2536-2539 whole-book serialization writes every pending stop
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4982 and 4621 PendingTrigger keeps margin reserved, so capital is the only cost bound
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6182 StopMarket is classified NonGtcOrder; no stop-specific limit found

**Risk:** Placing N far-from-market stops costs the attacker only the margin they reserve, and their own fees, if any. This is worse if reduce-only stops reserve zero margin, which I did not verify. Each stop adds about 100+ B of state to the market's book. Every fill-producing order in that market by any user then pays O(N) for the retain (up to 10x in a cascade). Cancel-all and whole-book serialization are also O(N). Example: 1M stops is about 100+ MB in one market. Each fill-producing order then costs about 1-3 ms just to scan stops, so a block with thousands of taker orders adds seconds of execution and stalls consensus. A user also cannot cancel one stop and must cancel_all, a UX gap compared with HL. Hyperliquid counts trigger orders toward the open-order limit, lets you cancel them by oid, and also caps open trigger (TP/SL) orders. This code has none of these.

**Fix:** 1) In order_book.rs `place_order`, register stops in `trader_orders` (or keep a separate per-trader stop count) so the cap at :410 includes them. A separate cap such as MAX_STOPS_PER_TRADER_PER_MARKET would also match HL's trigger-order limit. Also add a global per-market cap on pending stops. 2) Make `cancel_order` fall back to removing from `pending_stops` by id; since the Vec is id-ascending (:1377), a binary search works. Keep the trader_orders bookkeeping consistent. 3) Replace the Vec scan with two BTreeMaps keyed by trigger price (buy stops ascending, sell stops descending). trigger_stops then pops only the triggered prefix, O(k log N), while keeping the id-ascending canonical order for serialization and the row store, for example by sorting the triggered batch by id. 4) Check that reduce-only stops cannot be placed with zero margin and no count limit. Items 1 and 3 change which orders are accepted and the order in which stops trigger, so they need a version-gated activation.

**Unsure:** I did not verify how much margin `prep.margin_reserved` charges for a stop (StopMarket uses price=0 in params?), or whether reduce-only stops reserve nothing, which would make the attack effectively free. I did not check RPC/executor-level rate limits, per-action fees, or per-block action caps that would slow placement. The 1-3 ms per 1M figure is an estimate, not a benchmark. I did not check whether the row-store path (TORUS_BOOK_ROWS) avoids serializing all stops every block.

</details>

**fable** — confirmed-bug, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

Pending stops are NOT counted toward the 200-order cap: the cap checks `trader_orders` (order_book.rs:410-411), but the StopMarket/StopLimit branches push to `pending_stops` and return `PendingTrigger` before `trader_orders.entry(..).push` is ever reached (order_book.rs:438-453, 474-489; the only trader_orders inserts are at 1198/1515 for resting orders). Pending stops are NOT cancellable by id: `cancel_order` looks up `order_index` only (order_book.rs:590-594) and returns `OrderNotFound` for a stop id; stops are only removed by `cancel_all` (651, 695) or batch cancel-all (cancel_batch.rs:477), i.e. the trader must nuke all resting orders too. `pending_stops` is a plain `Vec<StopOrder>` (order_book.rs:251) scanned in full with `retain` on every fill-producing place_order/modify (575-578, 780, 1272-1295), fully borsh-serialised every save via `stop_rows()` (1375-1390) and `serialize` (2536-2540), and diffed against a RocksDB prefix scan + HashSet in `diff_stop_rows` (native_executor.rs:2985-3000, comment assumes "the stop set is tiny"). No per-trader or per-market cap on stops exists anywhere (grep for MAX_STOPS/max_stops: none).

- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:2536-2540 — classic serialize writes all stops
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:2980-3000 — diff_stop_rows prefix-scans all persisted stop rows into a HashSet per save; comment 'the stop set is tiny'
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4124-4130,4617-4623 — PendingTrigger keeps margin_reserved held (so each stop costs the trader reserved margin)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:3776 — dust_stop_order_rejected test exists (min size enforced)

**Risk:** DoS: a trader can place unbounded stops per market (cap bypass), each at a never-triggering price. Cost per stop is only the reserved margin for a minimum-size order (margin IS held, per executor 4124-4130), so with e.g. $1 min notional at 50x, ~$0.02-$1 per stop; 100k stops for ~$2k-$100k. Effect: every fill in that market pays O(N) retain over 100k StopOrders (~100+ byte structs, >10MB scan) on the consensus exec path; every block save borsh-serialises all N stops and does an N-row RocksDB prefix scan + HashSet build; full-book serialize grows unboundedly. Degrades block exec latency for all validators and all users of that market. Secondary bug: a trader cannot cancel a single stop by id (OrderNotFound), only cancel_all — margin stays locked until they drop all resting orders; Hyperliquid lets trigger orders be cancelled by oid and counts them toward its open-order limit, so this is also a parity gap.

**Fix:** 1) order_book.rs place_order: count stops toward the cap — change line 410 to `trader_orders.len() + pending_stops.iter().filter(|s| s.trader==trader).count()` or better keep a `HashMap<Address,usize>` stop count (also maintained in cancel_all/trigger/cancel_batch); reject with Rejected when sum >= 200. 2) cancel_order: before the order_index lookup, `if let Some(pos)=self.pending_stops.iter().position(|s| s.id==order_id)` remove it, return a synthetic Order (or add `cancel_stop(id) -> Result<StopOrder>` and have native_executor's cancel path try it and release margin_reserved). 3) Optionally index stops by trigger price (BTreeMap<FixedPoint, Vec<StopOrder>> per side) so trigger_stops only touches crossed prices; with the per-trader cap this becomes secondary. Add tests: stop counts toward 200 cap; cancel_order(stop_id) removes it and releases margin; determinism test covers new map ordering.

**Unsure:** Did not verify exact min-notional / margin formula for stops (reduce_only stops may reserve zero margin, which would make the DoS nearly free — check prep.margin_reserved for reduce_only in native_executor). Did not check whether RPC/native_executor cancel path has any separate stop-cancel handling beyond cancel_order (grep found none). Trigger-direction validation at 423-434 is skipped when last_trade_price is None (new market), not relevant to DoS but noted.

</details>

### modify-invariants

**opus** — confirmed-bug, impact critical, effort S, lockstep yes

I could not refute this; the code confirms all three parts. `OrderBook::modify_order` cancels the order and calls `insert_order`, which pushes it straight into the price level with no matching and no cross check. A re-priced order can therefore rest through the opposite best, leaving a crossed book. `new_qty` <= 0 skips the in-place path, because that path only runs when 0 < q < remaining. It then falls through to cancel-and-reinsert with `remaining_qty = q`, so a zero-quantity or negative-quantity order rests on the book. `exec_modify_order` changes the book first and checks margin second. When margin is short it returns an error with no rollback: the bigger order stays on the book and nothing is reserved for it. It also never receives `sender`, so there is no ownership check: anyone can modify anyone's order, while cancel does check the owner.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:709-726: the in-place path only runs for new_price None with 0 < new_q < remaining_qty; any other new_q falls through
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:756-772: cancel_order(id) then replacement.price/remaining_qty = new values with no validation (q can be 0 or negative, p can be 0 or negative), then insert_order
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1185-1214: insert_order does book.entry(price).push_back(order) with no match against the opposite side and no best_bid < best_ask check
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5368: book.modify_order(...) runs before any margin computation
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5392-5401: if bal.available < delta it returns err, but the book was already changed at 5368 and nothing restores old_order; dirty_books was already inserted at 5369
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5403-5410: when new_margin < old_margin, delta = old - new; with negative qty the new notional is negative, so the release exceeds the order's real margin (capped only by bal.order_margin)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3250-3254: ModifyOrder is dispatched as exec_modify_order(ctx, order_id, ...) without sender
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5164-5175: exec_cancel_order does check order.trader != sender (modify has no such check)
- grep found no checkpoint/rollback/backup of books in native_executor.rs or app.rs, and no validation of new_qty/new_price in torus-bridge or torus-consensus src

**Risk:** These are the concrete failing sequences.
(1) Crossed book: Alice has bid #1 at 99 x 1. Bob has ask #2 at 101 x 1. Alice sends ModifyOrder{1, new_price=Some(105), new_qty=None}. Bid 105 now rests and best_bid 105 > best_ask 101, with no fill. Later matching and mark/oracle mid logic that assumes an uncrossed book give wrong prices, and an arbitrageur can lift or hit at stale prices.
(2) Zero quantity: ModifyOrder{1, None, Some(0)}. Since 0 is not > 0 it falls through and the order re-rests with remaining_qty = 0, which is a ghost order. That margin is released, yet the price level still shows up in depth and in best_bid/ask, and matching may hit a 0-qty maker.
(3) Negative quantity: Some(-10) gives a negative notional. The release is old_margin - new_margin, which is larger than old_margin and capped only by the trader's total order_margin. That frees margin backing their other orders, while a negative-quantity order rests on the book.
(4) No rollback: a trader with available = 0 holds ask 100 x 1 at 20x, so margin is 5. They send ModifyOrder{id, None, Some(1000)}. The book now holds 100 x 1000, the margin check fails (needs 4995, has 0), and the call returns err. The 1000-lot order stays live with only 5 of margin, so a margin bypass costs one failed transaction.
(5) No ownership check: Mallory can modify any order by id, for example re-pricing a victim's bid to cross and fill at a bad price. Mallory can also grow it by a huge amount: it is charged to the victim, and if the victim's margin is short the order still stays enlarged because of (4).
Real Hyperliquid rejects all of these. It requires the sender to own the order, validates size and tick, and treats a modify as cancel plus a new order that matches immediately or is rejected (ALO). It also does the margin check before touching the book.

**Fix:** 1. In native_executor.rs, pass `sender` into exec_modify_order and require old_order.trader == *sender, as cancel does at 5170.
2. Validate inputs before touching the book: new_qty > 0; new_price > 0 and on a valid tick; size/lot and minimum notional rules the same as PlaceOrder.
3. Compute new_margin from old_order plus the new values and check bal.available >= delta before calling book.modify_order. Alternatively, keep old_order and on failure call book.cancel_order(id) then reinsert the old order (priority is lost; better to check first).
4. In OrderBook::modify_order (order_book.rs:756), reject q <= 0 with an error. If the new price would cross (bid >= best_ask or ask <= best_bid), either reject the modify (ALO semantics) or route the replacement through the normal place/match path instead of the raw insert_order. HL parity is to cancel and place a new order through matching.
5. Add tests: a crossing modify, a zero/negative qty modify, a failed-margin modify that leaves the book unchanged, and a non-owner modify that is rejected.

**Unsure:** I did not check whether an outer layer rejects these first: the app.rs mempool/ante, an RPC signature path that limits a modify to the owner, or a whole-block state revert on an action error. A grep for checkpoint/rollback found nothing. I did not read the match/fill path, so I have not confirmed how it handles a 0-qty or crossed resting maker. I also did not check whether the trigger_stops or mark-price code assumes an uncrossed book.

</details>

**fable** — confirmed-bug, impact critical, effort M, lockstep yes

OrderBook::modify_order has two paths: an in-place path only when new_price is None and 0 < new_qty < remaining; everything else (price change, qty increase, qty == remaining, qty <= 0) does cancel_order + insert_order, which appends straight into bids/asks with no would_cross check, no execute_match, and no validation of new_price/new_qty sign. So a modify can leave a crossed book and can rest an order with zero or negative remaining_qty (both are explicitly asserted against in verify_invariants). In the executor, exec_modify_order calls book.modify_order and marks the book dirty first, and only afterwards computes the margin delta; on "insufficient margin" it returns err without re-inserting the old order, so the enlarged/repriced order stays resting unmargined. Additionally exec_modify_order receives no sender and does no ownership check (unlike exec_cancel_order), so any account can modify any order.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:702-746 — in-place branch only when new_price.is_none() and `new_q > ZERO && new_q < order.remaining_qty`; otherwise falls through
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:748-768 — fallback: `let old = self.cancel_order(order_id)?; replacement.price = p; replacement.remaining_qty = q; self.insert_order(replacement.clone())` — no sign checks, no cross check, no matching
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1185-1215 — insert_order just `book.entry(price).or_default().push_back(order)`; would_cross (1217-1222) is never consulted on this path
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:927-945 — verify_invariants asserts best_bid < best_ask and all remaining_qty > 0, i.e. both states produced by modify are declared invalid by the book itself
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3250-3254 — dispatch calls exec_modify_order(ctx, order_id, new_price, new_qty) without sender
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5361-5400 — book.modify_order() and dirty_books.insert happen first; `if bal.available < delta { return err(...) }` with no rollback of the already-mutated book
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5167-5170 — exec_cancel_order does check `order.trader != *sender`; modify has no equivalent
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5400-5407 — release path: `delta = old_margin - new_margin; release = delta.min(bal.order_margin)` — a negative new notional (negative price or qty) inflates delta and releases other orders' margin

**Risk:** Failing sequences. (1) Crossed book: trader A rests bid id=1 @100 x10, trader B rests ask id=2 @101 x10. A sends ModifyOrder{1, new_price:Some(105), new_qty:None}. modify_order cancels 1 and push_backs it into bids[105]; best_bid=105 >= best_ask=101, no fill emitted; verify_invariants panics; the book stays crossed until some taker arrives, and state-root/explorer consumers see a crossed L2. (2) Zero/negative qty: ModifyOrder{1, None, Some(0)} (or from_raw(-N)) skips the in-place guard and re-inserts with remaining_qty=0/negative; invariant 3 violated, and with negative price/qty the executor's release branch computes delta > old_margin and refunds up to all of bal.order_margin, i.e. margin backing other resting orders. (3) Margin bypass: A has one bid @100 x10 with available=0 (50 locked). A sends ModifyOrder{1, None, Some(100)}; book now rests 100 units; executor computes delta=450 > available=0, returns err, but does not restore the x10 order — A has 10x the exposure for the original 50 margin, and dirty_books already flags the market so the mutated book is persisted. (4) Ownership: any sender can run (1)-(3) against any other trader's order_id. Hyperliquid treats modify as cancel+new-order with full order validation/matching and margin checks; none of that holds here.

**Fix:** torus-core order_book.rs modify_order: reject new_price <= 0 or new_qty <= 0 up front (CoreError::InvalidPrice/InvalidQuantity); for the price-change path, after cancel_order build the replacement and route it through the same logic as place_order (would_cross -> execute_match for non-post-only, or reject post-only), returning fills, instead of raw insert_order. native_executor.rs exec_modify_order: take `sender`, look up `book.get_order(order_id)` and reject if `order.trader != *sender`; compute old/new notional and margin delta from the old order plus the requested fields BEFORE calling book.modify_order, and only call modify_order (and dirty_books.insert) once the balance check passes; alternatively keep the order of ops but on failure re-insert the saved old order via cancel_order + insert_order. Add tests: modify-to-crossing-price produces fills or rejection, modify to qty 0 is rejected, modify with insufficient margin leaves the original order untouched, modify by non-owner is rejected.

**Unsure:** Did not read crates/torus-rpc/src/lib.rs:1269 or any mempool/pre-check path, so an upstream RPC-level validation of new_price/new_qty > 0 or ownership may exist (it would not protect direct/consensus-level submissions). Did not confirm whether the executor's loop `for book in ctx.order_books.values_mut()` can accidentally modify a same-id order in another market (ids are stated to be globally coordinated via set_next_order_id). Did not run anything; fill emission on the crossed-book case is inferred from the absence of any execute_match call in the fallback path.

</details>

### session-scope-privilege

**opus** — confirmed-bug, impact high, effort S, lockstep yes

SessionScope::Full is a denylist. It allows every action except CreateSession, RevokeSession, Withdraw, Delegate, Undelegate, PermanentStake and ClaimRewards, and requires_eip712 uses the same seven. A Full-scope session key can therefore sign RotateValidatorKey, RegisterValidator, UpdateCommission, JailVote, UnjailSelf, TopUpSelfStake, SubmitProposal, Vote and SubmitOraclePrices. ListMarket, DelistMarket and UpdateMarketParams are also allowed, but they are no-op stubs that return ok with 0 effect. The executor gets only the resolved owner `sender`, so handlers such as exec_rotate_key cannot tell a session signature from an owner signature. Expired sessions are never pruned: count_sessions_for_owner counts every SESSIONS row whose owner matches and ignores expiry, and delete_session is only called from RevokeSession. Expired sessions keep counting toward MAX_SESSIONS_PER_ADDRESS=5 until the owner revokes them one by one (each revoke needs EIP-712), so after 5 sessions expire, new CreateSession calls fail with "max 5 active sessions exceeded".

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:244-252 SessionScope doc: Full = 'Everything except CreateSession, RevokeSession, Withdraw, Delegate, Undelegate, PermanentStake, ClaimRewards'
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:276-285 Full => !matches!(...) denylist; validator/governance/oracle actions are not excluded
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:748-759 requires_eip712 covers the same 7 actions only; RotateValidatorKey/RegisterValidator/Vote/SubmitOraclePrices are absent
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:817-835 resolve_sender: on a session sig it checks requires_eip712, expiry, scope.allows and then returns session.owner. Only the owner address goes downstream
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3276-3315 dispatch passes `sender` to exec_submit_oracle_prices, exec_vote, exec_register_validator, exec_jail_vote, exec_unjail_self, exec_rotate_key with no signature-type info
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5570-5585 exec_rotate_key calls staking.submit_key_rotation(*sender, ...) with no extra auth
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3327-3336 ListMarket/DelistMarket/UpdateMarketParams are stubs returning ok(…,0)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5615-5627 create_session rejects if count_sessions_for_owner >= MAX_SESSIONS_PER_ADDRESS
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:742-745 MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS=24h, MAX_SESSIONS_PER_ADDRESS=5
- crates/torus-state/src/db.rs:715-730 and crates/torus-state/src/backend.rs:85-96 count_sessions_for_owner counts all rows with matching owner and does not check expiry
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5675 delete_session is only called in exec_revoke_session (grep: no other non-test callers, no prune path)

**Risk:** Privilege: if a Full session key leaks (it is a 24h hot key held by a frontend or bot), whoever holds it can rotate the validator's consensus key, which can lead to validator takeover or equivocation slashing. It can also cast governance votes and file proposals, submit oracle prices as the validator (price manipulation if the owner is an oracle-eligible validator), change commission, jail-vote other validators, and register validators. On Hyperliquid, agent/API wallets can only place, cancel and modify orders. Validator, governance, oracle and transfer actions need the master key or the validator's own signer. The Full scope therefore breaks parity and widens the attack surface well beyond trading. Liveness/UX: expired sessions permanently use up the 5 slots. A user who opens 5 sessions (for example one per day) is locked out of new sessions until they send manual EIP-712 RevokeSession calls for the dead keys. Expired rows also stay in state forever, so the SESSIONS CF grows without bound. count_sessions_for_owner scans the whole CF on every CreateSession, which gets slower as the CF grows (a cheap DoS on execution time).

**Fix:** 1) Add the validator, governance and oracle actions to the requires_eip712 list in crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:748: RotateValidatorKey, RegisterValidator, UpdateCommission, JailVote, UnjailSelf, TopUpSelfStake, SubmitProposal, Vote, SubmitOraclePrices, ListMarket, DelistMarket, UpdateMarketParams. Mirror the same list in the SessionScope::Full exclusion (lib.rs:276), ideally by making Full = `!requires_eip712(action)` so the two cannot drift. A cleaner option is to make Full an allowlist of Trading plus TransfersOnly, which matches HL agent semantics. This changes consensus, so roll it out to the whole fleet in lockstep, as the existing O2/G3 warning describes. 2) In exec_create_session (native_executor.rs:5615), before the count check, prune the owner's expired sessions with deterministic, ms-based logic: iterate the owner's rows and call delete_session where expiry <= now_ms. Alternatively, change count_sessions_for_owner to take now_ms and count only rows with expiry > now_ms. Prefer pruning, because it also bounds state growth. It is also consensus-affecting, since it changes the state root. 3) Optionally add a secondary owner->pubkey index so counting does not require a full-CF scan. Add tests: a Full session signing RotateValidatorKey or Vote is rejected with RequiresEip712, and 5 expired sessions do not block a 6th CreateSession.

**Unsure:** I did not read the bodies of exec_vote, exec_register_validator, exec_submit_oracle_prices or staking.submit_key_rotation, so per-handler checks (oracle-submitter or validator-membership checks keyed on sender) are unverified. They would not stop the session holder anyway, because sender is the owner. I did not check whether NativeStateOverlay::iterate_cf includes pending (same-block) session writes, which could let the 5-session cap be bypassed within one block. I also did not confirm whether any CLI or frontend actually issues Full-scope sessions. RPC lib.rs:1394 uses Full only in a test fixture. The comparison with HL agent-wallet permissions comes from external knowledge, not from code.

</details>

**fable** — confirmed-bug, impact high, effort S, lockstep yes

Full-scope session keys are allowed to sign every NativeAction except the seven in a hardcoded denylist (CreateSession, RevokeSession, Withdraw, Delegate, Undelegate, PermanentStake, ClaimRewards). That denylist is duplicated verbatim in SessionScope::Full.allows() and in requires_eip712(); neither mentions RotateValidatorKey, RegisterValidator, Vote, JailVote, SubmitProposal, SubmitOraclePrices or ListMarket, so a Full session key can perform all of those validator/governance/oracle actions on behalf of its owner, and the executor dispatch has no additional signature-kind check. Separately, expired sessions are never pruned: count_sessions_for_owner scans CF_SESSIONS and counts every row for the owner without checking expiry, delete_session is only called from exec_revoke_session (and a test), so 5 expired 24h sessions permanently block new CreateSession until the owner explicitly revokes them with an EIP-712 RevokeSession.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:276-285 — SessionScope::Full => !matches!(CreateSession\|RevokeSession\|Withdraw\|Delegate\|Undelegate\|PermanentStake\|ClaimRewards); everything else allowed
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:748-758 — requires_eip712() has the identical 7-variant list; no validator/governance/oracle variants
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:820-838 — resolve_sender: Session path checks requires_eip712, expiry, scope.allows, then returns session.owner; this is the only gate
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:1144-1149 — batch verify path applies the same requires_eip712 + scope.allows checks
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:637-676 — NativeAction has Vote, SubmitOraclePrices, RegisterValidator, JailVote, RotateValidatorKey, ListMarket variants
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3276-3335 — dispatch for SubmitOraclePrices/Vote/RegisterValidator/JailVote/RotateValidatorKey/ListMarket takes only `sender`; grep for any session/signature-kind guard in native_executor.rs returned nothing
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5614-5625 — exec_create_session rejects when count_sessions_for_owner(sender) >= MAX_SESSIONS_PER_ADDRESS (5)
- crates/torus-state/src/db.rs:715-729 — count_sessions_for_owner iterates CF_SESSIONS and counts rows with data.owner == owner; no expiry filter
- crates/torus-state/src/db.rs:709-711 — delete_session is a plain CF delete; callers are only native_executor.rs:5675 (exec_revoke_session) and app.rs:9227 (test)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5598-5612 — session expiry capped at MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS = 24h, so sessions routinely expire

**Risk:** A leaked or compromised Full-scope session key (hot key on a trading bot, 24h lifetime) can rotate the owner's validator consensus key (RotateValidatorKey), register the owner as a validator with the attacker's pubkey, cast governance/jail votes, submit proposals, and submit oracle prices if the owner is an oracle-submitting validator. Hyperliquid's agent/API wallets are trading-only and cannot perform validator or governance operations, so this is a parity and security gap. The non-pruning of expired sessions means an active user who creates a fresh 24h session daily hits 'max 5 active sessions exceeded' on day 6 and must spend an EIP-712 RevokeSession per stale key; the error message 'active sessions' is also misleading because expired ones count.

**Fix:** 1) Extend the denylist once and derive both checks from it: in crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs make requires_eip712() also match RotateValidatorKey, RegisterValidator, JailVote, Vote, SubmitProposal, SubmitOraclePrices (and ListMarket if it is ever user-signable), and change SessionScope::Full.allows() in lib.rs:276 to `!requires_eip712(action)` so the two lists cannot drift. This is consensus-affecting (same lockstep-deploy warning as lib.rs:257-264). 2) In crates/torus-state/src/db.rs count_sessions_for_owner, take a `now_ms` argument and skip rows with data.expiry <= now_ms (and update StateBackend trait in backend.rs:85/198 plus the call at native_executor.rs:5615 passing ctx.timestamp*1000); optionally delete expired rows in exec_create_session before counting so CF_SESSIONS does not grow unbounded. Add tests: Full-scope session signing RotateValidatorKey/Vote must fail with SessionScopeViolation; 5 expired sessions must not block CreateSession.

**Unsure:** Did not read exec_rotate_validator_key / exec_register_validator / exec_vote bodies to confirm they have no implicit session rejection (dispatch at native_executor.rs:3276-3335 passes only `sender`, and grep for session/signature-kind guards in native_executor.rs was empty, so very likely none). Did not check whether RPC-side submission (torus-rpc) adds a pre-filter for session-signed governance actions; even if it did, consensus-path validation (eip712.rs:1144) would still accept them. Did not verify whether SubmitProposal is intended to be user-signable; ListMarket exec is a no-op (line 3335).

</details>

### exec-determinism

**opus** — not-a-bug, impact low, effort S, lockstep no

I found no concrete site in native_executor.rs or app.rs where HashMap/HashSet iteration, floating point, wall-clock time or thread scheduling changes consensus state writes. Every HashMap walk that touches state is sorted first or only feeds commutative work. Settlement is sorted with market_results.sort_by_key(market_id). Dirty books and save-books are sorted. Balance and position caches flush in sorted key order. Boot-load market ids are sorted. Cancel-all walks books in HashMap order, but it only adds up a FixedPoint margin total and applies one clamped release per action, so order does not matter. Floats and Instant::now appear only in metrics and timers. Wall-clock time is used once, for the proposer's header timestamp (app.rs:4734), and execution reads that value from the header, so all nodes see the same number. The remaining weak points are not divergence bugs: execute order depends on unwritten invariants (globally unique order ids, commutative sums), and the header timestamp is never checked.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- native_executor.rs:3631 market_batches is a HashMap; 3824 builds worker_batches by walking it in HashMap order; 3842 match_parallel returns results in that order
- native_executor.rs:3877-3883 A5 comment plus market_results.sort_by_key(\|m\| m.market_id), so settlement order is fixed (the trade_index and .min clamps depend on order)
- native_executor.rs:3664-3679 group_of HashMap is only a lookup; groups Vec is built in first-appearance order
- native_executor.rs:179-188 BalanceCache::flush_all sorts dirty addrs before put_native_balance
- native_executor.rs:2590-2591, 2778-2785, 2851-2852 dirty_books/order_books collected then sort_unstable
- native_executor.rs:2164, 2332-2333 boot load market_ids sorted; 2323 store_orders.keys() only used for a fatal-exit check (error message could name a different market on different nodes, but it is fatal either way)
- native_executor.rs:935-942 drain_books_parallel zips books with assign_chunks; caller sorts books at 2785, so LPT assignment is deterministic and only affects which worker drains
- native_executor.rs:5236-5263 exec_cancel_all None path walks order_books.keys() in HashMap order, adds up FixedPoint margin (commutative) and applies one .min(order_margin) release afterwards; the result does not depend on order
- native_executor.rs:5288-5330 exec_cancel_all_run uses the same HashMap-ordered market_ids for every action in the run; per-action release is a commutative sum then one clamp
- native_executor.rs:5168-5200 cancel_order and 5354+ modify_order take the first book in values()/values_mut() order that holds order_id; this is safe only because ids are global (4103 ctx.next_global_order_id)
- native_executor.rs:1542-1543 the only f64 outside metrics is a nanoseconds-to-seconds helper; all other f64 is .observe(...as_secs_f64())
- app.rs:4734-4737 build_proposal sets the header timestamp from SystemTime::now(); execution uses torus_block.header.timestamp (1680, 1857, 1870), so it is deterministic
- app.rs:1752 seen_in_block HashSet is used only for membership dedup during an in-order Vec walk; 2470 extend_into is a set union
- grep found no timestamp monotonicity or drift check in app.rs's non-test code (only header.timestamp reads at 1680/1857/1870/4635)

**Risk:** There is no divergence today. Three latent risks remain. (1) cancel_order and modify_order walk HashMap books and take the first match, which is safe only while order ids stay globally unique. If ids ever become per-book (for example a market re-seeded with set_next_order_id below the global counter), nodes would cancel or modify different orders and diverge. (2) The cancel-all paths are safe only while the per-market sum stays commutative. Moving the .min clamp inside the per-market loop, or emitting per-market events or results in that order into anything hashed, would make nodes diverge. (3) The header timestamp is never checked for monotonicity or drift against wall clock or parent. A malicious proposer can set any timestamp, which skews funding, oracle staleness (5600-5606 now_ms) and order expiry. That stays deterministic across nodes, but it is a manipulation vector, unlike HL's bounded block time.

**Fix:** These are optional hardening steps, since nothing currently diverges. (a) Switch NativeExecContext.order_books, margin_configs and dirty_books (native_executor.rs:1347-1356) to BTreeMap/BTreeSet, or sort the keys in exec_cancel_all (5236) and exec_cancel_all_run (5288), so iteration order no longer depends on a comment-level invariant. (b) In cancel_order and modify_order, look up the market from an order_id-to-market index instead of scanning values(), or add a debug_assert that exactly one book matches. (c) In app.rs's validate/execute path, reject a header whose timestamp is below the parent's or more than N seconds past local wall clock, and have build_proposal use max(now, parent.timestamp). (d) Add a CI determinism test that runs the same block on two contexts built with different RandomState seeds and compares state roots.

**Unsure:** Not checked: (1) inside torus-core order_book.rs and market_workers.rs (e.g. whether OrderBook uses BTreeMap internally, and whether match_parallel per-market output is deterministic). (2) The parallel settle path (settle_market_results_parallel, around 4331-4490) and phase2_parallel_prepare, beyond their claim to match serial byte for byte. (3) The EVM crate. (4) Whether node-local trade_index or receipts feed any hashed root. (5) Whether hotstuff validation outside app.rs bounds the timestamp. (6) Whether env-dependent engine/settle modes (TORUS_* thresholds) truly produce identical output; the comments say they do, but I did not verify it.

</details>

**fable** — partial, impact medium, effort S, lockstep no

The executor is largely determinism-hardened: order books are BTree-backed with HashMaps used only as indexes; order IDs are globally unique (ctx.next_global_order_id) so the HashMap::values() scans in exec_cancel_order/exec_modify_order are outcome-independent of order; save-path dirty_books are sorted before drain; boot rebuild sorts market ids; parallel engine/settle shards are sender/market-disjoint with a canonical apply pass; no floats in state math (f64 only in metrics/timing); no wall clock in exec (ctx.timestamp is the block's). Two residual hazards remain: (1) exec_cancel_all (market_id=None) and exec_cancel_all_run iterate `ctx.order_books.keys()` UNSORTED (std RandomState, random per process), so the cross-market cancel sequence and balance write sequence differ per node — state bytes still converge because the margin sum is commutative integer FixedPoint and puts are keyed, but it is one `sort_unstable()` away from being safe if any ordered journal/log ever consumes `cancelled`; (2) consensus-visible per-node env toggle TORUS_BOOK_ROWS (BookMode) changes persisted row layout/state root; it is documented as fleet-uniform/fresh-genesis but nothing in the executor enforces fleet agreement, so a misconfigured validator silently forks on state root.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**

- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:169-171, 3690-3692, 4061-4073 BalanceCache::merge_disjoint, worker shards disjoint by sender; :229 cross-market mutation on apply thread in canonical order; :4482-4496 plans zipped index-for-index with market_results
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1542-1543 only f64 is SaveTimings::secs (metrics); torus-core/src/order_book.rs:4701 only f64 is a bench print
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3842, 4968, 5606, 5716 all time inputs come from ctx.timestamp (block header), no SystemTime in exec
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:505-520, 556-563 BookMode from TORUS_BOOK_ROWS is 'Consensus-visible', 'Fleet-uniform, fresh genesis to change', read per process via OnceLock, not enforced
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:4734-4737 SystemTime::now only in build_proposal (proposer-side header timestamp); :1752 seen_in_block HashSet used for membership only
