### hl-api-compat

**opus** — absent, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes

There is no HL-compatible API surface. torus-rpc only offers jsonrpsee methods: torus_getOrderBook, getPosition, getOpenOrders, getUserTrades, getMarkPrice, submitNativeAction(s)(Bin), a subscribe method, and so on. Nothing serves HTTP /info or /exchange, and axum is only a dependency of torus-explorer. Reads could be handled by a stateless translator (HL /info -> torus_* RPC). Writes cannot, because the node verifies signatures only as ActionSignature::Eip712 over per-action typed structs (domain {name:"Torus",version:"1",chainId:7778,verifyingContract:0}, e.g. PlaceOrder(uint64 marketId,...,uint64 clientOrderId,bool hasClientOrderId,uint64 nonce)) or as Ed25519 session signatures. HL SDKs sign an L1 action differently: keccak(msgpack(action)||nonce||vault flag) becomes the connectionId in Agent(string source,bytes32 connectionId) under domain {name:"Exchange",chainId:1337}. User actions use the HyperliquidSignTransaction domain. A shim cannot re-sign for the user, so a third, consensus-level signature variant is needed. Field mapping is mostly clean: MarketId is u64, which maps to HL asset idx if perp ids are dense from 0 and spot is offset by 10000. FixedPoint uses 1e8 i128, which maps to HL decimal strings. TIF GTC/IOC/PostOnly maps to Gtc/Ioc/Alo. CancelOrder/CancelAllOrders/ModifyOrder exist. Nonces are ms timestamps (60s window), like HL. The real blocker is cloid: it is u64 in torus (PlaceOrderParams.client_order_id: Option<u64>) and 128-bit in HL.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:100-222 — only jsonrpsee #[method] endpoints (getOrderBook, getPosition, getOpenOrders, getUserTrades, submitNativeAction, submitNativeActionsBin, subscribe); no /info or /exchange
- grep: 'axum' only in crates/torus-explorer/Cargo.toml:9; no '/info' or '/exchange' or hyperliquid route anywhere in crates
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:7,24 — Domain {name:"Torus",version:"1",chainId:7778,verifyingContract:0x0}; TORUS_CHAIN_ID=7778
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:269-280 — PlaceOrder typehash: per-field typed struct with uint64 clientOrderId + bool hasClientOrderId + uint64 nonce (not HL's msgpack/Agent connectionId scheme)
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:852-855 — validate() rejects any chain id != TORUS_CHAIN_ID
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:332-340 — ActionSignature has only Eip712(Signature) and Session{ed25519}; no HL phantom-agent variant
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1060-1068 — PlaceOrderParams.client_order_id: Option<u64>; crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:47,107 same u64
- crates/torus-rpc/src/types.rs:337 — RPC exposes client_order_id as Option<String> (presentation is flexible; storage is not)
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:19,52-56 — MarketId=u64; FixedPoint(i128) with 8 decimals
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-597 — NativeAction has PlaceOrder, PlaceOrderBatch, CancelOrder{order_id}, CancelAllOrders, ModifyOrder; no cancel-by-cloid variant
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:706-709 — TIF GTC/IOC/FOK/PostOnly (maps to HL Gtc/Ioc/Alo; FOK has no HL equivalent)
- crates/torus-integration-tests/tests/rate_limit_mev.rs:138 — nonces are ms timestamps, Hyperliquid-style

**Risk:** HL SDKs (python/ts/rust) and bots compute their signature over HL's msgpack-plus-phantom-agent hash under chainId 1337 "Exchange". Torus's recover_sender will recover a garbage address from that signature or reject it, so no unmodified HL bot can trade. An off-chain shim cannot fix this without custody of user keys. A shim-held Torus session key would make the shim a custodian/agent, which is a trust regression. Separately, any 128-bit cloid would be truncated or hashed into u64. That breaks cancelByCloid round-trips and can cause cloid collisions per user, and once HL signing is honoured, the node must re-derive HL msgpack bytes losslessly from on-chain fields. Reads-only parity (/info) is low risk and achievable off-chain.

**Fix:** Phase 1 (no consensus change): add an HL-shaped HTTP server, preferably a new crate torus-hlapi on axum, or a route set in torus-node. POST /info with type in {meta, metaAndAssetCtxs, allMids, l2Book, clearinghouseState, openOrders, frontendOpenOrders, userFills, orderStatus}, each translated to the existing torus_* jsonrpsee calls (torus.rs:100-213). Asset idx = MarketId (perps) or 10000+spot idx. Prices are 1e8 FixedPoint rendered as strings with szDecimals. Add a WS adapter over torus_subscribe. Phase 2 (consensus-breaking): (a) Add ActionSignature::HlAgent{sig}, plus eip712.rs hl_l1_signing_hash(action, nonce, vault) = Agent{source:"a"|"b", connectionId: keccak(msgpack(hl_action)||nonce_be||0x00)} under domain {name:"Exchange",version:"1",chainId:1337,verifyingContract:0}. Also add the user-signed HyperliquidSignTransaction variants for withdraw and transfer. The node must canonically rebuild the HL msgpack from NativeAction fields, which needs an rmp-serde dep with exact HL field order and float-string formatting. (b) Widen client_order_id to Option<u128> or [u8;16] in PlaceOrderParams, order_book.rs:47/107 and the PlaceOrder typehash (uint128 clientOrderId); the action-hash encoders also change. (c) Add NativeAction::CancelByCloid{market_id, cloid} and HL-style ModifyOrder by oid|cloid. (d) Map HL grouping (normalTpsl/positionTpsl) and trigger orders onto existing StopMarket/TP types. Hook HlAgent into recover_sender/resolve_sender/batch_verify (eip712.rs:764-1155) and the trust-cache keying.

**Unsure:** I did not verify these, because of the time box. (1) Whether MarketIds are dense from 0 and whether spot markets have a separate index space. (2) Whether torus has a vaultAddress, expiresAfter or approveAgent equivalent; CreateSession (lib.rs:662) is Ed25519, not an HL-style secp256k1 API wallet, so HL approveAgent would need its own mapping. (3) Whether trigger-order and TP/SL OrderType variants cover HL's tpsl/grouping semantics. (4) Torus nonce rules versus HL's 'highest 100 nonces per signer' rule; I only confirmed the 60s ms window (eip712.rs:27). (5) Whether a candle/funding-history source exists for /info candleSnapshot and fundingHistory. The HL signing scheme details are from my own knowledge of the HL SDK and were not checked against an external source.

</details>

**fable** — design, impact high, effort XL, lockstep yes

Torus has no HL-shaped surface today: the RPC is a jsonrpsee `torus_*` namespace (getOrderBook/getMarkets/getPosition/getBalances/getOpenOrders/getUserTrades/getMarkPrice/submitNativeAction...) and actions are `SignedNativeAction{action, nonce(ms), signature}` signed under an EIP-712 domain {name "Torus", version "1", chainId 7778, verifyingContract 0x0} with one typed struct per NativeAction variant (e.g. `PlaceOrder(uint64 marketId,bool isBuy,int128 price,int128 quantity,uint8 orderType,uint8 timeInForce,bool reduceOnly,uint64 clientOrderId,bool hasClientOrderId,uint64 nonce)`). Hyperliquid signs a phantom `Agent(string source,bytes32 connectionId)` under domain {name "Exchange", version "1", chainId 1337} where connectionId = keccak(msgpack(action) || nonce || vault flag), so an HL SDK signature is over entirely different bytes and cannot be verified by Torus's current validator/proposer path. A stateless read-side /info shim and a /exchange shim that translates request/response JSON are feasible; a non-custodial /exchange shim is NOT feasible without a consensus-level change to accept the HL signature scheme (and either carry raw HL action bytes or canonically re-msgpack the translated action). Reads map reasonably (l2Book<-getOrderBook, meta<-getMarkets with asset index = position in a shim-maintained stable universe table, openOrders<-getOpenOrders, userFills<-getUserTrades, allMids<-getMarkPrice per market); clearinghouseState needs N getPosition calls since getPosition is per (trader, market_id); candleSnapshot and funding history have no RPC backing in the method list I read.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:7,24: domain {Torus,1,7778,0x0}; TORUS_CHAIN_ID=7778
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:163-175: eip712_domain_separator hard-codes name/version/chainId/verifyingContract
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:195-247: per-variant struct hash over NativeAction fields (not over serialized bytes) - incompatible with HL connectionId=keccak(msgpack(action)+nonce)
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:252-271: PlaceOrder fields encode clientOrderId as uint64 + hasClientOrderId bool; typehash string fixes width
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:27,860-863: nonce is ms timestamp, +/-60s window (HL SDK default nonce = now ms, so compatible in principle)
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:16,19: OrderId = u128, MarketId = u64 (HL oid is u64 JSON int; HL asset is u32 index into meta.universe)
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-660: NativeAction variants - no CancelByCloid, no UpdateLeverage/UpdateIsolatedMargin, no TWAP, no batchModify; CancelOrder/ModifyOrder key on order_id only
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1060-1095: PlaceOrderParams.client_order_id: Option<u64>; OrderType Limit/Market/StopMarket/StopLimit; TIF GTC/IOC/FOK/PostOnly (HL Gtc/Ioc/Alo + trigger tp/sl map; no tp-vs-sl or positionTpsl grouping)
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:332-340: ActionSignature = Eip712(secp256k1) \| Session(ed25519) - no slot for HL agent-style signature
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:951-957: SignedNativeAction{action, nonce, signature}
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:100-213: torus_* method list (getOrderBook(market_id: String), getPosition(trader, market_id), getMarkets, getOpenOrders, getUserTrades, getMarkPrice, submitNativeAction -> String hash); no candles/funding-history method
- crates/torus-rpc/src/types.rs:328,337: order_id and client_order_id serialized as String in RPC (HL expects oid as int, cloid as 0x-hex16)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs:179,204 and validator.rs:321,363: senders recovered from EIP-712 signatures in consensus path - any new signature scheme must be accepted here by all validators

**Risk:** Without HL-compatible signing, every HL SDK/bot (hyperliquid-python-sdk, TS SDK, Hummingbot connector, CCXT hyperliquid) fails at the first /exchange call; only a custodial shim (shim holds the user's key and re-signs as Torus EIP-712) works, which is a security regression and not real parity. Cloid: HL cloid is 128-bit (0x + 32 hex) and bots rely on cancelByCloid/round-trip; Torus u64 cloid + no CancelByCloid means the shim must keep a lossy cloid->u64/order_id table, which breaks on shim restart and across shim instances. OrderId u128 as JSON string vs HL integer oid breaks TS SDK parsing and Python type hints. Synchronous HL order responses (statuses: resting{oid}/filled/error) vs Torus async hash return forces the shim to block until inclusion, adding block-time latency and a new failure mode (timeout with unknown state). Asset indexes must be stable across market delistings or bots trade the wrong market.

**Fix:** Phase 1 (no consensus change, L): new crate `torus-hl-shim` (axum) exposing POST /info and /exchange. /info: translate type l2Book->torus_getOrderBook, meta/metaAndAssetCtxs->getMarkets+getMarkPrice+getOpenInterest, clearinghouseState->getBalances + getPosition per market, openOrders->getOpenOrders, userFills->getUserTrades; maintain a persisted universe table [asset_index -> MarketId] appended on ListMarket and never compacted on DelistMarket; convert FixedPoint<->HL decimal strings and derive szDecimals from lot_size. /exchange in phase 1 only accepts Torus-signed payloads (SDK fork) or an explicit agent-key mode where the user does a Torus `CreateSession` and the shim signs with the ed25519 session key (ActionSignature::Session, lib.rs:336) - this is the closest analogue to HL's approveAgent flow and keeps the shim non-custodial of the main key. Phase 2 (consensus-breaking, XL): add `ActionSignature::HlAgent{sig, raw_action: Vec<u8>}` in torus-types/src/lib.rs and a verifier in eip712.rs that recomputes HL's connectionId = keccak(raw_msgpack || nonce_be || 0x00) and the Agent typehash under domain {Exchange,1,1337}, then deterministically decodes raw_action into NativeAction in the executor; widen `client_order_id` to Option<u128> (update PlaceOrder typehash string at eip712.rs:273-276, action_hash encoding lib.rs:712, RPC types.rs:337) and add `NativeAction::CancelByCloid{market_id, cloid}` plus `UpdateLeverage{market_id, leverage, cross}`; expose oid as a u64-fitting integer (verify OrderId construction fits). Shim then returns HL status shapes by waiting on the streams.rs subscription for the action hash.

**Unsure:** Did not verify how OrderId u128 values are constructed (whether they fit u64 in practice) or FixedPoint's decimal scale; did not read streams.rs to confirm a per-action-hash inclusion notification exists; did not confirm absence of funding-history/candle RPCs beyond the trait method list in torus.rs:100-213; HL signing details (Agent typehash, chainId 1337, msgpack connectionId, nonce window of ~2 days/100-nonce set) are from my knowledge of the HL SDK, not from repo code.

</details>

### ingress-rate-limits

**opus** — partial, impact medium, effort M, lockstep no

The native-action limits that exist are capacity caps, not budgets earned by trading. The mempool caps pending native actions at 512 per sender. Block selection takes at most 64 actions per sender per block; this is a proposer-local env override, and anything left over waits for the next block. A PlaceOrderBatch must hold between 1 and the batch cap orders. The whole pool is capped at 65536 entries. Once the pool holds more than (recent commit rate x 20s horizon), ingress sheds everything except cancels before verifying signatures; this check is global, not per address. The only time-windowed per-address limiter (TxSubmitLimiter, 50 per 10s) is wired only into EVM eth_sendRawTransaction, not into native submit. Nothing resembles HL's per-address request budget earned from traded volume (about 1 request per 1 USDC traded plus an initial buffer). Resting orders are capped at 200 per trader per market at exec time, but there is no account-wide open-order cap scaled by volume (HL: 1000 base, up to 5000).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-mempool/src/rate_limit.rs:180 NATIVE_PER_SENDER_CAP = 512 (max pending native actions per sender in pool)
- crates/torus-mempool/src/native_pool.rs:195-198 per-sender pool cap returns NativeSenderQueueFull
- crates/torus-mempool/src/rate_limit.rs:58-70 NATIVE_PER_BLOCK_CAP=64 per sender per block, proposer-local, env TORUS_NATIVE_PER_BLOCK_CAP
- crates/torus-mempool/src/native_pool.rs:261-275 drain enforces per-sender-per-block cap; excess stays in pool
- crates/torus-mempool/src/rate_limit.rs:125-176 global admission limit = commit rate x horizon (20s default), floor 4 blocks; 0 disables
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:422-433 pre-verify shed of non-cancels when pool full or admission backlogged (global, not per address)
- crates/torus-mempool/src/rate_limit.rs:383-405 order_count/validate_batch_size: batch must be 1..=NATIVE_ORDERS_PER_BATCH_CAP
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:304 validate_batch_size called at native ingress before sig verify
- crates/torus-rpc/src/lib.rs:190-226 TxSubmitLimiter: per-sender count per 10s window
- crates/torus-rpc/src/lib.rs:309 TxSubmitLimiter::new(50) and crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:625-628: the only call site is EVM send_raw_transaction (grep shows no native use)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:28,411 MAX_ORDERS_PER_TRADER_PER_MARKET = 200 resting-order cap, enforced at exec
- crates/torus-mempool/src/lib.rs:96 EVM pool max_per_sender = 16

**Risk:** Any funded or signed address can keep 512 actions pending and get up to 64 per block, whatever it has traded. That falls short of HL in three ways. First, there is no time-windowed per-address throttle on native RPC ingress, so one address can churn place/cancel indefinitely. The only brakes are dedup, the nonce window and the pool cap. Second, the admission shed is global: one spammer filling the pool to the backlog threshold makes every other user's non-cancel actions get the "busy" response (cancels are exempt). Third, the 200-per-market resting cap multiplied by the number of markets gives no account-wide cap. The 64-per-block cap is not consensus-validated; that is by design, but a byzantine proposer can ignore it. The cost of spam is signature verification, gossip and DA writes on every node. HL's volume-based budget also makes sybil spam cost money, because new addresses only get a small initial allowance.

**Fix:** 1) Add a native per-address request budget in torus-mempool. Keep a per-sender counter of actions in a rolling window (reuse the TxSubmitLimiter shape, or a token bucket). Check it in the native submit path at torus-rpc/src/torus.rs around line 304, after the sender is recovered. Charge order_count(), not one per action, and exempt cancels or charge them less. 2) Parity version: add per-address `cum_volume` to state, updated in the native_executor fill path. Set the budget to an initial buffer (HL uses 10k) plus 1 per 1 USDC of cumulative volume, minus requests used. Keep it in state so it is the same on every node, and decrement it at exec in native_executor (then it is consensus-breaking). Ingress can keep a local approximate pre-check. 3) Add an account-wide open-order cap in torus-core (count trader_orders across all markets) at 1000 plus volume tiers up to 5000. Reject new non-reduce-only orders over the cap, as HL does. 4) Optionally, make the admission shed per sender: shed the senders with the most pending actions first rather than every non-cancel.

**Unsure:** The ingress-only per-address limiter (fix 1) does not break consensus. A state-backed volume budget and an account-wide open-order cap enforced at exec (fixes 2-3) would. I did not check torus-network gossip ingress for its own per-peer or per-sender limits. I did not read where the native nonce window is enforced; it bounds replay, not rate. I did not check whether the session-key path adds any per-session limits. I did not look for a websocket/HTTP connection-level limiter such as tower governor (grep for "governor" found nothing in torus-rpc).

</details>

**fable** — partial, impact medium, effort M, lockstep no

Native-action ingress has NO per-address rate limiter: the only per-sender throttle at RPC is TxSubmitLimiter (50 tx / 10 s sliding window) and it is applied solely to EVM eth_sendRawTransaction, not to torus_submitAction/batch endpoints. Native actions are guarded by structural caps instead: PlaceOrderBatch size validation (1..=NATIVE_ORDERS_PER_BATCH_CAP) at ingress, a pool-wide admission limit (recent commit rate x 20 s horizon, floor 4 blocks) that sheds non-cancels pre-verify with "busy, retry", a per-sender pending-pool cap of 512 actions (NativeSenderQueueFull), a global pool cap of 65536, and proposer-local per-block caps (64 actions/sender, 400 actions and 200k orders total). The only open-order cap is in the matching engine: MAX_ORDERS_PER_TRADER_PER_MARKET = 200 (rejection at execution, so spam still costs consensus/DA). Nothing is volume-derived (no HL-style address budget earned from traded volume), no per-IP limiting, and no cumulative open-order cap across markets.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-rpc/src/lib.rs:190-220 TxSubmitLimiter: per-sender (count, window_start) with 10 s window; lib.rs:309 constructed as TxSubmitLimiter::new(50)
- crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:624-629 send_raw_transaction is the only caller of check_sender (grep over torus-rpc/torus-node found no other call site)
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:302-310 native verify path: validate_batch_size + validate_known_markets + signature verification; no per-sender counter
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:420-450 and 1109-1121 pre-verify shed: pool full or native_admission_backlogged() rejects non-cancel actions (global, not per-address)
- crates/torus-mempool/src/rate_limit.rs:131-176 ADMISSION_RATE_WINDOW_MS=10_000, DEFAULT_ADMISSION_HORIZON_MS=20_000, admission_limit = commit rate x horizon, floored at 4 x block cap; 0 = off
- crates/torus-mempool/src/rate_limit.rs:178-180 NATIVE_PER_SENDER_CAP=512; rate_limit.rs:57-58 NATIVE_PER_BLOCK_CAP=64; rate_limit.rs:98 NATIVE_TOTAL_BLOCK_CAP=400; rate_limit.rs:215 NATIVE_ORDERS_PER_BLOCK_CAP=200_000 (all proposer-local selection policy, not validate_block)
- crates/torus-mempool/src/native_pool.rs:194-213 per-sender cap -> NativeSenderQueueFull; pool cap 65536 -> NativePoolFull with cancel-priority eviction
- crates/torus-mempool/src/rate_limit.rs:390-403 validate_batch_size rejects empty or oversize PlaceOrderBatch
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:28 MAX_ORDERS_PER_TRADER_PER_MARKET=200; order_book.rs:409-417 rejects at place time
- grep for volume/cum_vlm/address budget in torus-rpc, torus-mempool, torus-core: no hits

**Risk:** A single address with a valid key can submit up to 512 pending native actions (each a batch of up to NATIVE_ORDERS_PER_BATCH_CAP orders) and refill continuously as blocks commit, paying only signature-verify cost on the RPC node; the admission limit is global so one spammer degrades admission for all users (everyone gets "busy"), and the 200-orders-per-market cap is only enforced after the action has consumed gossip, DA and block space. HL parity gap: no volume-earned action budget (HL: 10k base + 1 action per $1 traded, cancels exempt-ish), no cumulative open-order cap (HL: 1000 per account), no per-IP throttling.

**Fix:** Add an address-budget limiter for native ingress: (1) in torus-rpc/src/torus.rs verify path (around line 302) call a new rate_limit::check_native_sender(sender, order_count(&action.action), is_cancel) before signature verification where cheap (sender is only known post-verify, so place it right after validate_with_sessions and before mempool admission); (2) implement it in torus-mempool/src/rate_limit.rs as a per-address token bucket keyed on torus_types::Address, charged by order_count (reuse the existing helper), with cancels exempt and a base allowance plus volume-earned refill read from the account's cumulative volume in torus-state (add a cum_volume field or reuse fee/volume tier data from torus-economics); (3) optionally make the matching-engine MAX_ORDERS_PER_TRADER_PER_MARKET companion a per-account global cap (e.g. 1000) checked in native_executor.rs before placement. Keep existing per-sender pool cap and admission limit as backstops.

**Unsure:** Did not read torus-node RPC server construction for any HTTP-layer (tower/jsonrpsee) per-connection or per-IP limits; grep over torus-node/src for RateLimit/governor/per_ip found none, but jsonrpsee server builder settings (max connections, max request body) were not inspected. Did not verify whether gossip-admitted actions (add_native_action_from_gossip) also honour NATIVE_PER_SENDER_CAP, nor whether torus-economics tracks per-address cumulative volume that a budget could draw on.

</details>

### realized-pnl

**opus** — present, impact low, effort S, lockstep no

The realized PnL logic is correct. The pure `fill_transition` handles open, increase (weighted-average entry), partial close, full close and flip. Every close component pays (fill_price - entry) * closed_qty for longs and the reverse for shorts. On a flip only the old position's size is used for the PnL, and the remainder opens at fill_price. The executor applies the same transition to both the taker and the maker of each fill and credits each side's `closed_pnl` to its `available` balance, in fill order, through `BalanceCache`. Per fill, realized PnL is not zero-sum between the two counterparties, because each side is measured against its own entry price. That matches Hyperliquid: the matching loss stays unrealized in the other holders' positions, so total equity (balances plus unrealized PnL) is conserved.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:434-526 fill_transition: None->open (pnl None); same_dir->weighted avg entry (pnl None); fill_qty<size partial close pnl_per*fill_qty; == full close returns (None, Some(pnl_per*fill_qty)); flip close_pnl=pnl_per*pos.size, remainder=fill_qty-pos.size opens at fill_price
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:309-331 apply_fill credits pnl via credit_realized_pnl (bal.available += pnl, lines 386-391)
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:362-382 apply_fill_cached_effect uses the identical fill_transition and touches no balance; returns closed_pnl
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4649-4677 per fill, both taker (is_buy = maker_side != Buy) and maker (is_buy = maker_side==Buy) apply the fill at the same qty/price; closed_pnl pushed as pnl_events
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4535-4549 pnl_events credited bal.available += pnl via bal_cache in fill order; balance load error or position fill_error rejects the order
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4718-4736 apply_fill_via_caches credits closed_pnl to bal_cache.available identically

**Risk:** There is no bug in the sign or the netting. Remaining parity gaps, not checked in depth: (1) FixedPoint truncation in `pnl_per*qty` and in the weighted-average `entry_price` (`total_cost/new_size`) can leave dust, so balances may drift by a few ulps over many fills. (2) A negative realized PnL is added straight to `available` with no floor at this point, so a deficit beyond the trader's equity relies on liquidation or ADL elsewhere. (3) If the taker side applies and the maker side then errors, the order is rejected, but I did not confirm that the taker's position-cache write is rolled back.

**Fix:** No change needed for correctness. Optional hardening:
- Add a property test asserting that sum(balance changes) + sum(unrealized PnL at mark) is unchanged across random fill sequences, including flips.
- Check that `pos_cache` is discarded or reverted when `fill_error` is set (around native_executor.rs:4672 and 4549).

**Unsure:** I did not verify these:
- Whether a mid-fill error (taker applied, maker failed) leaves a partially mutated `pos_cache` that later gets flushed.
- FixedPoint rounding mode, and dust accumulation from it.
- Whether fees are settled separately from realized PnL.
- That liquidation and ADL paths use the same `fill_transition`.

</details>

**fable** — not-a-bug, impact low, effort S, lockstep no

Realized PnL is computed in the pure `fill_transition` (crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:434-516) for partial close, full close and flip with the correct sign convention (long: fill-entry; short: entry-fill) times the closed quantity only (flip uses pos.size, remainder opens fresh at fill_price). The executor credits that `closed_pnl` to `bal.available` through the per-batch BalanceCache on both the sequential (`apply_fill_via_caches`, native_executor.rs:4712-4738, called for taker then maker at 4178-4200) and parallel (recorded pnl_events replayed in fill order, 4535-4543) paths, including `Some(ZERO)` so a flat close still materializes the balance row. Both counterparties see the same fill.price and fill.quantity, so cash flows are symmetric; realized PnL across all traders nets to zero over the full open->close lifecycle except for FixedPoint truncation dust (i256 mul/div truncating toward zero at 1e-8 scale in torus-types/src/lib.rs:89,103, plus the weighted-average entry division at position.rs:461-464), which is the same order of dust Hyperliquid itself has with fixed-decimal entry prices.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:466-516: partial/full/flip branches compute pnl_per by side and multiply by the closed qty only; flip opens remainder at fill_price with realized_pnl reset
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:318-331: classic apply_fill credits pnl via credit_realized_pnl (bal.available += pnl, 386-391)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4712-4738: apply_fill_via_caches credits effect.closed_pnl to bal_cache (available += pnl)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4178-4200: sequential path applies taker then maker for each fill with the same fill.quantity/fill.price, opposite is_buy
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4656-4675, 4535-4543: parallel path records (side, trader, pnl) events in fill order, then replays into bal_cache in that order
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:87-103: checked_mul/checked_div use i256 then truncating division by SCALE (10^8)

**Risk:** No exploit path found. Residual: (1) truncation dust of up to 1e-8 per fill side can leave the system a few sats off exact zero-sum over many fills (insurance/fee pool is not reconciled against it); (2) on a backend I/O error between the taker and maker fill application (native_executor.rs:4200-4221, `break` then `continue`), the taker's position/PnL stay in pos_cache/bal_cache while the maker's are not applied, so unless the whole batch is discarded on that error the pair is unbalanced — only reachable on storage failure, not by a user.

**Fix:** None required for correctness. Optional hardening: add a property test in crates/torus-core/src/position.rs that drives random fill sequences through fill_transition for a buyer/seller pair and asserts sum(realized) + sum(unrealized at any common mark) == 0 within SCALE dust; and in the executor, make a mid-order fill failure abort the batch (or roll back the taker's cache entries) rather than `continue`.

**Unsure:** Did not verify whether a fill-application error aborts/rolls back the whole batch (would eliminate residual (2)). Did not find an explicit zero-sum/conservation test (grep for conserv|zero_sum in torus-core and torus-bridge tests returned nothing); fill_transition unit tests were not located within the time box. Did not check fee deduction or funding interaction with realized PnL.

</details>

### insurance-fund

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

The insurance fund is a single raw i128 under key b"insurance_fund" in CF_NATIVE_BALANCES (liquidation.rs:59, 432-450). In production the only thing that touches it is execute_liquidation, which adds a fixed penalty (DEFAULT_LIQUIDATION_PENALTY_BPS × notional) to it on every liquidation (liquidation.rs:209-218). Nothing ever spends it. socialize_loss, the only function that draws it down (liquidation.rs:344-365), has no caller outside tests. The native executor sends any remaining_deficit straight to auto_deleverage and ignores the result (native_executor.rs:5971-5979). The fund is not seeded at genesis, and no RPC exposes it: grep finds no "insurance" in torus-rpc, torus-consensus, torus-economics, torus-node or any json/toml config. When there is a deficit, the trader's balance is clamped to 0 (liquidation.rs:233-239) and the fund, empty or full, is skipped. Whatever loss auto_deleverage cannot cover is dropped without a log or error.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:59 const INSURANCE_FUND_KEY = b"insurance_fund" (a raw key inside CF_NATIVE_BALANCES)
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:209-218 penalty = notional*penalty_bps/10000 is added to the fund before the trader's solvency is checked
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:220-239 trader bal.available += pnl - penalty; a negative balance is clamped to 0 and returned as remaining_deficit, so the penalty is credited to the fund even when the trader cannot pay it (unbacked)
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:344-365 socialize_loss takes from the fund first, then spreads the rest across traders; 418-426 logs any unrecoverable deficit with a warning
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5965-5979 the only production liquidation path: on remaining_deficit>0 it calls auto_deleverage (result discarded with let _ =); it never calls socialize_loss and never reads the fund
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:282-330 auto_deleverage closes profitable counterparties and credits their realized PnL; any loss_amount left after the loop is not passed back to the caller
- grep 'insurance' across crates/torus-rpc, torus-consensus, torus-economics, torus-node and *.json/*.toml config: no hits (genesis does not seed it, RPC does not expose it)
- grep 'socialize_loss' outside liquidation.rs and tests: no hits

**Risk:** Losses are never covered by the insurance fund (Hyperliquid covers them through the HLP/liquidator vault), so the fund only grows and serves no purpose. Two accounting problems follow. (1) The fund is credited a penalty the bankrupt trader never paid, because the trader's balance is clamped to 0 after the penalty is subtracted. Value is minted into the fund on exactly the liquidations that leave a deficit. (2) A deficit that ADL cannot fully cover disappears with no log. Its counterparties' PnL is still credited in full, so total balances can exceed the collateral backing them, and the protocol goes insolvent with no trace. Users and operators also cannot see the fund's balance over RPC, unlike Hyperliquid's public vault and clearinghouse state.

**Fix:** 1. In execute_liquidation, cap the penalty at what the trader can pay: penalty_paid = min(penalty, max(0, bal.available + pnl (+ isolated_margin))), and credit only that amount. 2. In native_executor.rs around 5971, on remaining_deficit > 0 first call a new LiquidationEngine::draw_insurance_fund(state, deficit) that returns the uncovered remainder. Send only that remainder to auto_deleverage, and change auto_deleverage to return the remaining loss too. Then either call socialize_loss on the rest or record it in a protocol bad_debt key with a metric and a warning. 3. Make get_insurance_fund pub. Add an RPC method (for example torus_getInsuranceFund, or a field on the existing clearinghouse/market state RPC) and an optional genesis seed amount in the genesis config. 4. Add a deterministic test for a deficit when the fund is empty and when it is partially funded. All of this changes state transitions, so it is consensus-breaking and needs a hard-fork/height gate.

**Unsure:** Not checked: whether the genesis builder writes raw CF_NATIVE_BALANCES keys some other way (I only grepped for "insurance"); whether a generic native-balance RPC could read the "insurance_fund" key by accident; whether the end of auto_deleverage (after line 330) logs leftover loss. Also not confirmed: whether ADL's PnL credit to counterparties, after the bankrupt position was deleted rather than taken over, creates value. That depends on how the trades are matched, which I did not trace.

</details>

**fable** — unwired, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

The insurance fund is a single raw key `b"insurance_fund"` in CF_NATIVE_BALANCES (liquidation.rs:59, 432-450) with private get/set. It is never seeded: `get_insurance_fund` returns ZERO when the key is absent, and a grep for "insurance" across all crates hits only liquidation.rs and crates/torus-core/tests/liquidation_tests.rs (which writes the key by hand at :364). It is credited only inside `execute_liquidation` (liquidation.rs:214-218) and debited only inside `socialize_loss` (liquidation.rs:358-365); neither path is reachable in production: `socialize_loss` has no caller outside liquidation.rs, and `run_liquidation_checks` (native_executor.rs:5922) is itself never called from app.rs, whose per-block tail runs only drain_core_writer/process_governance/distribute_fees/process_epoch_boundary (app.rs:1937-1940). No RPC method in crates/torus-rpc references it.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:59 INSURANCE_FUND_KEY = b"insurance_fund" (no genesis seed anywhere; grep across crates hits only this file and a test)
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:432-440 get_insurance_fund returns FixedPoint::ZERO when key absent/wrong length
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:209-218 execute_liquidation credits 2.5% notional penalty to fund
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:233-239 deficit computed, trader balance clamped to ZERO, deficit returned in LiquidationResult; fund NOT touched here
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:345-367 socialize_loss drains fund first, then socializes remainder across traders; with empty fund (fund_balance == 0) the whole loss is socialized
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5965-5979 run_liquidation_checks: on remaining_deficit > 0 it calls auto_deleverage only, never socialize_loss, and ignores the ADL result (let _ =)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5922 run_liquidation_checks defined; grep shows no caller outside its own definition
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1937-1940 per-block tail: drain_core_writer, process_governance, distribute_fees, process_epoch_boundary only
- crates/torus-rpc: grep for "insurance" returns nothing

**Risk:** HL parity gap: Hyperliquid's HLP/insurance vault is funded, absorbs liquidation deficits before ADL, and is queryable. Here the fund is zero at genesis and dead code in production. Even if `run_liquidation_checks` were wired, a deficit (liquidation.rs:233-239) is clamped off the trader's balance (bad debt silently erased, creating unbacked balance), the insurance fund is never consulted for the deficit, and the deficit goes straight to auto_deleverage whose result is discarded; `socialize_loss` (the only fund-debit path) is unreachable. With an empty fund, socialize_loss would push 100% of the loss onto other traders' positions.

**Fix:** 1) Seed: add an optional `insurance_fund` amount to native genesis config and write the key in the genesis state-build path (make get/set pub(crate) or add `LiquidationEngine::seed_insurance_fund`). 2) Wire: in native_executor.rs run_liquidation_checks, on lr.remaining_deficit > 0 call `socialize_loss` (fund first) before/instead of `auto_deleverage`, and propagate errors instead of `let _ =`; call run_liquidation_checks from the app.rs:1937 tail with mark/oracle prices once those are computed. 3) Expose: add `torus_getInsuranceFund` in crates/torus-rpc reading CF_NATIVE_BALANCES/insurance_fund via a pub getter. 4) Add a test asserting deficit draws from fund before ADL.

**Unsure:** Did not read the native genesis/state-bootstrap code directly; conclusion that it is unseeded rests on a repo-wide grep for "insurance" returning only liquidation.rs and one test. Did not verify whether a separate HLP-style vault exists under another name in torus-economics.

</details>

### end-of-block-hook

**opus** — partial, impact critical, effort L, lockstep yes

There is a deterministic end-of-block tail. It runs inside `execute_committed_block_with` (crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1425), right after the two `NativeExecutor::execute_batch` calls (app.rs:1902-1903) and the fatal-error check. It calls `drain_core_writer`, `process_governance`, `distribute_fees` and `process_epoch_boundary`, in that order (app.rs:1937-1940). There is no begin-block hook. `NativeExecutor::aggregate_oracle_prices` (native_executor.rs:5904) and `run_liquidation_checks` (native_executor.rs:5923) exist, but the only hits for either name in crates/ are their definitions, so they are never called. I found no funding, TWAP or trigger driver: the grep found no `settle_funding`, `apply_funding`, `check_triggers` or `twap` names in crates/.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1425 `fn execute_committed_block_with(` is the function that contains the exec pipeline
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1902-1903 NativeExecutor::execute_batch(&mut ctx, &pre_evm) / (&post_evm)
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1909-1925 the fatal_error fail-stop returns before the tail phases
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1936-1940 the tail: drain_core_writer, process_governance, distribute_fees(computed_fee_revenue), process_epoch_boundary. This is the existing end-block hook point
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5903-5921 aggregate_oracle_prices(ctx, markets, validator_stakes) calls ctx.oracle.aggregate_price(market, ctx.block_height, stakes)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5923-5935 run_liquidation_checks(ctx, traders, oracle_prices) iterates over margin_configs and uses LiquidationEngine::check/execute/auto_deleverage (lines 5938-5976)
- grep -rn aggregate_oracle_prices\|run_liquidation_checks over crates/: the only hits are the definitions at native_executor.rs:5904 and :5923, so neither has a caller
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6025-6029 process_epoch_boundary returns early unless EpochManager::is_epoch_boundary; this is the gating pattern to copy for a funding interval

**Risk:** Oracle prices are submitted (exec_submit_oracle_prices at native_executor.rs:5685) but never aggregated. Underwater positions are never swept or ADL'd. Funding, TWAP slices and stop/TP triggers have no driver at all. The perps engine therefore cannot behave like Hyperliquid, where every block runs oracle/mark updates, liquidations, funding accrual, TWAP slices and trigger evaluation. Because the tail sits behind the fail-stop and before the overlay flush, anything added there commits atomically with the block's state.

**Fix:** Add one entry point in native_executor.rs (next to process_epoch_boundary, about line 6025): `pub fn end_block<T>(ctx: &mut NativeExecContext<T>)`. It would run, in a fixed order: (1) aggregate_oracle_prices over listed markets, using validator stakes from ctx.staking; (2) read the aggregated prices; (3) evaluate stop/TP triggers and place them into the books; (4) TWAP slices whose next_slice_height <= ctx.block_height; (5) run_liquidation_checks, over the trader set from a deterministic sorted index such as a BTreeSet of open-position addresses, not a HashMap; (6) funding accrual gated on ctx.block_height % funding_interval == 0, or on the timestamp hour boundary from ctx.block_timestamp. Call it at crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1937, immediately after `drain_core_writer` and before `process_governance`. Liquidation and trigger fills then flow through the same writer and fee path. Matched orders from triggers and TWAP must run before `drain_core_writer`, or the writer has to be drained a second time. Optionally add a `begin_block` before app.rs:1902 for oracle aggregation, so the prices are fresh for that block's matching. Every replay path (the test harness at app.rs:12926-12928) must call the same hook.

**Unsure:** I did not check whether other execution paths (exec_pipeline.rs, the proposal/speculative exec path, RPC simulate) duplicate this tail and would need the hook too; the comment at app.rs:1988 mentions exec_pipeline.rs. I did not confirm whether margin_configs, the trader position index or the oracle market list iterate deterministically (HashMap vs BTreeMap). For funding, TWAP and triggers I only grepped the bridge and core lib for keywords; I did not do a full search of the torus-core modules, so data types may exist without a driver.

</details>

**fable** — partial, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

There is a deterministic per-block tail in the exec pipeline: `TorusApp::execute_committed_block_with` (crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1425) builds a `NativeExecContext` (height, timestamp, epoch, proposer) at app.rs:1852-1879, runs `execute_batch(pre_evm)` / `execute_batch(post_evm)` at app.rs:1902-1903, then a fixed post-engine tail at app.rs:1937-1940: `drain_core_writer`, `process_governance`, `distribute_fees`, `process_epoch_boundary`. That tail is the natural end-of-block driver. However it only runs inside `if has_native || computed_fee_revenue > 0` (app.rs:1655); empty and pure-EVM blocks skip the native path entirely and just write a marker (app.rs:2305-2320), so funding/liquidation/TWAP/stop triggers would NOT run on quiet blocks today. The helpers `aggregate_oracle_prices` (native_executor.rs:5904) and `run_liquidation_checks` (native_executor.rs:5923) exist but have no caller outside native_executor.rs; stop triggering happens only reactively on fills inside `OrderBook::match_order` (order_book.rs:577-579), and `OrderBook::check_stops` (order_book.rs:779) has no per-block caller; no funding or TWAP driver exists in app.rs/native_executor.rs at all.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1425 fn execute_committed_block_with — the single deterministic entry for a finalized block
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1655 `if has_native \|\| computed_fee_revenue > 0 {` — native ctx/exec tail gated on block having native actions or fees
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1852-1879 NativeExecContext::new_env(overlay, height, timestamp, epoch, epoch_length, max_validators, proposer, treasury, dev_pool, &mut resident_books)
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1902-1903 NativeExecutor::execute_batch(&mut ctx,&pre_evm); execute_batch(&mut ctx,&post_evm)
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1937-1940 drain_core_writer; process_governance; distribute_fees; process_epoch_boundary — the existing end-of-block tail
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:2305-2320 blocks with no native actions/fees write marker only (pipeline_handoff Job::Marker or write_native_applied_height), no ctx built
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5904 pub fn aggregate_oracle_prices(ctx, markets, validator_stakes) — defined, uncalled from app.rs
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5923 pub fn run_liquidation_checks(ctx, traders, oracle_prices) — defined, uncalled from app.rs
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6025 process_epoch_boundary gates on EpochManager::is_epoch_boundary(ctx.block_height, ctx.epoch_length) — template for height-gated periodic work
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:577-579 trigger_stops only when !fills.is_empty() inside match_order; order_book.rs:779 check_stops has no non-test caller

**Risk:** Without a block-level driver that runs on every block, HL-style mechanics (funding every block/hour, mark-price/oracle aggregation, liquidation sweeps when price moves without fills, TWAP sub-order slices, stop triggers off mark/oracle price) cannot happen on blocks with no native actions — positions can sit underwater or stops stay untriggered until some unrelated trade lands. The existing bl2 fast path (app.rs:1520-1526) also assumes empty blocks have no state writes, so a new driver must go through the overlay/ctx or it will break the pipelined-flush invariant.

**Fix:** Add `NativeExecutor::end_of_block(ctx: &mut NativeExecContext<T>)` in crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs next to process_epoch_boundary (~line 6025), ordered: aggregate_oracle_prices -> funding accrual (new, height/timestamp-gated like is_epoch_boundary) -> TWAP slice emission -> per-market `book.check_stops()` against mark price -> run_liquidation_checks. Call it in app.rs at line 1937, between `drain_core_writer` and `process_governance` (so liquidation fills are drained before fee distribution — or after drain again if it produces fills). Then relax the gate at app.rs:1655 to `has_native || computed_fee_revenue > 0 || needs_block_hook(height, timestamp)` so quiet blocks build a ctx when a periodic task is due; the no-ctx branch at app.rs:2305 must use the same predicate. Keep the hook inside the ctx/overlay so the bl2 pipelined path (app.rs:1520) stays valid.

**Unsure:** Did not read the bodies of execute_batch_phases (native_executor.rs:3469-4712) in full, so a liquidation/oracle-aggregate call could be buried there under another name; grep for aggregate_oracle_prices/run_liquidation_checks callers found none outside native_executor.rs. Did not inspect torus-core for any funding-rate module (only grepped bridge/consensus/node). resident_books/BookMode interaction for a hook that mutates books on a block with zero actions was not verified.

</details>

### oracle-publisher

**opus** — absent, impact critical, effort L, lockstep yes

The repo has no validator oracle publisher: no sidecar or daemon fetches CEX prices and submits SubmitOraclePrices. tools/ holds only bench-throughput, faucet, matched-bench, tx-flood and wallet. crates/torus-node has no match for oracle, price_feed, binance or pyth. Every "oracle" hit in devnet/ and testnet/ is the TORUS_INCREMENTAL_ORACLE state-root cross-check, which has nothing to do with prices. The on-chain side is only half there. SubmitOraclePrices runs: it checks the sender is an active validator and stores each submission. But aggregate_oracle_prices and run_liquidation_checks are never called outside their own definitions, and consensus app.rs never mentions oracle, liquidation or funding in the block lifecycle. So no aggregated price is ever written, even if someone submitted prices. Devnet and testnet therefore run with no oracle price. RPC get_mark_price hits CoreError::NoOraclePrice and returns mark and index as 0. The only live price signal is the order book's last_trade_price.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- `ls tools`: only bench-throughput, faucet, matched-bench, tx-flood, wallet. `ls devnet` / `ls testnet`: no oracle or price-feed scripts
- grep -i 'oracle\|mark_price\|price_feed\|binance\|coinbase\|pyth' crates/torus-node/src returned nothing
- devnet/bake-a16-s426.sh:161-168: 'oracle' means TORUS_INCREMENTAL_ORACLE, a state-root cross-check, not prices
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3276: dispatches SubmitOraclePrices
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5685-5722: exec_submit_oracle_prices checks for an active validator and calls ctx.oracle.submit_price per market
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5904-5920: aggregate_oracle_prices is pub, but grep across crates finds no call site except its definition
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5923-5960: run_liquidation_checks takes oracle_prices as a parameter and also has no non-test caller
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs: the only 'oracle' match is line 8331 (a comment about a streaming predicate). No liquidation, funding or oracle aggregation hooks
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:274-295: get_price reads only the aggregated key in CF_NATIVE_ORACLE and returns NoOraclePrice if it is missing
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1604-1611: get_mark_price maps an oracle error to mark=index=0
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1619-1640: last_trade_price comes from the book layout, the only populated price

**Risk:** There is no Hyperliquid-style oracle. Hyperliquid validators publish weighted-median CEX spot prices about every 3s, and that feeds the oracle/index price, the mark price, funding and liquidations. Here mark and index read 0 on every network. Liquidations and funding have no price input and are not even invoked from the block lifecycle. Perps are therefore not risk-managed, and adding a publisher alone would do nothing because aggregation is never triggered.

**Fix:** 1) Wire aggregation into the consensus end-of-block path in crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs, or in the native executor's block finalize. After the block's txs run, call NativeExecutor::aggregate_oracle_prices(ctx, listed_markets, active_validator_stakes). Then feed the get_price results, skipping stale ones, into run_liquidation_checks and funding. This is consensus-breaking. 2) Add a publisher, either a tools/oracle-publisher binary or a task inside torus-node gated by a validator key flag. It would poll CEX REST/WS endpoints (Binance, OKX, Bybit and others), take a weighted median per market, sign with the validator key and submit NativeAction::SubmitOraclePrices every N blocks. 3) For devnet, add a deterministic mock-price mode, such as a fixed or random-walk feed, to the devnet compose file.

**Unsure:** The no-caller finding comes from grep over crates/ with tests excluded. I did not use code_graph, so a call through a macro or trait could be missed. Funding-rate code paths were not traced in full. I did not inspect the tools/ subdirectories internally (e.g. matched-bench), though a grep for oracle/SubmitOracle in tools/ outside .rs files found nothing. I also did not run a full .rs grep of tools/. Genesis seeding of CF_NATIVE_ORACLE was checked only by grepping crates/torus-genesis/src for 'oracle' (no hits).

</details>

**fable** — absent, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes

There is no validator oracle publisher anywhere: tools/ contains only bench-throughput, faucet, matched-bench, tx-flood, wallet; crates/torus-node/src has main.rs, forward_batcher.rs, keystore.rs and two wedge bins; devnet/ and testnet/ scripts never mention oracle prices (the only "oracle" there is TORUS_INCREMENTAL_ORACLE, a state-root cross-check flag, unrelated). - crates/torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:332 docstring claims step '7. Oracle submissions + aggregation' but grep for aggregate/liquidation/funding/oracle in validator.rs body returns only that docstring line
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5951-5959 run_liquidation_checks skips a market with tracing::warn when no valid oracle price

**Risk:** Hyperliquid parity gap: HL validators each run a price publisher pulling Binance/OKX/Bybit/etc. spot and compute a stake-weighted median oracle every ~3s that drives funding, mark price, and liquidations. Here no live network has any oracle price, so mark price == entry price, liquidations never fire (silently skipped), funding has no index, and the aggregation step appears not wired into block execution — the perps economics are effectively inert on devnet/testnet.

**Fix:** 1) Add tools/oracle-publisher (or a `torus-node --oracle` task in crates/torus-node/src/main.rs): loop every N blocks, fetch CEX spot (e.g. Binance/OKX/Bybit REST, median of sources) for each listed market, build NativeAction::SubmitOraclePrices(OracleSubmission{prices, timestamp}), sign with the validator keystore (keystore.rs), submit via the node's native-action RPC. 2) Wire Self::aggregate_oracle_prices(ctx, &listed_markets, &validator_stakes) into validate_block_with_native_inner (validator.rs) at the documented step 7, before run_liquidation_checks, so aggregated prices land in CF_NATIVE_ORACLE. 3) For devnet, add a fixed/random-walk price mode to the publisher (no network) and start it from devnet/start.sh / docker-compose.yml for each validator. 4) Integration test: publisher -> block -> RPC mark_price reflects aggregated value.

**Unsure:** I did not read the full body of validate_block_with_native_inner; the "aggregation not wired" claim rests on grep showing no call to aggregate_oracle_prices/aggregate_price outside native_executor.rs:5913 and no 'oracle'/'liquidation' tokens in validator.rs beyond the docstring. Aggregation could conceivably be invoked via a differently named helper in app.rs (grep for 'oracle' in app.rs hit only an unrelated comment at 8331, so unlikely). Did not check whether the wallet tool can sign arbitrary NativeActions (would ease publisher implementation).

### margin-tier-defaults

**opus** — confirmed-bug, impact critical, effort L, lockstep yes

In production, `NativeExecContext.margin_configs` starts as an empty HashMap and nothing outside tests ever inserts into it. Every lookup therefore returns None. Order reserve, cancel, cancel-all and modify all fall back to a hardcoded flat 20x (margin = notional/20). There are no notional tiers, no per-asset max leverage, and no maintenance-margin concept on that path. The real config model (`MarketMarginConfig::new`) does use maintenance = 50% of initial at the tier's max leverage, which matches HL's rule. But its default tiers (50x up to $100k, 20x up to $1M, 10x up to $10M, 5x above) are one global ladder rather than HL's per-asset limits. Its `max_leverage` field is never read; only `tiers` are. The liquidation sweep `run_liquidation_checks` only loops over `margin_configs` entries, and it has no non-test caller anyway. So right now no maintenance check or liquidation runs at all.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1842 margin_configs: HashMap::new() at ctx construction; grep finds `margin_configs.insert` only in crates/torus-bridge/tests/maker_margin_release_tests.rs:500,503,664
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4805-4817 reserve_for_qty_cfg: cfg.map(effective_max_leverage(tiers)).unwrap_or(20), margin = notional/max_lev
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5189-5193, 5223-5227, 5242-5246, 5323-5327, 5376-5385 same unwrap_or(20) fallback in cancel / cancel_all / batch cancel / modify
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:24-43 default_margin_tiers: 50x<=100k, 20x<=1M, 10x<=10M, 5x unlimited (global, not per-asset)
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:61-78 MarketMarginConfig{max_leverage, maintenance_factor_bps}; new() sets maintenance_factor_bps=5000 and tiers=default_margin_tiers(); max_leverage not used by any formula (only tiers read at 106, 217, 238)
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:201-228 total_maintenance_margin applies ONE market's config tiers to every cross position across all markets
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5922-5945 run_liquidation_checks iterates only ctx.margin_configs entries (empty means a no-op); grep shows no caller outside its definition, and crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs has no liquidation/margin_configs references
- grep: MarginEngine::check_initial_margin / check_margin_at_match have no production callers (only liquidation.rs:124,166 use maintenance helpers)

**Risk:** Production differs from HL in three ways. (1) Every market uses one flat 20x, whatever the asset or position size. HL has per-asset caps (e.g. BTC 40x, many alts 3-10x) and tiered caps for large notional. Small-cap markets can be opened at 20x, far beyond HL limits. (2) No maintenance margin is ever enforced, and the liquidation sweep is empty and unwired. Under-collateralised positions are never liquidated, so bad debt piles up with no backstop. (3) If configs were ever populated, cross maintenance would apply the wrong market's tiers to other markets' positions. Also, the declared `max_leverage` would be ignored, so `MarketMarginConfig::new(id, 3)` would still allow up to 50x through the default tiers.

**Fix:** 1. Add per-asset margin params to market registration or genesis: maxLeverage plus a HL-style marginTable of (lowerBoundNotional, maxLeverage) tiers. Store them in state and load them into ctx.margin_configs at ctx construction (native_executor.rs ~1842) and on market creation. 2. In effective_max_leverage callers, clamp to min(config.max_leverage, tier). Or simpler: drop max_leverage and make tiers authoritative, with tier[0] = asset max. 3. Replace each unwrap_or(20) with an explicit error or a per-market required config (no silent default), or with one shared const DEFAULT_MAX_LEVERAGE. 4. Change total_maintenance_margin to look up each position's own market config (pass a &HashMap<MarketId, MarketMarginConfig>). Keep maintenance = initial at max leverage x 0.5 (5000 bps), as HL does. 5. Call run_liquidation_checks from the block-end path in consensus app.rs / native_executor's end-block, using the oracle mark prices.

**Unsure:** I did not check whether some other liquidation or maintenance path exists outside torus-bridge and app.rs. The grep for "liquidat" in torus-consensus/src found nothing, but crates/torus-core block processing or EVM precompiles were not checked fully. I also did not check whether the user's chosen per-position leverage is stored or enforced anywhere else (e.g. a position-open path in torus-core/position.rs). HL per-asset values are cited from general knowledge, not checked against current HL meta.

</details>

**fable** — confirmed-bug, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes

In production `NativeExecContext.margin_configs` is initialized to `HashMap::new()` and is never populated by any non-test code (the only `margin_configs.insert` / `MarketMarginConfig::new` call sites are in tests). Every executor margin path therefore hits the `None` branch: order-margin reserve, cancel release, modify delta, and settle-plan releases all use `.unwrap_or(20)` — a flat 20x for every market and every notional, ignoring both the per-market `max_leverage` field and the `default_margin_tiers()` ladder (50x <=100k, 20x <=1M, 10x <=10M, 5x above). The maintenance factor (`maintenance_factor_bps`, default 5000 = 50% of initial, which does match HL's "maintenance = half of initial at max leverage" rule) is only consumed via `MarginEngine::check_isolated_maintenance` / `total_maintenance_margin` / `LiquidationEngine`, which the executor never reaches: `run_liquidation_checks` iterates `ctx.margin_configs` (empty), and `MarginEngine::` is not referenced anywhere in native_executor.rs. Net: no per-asset max leverage, no tiers, and no maintenance-margin enforcement are active in production; `exec_place_order` also never calls `check_initial_margin`, so a user-requested leverage is never validated against a tier.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1356 `pub margin_configs: HashMap<MarketId, MarketMarginConfig>`; :1842 constructed as `HashMap::new()` with no later population in non-test code (grep of `margin_configs.insert` hits only crates/torus-bridge/tests/maker_margin_release_tests.rs:500,503,664)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4808-4818 `reserve_for_qty_cfg`: `cfg.map(\|c\| effective_max_leverage(&c.tiers, notional)).unwrap_or(20)` — flat 20x when config missing (doc comment at :4784 says 'default 20x')
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5189-5193, 5223-5229, 5242-5248, 5323-5329, 5377-5385 — cancel, cancel_all, batch cancel, modify all use the same `.unwrap_or(20)` fallback
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5922-5938 `run_liquidation_checks` iterates `ctx.margin_configs` → zero markets checked when empty
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:23-43 `default_margin_tiers()` = 50x/20x/10x/5x ladder; :46-53 `effective_max_leverage` falls back to 1x; :61-77 `MarketMarginConfig` with `maintenance_factor_bps: 5000` (50% of initial) and `max_leverage` field — note `max_leverage` is not used by `effective_max_leverage`, only `tiers`
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:96-112 `check_initial_margin` validates requested leverage vs tier — grep shows no caller in native_executor.rs (no `MarginEngine::` references)
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:166-180 maintenance = (notional/max_lev) * maintenance_factor_bps/10000 — HL-shaped formula, but unreachable in production because configs are empty

**Risk:** Parity gap and economic-safety hole: HL enforces per-asset max leverage (e.g. BTC 40x/ETH 25x/alts 3-20x, with notional-based tiers) and liquidates at maintenance = initial/2 at max leverage. Here every market reserves 1/20 of notional regardless of asset or size (a 50M-notional alt position gets 20x, HL would cap it at 3-5x), the maintenance factor is dead code, and no liquidation engine runs through the executor path, so underwater positions are never force-closed and bad debt accrues to the insurance fund/LPs. Also a config injected later with `max_leverage` set but default tiers would silently be ignored, because only `tiers` drives `effective_max_leverage`.

**Fix:** 1) Populate `margin_configs` at context construction (native_executor.rs ~:1842) from a persisted per-market table (genesis + governance `set_margin_config` action): `MarketMarginConfig { market_id, max_leverage, maintenance_factor_bps: 5000, tiers }`. 2) Make `MarketMarginConfig::new` derive tiers from `max_leverage` (cap each default tier at `max_leverage`) and/or make `effective_max_leverage` take `min(tier.max_leverage, config.max_leverage)` so the per-asset cap is honored (margin.rs:46-53, 70-77). 3) Replace the five `.unwrap_or(20)` fallbacks with a single `fn market_cfg(&self, mid) -> &MarketMarginConfig` that returns a conservative default (e.g. 3x) or rejects the order for unconfigured markets. 4) Wire `MarginEngine::check_initial_margin` into `exec_place_order` (:4906) and call `run_liquidation_checks` from the block pipeline (app.rs) once configs exist. Add a test asserting an unconfigured market does not get 20x.

**Unsure:** Did not verify whether `run_liquidation_checks` has any caller in app.rs/consensus (grep pattern only covered `check_liquidations(`); even if called, it is a no-op with empty configs. Did not check whether a separate liquidation path (e.g. a keeper/RPC action or torus-economics) enforces maintenance independently of `margin_configs`. HL per-asset leverage numbers cited from memory, not fetched.

### funding-design

**opus** — absent, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes

There is no funding engine. torus-core has no use of "funding" anywhere. `Position` (position.rs:52-62) has no funding index field. The only trace is `MarketParams.max_funding_rate_bps` (torus-types/src/lib.rs:1161), which gets serialized and is never read. Proposed design, using lazy index-based settlement:
(1) A new `torus-core/src/funding.rs` keeps a per-market `FundingState { cum_index: signed FixedPoint quote-per-unit, premium_sum, n_samples, last_sample_ts, last_settle_ts }` in its own state key.
(2) `Position` gets `entry_funding_index` (schema v2). Owed funding = signed_size * (cum_index - entry_funding_index). It is settled inside `fill_transition` before any size change, and the index is then reset.
(3) Premium is sampled in the exec tail of app.rs every 5s of block time, using impact bid/ask walked from the resident `ctx.order_books` and the oracle price. The hourly rate HL-style is avg_premium + clamp(interest - avg_premium, ±0.05%), divided by 8 and capped at 4%/h. `cum_index` then increases by rate * oracle_px.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:52-62 Position fields: trader, market_id, is_long, size, entry_price, realized_pnl, isolated_margin, margin_type. No funding index.
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:84-99 POSITION_SCHEMA_VERSION=1 with a hand-written Borsh codec. Adding a field needs a v2 that still decodes v1, with index 0.
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:309-327 apply_fill and 364-381 apply_fill_cached_effect both go through fill_transition (434). This is the one place to settle funding before a size change. closed_pnl is already returned to the caller's BalanceCache.
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156-1162 MarketParams.max_funding_rate_bps exists. It is only serialized (lib.rs:828, 906) and nothing in torus-core reads it.
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:798,803 best_bid/best_ask; 898,912 bid_depth/ask_depth return an allocated Vec. No impact-price walk.
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:274-286 OracleManager::get_price(market, block) reads the aggregated price with a staleness check, so it can serve as the funding reference price.
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1339-1369 NativeExecContext has positions, oracle, order_books (resident), margin_configs, block_height, timestamp.
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1937-1940 exec tail: drain_core_writer, process_governance, distribute_fees, process_epoch_boundary. This is the natural hook for sample/settle funding.
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5904 aggregate_oracle_prices and 5923 run_liquidation_checks exist, but a grep shows app.rs calls neither (the only non-test hit was distribute_fees at app.rs:1939). Oracle aggregation and liquidation are not wired into block exec either.

**Risk:** Without funding, perp prices are not anchored to spot. Basis can drift without limit, longs and shorts carry for free, and HL API parity fails (fundingHistory, userFunding, predictedFundings, the funding/premium fields in metaAndAssetCtxs). There is also a hidden dependency: funding needs a fresh deterministic oracle price at exec time. Oracle aggregation does not appear to be called from app.rs, so either the funding hook calls aggregate_oracle_prices first, or every funding sample sees a stale price or no price at all. Everything here must use the block-header timestamp, never wall clock, and integer FixedPoint math, or validators will diverge.

**Fix:** 1. New crates/torus-core/src/funding.rs (~250 LOC):
   - `FundingState` with a Borsh codec. Key: `funding_key(market)` in CF_NATIVE_ORACLE, or a new CF.
   - `FundingConfig { interest_rate_8h=0.0001, clamp=0.0005, cap_per_hour=0.04 (or MarketParams.max_funding_rate_bps), impact_notional (20k BTC/ETH, 6k others), sample_interval_s=5, settle_interval_s=3600 }`.
   - `premium(impact_bid, impact_ask, oracle)` = (max(ib-o,0) - max(o-ia,0)) / o.
   - `sample()` and `settle_hour()`. settle_hour bumps cum_index and resets the accumulators.
2. order_book.rs (~60 LOC): `impact_px(side, notional) -> Option<FixedPoint>`, which walks levels until the notional is filled and needs no Vec allocation. If depth is insufficient, return None and skip the sample.
3. position.rs (~80 LOC):
   - Add `entry_funding_index` and bump POSITION_SCHEMA_VERSION to 2, with v1 decoding as 0.
   - Give fill_transition a `cum_index` argument. It returns funding_paid, credited/debited alongside closed_pnl (extend FillEffect), and resets entry_funding_index on open/increase/flip.
   - Add a `pending_funding(cum_index)` helper.
4. margin.rs and liquidation.rs (~40 LOC): include unsettled funding in account equity, isolated margin, and the liquidation check.
5. native_executor.rs (~100 LOC): `NativeExecutor::process_funding(ctx)`. For each market in margin_configs:
   - get the oracle price;
   - if ctx.timestamp has crossed the next 5s boundary, compute impact px from ctx.order_books and sample;
   - at the hour boundary, call settle_hour.
   - Optional eager sweep at settlement: realize all positions at the hour, which matches HL's userFunding history exactly. Costs O(positions)/h.
6. app.rs ~1937: call process_funding after drain_core_writer (after aggregate_oracle_prices, which also needs wiring).
7. torus-rpc (~150 LOC): fundingHistory, userFunding, predictedFundings, and funding/premium/impactPxs in metaAndAssetCtxs.
Total ~700 LOC of code, ~400 LOC of tests (golden vectors for premium/clamp/cap, a v1 to v2 position-decode test, and a determinism test across settle modes and parallel settle).

**Unsure:** Things I did not read:
- The parallel settle path (parallel_settle_tests), where fill_transition is called concurrently. The cum_index must be a per-block snapshot passed in read-only, so I believe this works, but I did not verify it.
- Whether a CF_NATIVE_ORACLE key or a new column family is preferable for state-root/manifest coverage.
- Whether oracle aggregation runs elsewhere, for example in a separate oracle-submission path outside the app.rs exec tail. I only checked that app.rs does not call aggregate_oracle_prices or run_liquidation_checks.
- Whether funding hits in torus-bridge tests are only fixture field names; I did not open them.
The HL constants (impact notional, the 4%/h cap, 5s sampling, the 1/8-per-hour convention) come from my knowledge of HL docs and were not checked against current HL in this session.

</details>

**fable** — design, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes

There is no funding engine today: the only funding artifact is `MarketParams.max_funding_rate_bps` (torus-types/src/lib.rs:1161), which is hashed into actions but never read at runtime; `Position` (torus-core/src/position.rs:52) has no funding field, "mark" is simply the aggregated oracle price everywhere (margin.rs:195, liquidation.rs:206, precompiles.rs:446), and the post-engine tail in app.rs (~1937-1941: drain_core_writer -> process_governance -> distribute_fees -> process_epoch_boundary) has no funding step. Proposed design (HL semantics: hourly rate = clamp(interest 0.01% - avg premium, ±0.05%) + premium, capped by max_funding_rate_bps; premium = (max(0,impact_bid-oracle) - max(0,oracle-impact_ask))/oracle): (1) per-market `FundingState { cum_index: FixedPoint /*quote per base, signed*/, premium_sum, premium_n, last_settle_ts, last_rate }` in a new CF `CF_NATIVE_FUNDING` (torus-state/src/cf.rs next to :42-45); (2) per-position `entry_funding_index: FixedPoint` added to `Position` with `POSITION_SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped 1->2 (position.rs:83, serde at :87-143, capacity hint :248); (3) sample premium each block from the in-memory `ctx.order_books` (native_executor.rs:1347) via a new `OrderBook::impact_price(side, notional)` walking `bid_queues()/ask_queues()` (order_book.rs:1355-1360, remaining_qty per order as in bid_depth :898) against `ctx.oracle.get_price(mid, ctx.block_height)` (oracle.rs:274, skip when `stale`); (4) settle in the same tail hook when `ctx.timestamp` (native_executor.rs:1365) crosses `last_settle_ts+3600`: `cum_index += rate * oracle_px`, then accrue to positions lazily on every touch (fill_transition position.rs:435, liquidation, margin equity) as `size*(cum_index-entry_index)*(long?-1:+1)` credited via `credit_realized_pnl` (position.rs:386; for Isolated, debit `isolated_margin` instead), plus an hourly full sweep over `iterate_cf(CF_NATIVE_POSITIONS, None)` to realise balances and write funding-history rows for RPC parity (fundingHistory/userFunding/clearinghouseState.cumFunding).

### spot-design

**opus** — design, impact high, effort XL, lockstep yes

No native spot clearinghouse exists. "Spot" today just means the EVM account balance in CF_ACCOUNTS: TransferToPerp and TransferToSpot only move TRS between the EVM and CF_NATIVE_BALANCES through the lockbox. CF_NATIVE_BALANCES is keyed by the bare 20-byte trader address and holds one perp-collateral NativeBalance {available, order_margin}. There is no token registry, no per-token balances and no spot markets. Proposed design:
(a) A new CF_SPOT_TOKENS token registry: token_index(u32 BE) -> {name, sz_decimals, wei_decimals, evm_contract: Option<Address>, deployer}. Index 0 is USDC/TRS.
(b) A new CF_SPOT_BALANCES for multi-token balances, keyed address(20) ‖ token(4 BE) -> {total, hold}. This matches HL's spotClearinghouseState and allows one prefix scan per user.
(c) Spot markets reuse OrderBook as-is. They get a MarketId from a reserved range (for example a high bit set, the same trick as HL's 10000+index) so they share CF_NATIVE_ORDER_BOOKS, CF_BOOK_ORDER_ROWS and ResidentBooks. A CF_NATIVE_MARKETS entry gets a kind: Spot{base, quote} discriminant.
(d) The executor branches on market kind: placing an order puts a hold on the quote (buy) or base (sell) instead of order_margin, and a fill swaps base and quote balances with no position. reduce_only and leverage are rejected for spot.
(e) TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot change meaning to "spot USDC token-0 <-> perp NativeBalance.available", plus a new SpotSend{token, to, amount} and an EVM link action.

**fable** — design, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes

Today there is no spot clearinghouse at all: the only "spot" concept is the EVM account balance in CF_ACCOUNTS (TRS only), and NativeAction::TransferToSpot is literally exec_withdraw_from_native (native perp USD margin -> CF_ACCOUNTS). CF_NATIVE_BALANCES is keyed by trader(20) -> borsh(NativeBalance{available, order_margin}) with a single implicit quote token; markets have no persisted registry (CF_NATIVE_MARKETS currently holds only the node-local __book_mode__ marker; MarketParams/MarketListing in torus-types are perp-shaped with max_leverage/maintenance_margin). OrderBook is market-agnostic (price/qty/side/Fill with maker/taker addresses) and is persisted by market_id(8 BE) keys, so spot books can reuse it unchanged; what differs is pre-trade reservation (lock base or quote token instead of margin) and settlement (token swap instead of apply_fill_via_caches position/PnL). Proposed minimal design: (1) token registry rows in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS under a 0x02-prefixed key: token_id(4 BE) -> borsh(TokenInfo{symbol, decimals, evm_contract: Option<Address>}), token 0 = TRS/quote; (2) spot balances in a NEW CF_NATIVE_SPOT_BALANCES keyed trader(20) ++ token_id(4 BE) -> borsh(SpotBalance{total, hold}) (keeps the perp NativeBalance row byte-identical, so existing root preimages are untouched); (3) spot market rows in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS under 0x01 prefix: market_id -> borsh(SpotMarket{base_token, quote_token, tick, lot}) with spot market_ids in a reserved high range (e.g. bit 63 set) so order_books: HashMap<MarketId, OrderBook> and dirty_books/save_order_books work unchanged; (4) new actions SpotPlaceOrder/SpotCancel (or a `spot: bool` branch keyed off market_id range in exec PlaceOrder) plus SpotTransfer{token, amount, to} and SpotToPerp/PerpToSpot(token 0 only); (5) a SpotSettlement path in native_executor: on place, move quote (buy, price*qty) or base (sell, qty) from total to hold; on each Fill, debit hold and credit counterparty total for both legs, release remainder on cancel; fees in quote token.
