### fix-market-registry

**opus** — stub, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: 700-1000 (registry ~250, executor wiring ~250, governance payloads ~120, migration ~80, tests ~300)

There is no market registry. The three admin actions are no-op stubs that return ok (native_executor.rs:3332-3336). Governance ListMarket hard-codes `market_id: 0` (5745). When that proposal executes, `GovernanceManager::execute_payload` writes a raw row to CF_NATIVE_MARKETS at key `0u64.to_be_bytes()` (governance.rs:1080-1100), so every listing overwrites the same row, and nothing ever reads that row back. UpdateMarketParams and DelistMarket proposals map to `None`, so they are text-only (5754). Both order paths create a book with tick=lot=1 for any market id they have not seen (sequential 4961-4964, parallel 3825-3828). `margin_configs` starts empty (1842) and nothing fills it from persisted state. Proposed design: a single `MarketRegistry` owned by NativeExecContext and stored in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS; ids are assigned when the listing executes; every book and margin config is created from the registry; orders for a market that is not listed, or not active, are rejected.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3327-3336 Admin actions are 'Intentional stubs' (ECON-PF-07): UpdateMarketParams, ListMarket and DelistMarket return NativeActionResult::ok(..., 0). There is no sender or authority check.
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5744-5756 ProposalAction::ListMarket -> ExecutionPayload::MarketListing { market_id: 0 // auto-assigned, ... }, with initial_margin derived from maintenance_margin_bps. UpdateMarketParams and DelistMarket -> None ('text-only for now').
- torus-economics/src/governance.rs:1080-1101 execute_payload MarketListing borsh-encodes base, quote, lot, tick and initial_margin, then calls put_cf_raw(CF_NATIVE_MARKETS, market_id.to_be_bytes()). With id 0, every listing collides on key 0. No reader of these rows was found (grep CF_NATIVE_MARKETS finds only the book-mode marker and next-order-id uses).
- torus-economics/src/governance.rs:186-193 ExecutionPayload::MarketListing fields. Borsh tag 2 at 229. Tag 3 = ValidatorRegistration at 290.
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4961-4964 exec_place_order: ctx.order_books.entry(market_id).or_insert_with(\|\| OrderBook::new(market_id, FixedPoint::ONE, FixedPoint::ONE)).
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3825-3828 Parallel Phase 3: order_books.remove(&market_id).unwrap_or_else(\|\| OrderBook::new(market_id, ONE, ONE)).
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1355-1356,1842 margin_configs: HashMap<MarketId, MarketMarginConfig> is set to HashMap::new() in the constructor and is never loaded.
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:2537,2553 CF_NATIVE_MARKETS already holds string-keyed rows __book_mode__ and __next_global_order_id__.
- torus-types/src/lib.rs:672-679,1156-1172 NativeAction admin variants. MarketParams {tick_size, lot_size, max_leverage, maintenance_margin_bps, max_funding_rate_bps}. MarketListing {base_asset, quote_asset, tick_size, lot_size, max_leverage, maintenance_margin_bps}.
- torus-core/src/margin.rs:61-68 MarketMarginConfig {market_id, max_leverage, maintenance_factor_bps, tiers}, built with MarketMarginConfig::new(id, max_leverage).
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:2054 rebuild_book uses OrderBook::new(market_id, meta.tick_size, meta.lot_size), so persisted books already carry their real tick and lot.

**Risk:** Today anyone can trade any u64 market id. That creates junk books with tick and lot of 1 that bloat the state root. Margin falls back to the `None` config because `margin_configs` is empty, so leverage and maintenance-margin limits are never set per market. Governance listings are lost: the market id is always 0, the row is overwritten each time and nothing reads it. Markets cannot be delisted or retuned. Hyperliquid has an explicit perp universe (meta with szDecimals, maxLeverage and onlyIsolated, plus delisted status, listed through validator vote or the deploy auction) and rejects orders for unknown assets. This gap blocks parity and also creates a state-growth DoS vector.

**Fix:** 1) New module torus-core/src/market_registry.rs:
   - `MarketStatus { Active, ReduceOnly, Delisted }`.
   - `MarketSpec { market_id, base_asset, quote_asset, tick_size, lot_size, max_leverage, maintenance_margin_bps, max_funding_rate_bps, status, listed_height }`, Borsh-encoded.
   - `MarketRegistry { specs: BTreeMap<MarketId, MarketSpec>, next_market_id: MarketId }` with:
     - `list(&MarketListing, height) -> Result<MarketId>`: validates tick>0, lot>0, 1<=max_leverage<=50 and 0<mm_bps<10000, and rejects a duplicate base/quote pair.
     - `update(id, &MarketParams)`
     - `delist(id)`
     - `get(id)`
     - `margin_config(id) -> MarketMarginConfig`
   - Persist each spec in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS at key `b"mkt/" ++ id.to_be_bytes()`, and the counter at `b"__next_market_id__"`. This follows the `__next_global_order_id__` pattern at 2553 and avoids the bare 8-byte keys governance writes today.
   - The row must be in the native consensus root. Verify this, because the comment at 2532 calls the book-mode marker in this CF node-local.
2) NativeExecContext (native_executor.rs:1339):
   - Add `pub markets: MarketRegistry`.
   - In the constructors (1595/1625/1688/1726, init at 1842), load the registry and fill `margin_configs` from `markets.margin_config(id)`. This also fixes the empty `margin_configs`.
   - Write registry rows only when they changed, the same way `save_order_books` does at 2581 and 2683.
3) Replace the stubs at 3332-3336 with three functions:
   - `exec_list_market`: assigns the id, then `order_books.insert(id, OrderBook::new(id, tick, lot))`, `dirty_books.insert` and `margin_configs.insert`.
   - `exec_update_market_params`: applies leverage, maintenance-margin and funding-cap changes immediately. Allow tick or lot changes only when the book has no resting orders, or require every resting price and size to be a multiple of the new values. Rebuild the margin config.
   - `exec_delist_market`: sets status to Delisted, cancels all resting and stop orders with reserve refunds (reuse the cancel path), and marks the book dirty. Settling open positions at the oracle mark is a follow-up.
   - Gate all three behind the governance path: a user-signed NativeAction admin variant returns err("not_authorized"). Add an internal entry point that the proposal executor calls.
4) Governance:
   - Delete the raw CF write in governance.rs:1080-1100 so the registry is the single writer. `execute_payload` should return or emit the payload and the native executor applies it to `ctx.markets` (in `exec_execute_proposal`, near 5730).
   - Drop `market_id` from `ExecutionPayload::MarketListing` (or ignore it) and assign the id at execution, not at submission, so two pending proposals cannot collide.
   - Add `ExecutionPayload::UpdateMarketParams{..}` and `DelistMarket{..}` with new append-only Borsh tags after the existing ones (check the PermanentUnlock tag).
   - Map them at 5754 instead of `None`, and carry `max_leverage` and `max_funding_rate_bps` through.
5) Stop auto-creating books:
   - In exec_place_order, before balance reservation (around 4940): `match ctx.markets.get(market_id) { Some(s) if s.status==Active || (ReduceOnly && params.reduce_only) => {}, _ => return err("place_order","unknown or inactive market") }`.
   - At 4964, use `get_mut` and handle a missing book.
   - In the parallel prepare phase, reject unknown or inactive markets before they enter `market_batches`; at 3828, replace `unwrap_or_else` with a skip and a fatal_error assert.
   - Check book_reader.rs:637 the same way.
6) Migration (consensus-breaking, behind an activation height): on the first load with an empty registry, create a spec for every existing book id using that book's own tick and lot, and the genesis default for leverage and margin. Set next_market_id to max_id+1. Also seed genesis markets from the genesis config.
7) Tests:
   - List, then place an order: tick and lot are enforced.
   - Placing an order on an unknown id is rejected and no book or state row appears.
   - Two governance listings get distinct ids 1 and 2.
   - Delist cancels orders, refunds reserves and rejects new orders; ReduceOnly allows only reduce-only orders.
   - UpdateMarketParams changes leverage, and is rejected for a tick change while orders rest.
   - A user-signed ListMarket is rejected.
   - The registry survives a reload with the same native root.
   - Sequential and parallel paths behave the same for unknown markets.

**Unsure:** Not read:
- Whether CF_NATIVE_MARKETS rows are in the native consensus root. The comment at 2532 says the book-mode marker in this CF is node-local, so registry rows might need to be excluded from, or included in, the root explicitly.
- The full ExecutionPayload tag list (PermanentUnlock's tag).
- `exec_execute_proposal` and the `GovernanceManager::execute_proposal` flow (governance.rs:961-1036), which decide how the payload gets back to the native executor.
- How genesis currently seeds markets, if it does at all.
- The parallel prepare phase, which is where the unknown-market check would go.
- Whether app.rs or the RPC layer already filters admin NativeActions by sender.
- The cancel helper to reuse for delisting.
Hyperliquid details (delist settlement at mark, a 50x leverage cap) are from my own knowledge of Hyperliquid, not from this repo.

</details>

**fable** — design, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~500-700 LOC across torus-types, torus-economics/governance.rs, torus-bridge/native_executor.rs, torus-rpc/torus.rs plus ~200 LOC tests

Market "registry" today is a bare Borsh row per market_id in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS (base, quote, lot_raw, tick_raw, initial_margin_raw) written only by governance execute_payload, and read by RPC get_markets/validate_known_markets. The executor never reads it: NativeAction::ListMarket/DelistMarket/UpdateMarketParams return ok with no state change and no authority check (any signer can submit them), governance ListMarket proposals hard-code market_id 0 so every listing overwrites the same row, UpdateMarketParams/DelistMarket proposals carry no execution payload ("text-only"), and the executor auto-creates OrderBook::new(id, ONE, ONE) for any market_id in exec_place_order and in the Phase-3 parallel path, so RPC's known-market check is the only guard (CoreWriter/EVM-originated orders bypass it). Proposed design: a consensus-level MarketRegistry keyed in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS with a versioned StoredMarket {base, quote, tick, lot, max_leverage, mm_bps, max_funding_bps, status: Active|Delisted(reduce_only)|Halted, listed_at}, a next_market_id counter row (like NEXT_GLOBAL_ORDER_ID_KEY), executor-side cache loaded at boot, book creation only from registry meta, and admin actions gated to the governance module (execution via proposal payload) rather than arbitrary signers.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3327-3336: ListMarket/DelistMarket/UpdateMarketParams match arms return NativeActionResult::ok(...,0) with no state write and no sender authority check (AUDIT ECON-PF-07 stub comment)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5744-5756: exec_submit_proposal maps ProposalAction::ListMarket to ExecutionPayload::MarketListing { market_id: 0 /*auto-assigned*/ ...}; UpdateMarketParams/DelistMarket proposals map to None ('text-only for now'); max_leverage and max_funding_rate_bps are dropped
- crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:1080-1100: execute_payload MarketListing writes key = market_id.to_be_bytes() (always 0) with Borsh(base, quote, lot_raw, tick_raw, initial_margin_raw) into CF_NATIVE_MARKETS -> every listing overwrites row 0
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4959-4964: exec_place_order ctx.order_books.entry(market_id).or_insert_with(\|\| OrderBook::new(market_id, FixedPoint::ONE, FixedPoint::ONE)) -- auto-creates tick=lot=1 book for any id
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3825-3828: Phase-3 parallel matching remove(&market_id).unwrap_or_else(\|\| OrderBook::new(market_id, ONE, ONE)) -- second auto-create site
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:2048-2054: rebuild_book builds OrderBook::new(market_id, meta.tick_size, meta.lot_size) from the persisted BookMeta, i.e. tick/lot live in book meta rows, not the registry
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:257-281: validate_known_markets checks CF_NATIVE_MARKETS only for PlaceOrder/PlaceOrderBatch at RPC ingress; not consensus-level
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:880-930: get_markets decodes StoredMarket from CF_NATIVE_MARKETS rows and hard-codes status: "active"
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156-1171: MarketParams {tick_size, lot_size, max_leverage, maintenance_margin_bps, max_funding_rate_bps}; MarketListing {base_asset, quote_asset, tick_size, lot_size, max_leverage, maintenance_margin_bps}
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:2549-2560: NEXT_GLOBAL_ORDER_ID_KEY counter row already lives in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS -- pattern to reuse for next_market_id
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:45: CF_NATIVE_MARKETS = "cf_native_markets"

**Risk:** Any address can submit ListMarket/DelistMarket/UpdateMarketParams and get a success receipt (silent no-op); governance listings all collide on market_id 0 so a second listing clobbers the first; orders for unregistered ids (via CoreWriter/EVM path or any ingress other than the RPC check) spin up tick=lot=1 books with no margin params, so leverage/maintenance-margin/funding are not per-market; delisting (HL reduce-only then settle) is impossible. Blocks HL parity for perp meta (universe/szDecimals/maxLeverage) and delist flow.

**Fix:** 1) torus-types/src/lib.rs: add `MarketStatus { Active, ReduceOnly, Delisted }` and a Borsh `StoredMarket` v2 (move the RPC-local StoredMarket into torus-types or torus-core): {version:u8, base, quote, tick_raw, lot_raw, max_leverage, maintenance_margin_bps, max_funding_rate_bps, status, listed_at_block}. Keep decoding v1 rows (5 fields) for compatibility. 2) torus-economics/src/governance.rs: extend ExecutionPayload with `MarketParamsUpdate{market_id, params}` and `MarketDelist{market_id}`; in execute_payload MarketListing, when market_id==0 read/increment a `__next_market_id__` counter row in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS (same pattern as NEXT_GLOBAL_ORDER_ID_KEY at native_executor.rs:2549) and reject if the key already exists; write StoredMarket v2 carrying max_leverage/mm_bps/funding from the listing; MarketParamsUpdate validates existence + tick/lot > 0 and rewrites the row; MarketDelist sets status=ReduceOnly (settlement/forced close is a later step). 3) native_executor.rs:5744-5756 exec_submit_proposal: map UpdateMarketParams/DelistMarket to the new payloads instead of None, and pass max_leverage/max_funding_rate_bps through. 4) native_executor.rs:3327-3336: replace the stubs with a sender check against the governance/admin module address (or simply reject with NativeActionResult::err("use governance proposal")) so no non-governance signer can get an ok receipt; alternatively keep variants only for ProposalAction. 5) Registry cache: add `markets: HashMap<MarketId, StoredMarket>` to NativeExecContext/executor, loaded at boot from CF_NATIVE_MARKETS (skip the 2 marker/counter keys and non-8-byte keys, same filter as torus.rs:903) and refreshed after each proposal execution in the block. 6) native_executor.rs:4959-4964 exec_place_order: replace or_insert_with(ONE,ONE) with lookup in the registry; unknown id -> NativeActionResult::err("place_order","unknown market"); status!=Active -> reject non-reducing orders; create book via OrderBook::new(id, m.tick, m.lot). 7) native_executor.rs:3825-3828 Phase-3: same, build from registry meta and never fall back to ONE/ONE (unreachable after step 6, so `expect`). 8) Use per-market max_leverage/mm_bps in margin checks where a global constant is used today (not located in this probe). 9) torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:880-930 get_markets: decode v2 and emit real status; validate_known_markets also rejects status==Delisted. Tests: governance_tests.rs: two ListMarket proposals get ids 1 and 2 (not both 0); UpdateMarketParams changes tick; delist flips status. native_executor tests: PlaceOrder on unlisted id rejected and no book created (order_books.len()==0); listed market book has registry tick/lot; non-governance sender ListMarket -> err; boot reload after listing shows registry entry.

**Unsure:** Did not locate where per-market leverage/maintenance margin is currently read in margin checks (may be a global constant) nor how genesis seeds CF_NATIVE_MARKETS (no writer found outside governance in the grep; genesis may use a different path). Did not read the RPC-local StoredMarket struct definition or the existing block-mode marker key names to confirm the key-filter logic for a registry loader. Whether EIP-712 encoding of ProposalAction (lib.rs:821) needs changes depends on keeping the action shapes unchanged, which the design above does.

</details>

### fix-unbonding

**opus** — unwired, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: ~60 LOC impl (sweep plus Phase 0 call) + ~150 LOC tests; +~150 LOC if the release-height index CF is added

Nothing in production ever releases unbonding funds. `StakingManager::undelegate` (staking.rs:130-185) moves the amount into `delegation.unbonding` with `release_block = current_block + UNBONDING_PERIOD`, and the native executor calls it from `exec_undelegate` (native_executor.rs:5440-5453). But `process_unbonding(delegator, validator, current_block)` (staking.rs:189-224) is only called from tests (staking.rs:1203, 1209, 1859). As a result, undelegated tokens stay locked forever, and every undelegate brings the account closer to the hard cap `MAX_UNBONDING_ENTRIES=100` (staking.rs:164), after which `undelegate` returns `TooManyUnbondingEntries`. Proposed design: add a deterministic sweep, `process_matured_unbondings(current_block)`, that walks CF_STAKING_DELEGATIONS in key order (delegator(20)‖validator(20)). Call it as Phase 0 of `NativeExecutor::process_epoch_boundary` (native_executor.rs:6025), which runs inside the block's state transition from app.rs:1940. Do not call it from app.rs `epoch_validator_set_updates` (app.rs:4074), which is cached and has side effects. A later step can move it to every block, using a release-height index.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:130-185 undelegate cuts delegation.amount and val.total_delegated, then pushes UnbondingEntry{amount, release_block: current_block + UNBONDING_PERIOD}; nothing is credited back
- crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:163-170 MAX_UNBONDING_ENTRIES=100 cap; since nothing drains the queue, an account hits the cap after 100 undelegates
- crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:189-224 process_unbonding works on one (delegator, validator) pair: drains entries with current_block >= release_block, calls credit_balance, and deletes the record when amount==0 and the queue is empty
- grep: process_unbonding is only called at staking.rs:1203, 1209, 1859 (tests)
- crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:836-841 credit_balance adds to state account.balance (the same balance that delegate debits)
- crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:880-903 delegations_for_validator does a full iterate_cf(CF_STAKING_DELEGATIONS, None) scan; its comment says it is kept off the per-block hot path
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5440-5453 exec_undelegate is the production caller of undelegate, using ctx.block_height
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6025-6100 process_epoch_boundary: gated by is_epoch_boundary; Phase A rewards log errors and continue; Phase B rotation
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1937-1940 per-block tail calls drain_core_writer, process_governance, distribute_fees, process_epoch_boundary(&mut ctx), all inside the exec overlay before flush
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:4074-4090 epoch_validator_set_updates also writes state (apply_pending_rotations) but is memoized by height; it is the wrong place for balance changes
- crates/torus-economics/src/types.rs:186-190 UnbondingEntry{amount: U256, release_block: u64}; crates/torus-economics/src/types.rs:313 UNBONDING_PERIOD = 7d / TARGET_BLOCK_TIME_SECS

**Risk:** Every undelegation in production locks funds for good: the balance never comes back, supply accounting drifts (the tokens are out of both total_delegated and balances), and a user is blocked from undelegating after 100 entries. On Hyperliquid, an undelegation unlocks after a fixed delay and the funds return automatically to the user's balance. Here the user can never get them back. Any release path must be deterministic across validators: same order, same block, same result on error. Otherwise state roots diverge.

**Fix:** 1) torus-economics/src/staking.rs: add `pub fn process_matured_unbondings(&self, current_block: u64) -> Result<(U256 /*released*/, u32 /*records touched*/)>`. It calls `self.state.iterate_cf(CF_STAKING_DELEGATIONS, None)`, decodes each value as Delegation, and keeps only those with `unbonding.iter().any(|e| current_block >= e.release_block)`. It then sorts the (key, delegation) pairs by raw key bytes. Do this explicitly; do not rely on the backend's iteration order. For each pair it splits the key into delegator=key[0..20] and validator=key[20..40] and calls the existing `process_unbonding(delegator, validator, current_block)`, so the credit, cleanup and delete logic exists in one place only. Add a doc comment stating the order: ascending delegator‖validator, entries released together. 2) torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs `process_epoch_boundary`: after the `is_epoch_boundary` guard and before Phase A, add Phase 0: `match ctx.staking.process_matured_unbondings(ctx.block_height) { Ok((amt, n)) => tracing::info!(%amt, n, "unbonding released"), Err(e) => tracing::error!(%e, "unbonding release failed") }`. Every node gets the same Err on the same state, so log-and-continue is deterministic, matching how Phase A handles errors. With this, the effective delay is UNBONDING_PERIOD plus at most epoch_length. Put that in the doc comment, or set `release_block` at the next epoch boundary. No change to app.rs is needed, because the call at app.rs:1940 already runs every block inside the overlay. Do NOT add it to app.rs:4074. 3) Optional (per-block parity, larger change): add a CF_STAKING_UNBONDING_QUEUE index keyed `release_block.to_be_bytes() ‖ delegator ‖ validator`. Write the index entry in undelegate. In the per-block tail (a new `NativeExecutor::process_unbonding_queue` called next to process_governance at app.rs:1938), prefix-scan keys <= current_block. That costs O(matured) per block instead of O(all delegations) per epoch. This is a schema change, so it needs a migration or genesis gating. 4) Also open: `slash` (staking.rs:392+, which uses delegations_for_validator) only slashes `del.amount`. Entries still unbonding escape slashing. Cosmos and HL-style chains slash in-flight unbonds for infractions committed before the undelegate. Track this as a follow-up. Tests (in staking.rs mod tests): (a) `sweep_releases_only_matured`: two delegators, one entry matured and one not. Assert the balances and the remaining entries. (b) `sweep_deletes_empty_delegation`: amount 0 with a single matured entry, so the record is gone after the sweep. (c) `sweep_deterministic_order`: run the sweep on two fresh state DBs built with the same operations inserted in different orders, and assert the state roots or account balances are identical. (d) `sweep_frees_cap`: 100 entries, sweep at maturity, then undelegate succeeds again. In native_bridge_tests.rs, extend near line 631: undelegate at block h, run process_epoch_boundary at the first boundary >= h+UNBONDING_PERIOD, and assert the balance is restored. Before that boundary, assert it is unchanged. Add an integration test in torus-consensus for the full undelegate-to-release round trip across an epoch, using a small epoch_length (like the 4 at app.rs:13218) with UNBONDING_PERIOD set through a cfg(test) override or a parameter.

**Unsure:** Not checked: whether `iterate_cf` returns keys in sorted order when reading through the exec overlay; that is why the design sorts explicitly. Whether UNBONDING_PERIOD can be parameterized for tests: genesis has unbonding_period_blocks at torus-genesis lib.rs:162, but staking.rs uses the const directly. Whether a chain that is already live needs an activation height for this change; it changes balances, so it affects state roots. HL's current values (1-day undelegation lockup, 7-day staking-to-spot withdrawal queue) are from memory and were not checked against this repo's intended parameters. I also did not read slash() in full to confirm that unbonding entries are never slashed; the grep shows it only uses del.amount.

</details>

**fable** — unwired, impact critical, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: ~60-90 LOC prod (staking.rs ~30, native_executor.rs ~15, app.rs ~2, optional index CF ~40) + ~120 LOC tests

`StakingManager::process_unbonding` (crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:189-224) is fully implemented (drains matured entries, credits delegator, deletes empty record) but has zero production callers; its only call sites are tests at staking.rs:1203, 1209, 1859. `undelegate` is wired (native_executor.rs:5447 via exec_undelegate at :3261) and pushes `UnbondingEntry{amount, release_block: current_block + UNBONDING_PERIOD}` (staking.rs:173-176), so undelegated funds are currently stranded forever: nothing ever credits them back and the `MAX_UNBONDING_ENTRIES=100` cap (staking.rs:164) eventually blocks further undelegates. There is no user-triggered withdraw action either (grep of torus-core/torus-rpc found only read-side RpcUnbonding). The block tail in app.rs:1937-1940 runs drain_core_writer -> process_governance -> distribute_fees -> process_epoch_boundary, which is the natural place to add a per-block unbonding sweep.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:189-224 process_unbonding: per-(delegator,validator) drain of matured entries, credit_balance, delete-if-empty; returns released U256
- crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:173-176 undelegate pushes UnbondingEntry with release_block = current_block + UNBONDING_PERIOD
- crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:164-169 MAX_UNBONDING_ENTRIES=100 cap -> TooManyUnbondingEntries; never drains without process_unbonding
- crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:1203,1209,1859 the only callers of process_unbonding are #[cfg(test)]
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5440-5453 exec_undelegate calls staking.undelegate(..., ctx.block_height) -- wired
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6025-6111 process_epoch_boundary gated by EpochManager::is_epoch_boundary(ctx.block_height, ctx.epoch_length); Phase A rewards, Phase B rotation
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1937-1940 block tail: drain_core_writer, process_governance, distribute_fees, process_epoch_boundary -- the insertion point
- crates/torus-economics/src/staking.rs:866-900 delegations_for_delegator (prefix scan) and delegations_for_validator (full scan of CF_STAKING_DELEGATIONS, key = delegator(20)++validator(20))
- crates/torus-state/src/backend.rs:36-44 iterate_cf doc: results in sorted key order; backend.rs:1114-1135 overlay impl merges into BTreeMap -> deterministic ascending key order
- crates/torus-economics/src/types.rs:313 UNBONDING_PERIOD = 7*24*3600/TARGET_BLOCK_TIME_SECS (blocks)
- crates/torus-economics/src/types.rs:143-148,188-191 Delegation{unbonding: Vec<UnbondingEntry>}, UnbondingEntry{amount, release_block}

**Risk:** Funds leak: every undelegate permanently locks tokens (debited at delegate, never credited back). After 100 undelegates per pair the delegator is bricked. Hyperliquid parity: HL's 1-day unstaking queue auto-releases to the spot balance with no user action; Torus today never releases at all. Also a consensus-determinism concern once wired: the sweep must use sorted key order and run at a fixed point in the block tail so all validators produce identical state roots.

**Fix:** 1) staking.rs: add `pub fn process_all_unbonding(&self, current_block: u64) -> Result<(U256, usize)>`: `let entries = self.state.iterate_cf(CF_STAKING_DELEGATIONS, None)?;` (sorted key order = deterministic), for each 40-byte key deserialize Delegation, skip if `unbonding.iter().all(|e| e.release_block > current_block)` (no write when nothing matured, keeps the state root untouched for idle pairs), else call `self.process_unbonding(d.delegator, d.validator, current_block)` and accumulate. Reuse existing fn; no new storage. Note the per-pair fn re-reads the key -- fine, or refactor an inner `process_unbonding_delegation(key, delegation, current_block)` shared by both.
2) native_executor.rs: add `pub fn process_unbonding<T: StateBackend>(ctx: &mut NativeExecContext<T>) -> NativeActionResult` next to process_governance (~:6113): calls `ctx.staking.process_all_unbonding(ctx.block_height)`, returns ok("unbonding_release", 1000) / err(...) with tracing::error on failure (log-and-continue like Phase A rewards). Per-block, not per-epoch: release_block is a block height and HL releases on maturity, not at epoch edges. If the full-CF scan cost is a concern on the hot path (ECON-FIND-30 note at staking.rs:881-885), gate it to every N blocks (e.g. `ctx.block_height % 100 == 0`) -- still deterministic; or add a secondary index CF `CF_STAKING_UNBONDING_DUE` keyed `release_block(8 BE) ++ delegator ++ validator` written in undelegate and prefix-scanned with upper bound current_block (cleanest, but schema addition).
3) app.rs:1937-1940: insert `NativeExecutor::process_unbonding(&mut ctx);` after process_governance and BEFORE distribute_fees/process_epoch_boundary so released balance is visible in the same block's epoch snapshot; keep that ordering fixed (consensus-critical). Check whether there is a second exec path (bl2 pipeline / replay) that builds the same tail and mirror it there.
Tests: (a) staking.rs unit: two pairs with mixed release_blocks; process_all_unbonding(before) releases 0 and leaves records untouched; at release releases only matured entries; empty records deleted; (b) determinism: build two StakingManagers with same delegations inserted in different order, run sweep, assert identical state (or identical released sums + remaining records); (c) native_executor integration: Undelegate action at height h, run blocks to h+UNBONDING_PERIOD, assert delegator balance credited and RpcUnbonding list empty; assert no credit at h+UNBONDING_PERIOD-1; (d) cap regression: 100 undelegates then advance past period, 101st undelegate succeeds (extends unbonding_queue_cap_allows_after_processing at staking.rs:1838 to go through the executor tail instead of a direct call).

**Unsure:** Did not verify whether app.rs has a second exec path (bl2 pipeline/replay) with its own block tail that must mirror the new call. Did not measure CF_STAKING_DELEGATIONS size to judge whether a per-block full scan is acceptable vs. needing the release_block index. Did not confirm current HL unstaking period (HL uses ~1 day unstaking queue; Torus UNBONDING_PERIOD is 7 days -- parity may also want the constant changed, out of scope here). Did not check genesis/state-root tests that would need regenerated fixtures.

</details>

### design-funding

**opus** — absent, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~850 prod + ~350 tests (funding.rs 350, executor 200, rpc 120, state 80, position 40, app 30)

There is no funding engine. Funding appears in source only as the `MarketParams.max_funding_rate_bps: u32` field (torus-types/src/lib.rs:1161), which is serialized into hashes and EIP-712 and never read by any logic. All other "funding" hits are test constants for collateral. `Position` (torus-core/src/position.rs:52) has no funding snapshot. `OrderBook` has best_bid/best_ask and depth, but nothing computes impact prices. The RPC trait (torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:100-213) has getMarkPrice and getOpenInterest but no fundingHistory or predictedFundings. Proposed design: add a `torus-core/src/funding.rs` FundingEngine. Each block it samples a premium from impact bid/ask computed off the OrderBook levels against the oracle price. Every 3600 s of block time it settles an HL-style rate, `clamp(avg_premium + clamp(r - avg_premium, ±0.05%), ±max_funding_rate_bps)` with r = 0.01%/8h → /8 per hour, into an i128 cumulative index per market. Each position stores the index at the time it was opened or last changed, and pays or receives `size * (cum_now - snap) * oracle_px` (sign by side) when touched or at settlement. One record per market per hour is persisted for a new `torus_fundingHistory` RPC.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156-1162 MarketParams has max_funding_rate_bps: u32 (the only funding field; it ends up only in hash/EIP-712 encoding at lib.rs:828,906 and eip712.rs:620)
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:52-62 Position has trader, market_id, is_long, size, entry_price, realized_pnl, isolated_margin, margin_type. No funding snapshot field
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:84-99 Borsh serialize uses POSITION_SCHEMA_VERSION=1. Adding a field needs a version bump to 2
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:240-258 OrderBook bids/asks are BTreeMap<FixedPoint, VecDeque<Order>>. last_trade_price exists
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:798-806 best_bid/best_ask only. No impact-notional walk. bid_queues/ask_queues iterators exist at :1355/:1360 and bid_depth/ask_depth at :898/:912
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1364-1366 NativeExecContext has block_height and timestamp. Timestamp is in SECONDS (comment at :5600)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5904-5920 aggregate_oracle_prices exists per market via ctx.oracle.aggregate_price
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5923-5960 run_liquidation_checks takes oracle_prices. grep shows no caller of it or of aggregate_oracle_prices in torus-consensus/src or torus-bridge/src, so these per-block hooks look unwired
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:61-68 MarketMarginConfig (market_id, max_leverage, maintenance_factor_bps, tiers). The executor keeps it in ctx.margin_configs
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:100-213 RPC methods getOrderBook...getMarkPrice(:210), getUserTrades(:213). No funding methods

**Risk:** Without funding, the perp price is not tied to the oracle: longs and shorts carry no cost, the basis can drift without limit, and the oracle-based liquidation and mark logic diverge from the book. This is a core Hyperliquid parity gap: HL uses hourly funding with 5 s premium sampling and impact prices, and the info endpoints fundingHistory, userFunding and predictedFundings depend on it. Funding changes balances and state, so it is consensus-critical. It must use integer/FixedPoint math only, be driven by block timestamp only (not wall clock), and run in deterministic BTreeMap market order.

**Fix:** 1) NEW crates/torus-core/src/funding.rs (~350 LOC):
- `struct FundingState { market_id, cum_index: i128 /*FixedPoint raw, signed, per 1 unit of size, quote units*/, premium_sum: i128, samples: u32, last_sample_ts: u64, last_settle_ts: u64 }` with Borsh (versioned).
- `fn impact_prices(book:&OrderBook, impact_notional:FixedPoint)->Option<(FixedPoint,FixedPoint)>`: walk ask_queues() ascending and bid_queues() in reverse, summing price*size until impact_notional (HL: 20k USDC for most assets) and returning the VWAP or the marginal px.
- `fn sample(&mut self, ts, impact_bid, impact_ask, oracle)`: premium = (max(impact_bid-oracle,0) - max(oracle-impact_ask,0))/oracle. Accumulate it once per SAMPLE_INTERVAL_S (5 s; with second-resolution timestamps use >=5 s since last_sample_ts).
- `fn settle(&mut self, ts, oracle, max_rate_bps)->Option<FundingRecord>`: when ts/3600 > last_settle_ts/3600, compute avg_premium, then rate = clamp(avg + clamp(INTEREST_1H - avg, -0.0005, 0.0005), ±max_funding_rate_bps/10_000). Apply cum_index += rate*oracle (signed, longs pay when positive) and reset the accumulator.
- `fn accrue(pos:&mut Position, cum_index)->FixedPoint`: payment = size*(cum_index - pos.funding_snapshot), negated for shorts. Set snapshot = cum_index.
2) crates/torus-core/src/position.rs: add `pub funding_snapshot: i128` and `pub cum_funding: FixedPoint` (lifetime paid, which HL exposes as cumFunding). Bump POSITION_SCHEMA_VERSION to 2 (allowed pre-launch per the ECON-FIND-31 comment). Call accrue() before any size change in the position-update path and on open/close (set the snapshot on open) (~40 LOC).
3) crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs: add `pub fn run_funding<T>(ctx:&mut NativeExecContext<T>)` next to aggregate_oracle_prices (:5904). For each market in BTreeMap order, call sample() using ctx books and the aggregated oracle price. On hourly settle(), iterate the positions of that market, accrue and credit/debit the quote balance (cross: account balance; isolated: isolated_margin). Write FundingRecord {market_id, ts, rate, premium, oracle_px} into state. Add a FundingState field on the ctx and load/save it with the books (~200 LOC).
4) crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs: call aggregate_oracle_prices, then run_funding, then run_liquidation_checks once per block after the native actions (none of them appear to be called today). Settlement must use torus_block.header.timestamp (~30 LOC).
5) crates/torus-state: column/prefix for FundingState per market plus an append-only funding_history keyed (market_id, hour_ts) for range scans (~80 LOC).
6) crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs: `#[method(name="getFundingHistory")](market_id, start_ts, end_ts?) -> Vec<FundingRecord>`, `getPredictedFunding(market_id)` (current avg premium → projected rate), `getUserFunding(user, start, end)`. Add a fundingRate/premium field to getMarkPrice/meta-style output (~120 LOC).
7) Tests (~350 LOC): impact px on a thin vs deep book; clamp at max_funding_rate_bps; zero-sum (sum of long payments = -sum of short payments at the same index); a snapshot taken on mid-hour open pays only the delta; no double-settle across a missing-block hour gap (settle once, using HL's single-period rule); determinism across restart (FundingState round-trip); RPC range query.

**Unsure:** I did not read the executor's position-mutation path (where fills update Position), so the exact hook point for accrue() is not named. I did not find where the per-block oracle aggregate or liquidation is invoked. The grep of torus-consensus/src and torus-bridge/src found no callers, but it may be called from another crate (for example torus-node), so "unwired" is unconfirmed. I did not check how torus-state persists per-market metadata (meta row) to reuse for FundingState. HL constants (20k impact notional, 0.01%/8h interest, ±0.05% clamp, 4%/h cap) are from my knowledge of HL docs, not the repo. max_funding_rate_bps is u32 bps per hour, presumably; its unit and period are undocumented in lib.rs:1161. MarketListing (lib.rs:1165) lacks max_funding_rate_bps, so listing defaults need deciding. Mark price derivation (getMarkPrice, torus.rs:210) was not read; HL mark uses median(oracle+EMA basis, book mid, CEX perps), which this design does not cover.

</details>

**fable** — absent, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~600 LOC + ~250 LOC tests

No funding engine exists: `max_funding_rate_bps` is only a field on `MarketParams` (torus-types/src/lib.rs:1161) that gets hashed/EIP712-encoded, never read by any executor path; `grep` for funding_index/cumulative_funding/settle_funding across crates returns nothing. `Position` (torus-core/src/position.rs:52-62, borsh schema v1 at :88-99) has no funding snapshot field, `NativeExecContext` (native_executor.rs:1339) has no funding state, and the post-engine tail in app.rs:1937-1940 runs only drain_core_writer / process_governance / distribute_fees / process_epoch_boundary. Proposed design: a new `torus-core/src/funding.rs` with a per-market `FundingState { cum_index: FixedPoint, last_settle_ts: u64, premium_samples: Vec<FixedPoint> (ring, len<=N) }` stored in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS under a `funding:{market_id}` key, a `funding_entry_index: FixedPoint` snapshot added to `Position` (schema v2), premium sampling each block from OrderBook best_bid/best_ask vs oracle price (impact px approximated from depth), hourly settlement in a new `NativeExecutor::settle_funding` step placed before `distribute_fees` in the app.rs tail, and a `torus_getFundingHistory` RPC backed by an append-only `CF_NATIVE_FUNDING` row per (market, settle_ts).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1155-1162 — MarketParams { tick_size, lot_size, max_leverage, maintenance_margin_bps, max_funding_rate_bps: u32 }; only consumers are hashing (lib.rs:828,906, eip712.rs:620)

**Risk:** Perps without funding have no mechanism anchoring mark to index: a persistent premium is free money for one side and the oracle-based liquidation engine (run_liquidation_checks) diverges from book price indefinitely. This is a core HL-parity gap (HL: 8-hour-equivalent rate, settled hourly, premium = impact px vs oracle, clamp ±4%/hr, fundingHistory + userFunding info endpoints).

**Fix:** 1) torus-core/src/funding.rs (new): `FundingState { cum_index: FixedPoint /*quote per 1 base, signed*/, last_settle_ts: u64, sample_sum: FixedPoint, sample_count: u32 }` with borsh via borsh_write_fp/borsh_read_fp from position.rs; `fn impact_price(book:&OrderBook, side, impact_notional:FixedPoint)->Option<FixedPoint>` walking bid_depth()/ask_depth() until cumulative notional >= impact_notional (fallback best_bid/best_ask); `fn premium(bid_impact, ask_impact, oracle)->FixedPoint` = (max(0,bid-oracle) - max(0,oracle-ask))/oracle; `fn hourly_rate(avg_premium, interest=1bp/8h, cap_bps)->FixedPoint` = clamp(avg_premium/8 + interest/8 ... per HL: rate = premium + clamp(interest-premium, ±0.05%), then clamp to ±max_funding_rate_bps/1e4). 2) Position: add `funding_entry_index: FixedPoint`, bump POSITION_SCHEMA_VERSION to 2 (position.rs:85-130), set from market cum_index in apply_fill/apply_fill_cached_effect when a position is opened/flipped; on size change settle accrued (size*(cum_index-entry_index)) into realized_pnl first. 3) MarketMarginConfig (margin.rs:61) gains `max_funding_rate_bps: u32` populated from MarketParams at list/UpdateMarketParams (native_executor.rs:3332, 5754). 4) NativeExecutor::sample_premium(ctx) each block (cheap: best_bid/ask + depth walk per market, oracle via ctx.oracle.get_price) and NativeExecutor::settle_funding(ctx) called in app.rs:1937 tail before distribute_fees when ctx.timestamp/3600 > last_settle_ts/3600: rate = hourly_rate(sample_sum/sample_count); cum_index += rate*oracle_px; write FundingState row to CF_NATIVE_MARKETS key `b\"funding:\"+market_id`; append `(market_id, u64::MAX-settle_ts) -> {rate, premium, oracle_px, cum_index}` to new CF_NATIVE_FUNDING (cf.rs). Payment is lazy: positions settle on next touch (fill/liquidation/close) via PositionManager::settle_funding(pos,&FundingState) which moves size*(cum_index - funding_entry_index) with sign by is_long into native balance (cross) or isolated_margin; margin.rs check_liquidation and unrealized_pnl callers must include pending funding. 5) RPC: torus.rs trait add `get_funding_history(market_id, limit) -> Vec<RpcFundingRate{market_id,timestamp,rate,premium,oracle_price}>` and `get_user_funding(trader)` computing pending per position; RpcPosition (types.rs:276) gains `pending_funding`. Est. core ~250 LOC, executor ~150, position/margin ~80, rpc ~120, tests ~250.

HL exact formula (8h interest 0.01%, hourly cap 4%) cited from memory, not verified against current HL docs.

### design-mark-price

**opus** — design, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~700-900 LOC: core ~250, tests ~250, executor and app wiring ~110, stop trigger ~40-80, precompile and RPC ~55, renames ~20

There is no mark price in the code today. The name "mark" is only a parameter: margin, liquidation and precompile PnL take the raw stake-weighted oracle price (`oracle_prices: &[(MarketId, FixedPoint)]`, `get_oracle_price_fp`), and stop orders fire on the book's own `last_trade_price`. Nothing calls `run_liquidation_checks` or `aggregate_oracle_prices`, and there is no funding or premium engine. Proposed design: a new `torus-core/src/mark_price.rs` with a per-market `MarkState { oracle_px, basis_ema, last_update_ms }`, updated once per block in the executor after oracle aggregation. It computes HL's mark as `median(oracle + EMA(mid - oracle), median(best_bid, best_ask, last_trade), cex_perp_mid_if_any)`, with impact bid/ask (book walked to a fixed impact notional) feeding a premium index for future funding. The result goes into a `CF_NATIVE_ORACLE` "mark" key next to the aggregated oracle price, and every consumer that now receives raw oracle prices reads `mark_prices` instead.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:101,161,182,194,206,215 - MarginEngine equity and maintenance margin take `oracle_prices` and look them up with `oracle_price_for` (253)
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:66-77 - unrealized_pnl and notional take `mark_price`, but every caller passes the oracle price
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:76,120-124,153-155,196-207,259-312 - check_liquidations, check_isolated_liquidation, execute_liquidation and ADC all use `oracle_price` for PnL, notional and fill price
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5904-5919 - aggregate_oracle_prices loops OracleManager::aggregate_price; a repo-wide grep finds no caller
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5923-5975 - run_liquidation_checks takes `oracle_prices` and skips a market that has no oracle price (FIX 5); a grep finds no caller in crates/
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1272-1290 - trigger_stops fires on `self.last_trade_price` only
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:798-809 - best_bid, best_ask and spread exist and can supply the book-mid input
- crates/torus-core/src/book_rows.rs:164 / book_reader.rs:419 - last_trade_price is persisted in the book meta row and can be read through read_last_trade_price
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:74-80,274-296 - OraclePrice {price, block_number, stale, num_reporters}, stored as StoredAggregatedPrice in CF_NATIVE_ORACLE; OracleManager::get_price has no EMA and no mark
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:446-449 - the position precompile computes unrealized PnL with get_oracle_price_fp (raw oracle)
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs - the struct and fn list has no ema/EMA (grep found nothing); no funding_rate or premium in torus-core or torus-bridge

**Risk:** With the raw oracle as mark, liquidations follow the validator oracle alone, so stale or lagging oracles produce wrong or missed liquidations, and liquidation and ADL settle at the oracle price (liquidation.rs:247). Stops fire on a single last trade on the local book, so a thin book can be wicked to trigger stops. HL triggers TP/SL on mark, not last trade. Both the margin engine and the liquidation sweep are effectively unwired today (no callers), so HL parity needs the mark price and the per-block sweep wired together. The design also needs the mark to be computed deterministically from consensus state: oracle aggregate, book state at end of block, and a basis EMA with integer fixed-point decay. It must not use wall-clock time, or nodes diverge.

**Fix:** 1) New file crates/torus-core/src/mark_price.rs (~250 LOC plus ~200 test LOC):
- Structs `MarkConfig { ema_half_life_blocks, impact_notional, max_dev_from_oracle_bps }` and `MarkState { basis_ema: FixedPoint, mark: FixedPoint, impact_bid, impact_ask, block }` with Borsh, stored in CF_NATIVE_ORACLE under a `mark:{market}` key next to aggregated_price_key.
- Functions:
  - `fn book_inputs(&OrderBook) -> (Option<mid>, Option<last_trade>, impact_bid, impact_ask)`, built from best_bid, best_ask, last_trade_price and a level walk to impact_notional.
  - `fn update(prev, oracle, inputs, cfg) -> MarkState`, where the EMA uses integer decay α = 1 - 2^(-1/half_life) precomputed as a FixedPoint, and `mark = median3(oracle + basis_ema, median3(bid, ask, last), oracle)`. When the book side is missing it falls back to oracle + basis_ema, and the result is clamped to ±max_dev of the oracle.
  - `premium = (max(impact_bid - oracle, 0) - max(oracle - impact_ask, 0)) / oracle`, a hook for a future funding engine.
- MarkManager: get_mark(market, block), plus a `mark_prices(markets) -> Vec<(MarketId, FixedPoint)>` that returns the same shape as `oracle_prices` today, so swapping it in is a one-line change at each consumer.
2) native_executor.rs (~80 LOC):
- Add `update_mark_prices(ctx, markets)`, run end-of-block after aggregate_oracle_prices and after matching, using resident books.
- Change run_liquidation_checks to take mark_prices. Liquidation PnL stays on mark, but HL also uses mark for the liquidation fill/backstop, so pass mark into execute_liquidation and auto_deleverage.
- Wire both into the end-of-block path in crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs (~30 LOC). Neither is called today.
3) margin.rs and liquidation.rs: only the parameter changes (rename oracle_prices to mark_prices). The math is already price-agnostic, ~20 LOC of renames.
4) order_book.rs trigger_stops (~40 LOC):
- Add `trigger_ref: Option<FixedPoint>` (mark) to OrderBook and set it from the executor before matching.
- Fire on mark when it is present and fall back to last_trade_price otherwise. Optionally add a per-order `TriggerRef::{Mark, Last}` flag, but that changes stop_rows serialization (schema byte bump, ~40 LOC) and the boot verify for stop rows.
5) precompiles.rs:446 get_oracle_price_fp: use the mark key and fall back to oracle (~15 LOC).
6) RPC (~40 LOC): expose markPx, oraclePx, impactPxs and premium in the market context, like HL's metaAndAssetCtxs.
Tests:
- median and EMA determinism, using fixed vectors that run identically across nodes.
- A thin-book wick does not trigger a mark-based stop.
- A stale oracle with a healthy book keeps mark within the clamp.
- A liquidation fires on mark rather than oracle.
- An app-level test that the end-of-block sweep runs and the state root is stable across replay.

**Unsure:** I did not read app.rs's end-of-block flow or check how the executor checks margin at order placement. The grep found no MarginEngine::* call in torus-bridge or consensus, so placement margin may be reservation-only and need its own mark hookup. I did not confirm whether a CEX perp-mid input exists for the third median term; without one, the design uses a 3-way median of oracle+EMA basis, the book median and the oracle. I did not check the RPC crate for existing markPx fields. The fallback when the oracle is stale (freeze the mark or use book-only) is a policy decision. I did not confirm that "no callers" for run_liquidation_checks and aggregate_oracle_prices holds outside crates/, for example in bins or node.

</details>

**fable** — design, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~450 (mark.rs 250, executor 80, order_book stops 60, margin/liq param rename 30, rpc 20) + ~150 tests

There is no mark price today: every margin/liquidation/PnL path takes a raw `&[(MarketId, FixedPoint)]` oracle vector (`oracle_price_for` in margin.rs, inline `.find()` in liquidation.rs and native_executor.rs), RPC `get_mark_price` returns the oracle price as both mark and index, and stop orders trigger solely off `OrderBook.last_trade_price`. No funding/premium/EMA code exists anywhere in crates (grep "funding" hits only torus-types action encodings). Proposed design: add `MarkPriceEngine` in a new `crates/torus-core/src/mark.rs` that, once per block after `aggregate_oracle_prices`, computes per market `mark = median(oracle + ema_basis, book_mid_or_impact, last_trade)` with HL semantics (basis EMA = oracle-relative premium of book mid, 150-block/~10-min decay; fall back to the available components if book is empty), persists a `StoredMarkPrice{mark, ema_basis, block}` in a new CF key next to `aggregated_price_key`, and exposes `mark_prices(ctx) -> Vec<(MarketId, FixedPoint)>` that replaces the oracle vector fed to margin, liquidation, ADL and RPC PnL; stops get a `TriggerSource::Mark` evaluated from the executor (not from inside the book) while funding/settlement keep raw oracle.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:101 check_initial_margin takes oracle_prices: &[(MarketId, FixedPoint)]; :194 and :215 cross_margin_equity/total_maintenance_margin call oracle_price_for(oracle_prices, ...) and name the result `mark`; :253 oracle_price_for helper
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:76,120,153-160 check_liquidations/check_cross_liquidation/check_isolated_liquidation all take oracle_prices; isolated does inline .find() and rejects <=0
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5904-5920 aggregate_oracle_prices (per-block oracle aggregation hook); :5923-5985 run_liquidation_checks takes oracle_prices, re-finds oracle_price and passes it to execute_liquidation and auto_deleverage
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:74-86 OraclePrice/StoredAggregatedPrice (price, block_number, num_reporters, stale); :274-296 get_price with staleness via max_oracle_age
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1272-1290 trigger_stops uses self.last_trade_price only; :422-467 StopMarket/StopLimit validate trigger vs current_price; :798/:803/:877 best_bid/best_ask/last_trade_price accessors exist
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:798-802 position unrealized PnL uses oracle.get_price(...).price, fallback entry_price; :1609,1638-1639 get_mark_price returns oracle price as both mark_price and index_price
- crates/torus-core/src/book_reader.rs:319 read_book_depth, :419 read_last_trade_price (rows-layout readers usable for mid/impact)
- grep: no `funding`/`premium`/`basis` symbol in torus-core, torus-bridge, torus-economics src

**Risk:** HL parity: HL marks positions, computes liquidation and triggers TP/SL off mark (median of oracle+EMA basis, book mid/impact, last trade), which resists both oracle lag and single-print book manipulation. Here a single stale oracle tick liquidates everyone, PnL shown to users ignores the local book, and stops fire on one wash trade. Any HL-style client (TP/SL semantics, mark-based margin display) will diverge.

**Fix:** 1) New `crates/torus-core/src/mark.rs` (~250 LOC): `pub struct MarkInputs{oracle: Option<FixedPoint>, best_bid, best_ask, last_trade: Option<FixedPoint>, prev_ema_basis: FixedPoint}`; `pub struct MarkPrice{mark, ema_basis, oracle, block}`; `pub fn compute_mark(inputs, cfg: &MarkConfig) -> Option<MarkPrice>` doing: mid=(bid+ask)/2 (or impact price via `book_reader::read_book_depth` walked to `cfg.impact_notional`), basis=mid-oracle, ema=prev+(basis-prev)/cfg.ema_window, c1=oracle+ema, c2=mid, c3=last_trade, mark=median of available components (>=2 required, else oracle). Borsh `StoredMarkPrice` + `mark_price_key(market_id)` in CF_NATIVE_ORACLE alongside `aggregated_price_key`. Unit tests: median with 3/2/1 inputs, EMA convergence, empty book fallback, zero-oracle rejection mirroring liquidation.rs:160. 2) `native_executor.rs` (~80 LOC): add `pub fn update_mark_prices(ctx, markets)` called right after `aggregate_oracle_prices` (:5904); read `ctx.oracle.get_price`, book best_bid/best_ask/last_trade_price (order_book.rs:798/803/877), write StoredMarkPrice; add `pub fn mark_prices(ctx, markets) -> Vec<(MarketId, FixedPoint)>`; feed that vector into `run_liquidation_checks` (:5923) and `MarginEngine::check_initial_margin` call sites instead of the oracle vector (rename params `oracle_prices`->`mark_prices` in margin.rs:101/161/182/206 and liquidation.rs:76/120/153, ~30 LOC mechanical). 3) Stops (~60 LOC): add `trigger_source: TriggerSource{LastTrade, Mark}` to the stop struct at order_book.rs:101 (borsh at :2260-2323, default LastTrade for back-compat) and a `pub fn trigger_stops_at(&mut self, price)` public wrapper around :1272 that the executor calls with the new mark after `update_mark_prices`. 4) RPC (~20 LOC): torus.rs:798 and :1609 read StoredMarkPrice via a `MarkReader`/`OracleManager::get_mark` and return mark vs index separately. 5) Keep raw oracle for funding when it lands (none exists). Integration test in torus-bridge: oracle 100, book 98/102, last 103 -> mark 100.x; liquidation fires at mark not oracle.

**Unsure:** Did not verify who (if anyone) calls `run_liquidation_checks` or `MarginEngine::check_initial_margin` from the executor/app: a grep of crates excluding tests found only their definitions, so the live order path may use `reserve_for_qty_cfg` (native_executor.rs:4799) and the liquidation driver may be unwired; if so the mark-price plumbing must also wire those. Did not read the executor per-block hook ordering in app.rs to confirm where `aggregate_oracle_prices` is invoked. HL's exact impact-notional and EMA window constants not checked; `impact_notional` should be a MarketMarginConfig field. Did not inspect book_rows.rs for the fastest mid read in rows layout.

### design-bands-oi

**opus** — absent, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~450-650 LOC: ~80 for the struct and pure checker in core, ~120 for the executor wiring at three sites plus the oracle snapshot, ~40 for the order_book market price cap, ~100 for OI state, persistence and the fill hook (including liquidation/ADL paths), ~40 for the types/governance plumbing, ~200 for tests

None of the four controls exist today. The executor's pre-book phase checks only the margin reserve, and that one check is copied in three places: exec_place_order, the serial batch loop and the parallel prep worker. OrderBook::place_order checks lot size, price > 0, tick size, orders per trader and market-order liquidity, but never compares a price with the oracle. A Market order sweeps the book with no worst-price limit; the only check is "has liquidity". There is no open-interest state and no per-market OI cap. "max_notional" exists only as the margin-tier cutoff in MarginTier, not as a per-order limit. Proposed design: add a per-market MarketRiskLimits (oracle_band_bps, market_slippage_bps, oi_cap, max_order_notional). Check it in one pure function, check_order_limits(), called from all three pre-book sites, using an oracle-price snapshot taken once per block. Market orders get a worst price (oracle ± slippage) that the book's matching loop enforces. Long OI per market is tracked incrementally from FillEffect.start_size inside apply_fill_via_caches.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4906-4955 exec_place_order: only the margin reserve before the book (Market reserves ZERO), no oracle or notional check
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3745-3790 serial batch loop: the same margin-only pre-book logic
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3996-4045 parallel prep worker: the same margin-only logic, which yields PrepOutcome::Reject{margin,msg}; it sees only margin_configs and the positions cache
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3731 PrepOutcome::Reject is stitched into results serially, so a new reject reason fits this path
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1339-1356 NativeExecContext holds order_books, dirty_books and margin_configs: HashMap<MarketId, MarketMarginConfig>, with no OI field
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4713-4737 apply_fill_via_caches: every fill passes through here and gets a FillEffect, the natural OI update hook
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:400-405 FillEffect{start_size (signed), closed_pnl}: with is_buy/qty, the OI delta can be computed with no extra reads
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:376-416 place_order validation: lot, price>0 (Limit only), tick (Limit only), MAX_ORDERS_PER_TRADER_PER_MARKET
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:507-523 Market order: rejected only if the opposite side is empty, with no slippage or price cap
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:16-48,61-68 MarginTier.max_notional is a leverage-tier cutoff; MarketMarginConfig{market_id,max_leverage,maintenance_factor_bps,tiers}
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:274-280 OracleManager::get_price(market_id, current_block) reads CF_NATIVE_ORACLE, a state read per call
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156-1162 MarketParams{tick_size,lot_size,max_leverage,maintenance_margin_bps,max_funding_rate_bps} has no risk-limit fields

**Risk:** Without bands, a fat-finger or manipulative limit order far from the oracle rests or fills. A Market order on a thin book sweeps to any price, and those prints feed mark, liquidations and PnL. Without an OI cap, one market's exposure (and so the insurance fund and ADL risk) is unbounded, which matters most for newly listed or illiquid perps. Hyperliquid enforces all of these at protocol level: an oracle/reference price band on limit orders, slippage-bounded market orders and per-asset OI caps that reject OI-increasing orders at the cap. Their absence is a parity gap and a manipulation risk.

**Fix:** 1) torus-core/src/margin.rs: add `pub struct MarketRiskLimits { oracle_band_bps: u32 /*e.g. 8000 = ±80%*/, market_slippage_bps: u32 /*e.g. 500*/, oi_cap: FixedPoint /*long-side notional or size; MAX = off*/, max_order_notional: FixedPoint }`. Either add it as `risk: MarketRiskLimits` on MarketMarginConfig with a serde default (it already reaches all three pre-book sites as margin_configs), or add a separate `risk_limits` map. Add a pure `pub fn check_order_limits(lim, oracle_px: Option<FixedPoint>, params, oi_now) -> Result<Option<FixedPoint /*market worst px*/>, String>`. Its rules: (a) for Limit/stop, |price-oracle|/oracle <= band, else reject "price too far from oracle"; (b) notional (price, or oracle for Market, times qty) <= max_order_notional; (c) when !reduce_only and oi_now >= oi_cap, reject "open interest cap reached". To avoid a per-order position read, the first version rejects every non-reduce-only order at the cap; a later version can allow orders that reduce the trader's own position via pos_cache. (d) For Market, return the worst px = oracle*(1±slippage).
2) native_executor.rs: before prep, build `oracle_snapshot: HashMap<MarketId, FixedPoint>` once per block via ctx.oracle.get_price, so the parallel workers do no state reads. Call check_order_limits at 4912 (exec_place_order), at about 3753 (serial loop) and at about 4002 (prep worker, which pushes PrepOutcome::Reject{margin:false}). Count rejects in orders_rejected_other.
3) Market slippage: carry the worst price into the book by setting params.price = worst_px on Market orders (the price field is unused for Market today). Then in OrderBook matching (order_book.rs after 523; the match loop was not read) stop matching a Market order once the best opposite level crosses order.price when the price is > 0, and cancel the rest IOC-style. Old Market orders with price 0 keep today's behavior, but the executor always sets the price, so this changes consensus.
4) OI tracking: add `pub open_interest: HashMap<MarketId, FixedPoint>` to NativeExecContext (1339), loaded and saved like the order_global_id counter (one key per market in a native CF, written only if dirty). Update it in apply_fill_via_caches: with s0 = effect.start_size and s1 = s0 ± qty, long OI += max(s1,0) - max(s0,0), applied for both taker and maker, which is O(1) per fill. Liquidation and ADL fills must go through the same hook or apply the same delta. Seed once at upgrade height by iterating positions, or start at 0 behind an activation height.
5) Governance and listing: add the fields to MarketParams/MarketListing (torus-types lib.rs:1156) and a governance action to set limits.
Tests: limit order outside the band rejected and inside accepted, in all three pre-book paths (serial, parallel prep, single), with byte-identical results between serial and parallel; a market order on a thin book stops at the slippage price and cancels the rest; the OI delta matches recomputing from all positions after random fills (property test); at the cap, an opening order is rejected and a reduce_only order accepted; a notional cap test; and a state-root determinism test across thread counts.

**Unsure:** I did not read the OrderBook matching loop (order_book.rs beyond line 540), so the exact place for the market worst-price stop is inferred. I did not check whether liquidation/ADL fills (around native_executor.rs:5926-5976) go through apply_fill_via_caches; if they bypass it, the OI hook needs a second call site. I also did not check how OraclePrice exposes its value or staleness, or how margin_configs is persisted and serialized (adding a field may need a migration rather than a serde default). The Hyperliquid values here (±80% band from the reference price, market slippage handled by the client as an IOC limit, OI cap rejecting OI-increasing orders) are from memory and not verified against current HL docs.

</details>

**fable** — absent, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~250 non-test + ~200 test

No order price bands, market-order slippage cap, OI cap/tracking, or max-notional check exists today. `OrderBook::place_order` (crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:367-420) only rejects dust (< lot_size), non-positive limit price, tick misalignment, and MAX_ORDERS_PER_TRADER_PER_MARKET; market orders carry price ZERO and sweep the book unbounded. The executor's `exec_place_order` (native_executor.rs:4906+) and the batched Phase 2 path (native_executor.rs:3755) only do margin reservation (`reserve_for_qty`) and never consult the oracle (`OracleManager::get_price`, oracle.rs:274) or per-market config. `MarketParams`/`MarketListing` (torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156-1172) have no band/OI/notional fields and `ListMarket`/`UpdateMarketParams` are no-ops in the executor (native_executor.rs:3332-3335), so there is no per-market risk-config row to hang limits on. Proposed design: add a `MarketRiskParams` row in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS (keyed per market, loaded into a `HashMap<MarketId, MarketRiskParams>` on `NativeExecContext`) and a per-market `MarketOi` counter maintained in `apply_fill`'s `FillEffect` path; enforce bands/slippage/notional in a single `validate_order_risk` called from both exec_place_order and the Phase 2 batched prepare, and enforce OI cap at fill time using the signed-size delta already available via `FillEffect.start_size`.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:367-420 place_order: only dust, price<=0, tick, order-count checks; no band/notional/slippage
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:240-253 OrderBook fields: tick_size, lot_size, last_trade_price; no oracle/OI fields
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1060-1080 PlaceOrderParams {market_id,is_buy,price,quantity,order_type,...}; OrderType::Market has no slippage/limit price
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156-1172 MarketParams/MarketListing: tick,lot,max_leverage,maintenance_margin_bps,max_funding_rate_bps only
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4906-4960 exec_place_order: margin reserve via reserve_for_qty, is_market skips reserve, OrderBook::new(market_id, ONE, ONE) default; no oracle read
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3755-3775 Phase 2 batched prepare duplicates reserve logic (second insertion point)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3332-3335 UpdateMarketParams/ListMarket are no-op results
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1339-1341 NativeExecContext has `oracle: OracleManager<T>`
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:274-290 OracleManager::get_price(market_id, current_block) -> OraclePrice{price,stale,...} reads CF_NATIVE_ORACLE per call
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:309-333 apply_fill returns FillEffect{start_size, closed_pnl}; signed size delta computable here
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:61-68 MarketMarginConfig {max_leverage, maintenance_factor_bps, tiers} - existing per-market config to extend
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:45 CF_NATIVE_MARKETS exists (already used for book-mode marker and global order id counter rows)

**Risk:** Without bands a fat-finger limit at 10x oracle rests and can be filled by a market order sweeping the book; a market order with no slippage cap can execute at arbitrary prices in a thin book, triggering cascading liquidations; without OI cap a single market can accumulate exposure beyond the insurance fund's capacity. HL enforces all four (limit orders must be within ~95% of oracle for most markets / 80% ask-side, market orders are IOC with a default 5% slippage, per-asset OI caps, max notional per order); parity requires all four.

**Fix:** 1) torus-types/src/lib.rs: add `pub struct MarketRiskParams { price_band_bps: u32 /*e.g. 9500 => limit must be within oracle*(1±band)*/, max_slippage_bps: u32 /*default 500*/, oi_cap: FixedPoint /*base-asset units, ZERO=unlimited*/, max_order_notional: FixedPoint }` (borsh+serde), and extend `MarketParams`/`MarketListing` and `ProposalAction::UpdateMarketParams` with it. Add `OrderType::Market` slippage override: new optional `slippage_bps: Option<u32>` on PlaceOrderParams, or convert market orders to IOC-limit at `oracle*(1±slippage)` (HL semantics). 2) torus-state: new key helpers in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS: `market_risk_key(market_id)` and `market_oi_key(market_id)` (OI stored as a single FixedPoint = sum of |position size| over longs, i.e. total long = total short). 3) native_executor.rs: on NativeExecContext add `risk_params: HashMap<MarketId, MarketRiskParams>` and `market_oi: HashMap<MarketId, FixedPoint>` loaded in `new_with_mode` (near line 1740 where OracleManager is built) and written back in `save_order_books`/`save_order_books_deferred` (lines 2581/2837) as dirty rows. Implement `exec_list_market`/`UpdateMarketParams` (lines 3332-3335) to persist the row. Add `fn validate_order_risk(ctx, params, oracle_px: Option<FixedPoint>) -> Result<(), String>` and call it in both `exec_place_order` (before reserve, ~line 4915) and Phase 2 batched prepare (~line 3755): (a) notional = price*qty (market: oracle*qty) <= max_order_notional; (b) Limit: price within [oracle*(1-band), oracle*(1+band)] unless reduce_only; skip when oracle stale/absent (log + allow, matching current liquidation 'skip if no oracle' policy at line 5951); (c) Market: rewrite to limit price = oracle*(1±slippage) with TimeInForce::IOC so OrderBook::place_order already bounds the sweep (no order_book.rs matching change needed). Oracle prices: read once per block into a `HashMap<MarketId, FixedPoint>` (ctx already builds `oracle_prices: &[(MarketId, FixedPoint)]` for run_liquidation_checks at line 5926; reuse it). 4) OI cap: in the fill-settlement loop that calls `apply_fill_cached_effect` (position.rs:364), compute delta_oi = max(|new_size|,0) - max(|start_size|,0) for the side that increases exposure; cheapest: track `market_oi += (|new|-|start|)` for BOTH maker and taker and halve for reporting, or track long-side only. Reject pre-match: in validate_order_risk, if `market_oi[m] + qty > oi_cap` and order is not reduce_only, reject (pessimistic, O(1), no per-fill rejection needed; fills can still slightly overshoot via partial reduces, which is acceptable and matches HL's 'open-increasing orders rejected' behavior). 5) Tests: order_book.rs tests for IOC-limit rewrite; native_executor tests: limit outside band rejected, reduce_only inside band allowed, market order rewritten to IOC at oracle±5%, notional cap, OI cap rejects opening but allows closing, OI counter survives save/reload (state root determinism). LOC: types ~40, state keys ~20, executor ~180 (validate fn ~60, ctx load/save ~50, list/update market ~30, OI accounting ~40), tests ~200.

**Unsure:** Did not read the fill-settlement loop (Phase 4) to confirm exactly where apply_fill_cached_effect is called per fill, nor whether OrderBook already supports IOC TimeInForce (TimeInForce enum exists on Order but variants not verified). Did not verify whether oracle prices are already loaded into a per-block map before Phase 2 (only saw run_liquidation_checks takes a slice). Exact HL band numbers (95%/80%, 5% default slippage, OI caps per asset) are from memory, not verified against current HL docs.

</details>

### design-tpsl

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: 900-1300 (incl ~300 tests)

Only plain stop orders exist. `OrderType::StopMarket{trigger}` and `StopLimit{trigger,limit}` are defined in torus-types. The book parks them in `OrderBook.pending_stops: Vec<StopOrder>` and fires them in `trigger_stops()`. That function compares against `last_trade_price`, not mark price, and runs only inside `place_order` after a fill. There is no tpsl flag, no order grouping (normalTpsl/positionTpsl), no parent/child link and no per-block mark-price sweep. `trigger_stops` calls `self.place_order(...)` and checks only `result.status`. The triggered order's `fills` are dropped, so its fills probably never reach executor settlement. The proposed design replaces this path with a per-block sweep that returns fills and adds TP/SL semantics and grouping, roughly 900-1300 LOC including tests.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1060-1069 PlaceOrderParams has {market_id,is_buy,price,quantity,order_type,time_in_force,reduce_only,client_order_id}: no tpsl or grouping field
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1072-1082 enum OrderType {Limit, Market, StopMarket{trigger}, StopLimit{trigger,limit}}
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:93-107 private struct StopOrder {id,trader,market_id,side,trigger_price,limit_price,quantity,tif,timestamp,reduce_only,client_order_id}: no tpsl kind, parent or position link
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:422-453 StopMarket placement checks trigger direction from side only (Buy: trigger>current, Sell: trigger<current), pushes to pending_stops and returns PendingTrigger. TP/SL direction depends on tp vs sl, not side
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:576-579 stops trigger only from place_order when fills are non-empty and !triggering_stops (last-trade driven, not mark)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1271-1336 trigger_stops(): uses last_trade_price, runs up to 10 cascade rounds and calls self.place_order(params, stop.trader, stop.timestamp). Only result.status==Rejected is inspected; result.fills is discarded
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:778-781 pub fn check_stops() is a manual trigger; grep finds no caller outside order_book
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1377-1414 pending_stops id-ascending invariant plus a rebuild push hook (deterministic sweep order already enforced)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:2536-2538 snapshot serializes pending_stops (needs a format bump for new fields)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4118-4135 executor treats PendingTrigger as a resting state for margin reservation and computes filled qty only from the top-level result.fills
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4775-4777 PendingTrigger is a no-op in metrics/status handling ('re-enters the matching funnel when triggered')
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5922-5940 run_liquidation_checks(ctx, traders, oracle_prices) is the existing per-market oracle-price sweep shape; grep across crates found no caller besides its definition
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6182 StopMarket is categorized as NonGtcOrder; eip712.rs:260-261 and precompiles.rs:800 encode StopMarket=2/StopLimit=3; rpc torus.rs:1896-1897 renders stop_market/stop_limit

**Risk:** HL parity: Hyperliquid triggers TP/SL on mark price, checked every block, using the `tpsl:"tp"|"sl"` + `isMarket` + `triggerPx` order shape and action-level `grouping: na|normalTpsl|positionTpsl`. Without these, bracket orders and position-sized TP/SL are impossible, and stops fire on manipulable last-trade prints. Separate from parity: fills from a triggered stop are probably dropped. The book reduces maker resting qty while the executor never settles positions, margin or fees for those fills. That is a plausible state/accounting divergence that already exists on main, and the fix belongs in the same work.

**Fix:** 1) torus-types/src/lib.rs (~80 LOC). Add `enum Tpsl { Tp, Sl }` and `OrderType::Trigger { trigger_px, is_market, limit_px, tpsl: Tpsl }`. Keep StopMarket/StopLimit as aliases that map to Sl/Tp by direction. Add `enum OrderGrouping { Na, NormalTpsl, PositionTpsl }` and a `BulkOrder { orders: Vec<PlaceOrderParams>, grouping }` NativeAction, as HL does. Update eip712.rs:260 type codes (4=Trigger), precompiles.rs:800 decoding, and rpc torus.rs:1896 rendering (~60 LOC).
2) torus-core/src/order_book.rs (~300 LOC). Extend StopOrder with `tpsl: Option<Tpsl>`, `parent: Option<OrderId>`, `position_tpsl: bool` and `active: bool`. Fire direction comes from (tpsl, side): a Sell TP fires when mark >= px and a Sell SL when mark <= px, mirrored for Buy. Relax the validation at 422-430 for tpsl orders. Add `pub fn sweep_triggers(&mut self, mark: FixedPoint, size_of: impl Fn(Address)->FixedPoint) -> Vec<(StopOrder, PlaceResult)>`, which returns every triggered PlaceResult with its fills. Iterate in id-ascending order (invariant at 1377). Delete the last-trade auto-trigger at 576-579, or route it through the same return path; at minimum stop discarding `result.fills` at 1315.
3) normalTpsl (~150 LOC). Children are inserted with active=false and parent=Some(oid). On each parent fill the executor calls `book.activate_children(parent_oid, filled_qty)`, which activates them, sizes them to the cumulative filled qty and forces reduce_only. If the parent is cancelled with zero fill, cancel the children. Hook this where fills are settled in native_executor.rs (around 4118-4135).
4) positionTpsl (~120 LOC). quantity=0 means the whole position. At sweep time the size is |ctx.positions[trader][market]| and reduce_only=true. Allow one TP and one SL per (trader, market), replace on re-submit, and auto-cancel when the position flattens. Do that in the executor's post-fill position update.
5) native_executor.rs (~200 LOC). Add `run_trigger_sweep(ctx, mark_prices: &[(MarketId, FixedPoint)])`, called once per block at the deterministic end-of-block point next to the oracle aggregate (5910-5916) and before run_liquidation_checks.
