**fable** — design, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~700-1000 LOC: types ~60, order_book.rs ~300 (+150 tests), native_executor.rs ~200 (+100 tests), rpc ~100

Current state: trigger orders exist only as StopMarket/StopLimit in OrderType (torus-types/src/lib.rs:1072-1082); the book keeps them in OrderBook.pending_stops: Vec<StopOrder> (order_book.rs:96-107, 251) and fires them in trigger_stops() off last_trade_price only, synchronously inside place_order after fills (order_book.rs:576-578, 1271-1337). There is no tpsl flag, no mark-price trigger, no parent-child linkage, and no position-linked resize. StopOrder has a hand-written Borsh layout persisted via stop_rows()/restore_stop_row()/diff_stop_rows (order_book.rs:1375-1412, 2382-2415; native_executor.rs:2985). Proposed design: (1) add `tpsl: Option<Tpsl>` (`Tpsl { kind: Tp|Sl, is_market: bool, grouping: Normal{parent: OrderId} | Position }`) to PlaceOrderParams/StopOrder, with trigger source = mark px; (2) a per-block sweep `NativeExecutor::trigger_tpsl_sweep(ctx, oracle_prices)` run next to run_liquidation_checks, calling a new `OrderBook::trigger_stops_at(mark_px)` (factor trigger_stops by price source); (3) normalTpsl: children stored in a `dormant: Vec<StopOrder>` set on the book, activated (moved to pending_stops) from the settle path when the parent fills (apply_fill_via_caches / settle_market_results_*), cancelled if parent cancelled (cancel_order); (4) positionTpsl: after each fill effect, resize or cancel every Position-grouped stop for (trader, market) to the new position size, sweep-side also drops them when the position is closed.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1060-1082 PlaceOrderParams has no tpsl/grouping field; OrderType = Limit\|Market\|StopMarket{trigger}\|StopLimit{trigger,limit}
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:96-107 StopOrder{id,trader,market_id,side,trigger_price,limit_price,quantity,time_in_force,timestamp,reduce_only,client_order_id} — no parent/tpsl fields
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:251,257 pending_stops: Vec<StopOrder>, triggering_stops recursion guard
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:420-490 place_order pushes stops into pending_stops with trigger-direction validation against current_price
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:576-578 stops only triggered when a place_order produced fills
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1271-1337 trigger_stops uses self.last_trade_price exclusively; re-places as Market/Limit via place_order, max 10 cascade rounds
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:778-780 pub check_stops() exists (manual trigger) — no non-test caller found by grep
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1375-1412 stop_rows()/restore_stop_row() persist StopOrder as custom Borsh, id-ascending invariant
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:2382-2415 hand-written BorshSerialize for StopOrder (field-by-field; extending layout requires version/tag bump)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:2985 diff_stop_rows writes stop rows per market at save
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5904,5923-5960 aggregate_oracle_prices / run_liquidation_checks take oracle_prices: &[(MarketId, FixedPoint)] — the natural per-block mark-price hook; grep found no non-test callers of either
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4713-4730 apply_fill_via_caches -> positions.apply_fill_cached_effect returns FillEffect (hook point for positionTpsl resize and normalTpsl activation)
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:52-76 Position has unrealized_pnl/notional(mark_price); PositionCache (551-601) merged per market
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:590,644,651,695 cancel_order/cancel_all remove pending stops by trader (child-cancel-on-parent-cancel hook)

**Risk:** Without mark-price triggering, TP/SL can be fired by a single wick in last-trade price (manipulable, HL uses mark px precisely to avoid this) and never fire on an idle book since trigger_stops only runs after a fill. Without positionTpsl, a user's SL stays sized to the original entry after partial closes, leaving residual exposure or over-closing (reduce_only only caps, does not resize). Without normalTpsl, SL/TP cannot be attached to an unfilled entry — a core HL order-form feature. Both are parity gaps that front-ends and HL API clients (orderType.trigger.tpsl, grouping na/normalTpsl/positionTpsl) depend on.

**Fix:** 1) torus-types/src/lib.rs: add `pub enum TpslKind{Tp,Sl}`, `pub enum OrderGrouping{Na, NormalTpsl, PositionTpsl}`, extend OrderType with `Trigger{ trigger_px, is_market, tpsl: TpslKind, limit_px: Option<FixedPoint> }` (or add `tpsl: Option<TpslKind>` to StopMarket/StopLimit) and add `grouping: OrderGrouping` to PlaceOrderParams; add NativeAction::PlaceOrderGroup(Vec<PlaceOrderParams>) for parent+children under one signature (reuse PlaceOrderBatch plumbing at native_executor.rs:3222/3514). 2) torus-core/src/order_book.rs: extend StopOrder with `tpsl: Option<TpslKind>`, `grouping`, `parent: Option<OrderId>`; bump stop-row encoding (new leading version byte; restore_stop_row accepts old layout) at 2382-2415/1402; add `dormant_stops: Vec<StopOrder>`; refactor trigger_stops(&mut self) into trigger_stops_at(price_source: FixedPoint) and add `pub fn trigger_tpsl(&mut self, mark_px)` that fires only tpsl-flagged stops by mark px (non-tpsl stops keep last-trade semantics); add `activate_children(parent: OrderId)`, `cancel_children(parent)`, `resize_position_tpsl(trader, new_size)`; tpsl stops always reduce_only=true. 3) native_executor.rs: in the per-block phase sequence (execute_batch_phases 3469; next to aggregate_oracle_prices/run_liquidation_checks 5904/5923) add `sweep_tpsl_triggers(ctx, oracle_prices)` iterating ctx books and calling trigger_tpsl(mark_px) BEFORE liquidation checks, routing resulting fills through the normal settle path; in settle (apply_fill_via_caches 4713 / settle_market_results_sequential 4081 & parallel 4328) after FillEffect: call book.activate_children(order_id) when parent fully filled, and book.resize_position_tpsl(trader, new_pos_size) (cancel when size==0); in exec cancel paths (3244) call cancel_children. 4) RPC: expose tpsl/grouping in order submission and in openOrders/frontendOpenOrders rows. Tests: order_book.rs unit tests (mark px triggers idle book; last-trade wick does not trigger tpsl stop; child dormant until parent fill; child cancelled with parent; positionTpsl resizes on partial close and cancels on flat; stop-row roundtrip old+new layout); executor integration test with oracle submission -> sweep -> fill.

**Unsure:** Did not read execute_batch_phases (native_executor.rs:3469) to confirm where/if aggregate_oracle_prices and run_liquidation_checks are actually invoked per block — my grep (excluding lines with 'fn ' or 'test') found no callers, suggesting the per-block oracle/liquidation sweep itself may be unwired, which would make the TP/SL sweep hook also need wiring. Did not read the RPC crate for open-orders response shape. Did not verify whether a separate mark-price (vs oracle price) computation exists; margin.rs:234 takes mark_price as a parameter, suggesting oracle price is used as mark today. Parallel settle (settle_market_results_parallel) may need the child-activation/resize bookkeeping done market-locally to preserve determinism — not verified.

</details>

### design-twap

**opus** — absent, impact medium, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~650 prod + ~300 tests (types 60, state CF 30, twap.rs 250, executor arms+scheduler 230, rpc 60, app wiring 20)

TWAP is absent. A case-insensitive grep for "twap" across crates/ returns nothing. NativeAction (torus-types/src/lib.rs:580) only has PlaceOrder, PlaceOrderBatch, CancelOrder, CancelAllOrders and ModifyOrder for orders, and OrderType (lib.rs:1072) only has Limit, Market, StopMarket and StopLimit. The proposed design follows Hyperliquid. Add a `TwapOrder` action (market, side, total size, duration in minutes, reduce_only, randomize) and a `TwapCancel` action. Store each parent as a `TwapState` row in its own CF. Each block, a deterministic `NativeExecutor::process_twaps(&mut ctx)` hook runs in the post-engine tail in app.rs (around lines 1937-1940), after execute_batch and before process_epoch_boundary. It sends each due slice through exec_place_order as an IOC market order, capped at 3% slippage from the oracle price. Hyperliquid works the same way: one slice every 30 seconds, catch-up is limited to 3x the normal slice size, and slices count as taker orders.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-597 NativeAction order variants: PlaceOrder, PlaceOrderBatch, CancelOrder{order_id}, CancelAllOrders, ModifyOrder. No TWAP.
- torus-types/src/lib.rs:1060-1082 PlaceOrderParams {market_id,is_buy,price,quantity,order_type,time_in_force,reduce_only,client_order_id}; OrderType = Limit\|Market\|StopMarket\|StopLimit
- torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1902-1903 NativeExecutor::execute_batch(&mut ctx,&pre_evm) then post_evm
- torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1909-1921 fatal_error fail-stop latch after batch (TWAP hook must sit after this check)
- torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1937-1940 post-engine tail: drain_core_writer, process_governance, distribute_fees, process_epoch_boundary. This is where the per-block TWAP scheduler goes.
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3210-3336 execute_action match on NativeAction (add TwapOrder/TwapCancel arms here)
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3469-3600 execute_batch_phases flattens Place/PlaceOrderBatch into FlatAction. TWAP actions go to FlatAction::Other (sequential path).
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4906-4935 exec_place_order(ctx,sender,&PlaceOrderParams): market orders skip the margin reserve and settle at fill. TWAP slices can reuse it.
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6025-6030 process_epoch_boundary(ctx) uses the block_height gate pattern; process_twaps should follow it
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5922-5945 run_liquidation_checks is an existing per-market sweep over ctx state
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:2985-3000 diff_stop_rows persists stops as rows keyed by market_id\|\|ROW_TAG_STOP\|\|order_id in CF_NATIVE_ORDER_BOOKS. This is the template for TWAP parent rows.
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1272-1290 trigger_stops keeps in-book pending state, which shows how conditional/parent orders are held today

**Risk:** Without TWAP there is no Hyperliquid parity for large-order execution. Users cannot split big orders, and anything outside the chain that tries to do this is not deterministic and pays a signature and nonce for every slice. Getting it wrong is a consensus risk: the scheduler has to be fully deterministic. It must iterate in a fixed order (BTreeMap by twap_id, not HashMap), compute time from block height or the block timestamp (never wall clock), and use deterministic randomization seeded from the block hash and twap_id. Otherwise validators will diverge on state roots.

**Fix:** 1) torus-types/src/lib.rs. Add `NativeAction::TwapOrder(TwapParams{market_id,is_buy,total_qty:FixedPoint,duration_mins:u32 (5..=1440),reduce_only,randomize:bool})` and `NativeAction::TwapCancel{twap_id:u64}`. Add a `TwapState{id,owner,params,start_height,start_ts,executed_qty,executed_notional,next_slice_height,status: Active|Finished|Canceled|Error(String)}`. Bump the action encoding version (~60 LOC).
2) torus-state. Add a new CF, CF_NATIVE_TWAPS, keyed by twap_id (u64 BE) plus a per-owner index prefix (~30 LOC).
3) crates/torus-bridge/src/twap.rs, a new module (~250 LOC). It holds `TwapBook{active: BTreeMap<u64,TwapState>, next_id}` loaded from and saved to the CF. Following the diff_stop_rows pattern, it writes only changed rows and deletes finished ones. Add `ctx.twaps: TwapBook` to NativeExecContext (native_executor.rs:1339).
4) native_executor.rs execute_action (around line 3332). Two arms (~80 LOC):
- exec_twap_order checks min/max duration, the market exists, a per-user cap on active TWAPs, and a minimum notional per slice. It then inserts the TwapState. It reserves no margin; that is checked per slice, as Hyperliquid does.
- exec_twap_cancel checks the owner and marks the TWAP Canceled. Slices that already filled are kept.
In execute_batch_phases (around line 3513), make sure both arms route to FlatAction::Other.
5) native_executor.rs, new `pub fn process_twaps(ctx)` (~150 LOC). It iterates over active TWAPs in id order. For each TWAP whose next_slice_height <= height (slice interval = 30s divided by block time, as a height delta):
- target = total * elapsed / duration; slice = min(target - executed, 3 * nominal_slice).
- Optional randomization: ±20% seeded from keccak(block_hash, id).
- Build a PlaceOrderParams with OrderType::Market and an IOC time-in-force. The price limit is oracle * (1 ± 3%), from ctx.oracle; this is the slippage cap.
- Call exec_place_order(ctx, &owner, &p). Read back the fill qty and notional from the result or the pending fills.
- An unfilled remainder is carried into the next catch-up. On a margin error, mark the TWAP Error; a reduce_only TWAP whose position has closed is marked Finished. When elapsed >= duration, mark it Finished.
6) app.rs, around line 1937. Call `NativeExecutor::process_twaps(&mut ctx);` after drain_core_writer and before distribute_fees, so slice fees go into the block's fee revenue. Mirror the same call in the replay and sync exec path (app.rs:12926 area) so state roots match.
7) torus-rpc. Add read endpoints twapStates(user) and twapSliceFills(user) (~60 LOC).
Tests (~300 LOC):
- A slice schedule sums exactly to the total.
- Catch-up is capped at 3x.
- A slice priced past the 3% band does not fill, and the remainder rolls forward.
- After a cancel no further slices are placed, and earlier fills are kept.
- Two executors replaying the same blocks reach an identical state root.
- A reduce_only TWAP finishes when the position closes.
- Restart persistence: load and save round-trip in the middle of a TWAP.

**Unsure:** I did not check:
- Whether TimeInForce has an IOC variant (I did not read its enum).
- How exec_place_order reports filled qty and notional back to a caller. Fills may only be visible through ctx pending_trade_fills.
- Where the block timestamp or block hash is available on NativeExecContext. Deterministic time and the seed depend on this.
- The exact replay/sync exec path near app.rs:12926. I only saw its execute_batch call, not whether it runs the same post-engine tail.
- The resident-book or level-authority save modes (BookMode), which might need TWAP rows folded into the deferred save, DeferredBookSave.
- That the Hyperliquid parameters are current as of today: 30s slices, 3% max slippage, 3x catch-up, 5 min to 24 h duration.

</details>

**fable** — absent, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~500-600 LOC (types 25, torus-core twap.rs 150, native_executor 240, app.rs 5, rpc/precompile 80) + ~200 LOC tests

No TWAP exists anywhere (grep -i twap over crates/ returns nothing). The only time/price-conditional order machinery is the per-book `pending_stops: Vec<StopOrder>` in torus-core/src/order_book.rs, which fires from `trigger_stops()` on last-trade-price, is persisted inside the book blob (`stop_count` + per-stop serialize) and as borsh rows via `stop_rows()`, and is cancelled only via trader-wide `retain`. The end-of-block tail in torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1937-1940 is `drain_core_writer -> process_governance -> distribute_fees -> process_epoch_boundary`, then `save_order_books[_deferred]` at app.rs:1995-2000; there is no per-block scheduler hook. Proposed design: a market-independent `TwapParent` store on `NativeExecContext`, two new `NativeAction` variants (`PlaceTwap`, `CancelTwap`), and a `NativeExecutor::run_twap_slices(ctx)` phase inserted after the two `execute_batch` calls and before `drain_core_writer`, emitting IOC child orders through the existing `exec_place_order` funnel with a per-slice slippage-capped limit price.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1060-1094: PlaceOrderParams{market_id,is_buy,price,quantity,order_type,time_in_force,reduce_only,client_order_id}; OrderType {Limit,Market,StopMarket{trigger},StopLimit{trigger,limit}}; TimeInForce {GTC,IOC,FOK,PostOnly} — no TWAP variant
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-598: NativeAction has PlaceOrder, PlaceOrderBatch, CancelOrder{order_id}, CancelAllOrders{market_id}, ModifyOrder — insertion point for PlaceTwap/CancelTwap
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:93-106: struct StopOrder{id,trader,market_id,side,trigger_price,limit_price,quantity,time_in_force,timestamp,reduce_only,client_order_id} — template for TwapParent
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:251 pending_stops: Vec<StopOrder>; 1272-1300 trigger_stops() loops up to 10 rounds on last_trade_price; 651/695 cancel via retain(trader)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1370-1385 stop_rows() borsh rows, id-ascending invariant; 2535-2540 stop_count + stop.serialize in book blob
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:798/803/877: best_bid(), best_ask(), last_trade_price() — inputs for the slippage cap
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1339-1372: NativeExecContext{positions,oracle,...,order_books,dirty_books,next_global_order_id,block_height,timestamp,epoch,...}
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3181-3188 execute() -> execute_action; 3217 PlaceOrder -> exec_place_order (defined 4906); 3244-3254 CancelOrder/CancelAllOrders/ModifyOrder dispatch
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5923 run_liquidation_checks, 5991 distribute_fees, 6025 process_epoch_boundary, 6107 process_governance, 6176 classify_action — existing per-block phases
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1902-1903 execute_batch(pre_evm)/execute_batch(post_evm); 1937-1940 tail: drain_core_writer, process_governance, distribute_fees, process_epoch_boundary; 1995-2000 save_order_books[_deferred]

**Risk:** Hyperliquid exposes TWAP as a first-class order (30s slices, 3% slippage cap per slice, cancelable, visible in frontend/API). Without it, parity-dependent clients, market-makers and the RPC order-type surface diverge; any off-chain TWAP bot built on PlaceOrder IOC loses determinism and atomic cancel semantics. Implementing it as a consensus-side scheduler is the only way it affects state-root deterministically across validators.

**Fix:** 1) torus-types/src/lib.rs: add `NativeAction::PlaceTwap(TwapParams)` and `NativeAction::CancelTwap{twap_id: u64}` next to PlaceOrder (~line 582); `pub struct TwapParams{market_id,is_buy,total_qty:FixedPoint,duration_secs:u64,reduce_only:bool,randomize:bool,client_order_id:Option<u64>}` (~25 LOC). 2) New crates/torus-core/src/twap.rs: `#[derive(BorshSerialize,BorshDeserialize)] pub struct TwapParent{id:u64,trader:Address,market_id,side,total_qty,filled_qty,slice_qty,interval_secs(=30),next_fire_ts:u64,end_ts:u64,created_block:u64,reduce_only,client_order_id,status:TwapStatus{Active,Done,Cancelled}}`; `pub struct TwapBook{parents: BTreeMap<u64,TwapParent>, next_id:u64}` with `place()`, `cancel(trader,id)`, `due(now)->Vec<&mut TwapParent>`, `rows()` mirroring `stop_rows()` (~150 LOC). 3) native_executor.rs: add `pub twaps: TwapBook` + `twaps_dirty: bool` to NativeExecContext (line ~1347); load/save in `new*`/`save_order_books` using a new CF key `twap/{id}` (same pattern as the stop rows, ~80 LOC); in `execute_action` add arms `PlaceTwap => exec_place_twap` (margin check via ctx.positions for total notional, lock slot) and `CancelTwap => exec_cancel_twap` (~70 LOC); add `pub fn run_twap_slices<T>(ctx)` (~90 LOC): for each parent with `next_fire_ts <= ctx.timestamp`, compute `qty = min(slice_qty, remaining)`, reference = `book.best_ask()/best_bid()` fallback `last_trade_price()`/oracle, limit = ref*(1±0.03) (slippage cap, HL = 3%), then call `exec_place_order(ctx, &parent.trader, &PlaceOrderParams{order_type:Limit, time_in_force:IOC, price:limit, quantity:qty, ...})`; advance `filled_qty` by the IOC result, `next_fire_ts += interval`, mark Done at `end_ts` or filled; mark `dirty_books` for the market. 4) app.rs:1903: insert `NativeExecutor::run_twap_slices(&mut ctx);` after the post_evm execute_batch and before `drain_core_writer` so slice fills go through the same pending_fills/trade-history path; keep it ahead of fee distribution. 5) classify_action (6176) + sort_native_actions: treat PlaceTwap as Place-class, CancelTwap as Cancel-class. 6) RPC (torus-rpc) + precompiles.rs:800 OrderType decode: expose `placeTwap`/`cancelTwap` + `twapState` query (~80 LOC). Tests: torus-core twap unit tests (slice math, due(), cancel), native_executor test: two blocks 30s apart produce one IOC child each, slippage-capped limit rejects when book is empty (no fill, parent stays Active), cancel removes parent and subsequent blocks produce no children, state-root determinism across two executors.

**Unsure:** Did not read exec_place_order (native_executor.rs:4906+) internals, so whether it can be called re-entrantly from a block-tail phase with the resident/market-worker book modes (execute_batch_engine_mode, 3406) without violating the market-worker ownership model is unverified; slice placement may need to go through the same batch funnel (FlatAction::Place at 3513) rather than a direct call. Did not confirm where book load/save CF keys are defined (book_rows.rs) for the parent persistence pattern. Hyperliquid's exact slice interval (30s) and 3% cap are from memory, not re-verified.

### design-cloid

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~900-1300 LOC: types+canonical bytes ~150, eip712 ~200, order_book index+persistence ~200, executor dispatch+batchModify ~200, RPC ~100, tests ~400

Today only an optional, non-unique `client_order_id: Option<u64>` exists. It is carried on PlaceOrderParams and Order, and it is persisted and EIP-712-hashed as uint64 plus a hasClientOrderId flag. Nothing indexes it: OrderBook has `order_index` (OrderId) and `trader_orders` (Address -> Vec<OrderId>) but no (trader, cloid) map. There is no cancelByCloid, modify-by-cloid, batchModify or expiresAfter. Expiry is only the fixed ±60s nonce window in eip712.rs. Proposed design: widen cloid to `Option<u128>` (Hyperliquid's 16-byte cloid); add an `OrderBook.cloid_index: HashMap<(Address, u128), OrderId>` that rejects a duplicate live cloid per trader; add the `OrderRef { Oid(OrderId), Cloid(u128) }` enum used by new `CancelByCloid` / `ModifyOrder{target: OrderRef, ...}` / `BatchModify(Vec<ModifyItem>)` variants; add `expires_after: Option<u64>` to `SignedNativeAction`, bound into every typehash, and check it against block time.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1060-1069 PlaceOrderParams has `client_order_id: Option<u64>` (u64, not 128-bit)

- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:240-272 OrderBook indexes: order_index HashMap<OrderId,OrderLocation>, trader_orders HashMap<Address,Vec<OrderId>>, order_seq; no cloid index

- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-598 NativeAction: PlaceOrder, PlaceOrderBatch, CancelOrder{order_id}, CancelAllOrders, ModifyOrder{order_id,new_price,new_qty}; no cloid/batch-modify variants

- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:859-865,886-891 only expiry mechanism is NONCE_WINDOW_MS ±60s check
- grep: crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3244/3250 dispatch CancelOrder/ModifyOrder; :6178/:6192 ActionCategory mapping; crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:1111 QueuedActionKind::CancelOrder (EVM precompile path, lines not read)

**Risk:** Market makers on Hyperliquid key everything off cloid. They place with a cloid and then cancel or modify by cloid without waiting for the oid round trip. They use batchModify for requotes and expiresAfter so a stale action cannot land late. Without these, Torus MM clients need an oid round trip before cancelling, and requotes cost N signed actions instead of 1. A delayed action can still land anywhere in the 60s window. A duplicate cloid on Torus is silently accepted today, so any future cloid lookup would be ambiguous. Every proposed change alters the canonical serialization, compute_action_hash preimage, persisted order rows and EIP-712 typehashes. That makes it a fresh-genesis consensus break, and signing SDKs and wallets must update together.

**Fix:** 1) torus-types/src/lib.rs: change `client_order_id: Option<u64>` to `Option<u128>` in PlaceOrderParams. Add `pub enum OrderRef { Oid(OrderId), Cloid(u128) }`. Add NativeAction variants `CancelByCloid { market_id: MarketId, cloid: u128 }`, change `ModifyOrder { target: OrderRef, new_price, new_qty }` (or add `ModifyByCloid`), and add `BatchModify(Vec<ModifyItem{target: OrderRef, new_price, new_qty}>)`, capped by a `batch_len_within_cap` analogue. Add `#[serde(default)] expires_after: Option<u64>` to SignedNativeAction. Update `append_canonical_bytes` (~:726) and `compute_action_hash_with_scratch` (:984) to tag-encode it. 2) torus-types/src/eip712.rs: in typehash strings use `uint128 cloid,bool hasCloid` (encode_u128 already exists at :107). Add `CancelByCloid(uint64 marketId,uint128 cloid,uint64 nonce)`, `ModifyItem(uint8 refKind,uint128 ref,int128 newPrice,bool hasPrice,int128 newQty,bool hasQty)`, and `BatchModify(bytes32 itemsHash,uint64 count,uint64 nonce)` using the same fold as hash_place_order_batch. For expiresAfter, the clean option is to append `uint64 expiresAfter` to every top-level typehash, or to wrap the struct hash as `Expiring(bytes32 inner,uint64 expiresAfter)` when it is Some, so that existing typehashes stay stable for the None case. Hyperliquid instead hashes it into the action msgpack. Add a check in validate/validate_with_sessions (:859, :886): `if let Some(e)=expires_after { if current_time_ms > e { Err(Expired) } }`. The deterministic check must also run at exec time in app.rs against block time, not the local clock. 3) torus-core/src/order_book.rs: add `cloid_index: HashMap<(Address,u128),OrderId>` to OrderBook (:240). Insert it in the insert path near :449/:485/:536 and reject an already-live cloid with a new CoreError::DuplicateCloid. Remove it on every exit path: cancel_order :590, cancel-all :645, fills/STP removal :1049-1135, stop triggers :1315. Add `pub fn resolve_cloid(&self, trader, cloid) -> Option<OrderId>`. Persistence :2280/:2358/:2476 changes from u64 to u128. The index is derived state, so rebuild it on reload instead of persisting it. 4) torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs: in the dispatch at :3244/:3250, resolve OrderRef to an OrderId through market book.resolve_cloid(sender, cloid), checking that the sender owns the order, then reuse the existing cancel/modify code. For BatchModify, loop the items with per-item status, following how PlaceOrderBatch is flattened. Update the ActionCategory mapping at :6178/:6192 and the precompiles.rs QueuedActionKind (:844, :1111, :1174, :1235) if EVM parity is wanted. 5) RPC (torus-rpc): accept a 0x-hex 16-byte cloid and expose an `orderStatus` lookup by cloid. Tests: duplicate-cloid rejection; cloid freed after fill or cancel and reusable; cancel/modify by a cloid from another trader fails; batchModify mixing oid and cloid; expired action rejected at admission and at exec; EIP-712 golden vectors for the new typehashes; cloid_index rebuilt after reload equals the live one (state-root determinism).

**Unsure:** I did not read the executor dispatch bodies at native_executor.rs:3244-3300, the precompiles.rs paths, append_canonical_bytes, or torus-rpc, so their exact edit shapes are inferred. I did not check whether modify_order's cancel+reinsert path (same id) would also need the cloid index refreshed; it probably does not if the id is kept. I also did not check whether order history or the explorer indexer (torus-explorer indexer.rs:311) stores cloids. Another choice is open: bind expiresAfter into every typehash (simpler, but it changes every action's hash) or use an optional wrapper typehash (keeps None-case vectors stable). Hyperliquid binds it into the msgpack action hash and treats an expired action as a nonce-consuming failure, and how Torus should handle nonce consumption for expired actions was not examined.

</details>

**fable** — design, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~600-800 LOC: torus-types ~120 (enum/struct/OrderRef), eip712.rs ~150 (new typehashes + expires_after threading), order_book.rs ~150 (cloid_index + serialization + cancel/modify-by-cloid), native_executor.rs ~150 (3 handlers + expiry check + sender on modify), mempool ~20, rpc ~60, tests ~200

Current state: cloid is `client_order_id: Option<u64>` on both `PlaceOrderParams` (torus-types/src/lib.rs) and `Order` (torus-core/src/order_book.rs:47), serialized as a 1-byte tag + 8 bytes (order_book.rs:2280-2286), and hashed into EIP-712 as `uint64 clientOrderId,bool hasClientOrderId` (eip712.rs:269-275). There is no per-trader (trader, cloid) index in `OrderBook` (only `order_index: HashMap<OrderId,_>` and `trader_orders: HashMap<Address,Vec<OrderId>>`, order_book.rs:247-249), so no uniqueness enforcement and no cancel/modify-by-cloid. `NativeAction` (lib.rs:580) has `CancelOrder{order_id}`, `CancelAllOrders`, `ModifyOrder{order_id,new_price,new_qty}` and `PlaceOrderBatch` but no `CancelByCloid`, `BatchModify`, or `expires_after`; `SignedNativeAction` (lib.rs:951) carries only `action`, `nonce`, `signature`, and replay protection is the 60s nonce drift window (eip712.rs:26). Proposed design: widen cloid to `Option<u128>` (HL's 16-byte hex cloid), add `cloid_index: HashMap<(Address,u128),OrderId>` to `OrderBook` maintained on place/cancel/fill-removal and rejecting duplicate live cloids per trader, add `OrderRef { Oid(OrderId) | Cloid(u128) }` used by new `CancelByCloid{market_id,cloid}`, `ModifyOrder{order: OrderRef,...}` and `BatchModify(Vec<ModifyItem>)` actions, and add `expires_after: Option<u64>` to `SignedNativeAction` checked at mempool admission and in the executor (`block_time_ms > expires_after` => reject, deterministic).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:47 — `pub client_order_id: Option<u64>` on Order
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:243-249 — book has bids/asks BTreeMap, order_index HashMap<OrderId,OrderLocation>, trader_orders HashMap<Address,Vec<OrderId>>; no cloid index
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:2280-2286 — Option<u64> cloid written as tag byte + 8 BE bytes (snapshot/serialization format; also 2358, 2408, 2476 read/write paths)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:702-708 — `modify_order(order_id, new_price, new_qty)` keyed by OrderId only
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-599 — NativeAction has PlaceOrder, PlaceOrderBatch(Vec<PlaceOrderParams>), CancelOrder{order_id}, CancelAllOrders{market_id}, ModifyOrder{order_id,new_price,new_qty}; no cloid variants, no BatchModify
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:951-957 — SignedNativeAction { action, nonce, signature }; no expires_after
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:269-275 — PlaceOrder typehash string includes `uint64 clientOrderId,bool hasClientOrderId,uint64 nonce`
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:195-240 — eip712_struct_hash dispatch per NativeAction variant (nonce threaded into every struct); 324 hash_cancel_order, 344 hash_modify_order, 303 hash_place_order_batch
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:26 — 60s nonce drift window is the only time-bound on actions
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3244-3254 — dispatch: CancelOrder -> exec_cancel_order(ctx, sender, id); ModifyOrder -> exec_modify_order(ctx, order_id, price, qty) with NO sender argument
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5359-5368 — exec_modify_order iterates every book and calls book.modify_order on the first that owns order_id; no trader ownership check visible in the first 30 lines
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1916 — RPC exposes client_order_id via hex_u64

**Risk:** HL SDKs and market-maker bots generate 128-bit cloids (16-byte hex) and rely on cancelByCloid / modify-by-cloid / batchModify to avoid oid round-trips; a u64 cloid with no uniqueness and no cloid-keyed actions means the HL exchange API surface cannot be mapped 1:1 and bots cannot dedupe retries. Lack of expiresAfter means a delayed signed action is valid for the full 60s nonce window with no tighter client-chosen bound. Changing the EIP-712 PlaceOrder typehash is a consensus/signature-breaking change for every existing signer (SDK, session keys, tests), so it must ship with a domain or version bump. Side observation: exec_modify_order does not receive `sender`, so unless an ownership check exists deeper in the function, any signer can modify any order id — worth verifying independently.

**Fix:** 1) torus-types/src/lib.rs: change `PlaceOrderParams.client_order_id: Option<u64>` -> `Option<u128>`; add `pub enum OrderRef { Oid(OrderId), Cloid(u128) }`; add variants `CancelByCloid { market_id: MarketId, cloid: u128 }`, `CancelOrderBatch(Vec<OrderRef>)` (optional), change `ModifyOrder { order: OrderRef, new_price, new_qty, new_cloid: Option<u128> }`, add `BatchModify(Vec<ModifyItem>)` where `ModifyItem { order: OrderRef, market_id, new_price, new_qty, new_cloid }`; add `expires_after: Option<u64>` to `SignedNativeAction`. 2) torus-core/src/order_book.rs: `Order.client_order_id: Option<u128>`; add `cloid_index: HashMap<(Address,u128),OrderId>` beside `order_index` (line 247); in place path (~449/485/536) reject `CoreError::DuplicateCloid` if `(trader,cloid)` live; remove on cancel/full-fill removal (~614); add `order_id_by_cloid(trader,cloid)->Option<OrderId>` and `cancel_by_cloid`, make `modify_order` accept `OrderRef` via resolution; bump the snapshot encoding at 2280/2358/2408/2476 to tag + 16 bytes with a format-version byte so old snapshots (8-byte) still decode. 3) torus-types/src/eip712.rs: PlaceOrder typehash -> `uint128 clientOrderId,bool hasClientOrderId` (append_place_order_fields line 251 uses encode_u128 at 107); new typehashes `CancelByCloid(uint64 marketId,uint128 cloid,uint64 nonce,uint64 expiresAfter)`, `ModifyOrder(uint8 refKind,uint128 ref,int128 newPrice,bool hasNewPrice,int128 newQty,bool hasNewQty,uint128 newCloid,bool hasNewCloid,uint64 nonce,uint64 expiresAfter)`, `BatchModify(bytes32 itemsHash,uint64 nonce,uint64 expiresAfter)` mirroring hash_place_order_batch (303); thread `expires_after` into `eip712_struct_hash(action, nonce, expires_after)` (195) with 0 = none; bump EIP712 domain `version` (163). 4) torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs: dispatch new variants at 3244-3254; `exec_cancel_by_cloid(ctx, sender, market_id, cloid)` resolves via `ctx.order_books[market_id].order_id_by_cloid(sender, cloid)` then reuses exec_cancel_order (5162); make exec_modify_order take `sender` and resolve OrderRef, reject if `order.trader != sender`; `exec_batch_modify` loops items with per-item results (same cap pattern as PlaceOrderBatch at 3485-3549); in the Phase-1 loop (3559) reject when `ctx.block_timestamp_ms > expires_after`. 5) torus-mempool/src/native_pool.rs: drop actions whose expires_after < now at admission. 6) torus-rpc/src/torus.rs: `order_to_rpc` 1916 -> hex_u128 cloid; add exchange endpoints for cancelByCloid/modify/batchModify. Tests: order_book.rs unit tests (duplicate cloid rejected, cloid freed after cancel and after full fill, modify-by-cloid keeps priority on qty decrease), eip712 typehash golden vectors, native_executor tests for cross-trader cloid cancel rejection and expired action rejection, snapshot round-trip for the widened cloid.

**Unsure:** Did not read the full exec_modify_order body (only 5359-5389) so cannot confirm whether an ownership check exists further down; did not read hash_modify_order (344) or hash_cancel_order (324) bodies, the mempool nonce-check site, or the snapshot format-version handling at 2358/2476 to confirm whether a version byte already exists. The `idx` command printed nothing (indexer not available in this shell), so file discovery was via grep.

### design-isolated

**opus** — unwired, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~700-1000 LOC: types and encoding ~120, core position/margin ~250, liquidation ~80, executor wiring and caches ~250, RPC ~80, tests ~300

torus-core already has the data model and the math: `MarginType {Cross, Isolated}` plus `Position.isolated_margin` (borsh v1), an isolated branch in `check_initial_margin`, `check_isolated_maintenance`, and per-position isolated liquidation. None of it can be reached. Every executor fill path hard-codes `MarginType::Cross`. `fill_transition` always opens positions with `isolated_margin = 0`. Margin is reserved at the tier max leverage, never at a leverage the user picks. `NativeAction`, `PlaceOrderParams` and the dispatch in `execute_action` have no `UpdateLeverage` or `UpdateIsolatedMargin`. Proposed design: add a per-(trader, market) `LeverageSetting {margin_type, leverage}` row in `PositionManager`; add the two new actions; on fills, read the setting and move initial margin from `order_margin` into `Position.isolated_margin`; cap isolated liquidation losses at `isolated_margin` so they never draw on the cross balance.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- torus-core/src/position.rs:45-62 MarginType enum and Position {isolated_margin, margin_type} already exist
- torus-core/src/position.rs:84-140 Position borsh v1 already serializes isolated_margin and the margin_type byte, so no Position schema bump is needed
- torus-core/src/position.rs:434-517 fill_transition: open and flip set isolated_margin = 0; increase and partial close never change isolated_margin; full close returns None, so isolated margin is never returned to the balance
- torus-core/src/margin.rs:93-145 check_initial_margin accepts leverage and margin_type; the Isolated branch only checks bal.available >= notional/leverage and does not lock anything
- torus-core/src/margin.rs:186-218 cross_margin_equity and total_maintenance_margin already skip non-Cross positions, which is correct isolation
- torus-core/src/margin.rs:232-249 check_isolated_maintenance: equity = isolated_margin + uPnL against maintenance at the tier max leverage
- torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:86-108 check_liquidations groups cross positions and checks each isolated position on its own
- torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:220-240 execute_liquidation: for an isolated position, bal.available += pnl - penalty + isolated_margin and the deficit is floored against the whole available balance, so an isolated loss eats cross collateral (not isolated)
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4663, 4730, 5048, 5068 every apply_fill / apply_fill_cached_effect call passes MarginType::Cross
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4784-4818 reserve_for_qty_cfg reserves notional / effective_max_leverage (default 20), with no user leverage
- torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-680 NativeAction has no leverage or margin actions; lib.rs:1060-1069 PlaceOrderParams has no leverage or margin_type field
- native_executor.rs:3210-3340 execute_action match: the new variants would go here (the Phase 1 non-place loop)
- native_executor.rs:5938-5965 the liquidation loop runs check_liquidations for each market config over all of a trader's positions, then executes each liquidation at the loop market's oracle_price, even when liq.market_id is a different market

**Risk:** Without this, the chain cannot match Hyperliquid's `updateLeverage` (asset, isCross, leverage) or `updateIsolatedMargin` (asset, isBuy, ntli). Every user is cross at the tier max leverage. If someone naively flips the margin_type passed at the fill sites to Isolated today, every new isolated position opens with `isolated_margin = 0`. It then fails maintenance and is liquidated in the next block. When it is liquidated, its loss is drawn from the shared available balance, so isolation does not exist. A separate latent bug: the per-market liquidation loop can liquidate a position at another market's price.

**Fix:** 1) torus-types/src/lib.rs: add `NativeAction::UpdateLeverage { market_id, is_cross: bool, leverage: u32 }` and `NativeAction::UpdateIsolatedMargin { market_id, delta: FixedPoint /* signed */ }`. Add canonical encodings for both, with new variant tags appended after DelistMarket. Update the signing encoding, the RPC/JSON parsers, and session-key `SessionScope` (both actions count as trading).
2) torus-core/src/position.rs: add a `LeverageSetting { margin_type, leverage: u32 }` state row keyed (trader, market_id), with `get_leverage_setting` (default Cross at tier max) and `put_leverage_setting`. Add `fn add_isolated_margin(&self, cache, trader, market, delta)`: it moves funds between `NativeBalance.available` and `Position.isolated_margin`. A withdrawal must keep isolated_margin + uPnL >= the initial margin at the current leverage, as on Hyperliquid. Change `fill_transition` to take a `margin_delta: FixedPoint`. Open and increase add the newly required initial margin (notional / user leverage). A partial close releases a pro-rata share. A full close or flip returns `Some(isolated_margin)` alongside the PnL event so the caller credits it back.
3) torus-core/src/margin.rs: add a `user_leverage: u32` parameter to `check_isolated_maintenance` and `check_initial_margin` (maintenance stays tier-based). Add `validate_leverage_change`. It rejects leverage above `effective_max_leverage`. It rejects a switch from cross to isolated (or back) while a position or open orders exist in that market. It allows lowering an isolated position's leverage only if free margin covers the higher initial margin; Hyperliquid also allows raising it.
4) torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs: handle both actions in `execute_action` (Phase 1, ~3210), via new `exec_update_leverage` and `exec_update_isolated_margin`. Change `reserve_for_qty`/`reserve_for_qty_cfg` to take the user's leverage instead of max_lev. This keeps the release telescoping exact, as long as the setting is frozen while orders rest; the action enforces that by rejecting changes when the trader has open orders in the market. At the four fill sites (4663, 4730, 5048, 5068), look up the trader's setting (cache it per batch next to PositionCache) and pass its margin_type. For isolated fills, convert the released `order_margin` into `isolated_margin` instead of returning it to `available`.
5) torus-core/src/liquidation.rs `execute_liquidation`: for an isolated position, compute residual = isolated_margin + pnl - penalty. If the residual is positive, credit it to available. If it is negative, it becomes `remaining_deficit` (insurance fund or ADL) and must never touch `bal.available`. Fix the executor loop at native_executor.rs:5938-5965: filter `liquidations` to `liq.market_id == *market_id`, or look up each liquidation's own oracle price, and do cross checks once per trader rather than once per market.
6) Tests: open an isolated position, check its isolated_margin is about notional/lev and the balance went down by the same amount; an isolated liquidation must leave cross positions and the available balance untouched; add margin then remove it, with the remove blocked below initial; changing leverage with open orders is rejected; a full close returns the margin; borsh round-trip of LeverageSetting; a determinism test of the batch path versus the serial path.

**Unsure:** I did not open: the exec_place_order margin reserve body (~4909-5000) and how order_margin is released to available on fills; the batch Phase-4 settle code at 4180/4656, to confirm the place to inject per-trader settings; the RPC action JSON parser and SessionScope; the auto_deleverage internals; the state-key layout for new rows (how get_position keys are built); and whether a migration or hard fork is needed for the new NativeAction tags (encoding at torus-types lib.rs:~682+). Hyperliquid's exact rules for changing leverage are from memory, not checked against its docs. The cross-market liquidation price issue comes from reading 5938-5965 and liquidation.rs:86-108 together; I have not confirmed it with a test.

</details>

**fable** — design, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~650-800 LOC: types 20, position.rs setting + fill accounting 120, executor handlers 150 + call-site/order-row threading 90, liquidation clamp 25, rpc 50, tests 250

The data model and the risk math already exist in torus-core but nothing upstream of it ever selects Isolated: Position carries margin_type + isolated_margin (position.rs:60-61, borsh at :95-96), MarginEngine::check_initial_margin branches on MarginType and takes a user leverage (margin.rs:90-145), and LiquidationEngine already splits cross-vs-isolated checks and uses pos.isolated_margin for isolated equity (liquidation.rs:87-108, :170-190). However the executor hardcodes MarginType::Cross at every apply_fill call site (native_executor.rs:4663, 4730, 5048, 5068), reserves order margin at the tier max leverage rather than a user-chosen leverage (reserve_for_qty_cfg :4807-4817, cancel release :5187-5193), fill_transition always writes isolated_margin = ZERO (position.rs:453), and NativeAction (torus-types/src/lib.rs:580) has no UpdateLeverage/UpdateIsolatedMargin variants and PlaceOrderParams (:1060) carries no leverage. Proposed design: a per-(trader,market) LeverageSetting {leverage, margin_type} stored in PositionManager with default (Cross, tier max) so current behavior is byte-identical; two new NativeAction variants appended at the enum tail; reserve/release and apply_fill read the setting; isolated fills move the reserved margin into pos.isolated_margin instead of back to available; execute_liquidation clamps isolated loss at isolated_margin.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:45-61 — MarginType enum, Position.isolated_margin / margin_type fields; :95-96 borsh-serialized; :147-150 NativeBalance{available, order_margin}; :453 fill_transition always sets isolated_margin ZERO
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:90-145 — check_initial_margin(leverage, margin_type): tier cap via effective_max_leverage, Isolated checks bal.available >= notional/leverage, Cross uses equity-maint
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:87-108 — check_liquidations splits cross group vs per-position isolated; :170-190 check_isolated_liquidation equity = isolated_margin + upnl, maintenance from tier max leverage; :219-227 execute_liquidation applies pnl then adds isolated_margin back to available (loss not clamped to isolated_margin)
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-650 — NativeAction has PlaceOrder/Cancel/Modify/Transfers/Staking/Governance/Oracle/Validator; no leverage or margin action; :1060-1069 PlaceOrderParams has no leverage/margin_type
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3210-3300 — execute_action dispatch; :4663, :4730, :5048, :5068 apply_fill / apply_fill_cached_effect pass MarginType::Cross literal
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4784-4817 — reserve_for_qty_cfg: margin = notional / effective_max_leverage (cfg-only, off-thread C3 invariant); :5187-5200 cancel release recomputes same formula and moves order_margin -> available
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5930-5985 — end-of-block loop per market config: check_liquidations -> execute_liquidation -> auto_deleverage on deficit
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:792-856 — user_state already renders margin_type string, isolated_margin and liquidation price from isolated_margin

**Risk:** HL parity: Hyperliquid exposes updateLeverage{asset,isCross,leverage} and updateIsolatedMargin{asset,isBuy,ntli}; without them every Torus position is cross at tier-max leverage, so users cannot cap risk per market and the UI cannot offer the isolated toggle. Also, execute_liquidation currently lets an isolated position's loss beyond isolated_margin bleed into the trader's cross available balance (liquidation.rs:219-227), which violates the core isolated guarantee once Isolated becomes reachable.

**Fix:** 1) torus-types/src/lib.rs: append `NativeAction::UpdateLeverage { market_id, leverage: u32, is_cross: bool }` and `NativeAction::UpdateIsolatedMargin { market_id, delta: FixedPoint }` at the enum tail (keeps existing variant indices). 2) torus-core/src/position.rs: add `LeverageSetting { leverage: u32, margin_type: MarginType }` + `get_leverage_setting/put_leverage_setting` beside get_native_balance (:275), default = (Cross, u32::MAX meaning 'tier max'); extend fill_transition (:441) with an `isolated_delta: FixedPoint` in FillEffect — on open/increase under Isolated add notional/leverage to pos.isolated_margin, on reduce/close release proportional isolated_margin (+closed_pnl) to available. 3) native_executor.rs: `exec_update_leverage` — reject if lev==0 or lev > effective_max_leverage(tiers, current notional) (CoreError::MaxLeverageExceeded exists, error.rs:45); reject margin_type switch while position or resting orders exist (HL rule); if Isolated with open position and new initial margin > isolated_margin, pull the difference from available (InsufficientMargin otherwise); store setting. `exec_update_isolated_margin` — require pos.margin_type==Isolated; delta>0: available -= delta, isolated_margin += delta; delta<0: require isolated_margin+delta >= notional(mark)/leverage, move to available. Wire both in execute_action (:3210). 4) Reserve/release: add `leverage: u32` to the resting order row so reserve_for_qty_cfg (:4807) and the cancel/settle releases (:5187, C3 off-thread workers) telescope with the leverage used at placement even if the setting changes later; reserve = notional / min(setting.leverage, tier max). 5) Replace the four `MarginType::Cross` literals (:4663, :4730, :5048, :5068) with the trader's setting, and move reserved order_margin into isolated_margin per FillEffect.isolated_delta instead of to available. 6) liquidation.rs execute_liquidation (:219-227): for Isolated, `let loss = pnl.max(-pos.isolated_margin)`; credit available with isolated_margin + loss − penalty; any excess goes to remaining_deficit (insurance/ADL path already handles it). Verify check_cross_liquidation (:135-141) excludes Isolated positions from cross equity. 7) torus-rpc/src/torus.rs user_state: add `leverage` from the setting; expose the two actions through the existing NativeAction submission path. Tests: margin.rs isolated test block (:381) extend; executor tests: leverage > tier rejected, isolated fill moves order_margin into isolated_margin, isolated liquidation leaves available untouched beyond isolated_margin, update_isolated_margin removal below initial margin rejected, cross<->isolated switch rejected with open position, reserve/release telescoping after leverage change.

**Unsure:** Did not read check_cross_liquidation body (liquidation.rs:117-160) to confirm it skips Isolated positions when summing cross equity; did not read the resting Order struct or the settle-worker release path (C3) to confirm adding a leverage field is feasible without breaking the byte-identical release invariant; did not check whether NativeAction uses index-based borsh (appending variants is safe) or hash-tagged encoding; did not verify whether RPC action submission is generic over NativeAction serde or per-variant.

</details>

### design-schedule-cancel

**opus** — absent, impact medium, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: ~250 prod (types ~50, state ~50, executor ~120, app ~5, rpc ~30) + ~200 tests

No dead-man switch exists today. Nothing in crates/ matches `schedule_cancel`, `ScheduleCancel` or "dead man", and `NativeAction` (torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-670) has only CancelOrder, CancelAllOrders and ModifyOrder for order cancellation. Proposed design: add a new action `NativeAction::ScheduleCancel { time_ms: Option<u64> }`. It writes a per-account record `{deadline_ms, day_index, triggers_today}` plus a deadline index made of one key per second. At the start of each block, a sweep `NativeExecutor::sweep_scheduled_cancels(ctx)` runs `exec_cancel_all(ctx, &addr, None)` for every account whose deadline has passed. Limits match HL: the deadline must be at least now+5s, an account can trigger at most 10 times per UTC day, and `None` removes the schedule.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-670 - NativeAction enum: no ScheduleCancel; the cancel variants are CancelOrder, CancelAllOrders and ModifyOrder; the canonical encoder (encode_place_order_params at ~672) means a new variant also needs a new tag byte
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3210-3336 - the execute_action match is where `ScheduleCancel => exec_schedule_cancel(ctx, sender, time_ms)` goes
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5209-5240 - exec_cancel_all(ctx, sender, None) loops over every order book, frees margin and marks dirty_books; the sweep can reuse it unchanged
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5591-5650 - exec_create_session: ctx.timestamp is in SECONDS (multiplied by 1000 to get now_ms) and it uses the validate/limit/put_session pattern; copy this pattern for scheduleCancel
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6164-6180 - ActionCategory/classify_action: ScheduleCancel should be classified as Cancellation (category 0)
- torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1901-1903 - per-block exec calls execute_batch(pre_evm) then execute_batch(post_evm); the sweep hook goes just before these, while the ctx is live
- torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1904-1921 - the fatal_error fail-stop check runs after the batches, so the sweep must not panic
- torus-state/src/db.rs:681-731 - sessions are kept as serde_json in cf_sessions; count_sessions_for_owner does a raw full rocksdb iterator scan (it skips any overlay), which the deadline index should NOT copy
- torus-state/src/cf.rs:124,196 - CF_SESSIONS constant plus registration in ALL_CF_NAMES; this shows how to add a new CF

**Risk:** Without a dead-man switch, a market maker whose client or connection dies keeps orders resting with nothing to cancel them, which is a real gap against HL's scheduleCancel. Design risks: (1) Determinism. The sweep must read state only through the StateBackend overlay. A full-CF iterator like count_sessions_for_owner reads the base DB and can differ from the overlay (uncommitted puts in the same block), so the index must be keyed for point lookups. (2) Units. Block time is in seconds and HL takes ms, so a deadline fires on the first block whose ts*1000 >= deadline, which can be up to about 1s late. (3) Ordering. If the sweep runs after the block's actions, orders that should already have been cancelled can match in that block, so run it before pre_evm. (4) Unbounded sweep. A large catch-up gap (halt or restart) must be capped, or the sweep must carry `last_swept_sec`.

**Fix:** 1) torus-types/src/lib.rs: add `ScheduleCancel { time_ms: Option<u64> }` to NativeAction, add a new canonical-encoding tag (0 = None, 1 + u64 BE = Some), and add `struct ScheduledCancel { deadline_ms: Option<u64>, day: u64, triggers_today: u8 }` plus constants `SCHEDULE_CANCEL_MIN_DELAY_MS = 5_000` and `SCHEDULE_CANCEL_MAX_TRIGGERS_PER_DAY = 10`. Check the session-scope gate: a ScheduleCancel sent with a session key should be allowed under the trading scope.
2) torus-state/src/cf.rs: add `CF_SCHEDULED_CANCEL` (register it in ALL_CF_NAMES). It holds two key kinds. `b'a' || addr20` maps to the ScheduledCancel record. `b'd' || deadline_sec_be8` maps to a Vec<Address>, the bucket of accounts due in that second. db.rs: add get/put/delete helpers like the session ones, and use point gets/puts only (no iteration) so overlay semantics hold. Also add `b'w'` for last_swept_sec.
3) native_executor.rs: in `exec_schedule_cancel(ctx, sender, time_ms)`, compute now_ms = ctx.timestamp*1000 and day = now_ms / 86_400_000, resetting triggers_today when the day changes. On Some(t): reject if t < now_ms + 5000. If triggers_today >= 10, reject with "too many scheduleCancel triggers today" (HL counts triggers, i.e. executed sweeps; also cap sets to about 10x/day to stop index spam). Remove the old deadline from its bucket, insert into the bucket for ceil(t/1000), and save the record. On None: remove the record and its bucket entry. Add a match arm at about line 3336. In classify_action, map ScheduleCancel to Cancellation.
4) Add `pub fn sweep_scheduled_cancels(ctx)`. It loops sec from last_swept_sec+1 to ctx.timestamp, capped at MAX_SWEEP_SECS (e.g. 3600; beyond that, jump ahead and sweep the capped window), drains each bucket in sorted order, and calls exec_cancel_all(ctx, &addr, None) for each address whose record deadline still matches. It then increments triggers_today, clears the deadline and writes last_swept_sec.
5) torus-consensus/src/app.rs:~1901: call `NativeExecutor::sweep_scheduled_cancels(&mut ctx)` before `execute_batch(&mut ctx, &pre_evm)`.
6) RPC (torus-rpc): accept a `scheduleCancel` action in the exchange endpoint and expose the current deadline and trigger count in an info query.
Tests: reject if the deadline is under 5s ahead; None clears the schedule; the sweep cancels all books and frees margin at the deadline block but not the block before; the 11th trigger in a day is rejected and the counter resets at the UTC day boundary; rescheduling moves the bucket and the old bucket does not fire; two nodes produce the same state root (determinism); a large timestamp gap stays within the cap.

**Unsure:** Hit the time box before reading these: the StateBackend trait surface (whether point put/get of raw CF bytes is available through the overlay, as put_cf_raw in write_trades_inline suggests); the session-scope authorization path (resolve_sender) for the new variant; the canonical encoder's tag numbering; the torus-rpc exchange action parser; and whether HL's 10/day limit counts set calls or executed triggers (I believe executed triggers, with the reset at 00:00 UTC). The `idx` command was not on PATH, so lookups used grep.

</details>

**fable** — absent, impact medium, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: ~250-350 LOC: types ~30, state CF + db accessors ~60, executor action + sweep ~90, RPC/queue plumbing ~30, tests ~120

No dead-man switch exists: grep for ScheduleCancel/scheduleCancel/dead-man across crates and docs returns nothing. The building blocks are all present: `NativeAction::CancelAllOrders { market_id }` (torus-types/src/lib.rs:594) executed by `exec_cancel_all` (native_executor.rs:5209) which walks every book via `OrderBook::cancel_all` (order_book.rs:644) and releases margin; block time is `ctx.timestamp` in SECONDS (native_executor.rs:1365, comment at 5600); per-account keyed state already has a template in CF_SESSIONS (`put_session`/`get_session`/`delete_session`, db.rs:684-712, cf.rs:124). Proposed design: new `NativeAction::ScheduleCancel { time_ms: Option<u64> }` (None = unschedule), a new `CF_SCHEDULED_CANCELS` column family keyed by sender address storing `{deadline_ms, triggers_today: u8, day_bucket: u64}`, and a per-block sweep at the top of `execute_batch` Phase 1 (before the action loop at native_executor.rs:3559) that iterates the CF, calls `exec_cancel_all(ctx, &addr, None)` for every entry with deadline_ms <= ctx.timestamp*1000, and deletes the row. Validation in the exec arm: `time_ms >= now_ms + 5000` else error; `triggers_today >= 10` (reset when day_bucket != now_ms/86_400_000) else error; count a trigger on each successful schedule (HL counts scheduled triggers, not firings).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-594 — NativeAction enum; CancelAllOrders { market_id: Option<MarketId> } is the variant to reuse; no schedule variant
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3247 — execute() dispatch arm for CancelAllOrders -> exec_cancel_all
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5209-5239 — exec_cancel_all walks all books for market_id None, marks dirty_books, computes margin release
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1365 — ctx.timestamp: u64 (block metadata); :5600-5606 comment confirms it is seconds, converted to ms via saturating_mul(1000) for session expiry — same conversion needed for scheduleCancel
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3559-3576 — Phase 1 sequential non-PlaceOrder loop; the sweep hook goes immediately before it so freed margin precedes Phase 2 reservation
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6178 — classify_action puts cancels in ActionCategory::Cancellation; ScheduleCancel needs an arm here
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6288 — QueuedActionKind::CancelAll -> NativeAction mapping (RPC queue path that must also learn the new action)
- crates/torus-state/src/db.rs:684-730 — get_session/put_session/delete_session/count_sessions_for_owner on CF_SESSIONS: the per-account row pattern to copy (serde_json value, raw key)
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:124,196 — CF_SESSIONS constant and ALL_CF_NAMES registry where a new CF must be added
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1902-1903 — execute_batch called twice per block (pre_evm, post_evm); sweep must run once per block, so gate it on a ctx flag set only for the first call
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:644 — OrderBook::cancel_all(trader, market_id) removes trader_orders and pending_stops

**Risk:** Without a dead-man switch, a market maker whose connectivity drops leaves resting quotes exposed indefinitely; HL's scheduleCancel is a standard MM safety primitive and its absence blocks API-level parity for any MM integration ported from Hyperliquid. Design pitfalls: the sweep must be deterministic (iterate CF in key order, or keep an in-memory BTreeMap<(deadline_ms, Address)> loaded at ctx construction and included in the state root), must run exactly once per block despite two execute_batch calls (app.rs:1902-1903), and the row must be part of root-hashed state so validators agree on firing height.

**Fix:** 1) torus-types/src/lib.rs:580 — add `NativeAction::ScheduleCancel { time_ms: Option<u64> }` plus a `ScheduledCancel { deadline_ms: u64, triggers_today: u8, day_bucket: u64 }` struct; add to the action-hash scratch test list (action_hash_scratch_tests.rs:62) and the signed-action allowlist comment at lib.rs:245 if sessions may issue it. 2) torus-state/src/cf.rs — `CF_SCHEDULED_CANCELS`, push into ALL_CF_NAMES; db.rs — `get_scheduled_cancel(addr)`, `put_scheduled_cancel(addr, &row)`, `delete_scheduled_cancel(addr)`, `iter_scheduled_cancels() -> Vec<(Address, ScheduledCancel)>` mirroring put_session (db.rs:699). 3) native_executor.rs — `exec_schedule_cancel(ctx, sender, time_ms)`: now_ms = ctx.timestamp*1000; None => delete row; Some(t): reject t < now_ms + 5_000; load row, reset triggers_today if day_bucket != now_ms/86_400_000; reject triggers_today >= 10; write row with triggers_today+1. Dispatch arm next to :3247; classify_action arm at :6178 (Cancellation category, so it orders with cancels); gas constant ~1_000. 4) `sweep_scheduled_cancels(ctx)` called once at the start of execute_batch before Phase 1 (:3559), guarded by a `ctx.swept_this_block: bool` set false at ctx construction in app.rs; for each row with deadline_ms <= now_ms (sorted by address for determinism): `exec_cancel_all(ctx, &addr, None)`, delete row, emit a NativeActionResult/event. 5) RPC: add `scheduleCancel` to the exchange endpoint decode and QueuedActionKind (:6288 mapping). Tests: new crates/torus-bridge/tests/schedule_cancel_tests.rs — (a) schedule then advance timestamp past deadline => all orders gone and margin released; (b) reject <5s ahead; (c) 11th schedule in same day rejected, next day accepted; (d) None unschedules and no sweep fires; (e) sweep fires once even with pre_evm+post_evm batches; (f) state-root determinism across two nodes with same block.

**Unsure:** Did not read the RPC exchange-action decode path (torus-rpc) or QueuedActionKind definition, so the RPC plumbing LOC is an estimate. Did not confirm whether CF_SESSIONS participates in the state root (state_root.rs unread); if it does not, the new CF must be explicitly added to the root computation or the sweep height will diverge between validators. HL's exact trigger-count rule (10 per day counting schedules vs firings) is from memory, not verified against current HL docs.

</details>

### design-subaccounts

**opus** — absent, impact medium, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~650-950 LOC: torus-types/lib.rs + eip712.rs ~200; torus-state cf/db/backend ~120; native_executor.rs ~200; app.rs ~60; torus-rpc ~80; tests ~250-300

The codebase has no subaccounts. A case-insensitive grep for subaccount/sub_account across crates/ finds nothing in any .rs file. All per-user state is keyed by a plain 20-byte Address: balances use key = trader.as_slice() in CF_NATIVE_BALANCES, and positions use trader(20)||market_id(8). So the cheapest design that matches Hyperliquid is to make each subaccount its own derived address, deterministically computed as keccak256("torus.sub" || master || idx)[12..]. Margin is then separate with no change to the key layout, and the work is mostly bookkeeping: a CF that maps sub to master, a CreateSubAccount action, a SubAccountTransfer action, and an "act-as" field. The act-as field lets the master's EIP-712 signature (or a session the master created) act for a sub it owns, much like Hyperliquid's vaultAddress. The existing session-key system (CreateSession, resolve_sender returning session.owner) is the closest pattern to copy.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:42-43 CF_NATIVE_POSITIONS / CF_NATIVE_BALANCES; cf.rs:93 native_nonce_key = sender(20)\|\|nonce(8): replay protection keyed by signer
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:202 position_key(trader,market_id) = trader(20)+market_id(8): a derived sub address gets its own positions with no schema change
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:147-150 NativeBalance{available, order_margin}; :275 get_native_balance / :286 put_native_balance keyed by trader address
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580 enum NativeAction; :662-669 CreateSession/RevokeSession variants (template for new variants); no subaccount variant
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:951-957 SignedNativeAction{action, nonce, signature}: no vault or act-as field
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:801-838 resolve_sender: Eip712 ecrecover, or Session -> session.owner after expiry/scope checks; this is where effective-sender mapping would go
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:748-758 requires_eip712 list (CreateSession, Withdraw, Delegate...), which new master-only actions would join
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:745 MAX_SESSIONS_PER_ADDRESS = 5: template for a MAX_SUB_ACCOUNTS limit
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3181 execute(ctx, sender, action) and :3210 execute_action dispatch; :3293-3301 TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot/Withdraw arms
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5591-5640 exec_create_session: expiry/count/exists checks pattern via ctx.state.count_sessions_for_owner/get_session
- crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:128-158 withdraw_from_native_to: checks native_bal.available then debits, the debit/credit pattern a sub transfer would reuse
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:124 CF_SESSIONS, listed at :196 alongside native CFs; db.rs:684-715 / backend.rs:58-85 get_session/put_session/count_sessions_for_owner accessors (template for sub-account accessors)
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:4614-4630 validate path calls batch_verify_native_actions with a get_session closure: the same resolver must also apply the act-as mapping

**Risk:** Without subaccounts, market makers and funds cannot keep strategies in separate margin accounts under one key, as they can on Hyperliquid. They need several EOAs, each funded on its own, and have no way to transfer internally under one signature. The new act-as field changes what gets signed and hashed, so it breaks consensus: every validator must deploy it together, either at a fresh genesis (like F-2) or behind a height-gated fork. If the act-as check is applied in the execute path but not in validate_body_checks_core (or the other way round), validators reach different verdicts on the same block and the chain forks. This is the same kind of split that already happened with sessions (the app.rs:4620 comment).

**Fix:** 1. State (torus-state). Add CF_SUB_ACCOUNTS with key sub(20) and value borsh{master, name, idx}, plus CF_SUB_ACCOUNT_INDEX with key master(20)||idx(4) and value sub(20). Register both in cf.rs's CF list / NATIVE_ROOT_CFS so they are in the state root. Add get_sub_account(sub) -> Option<SubAccountInfo>, put_sub_account, and count_sub_accounts_for_master to db.rs and backend.rs, mirroring the get_session / put_session / count_sessions_for_owner accessors at db.rs:684-715 and backend.rs:58-85 and their overlay versions at backend.rs:178-197.

2. Types (torus-types/lib.rs). Add `NativeAction::CreateSubAccount { name: [u8; 16] }` and `NativeAction::SubAccountTransfer { sub: Address, is_deposit: bool, amount: U256 }`, plus canonical_bytes encodings for both. Add `vault: Option<Address>` to SignedNativeAction and bind it into eip712_struct_hash and the signed-action content hash. Add a helper `derive_sub_address(master, idx)`.

3. Signing (eip712.rs). Add CreateSubAccount and SubAccountTransfer to requires_eip712 (master key only). Add `pub const MAX_SUB_ACCOUNTS_PER_MASTER: usize = 10`. Add `resolve_effective_sender(signed, ts, session_lookup, sub_lookup)`: call resolve_sender to get the signer. If `vault` is set, require sub_lookup(vault).master == signer and that the action is not in requires_eip712 or another master-only set (Withdraw, staking, sessions, CreateSubAccount), then return vault. Otherwise return the signer. Sessions owned by the master can then trade for its subs if SessionScope allows it.

4. Executor (native_executor.rs). Add `exec_create_sub_account`: the sender must not itself be a sub, the count must be below the max, and the new address must not collide with an existing balance or position. Optionally gate creation on a minimum lifetime volume, as Hyperliquid does. Add `exec_sub_account_transfer`: check sub_lookup(sub).master == sender, then move NativeBalance.available between master and sub with PositionManager get_native_balance / put_native_balance, using both writes in one overlay as lockbox.rs:128-158 does. A transfer out of the sub must apply the same free-collateral or maintenance-margin check as exec_withdraw_from_native. Add both arms to execute_action near :3293 and to the classification match near :6193.

5. Consensus (app.rs). Switch the execution path and validate_body_checks_core (~:4625) to resolve_effective_sender with a state_db.get_sub_account closure. Keep nonces keyed by the signer (master), as Hyperliquid does.

6. RPC (torus-rpc). Add an info query `subAccounts(master)` that lists subs with their balances and positions.

7. Tests:
- Derived-address determinism.
- Create limit, plus a sub trying to create a sub.
- Transfer conservation.
- Transfer-out blocked while the sub's margin is in use.
- A non-master trying to act as a sub is rejected.
- A Withdraw signed by the master with vault set is rejected.
- A session acting as a sub, covering both the validate path and the execute path.
- Liquidating a sub does not touch the master's balance.

**Unsure:** I did not read these, so they are gaps: (1) Whether NativeBalance.available already accounts for unrealized PnL and position margin, or whether withdrawal uses a separate account-equity check. I did not read exec_withdraw_from_native (native_executor.rs:5811 onward), and that decides the margin check for transfers out of a sub. (2) The exact NATIVE_ROOT_CFS membership. I saw CF_SESSIONS listed at cf.rs:196 but not which list that is. (3) The execution-path sender resolution in app.rs (~L300) and how the parallel PlaceOrderBatch path in execute_batch carries the sender. vault would have to go through that path as well. (4) Whether the order/fill/liquidation engines in torus-core assume anything about trader addresses beyond them being 20-byte keys. I believe they don't, but I did not check. (5) Hyperliquid's exact sub-account rules (a volume threshold to unlock, a cap of about 10 subs) are from memory and not checked here.

</details>

**fable** — absent, impact medium, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~600-800 LOC: torus-types ~180 (variants, encoding, struct, resolve_sender), torus-state ~80 (CF + backend accessors), torus-bridge ~250 (3 handlers + classify), torus-rpc ~60, tests ~200

No subaccount concept exists: grep for SubAccount/sub_account in torus-core, torus-bridge, torus-state returns nothing, and NativeAction (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-700) has only TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot/Withdraw as transfers. All native state is keyed by a single 20-byte Address: CF_NATIVE_BALANCES is keyed by trader.as_slice() (lockbox.rs:216) and positions by position_key(trader, market_id)=addr(20)+market(8) (position.rs:202). Proposed design: a subaccount IS a fresh 20-byte Address (derived deterministically, e.g. keccak(master||index)[12..]) with a CF_SUBACCOUNTS record {master, name, created_at}; every balance/position/order/nonce row then keys naturally by the sub address with zero changes to torus-state keying, giving separate margin for free. Master authority is injected at the existing SignedNativeAction::resolve_sender hook (eip712.rs:801) which already maps session-key -> owner via SessionData.owner (native_executor.rs:5643-5664): add an optional `act_as: Option<Address>` on the envelope; when set and CF_SUBACCOUNTS[act_as].master == recovered signer, the executor runs execute_action(ctx, &act_as, action) (native_executor.rs:3210).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-700 — NativeAction enum: transfers are only TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot/Withdraw; no subaccount variants
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:202-207 — position_key(trader,&market_id) = 20-byte addr + 8-byte market; a sub as its own Address reuses this unchanged
- crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:11,216 — CF_NATIVE_BALANCES keyed by trader.as_slice(); same reuse argument
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:41-45,85,124 — CF_NATIVE_ORDERS/POSITIONS/BALANCES/NONCES/SESSIONS; a new CF_SUBACCOUNTS slots in beside CF_SESSIONS
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:244-256 — SessionScope {Trading,TransfersOnly,Full} + allows(); model for a per-sub permission scope
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:951-957 — SignedNativeAction {action, nonce, signature}; act_as field goes here
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:764,778,801,835,871 — recover_sender / verify_session_signature / resolve_sender (scope.allows check) / validate_with_sessions: the single sender-resolution point to extend
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3210-3214 — execute_action(ctx, sender, action): sender is the only identity; substitute the sub address here
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3292-3302 — Transfer handlers exec_deposit_to_native / exec_withdraw_from_native / exec_withdraw_to(ctx, sender, to, amount): template for SubAccountTransfer
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5591-5675 — exec_create_session/exec_revoke_session: owner stored in SessionData, 'not session owner' check; CreateSubAccount mirrors this incl. max-per-owner cap (count_sessions_for_owner at :5615)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6164-6200 — ActionCategory + classify_action; new variants must be classified (Lockbox for transfer, Other for create/rename)

**Risk:** Hyperliquid parity gap: HL users rely on subAccountTransfer / createSubAccount / subAccountModify for strategy isolation and separate margin pools; market makers and vault operators cannot run isolated books on Torus today. Without a sub-as-address design, any alternative (composite keys) would re-key CF_NATIVE_BALANCES/POSITIONS/ORDERS/NONCES and the position_key layout, a fresh-genesis consensus change touching the parallel per-market exec pipeline.

**Fix:** 1) torus-types/src/lib.rs: add NativeAction::CreateSubAccount{name:[u8;32]}, SubAccountModify{sub:Address,name}, SubAccountTransfer{sub:Address,is_deposit:bool,amount:U256}; extend canonical_bytes + eip712_struct_hash (eip712.rs:195) + requires_eip712 (:748); add `pub struct SubAccountData{master:Address,name:[u8;32],created_at:u64}`; add `act_as: Option<Address>` to SignedNativeAction (:951) and bind it into compute_action_hash preimage (consensus format change, fresh genesis like F-2). 2) torus-types/src/eip712.rs resolve_sender/validate_with_sessions (:801,:871): after recovering signer (ECDSA or session->owner), if act_as is Some, require lookup(act_as).master == signer, deny act_as for CreateSubAccount/CreateSession/RevokeSession/Withdraw/Delegate/*Stake (same denylist as SessionScope::Full), return act_as as effective sender. 3) torus-state/src/cf.rs: CF_SUBACCOUNTS = "cf_subaccounts" keyed by sub addr; add get_subaccount/put_subaccount/count_subaccounts_for_master to StateBackend (backend.rs) and a master->subs index key (master(20)||index(1)) for RPC listing. 4) torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs: exec_create_subaccount (derive addr = keccak(master||count)[12..], cap e.g. 10 per master, reject if CF_ACCOUNTS/CF_NATIVE_BALANCES already non-empty at that addr), exec_subaccount_modify, exec_subaccount_transfer (master-signed only: move CF_NATIVE_BALANCES between master and sub via the lockbox credit/debit helpers at lockbox.rs:67-162, reject if withdrawing below sub's cross-margin maintenance via MarginEngine::cross_margin_equity/total_maintenance_margin at margin.rs:179,202); classify_action: transfer->Lockbox, create/modify->Other. 5) Limits: subs cannot CreateSubAccount, CreateSession, Withdraw, stake or vote (enforced at step 2); nonces stay per-sub via CF_NATIVE_NONCES keyed by effective sender. 6) torus-rpc: torus_subAccounts(master) query + act_as in torus_submitNativeAction; mempool rate_limit check_sender (rpc lib.rs:208) should key on signer not sub. Tests: eip712 tests for act_as resolution/denylist; executor tests mirroring the session-key tests at lib.rs:1822-1865 for create/transfer/margin-guard; a determinism test that sub address derivation matches across validators.

**Unsure:** Did not read resolve_sender body (eip712.rs:801-845) or the NativeExecContext fields, so whether act_as can be resolved there without a state handle (validate_with_sessions takes a closure F for session lookup; a second closure or a combined trait is likely needed) is unverified. Did not confirm how CF_NATIVE_NONCES is keyed in the executor (grep for check_nonce/bump_nonce returned nothing in native_executor.rs; may live in app.rs/mempool). Whether cross-margin equity is computed per-address today (so separate margin truly falls out of sub-as-address) was inferred from position_key/balance keying, not from reading cross_margin_equity. HL also lets subs be queried via master API wallet without act_as; RPC read-side parity not scoped.
