### design-order-history

**opus** — absent, impact medium, effort L, lockstep no · LOC: ~1,600-1,800 total (~1,150 production + ~450-650 tests) across order_book.rs, new torus-state/src/order_rows.rs, cf.rs, bg_writer.rs, native_executor.rs, app.rs, torus-rpc torus.rs/types.rs/streams.rs/lib.rs

Nothing stores the order lifecycle today. OrderStatus (Filled/PartiallyFilled/Resting/Cancelled/Rejected/PendingTrigger) only exists inside PlaceResult. NativeActionResult carries no order id or status. Cancels, self-trade-prevention cancels and stop triggers (OrderBook::trigger_stops) leave no record. Fills are the only thing persisted after execution: trade_rows::encode_block writes them to the node-local CFs CF_NATIVE_TRADES and CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES through the background writer in app.rs, and the newTrades and userFills streams publish them. I found no pruning of those trade CFs. The design copies that fill pipeline for order events: a per-block Vec<OrderEvent> gathered in NativeExecContext, a new order_rows.rs module that encodes it into node-local CFs off the execution thread, a block-height index for pruning, RPCs for orderStatus, historicalOrders and orderUpdates, and a new torus_subscribe kind called orderUpdates.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:65-91 PlaceResult{order_id,status,fills,self_trade_cancels} and the OrderStatus enum. Status is only returned to the caller, never stored
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1272-1310 trigger_stops drains pending_stops into a local `triggered` Vec and re-places each as Market/Limit. Nothing outside the book sees the trigger
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:39-44 NativeActionResult{action_type,success,error,gas_used}, with no oid or status
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1375-1395 defer_trades and trade_history flags. Fill rows go to node-local CFs outside the consensus root
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1399 pending_fills: Vec<TradeFill>, the per-block buffer to copy for order events
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3190-3203 write_trades_inline calls encode_block (the inline path)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5162 exec_cancel_order, 5209/5279 exec_cancel_all(_run), the cancel hook points
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:2194-2232 Arc<BlockFills> is shared by fill_sink.send_fills and trade_writer.send_encode_then (EncodeRows closure, sync fallback)
- crates/torus-state/src/trade_rows.rs:24-34,130-218 format meta key, key layouts (market\|block\|chunk, trader\|block) and encode_block. This is the template to copy
- crates/torus-state/src/trade_rows.rs:55-90 FillExtras already carries maker/taker order ids, but only when a stream is subscribed
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:76-77 CF_NATIVE_TRADES / CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES definitions. grep found no prune or delete_range of them except the format-reset in trade_rows.rs:233
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:200-224 getOpenOrders (live book), getUserTrades and the subscribe(sub_type, params) jsonrpsee subscription
- crates/torus-rpc/src/streams.rs:25-32 StreamKind {NewTrades, UserFills}. orderUpdates would be a third variant

**Risk:** Without it there is no HL-parity orderStatus, historicalOrders or orderUpdates. Clients can't learn why an order disappeared (cancelled, self-trade-prevention cancel, liquidation, trigger fired, rejected) and can't look up an order by cloid after it leaves the book. Separately, trade-history CFs have no pruning I could find, so node disk grows without limit. Order events are about 3-5x more frequent than fills, so adding them without pruning would make that worse. Everything here is node-local output, so it does not touch consensus, as long as no event is read back during execution and the state root ignores these CFs, as it already does for the trade CFs.

**Fix:** 1) torus-core order_book.rs: give OrderBook a `pub triggered_log: Vec<(stop_id, placed_order_id)>`. trigger_stops (around 1300) pushes to it, and the executor drains it after each place. Optionally add a terminal reason on the self-trade-prevention cancels already in PlaceResult. About 40 LOC.
2) torus-state, new src/order_rows.rs, modelled on trade_rows.rs:
   - `OrderEvent{oid:u128, cloid:Option<u64>, trader, market, side, px_raw, orig_sz_raw, rem_sz_raw, kind: Placed|Resting|Filled|PartiallyFilled|Cancelled(reason)|Rejected(reason)|Triggered|Expired, block, seq:u32, ts}`.
   - Four CFs in cf.rs: CF_NATIVE_ORDER_STATUS (oid -> latest event, overwritten in place, used by orderStatus); CF_NATIVE_ORDER_CLOID ((trader, cloid) -> oid); CF_NATIVE_USER_ORDERS (trader | block_be | seq -> event, used for historicalOrders and orderUpdates backfill as a reverse prefix scan); CF_NATIVE_ORDER_BY_BLOCK (block_be -> list of (trader, oid) touched, the pruning index).
   - `encode_block_orders(block, ts, &[OrderEvent], &mut PackedCfBatch)`, decode functions, and META_ORDER_HISTORY_FORMAT with an ensure_* reset like ensure_trade_history_format.
   - About 350 LOC plus 200 of tests.
3) native_executor.rs: add `pending_order_events: Vec<OrderEvent>` next to pending_fills (line 1399). Push events from:
   - the place path, using the PlaceResult status and self_trade_cancels;
   - exec_cancel_order (5162) and exec_cancel_all_run (5279);
   - the triggered_log drain;
   - run_liquidation_checks (5923) forced cancels;
   - margin and reduce-only rejects.
   Gate it on the existing trade_history flag (or a new order_history flag) and a sink wants() check, so validators pay nothing. Under defer_trades the events are handed off with the fills, and write_trades_inline (3190) gets a matching inline write. About 200 LOC.
4) app.rs around 2194: put order events into the same Arc (rename BlockFills to BlockOutput, or add a field), add a sink.send_order_events call, and fold the order encoding into the same EncodeRows closure so it uses the existing bg_writer and sync fallback. About 60 LOC.
5) Pruning: a node-local retention window (TORUS_ORDER_HISTORY_BLOCKS, plus the same knob for trades). Every N blocks the bg_writer thread:
   - scans CF_NATIVE_ORDER_BY_BLOCK below the cutoff;
   - deletes the matching USER_ORDERS rows;
   - deletes ORDER_STATUS and CLOID rows only when the order is terminal, never resting orders;
   - range-deletes the index;
   - stores the low watermark in CF_CONSENSUS_META.
   A per-user cap (HL returns at most 2000 historicalOrders) is enforced at read time with the limit, not by deleting rows. About 150 LOC. The same pruner should also be extended to CF_NATIVE_TRADES and CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES.
6) RPC, torus.rs and types.rs:
   - torus_orderStatus(user, oid | cloid) -> {status, statusTimestamp, order} or "unknownOid";
   - torus_historicalOrders(user, limit<=2000);
   - torus_getOrderUpdates(user, fromBlock, limit) for backfill.
   For orders still on the book, read the live book first, the way getOpenOrders does. About 250 LOC.
7) streams.rs: add StreamKind::OrderUpdates(Address), a parse_stream_kind arm, and an orders_for_user builder that, like userFills, serializes once per user per block. Also add an ensure that blocks executed before anyone subscribed are skipped. About 120 LOC.
8) Tests:
   - order_rows round-trip and key ordering;
   - executor emits the right event sequence for place, partial fill, cancel, self-trade-prevention, stop trigger, IOC remainder and FOK reject;
   - pruner keeps resting orders;
   - RPC tests for orderStatus and historicalOrders;
   - a WS orderUpdates test in subscribe_ws_tests.
   About 450 LOC.

**Unsure:** Not read:
- the place-order executor function, so I don't know the exact hook line, or where reduce-only and margin rejects happen;
- run_liquidation_checks internals (whether liquidations cancel resting orders);
- bg_writer.rs, so I haven't confirmed it can run a periodic pruner task;
- the getOpenOrders body (1468) and RpcOpenOrder fields;
- whether TIF expiry or a GTT exists, which decides whether an Expired event is needed.
That no trade-CF pruning exists comes from a grep for prune/delete_range/retention only. A node-level or compaction-filter pruner elsewhere (for example in torus-node main.rs) could have been missed. I also didn't confirm that the native state root excludes all CF_NATIVE_* node-local CFs. The trade CFs say so in comments, and the new CFs must be registered the same way.

</details>

**fable** — absent, impact high, effort L, lockstep no · LOC: ~950-1100 LOC (state order_rows ~350, executor ~150, app ~60, rpc+ws ~300, pruner ~80, tests ~200)

There is no order-lifecycle history today: the only post-execution persisted stream is fills (trade_rows.rs: CF_NATIVE_TRADES / CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES, packed per block by the BackgroundCfWriter, read by torus_getTradeHistory/getUserTrades, and fanned out to WS `userFills`/`newTrades` via the FillSink trait). Order placement/cancel/reject/trigger outcomes exist only transiently in-execution (PlaceResult.status: Filled/PartiallyFilled/Resting/Cancelled/Rejected/PendingTrigger; PrepOutcome::Reject{msg}; self_trade_cancels; book row ops) and are counted in metrics, never recorded. `torus_getOpenOrders` reads live book rows only (book_reader::read_open_orders), so a cancelled, rejected or fully-filled order id becomes unqueryable the block it leaves the book. Proposed design: mirror the fills pipeline exactly — executor collects `OrderEvent{order_id, trader, market, kind(Placed/Filled/Cancelled/Rejected/Triggered), status, remaining, reason, action_index}` per block into ctx (same as pending_fills), app.rs wraps them in a `BlockOrderEvents` Arc shared by a new `OrderEventSink` (WS `orderUpdates`) and the same trade_writer (new CF_NATIVE_ORDER_EVENTS keyed `address[20] | !block u64` with one packed row per (trader, block), plus CF_NATIVE_ORDER_STATUS keyed `order_id u128` -> latest status row), node-local, outside the consensus root.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-state/src/trade_rows.rs:1-15 — trade history is node-local packed rows in CF_NATIVE_TRADES (market\|block\|chunk) and CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES (address\|!block), built once per block, idempotent on crash-replay; this is the template to copy
- crates/torus-state/src/trade_rows.rs:83-90 — `trait FillSink { wants_fills(); send_fills(Arc<BlockFills>) }` is the WS hand-off; an OrderEventSink twin is the WS orderUpdates path
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:2182-2215 — per-block fills are wrapped in Arc<BlockFills>, sent to fill_sink then to trade_writer via EncodeRows closure; the order-event hand-off slots in here
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1899 and 2051 — ctx.record_fills gated by sink.wants_fills(); ctx.take_pending_fills_and_extras() drains per block (native_executor.rs:1953)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:36-93 — Order has client_order_id/original_qty/remaining_qty; PlaceResult{order_id,status,fills,self_trade_cancels}; OrderStatus {Filled,PartiallyFilled,Resting,Cancelled,Rejected,PendingTrigger} — all lifecycle states already exist as values, just not persisted
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:410-420 — PrepOutcome::Reject{margin,msg} carries the reject reason string; 4770 orders_cancelled_partial_fill, 4776 trigger re-entry, 5968 liquidations_triggered: the exact sites to emit events
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1539 — take_row_ops() yields (OrderId, Option<row>) per block: None = order left the book (fill/cancel), usable as a cheap lifecycle hook
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:938-975 and 1645-1651 — getTradeHistory/getUserTrades reverse-iterate prefix keys with limit<=1000 and honor pruned_up_to; historicalOrders follows the same shape
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:201,1468-1486 — getOpenOrders reads live rows only via book_reader::read_open_orders; no history
- crates/torus-state/src/pruner.rs:50 — cf_native_trades is listed as HARD TO PRUNE (market prefix, not height); the user-keyed CF with !block suffix is prunable per-user only by iteration, so a new height-leading index CF or periodic per-prefix sweep is required
- crates/torus-state/src/pruner.rs:150-232 — maybe_prune only delete_range's CF_BLOCK_BODIES and CF_RECEIPTS by height prefix

**Risk:** HL parity gap: HL exposes `orderStatus` (by oid or cloid), `historicalOrders` (last 2000 per user with status filled/canceled/rejected/triggered/marginCanceled etc.) and WS `orderUpdates`. Frontends/bots cannot learn why an order vanished (reject vs fill vs STP-cancel vs IOC remainder cancel) or track a cloid once off-book. Trade history alone cannot answer "was my order rejected and why".

**Fix:** 1) crates/torus-state/src/order_rows.rs (new, ~350 LOC): `OrderEvent{order_id:u128, client_order_id:Option<u64>, trader, market, kind:u8 (Placed/Filled/Cancelled/Rejected/Triggered/MarginCancelled), status:u8, orig_qty, remaining, price, reason_code:u8, timestamp}`; `BlockOrderEvents{height,timestamp,events}`; `trait OrderEventSink{wants_events, send_events}`; `encode_block()` -> PackedCfBatch for two new CFs in cf.rs: CF_NATIVE_USER_ORDER_EVENTS (`address[20]|!block u64`, packed n×event) and CF_NATIVE_ORDER_STATUS (`order_id u128` -> latest event); plus a height-leading CF_NATIVE_ORDER_EVENTS_BY_HEIGHT (`block u64|address[20]`) so pruner can delete_range by height and then delete the user rows it names. 2) native_executor.rs (~150 LOC): add `pending_order_events: Vec<OrderEvent>` + `record_order_events` flag beside pending_fills (1393-1403); push at PlaceResult handling (status Resting/PartiallyFilled/Filled/Cancelled/Rejected), PrepOutcome::Reject (420), self_trade_cancels, CancelOrder/CancelAllOrders paths (~1242, 4770), trigger fire (4776), liquidation cancels (5968); `take_pending_order_events()` next to 1953. Gate by `trade_history || sink.wants_events()` (same as 1899). 3) app.rs (~60 LOC): mirror 2182-2215 — Arc<BlockOrderEvents> -> order_sink + trade_writer EncodeRows; `set_order_event_sink`. 4) torus-rpc (~300 LOC): torus.rs add `torus_getOrderStatus(order_id | {user, cloid})`, `torus_getHistoricalOrders(user, limit<=2000, market?)` (reverse-iterate like 1645), types.rs RpcOrderEvent/RpcOrderStatus; streams.rs add `orderUpdates {user}` kind beside `userFills` (59-65) with per-block fan-out like 220-261. 5) pruner.rs (~80 LOC): retain window for the by-height CF, delete the referenced user rows; keep ORDER_STATUS unpruned or TTL by height stored in value. 6) Tests: order_rows encode/decode roundtrip + idempotent rewrite; executor unit tests asserting one event per lifecycle transition (reject reason, IOC remainder cancel, STP cancel, trigger); streams.rs test `order_updates_stream_filters_by_address` modeled on 828; RPC test getHistoricalOrders ordering + pruned_up_to clamp. Total ~950-1100 LOC incl. tests.

**Unsure:** Did not read the exact PlaceOrder result-handling site in native_executor.rs (3700-3800, 4740-4790) or the CancelOrder path to confirm every transition is reachable from one function; count of emission sites may be higher (sharded prepare vs serial). Did not verify whether the committer writes native-action receipts to CF_RECEIPTS that could carry reject reasons already (committer.rs:44,154 only grepped). Stop/trigger order storage (StopOrder struct, order_book.rs:93) and its persistence were not read, so the Triggered event hook location is approximate. Pruning of user-prefixed CFs is listed as deferred for trades; my by-height index proposal is untested against the pruner's delete_range style.

</details>

### design-clearinghouse-rpc

**opus** — design, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: Phase A (RPC only, uses existing state): ~400-500 LOC (types.rs ~120, torus.rs ~250, liquidation_price helper + tests ~120). Phase B (funding, persisted margin config, incremental OI, 24h volume, real mark px): ~700-1000 LOC across torus-core/funding.rs, position.rs, native_executor.rs, torus-state/cf.rs, plus migration and tests.

Today torus_* RPC is split per position and per market. getPosition returns one (trader, market) pair, getBalances returns totals, and getMarkets/getOpenInterest/getMarkPrice each return one field per market. Nothing aggregates them the way HL's clearinghouseState/metaAndAssetCtxs do. The math already exists in torus-core but nothing calls it from RPC: MarginEngine::cross_margin_equity, total_maintenance_margin and LiquidationEngine's cross check. Proposed design: add two read-only methods, getClearinghouseState(trader) and getMetaAndAssetCtxs(), built from PositionManager.positions_for_trader, get_native_balance, OracleManager.get_price and the per-market MarketMarginConfig. Three things are missing from state: (1) funding (no funding engine, rate or cumulative index exists, only MarketParams.max_funding_rate_bps), (2) 24h volume and prevDayPx (no rolling aggregate), (3) a persisted per-market margin config RPC can read (it sits only in the executor's in-memory HashMap). Mark price is also just the oracle price, and getOpenInterest scans the whole CF.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:100-214 - TorusApi methods: getPosition, getBalances, getMarkets, getOpenInterest, getMarkPrice. No account-wide or all-markets context method
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:772-829 - get_position handles a single market only. Mark comes from OracleManager.get_price and falls back to entry price. Liq px is a 'simplified' entry -/+ isolated_margin/size, so it is ZERO for cross positions (isolated_margin==0) and ignores maintenance margin
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:831-876 - get_balances sums order_margin + isolated_margin as total_margin_used. Cross margin used, account value and withdrawable are not computed
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:880-935 - get_markets decodes StoredMarket (torus.rs:55-62: base/quote/lot/tick/initial_margin_raw). It returns no szDecimals, maxLeverage, maintenance or funding params, and status is hardcoded to 'active'
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1557-1601 - get_open_interest does a full scan of CF_NATIVE_POSITIONS filtered by market (O(all positions) per market)
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1604-1648 - get_mark_price sets mark_price == index_price == the oracle price. last_trade_price comes from book_reader::read_last_trade_price or the OrderBook blob
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:179-200 - cross_margin_equity = available - order_margin + sum of cross uPnL (needs an oracle_prices slice)
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:202-229 - total_maintenance_margin = notional/effective_max_leverage * maintenance_factor_bps/10000 over cross positions. margin.rs:66,75: default maintenance_factor_bps 5000
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:72-98 - check_liquidations takes a single &MarketMarginConfig plus oracle_prices. Cross positions are checked as a group
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:52-61,66,76,260 - Position {size, entry_price, realized_pnl, isolated_margin, margin_type}, unrealized_pnl(mark), notional(mark), positions_for_trader prefix scan. No funding fields (no cumFunding or lastFundingIndex)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1356 - margin_configs: HashMap<MarketId, MarketMarginConfig> lives in the executor, not in a CF that RPC reads
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1156-1162 - MarketParams has max_funding_rate_bps and maintenance_margin_bps. grep of 'funding' across crates matches only torus-types lib.rs/eip712.rs, so there is no funding engine
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:41-159 - native CFs (orders, positions, balances, order_books, markets, oracle, trades, user_trades, ...). There is no funding, volume or margin-config CF

**Risk:** HL clients (SDKs, frontends, liquidation bots) depend on clearinghouseState and metaAndAssetCtxs as their main reads. Without them a client makes N+1 calls per account and gets wrong answers. Cross positions show liq px 0. The withdrawable amount does not subtract cross maintenance or initial margin. Funding, OI notional and 24h volume are absent or wrong, so a UI cannot render a market list or account panel matching HL. The liq px shown by RPC can also differ from what LiquidationEngine actually triggers on, which misleads users about liquidation risk. The RPC methods alone do not change consensus. Adding funding and persisted margin config does.

**Fix:** Phase A, RPC only, no consensus change (about 450 LOC):
1. In crates/torus-rpc/src/types.rs add RpcClearinghouseState {assetPositions: Vec<RpcAssetPosition>, marginSummary, crossMarginSummary: RpcMarginSummary{accountValue, totalNtlPos, totalRawUsd, totalMarginUsed}, crossMaintenanceMarginUsed, withdrawable, time}. RpcAssetPosition {coin/market_id, szi (signed), entryPx, positionValue, unrealizedPnl, returnOnEquity, leverage{type, value}, liquidationPx, marginUsed, maxLeverage, cumFunding: null until Phase B}. Add RpcMeta {universe: [{name, szDecimals, maxLeverage, onlyIsolated}]} and RpcAssetCtx {markPx, oraclePx, midPx, funding, openInterest, dayNtlVlm, prevDayPx, premium, impactPxs}.
2. In crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs add #[method(name="getClearinghouseState")] and #[method(name="getMetaAndAssetCtxs")]. Factor out a helper oracle_prices_for(&[MarketId], height) -> Vec<(MarketId, FixedPoint)> to replace the duplicated OracleManager::new code in get_position and get_mark_price. Compute accountValue with MarginEngine::cross_margin_equity, crossMaintenanceMarginUsed with total_maintenance_margin, and withdrawable = max(0, accountValue - cross initial margin - order_margin). That matches HL, where withdrawable subtracts initial margin, not maintenance.
3. Liq px: add a pure fn in crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs, liquidation_price(pos, equity_excl_pos, other_maint, cfg), that inverts the check_cross_liquidation condition: for cross, the price p where equity(p) = maint(p); for isolated, (isolated_margin - maint)/size. Use it in both getPosition (replacing the 'simplified' block at torus.rs:804-813) and the new method, so RPC and the engine agree. Unit-test that the engine liquidates at the returned px.
4. OI: per market, reuse the get_open_interest loop but run one full CF_NATIVE_POSITIONS scan for all markets and fill a HashMap<MarketId, (long, short)>. That is acceptable for an RPC until Phase B.

Phase B, consensus-affecting state (about 600-900 LOC):
(a) Add CF_NATIVE_MARKET_CTX in torus-state/src/cf.rs, keyed by market_id. It holds a persisted MarketMarginConfig (max_leverage, maintenance_factor_bps, tiers) written at listing time from MarketParams. The executor margin_configs HashMap (native_executor.rs:1356) becomes a cache over it. Extend StoredMarket with maintenance and funding params.
(b) Funding engine in torus-core/src/funding.rs: hourly premium = (impact mid - oracle)/oracle, clamped by max_funding_rate_bps. Keep a cumulative funding index per market in the ctx row. Add Position.last_funding_index plus cum_funding (borsh migration). Settle on position touch and at the funding tick in native_executor.
(c) Maintain OI incrementally in the ctx row in PositionManager save/delete paths, instead of scanning.
(d) 24h volume and prevDayPx: keep a ring of 24 hourly buckets (ntl volume, open px) per market in the ctx row, updated where fills are written to CF_NATIVE_TRADES. This could instead be computed off-consensus in the RPC node from CF_NATIVE_TRADES via streams.rs, which avoids the consensus change.
(e) Mark px: HL uses median(oracle-adjusted book price, book mid, external perp). Compute it from book_reader mid + oracle in a mark_price(mid) helper and use the same value in liquidation.
Tests: RPC golden tests in crates/torus-rpc/src/lib.rs test module for 1 cross + 1 isolated position (accountValue, withdrawable, liqPx matching LiquidationEngine), and funding-index settlement tests in torus-core.

**Unsure:** Phase A alone is not consensus-breaking. Phase B is: funding, the persisted margin config and position fields. Not verified: whether margin_configs in native_executor.rs:1356 is rebuilt from some persisted source on restart (I did not read where it is populated), and whether app.rs or the executor already runs a funding tick under another name (grep for 'funding' found only torus-types). I did not read check_cross_liquidation's body, so the exact formula for inverting liq px still needs checking. I did not check streams.rs for an existing volume aggregator, or whether StoredMarket's initial_margin_raw is the only margin param persisted in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS.

</details>

**fable** — design, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: Phase A ~350 (rpc types + 2 methods + liq px helper + tests); Phase B ~250 (StoredMarket schema, OI aggregate, executor load); Phase C ~500-700 (funding engine + volume window). Total ~1100-1300.

Today the RPC exposes only per-market, per-trader primitives: getPosition (one market, with a fake liq px = entry -/+ isolated_margin/size, ignoring maintenance factor and cross mode), getBalances (sums order_margin + isolated_margin, no equity/unrealized/withdrawable), getOpenInterest (full CF_NATIVE_POSITIONS scan per call), getMarkPrice (mark == index == oracle price), getMarkets (StoredMarket: base/quote/lot/tick only). Proposed design: (1) torus_clearinghouseState(trader) built in torus-rpc/src/torus.rs by calling PositionManager::positions_for_trader + get_native_balance once, OracleManager::get_price per market, then reusing MarginEngine::cross_margin_equity / total_maintenance_margin and the per-position maintenance math from check_isolated_maintenance to produce accountValue, totalNtlPos, totalMarginUsed, maintenanceMargin, withdrawable = max(0, available - order_margin - sum(initial margin of cross positions)), and per-position liqPx derived by solving equity(mark)=maintenance(mark) (closed form per position: long liqPx = entry - (margin - maint_at_entry)/size adjusted by maintenance_factor_bps; cross liqPx needs the whole account). (2) torus_metaAndAssetCtxs() iterating CF_NATIVE_MARKETS for meta (name, szDecimals from lot_size, maxLeverage from margin config) and per-market ctx {markPx, oraclePx, openInterest, funding, prevDayPx, dayNtlVlm}. Missing state: no funding engine at all (only a governance param max_funding_rate_bps in torus-types; zero funding references in native_executor.rs or torus-core); no premium/mark-price distinct from oracle; no per-market OI aggregate (OI requires full position-CF scan); no 24h volume / prevDayPx rolling window; MarketMarginConfig lives only in the executor's in-memory HashMap (ctx.margin_configs), not in state, so RPC cannot read max_leverage/maintenance_factor_bps without a new CF or a shared handle.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:772-829 get_position: liquidation_price = entry -/+ isolated_margin/size, no maintenance factor, cross positions get 0; unrealized uses oracle price fallback entry
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:831-878 get_balances: total_margin_used = order_margin + sum(isolated_margin); no unrealized PnL, equity, or withdrawable
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1557-1602 get_open_interest: full iterator over CF_NATIVE_POSITIONS filtered by market (28-byte key) on every call
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1604-1643 get_mark_price: mark_price and index_price both = oracle.get_price(); last trade px from book meta row
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:55-62 StoredMarket {base_asset, quote_asset, lot_size_raw, tick_size_raw, initial_margin_raw(dead_code)} - no max leverage, funding, or volume
- crates/torus-rpc/src/types.rs:276-357 RpcPosition/RpcBalances/RpcMarketInfo/RpcOpenInterest/RpcMarkPrice shapes
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:179-229 MarginEngine::cross_margin_equity (available - order_margin + cross uPnL) and total_maintenance_margin (initial = notional/effective_max_leverage; maint = initial*maintenance_factor_bps/10000)
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:18-67 MarginTier{max_notional,max_leverage}, MarketMarginConfig{market_id,max_leverage,maintenance_factor_bps,tiers}
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:52-76 Position{trader,market_id,is_long,size,entry_price,realized_pnl,isolated_margin,margin_type}, unrealized_pnl(mark), notional(mark); NativeBalance{available,order_margin} at 147-149
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:114-135 check_cross_liquidation: equity < maintenance => flag all cross positions
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1356,1842 margin_configs: HashMap<MarketId,MarketMarginConfig> in-memory on executor ctx, initialised empty; 5931-5945 liquidation sweep iterates it
- grep -c funding over native_executor.rs and torus-core/src/*.rs returned no matches; only torus-types/src/lib.rs:1161 max_funding_rate_bps governance param
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:42,45,76 CF_NATIVE_POSITIONS, CF_NATIVE_MARKETS, CF_NATIVE_TRADES

**Risk:** Without a clearinghouseState equivalent, frontends/SDKs cannot show account value, cross-margin health, or a correct liquidation price (current getPosition liq px is wrong for cross and ignores maintenance factor, so a UI built on it would mislead users about liquidation risk). Without metaAndAssetCtxs there is no funding rate, premium, OI, or 24h volume surface at all, which is a hard HL parity gap and blocks any HL-compatible SDK/UI port. The in-memory margin_configs means RPC answers can diverge from what the executor actually enforces.

**Fix:** Phase A (RPC-only, ~350 LOC): in crates/torus-rpc/src/types.rs add RpcClearinghouseState{marginSummary{accountValue,totalNtlPos,totalRawUsd,totalMarginUsed}, crossMaintenanceMarginUsed, withdrawable, assetPositions: Vec<RpcAssetPosition{coin/marketId, szi(signed), entryPx, positionValue, unrealizedPnl, returnOnEquity, leverage{type,value}, liquidationPx, marginUsed, maxLeverage}>} and RpcAssetCtx{markPx, oraclePx, midPx, funding, openInterest, prevDayPx, dayNtlVlm, premium}; in torus.rs add #[method(name="clearinghouseState")] and #[method(name="metaAndAssetCtxs")]. Implement clearinghouseState via PositionManager::positions_for_trader + get_native_balance + OracleManager::get_price per market, MarginEngine::cross_margin_equity/total_maintenance_margin, and a new torus-core/src/margin.rs fn liquidation_price(pos, cfg, equity_other) solving entry +/- (margin_available - maint)/size (isolated: margin_available=isolated_margin; cross: account equity minus other positions' maintenance). Phase B (state, ~250 LOC): persist MarketMarginConfig per market into CF_NATIVE_MARKETS (extend StoredMarket with max_leverage, maintenance_factor_bps, tiers) and have native_executor load ctx.margin_configs from it so RPC and executor agree; add per-market OI aggregate row (CF_NATIVE_MARKETS key market_id||b"oi") updated in PositionManager::apply_fill_cached_effect / flush_all so getOpenInterest and assetCtx stop scanning positions. Phase C (new engine, ~500+ LOC): funding -- premium = (mark - oracle)/oracle sampled per block, hourly rate = clamp(avg premium + interest, max_funding_rate_bps), cumulative_funding per market row, settle on position touch or per-epoch in native_executor; plus a 24h rolling trade-volume/prevDayPx ring (per-block buckets in CF_NATIVE_TRADES side table) feeding dayNtlVlm. Tests: torus-rpc/src/lib.rs tests next to torus_get_position_open (2641) and torus_get_balances_with_margin (2749): cross account with two positions asserts accountValue = available - order_margin + sum uPnL, withdrawable, and liqPx such that re-evaluating check_cross_liquidation at liqPx flips to Some; metaAndAssetCtxs test with seeded CF_NATIVE_MARKETS asserts OI and mark/oracle fields.

**Unsure:** Did not read how CF_NATIVE_MARKETS rows are written by governance (torus-economics/src/governance.rs:1100) so StoredMarket extension may need a borsh version bump; did not confirm whether any oracle premium/EMA exists in oracle.rs beyond aggregate_price; did not check streams.rs for an existing volume aggregator. Phases B/C are consensus-breaking (new state rows, funding settlement); Phase A is RPC-only and not.

</details>

### collateral-asset

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: decimals fix ~30-60 LOC + tests; USD-stable collateral + bridge + oracle quoting ~1500-3000 LOC

Torus has no stablecoin. The only margin collateral is the chain's native EVM balance token (TRS). Lockbox::deposit_to_native takes it out of CF_ACCOUNTS (the EVM account balance) and adds it to NativeBalance{available, order_margin} in CF_NATIVE_BALANCES. All perp margin, PnL and equity are plain FixedPoint (i128, 8 decimals) values with no asset tag. So PnL is implicitly in TRS units, while order and oracle prices are unitless 8-decimal numbers that implicitly mean "quote per base", so the quote currency is TRS by default. Hyperliquid instead uses USDC as both collateral and quote, with 6 decimals on HyperCore (8 for perp sizes/prices within its rules). There is also a likely decimals mismatch: torus-economics defines TRS as 18-decimal (10,000 TRS = 10^22 wei), but lockbox fp_to_u256/u256_to_fp copy raw wei straight into FixedPoint raw (8 decimals) with no 10^10 rescale.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:45-56 FixedPoint is an i128 with DECIMALS=8, SCALE=1e8, described as 'Follows Hyperliquid's pattern'
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:147-150 NativeBalance { available: FixedPoint, order_margin: FixedPoint }: no asset/denom field, so there is one collateral
- crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:1-3,27-31 Lockbox moves 'asset' between the EVM balance and the native balance; the doc comment says 'Both sides use the same 8-decimal FixedPoint denomination'
- crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:40-55 deposit reads get_evm_balance (CF_ACCOUNTS native balance), subtracts evm_amount and adds the amount to native_bal.available
- crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:229-246 fp_to_u256 / u256_to_fp are raw identity casts with no 10^10 scaling
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5811-5858 exec_deposit_to_native/withdraw_from_native/withdraw_to take a U256 amount and call u256_to_fp, then Lockbox
- crates/torus-economics/src/types.rs:302 'Minimum self-delegation ... 10,000 TRS = 10^22 wei' means TRS has 18 decimals on the EVM side
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:122,178-184 isolated and cross margin both read positions.get_native_balance; equity = balance + unrealized PnL
- grep for usdc\|stablecoin across crates/*.rs: zero hits; grep for quote\|usd in torus-core/src/oracle.rs: zero hits

**Risk:** (1) Decimals: if EVM balances are 18-decimal wei, depositing 1 TRS (1e18 wei) credits 1e10 'whole' collateral units in FixedPoint. Margin checks, liquidation thresholds, fee and funding math then run against inflated numbers. Withdrawals round-trip consistently, so no funds are created, but the economic meaning (prices, leverage, min sizes) is off by 10^10 unless every price is also quoted in wei. (2) Parity: with volatile TRS as collateral, PnL and margin move with the TRS price as well as the perp price, so a TRS crash liquidates everyone at once. HL avoids this by settling everything in USDC. Oracle prices would need to be TRS-quoted, or there must be a USD-to-TRS conversion, and there is neither. (3) There is no stablecoin bridge or ERC20 collateral path. The Lockbox only touches the native gas balance.

**Fix:** Short term: decide what a raw unit means. Either rescale in lockbox.rs fp_to_u256/u256_to_fp (multiply/divide by 10^10, reject or keep dust below 1e-8), or document that TRS EVM balances are 8-decimal and fix economics/types.rs to match. Add a test that deposit_to_native of 1e18 wei credits FixedPoint::ONE. For HL parity: (a) add a collateral token id, e.g. a `collateral: AssetId` constant or config in MarketMarginConfig (margin.rs:61), or one chain-wide USD-stable collateral; (b) create a native USDC-like balance: either a bridged ERC20 locked through a new Lockbox::deposit_erc20_to_native that reads the ERC20 storage slot in torus-evm, or a native-ledger stable minted by a bridge validator-set attestation (like HL's Arbitrum bridge2 with validator signatures and a dispute period), with withdraw_to burning and emitting a bridge event; (c) make the oracle (torus-core/src/oracle.rs) publish USD-quoted mark/index prices so that PnL = size*(px diff) lands directly in USD collateral; (d) keep TRS for gas, staking and fees, and optionally allow TRS as non-USD collateral with a haircut later. Tests: lockbox decimals round-trip, margin equity unchanged across collateral-price moves, bridge deposit/withdraw replay protection.

**Unsure:** I did not check how CF_ACCOUNTS balances are actually scaled at genesis or in torus-evm. If genesis mints 8-decimal balances, the 'mismatch' is only an inconsistency with the 10^22-wei comment in economics/types.rs:302, not a live bug. I did not read oracle.rs beyond a grep, so how prices are quoted (TRS or USD) comes from the absence of quote/usd references, not from reading the code. I did not check torus-rpc for HL-style info endpoints that report USDC fields, and did not check whether any ERC20 or bridge contracts exist outside crates/.

</details>

**fable** — confirmed-bug, impact critical, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: Phase 1 ~80-150 LOC (lockbox conversions + callers + tests); Phase 2 stablecoin collateral + bridge ~800-1500 LOC across torus-types, torus-core/lockbox.rs, torus-evm, native_executor.rs, torus-rpc

Torus has no stablecoin collateral: the perp margin asset is the native token TRS, held in a per-address `NativeBalance { available, order_margin }` (CF_NATIVE_BALANCES) denominated in `FixedPoint` with DECIMALS=8 / SCALE=10^8. Collateral enters only via the Lockbox from the EVM account balance (TRS in wei, 18 decimals; genesis `stake_to_power` divides by 10^18), and `fp_to_u256`/`u256_to_fp` are raw-integer identity conversions, so 1 EVM TRS (10^18 wei) becomes 10^10 native collateral units — a 10^10 denomination mismatch already flagged by the Astra audit but unresolved in code. Markets carry a free-form `quote_asset: String` in `MarketListing` that is never used for settlement; oracle prices are bare `(MarketId, FixedPoint)` with no stated quote currency, so PnL, margin tiers (max_notional 100k/1M/10M "units"), and prices are all implicitly in the same unnamed 8-dec unit. HL parity (USDC-margined, USD-quoted perps, USD PnL) therefore requires both fixing the wei↔FixedPoint scale and introducing a stable quote/collateral asset.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:55-56 — FixedPoint DECIMALS=8, SCALE=100_000_000
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:145-150 — NativeBalance { available, order_margin } FixedPoint, 'separate from EVM balance'
- crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:1-4,27-31 — Lockbox moves EVM balance <-> native balance; comment claims 'Both sides use the same 8-decimal FixedPoint denomination'
- crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:40-72 — deposit_to_native: evm_amount = fp_to_u256(amount), debits CF_ACCOUNTS balance, credits native_bal.available += amount (same raw integer)
- crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:229-247 — fp_to_u256 / u256_to_fp are raw identity conversions (no 10^10 rescale)
- crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs:181-186 — get_evm_balance reads first 32 bytes of CF_ACCOUNTS as U256 (EVM wei balance)
- crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:295-301 — stake_to_power divides U256 wei by 10^18 'to get whole TRS' (EVM side is 18-dec)
- crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:209-214 — GenesisNativeBalance.available 'collateral … Scaled by 10^8'; testnet/genesis-weighted-base.json:1292-1310 pre-funds 1e12 'available' per account
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:609-613 — NativeAction::Withdraw 'Withdraw TRS to EVM address' (collateral is TRS)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5843-5858 — exec_withdraw_to: u256_to_fp(amount) then Lockbox::withdraw_from_native_to
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1164-1172 — MarketListing { base_asset, quote_asset: String, ... } quote_asset is a label only
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5747 and crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:923 — quote_asset only copied through to listing/RPC, never used in settlement
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1146-1149 — OracleSubmission { prices: Vec<(MarketId, FixedPoint)>, timestamp } no quote asset
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:24-42 — default_margin_tiers max_notional 100k/1M/10M * SCALE, unit unnamed
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:58,66 — realized_pnl / unrealized_pnl(mark_price) in FixedPoint (same unit as collateral)
- docs/audits/astra-round1-2026-09-24.md:26 — 'Wallet and lockbox disagree by a factor of 10^10' (audit finding, unresolved)

**Risk:** (1) Economic: 1 TRS deposited via Lockbox is credited as 10^10 collateral units, and withdrawal does the reverse, so any user whose native balance did not originate from a lockbox deposit (genesis native_balances, trading PnL, liquidation payouts) withdraws at a 10^10 wrong rate; margin tiers/notional caps are meaningless until the unit is fixed. (2) Parity: HL margins in USDC with USD-quoted oracle prices, so PnL is dollar-stable; Torus margins in volatile TRS with prices in an unnamed unit, meaning a TRS/USD oracle, USD-denominated PnL, and a bridged stablecoin are all absent. Any HL-compatible client/API (USDC balances, accountValue in USD) cannot map onto this without a conversion layer.

**Fix:** Phase 1 (bug): in crates/torus-core/src/lockbox.rs replace the identity `fp_to_u256`/`u256_to_fp` with explicit `wei_to_fp` (divide by 10^10, reject/handle dust) and `fp_to_wei` (multiply by 10^10), update callers in native_executor.rs (exec_deposit_to_native ~5811, exec_withdraw_to 5843, TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot) and the lockbox.rs:30 doc comment; add round-trip tests (1e18 wei -> 1e8 raw -> 1e18 wei; dust < 1e10 wei rejected) plus a genesis compatibility decision for existing native_balances. Phase 2 (parity design): add a `CollateralAsset` enum/const (USDC-like 6-dec stable vs TRS) in torus-types next to FixedPoint; introduce a stablecoin bridge path — either an ERC20 precompile/lockbox variant in torus-core/src/lockbox.rs that debits a canonical USD-stable ERC20 (torus-evm) into NativeBalance, or a native spot-token registry; make `MarketListing.quote_asset` a validated enum tied to the collateral asset and have `OracleSubmission` prices documented as quote-asset-denominated (add a TRS/USD market for native-token conversion); keep FixedPoint 8-dec but convert at the bridge boundary (USDC 6-dec -> 8-dec). Tests: margin/PnL unit tests in margin.rs and position.rs asserting notional = qty*price in quote units, and RPC types.rs exposing quote_asset consistently.

**Unsure:** Did not read exec_deposit_to_native (native_executor.rs:5811) or TransferToPerp/TransferToSpot bodies to confirm they use the same identity conversion (withdraw does). Did not verify whether the EVM precompile/wallet path parses TRS at 18 decimals in code (relied on audit line 26 and genesis stake_to_power). Did not check torus-economics for any USD-denominated fee accounting or whether a 'USD' market/oracle already exists in testnet genesis listings.

</details>

### px-sz-rules

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: 300-450 (validator ~60, meta/governance/genesis plumbing ~120, RPC ~60, tests ~150)

Torus uses fixed 8-decimal FixedPoint (SCALE=1e8) with a per-market tick_size/lot_size pair, set at listing or genesis and stored in the book meta. The only checks are in OrderBook::place_order. qty must be >= lot_size (a dust check), but qty is never required to be a multiple of lot_size. A Limit price must satisfy price.raw() % tick_size.raw() == 0, and that check is skipped for non-Limit orders and when tick_size is 0. modify_order cancels the order and re-inserts it with no tick or lot validation, so a modify can rest an off-tick price or an off-lot size. There is no szDecimals concept, no 5-significant-figure price rule, no (6 - szDecimals) / (8 - szDecimals for spot) decimals cap, and no HL-shaped meta/universe endpoint. RPC only exposes lotSize/tickSize strings in RpcMarketInfo. The InvalidTickSize/DustOrder error variants exist but are not used: rejections come back as a bare OrderStatus::Rejected with no reason.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:55-56 FixedPoint DECIMALS=8, SCALE=1e8 (HL wire uses decimal strings; any precision beyond 8dp is rejected by the parser near line 200)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:252-253 OrderBook has tick_size/lot_size fields; :329 new(market_id, tick_size, lot_size)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:376-383 dust rejection: only `params.quantity < self.lot_size`, no multiple-of-lot check
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:396-405 tick check only for OrderType::Limit and tick_size>0: `params.price.raw() % self.tick_size.raw() != 0`
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:702-775 modify_order: qty-decrease in place with no lot check; otherwise cancel_order + insert_order with new price/qty and no tick or lot validation
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5368 exec_modify_order calls book.modify_order directly; no tick/lot check in lines 5320-5368
- crates/torus-core/src/error.rs:17-35 InvalidTickSize / DustOrder variants defined; grep finds no construction sites outside error.rs
- crates/torus-rpc/src/types.rs:300-307 RpcMarketInfo {marketId, baseAsset, quoteAsset, lotSize, tickSize, status}: no szDecimals/maxLeverage/name
- crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs:190-191,278-279 market listing carries lot_size/tick_size as raw i128; crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:201-203,428-429 genesis parses them from strings ('1.0','0.01' in test at :914-915)
- grep for szDecimals\|sz_decimals\|metaAndAssetCtxs\|universe across crates: no hits

**Risk:** HL SDKs (python/TS) round prices to 5 sig figs and max (6 - szDecimals) decimals, and round sizes to szDecimals, using the szDecimals read from info.meta. Torus has no szDecimals in its metadata, so SDK clients cannot compute valid rounding. A price that HL accepts (for example 5 sig figs on a large price) is rejected here unless it happens to land on the fixed tick. Static ticks also cannot follow price scale the way HL's sig-fig rule does: a BTC tick suited to 60k is wrong at 6k. A size that is not a multiple of lot_size is accepted, so resting orders and positions can carry sub-lot precision. Modify (and probably the HL batchModify equivalent) skips both checks, so off-grid prices can rest on the book; this breaks the book invariants that integer price levels assume. Silent Rejected with no reason string breaks SDK error handling, since HL returns 'Order has invalid price' / 'Order has invalid size' style strings. Adding validation is consensus-breaking: it changes the accept/reject set, which feeds state.

**Fix:** 1) Add `sz_decimals: u8` to the market meta in torus-core/src/book_rows.rs (lines 160-215 encode/decode, add a version byte), to the governance ListMarket params (torus-economics/src/governance.rs:190-290, 1084-1096), and to the genesis market (torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:192-203, 428-441). Derive lot_size = 10^-sz_decimals so the two cannot disagree. 2) Add `fn validate_px_sz(px, sz, sz_decimals, is_spot) -> Result<(), CoreError>` in torus-core/src/order_book.rs, implementing HL rules: sz must be a multiple of 10^-szDecimals; px must have <=5 significant figures unless it is an integer; px decimals must be <= (6 or 8 for spot) - szDecimals. Make the tick check dynamic or replace it with this rule. Call it from place_order (replacing lines 376-405, and applying it to trigger/stop prices as well) and from modify_order before cancel_order (line ~758) and in the qty-decrease path. Construct CoreError::InvalidTickSize/DustOrder and return the reason to the RPC layer. 3) Add szDecimals (and name, maxLeverage) to RpcMarketInfo (torus-rpc/src/types.rs:300) and to torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:924, and add an HL-shaped info `meta` / `metaAndAssetCtxs` with `universe[{name, szDecimals, maxLeverage}]`. 4) Tests in order_book.rs tests: 5-sig-fig accept/reject table taken from HL docs (e.g. 1234.5 ok, 1234.56 rejected, 123456 integer ok, 0.0012345 with szDecimals=0 ok), off-lot size rejected, modify to an off-tick price rejected, and a migration test for book_rows meta decoding. Gate it behind a fork height for replay.

**Unsure:** Two things are unconfirmed. First, whether the executor's place path (native_executor.rs) pre-validates px/sz before OrderBook::place_order: I only checked the modify path at 5320-5368. Second, whether stop/trigger prices get any tick check: the place_order tick check is gated on OrderType::Limit, so they are likely unchecked. I did not read the governance listing executor (native_executor.rs ~5700-5750) closely enough to confirm whether it rejects tick_size/lot_size <= 0. Only a grep turned up no check there. I did not check spot markets or whether an HL-compatible /info endpoint exists under another name. I did not read the HL-compat order wire (if any) that converts string px/sz to FixedPoint.

</details>

**fable** — partial, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: ~150-250 LOC (types+book+borsh+executor validation+rpc field+tests)

Torus has a single global 10^8 FixedPoint (torus-types) and per-market `tick_size`/`lot_size` FixedPoints set at listing (MarketListing) and stored on OrderBook. Enforcement in OrderBook::place_order is: reject if `quantity < lot_size` (a minimum, NOT a lot-multiple check), and reject if `price.raw() % tick_size.raw() != 0` — but only for OrderType::Limit; Market, StopMarket trigger and StopLimit limit/trigger prices are never tick-checked. There is no szDecimals concept, no "5 significant figures" price rule, no `(6 - szDecimals)` decimal cap, no rounding helper, and no validation that a listing's tick/lot are positive or powers of ten. RPC `RpcMarketInfo` exposes `lotSize`/`tickSize` as decimal strings but no `szDecimals`, so an HL SDK cannot derive its rounding from the Torus meta endpoint.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:52-56 — `pub struct FixedPoint(i128)`, `DECIMALS = 8`, `SCALE = 100_000_000`: one global precision for both px and sz, no per-asset decimals
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1060-1069 — PlaceOrderParams carries price/quantity as FixedPoint; no decimals/precision metadata
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1165-1172 — MarketListing { tick_size, lot_size, max_leverage, maintenance_margin_bps }: no sz_decimals field
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:376-384 — dust check `params.quantity < self.lot_size` (minimum only; quantity need not be a multiple of lot_size)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:396-406 — tick check `price.raw() % tick_size.raw() != 0` gated on `matches!(order_type, OrderType::Limit)` and `tick_size > ZERO`; non-Limit prices and trigger prices bypass
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:252-253,329-338 — tick_size/lot_size are plain fields on OrderBook, set in `new()`
- crates/torus-rpc/src/types.rs:299-307 — RpcMarketInfo { marketId, baseAsset, quoteAsset, lotSize, tickSize, status }: no szDecimals / maxDecimals
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:924-925 — lotSize/tickSize rendered via dec_fp from raw i128
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5744-5749 — ProposalAction::ListMarket passes listing.tick_size/lot_size straight through (no validation seen at that site)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4906+ — exec_place_order does margin reserve/rejection but no px/sz precision checks (delegates to OrderBook)

**Risk:** HL SDKs (hyperliquid-python-sdk, rust SDK) round px to 5 sig figs and sz to szDecimals from the `meta` endpoint before signing; against Torus they have no szDecimals to read and tick/lot semantics differ (lot is a floor not a grid; tick ignored for stop/market prices). Result: orders that HL would accept get rejected (e.g. qty 1.5 with lot 1.0 accepted here but HL would reject; price with 7 sig figs passes Torus tick check if tick is 1e-8). Also a stop-limit with an off-tick limit price enters the book unaligned, breaking price-level invariants and parity. Unvalidated listing tick/lot (zero or non-power-of-ten) silently disables the checks.

**Fix:** 1) Add `sz_decimals: u8` (and optionally `max_px_decimals`) to `MarketListing` (torus-types/src/lib.rs:1165) and to `OrderBook` (order_book.rs:252) plus borsh ser/de at order_book.rs:2503/2552 and book_rows.rs:160. 2) In torus-core add `fn validate_px_sz(price, qty, sz_decimals, is_limit) -> Result<(), OrderError>`: sz must be a multiple of 10^(8-sz_decimals); px must have <=5 significant figures and <= (6 - sz_decimals) decimals (integer prices exempt from sig-fig rule, as HL does); call it from `OrderBook::place_order` before line 376, applying the tick/px check to StopLimit.limit, StopMarket/StopLimit.trigger, and Market limit-price if present (not just Limit). Change dust check to `qty.raw() % lot_size.raw() != 0` in addition to `< lot_size`. 3) Validate at listing time (native_executor.rs:5744 / wherever ListMarket is applied) that tick_size and lot_size are positive powers of ten consistent with sz_decimals. 4) Expose `szDecimals` (and `maxLeverage`) in `RpcMarketInfo` (torus-rpc/src/types.rs:299) so an HL `meta`-shaped response can be built. Tests: order_book.rs tests near 3759/3830 — add cases: qty 1.5 w/ lot 1.0 rejected; px 12345.6 w/ szDecimals 2 rejected (6 sig figs); px 123456 integer accepted; StopLimit with off-tick limit rejected; RPC test asserting szDecimals in getMarkets.

**Unsure:** Did not read FixedPoint::from_str (torus-types/src/lib.rs:181) to confirm whether decimal-string parsing truncates or rejects >8 decimals; did not find the ListMarket apply path that could validate tick/lot (grep at native_executor 5744 only shows passthrough); did not check whether EVM CoreWriter PlaceOrder path or RPC submit path performs any extra rounding before reaching OrderBook. Exact HL rule nuance (integer prices exempt from 5-sig-fig; spot uses 8 - szDecimals) stated from HL docs, not verified live.

</details>

### market-metadata

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: 250-450

Torus keeps market metadata in CF_NATIVE_MARKETS. Each entry is keyed by a u64 market_id and holds borsh(base_asset, quote_asset, lot_size_raw, tick_size_raw, initial_margin_raw). torus_getMarkets returns {market_id (hex), base_asset, quote_asset, lot_size, tick_size, status}, and status is always the hardcoded string "active". Hyperliquid's meta fields do not exist. There is no name/symbol string such as "BTC", no szDecimals (Torus uses a FixedPoint lot_size), no maxLeverage, no onlyIsolated, and no dense asset index (the u64 market_id plays that role). initial_margin is stored but the RPC never reads it (dead_code). maxLeverage lives only in the runtime MarketMarginConfig and the governance MarketListing type. In the executor, margin_configs starts as an empty HashMap and no non-test code inserts into it, so every market falls back to 20x in reserve_for_qty_cfg. The testnet genesis (testnet/genesis-weighted-base.json) seeds 100 USD-quoted perps: ids 1-10 are BTC, ETH, SOL, AVAX, ARB, OP, DOGE, LINK, MATIC and APT, and ids 11-100 are synthetic S11..S100. The genesis note says their tick and lot values are cosmetic.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:189-206 GenesisMarket {market_id u64, base_asset, quote_asset, lot_size, tick_size, initial_margin}; the doc comment says CF_NATIVE_MARKETS is OFF the consensus state root
- crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:424-451 seeds CF_NATIVE_MARKETS with the borsh layout that must match RPC StoredMarket and governance MarketListing
- crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:667-684 test asserts 100 markets with ids 1..=100 (1-10 named, 11-100 synthetic S11..S100)
- testnet/genesis-weighted-base.json:337-350 market 1 BTC/USD lot 1.0 tick 1.0 initial_margin 5.0; note says 'tick/lot cosmetic, runtime order book auto-creates tick=lot=1.0'; 100 market_id entries in total
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:55-62 StoredMarket; initial_margin_raw is #[allow(dead_code)]
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:114-119, 880-930 get_markets(offset, limit) scans CF_NATIVE_MARKETS, max 500 per page, status hardcoded 'active'
- crates/torus-rpc/src/types.rs:300-307 RpcMarketInfo {market_id, base_asset, quote_asset, lot_size, tick_size, status}
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1165-1172 MarketListing {base_asset, quote_asset, tick_size, lot_size, max_leverage, maintenance_margin_bps}
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:24-44 default tiers 50x/20x/10x/5x by notional; 60-79 MarketMarginConfig {max_leverage, maintenance_factor_bps 5000, tiers}
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1842 margin_configs: HashMap::new(); a grep found no non-test inserts; 4813-4816 unwrap_or(20) fallback
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:511,548 EVM precompile getMarkets() returns only (bytes32[] ids, bool[] active)

**Risk:** Hyperliquid clients and SDKs expect info{type:"meta"} to return a universe[{name, szDecimals, maxLeverage, onlyIsolated}], where the position in the array is the asset index. Torus provides none of these fields, so an HL-compatible frontend cannot round sizes or prices and cannot display or enforce leverage limits. Leverage set per market in genesis or by governance (MarketListing.max_leverage) apparently never reaches the executor, which always uses a flat 20x for reserves while the default tiers allow up to 50x for liquidation. The metadata CF sits outside the consensus root, so validators can quietly disagree on metadata. Tick and lot values are cosmetic, so what the RPC reports may not match what the book enforces.

**Fix:** 1) Extend GenesisMarket in torus-genesis/src/lib.rs, StoredMarket in torus-rpc/src/torus.rs and MarketListing in torus-types/src/lib.rs with max_leverage: u32, sz_decimals: u8 (or derive it from lot_size) and only_isolated: bool. Version the borsh layout, for example by appending fields and reading them with a fallback. 2) At executor init, load CF_NATIVE_MARKETS into NativeExecContext.margin_configs (native_executor.rs:1842) as MarketMarginConfig::new(id, max_leverage). Apply governance ListMarket (native_executor.rs:5744) to the same map. 3) Make the order book use the stored tick and lot instead of auto-creating tick=lot=1.0. 4) Add name (base-quote), szDecimals, maxLeverage, onlyIsolated and a real status to RpcMarketInfo, and optionally add an HL-shaped torus_meta endpoint that returns universe[] ordered by market_id. 5) Consider moving market metadata into the consensus-rooted state. Tests: a genesis round-trip of the new fields, an RPC get_markets test (lib.rs:2791) asserting the new fields, and an executor test showing that a market with max_leverage=5 reserves notional/5.

**Unsure:** I did not read where the order book auto-creates tick=lot=1.0, so the claim that tick and lot are not enforced relies on the genesis note. A grep found no non-test code that inserts into margin_configs, but a mutation through a helper such as entry() or a setter could have been missed. I did not inspect the devnet/ genesis files (the listing showed only bench scripts) or the full governance MarketListing execution path. I also did not check how isolated-margin mentions in position.rs/margin.rs relate to an onlyIsolated flag.

</details>

### exec-timestamps

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: 250-450 (header field + canonical bytes + validate rules + ctx rename + order_book/fill/RPC plumbing + tests)

Execution uses one clock: `TorusBlockHeader.timestamp`, a u64 in whole UNIX seconds. The proposer sets it from its own wall clock with `SystemTime::now().as_secs()` in `build_proposal`. I found no check in `validate_block` or anywhere else in torus-consensus that a block's timestamp is later than its parent's or within some allowed drift, so a proposer can pick any value. That seconds value goes straight into `NativeExecContext.timestamp` and into `batch_verify_native_actions_cached`. Everything else is in milliseconds, as on Hyperliquid: the nonce window (`NONCE_WINDOW_MS` = 60,000, ±60s), session expiry (`MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS`, and `created_at`/`expiry` stored in ms) and mempool eviction. So the executor converts with `ctx.timestamp * 1000`, which only gives 1-second precision. Order-book placement, matching, oracle price submission and fill rows all use the seconds value. Hyperliquid uses a millisecond block time, so we are behind it in two ways: precision is 1000x coarser, and we have no limit on proposer-chosen timestamps.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:4734-4737 build_proposal: `let timestamp = SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or_default().as_secs();` — the proposer's local wall clock, in seconds
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:4785-4790 the header is built with `timestamp,`, taken without change from the proposer's clock
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1680 batch_verify_native_actions_cached(&native_actions, torus_block.header.timestamp, ...) — the header seconds are passed to signature, session and nonce verification
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1857,1870 NativeExecContext::new_with_mode/new_env(..., torus_block.header.timestamp, ...)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1365 `pub timestamp: u64` (block metadata in NativeExecContext)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5606-5610 CreateSession: `let now_ms = ctx.timestamp.saturating_mul(1000); if expiry > now_ms + MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS ... if expiry <= now_ms` — seconds times 1000, so session timestamps only have 1-second precision
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5647 created_at: now_ms
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:4968 book.place_order(params, sender, ctx.timestamp) and :3842 match_parallel(worker_batches, ctx.timestamp) — order and fill timestamps are in seconds
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5716 oracle submit_price(..., ctx.block_height, ctx.timestamp)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3203 encode_block(ctx.fills_block, ctx.timestamp, ...) — fill rows carry seconds
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:27 `pub const NONCE_WINDOW_MS: u64 = 60_000;`
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:742 MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS = 24h in ms
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:845-866 validate(current_time_ms): nonce must be within ±NONCE_WINDOW_MS of current_time_ms
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:832 resolve_sender: `if current_timestamp > session.expiry { SessionExpired }` — session.expiry is stored in ms
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:1056,1066 batch_verify_native_actions_cached(timestamp: u64) passes `timestamp` unchanged to batch_verify_impl; the parameter name has no unit
- crates/torus-mempool/src/native_pool.rs:454-459 evict_expired(now_ms) uses NONCE_WINDOW_MS (the mempool side works in ms)
- grep for timestamp checks in crates/torus-consensus/src (header.timestamp compared with the parent, drift, MAX_FUTURE) found nothing outside the uses listed above; validate_block is at app.rs:4915
- a grep for funding_rate or twap in crates/*/src matched only torus-types (the max_funding_rate_bps market param at eip712.rs:1161); no funding or TWAP scheduler appears in torus-core, torus-bridge or torus-economics

**Risk:** (1) The proposer controls the clock with no limit. A byzantine leader can set the timestamp far in the past or future. Because batch verify checks the ±60s nonce window and session expiry against this value, it can censor or re-admit actions in bulk, keep expired sessions alive, or skew order and fill timestamps and oracle price times. Timestamps can also go backwards between blocks. (2) Possible unit mismatch (not verified): if batch_verify_impl passes the seconds-based header timestamp straight into the nonce check or `current_timestamp > session.expiry` without multiplying by 1000, then seconds (~1.7e9) are compared with ms values (~1.7e12). Every nonce would look too far in the future, and sessions would never expire during execution. Native actions apparently do execute today, so a *1000 probably happens inside batch_verify_impl, but I did not read that code. (3) Precision: with second resolution, every fill in a block shares one timestamp, while Hyperliquid fills carry ms time. Session `created_at` and expiry checks are rounded to the second. Anything that fires on a time boundary (hourly funding, TWAP slices every 30s, order expiry) can be off by up to 999ms, and by much more if the proposer skews the clock. RPC/WS consumers that expect HL-style ms `time` fields get seconds*1000 or plain seconds. (4) I found no funding or TWAP schedule driven by block time. When those are added, they will inherit both problems.

**Fix:** 1) Move the header to milliseconds. Add `timestamp_ms: u64` to TorusBlockHeader, or redefine `timestamp` as ms and gate the change by height or fork. Set it in build_proposal (app.rs:4734) with `.as_millis() as u64`, clamped to `max(now_ms, parent.timestamp_ms + 1)`. Include it in `canonical_header_bytes`. 2) Add timestamp rules in validate_block / validate_block_for_sync (app.rs:4915/4953): reject when `ts <= parent.ts` (strictly increasing) or `ts > local_now_ms + MAX_FUTURE_DRIFT_MS` (e.g. 2-5s); optionally also reject `ts < parent.ts + MIN_BLOCK_INTERVAL`. Sync replay should check only that timestamps increase, not drift against the local clock. 3) Name the unit everywhere. Rename `NativeExecContext.timestamp` to `timestamp_ms` (native_executor.rs:1365) and drop the `* 1000` at :5606. Rename the `timestamp` parameter of `batch_verify_native_actions_cached` (eip712.rs:1056) to `now_ms`, and check that batch_verify_impl compares the nonce window and `session.expiry` in ms. 4) Order-book `timestamp` (order_book.rs:45/60), fill rows (encode_block at native_executor.rs:3203) and the oracle submit_price get ms values. RPC `time` fields then pass them through unchanged, as HL does. 5) Future funding and TWAP: schedule from `timestamp_ms` boundaries, e.g. `floor(ts_ms/3_600_000)` changing between parent and child triggers funding settlement, with catch-up when a block skips more than one boundary. Do not schedule from block height. Tests: a proposal timestamp equal to the parent's or behind it is rejected; a future-drift proposal is rejected; a nonce at exactly ±60,000ms from the block's ms time passes, one ms beyond fails; a session that expired 1ms before the block time is rejected during execution; a determinism test replaying with mixed ms timestamps.

**Unsure:** I did not read batch_verify_impl (eip712.rs after ~1100), so I do not know whether it multiplies the seconds header timestamp by 1000 before the NONCE_WINDOW_MS check and the session.expiry check at eip712.rs:832. Native actions apparently execute, which suggests it does, but the call site passes plain header seconds, and the `* 1000` at native_executor.rs:5606 suggests ctx.timestamp is in seconds. Not verified: whether hotstuff_rs or another layer, outside the grep I ran, checks timestamps in validate_block (I read only its line number at app.rs:4915, not its body); the units of order_book.rs timestamps and RPC `time` fields; whether funding or TWAP logic exists under names other than funding_rate/twap/funding_interval (my grep found none in torus-core, torus-bridge or torus-economics).

</details>

**fable** — confirmed-bug, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: A: ~10 LOC + tests; B+C+D: ~150-250 LOC across app.rs, native_executor.rs, eip712.rs, torus-evm executor.rs, RPC serializers, plus tests

Execution uses header.timestamp, a u64 in SECONDS set by the proposer from local wall clock (SystemTime::now().as_secs()) in build_proposal; validate_block performs no timestamp check at all (no parent-monotonicity, no drift bound, no future bound), so the proposer's clock is trusted unconditionally. Session expiry and nonces are MILLISECOND quantities (MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS, NONCE_WINDOW_MS=60_000). create_session correctly scales ctx.timestamp*1000, but the in-block session-key verify path passes raw header.timestamp (seconds) into batch_verify_native_actions_cached, which compares `timestamp <= session.expiry` (ms) -- seconds are ~1000x smaller than any ms expiry, so expired session keys are never rejected during block execution. The nonce window is enforced only in the mempool against local wall-clock ms, not against block time, so execution has no deterministic nonce-time check. No funding or TWAP scheduling code exists in torus-core/torus-bridge/torus-consensus (grep for funding/twap hits only torus-types), so there is nothing to compare to HL's ms-scheduled funding/TWAP.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:4734-4737 — build_proposal sets timestamp = SystemTime::now()...as_secs() (proposer local clock, seconds)
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:4915-4950 — validate_block body contains zero references to timestamp (grep count 0): no bound/monotonic check
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1678-1680 — batch_verify_native_actions_cached(&torus_block.native_actions, torus_block.header.timestamp, ...) passes seconds
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:1074-1076,1148-1149 — batch_verify_native_actions_cached_with_mode(timestamp) does `timestamp <= session.expiry` with expiry in ms
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5600-5611 — create_session comment says block timestamp is SECONDS; now_ms = ctx.timestamp*1000 compared to expiry/MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:27,742 — NONCE_WINDOW_MS=60_000, MAX_SESSION_EXPIRY_MS=24h ms
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:845-863 — validate(current_time_ms) nonce window check in ms
- crates/torus-mempool/src/lib.rs:439-471 — mempool nonce window uses SystemTime::now() local ms, not block time
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:103-105 — comment confirms the 60s nonce window gates mempool only
- crates/torus-evm/src/executor.rs:533 — EVM block.timestamp = cfg.timestamp (seconds, EVM-conventional)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3842,4968 — matching/place_order consume ctx.timestamp (seconds)

**Risk:** (1) Expired session keys remain valid for in-block signature verification indefinitely (seconds vs ms comparison at eip712.rs:1149) -- a security hole: a leaked 24h session key never stops working at execution. (2) Proposer can set any timestamp with no validator bound; since session expiry, order timestamps and fills use it, a malicious/buggy proposer can skew time (also feeds EVM block.timestamp). (3) Nonce window is non-deterministic (mempool wall clock), so validators may disagree on tx admission; HL enforces nonce window against block time in ms. (4) Second precision vs HL's ms timestamps makes trade/fill timestamps coarser than HL API consumers expect (HL returns ms `time` fields). Funding/TWAP are absent entirely, so the schedule question is moot until implemented.

**Fix:** A) Fix the unit bug: in app.rs:1680/1857/1870 pass `header.timestamp.saturating_mul(1000)` (or better, convert header.timestamp to ms at the source). Add a test in eip712.rs: session with expiry = now_ms - 1 must be rejected by batch_verify_native_actions_cached when given block seconds. B) Switch header.timestamp to ms: change build_proposal (app.rs:4734) to .as_millis() as u64, drop the *1000 in native_executor.rs:5606, divide by 1000 when populating torus_evm cfg.timestamp (executor.rs:533), and update the ctx.timestamp consumers (place_order, match_parallel, encode_block fills_ts) plus RPC trade/fill serializers; bump header schema/migration. C) Add proposer timestamp bounds in validate_block (app.rs:4915): require timestamp >= parent.timestamp and timestamp <= local_now + MAX_DRIFT (e.g. HL-like few seconds), rejecting otherwise; tests: monotonic violation and future-drift rejection. D) Make nonce window deterministic: apply SignedNativeAction::validate(current_time_ms = header ms) in the execution path (native_executor) rather than only mempool, so all validators agree. E) Funding/TWAP: when implemented, key schedules off header ms (HL: hourly funding, TWAP 30s slices) in torus-core.

Did not confirm whether any later executor step re-checks session expiry in ms (resolve_sender at eip712.rs:801-832 does `current_timestamp > session.expiry` but I did not trace its in-block caller/unit).
