### oracle-spam

**opus** — partial, impact medium, effort S, lockstep yes · LOC: 60-120 including tests

Only an active (non-jailed) registered validator can submit: exec_submit_oracle_prices checks staking.get_validator(sender), so ordinary users can't spam this action. Nothing is charged for it. The handler returns a flat gas_used=1000 no matter how many prices are in the submission, and ctx.total_native_fees is never incremented anywhere in native_executor.rs (it is set to 0 and then only read). There is no per-validator, per-block limit and no cap on `prices` length. Market IDs are not checked against listed markets. Storage is keyed by (market_id, validator, block_number), so repeats in the same block overwrite each other. But a validator can write rows for arbitrary nonexistent market IDs. Those rows are never pruned, because pruning only happens inside collect_submissions for markets that get aggregated, at most 100 keys per call. So a malicious or compromised validator key can grow CF_NATIVE_ORACLE without bound at zero cost. This differs from Hyperliquid, where validators publish oracle prices on a fixed cadence (roughly every 3 seconds), one vote per validator per asset, and only for listed perp assets.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3276-3281 dispatch SubmitOraclePrices -> exec_submit_oracle_prices (submission timestamp is ignored)
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5685-5720 checks only that the validator exists and has status Active; loops over every (market_id, price) with no length cap and no listed-market check; returns ok(..., 1000) as a flat gas figure
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1374,1853,5995 total_native_fees is declared, set to 0 and read at the epoch boundary, but never incremented (grep found no += and no assignment)
- torus-core/src/oracle.rs:181-196 submit_price writes put_cf_raw(CF_NATIVE_ORACLE, key(market, validator, block)) with no validation
- torus-core/src/oracle.rs:300-335 collect_submissions prunes old rows only for the market being aggregated, prune_limit=100 per call
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5902-5913 aggregate_oracle_prices runs only over the `markets` slice it is given (listed markets), so rows for unlisted market IDs are never pruned
- torus-types/src/lib.rs:1146-1149 OracleSubmission { prices: Vec<(MarketId, FixedPoint)>, timestamp } has no length bound; the encoding at lib.rs:870-877 writes the length as u32
- torus-mempool/src/rate_limit.rs:180 NATIVE_PER_SENDER_CAP=512 caps pending actions per sender in the pool; this is the only per-sender throttle found

**Risk:** A single validator key (stolen, compromised, or malicious) can send up to 512 pending submissions per sender per block, each with an unbounded `prices` vector. That costs nothing and permanently grows CF_NATIVE_ORACLE through junk market IDs, which bloats state and snapshots. It also adds iterate_cf cost per market prefix. Within real markets, one validator only ever affects its own latest row (latest_per_validator), so the effect on aggregation is limited. The weighted median, outlier rejection and the single-reporter 10% bound also limit price manipulation. The main issue is unbounded storage growth and block-space spam.

**Fix:** 1) In exec_submit_oracle_prices (native_executor.rs:5685), reject the submission when prices.len() is greater than the number of listed markets, or above a constant such as MAX_ORACLE_PRICES_PER_SUBMISSION = 256 in torus-types, also enforced at RPC ingress. Reject duplicate market IDs, and reject any market_id that isn't a listed market (use the same listed-markets source that feeds aggregate_oracle_prices). Also reject price <= 0. 2) Allow one submission per validator per block: keep a ctx-scoped HashSet<Address> of validators that have already submitted and reject repeats. That makes it deterministic and matches Hyperliquid's one vote per validator per round. 3) Prune per validator on write: before put_cf_raw, delete that validator's earlier rows for the market. Or change the key to (market, validator) only, holding the latest submission, which makes storage O(markets x validators). 4) Decide on fees: either keep oracle submissions free, as Hyperliquid does for validator oracle votes, but take them out of NATIVE_PER_SENDER_CAP accounting and give them a dedicated per-block slot, or charge real gas. Separately, the fact that total_native_fees is never incremented affects every native action and is its own finding. Tests to add: an unlisted market_id is rejected; a second submission in the same block is rejected; a submission over the length cap is rejected; storage row count stays constant across N blocks for a fixed validator set.

**Unsure:** I did not confirm whether an agent/session key signing for a validator address resolves to that validator as `sender` for SubmitOraclePrices; I found no agent-scope check in the grep. If agent keys can act for validators, a leaked session key can spam this action too. I did not find where app.rs calls aggregate_oracle_prices or how it builds the markets list. I also did not check whether the mempool or RPC rejects SubmitOraclePrices from non-validators before they reach a block; non-validator submissions fail at exec but may still use block space.

</details>

**fable** — partial, impact medium, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: ~120-180 lines across native_executor.rs, oracle.rs, lib.rs, rate_limit.rs plus tests

SubmitOraclePrices is gated only on the sender being a registered Active validator (exec_submit_oracle_prices, native_executor.rs:5690-5710); each (market, price) pair is written unconditionally to CF_NATIVE_ORACLE under key "sub"+market_id+validator+block_number (oracle.rs:139-144, 196-199). There is no fee or balance debit on this path — the handler returns NativeActionResult::ok("submit_oracle_prices", 1000) with no charge code anywhere (grep for native action fee hit nothing), and no oracle-specific per-validator-per-block limit exists; the only caps are the generic proposer-local mempool ones (NATIVE_PER_BLOCK_CAP=64 actions/sender/block, NATIVE_PER_SENDER_CAP=512 pending; rate_limit.rs:58,180), which validate_block does not enforce. Storage per block is bounded to one key per (market, validator) because repeat submissions in the same block overwrite the same key, but a validator can submit for arbitrary market_ids (no market-exists check in the handler), creating unbounded "sub"+bogus_market keys; pruning happens only lazily inside collect_submissions for the market being aggregated, max 100 keys per call (oracle.rs:325-331), so junk-market keys are never pruned. Session keys: SessionScope::Trading and TransfersOnly exclude SubmitOraclePrices (lib.rs:263-275), but Full is documented as "everything except CreateSession/RevokeSession/Withdraw/staking" (lib.rs:249-250), so a Full-scope session key of a validator address can submit oracle prices.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5685-5721 — exec_submit_oracle_prices: only checks ctx.staking.get_validator(sender).status == Active, then loops submit_price per pair, returns ok(...,1000); no fee, no count/market check
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:139-144 — submission_key = "sub"+market_id(8)+validator(20)+block_number(8); same-block resubmits overwrite
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:178-199 — submit_price: borsh-serializes and put_cf_raw unconditionally, no validation of market existence or price sanity
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:296-333 — collect_submissions iterates whole market prefix each aggregation, prunes <=100 stale keys per call (prune_limit=100); only invoked from aggregate_price
- crates/torus-core/src/oracle.rs:117-129 — OracleConfig: max_oracle_age=100, min_oracle_reporters=3, aggregation_window=10
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5905-5915 — aggregate_oracle_prices iterates only listed `markets`, so submissions under unlisted market_ids are never read or pruned
- crates/torus-mempool/src/rate_limit.rs:57-70 — NATIVE_PER_BLOCK_CAP=64 per sender per block, proposer-local, env-overridable, validate_block does not reject on it
- crates/torus-mempool/src/rate_limit.rs:177-180 — NATIVE_PER_SENDER_CAP=512 pending per sender
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:242-275 — SessionScope: Trading/TransfersOnly exclude SubmitOraclePrices; Full documented to allow everything except session/withdraw/staking
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6164-6201 — ActionCategory::Oracle used only for block ordering (post-EVM), not for fee/limit

**Risk:** A single active validator (or anyone holding a Full-scope session key for a validator address) can push up to 64 SubmitOraclePrices actions per block, each carrying an unbounded prices Vec (bounded only by block byte cap of 12MB), with no fee. Per listed market the state growth is bounded (1 key per validator per block, pruned lazily at 100/aggregation — which can lag behind a 64-actions/block writer across many validators), but for arbitrary unlisted market_ids the keys are never pruned, so CF_NATIVE_ORACLE grows without bound; also each aggregation does a full prefix scan, so a market flooded with history keys from many validators raises per-block execution time. Hyperliquid's oracle is validator-internal (not a user-signed action), so parity requires this path to be gas-metered or structurally limited.

**Fix:** 1) In exec_submit_oracle_prices (native_executor.rs:5685): reject if prices.len() > N (e.g. number of listed markets) and reject market_ids not in ctx's listed-market set (reuse whatever market registry aggregate_oracle_prices' `markets` slice comes from); dedupe market_ids. 2) Add a per-block idempotency check: in OracleManager::submit_price (oracle.rs:178) return CoreError if submission_key already exists for (market, validator, block_number), or have the executor track a `oracle_submitted: HashSet<Address>` per block in NativeExecContext and reject second submission. 3) Charge a flat native action fee or bump the nonce-weighted cost for ActionCategory::Oracle at the mempool admission layer (rate_limit.rs) with a dedicated ORACLE_PER_SENDER_PER_BLOCK_CAP=1. 4) Make SessionScope::Full.allows (lib.rs:255) exclude SubmitOraclePrices (validator-only signer). 5) Prune eagerly: in submit_price delete the key at block_number - max_oracle_age for the same (market, validator) (O(1)) instead of relying on the 100/aggregation lazy prune. Tests: native_executor tests for duplicate-in-block rejection, unlisted market rejection, oversized vec rejection; oracle.rs test that key count per (market,validator) stays <= aggregation_window+1 after 1000 blocks; lib.rs test that Full scope denies SubmitOraclePrices.

**Unsure:** Did not read SessionScope::Full match arm body (lib.rs ~276-290) to confirm it literally allows SubmitOraclePrices — inferred from the doc comment at lib.rs:249-250. Did not confirm whether any upstream (RPC/mempool admission or app.rs) charges a native action fee or nonce cost; grep for fee-charging in bridge/app found nothing, but torus-economics or torus-rpc may debit elsewhere. Did not verify where/how often app.rs calls aggregate_oracle_prices (per block vs on demand), which determines how often the lazy prune runs. Did not check whether the EIP-712 verify path restricts SubmitOraclePrices to validator signers before execution.

</details>

### eip712-replay

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: ~150-300 LOC (signature threading across ~10 call sites, plus tests and SDK signer)

Native actions are signed under one fixed EIP-712 domain, `{name:"Torus", version:"1", chainId:7778, verifyingContract:0x0}`, built by `eip712_domain_separator()`. Every recovery path uses it: ECDSA recover, ed25519 session verify and `resolve_sender`. Because the domain is a compile-time constant with no network field, a signature made for any Torus network (testnet, devnet, mainnet) is valid on all of them, as long as the nonce (a timestamp in ms) is within ±60s and the same account or session key exists on the other network. In a different way, the node cannot run under any other chainId. `validate()` only checks that the configured genesis chain_id equals the constant 7778, so a network with a distinct id would reject every native action instead of using its own domain. Replay from other EVM chains is blocked (different domain name and chainId; HL uses 1337). There is no HL-style split between L1 actions (phantom agent with source "a"/"b" for mainnet/testnet) and user-signed actions (signatureChainId plus hyperliquidChain "Mainnet"/"Testnet" in the struct).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:7 doc: Domain { name: "Torus", version: "1", chainId: 7778, verifyingContract: 0x0 }
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:24 pub const TORUS_CHAIN_ID: u64 = 7778 (compile-time constant, not configurable)
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:163-175 eip712_domain_separator() hardcodes "Torus", "1", TORUS_CHAIN_ID, Address::ZERO; takes no network parameter
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:764-770, 786-788, 811-813, 826-828: recover_sender / verify_session_signature / resolve_sender all call eip712_domain_separator() (ed25519 session sigs are domain-bound too, which is good)
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:848-857 validate(): `if expected_chain_id != TORUS_CHAIN_ID` returns ChainIdMismatch. It compares the node config to the constant and does not put the configured id into the domain
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:860-865 nonce freshness: within +-NONCE_WINDOW_MS (60_000) of current time
- crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:512,533 mempool chain_id = chain_config.chain_id from genesis, so a genesis with chain_id != 7778 makes the mempool reject all native actions
- crates/torus-evm/src/executor.rs:19 separate EVM TORUS_CHAIN_ID = 7778 (EVM txs use EIP-155 with the same id, also shared across networks)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:370, proposer.rs:210, consensus/app.rs:1678,4633: consensus-path verification (resolve_sender / batch_verify_native_actions[_cached]) uses the same fixed domain and does not check chain id

**Risk:** Testnet to mainnet replay: a user who uses the same key on testnet and mainnet (common with HL-style wallets) signs testnet orders, withdrawals or transfers whose signatures are valid byte-for-byte on mainnet. Anyone watching the testnet mempool or RPC can resubmit them to mainnet within the 60s nonce window. That covers withdrawals and transfers if those are native actions; requires_eip712 actions still recover the same address. The same applies between any two Torus deployments (devnets, forks, bench clusters). HL prevents this with source "a" (mainnet) vs "b" (testnet) inside the phantom-agent hash for L1 actions, and with hyperliquidChain "Mainnet"/"Testnet" in user-signed actions. Separately, the hardcoded constant means a distinct testnet chainId cannot be configured at all: genesis with any other id bricks native-action intake in the mempool. EVM txs also share chain id 7778 across networks, which is the standard EIP-155 cross-network replay problem.

**Fix:** Minimal option (A): make the domain depend on the network. Change `eip712_domain_separator()` to `eip712_domain_separator(chain_id: u64)` (or cache it per chain_id in a OnceLock map). Thread chain_id from genesis `chain_config.chain_id` (torus-types/src/lib.rs:1223) through `recover_sender`, `verify_session_signature`, `resolve_sender`, `batch_verify_native_actions[_cached]`, `sign_native_action[_with_session]`, and the call sites in consensus/app.rs:1678,4633, bridge/validator.rs:370, bridge/proposer.rs:210, rpc/torus.rs:1954 and the mempool. Remove the `expected_chain_id != TORUS_CHAIN_ID` guard in validate/validate_with_sessions (lines 852, 880), since the domain itself now enforces the chain. Assign distinct ids per network (e.g. mainnet 7778, testnet 7779) and make torus-evm's TORUS_CHAIN_ID come from genesis too. HL-parity option (B): add a `source`/network byte to the struct hash, in the style of HL's phantom agent `Agent{source:string,connectionId:bytes32}` with "a"/"b", and add a `hyperliquidChain`-style field to user-signed transfer and withdraw types. Tests: (1) a signature made with the testnet domain fails `recover_sender` under the mainnet domain (recovers a different address, so the action is rejected); (2) a genesis with chain_id 7779 accepts actions signed for 7779; (3) the cross-domain vector is pinned in action_hash_scratch_tests.rs. This changes consensus: every signing hash changes, so it needs a coordinated fork or genesis reset, plus SDK and client signer updates.

**Unsure:** I did not check whether the executor keeps a per-account nonce set (HL keeps the 100 highest nonces). Without one, replay within the 60s window is possible even on a single chain. I also did not check whether any testnet genesis or config in the repo uses a chain_id other than 7778 (if one does, its native-action intake would already be broken). I did not inspect which NativeAction variants (withdraw/transfer) are in requires_eip712, or the RPC/SDK signer code paths. EVM-side replay protection (EIP-155 on 7778) was not checked beyond the constant.

</details>

**fable** — partial, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: ~120-200 LOC across eip712.rs (signature threading), app.rs (2 call sites + struct field), torus.rs (2 call sites), bench, plus ~60 LOC tests

The native-action EIP-712 domain is a compile-time constant: name "Torus", version "1", chainId 7778, verifyingContract 0x0 (crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:163-175, TORUS_CHAIN_ID at :24). There is no testnet/mainnet discriminator anywhere in the signed payload (no HL-style `source: "a"/"b"` field, no genesis-derived domain), so a signature produced for any Torus network (devnet, testnet, mainnet) verifies identically on every other Torus network with the same action and nonce — cross-network replay is possible within the +/-60s nonce window. Cross-chain replay from foreign EVM chains is not possible because 7778 and the "Torus"/"1" name-version are baked into the separator; the inverse (a Torus native-action signature replayed to another chain) is likewise domain-bound. Separately, the `validate`/`validate_with_sessions` chain-ID guard (eip712.rs:852, :880) only compares the node's configured chain_id against the hardcoded 7778 (it does not change the domain), and the consensus/exec batch path `batch_verify_native_actions_cached` (eip712.rs:1054, called from torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1678 and :4633) takes no chain_id at all, so a node running with a non-7778 genesis chain_id would reject actions on the RPC path but accept them in block execution.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:7 — module doc: Domain { name: "Torus", version: "1", chainId: 7778, verifyingContract: 0x0 }
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:24 — `pub const TORUS_CHAIN_ID: u64 = 7778;` hardcoded
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:163-175 — `eip712_domain_separator()` takes no args; encodes constant name/version/7778/Address::ZERO
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:681-686, :764-767, :1129 — sign_native_action, recover_sender, and batch verify all call the arg-less `eip712_domain_separator()`
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:846-868 — `validate()` guard: `if expected_chain_id != TORUS_CHAIN_ID { return Err(ChainIdMismatch) }` — compares node config against the constant, never alters the domain
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:1029-1037, :1054-1059 — `batch_verify_native_actions[_cached]` signature is (actions, timestamp, session_lookup[, verified_lookup]) — no chain_id parameter
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1678-1681 — block execution verifies via batch_verify_native_actions_cached with no chain_id
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:290-307, :1132-1138 — RPC submit path passes `self.chain_id` into validate_with_sessions / verify_one_action
- crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:505-517 — chain_id comes from genesis file or default_chain_config(); crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1370,1394 show chain_id: 1 in example genesis JSON, i.e. genesis chain_id is configurable and can differ from 7778
- crates/torus-evm/src/executor.rs:18-19 — a second, separate `TORUS_CHAIN_ID = 7778` constant for the EVM side
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:1-5 — replay protection within a network is only the ms-timestamp nonce; NONCE_WINDOW_MS = 60_000 at :27

**Risk:** Testnet->mainnet (and devnet->mainnet) replay: a user who signs a Withdraw/TransferToPerp/PlaceOrder on testnet with a fresh nonce can have that exact signed action relayed to mainnet by anyone who sees it (testnet RPCs, block explorers, gossip) within ~60s, and it will verify and execute against their mainnet account. HL prevents this with the phantom-agent `source` field ("a" mainnet, "b" testnet) hashed into the agent connectionId, plus chainId 1337 in the domain; Torus has only the fixed 7778 domain. Secondary: the RPC-path chain-id check vs the exec-path's absence of one is an inconsistency that would let blocks containing actions execute on a mis-configured (non-7778) network while the RPC rejects them, and offers no actual network separation.

**Fix:** 1) Make the domain network-specific: change `eip712_domain_separator()` (crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:163) to `eip712_domain_separator(chain_id: u64)` and thread the genesis `ChainConfig.chain_id` (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1223) through `sign_native_action`, `SignedNativeAction::recover_sender`/`verify_session_signature`/`validate*`, and `batch_verify_native_actions[_cached][_with_mode]` (eip712.rs:1029/1054/1074). Update call sites: torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1678 and :4633 (pass `self.chain_id`/config.chain_id), torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:307/:1138, torus-bridge/benches/exec_place_batch.rs:15. Delete the `expected_chain_id != TORUS_CHAIN_ID` guard at eip712.rs:852/:880 (becomes redundant) or keep it as a sanity assert. 2) Assign distinct chain IDs per network (e.g. mainnet 7778, testnet 7779) in genesis and align `torus_evm::TORUS_CHAIN_ID` usage (executor.rs:19, app.rs:3709/6013/6731) with the genesis value instead of a second constant. Alternatively, mirror HL more closely by adding a `source`/network string field to every struct hash (hash_* fns from eip712.rs:195 on), but the chainId route is the idiomatic EIP-712 way and wallets display it. 3) Tests: in eip712.rs test module add `sign_on_chain_a_fails_to_recover_on_chain_b` (sign with chain_id 7779, verify with 7778 -> recovered address != signer / Err), extend `validate_chain_id_mismatch` (eip712.rs:1542), and a consensus-level test in app.rs asserting a block carrying an action signed under another chain_id yields `None` sender from batch_verify. 4) Memory note: any existing signed fixtures/test vectors keyed to the old domain will need regeneration.

**Unsure:** Did not confirm whether a testnet genesis currently exists with chain_id != 7778 (main.rs:584 references default testnet bootstrap nodes; lib.rs:1370/1394 example genesis uses chain_id 1). If testnet already runs with chain_id 7778 the replay is live today; if it runs with a different chain_id, the RPC path rejects all native actions (ChainIdMismatch) while the exec path accepts them — either way the domain is not network-bound. Did not read the mempool admission path (crates/torus-consensus/src/mempool.rs) to confirm whether it validates chain_id before gossip. Did not read the HL reference implementation; HL comparison is from recall (chainId 1337, name "Exchange", version "1", verifyingContract 0x0, phantom agent source "a"/"b").

</details>

### evm-wallet-compat

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort M, lockstep no · LOC: ~350-600 LOC (tags, blockHash and topics fixes ~80; fee percentiles ~80; estimateGas cap ~30; missing simple methods ~200; filters and tracing more)

MetaMask and Foundry can do the basic flows on Torus. The methods they need on a custom network are all in torus-rpc/src/eth.rs: chainId, blockNumber, getBalance, getCode, getStorageAt, getTransactionCount, gasPrice, maxPriorityFeePerGas, sendRawTransaction, getTransactionByHash, the receipt and block getters, call, estimateGas, getLogs, feeHistory, and subscribe (newHeads, logs, newPendingTransactions). Blocks carry baseFeePerGas, so EIP-1559 is detected. The chain id is 7778. Several real gaps remain, and two of them return wrong data without an error. (1) resolve_block_tag only knows latest, pending and earliest. The "safe" and "finalized" tags, which viem and ethers use, fail as a number parse. (2) LogFilter has no blockHash field (EIP-234). serde drops it, so getLogs({blockHash}) returns the logs of the latest block. (3) The "logs" subscription filters on address only and ignores topics. A filter that fails to parse becomes "all logs". An unknown subscription kind is accepted and then never emits anything. (4) The feeHistory reward array is always 0x0 and maxPriorityFeePerGas is a fixed 1 gwei, so wallets cannot price tips from the market. (5) estimateGas does a sound binary search with a 21000 floor and returns the revert reason. But it starts the upper bound at the 30M block limit with no cap from the caller's balance or tx.gas. eth_call and estimateGas reject any historical block, so an anvil --fork-url pinned to a block number breaks as soon as the chain moves on. (6) Many methods are missing: eth_syncing, eth_accounts, eth_getBlockReceipts, the eth_newFilter/getFilterChanges family, getTransactionByBlock*AndIndex, getBlockTransactionCount*, eth_createAccessList, eth_getProof and debug_trace*. HyperEVM-specific features are absent: the dual small/big block model and the big-block opt-in.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:33-78 the whole eth_ namespace: chainId through feeHistory, plus subscribe
- crates/torus-evm/src/executor.rs:19 TORUS_CHAIN_ID = 7778; :73 DEFAULT_BLOCK_GAS_LIMIT = 30_000_000
- crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:442 baseFeePerGas is exposed in RpcBlock
- crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:607-621 gasPrice = latest base fee (1 gwei fallback); maxPriorityFeePerGas is a fixed ONE_GWEI
- crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:990-1054 feeHistory: up to 1024 blocks, base fee and gasUsedRatio are real, but every reward percentile is hardcoded "0x0"
- crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:865-924 estimateGas: rejects any block other than latest (873), binary search lo=21000 hi=DEFAULT_BLOCK_GAS_LIMIT, revert data returned; the in-loop tx_env (916) drops the nonce default, which is harmless because call mode disables the nonce check (executor.rs ~190)
- crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:164-213 build_call_tx_env: a missing gas defaults to 30M; gas_price falls back to maxFeePerGas, else 0
- crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:926-988 getLogs: MAX_LOG_BLOCK_RANGE 10_000, MAX_LOGS 10_000, check_pruned; from/to default to latest
- crates/torus-rpc/src/types.rs:235-242 LogFilter has only from_block/to_block/address/topics: no blockHash and no deny_unknown_fields
- crates/torus-rpc/src/types.rs:100-106 resolve_block_tag handles latest\|pending\|earliest only
- crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:1101-1139 the logs subscription filters by address only; a bad filter is turned into None by .ok()
- crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:1162-1166 an unknown subscription kind is accepted (sink already accepted at 1078) and only logged
- crates/torus-rpc/src/eth.rs:1063-1075 MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS 1000, enforced globally

**Risk:** Wrong data with no error is the worst case. An indexer or a viem/ethers app that queries getLogs by blockHash (common for reorg-safe log fetching) gets the logs of the wrong block. Topic-filtered WS log subscriptions deliver events from every topic of a contract, so a dapp listening for one event decodes the wrong ones. Any client that reads with blockTag "finalized" or "safe" gets hard errors; viem's actions and ethers' FinalizedBlock are examples, and with HyperBFT's instant finality these tags should simply map to latest. Tip estimates of 0 or a fixed 1 gwei are fine on a chain that is not congested, but under load wallets will underprice. If the priority fee is burned, as on HyperEVM, the fixed value is acceptable. Forking with anvil or Foundry and tracing with cast run or debug_trace fail, which matters for developers who want parity with HyperEVM, where tracing works.

**Fix:** 1) In types.rs resolve_block_tag, add "safe" | "finalized" => Ok(latest), because HyperBFT finality is instant. Accept EIP-1898 objects {blockNumber|blockHash} in the call, estimateGas and getBalance parameters. 2) Add `block_hash: Option<String>` to LogFilter. In get_logs, when it is set, resolve the hash to a height (block-hash index; the read path behind eth_getBlockByHash should already provide one), reject it in combination with from/to (-32602), and set from = to = that height. Add #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] or validate explicitly. 3) In the eth.rs subscribe "logs" arm, apply matches_topics as well. Also, in the "logs" arm, reject a filter that fails to parse instead of falling back with .ok(), and move the kind match before pending.accept() so an unknown kind is rejected with -32602. 4) In fee_history, compute reward percentiles from the effective tips of the block's receipts (get_block_receipts is already called in get_logs). Make max_priority_fee_per_gas a percentile over recent blocks, with ONE_GWEI as the floor. 5) In estimate_gas, cap hi at min(tx.gas, block gas limit, balance - value / feeCap) when a fee is given, as geth does, and drop the redundant first execution when it succeeds at hi. 6) Add the cheap methods: eth_syncing (false), eth_accounts ([]), eth_getBlockReceipts (reuse get_block_receipts), getBlockTransactionCountBy*, getTransactionByBlock*AndIndex, eth_createAccessList (revm access-list inspector), and later the eth_newFilter family plus debug_traceTransaction. Tests in torus-rpc: blockHash getLogs returns that block's logs; topic-filtered subscription; "finalized" resolves; feeHistory rewards are nonzero after a tipped tx; estimateGas with maxFeePerGas from a low-balance account.

**Unsure:** Not read: whether getBalance, getCode, getStorageAt and getTransactionCount honor or reject historical block tags (only call and estimateGas were confirmed to reject, at 824 and 873). Not read: whether the executor's call mode disables the balance check (this decides whether estimateGas fails for wallets that send maxFeePerGas). Not read: whether an EIP-1898 object parameter deserializes at all. Not read: the hash-to-height index used by eth_getBlockByHash. Not read: whether the priority fee goes to validators or is burned. Not checked: net_version (net.rs:23 returns chain_id.to_string(), so it looks fine). Not verified: HyperEVM's current method set and the dual-block details (chain id 999, 2M/30M gas small and big blocks); these are from prior knowledge. No live test was run against MetaMask, viem or Foundry.

</details>

### trade-retention

**opus** — partial, impact medium, effort M, lockstep no · LOC: ~250-400 (RPC method + cursor ~150, retention compaction filter/config ~100, tests ~150)

Fill history lives in two node-local column families written once per block by trade_rows::encode_block: CF_NATIVE_TRADES, keyed (market, block, chunk), and CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES, keyed (addr, !block) so the newest block comes first. Nothing ever prunes them. The only deletes I found are the one-time format-migration wipe in ensure_trade_history_format and the TORUS_TRADE_HISTORY=0 off switch. So they keep every fill, with no retention window. The user query path cannot answer HL-style requests. getUserTrades takes only (trader, market?, limit), caps limit at 1000, and offers no time or block range and no cursor, so you cannot fetch 10k recent fills or page past the newest 1000. There is no userFillsByTime equivalent. Block-range queries exist only per market (getTradeHistoryRange, cap 5000) and by block number, not by timestamp. A live userFills WS stream does exist (streams.rs).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-state/src/trade_rows.rs:1-15 module doc: packed rows, one per (market,block,chunk) and one per (trader,block); node-local, outside consensus root, read only by RPC
- crates/torus-state/src/trade_rows.rs:148-155 user_trade_key = addr[20] \| !block (newest-first under forward iteration)
- crates/torus-state/src/trade_rows.rs:167-220 encode_block writes rows; the user row value holds timestamp u64 + entries {trade_index, market, price, qty, taker_side, role}
- crates/torus-state/src/trade_rows.rs:225-240 ensure_trade_history_format: delete_range of both CFs only on a format mismatch (migration, not retention)
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:534-536 TORUS_TRADE_HISTORY=0 disables the rows; default on; no retention knob
- grep for prune/retention near trade/fill/history in torus-state/src, native_executor.rs, app.rs: no hits
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:213-219 getUserTrades(trader, market_id?, limit) signature: no time range, no cursor
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1652 limit.unwrap_or(100).min(1000)
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1665-1716 prefix scan from addr, newest first, market filter applied after decode, stops at limit; it does not use timestamp
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:191-197,1413-1423 getTradeHistoryRange(market, from_block, to_block, limit) per market only, cap 5000
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:938-944 getTradeHistory per market, limit cap 1000, newest only
- crates/torus-rpc/src/streams.rs:1,59-61 userFills WS stream exists (live only)

**Risk:** HL clients and SDKs call userFills (newest 2000) and userFillsByTime(user, startTime, endTime, aggregateByTime), and page by moving startTime forward, up to the 10k most recent fills. Here a user with more than 1000 fills cannot read older ones at all, a time window cannot be requested, and active traders' rows grow without bound on every node. Explorers and tax tools that need full history therefore have to run getBlockTrades over every block. On the retention side, disk growth is unbounded (the s77 packed rows reduce bytes but do not cap them).

**Fix:** 1) torus-rpc/src/torus.rs: add getUserFillsByTime(trader, start_ms, end_ms?, limit?, aggregate?). Because the key is (addr, !block), the scan seeks to user_trade_key(addr, block_hi), not just the bare prefix. Map time to block either by binary-searching block timestamps (block headers/meta) or by scanning newest-first and comparing the decoded row timestamp (trade_rows::decode_user_row already returns timestamp), stopping once timestamp < start. Return at most 2000 per call, oldest-first, so the client can page by advancing startTime, which is HL semantics. 2) Give getUserTrades an optional before_block/cursor parameter (resume from user_trade_key(addr, cursor_block-1), plus trade_index for a block split mid-row), and raise the cap from 1000 to 2000 for HL userFills parity. 3) Retention: add a TORUS_TRADE_HISTORY_KEEP_BLOCKS (or a per-user N-fills) policy. For CF_NATIVE_TRADES a periodic delete_range per market below a cutoff block is cheap, because block sits in the key after the market. For CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES, block is the key suffix after the address, so pruning needs either a per-address delete_range over [user_trade_key(a, cutoff), user_trade_key(a, 0)] for each address seen, or a RocksDB compaction filter that drops rows whose decoded timestamp or block is below the cutoff. The compaction filter is simplest and node-local, so it is not consensus-breaking. Tests: extend torus-rpc/src/lib.rs tests (next to trade_history_limit_spans_chunk_boundary_newest_first): 10k fills over many blocks with time-window paging and no gaps or duplicates; also a cursor test and a prune test in torus-state trade_rows tests.

**Unsure:** I did not read the rest of the getTradeHistoryRange body (past torus.rs:1440) or getBlockTrades. I did not check whether a block-timestamp index exists for mapping time to block. I did not check RocksDB CF options in torus-state cf.rs for a TTL or compaction filter; the grep found no prune/retention code, but cf.rs options were not inspected. I also did not check whether an off-node indexer (explorer) serves HL-style fill history instead.

</details>

**fable** — partial, impact medium, effort M, lockstep no · LOC: 150-300 (RPC method + cursor + tests); +150 if trade-CF retention added to pruner

Trade history is stored as packed per-block rows in two node-local RocksDB CFs (CF_NATIVE_TRADES keyed market|block|chunk, CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES keyed address|!block) and is never pruned: the StatePruner only delete_range's cf_block_bodies and cf_receipts, so trade CFs grow unbounded (archive by default). RPC exposes torus_getTradeHistory (market, newest-first, limit capped at 1000), torus_getTradeHistoryRange (market, from_block/to_block, limit capped at 5000) and torus_getUserTrades (trader, optional market, newest-first, limit capped at 1000). There is no user-fills-by-time or by-block-range method and no cursor/pagination on getUserTrades: a user cannot fetch 10k fills (cap 1000, no offset/cursor) nor filter by timestamp, so HL userFillsByTime (startTime/endTime, up to 2000 per call, 10k most-recent via userFills with aggregateByTime) has no equivalent. Timestamps are stored in each row header, so time-range filtering is feasible but needs block<->time resolution since keys are block-indexed.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-state/src/trade_rows.rs:1-15 — module doc: packed rows, CF_NATIVE_TRADES key market u64\|block u64\|chunk u16, CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES key address[20]\|!block u64, value header ver\|timestamp u64\|n; both CFs node-local, read only by RPC trade-history methods
- crates/torus-state/src/trade_rows.rs:32 — TRADE_CHUNK_FILLS = 1024 fills per market row
- crates/torus-state/src/trade_rows.rs:149-156 — user_trade_key uses !block so forward iteration is newest-first
- crates/torus-state/src/pruner.rs:1-40,72,206-226 — pruner only delete_range_cf on CF_BLOCK_BODIES and CF_RECEIPTS; trade CFs not in the prunable list
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:121-126,940-990 — getTradeHistory(market_id, limit): limit.unwrap_or(100).min(1000), reverse iterate, stops at pruned_up_to (which only tracks body pruning)
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:190-197,1418-1465 — getTradeHistoryRange(market_id, from_block, to_block, limit): limit.unwrap_or(1000).min(5000), forward scan between trade_key(mid,from,0) and trade_key(mid,to+1,0)
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:213-219,1645-1720 — getUserTrades(trader, market_id?, limit): limit.unwrap_or(100).min(1000), prefix scan newest-first, no from/to block, no time filter, no cursor; market filter applied post-decode
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1777 — subscribe error text points users to getTradeHistoryRange / getUserTrades as the backfill path
- crates/torus-rpc/src/lib.rs:250,308 — pruned_up_to AtomicU64 shared with StatePruner; defaults 0

**Risk:** HL parity gap: HL offers userFills (most recent 2000, 10k with aggregateByTime) and userFillsByTime(startTime, endTime) with pagination by time. Torus users/frontends/tax tools can only pull the latest 1000 user fills with no way to page further back or by time window, so full fill-history export is impossible via RPC. Separately, unbounded trade CF growth with no retention policy means disk grows forever on every node, while market-history queries can silently truncate on pruned_up_to even though the trade rows themselves still exist (getTradeHistory breaks at block < pruned_up_to despite the pruner never touching CF_NATIVE_TRADES).

**Fix:** 1) Add torus_getUserTradesByTime(trader, start_time, end_time?, market_id?, limit) and/or torus_getUserTradesRange(trader, from_block, to_block, limit) in crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs next to get_user_trades: seek with user_trade_key(trader, to_block) (keys are !block so Forward from the newest wanted block), stop when parsed block < from_block; for time bounds, read the row header timestamp (decode_user_row) and skip rows with timestamp outside [start,end]; add a 'before_block' cursor param to existing get_user_trades so clients can page past 1000 (returns next cursor = last block - 1). Cap limit at 2000 to match HL and keep scan bounded. 2) Decide retention: add CF_NATIVE_TRADES/CF_NATIVE_USER_TRADES to crates/torus-state/src/pruner.rs as an optional separate 'trade_history_retention_blocks' in PrunerConfig; market CF prunes with delete_range per market prefix (market|cutoff), user CF cannot delete_range by height (height is suffix) so either keep it unpruned, or add a secondary block->trader index at encode_block time (trade_rows.rs:167). 3) Fix getTradeHistory to not stop at pruned_up_to (torus.rs:979) unless trade CFs are actually pruned, or track a separate trades_pruned_up_to. Tests: torus-rpc unit tests writing rows via encode_block into a temp StateDb, assert by-time/by-block filtering, cursor paging across >1000 fills, and that market history is served below pruned_up_to.

**Unsure:** Did not read native_executor.rs:5087 write path or torus-node main.rs config to confirm there is no separate trade-CF retention knob (grep for retention/CF_NATIVE_TRADES outside tests found none, so likely absent). Did not verify whether an external indexer/explorer (docs/perf/s65-explorers) is intended as the long-history path instead of node RPC. HL limits (2000/call, 10k aggregateByTime) are from recall, not re-verified against current HL docs.

</details>

### node-roles

**opus** — partial, impact medium, effort M, lockstep no · LOC: 300-600 (sentry and reserved peers ~250; observer commit feed ~150; NodeRole refactor ~80)

There are two roles: validator and non-validator RPC node. The RPC node is turned on with `--rpc-only` or `rpc_only` in the config file. It needs no validator key: it generates a throwaway ed25519 key that serves only as its network identity, and it passes `signing_key=None` into TorusApp. It runs the same consensus replica as a validator and the same RPC/WS server, so it can follow the chain and serve RPC/WS. It follows consensus through the gossip mirror of consensus broadcasts and fetches blocks over the block-sync protocol. On the network side, swarm.rs adds non-validator peers to peer_map when they identify themselves, removes them on disconnect, and leaves them out of the validator-only direct fan. Compared with Hyperliquid: there is no sentry role or private-validator topology, no read-only gating or tx-forwarding policy specific to the role, and no Hyperliquid-style node data outputs (fills, order statuses, trades files) beyond the WS streams. The one setting that changes by role is the all-market newTrades stream.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:159-162 `--rpc-only` flag: 'non-validator RPC node. Syncs blocks from peers but does not participate in consensus. No validator key required.'
- crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:288-289 config-file rpc_only overrides the CLI flag
- crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:448-458 rpc-only generates an ephemeral SigningKey 'for network identity'; without --rpc-only, startup fails if there is no keystore or validator key
- crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:558-569 signing_key_for_app = None when rpc_only, so TorusApp gets no proposer key
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:4767-4771 with signing_key None, sig_attestation is [0u8;64], so a node without a key cannot produce a valid proposal
- crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:921-945 the RPC server starts on every node type; the only role-dependent setting is all_market_trades(…, cli.rpc_only)
- crates/torus-rpc/src/streams.rs:81-96 all_market_trades_allowed is on by default for rpc_only and off for validators
- crates/torus-network/src/config.rs:54-59 consensus_gossip_mirror: RPC nodes follow consensus via gossip; with TORUS_CONSENSUS_GOSSIP_MIRROR=0, observers lose their live consensus feed
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:1704-1711 non-validator peers are added to peer_map on identify so their block-sync requests are accepted
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:2113-2120 non-validator peers are removed from peer_map on disconnect
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:685-700 is_validator_peer: banned non-validators stay dropped, while validators are exempt from bans
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:4896-4926 tests: direct-fan targets are validators that are in peer_map, minus self and observers
- crates/torus-network/src/config.rs:10-11,197-204 bootstrap_peers only; config.rs has no sentry, private-peer or persistent-peer settings

**Risk:** 1) Following the chain depends on the gossip mirror. The stated end state, TORUS_CONSENSUS_GOSSIP_MIRROR=0 with the direct fan on, leaves RPC nodes without a live consensus feed, so they fall back to block sync and lag or stall. Hyperliquid non-validators get a dedicated block stream from validators or root peers. 2) There is no sentry topology, so validators must be reachable on public p2p, which exposes them to DoS. Hyperliquid validators can sit behind sentry nodes with reserved or private peers. 3) An RPC node runs the full hotstuff replica with a key outside the validator set, so it does consensus work it never uses. This is not a parity gap, but it is a cost. 4) There is no flag for node data output (fills, order statuses, raw blocks) like Hyperliquid's --write-fills, --write-order-statuses and --serve-info. Indexers would have to scrape the WS streams instead.

**Fix:** (a) Give RPC nodes a feed that does not depend on the gossip mirror. In torus-network/src/swarm.rs, add a committed-block or QC push to subscribed non-validator peers (opt-in, rate-capped). Alternatively, keep the mirror forced on whenever any non-validator is mapped, and add a test that an observer keeps up while the mirror is off. (b) Add a sentry mode. In torus-network/src/config.rs, add `reserved_peers` and `private_mode` (validator dials only reserved sentries, kademlia off, no advertised addresses). In swarm.rs, have a sentry relay consensus messages from the validator it protects through the existing direct path. Wire both through main.rs CLI flags `--reserved-peers` and `--sentry-for`. (c) Optional: in main.rs, make --rpc-only an explicit `NodeRole` enum (Validator, Rpc, Sentry) instead of a bool, and add opt-in file sinks for fills and order statuses next to torus-rpc/src/streams.rs. Tests: a swarm test that a non-validator receives commits with the mirror off; a config-parse test for reserved peers; a test that a private validator never adds a non-reserved address.

**Unsure:** Not verified: whether hotstuff-rs on an RPC node fully skips voting with a key outside the validator set (presumed, not read); where the RPC server sends transactions on an RPC node (the leader_vk_fn forwarding at main.rs:949+ was not read); and how sync.rs catch-up behaves for a node starting far behind (only the header was skimmed). The Hyperliquid comparison is from general knowledge (hl-visor run-non-validator, root/reserved peers, sentry setup, --write-fills and --serve-info flags), not checked against current Hyperliquid docs.

</details>

**fable** — present, impact low, effort S, lockstep no · LOC: doc fix ~15 LOC; optional RPC bind/sentry flag ~40 LOC; observer tagging ~30 LOC

A non-validator role exists and is wired end-to-end: `torus-node --rpc-only` (CLI flag or `rpc_only` in TOML) runs the same binary without a validator key (ephemeral libp2p identity), constructs TorusApp with `signing_key = None` so it never proposes/votes, still runs the hotstuff_rs replica with block-sync configured, follows consensus via the gossipsub mirror (`consensus_gossip_mirror` default ON; direct-fan targets exclude non-validators), and serves the full JSON-RPC/WS surface including on-commit WebSocket stream handlers and leader-forwarding of submitted txs to the current leader. RPC nodes are registered in the peer map on identify so their block-sync requests pass `verify_sender_key`, and are pruned from the map on disconnect. There is no separate "sentry" concept (validator hidden behind proxy nodes), no role gating of RPC endpoints on validators (validators expose the same RPC/WS, with only one WS subscription type restricted), and no explicit observer handshake/role advertisement in torus-network beyond "not in validator set".

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:88 about = "Torus-hyperBFT node (validator or RPC-only)"

The gaps: (1) validators expose the same public RPC/WS by default, so no sentry-style isolation; (2) no role advertisement in the identify/handshake, so peer scoring and fan logic infer role solely from validator-set membership; (3) docs/node-operator-guide.md 'non-validator' example omits --rpc-only and requires a keystore, so operators may run a validator-keyed node thinking it is a follower.

### p2p-discovery

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort L, lockstep no · LOC: 500-900

torus-network runs libp2p over QUIC with Kademlia (server mode, MemoryStore), identify, and gossipsub (Strict signed validation) on 3 topics: /torus/consensus/1.0, /torus/transactions/1.0, /torus/native-actions/1.0. Bootstrap is a CSV of /p2p multiaddrs plus one hardcoded testnet peer. Validators are pinned as gossipsub explicit peers and redialed by mesh maintenance. DoS protection is all app-level and hand-rolled: connection_limits (80/20 in/out split, 2 conns per peer), an allow_block_list fed by a JSON permanent-ban file, a custom PeerScoring (score 100, temp ban at 0, permanent ban at -50), per-peer tx and consensus rate limiters, size caps on receive, and a dial filter that only allows global addresses. Gaps: libp2p gossipsub peer scoring is not configured, nothing is per-IP or per-subnet, there is no limit on pending or handshaking connections, there is no sentry or private-peer mode, and any peer that completes identify is accepted. So the node works for a known validator set with permissioned sentries. It is not ready for permissionless validators or for public sentries facing unknown peers at Hyperliquid's scale.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-network/src/behaviour.rs:13-15 topic consts CONSENSUS_TOPIC/TX_TOPIC/NATIVE_ACTION_TOPIC
- crates/torus-network/src/behaviour.rs:80-88 gossipsub_config sets only heartbeat/max_transmit/queue_len/ValidationMode::Strict — no peer_score_params, no flood_publish tuning, no mesh D params
- crates/torus-network/src/behaviour.rs:203-206 Kademlia MemoryStore, kad::Mode::Server unconditionally (every node, including validators, answers DHT queries)
- crates/torus-network/src/behaviour.rs:212-221 connection_limits: inbound 80%/outbound 20% of max_peers, per-peer 2; no with_max_pending_incoming/outgoing
- crates/torus-network/src/behaviour.rs:223-224 allow_block_list::Behaviour (block list only, no allow-list mode)
- crates/torus-network/src/config.rs:11-13,36-42 bootstrap_peers, max_peers(100), tx_rate_limit_per_peer(100), consensus_rate_limit_per_peer(50), ban_list_path
- crates/torus-network/src/config.rs:170-205 parse_bootstrap_peers CSV + TESTNET_BOOTSTRAP_PEERS single hardcoded 95.111.231.121 node
- crates/torus-network/src/transport.rs:1-45 GlobalOnlyTransport refuses dials to non-global addrs, bootstrap addrs exempt
- crates/torus-network/src/peer_scoring.rs:16-29 INITIAL_SCORE 100, TEMP_BAN 0 (1h), PERM_BAN -50, penalties 20/5/10, reward 1
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:685-701 is_validator_peer / should_drop_banned_gossip: validators are exempt from bans (bounded only by per-author rate limiters)
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:913-919 subscribe_gossip_topics; v2 zstd topic removed as DoS vector (s364)
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:965-971 permanently banned peers loaded into block_list at startup
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:1060-1095 mesh maintenance: kademlia.bootstrap() + dial unconnected validators + gossipsub.add_explicit_peer(validator)
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:1677-1705 identify::Received: ban check, then adds global listen addrs to kademlia and registers non-validator peers into peer_map (any peer completing identify is admitted)
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:2844-2870 verify_sender_key binds claimed ed25519 key to authenticated PeerId via peer_map

**Risk:** With public sentries or permissionless validators, an attacker can open many Sybil PeerIds from one IP or subnet. Nothing limits connections per IP, so they can fill the 80 inbound slots (eclipse risk for a sentry-less validator). The custom ban only fires after the attacker misbehaves, and a fresh PeerId resets its score to 100. Without gossipsub score params, the mesh has no defence against grafting or IHAVE/IWANT spam and no opportunistic graft, and the mesh can be filled with low-quality peers. Validators run Kademlia in Server mode and publish their addresses, so they cannot hide behind sentries the way Hyperliquid validators do. Banned validators are always exempt, so a malicious validator that permissionless entry lets in is limited only by the rate limiters. One hardcoded bootstrap node is a single point of failure.

**Fix:** 1. In behaviour.rs `gossipsub_config`, add `PeerScoreParams` and `PeerScoreThresholds` through `gossipsub::Behaviour::with_peer_score`. Set per-topic weights for the 3 topics (a high invalid-message penalty on consensus, P3 mesh delivery on native-actions). Report validation results by switching to `validate_messages()` and calling `report_message_validation_result` from the swarm.rs gossip handler (around lines 1270-1340), so oversized or invalid messages count against gossipsub's own score. 2. In behaviour.rs `with_limits_and_heartbeat`, add `with_max_pending_incoming` and `with_max_pending_outgoing`. Add a small per-IP connection-limit behaviour, for example a HashMap<IpAddr, u32> checked in `handle_pending_inbound_connection`. 3. Add `NetworkConfig.node_role` = Validator | Sentry | Public. A Validator uses `kad::Mode::Client`, enables allow-list mode (`allow_block_list::AllowedPeers`) restricted to the sentries plus the validator set, and sets `identify.hide_listen_addrs`. A Sentry relays and keeps public peer slots. 4. Make `TESTNET_BOOTSTRAP_PEERS` a list of 3 or more nodes in different regions, or load it from a DNS seed. 5. In swarm.rs identify handling (1677-1705), cap how many non-validator peers are registered into peer_map, so it cannot grow without bound. Tests: a swarm test where N PeerIds from one IP should be limited, a gossipsub score test where an invalid consensus message drops the peer below the graylist threshold, and a test that a validator in Validator role refuses a non-allow-listed inbound peer.

**Unsure:** I did not read the request_response Request handlers (swarm.rs:1461, 1718, 1809, 1910), so I have not confirmed whether sync, block-data and DA requests from unknown, non-validator peers are rate-limited or served without limit. I did not read bridge.rs:260-330 in full (dial-filter wiring and the `explicit` dials) or the TxGossipState details. The comparison with Hyperliquid's current sentry and permissionless-validator setup (whitelisted validator peers, public non-validator nodes gossiping from seed IPs) is from general knowledge, not checked against current Hyperliquid docs. I also did not check whether the ConsensusRateLimiter keys on the gossip author or on the forwarding peer.

</details>

**fable** — partial, impact high, effort L, lockstep no · LOC: 400-700

torus-network has a real libp2p stack: Kademlia DHT in Server mode plus Identify for discovery, static bootstrap peers (CLI --p2p-peers or a single hardcoded testnet seed), three gossipsub topics (consensus, tx, native-actions) with Strict signed validation, and DoS controls: connection_limits (80/20 inbound/outbound split of max_peers=100, 2 conns/peer), allow_block_list bans driven by a local PeerScoring (temp ban at score 0, perm at -50, persisted ban file), per-author consensus rate limiter, per-peer tx rate limit + dedup, and message size caps. Non-global addresses are filtered from Kademlia unless allow_private_addrs. However there is no gossipsub peer-scoring (with_peer_score) so unknown peers can fill the mesh and eclipse validators; no identity/stake gate on inbound connections (any peer can consume the 80 inbound slots, and validators get no reserved inbound slots); only one hardcoded seed; no sentry/validator-private-peer concept; and no request-rate limits on the sync/block-data/native-da request_response protocols from unknown peers.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-network/src/behaviour.rs:24-47 TorusBehaviour = gossipsub + direct/sync/block_data/native_da/native_da_shards request_response + kademlia + identify + connection_limits + allow_block_list
- crates/torus-network/src/behaviour.rs:203-206 kad::Behaviour with MemoryStore, set_mode(Server)
- crates/torus-network/src/behaviour.rs:212-220 connection limits: max_inbound = 80% of max_peers, outbound 20%, max_established_per_peer 2; no reserved validator slots
- crates/torus-network/src/behaviour.rs:81-87 gossipsub ConfigBuilder: max_transmit_size + ValidationMode::Strict; no .with_peer_score anywhere in swarm.rs (grep returned none)
- crates/torus-network/src/config.rs:7-68 NetworkConfig: bootstrap_peers, max_peers, tx_rate_limit_per_peer, consensus_rate_limit_per_peer, ban_list_path, allow_private_addrs
- crates/torus-network/src/config.rs:196-206 TESTNET_BOOTSTRAP_PEERS has exactly one hardcoded seed (95.111.231.121); default_bootstrap_peers() parses it
- crates/torus-network/src/config.rs:138-166 is_global_addr filters loopback/private/CGNAT/ULA
- crates/torus-node/src/main.rs:581-593 bootstrap_peers from cli.p2p_peers CSV, else default_bootstrap_peers()
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:951-958 three IdentTopics: CONSENSUS_TOPIC, TX_TOPIC, NATIVE_ACTION_TOPIC
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:2007-2034 ConnectionEstablished: disconnect only if banned AND not validator/recently-deposed; else kademlia.bootstrap(); no stake/allowlist gate for unknown peers
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:1677-1705 Identify::Received: add global listen addrs to kademlia; registers non-validator peers (RPC nodes) so their direct messages are accepted
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:2164-2176 Kademlia RoutingUpdated evicts non-global addrs
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:685-700 is_validator_peer / should_drop_banned_gossip: validators exempt from bans
- crates/torus-network/src/swarm.rs:1263-1420 gossip Message arm: penalize propagation_source on invalid consensus/native-action; consensus_rate_limiter keyed by author (line 1326); tx_gossip_state.should_accept per peer (1419)
- crates/torus-network/src/peer_scoring.rs:16-29 INITIAL_SCORE 100, TEMP_BAN at 0 (1h), PERM_BAN at -50, penalties 20/5/10
- crates/torus-network/src/caps.rs:23-49 size caps: direct 8MB, native-da 8MB, block-data 16MB, gossip 2MiB

**Risk:** For permissionless validators / public sentries: a Sybil operator can open ~80 inbound connections (and dial the remaining 20 are outbound-only slots from our side) with fresh PeerIds, filling max_peers and crowding validators out of inbound slots, since nothing reserves connection capacity for validator-set peers and bans are per-PeerId with INITIAL_SCORE 100 (cheap to rotate). Without gossipsub peer scoring, mesh eclipse/graft-spam and IHAVE/IWANT amplification on the consensus topic are unpenalized by the router. Sync/block-data/native-da request_response handlers have size caps but no per-peer request rate limit, so an unknown peer can repeatedly request 16MB block bodies. A single hardcoded seed is a liveness SPOF for discovery. HL by contrast runs validators behind operator-run non-validating nodes and lets validators keep private peer links.

**Fix:** 1) behaviour.rs: enable gossipsub peer scoring (gossipsub::PeerScoreParams/PeerScoreThresholds via Behaviour::with_peer_score) with topic params for CONSENSUS_TOPIC; wire score-driven graylist. 2) swarm.rs ConnectionEstablished / connection_limits: add validator-reserved inbound capacity -- when inbound count >= max_inbound - validators.len(), disconnect unknown (non-peer_map, non-validator) peers; alternatively use allow_block_list AllowedPeers mode behind a new NetworkConfig.validator_only_inbound flag for the validator tier, with a sentry tier (new config.rs field `private_peers: Vec<(PeerId,Multiaddr)>` always dialed, never evicted, exempt from scoring). 3) Add per-peer token-bucket rate limiting for inbound request_response (sync_proto, block_data, native_da, native_da_shards) in the swarm Message{Request} arms, reusing ConsensusRateLimiter::check_and_increment keyed by requester PeerId, penalize via PENALTY_EXCESSIVE_RATE. 4) config.rs: make TESTNET_BOOTSTRAP_PEERS a list of >=3 seeds (dns4 entries) and persist Kademlia routing table / last-known peers to disk for restart discovery. 5) Tests: peer_scoring/swarm unit tests for reserved-slot eviction of unknown peers, request-rate ban, and gossipsub score params build.

**Unsure:** Did not read the request_response inbound handler arms (sync/block-data/native-da) in swarm.rs to confirm absence of per-peer request throttling -- inferred from grep (no rate-limit calls near those protocols). Did not verify whether hotstuff validator-set changes are permissionless on-chain (staking registration) vs genesis-only; is_validator_peer reads shared.validators updated by update_validator_set. Did not check whether a dedicated node-type (validator vs RPC/sentry) flag exists in torus-node beyond the Identify non-validator registration. Time-boxed to 5 tool calls.

### upgrade-mechanism

**opus** — absent, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: 600-1200 (core gating plus halt-height ~400; governance scheduling and visor tool ~500+)

There is no protocol upgrade mechanism. Nothing versions the state transition: there is no protocol or app version in block headers or in ChainConfig, no feature flags activated at a block height, no halt-height, no on-chain upgrade or governance transaction, and nothing like hl-visor. What does exist is narrower. Positions and native balances carry per-record schema version bytes that hard-reject a mismatch. A node-local trade-history format marker wipes and rebuilds that history. libp2p protocol and topic strings are versioned. A few consensus parameters come from genesis, and setting them to 0 turns them off (backoff_cap, the commit-lag cap). The EVM spec is hardcoded to CANCUN. The roadmap tags changes [LOCKSTEP] ("all validators must upgrade together") and treats a fleet upgrade as a manual operation, with no tooling for it.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1222-1260 ChainConfig: chain_id, gas, fees, timeout/backoff params; no protocol_version and no activation-height fields
- crates/torus-genesis/src/lib.rs:58-80 Genesis struct: no version or fork-schedule field
- crates/torus-consensus/src/genesis.rs:10-13 GenesisConfig {chain_id, validators} only
- crates/torus-core/src/position.rs:84-112 POSITION_SCHEMA_VERSION=1; deserialize hard-errors on mismatch ('BREAKING CHANGE acceptable pre-launch'), no migration path; same for NATIVE_BALANCE_SCHEMA_VERSION at :164-184
- crates/torus-state/src/trade_rows.rs:25-30,221-238 ensure_trade_history_format: on startup, if the CF_CONSENSUS_META marker != 2, wipe the trade CFs (node-local only) -- the only versioned-migration pattern in the repo
- crates/torus-evm/src/executor.rs:186,209,259,274,402,417 SpecId::CANCUN hardcoded; no per-height spec selection
- crates/torus-network/src/behaviour.rs:13-14 CONSENSUS_TOPIC '/torus/consensus/1.0', TX_TOPIC '/torus/transactions/1.0' (wire-protocol versioning only)
- docs/Torus-hyperBFT-roadmap.md:20 [LOCAL]/[LOCKSTEP]/[CONSENSUS-SAFETY] labels; :169-170 the zstd gossip flip waits on a 'full-fleet upgrade' coordinated by hand
- grep for activation_height\|fork_height\|feature_flag\|halt_height\|protocol_version\|Upgrade tx enums across crates/: no hits

**Risk:** Every [LOCKSTEP] change, which is any change to execution semantics, needs every validator to swap binaries at the same moment. If even one validator runs a different binary, the state roots diverge or the chain halts. Without height-gated activation, a new binary also cannot replay old blocks with the old rules, so a sync from genesis breaks after the first semantic change. The schema-version bytes hard-reject old data, so any later change to Position or NativeBalance makes existing databases unreadable. Hyperliquid avoids this with hl-visor (it auto-pulls signed binaries and restarts the node) plus coordinated upgrade heights. Torus has neither.

**Fix:** 1) Add `protocol_version: u32` and `upgrades: BTreeMap<String /*feature*/, u64 /*activation height*/>` to torus-genesis Genesis and to torus_types::ChainConfig, both with #[serde(default)]. Add a `fn active(&self, feature, height) -> bool` helper on ChainConfig. 2) Thread the block height into the native_executor and app.rs execute/validate paths so that each new semantic change sits behind `cfg.active("x", h)`. 3) Add a consensus-state key in CF_CONSENSUS_META (following the ensure_trade_history_format marker pattern) to record the app version that is running. Add `--halt-height` to torus-node, which stops cleanly after committing height H so operators can swap binaries. 4) Optionally add a governance tx `ScheduleUpgrade{name,height,binary_hash}` stored in state. Nodes would refuse to execute at that height or later unless their build supports the named upgrade, which gives a deterministic halt instead of a fork. 5) Add a visor-like wrapper in tools/ that watches the halt marker, verifies a signed binary, and restarts the node. 6) Change the Position and NativeBalance deserializers to accept version N-1 and migrate it, instead of hard-rejecting it. 7) Make the EVM SpecId depend on height. Tests: a replay test where one binary executes blocks on both sides of an activation height and produces the expected roots; a halt-height test; a mixed-schema deserialize test.

**Unsure:** I did not search the devnet/, testnet/, tools/ or ci/ scripts for deploy or rolling-upgrade helpers. They could contain fleet-restart shell scripts, which would be operations tooling, not protocol versioning. I did not read whether hotstuff_rs block headers have a spare data field that could carry a version. I also did not check whether app.rs already compares any genesis-sourced parameter against height; my greps found no such pattern.

</details>

**fable** — absent, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~600-1000 Rust (types+gates+validation+governance) plus ~300 for a visor binary and docs

There is no protocol-version field, no height-gated feature activation, and no coordinated upgrade tooling (nothing like hl-visor) in the repo. `ChainConfig` (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1222-1248) carries chain_id, fees, timeouts, etc. but no `protocol_version`/activation heights; the EVM is hard-pinned to `SpecId::CANCUN` at every call site in crates/torus-evm/src/executor.rs; and consensus-semantics changes are shipped by convention as "LOCKSTEP-DEPLOY" comments (native_executor.rs:3522, torus-types lib.rs:257) that require the whole fleet to upgrade before any block carries the new behaviour, with no on-chain enforcement. Upgrade handling that does exist is purely storage-level backward compatibility (serde defaults for new ChainConfig fields, borsh `unwrap_or` for new GovernanceParams fields, dual legacy-JSON/tagged-bin block-body decoding, per-record schema-version bytes) plus per-peer multistream protocol versioning on the wire (`/torus/direct/1.0` vs `2.0`). Ops-side, the only runbook is a manual stop-the-fleet relaunch (docs/ops/s442-relaunch/relaunch-runbook.md) that tells validators to disable auto-restart and act "in lockstep" in a coordinated window.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1222-1248 — `pub struct ChainConfig` fields: chain_id, chain_name, evm_gas_limit, base_fee_per_gas, epoch_length, max_validators, min_stake, fee_*_bps, treasury/dev_pool addresses, timeout_base_ms, backoff_factor; no protocol_version or activation-height fields
