**Risk:** Every consensus-semantics change today is a manual, out-of-band fleet coordination with no on-chain safeguard: if one validator restarts on the old binary (which already happened per relaunch-runbook.md:54-55) or a lockstep window is missed, nodes compute divergent state roots and fork. Hyperliquid ships hl-visor (auto-fetch + restart of hl-node binaries) and versioned, height-coordinated protocol changes, so Torus has a real parity gap in both operational tooling and protocol-level activation.

**Fix:** 1) Protocol versioning: add `protocol_version: u32` (serde default 0) and `upgrades: Vec<ScheduledUpgrade { name, activation_height, min_binary_version }>` to `ChainConfig` in crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs; expose `fn feature_active(cfg, name, height) -> bool`. 2) Height gates: replace the two LOCKSTEP-DEPLOY comment sites (native_executor.rs:~3528 `batch_len_within_cap` skip; torus-types lib.rs:257 SessionScope widening) with `if feature_active(..)` checks keyed on block height; route EVM `SpecId` in torus-evm executor.rs through the same table instead of hard-coded CANCUN. 3) Enforcement: in crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs block validation, reject proposals whose header `protocol_version` < the active version at that height, and have the node refuse to start (or log+halt) if its binary's `BINARY_PROTOCOL_VERSION` < a scheduled upgrade's `min_binary_version` within N blocks. 4) Governance path: add an `UpgradeProposal` variant in crates/torus-economics/src/governance.rs that writes a `ScheduledUpgrade` into state on passing (borsh default-on-absent like line 500). 5) Ops: a `torus-visor` bin (new crate or scripts/) that polls a signed release manifest, downloads the binary, verifies hash/signature, and restarts torus-node at the activation height; document in docs/node-operator-guide.md. Tests: serde round-trip of ChainConfig with/without `upgrades`; stateright/unit test that a pre-activation block carrying an oversize batch is executed and a post-activation one is skipped; app.rs validate_block rejects stale protocol_version headers.

**Unsure:** Did not read specs/consensus or hotstuff_rs for any view/epoch-based versioning; did not inspect block header struct to confirm it lacks a version field (grep for protocol_version returned nothing repo-wide, which is strong but indirect). `scripts/` listing returned no deploy tooling but I did not check for a Makefile/justfile or systemd unit templates.

</details>

### multisig

**opus** — absent, impact medium, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~600-900 LOC (types+eip712 ~200, state ~80, validator/proposer helper ~120, executor ~120, rpc ~60, tests ~300)

Torus has no multi-sig at any layer. A case-insensitive grep for multisig/multi_sig/Gnosis/SafeProxy across the crates finds nothing. There are no Safe contracts and no multisig precompile in crates/torus-evm/src (bloom, eip1559, error, executor, lib, precompile_provider). EVM users could deploy their own Safe bytecode, but that Safe could not sign native actions. On the native side, every SignedNativeAction carries exactly one ActionSignature, which is either Eip712 (secp256k1) or Session (ed25519). resolve_sender maps that one signature to one Address, and the validator/proposer use that address as the actor and nonce key. Design sketch for HL parity: (a) a new action ConvertToMultiSigUser{authorized_users: Vec<Address>, threshold: u8}, which is EIP-712-only and stores a MultiSigConfig on the account; (b) a wrapper action MultiSig{multisig_user, outer_signer, inner: Box<NativeAction>, signatures: Vec<Signature>}. The outer signer must be one of the authorized users. Each inner signature is an EIP-712 signature over (multisig_user, outer_signer, inner action hash, nonce) and must recover to a distinct authorized user, with count >= threshold. The effective sender becomes multisig_user. Once converted, a multisig account's own direct EIP-712 or session signatures are rejected.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:332-340 ActionSignature has only Eip712(Signature) \| Session{session_pubkey, sig}: no multi-signature variant
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:344-349 SessionData{owner, expiry, scope, created_at}: the closest existing delegation primitive (like HL agents), owner -> key; a template for storing MultiSigConfig
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-677 NativeAction enum: orders, transfers, staking, governance, oracle, validator, CreateSession/RevokeSession, market admin; no ConvertToMultiSigUser or MultiSig wrapper
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:951-958 SignedNativeAction{action, nonce, signature: ActionSignature}: a single signature per envelope
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:748-759 requires_eip712() lists which actions may not use session keys; ConvertToMultiSigUser/MultiSig would need adding
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:801-830 resolve_sender: Eip712 -> ecrecover; Session -> ed25519 verify + session_lookup; returns one Address
- crates/torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:368-391 validate loop: sender = resolve_sender(...); the nonce replay key is (sender, nonce) and it pushes (sender, action): the hook point where a MultiSig wrapper would rewrite sender to multisig_user
- crates/torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs:210 same resolve_sender call on the proposer side (must mirror validator)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3210-3214 execute_action(ctx, sender, action) dispatch; 3318-3325 CreateSession/RevokeSession arms (the model for exec_convert_to_multisig)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6164-6200 ActionCategory/classify_action: MultiSig must classify by its inner action
- grep for multisig\|multi_sig\|gnosis\|SafeProxy over crates/: zero hits in code

**Risk:** HL users with team or treasury accounts (vault leaders, market-maker desks, HIP-3 deployers) need M-of-N control over native funds and trading. Today one compromised EOA key or session key gives full control, including Withdraw. A Safe on the EVM side does not help, because the native layer only accepts ECDSA or ed25519 signatures from a single owner, not a contract. Without this, the parity gap blocks institutional use of native features.

**Fix:** 1) torus-types/src/lib.rs: add `pub struct MultiSigConfig{authorized_users: Vec<Address>, threshold: u8}`. Add NativeAction::ConvertToMultiSigUser{config: Option<MultiSigConfig>} (None converts back to a normal user, and that requires multisig approval). Add NativeAction::MultiSig{multisig_user: Address, outer_signer: Address, inner: Box<NativeAction>, signatures: Vec<Signature>}. Update canonical_bytes/append_canonical_bytes and the eip712_struct_hash type strings. Cap authorized_users at 10 and signatures at 10, and reject nested MultiSig. 2) torus-types/src/eip712.rs: add both new actions to requires_eip712. Add `multisig_payload_hash(multisig_user, outer_signer, inner, nonce)` and `fn resolve_multisig(&self, outer: Address, cfg_lookup) -> Result<Address>`, which recovers each inner signature, checks it is in authorized_users, dedups, checks count >= threshold, and checks outer == recovered envelope signer and that outer is authorized. 3) torus-state: add a CF or key prefix `multisig_cfg/{addr}` with get_multisig_config/put_multisig_config, mirroring get_session. 4) torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:368 and proposer.rs:210: after resolve_sender, if the action is MultiSig then sender = resolve_multisig(...)? and the action becomes *inner. Also reject a non-wrapped action whose sender has a MultiSigConfig, including session-signed ones. The nonce key should be (multisig_user, nonce), as on HL. This must be identical in both files, ideally through one shared helper. 5) native_executor.rs:3318 area: add exec_convert_to_multisig(ctx, sender, cfg), which validates 1<=threshold<=len, no dupes, and no self; revokes active sessions on conversion; and writes state through the native trie so it enters the state root. Make classify_action (6177) recurse into inner. 6) RPC: torus-rpc must accept the new variants (serde enum), and info gets userToMultiSigSigners. Tests: threshold met/unmet, a duplicate signer counted once, a non-authorized signer, a direct-signature rejection after conversion, nonce replay of the wrapper, a nested-wrapper rejection, proposer/validator agreement, and a state-root determinism check.

**Unsure:** Not read: the exact eip712_struct_hash per-variant encoding (how new variants are typed), the torus-state session storage functions (get_session location), the torus-rpc submit path, and whether native_executor re-resolves the sender elsewhere (for example crash replay in app.rs). I did not check if any Safe-like contract is deployed at genesis in a non-.rs file (only crates/ .rs/.toml/.md were grepped; there is no contracts/ dir). The `idx` tool was unavailable, so grep was used instead.

</details>

**fable** — absent, impact medium, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~600-900 LOC: types+encoding ~150, state CF/db/backend ~80, eip712 verify ~150, executor arms ~200, RPC ~50, tests ~250

Torus has no multi-sig account concept anywhere: no native action variant, no state table, no signature variant, and no EVM Safe/Gnosis integration (the only "safe" hits in crates/torus-evm are "revert-safety" comments). Native identity is single-signer: `ActionSignature` is a two-variant enum (`Eip712(Signature)` secp256k1 ecrecover, or `Session{session_pubkey, sig}` ed25519 delegating to an `owner: Address` stored in `cf_sessions`), and `SignedNativeAction::resolve_sender` returns exactly one `Address` per action, which `execute_action(ctx, sender, action)` then uses as the account. The closest existing primitive is the session-key machinery (CreateSession/RevokeSession + SessionData{owner,expiry,scope}), which is a 1-to-1 delegation, not an M-of-N authorization. A design sketch grounded in those files is given in `fix`.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:332-340 — `enum ActionSignature { Eip712(Signature), Session{session_pubkey,sig} }`; no multisig variant
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:344-349 — `SessionData{owner, expiry, scope, created_at}`: the only account-delegation state object
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:580-690 — `enum NativeAction` full variant list (orders, transfers, staking, governance, oracle, validator, CreateSession/RevokeSession, admin); no ConvertToMultiSigUser / MultiSig
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:951-957 — `SignedNativeAction{action, nonce, signature: ActionSignature}` single-signature envelope
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:764-774 — `recover_sender` single ecrecover; eip712.rs:801-830 `resolve_sender(current_timestamp, session_lookup)` returns one Address, Session path maps pubkey -> SessionData.owner
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:965-975 — `recover_senders_phase1` parallel ecrecover; session actions deferred to sequential phase 2 (place where multisig verification would also slot)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3210-3214 — `execute_action(ctx, sender: &Address, action)` takes a single pre-resolved sender
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:3318-3324 — CreateSession/RevokeSession dispatch; 5591-5650 `exec_create_session` uses ctx.state.get_session/put_session (pattern to copy for multisig state)
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:123-124 — `CF_SESSIONS` column family; no CF for multisig config
- crates/torus-state/src/db.rs:684-709 — get_session/put_session/delete_session; backend.rs:58-75 StateBackend trait equivalents
- crates/torus-evm/src/executor.rs — grep for safe/multisig/gnosis: only 'revert-safety' comment at line 21; no Safe contract support

**Risk:** HL parity gap: Hyperliquid supports convertToMultiSigUser (a user becomes an M-of-N account controlled by `authorizedUsers` with `threshold`) and the `multiSig` action wrapper (one leader submits an inner action plus N signatures; nonce belongs to the multisig user). Without it, institutional/treasury accounts on Torus cannot be jointly controlled natively; the only workaround is an EVM Safe contract, which cannot sign native CLOB actions at all (native sender is derived purely from ecrecover/session, and no contract-address path exists). Also validator/governance actions (RegisterValidator, SubmitProposal, Vote) are single-key only, which is an operational-security gap for operators.

**Fix:** Design (mirrors HL semantics, grounded in existing files):\n1. types (crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs): add `pub struct MultiSigConfig { authorized_users: Vec<Address>, threshold: u8, created_at: u64 }` next to SessionData (~line 344). Add NativeAction variants `ConvertToMultiSigUser { authorized_users: Vec<Address>, threshold: u8 }` (None/empty + threshold 0 = revert to single-key, per HL) and `MultiSig { multi_sig_user: Address, inner: Box<NativeAction>, inner_nonce: u64, signatures: Vec<Signature> }` in the NativeAction enum (~line 580); extend `canonical_bytes` / `eip712_struct_hash` encoders (lib.rs ~700+, eip712.rs) with the new tags; add both to `requires_eip712` (eip712.rs ~745-758) so session keys cannot wrap them.\n2. state: `CF_MULTISIG` in crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs (after CF_SESSIONS line 124); `get_multisig/put_multisig/delete_multisig` in db.rs (copy 684-709) and the StateBackend trait in backend.rs (copy 58-75).\n3. verification (crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs): in `resolve_sender` (801), keep the outer leader ecrecover; add `SignedNativeAction::verify_multisig<F>(&self, lookup: F)` that for `MultiSig{..}` computes the inner signing hash over (multi_sig_user, inner, inner_nonce) with a distinct EIP-712 type, ecrecovers each sig, dedups, checks every signer in `MultiSigConfig.authorized_users` and count >= threshold, and that the leader is itself an authorized user. Hook into `recover_senders_phase1` (965) phase 2 (sequential, state-aware) alongside session resolution.\n4. executor (crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs): in `execute_action` match (3210) add arms: `ConvertToMultiSigUser` -> `exec_convert_to_multisig(ctx, sender, ..)` (validate 1<=threshold<=len<=~10, reject if sender already has open sessions or is a validator? -- decide), writes CF_MULTISIG; `MultiSig{..}` -> after verify, re-enter `execute_action(ctx, &multi_sig_user, inner)` and consume `(multi_sig_user, inner_nonce)` via the existing nonce path, while the outer `(leader, nonce)` is consumed as usual. Reject nested MultiSig and MultiSig wrapping PlaceOrderBatch unless batch flatten path (execute_batch) is taught about it. A converted user must reject direct Eip712/Session actions (check in phase-2 resolve: if CF_MULTISIG has the sender and action is not MultiSig -> error MultiSigRequired).\n5. RPC (crates/torus-rpc): `torus_userMultiSigConfig(address)` query; EIP-712 typed-data docs for the inner struct.\nTests: eip712.rs unit tests for inner hash determinism and threshold/dup-signer rejection; native_executor tests mirroring the session tests (~5590-5680) for convert/revert/wrapped PlaceOrder/nonce accounting; app.rs differential test that phase1/phase2 ordering is unchanged for non-multisig actions.

**Unsure:** Did not read the nonce-consumption code path or `execute_batch` flatten logic, so the exact place to charge the inner (multi_sig_user, inner_nonce) nonce and how to keep the batch path from bypassing the wrapper is unverified. Did not confirm whether `requires_eip712` is the only session-scope guard. EVM side: only grepped torus-evm/src for safe/multisig/gnosis; a Safe contract could of course be deployed on the EVM without code changes, but there is no bridge from an EVM contract address to native action authorship (resolve_sender is ecrecover-only), which is the real blocker for "Safe-only".

</details>

### thin-book-manipulation

**opus** — confirmed-bug, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: 250-450

Marks, margin, liquidation checks, liquidation execution and RPC mark_price all read only the validator-aggregated oracle price, not the book. The exception is stop orders. Both StopMarket and StopLimit trigger on `last_trade_price` (order_book.rs:1271-1335), and their trigger direction is also validated against `last_trade_price` (order_book.rs:424, 460). Hyperliquid triggers TP/SL on mark price instead. On a thin book with no price bands, a 1-lot print at any price sets LTP (order_book.rs:555) and fires every resting stop on that side. The resulting market orders sweep the thin book, which prints new LTPs, and the cascade loop (up to 10 rounds) fires more stops. The attacker's resting orders collect the fills. Separately, the book has no oracle-relative bands and no OI cap, and the manipulation-resistance of the oracle depends on an external validator feed that is not in this repo. A JELLY-style attack (pumping the external index) therefore hits liquidations directly.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1271-1335 trigger_stops: `let price = match self.last_trade_price`, fire if `current_price >= stop.trigger_price` (buy) / `<=` (sell), converts to OrderType::Market, loops up to 10 times while LTP changes
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:420-470 StopMarket/StopLimit placement validates trigger direction vs last_trade_price
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:555 `self.last_trade_price = Some(last_fill.price)`: any fill of any size sets the trigger price
- torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:192-240 execute_liquidation closes 'at oracle price' and deletes the position, never touching the book, so book prints cannot set the liquidation price
- torus-core/src/margin.rs:194,215 equity/maintenance margin use oracle_price_for(oracle_prices)
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5923-5985 run_liquidation_checks uses oracle_prices only and skips the market if the oracle is missing
- torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1604-1640 get_mark_price: mark_price = index_price = oracle.get_price; last_trade_price is reported as a separate field only
- torus-core/src/oracle.rs:200-260 aggregate_price: stake-weighted median plus outlier rejection; the 10%/block deviation cap applies only when filtered.len()==1
- grep: no producer of SubmitOraclePrices outside native_executor/types, so the validator price source is off-repo
- grep: no open_interest/oi_cap or price-band code in torus-core/torus-bridge

**Risk:** 1) Stop-hunt on a thin market. The attacker posts a resting order just past a stop cluster, then crosses 1 lot at that price. LTP moves, all stops fire as unbounded market orders (no slippage cap, no bands), they sweep the empty book, new prints cascade further, and the attacker's resting orders take the fills. Victims get executed far from the oracle/mark price. On HL the TP/SL trigger is mark, which mixes oracle and a book median, and orders are bounded by oracle bands, so this works far less well. 2) JELLY path. Liquidations close at the oracle price with no counterparty: the position is deleted (liquidation.rs) and any shortfall goes to ADL. Pumping the external index the validators read pushes the oracle up to 10%/block per reporter only in the single-reporter case; with multiple reporters there is no rate limit. With no OI caps, an attacker can build a large position in a thin market and force losses onto the insurance fund or ADL. 3) Since mark = oracle with no book component, the mark cannot be pushed through the book. However, a stale or halted oracle means stale margin while the book trades freely.

**Fix:** (a) In torus-core/src/order_book.rs, give the book a `mark_price: Option<FixedPoint>` set by the executor each block, from the oracle (or HL-style median(oracle+EMA(mid-oracle), book mid, CEX perp)). trigger_stops() and the trigger-direction checks at :424/:460 read mark instead of last_trade_price. Call trigger_stops from the executor after the oracle aggregates in native_executor.rs (aggregate_oracle_prices, ~5904), not from fills. (b) Add oracle price bands in place_order: reject limit orders more than X% from oracle (HL uses 95%/5x style bounds), and cap stop-triggered market orders with a slippage limit (e.g. 10% from mark, as HL does with its 10% market-order slippage). (c) Add a per-market OI cap to MarketMarginConfig, enforced on position increase. (d) Rate-limit the oracle (max bps change per block) whatever the reporter count, in oracle.rs aggregate_price. Tests: thin-book stop-hunt (1-lot print does not trigger stops when the oracle is unchanged), band rejection, OI cap rejection, and an oracle step-limit with 3+ reporters.

**Unsure:** I did not read every place_order call site in native_executor, so an oracle band could exist there that the grep missed. I found no hits for band/oi_cap. I did not inspect the TP/SL (tpsl) or trigger-order paths beyond OrderBook::trigger_stops; there may be a separate HL-style trigger mechanism. I did not verify where off-repo validators get their price (it could be the book's own LTP, which would make the oracle itself manipulable). I did not check funding computation inputs beyond a grep, which showed no LTP/mid use in torus-economics. Separately, liquidation deletes the position with no counterparty, which is an OI-imbalance concern outside this question.

</details>

**fable** — confirmed-bug, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: 150-250

Stop triggers are driven purely by the book's own last_trade_price: OrderBook::trigger_stops (order_book.rs:1272-1340) loops up to 10 times firing every pending stop where last_trade_price crosses trigger_price, converting them to Market/Limit orders in-place; trigger-direction validation at placement (order_book.rs:424,460) also uses last_trade_price. Liquidations do NOT read the book: run_liquidation_checks (native_executor.rs:5923-5965) and LiquidationEngine (liquidation.rs:206,270,312) use validator-submitted oracle prices aggregated by stake-weighted median with MAD outlier rejection (oracle.rs:200-258). The RPC liquidation price (torus.rs:805-813) is a naive entry ± isolated_margin/size that ignores maintenance_factor_bps and the oracle; RPC unrealized PnL uses the oracle, falling back to entry_price (torus.rs:797-801). There is no order-placement price band anywhere (grep for price_band/max_deviation/PriceBand hits only oracle.rs:236-250, which is a 10%/block cap on the oracle when only one reporter survives filtering).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:1272-1340 trigger_stops reads self.last_trade_price only; fires stops as Market orders in a 10-iteration cascade loop
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:424-433,460-469 stop trigger-direction validation compares against last_trade_price
- torus-core/src/order_book.rs:555 last_trade_price set from last fill of any match (any size)
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5923-5965 run_liquidation_checks uses oracle_prices arg; skips market if no oracle price > 0
- torus-core/src/oracle.rs:1,200-258 validator-submitted, stake-weighted median + reject_outliers (3*MAD); oracle.rs:236-250 10% per-block deviation cap only when a single reporter remains
- torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:206,270,312 PnL/liquidation math uses oracle_price
- torus-core/src/margin.rs:195,247,253 margin checks use mark from oracle_price_for (oracle list), not book
- torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:797-813 RPC mark = oracle.get_price fallback entry_price; liquidation_price = entry ± isolated_margin/size (no maintenance factor)
- grep across crates for price_band\|max_deviation\|band_bps\|PriceBand: only torus-core/src/oracle.rs matched — no order-placement band

**Risk:** Concrete path on a thin market (no bands, trigger on last print): attacker (two accounts, or one if self-trades fill rather than cancel) rests a bid at P_trigger where known sell-stops cluster (or simply far below the current print), rests deep bids below, then crosses a dust-size sell into it. One tiny fill sets last_trade_price = P_trigger (order_book.rs:555); trigger_stops fires all sell stops at or above that as Market orders, which walk the thin book into the attacker's resting bids, printing lower, which re-triggers more stops (up to 10 loops in one tx). Attacker buys the stop flow at a discount and closes against the oracle-based mark. Cost is one dust trade; no oracle move needed. Unlike HL JELLY, liquidations here are oracle-only so the cascade cannot directly force liquidations, but it still extracts stop-order holders' margin and, if validators source their oracle submissions from this book (not verified), could feed back into the oracle. HL triggers stops on mark price (oracle/book-EMA/external median) and rejects orders beyond a band from the oracle; this book does neither.

**Fix:** 1) Decouple stop triggering from the fill path: change OrderBook::trigger_stops (order_book.rs:1272) to take `trigger_px: FixedPoint` and make it pub; stop calling it from match/fill (find the call site that sets triggering_stops) and instead add `NativeExecutor::run_stop_triggers(ctx, oracle_prices)` in native_executor.rs next to run_liquidation_checks (:5923), invoked after aggregate_oracle_prices (:5904) each block, passing the aggregated oracle (or a mark = median(oracle, book mid, last) computed in a new `mark_price()` helper in torus-core). Keep last_trade_price only as a fallback when no oracle price exists. Also use the same px for direction validation at order_book.rs:424/460. 2) Add a placement band: in the PlaceOrder exec path (native_executor.rs ~3758 where reserve_for_qty is computed) reject Limit/StopLimit prices more than N bps (config on MarketMarginConfig, e.g. 2000 bps) from the oracle price, and reject Market orders whose fills would cross beyond the band (HL: market orders are IOC limit at ±slippage). 3) Fix RPC liq px (torus.rs:805): compute from the maintenance formula in margin.rs:234-248 (entry, leverage, maintenance_factor_bps) using the oracle mark. Tests: order_book.rs unit test proving a dust fill at trigger_px with stops pending does NOT fire until the executor passes an oracle px; native_executor test for band rejection; rpc test that liquidation_price matches margin.rs maintenance threshold.

**Unsure:** Did not read where trigger_stops is invoked from (presumably end of place_order/match) nor whether self-trade prevention cancels the resting order (self_trade_cancels suggests it does, so attacker needs two accounts). Did not verify where validators source oracle submissions (if from this book's last/mid, the JELLY feedback loop into liquidations is live). Did not inspect torus-consensus app.rs ordering of aggregate_oracle_prices vs order execution within a block.

</details>

### matching-fuzz

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort M, lockstep no · LOC: ~600-900 LOC (≈80 for invariant extensions, ≈200 for book proptest additions, ≈350 for the executor proptest plus its strategies, ≈100 for the cargo-fuzz harness)

There is some property testing, but not much. One proptest file, crates/torus-core/tests/fuzz_tests.rs (126 lines, 200 cases), places, cancels and modifies orders on a bare OrderBook and calls OrderBook::verify_invariants (order_book.rs:926) after each step. verify_invariants checks four things: the book is not crossed (best_bid < best_ask), order_index.len() equals the number of resting orders, every remaining_qty is above zero, and no price level is empty. There is no cargo-fuzz target and no proptest outside torus-core. Margin and value conservation is checked only by stress.rs: verify_value_conservation (sum of available balances plus unrealized PnL is within 1000 raw units of the initial funding), run on deterministic seeded actions in tests marked #[ignore]. It is not a property test and it does not cover the margin, liquidation or funding paths.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:924-955 verify_invariants checks four invariants: not crossed, order_index count matches resting orders, remaining_qty > 0, no empty levels
- crates/torus-core/tests/fuzz_tests.rs:11-43 arb_order_params always uses market_id=1, reduce_only=false, client_order_id=None; price 1..500, qty 1..100, 20 traders; the GTC/IOC/FOK and Limit/Market mix is random
- crates/torus-core/tests/fuzz_tests.rs:45-46 ProptestConfig::with_cases(200)
- crates/torus-core/tests/fuzz_tests.rs:59-65 the only per-fill check is fill.quantity > 0 (no check of fill price against the limit, of priority, or of qty conservation)

- crates/torus-core/tests/fuzz_tests.rs:100-125 the modify test only ever sets qty to fp(1) on the most recent resting order; price is never modified

- crates/torus-core/src/order_book/matching_entry_tests.rs:190-226 exhaustive grid differential test of new vs legacy matching traversal, which calls verify_invariants
- crates/torus-integration-tests/tests/stress.rs:85-123 verify_all_book_invariants plus verify_value_conservation (available + unrealized ≈ initial, epsilon 1000 raw)

**Risk:** Matching and margin are the code paths most likely to break consensus, and today they have only shallow, single-crate property coverage. Bugs that would go unnoticed include: order_index or trader_orders pointing at the wrong price or side; price-time priority violations; fills priced through the taker's limit; taker or maker quantity not conserved; tick or lot misalignment; reduce_only increasing a position; long and short open interest not matching; fees or insurance-fund flows not conserving value; accounts ending a block below maintenance margin without being liquidated. Any of these could change the state root silently or let value leak. Hyperliquid parity needs at least executor-level conservation and margin-health invariants under randomized action streams that include liquidations and funding.

**Fix:** 1) Add more checks to OrderBook::verify_invariants (order_book.rs:926): every order_index entry resolves to an order at the recorded side and price; trader_orders equals the set of resting ids grouped by owner; seq increases within each level (FIFO); every price is a multiple of tick and every qty a multiple of lot; the pending_stops ordering check (cf. :1378); with the level_hash_cache enabled, the cache equals a scratch recompute. 2) In fuzz_tests.rs, add per-op checks: sum of fill qty + remaining == original qty for the taker; each fill price is within the taker's limit and equals the maker's resting price; fills come out in price-time order; FOK either fills completely or produces no fills; IOC never rests. Also widen the strategies to cover price modify, reduce_only, several market_ids, client_order_id, post-only/ALO and stop orders, and raise cases to 1000+ behind a PROPTEST_CASES env var. 3) New crates/torus-bridge/tests/executor_prop.rs: a proptest over Vec<(Address, NativeAction)> (place, cancel, oracle/mark update, funding tick, liquidation) run through NativeExecutor::execute_batch. After each batch assert value conservation including fees (balances + unrealized PnL + fee sinks + insurance fund == deposits), long OI == short OI per market, no non-liquidated account below maintenance margin, and two runs giving the same state root. 4) Add cargo-fuzz under fuzz/ with a target that decodes arbitrary bytes into action sequences, runs them through the executor, and calls the same invariant fn. 5) Move stress.rs verify_value_conservation into a shared test-util so the proptest and stress suites both use it, and un-ignore a smaller version.

**Unsure:** I did not read the margin.rs or liquidation.rs unit tests, so there may be targeted (non-property) margin-health tests there. I did not check whether parallel_settle_tests.rs:390 uses a seeded randomized approach similar to the level_rows differential tests. I did not confirm that stress.rs conservation accounts for fees (fee sinks seem to be excluded, which would point to fee-free test configs). Git history shows the GitHub Actions workflow was archived in s80 (commit 3857955; I did not open it), so I did not verify whether the proptests run anywhere automatically.

</details>

### bench-trading-semantics

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort L, lockstep no · LOC: ~600-1000 (generator mix ~250, oracle walker ~100, invariant checks ~200, differential test ~300); populating margin_configs is a separate consensus change

The load generators (tools/bench-throughput, tools/tx-flood, matched-bench) send only GTC Limit orders with reduce_only=false. The action set is PlaceOrder, PlaceOrderBatch, CancelOrder, CancelAllOrders, CreateSession and RevokeSession. They never send StopMarket/StopLimit, Market, IOC/ALO, ModifyOrder, reduce-only orders, oracle price updates, transfers or withdraws. The benches do cover multiple markets (--markets, --markets-per-sender) and many traders, with 20 senders by default and econ mode scaling to thousands of senders. But econ mode pins each (sender, market) pair to one side by parity, so positions only ever grow: apply_fill's reduce and close paths, realized PnL, STP and self-trade never run. The mid price stays fixed, and the code's own comment says liquidation never runs because margin_configs is never populated. A grep found inserts into it only in tests. The only correctness check at scale is matched-bench's cross-node agreement: block hash, header stateRoot (0x0 on this branch), and a sha256 digest over order books, open interest and the balances of 50 senders. That catches nondeterminism but not wrong-but-deterministic accounting.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- tools/bench-throughput/src/main.rs:239-262 random_place_order: always OrderType::Limit, TimeInForce::GTC, reduce_only:false, random side around a 60k mid
- tools/bench-throughput/src/main.rs:584-620 econ_place_order: Limit/GTC/reduce_only:false, fixed mid +/- band ticks
- tools/bench-throughput/src/main.rs:571-578 econ_side_is_buy: one side per (sender,market), comment says 'apply_fill's reduce/close paths never trigger'
- tools/bench-throughput/src/main.rs:491-498 comment: CancelOrder releases only the unfilled part; maker-fill margin is 'permanently stranded'; 'liquidation never runs (it iterates the empty margin_configs)'
- tools/bench-throughput/src/main.rs:513-516 crossing shape avoids self-trade/STP on purpose
- tools/bench-throughput/src/main.rs:622-646 econ_action: only CancelAllOrders{market_id:None} or PlaceOrder/PlaceOrderBatch
- tools/bench-throughput/src/main.rs:132-145 --markets / --markets-per-sender multi-market and locality shapes (multi-market IS covered)
- grep of NativeAction:: in bench-throughput: only CancelAllOrders, CancelOrder, CreateSession, PlaceOrder, PlaceOrderBatch, RevokeSession
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:1072-1082 OrderType has Market, StopMarket, StopLimit, none of which the benches send
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:594 NativeAction::ModifyOrder exists, but the benches never send it
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1842 margin_configs: HashMap::new(); a grep found inserts only in crates/torus-bridge/tests/maker_margin_release_tests.rs:500,503,664
- tools/matched-bench/README.md:106-113 agreement = block hash + header stateRoot (0x0 on this branch) + RPC digest of order books/OI/balances of 50 bench senders; native state root not exposed
- grep of tools/bench-throughput, tools/tx-flood and bench/ for TriggerOrder\|ModifyOrder\|Liquidat\|reduce_only: true\|Market,: no hits

**Risk:** Most of the hard state-machine paths are never exercised under load: realized PnL and position reduce, flip and close; stop triggering on a moving mark; liquidation and ADL with socialized loss; modify (cancel-replace margin re-reservation); reduce-only clamping; IOC/Market margin release; and funding over a moving oracle price. These paths are where Hyperliquid-class bugs hide: margin leaks, double release, negative balances, OI drift and nondeterministic trigger ordering across parallel market workers. All three nodes would agree on the same wrong numbers, and the digest only checks 50 senders, so a deterministic accounting bug passes the agreement gate. Reported throughput (~90k fills/s) is for the cheapest path. Parity throughput with real liquidation and trigger scans per block is unmeasured. Because margin_configs is empty in production, liquidation is effectively dead code on a live chain, which is a correctness gap in its own right, not just a bench gap.

**Fix:** 1) Add a `--mix` mode to tools/bench-throughput/src/main.rs: a weighted generator next to econ_action that sends ModifyOrder, IOC and Market orders, StopMarket/StopLimit with triggers near the mid, reduce_only closes, and per-sender side flips, so apply_fill's reduce, close and flip paths run. 2) Move the mid with a random walk. A designated oracle sender issues SubmitOraclePrices (or UpdateMarketParams) each N blocks, so stops fire and positions go underwater. 3) Populate margin_configs from genesis or ListMarket for bench markets (native_executor.rs:1842 currently builds an empty HashMap) so liquidation actually runs, and add a high-leverage cohort that is meant to get liquidated. 4) In tools/matched-bench/summarize.py, next to the agreement block (~line 754), add invariant checks on the quiesced state, not just cross-node equality: sum of all balances + order_margin + insurance == genesis supply; sum of longs == sum of shorts == OI per market; no negative available balance; and order_margin equal to the sum of resting-order reservations for every sender. That means digesting all senders, not 50. 5) Add a proptest/differential test in crates/torus-bridge/tests that replays the mixed generator through native_executor and compares against a simple single-threaded reference ledger. That is how you catch deterministic-but-wrong results from the parallel market workers.

**Unsure:** I did not read tools/tx-flood/src/main.rs beyond a grep, which found no trigger, modify or liquidation actions. I did not check whether the maker-margin leak described in the bench comment (main.rs:494-497) is now fixed: crates/torus-bridge/tests/maker_margin_release_tests.rs suggests it might be, in which case the comment is stale. I also did not check whether trigger and stop orders are fully wired in native_executor (book_reader.rs has StopRow), or whether margin_configs gets populated through some path other than a direct insert, such as UpdateMarketParams or ListMarket handlers assigning the whole map. Populating margin_configs on a live chain would change state transitions and so would be consensus-breaking; the bench-only changes are not.

</details>

Oracle outage or an empty book would currently show as a quiet dashboard rather than a page.

**Fix:** 1) crates/torus-telemetry/src/lib.rs: add Family<Vec<(String,String)>, Gauge/Counter> keyed by market: fills_total{market}, fill_notional_total{market}, open_interest{market}, mark_price{market}, oracle_price{market}, oracle_age_blocks{market}, oracle_reporters{market}, funding_rate{market}, book_best_bid/best_ask/spread{market}, book_depth_levels{market,side}, liquidations_total{market}, liquidation_notional_total{market}, oracle_missing_skipped_liquidations_total{market}, plus global insurance_fund_balance. 2) native_executor.rs: at the three orders_matched.inc_by sites (4247/4573/5101) also inc fills_total/fill_notional by market; at 5961 inc oracle_missing_skipped_liquidations_total instead of only tracing::warn; at 5968 add market label + notional from lr. 3) crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1883 (end-of-block hook that sets exec_resting_orders): iterate markets and set OI (reuse the logic behind torus-rpc get_open_interest, torus.rs:1557), oracle_age_blocks = block_height - OraclePrice.block_number, oracle_reporters, best_bid/best_ask/spread from OrderBook (order_book.rs:798-808), insurance-fund balance from liquidation.rs state. 4) monitoring/alerts/trading.yml: OracleStale (oracle_age_blocks > max_oracle_age), OracleSkippedLiquidations rate>0, InsuranceFundDrop (delta<0 over 1h), SpreadBlowout, OIDrop, LiquidationNotionalSpike. 5) monitoring/dashboards/trading.json: per-market panels for the above. Tests: extend crates/torus-bridge/tests/funnel_metrics_tests.rs with per-market fill/liquidation label assertions and an oracle-missing-skip counter test.

**Unsure:** Did not read liquidation.rs to confirm whether an insurance fund balance is actually tracked as state or only mentioned; did not confirm whether funding rate / mark price state exists in torus-core (grep for funding_rate in core/economics returned no pub items in the time box). view_metrics.rs had no pub fields matched by my grep; may hold consensus-only metrics. Dashboard JSON expressions were sampled via grep, not read in full.

### evm-corewriter-latency

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: stop-order fix ~20; results CF + read precompile + RPC ~250; configurable delay/range drain ~80; ordering change ~10 + tests ~150

CoreWriter (0x0810) and CoreWriterStaking (0x0811) do not execute anything during the EVM call. They write a QueuedAction into CF_CORE_WRITER_QUEUE under the key (block_queued+1, seq), through the EVM tx's journaled overlay, so a reverted frame drops the write. In block N+1, NativeExecutor::drain_core_writer runs the queued actions after both native execute_batch calls and before governance, fees and epoch. In effect the delay is one block, and queued EVM actions always run after every native action in that block. HL works differently: it delays CoreWriter actions by a few seconds and runs them after the EVM block. Torus has no feedback path at all. drain_core_writer's Vec<NativeActionResult> (and any drain error) is thrown away with `let _ =` in app.rs. No receipt, log or queryable status reaches EVM or RPC. placeOrder hands back a made-up order_id ((block+1)<<64|seq) that is not the real core order id. On top of that, StopMarket/StopLimit (order_type 2/3) pass validation but are silently turned into Limit orders, and the TorusBlock.core_writer_actions field is always empty or unused.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:779-863 core_writer validates and enqueues QueuedAction{block_queued: current_block}; placeOrder returns synthetic order_id ((current_block+1)<<64 \| seq), cancelAll returns 0
- torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:1000-1015 CoreWriterQueue::enqueue: target_block = block_queued + 1, key = target_block BE ++ seq BE, so it is a fixed one-block delay with no time-based delay
- torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:1019-1040 drain iterates prefix and silently skips entries that fail borsh decode (no error, entry deleted)
- torus-evm/src/executor.rs:21-50 NativeJournalInspector checkpoints/reverts the writer-precompile journal per call frame (revert-safe enqueue)
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5870-5900 drain_core_writer: drains queue for ctx.block_height, guards block_queued >= height, executes via Self::execute and returns results
- torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6266-6310 core_writer_to_native: reduce_only=false, client_order_id=None; decode_order_type maps 2/3 (Stop*) to Limit
- torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1585 EVM executor invoked before native ctx is built (EVM in block N enqueues for N+1)
- torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1902-1937 execute_batch(pre_evm), execute_batch(post_evm), then `let _ = NativeExecutor::drain_core_writer(&mut ctx);` throws away the results and errors
- torus-types/src/lib.rs:408-409 TorusBlock.core_writer_actions documented as 'from previous block's EVM' but proposer.rs:164,298 always set vec![]

**Risk:** If EVM contracts (vaults, strategies) can't see CoreWriter outcomes, they can't tell whether an action failed. They read back the fake order_id, which can't be used to cancel, because cancelOrder needs the real core id. Stop orders sent from EVM quietly become resting limit orders at the trigger price, which can produce wrong-side fills (a correctness/funds risk). Running queued actions after all of block N+1's native actions is deterministic, but it differs from HL's documented ordering. Because the delay is exactly one block (around 70ms or whatever the block time is) rather than HL's few seconds, EVM-to-core front-running mitigation is weaker than in HL. A queued entry that fails to decode is deleted with no trace.

**Fix:** 1) Bug fix (small): in native_executor.rs decode_order_type, map 2/3 to the real stop variants, or reject them in core_writer (precompiles.rs:801) until stops are supported. Add a test in torus-core/tests/precompile_tests.rs or native_bridge_tests.rs. 2) Feedback: in app.rs:1937, keep drain_core_writer's results. Persist each result keyed by (target_block, seq) in a new CF (e.g. CF_CORE_WRITER_RESULTS, in torus-state/src/cf.rs) with ok/err, the real order_id and an error string. Expose it through a read precompile (e.g. a coreWriterStatus(uint64 block, uint64 seq) view next to 0x0800-range readers) and an RPC method in torus-rpc. Optionally emit a synthetic log/receipt. Return the drain Err as fatal_error instead of ignoring it. 3) HL-style delay: change CoreWriterQueue::enqueue to key on a target timestamp or a configurable target_block = block_queued + DELAY_BLOCKS (a governance param), and drain all keys <= the current block (a range scan, not an exact prefix). 4) Ordering: either document that 'queued EVM actions run after all native actions of the drain block', or move drain_core_writer ahead of execute_batch(pre_evm) so it matches HL's 'EVM block then its core actions' sequencing. Both choices need a pinned determinism test in crates/torus-integration-tests/tests/cross_vm_write.rs. 5) Either remove TorusBlock.core_writer_actions or populate and verify it. Changing it alters the block wire format.

**Unsure:** I did not read sort_native_actions or the EVM execution block around app.rs:1570-1600 in full, so the exact pre_evm/post_evm semantics and whether EVM state commits before the native ctx were not verified. I did not check whether torus-rpc already exposes CF_CORE_WRITER_QUEUE pending entries; torus-rpc/src/lib.rs references CoreWriter but I didn't read it. I did not read the staking path's (core_writer_staking at precompiles.rs:869-945) validation. HL's exact delay semantics are from memory: actions are delayed a few seconds and run after the EVM block, with no on-EVM failure callback. I also did not verify whether the order_type 2/3 to Limit downgrade is covered by an existing test.

</details>

**fable** — partial, impact medium, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: 150-300

CoreWriter (precompile 0x0810, staking 0x0811) enqueues actions into CF_CORE_WRITER_QUEUE keyed by (block_queued+1, seq) through the per-tx journaled StateBackend overlay (so a reverted EVM tx drops the enqueue, T4.4), and NativeExecutor::drain_core_writer executes exactly the entries keyed to the current height after both native execute_batch phases of that block. So the delay is deterministic one block (not HL's wall-clock "few seconds"), and drained actions run after all native actions of block N+1, not interleaved. Failure feedback to EVM is absent: drain results are discarded with `let _ =` in app.rs, no event/receipt/RPC exposes them, and placeOrder returns a synthetic order_id ((block+1)<<64|seq) that is not what the engine assigns at execution (core_writer_to_native sets client_order_id: None), so the EVM caller cannot correlate or cancel its order. TorusBlock.core_writer_actions is always vec![] in proposer/app (unwired field).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:779-862 core_writer(): placeOrder/cancelOrder/cancelAll build QueuedAction{block_queued: current_block} and return order_id = ((current_block+1)<<64)\|seq
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:1000-1012 CoreWriterQueue::enqueue: target_block = block_queued+1, key = target_block BE \|\| seq BE, put_cf_raw via StateBackend (journaled overlay)
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:1017-1040 drain(): prefix-iterate current block, delete entries; malformed entries silently dropped
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5870-5900 drain_core_writer: drain at ctx.block_height, skip if block_queued >= block_height, execute via Self::execute, returns Vec<NativeActionResult>
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1902-1903,1937: execute_batch(pre_evm), execute_batch(post_evm), then `let _ = NativeExecutor::drain_core_writer(&mut ctx)` — results discarded; same at app.rs:12928
- crates/torus-bridge/src/validator.rs:330-339 documented order: native cancels, non-GTC, EVM txs, GTC, CoreWriter drain, lockbox, oracle, governance, liquidation, fees
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:6266-6285 core_writer_to_native: PlaceOrder with client_order_id: None, reduce_only false
- crates/torus-evm/src/executor.rs:20-35 NativeJournalInspector: writer-precompile journal checkpoint/commit/revert per call frame (T4.4)
- crates/torus-bridge/src/proposer.rs:164,298 and app.rs:1243 core_writer_actions: vec![] — block field never populated
- docs/Torus-hyperBFT-review.md:111 earlier finding of direct RocksDB writes from precompiles (now addressed by T4.4 overlay per executor.rs:24)

**Risk:** HL parity: HL CoreWriter actions are also fire-and-forget with no EVM-side failure feedback, so the discarded results match HL semantics in spirit; but HL exposes resulting order ids/cloids and failures through the core API, whereas Torus returns a synthetic order_id the engine never uses, so EVM contracts cannot cancel or track orders they placed (cancelOrder(bytes32) with that id will target a nonexistent order). The delay is one block (~sub-second at Torus block times) versus HL's few-second delay — shorter, but the stated anti-frontrunning intent is preserved since the action is invisible until N+1. Drain errors from CoreWriterQueue::drain are swallowed (`let _ =`), so a backend error silently loses queued actions and diverges from the documented FIX EVM-FIND-12 intent.

**Fix:** 1) Make the EVM-returned id real: either (a) have core_writer_to_native set client_order_id = Some(synthetic id) and have CancelOrder resolve via the cloid index, or (b) reserve the engine order id at enqueue time (expose book.next_order_id reservation through StateBackend) — touch precompiles.rs:core_writer and native_executor.rs:core_writer_to_native/execute PlaceOrder. 2) Persist drain results: change app.rs:1937 and :12928 to capture Vec<NativeActionResult>, log errors, and emit them into the block's exec receipts / a `core_writer_results` RPC (torus-rpc/src/lib.rs) so contracts/off-chain can observe failures (HL-style core API visibility). 3) Populate TorusBlock.core_writer_actions from the drained set (or delete the field) so block bodies are self-describing for replay. Tests: integration test in crates/torus-integration-tests/tests/cross_vm_write.rs: placeOrder via EVM in block N, assert order resting in N+1 with id matching the precompile return value, cancelOrder with that id succeeds in N+2; test that drain errors surface in results.

**Unsure:** Did not confirm where EVM transactions execute inside app.rs relative to pre_evm/post_evm batches (sort_native_actions at app.rs:1812 splits them, but the EVM execute_block call site was not located in the time box) — the validator.rs doc order (EVM between non-GTC and GTC) is assumed. Did not read the engine's PlaceOrder id assignment to prove the synthetic id mismatch; inferred from core_writer_to_native passing client_order_id: None and book.next_order_id() being the engine's id source. Did not verify whether any RPC or fill-sink exposes drained results indirectly.

</details>

### precompile-coverage-plan

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: ~500-700 LOC for the 10 state-backed readers plus tests; spot/vault/token readers depend on new subsystems (thousands of LOC)

Torus has 4 reader precompiles, each with a few selectors, plus 3 writers. They are 0x0800 OrderBookReader (getOrderBook, getPosition, getOpenOrders), 0x0801 BalanceReader (getBalances, getMarkets), 0x0802 OracleReader (getPrice, getAllPrices) and 0x0803 StakingReader (getStakingInfo, getValidators). The writers are 0x0810, 0x0811 and 0x0820. Hyperliquid instead uses one precompile per query, starting at 0x...0800 (position 0x800, spotBalance 0x801, userVaultEquity 0x802, withdrawable 0x803, delegations 0x804, delegatorSummary 0x805, markPx 0x806, oraclePx 0x807, spotPx 0x808, l1BlockNumber 0x809, perpAssetInfo 0x80a, spotInfo 0x80b, tokenInfo 0x80c, then bbo and accountMarginSummary after that). Torus also reuses 0x0800-0x0803 for different ABIs, so an HL-written contract calling 0x800/0x801/0x802/0x803 will hit the wrong decoder and revert with UnknownSelector. Coverage, judged by whether the underlying data exists: position is partial (in getPosition). oraclePx is present (getPrice). delegations and delegatorSummary are partial (getStakingInfo only returns the total and the first validator). withdrawable, markPx, bbo, l1BlockNumber, perpAssetInfo and accountMarginSummary can be built from existing state and helpers. spotBalance, spotPx, spotInfo, tokenInfo and userVaultEquity have no backing state, because there are no spot or vault column families.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:30-36 address constants are 0x0800-0x0803 readers and 0x0810/0x0811/0x0820 writers
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:47-52 precompile_gas is a flat GAS_PRECOMPILE_READ for 0x0800..=0x0803
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:65,76-80 ALL_PRECOMPILE_ADDRESSES has 7 entries and is_precompile matches 0x0800..=0x0803\|0x0810..=0x0811\|0x0820
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:313-320 dispatch match in execute_precompile_inner, keyed by address and then by selector
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:425-466 read_position returns (int128 signedSize, entry, uPnL from the oracle, realized, isolatedMargin) and has no leverage or cross flag; HL's Position is (int64 szi, uint64 entryNtl, int64 isolatedRawUsd, uint32 leverage, bool isIsolated)
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:519-546 read_balances returns available, evm balance, order_margin and available again; the last word is a duplicate placeholder, and these are the raw inputs for a withdrawable value
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:591-610 read_oracle_price reads CF_NATIVE_ORACLE as a 16B price plus an 8B block; it is the oraclePx equivalent, and the same layout already carries a block number
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:685-737 read_staking_info scans CF_STAKING_DELEGATIONS by the 20B staker prefix but returns only the total and the first validator; this is roughly HL's delegatorSummary, with no per-validator delegations array
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:179-199 cross_margin_equity(positions, trader, oracle_prices) and total_maintenance_margin are reusable for accountMarginSummary and withdrawable
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:798,803 best_bid/best_ask exist on OrderBook; crates/torus-core/src/book_reader.rs:319 read_book_depth and :419 read_last_trade_price are layout-aware readers usable for bbo and markPx
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:4-159 CF list has no spot, token or vault column family (only CF_NATIVE_BALANCES/POSITIONS/MARKETS/ORACLE etc.)
- crates/torus-evm/src/precompile_provider.rs:145-152 warm_addresses/contains are driven entirely by ALL_PRECOMPILE_ADDRESSES and is_precompile, so new addresses need changes only in torus-core

**Risk:** HL contracts (for example hyper-evm-lib's L1Read.sol) call fixed addresses with selector-less, ABI-tuple inputs such as abi.encode(user, uint16 perp). On Torus those calls land on 0x0800-0x0803, which expect a 4-byte selector, so they fail or decode the wrong data. Every HL L1Read consumer (vaults, lending, perp hooks) is therefore unportable as written. Units also differ: HL uses uint64 with szDecimals/weiDecimals, while Torus returns 128-bit FixedPoint raw values.

**Fix:** Plan, cheapest first, all in crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs, with no EVM-crate changes beyond what follows from ALL_PRECOMPILE_ADDRESSES.
(0) Address-space decision, which is consensus-relevant. Move the Torus selector-style readers out of HL's range: keep them as legacy at 0x0800-0x0803 behind a fork height, or relocate them to e.g. 0x0900-0x0903. Then add HL-ABI readers at 0x0800-0x0810 that take abi.encode(args) with no selector. Raise the ALL_PRECOMPILE_ADDRESSES size, update the is_precompile / is_reader_precompile / precompile_gas ranges, and add arms to the execute_precompile_inner match at :313.
(1) Can be done now with existing state, about 20-60 LOC each, one fn plus one dispatch arm each:
- l1BlockNumber: return current_block, which is already passed in.
- oraclePx(uint32 idx): reuse read_oracle_price/get_oracle_price_fp and convert to a uint64 scaled value.
- markPx: use get_oracle_price_fp, or book_reader::read_last_trade_price as a fallback (HL mark is a median of oracle, book mid and last trade; start by mirroring Torus's liquidation mark).
- position(user, perp): rework read_position into HL's tuple; leverage and isIsolated come from Position.margin_type.
- withdrawable(user): NativeBalance.available - order_margin - total_maintenance_margin, clamped at zero.
- accountMarginSummary(perpDex, user): MarginEngine::cross_margin_equity plus total_maintenance_margin, plus an ntlPos sum over positions_for_trader.
- bbo(asset): best_bid/best_ask via book_reader (layout-aware like read_order_book at :373), returning (uint64 bid, uint64 ask).
- delegatorSummary(user): reuse the read_staking_info scan; add undelegated and nPendingWithdrawals as 0 until unbonding is tracked.
- delegations(user): same prefix scan, but emit a Delegation[] (validator, amount, lockedUntil).
- perpAssetInfo(perp): decode the CF_NATIVE_MARKETS value (coin, szDecimals, maxLeverage).
(2) Blocked on missing state (needs spot, token and vault subsystems first): spotBalance, spotPx, spotInfo, tokenInfo, userVaultEquity. Reserve their addresses and return a revert such as "unsupported", or zeros, so contracts can feature-detect.
Shared helpers to add once: hl_abi::decode_args (no selector) and a FixedPoint-to-u64 scaler per market szDecimals.
Tests: one per precompile in crates/torus-evm/tests/evm_tests.rs and crates/torus-integration-tests/tests/cross_vm_read.rs, calling it with HL-encoded input and asserting the decoded tuple. Also a dispatch test asserting that the legacy addresses stay routed below the fork height.

**Unsure:** I gave HL's exact addresses and tuple layouts for bbo (0x80e?) and accountMarginSummary (0x80f?) from memory and did not check them against hyper-evm-lib L1Read.sol; that should be done before implementing. I did not read the CF_NATIVE_MARKETS value format (whether it holds szDecimals or maxLeverage) or Position.margin_type and leverage fields. I did not check whether the RPC or consensus layer gates reader addresses elsewhere. I did not read the precompile_provider.rs run() body at lines 69-104.

</details>

**fable** — partial, impact medium, effort M, lockstep yes · LOC: ~200 LOC precompiles.rs + ~150 LOC tests; spot/vault/token precompiles out of scope (need new state)

Torus has 4 reader precompiles (0x0800-0x0803) exposing 9 selectors: getOrderBook/getPosition/getOpenOrders (0x0800), getBalances/getMarkets (0x0801), getPrice/getAllPrices (0x0802), getStakingInfo/getValidators (0x0803). Against HL's 15 L1Read precompiles: position, oraclePx, delegations/delegatorSummary (partially, via getStakingInfo), and markPx-as-oracle are covered; bbo, accountMarginSummary, withdrawable, l1BlockNumber, perpAssetInfo and a true markPx are NOT exposed but every input they need already exists as a native helper; spotBalance, userVaultEquity, spotInfo, tokenInfo are ABSENT at the state layer (no spot/token/vault CFs exist in torus-state cf.rs), so they cannot be added cheaply. All reads are hand-rolled ABI (no alloy-sol-types) with a flat 2,600 gas and run through one dispatcher, so adding selectors is mechanical.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:30-33 — four reader address consts 0x0800-0x0803; :47-53 precompile_gas flat GAS_PRECOMPILE_READ=2600 for all readers
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:288-324 execute_precompile_inner: dispatch match on id, read_only default-deny via is_reader_precompile (:87-89 range 0x0800..=0x0803)
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:330-345 order_book_reader selectors getOrderBook/getPosition/getOpenOrders; :425-466 read_position returns (signedSize, entryPx, uPnL, rPnL, isolatedMargin) == HL position minus leverage/liquidationPx
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:505-513 balance_reader: getBalances(address)/getMarkets(); :519-546 read_balances returns native available, EVM balance, order_margin, available
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:573-585 oracle_reader getPrice(bytes32)/getAllPrices(); :654-663 get_oracle_price_fp reads CF_NATIVE_ORACLE
- crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs:671-679 staking_reader getStakingInfo/getValidators; :685-733 read_staking_info sums CF_STAKING_DELEGATIONS, returns (delegated, permanent, rewards, firstValidator) — only first validator, not per-validator list
- crates/torus-evm/src/precompile_provider.rs:69-143 run(): gas check, execute_precompile(_read_only)(&address,input,caller,&self.journal,self.current_block) — current_block already threaded in (l1BlockNumber is free)
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:179-199 cross_margin_equity(positions,trader,oracle_prices); :202-229 total_maintenance_margin(...,config,oracle_prices) — inputs for accountMarginSummary/withdrawable exist
- crates/torus-core/src/book_reader.rs:319 read_book_depth(state,market,layout)->BookDepth{bids,asks} and :419 read_last_trade_price — inputs for bbo and markPx
- crates/torus-rpc/src/torus.rs:1604-1640 get_mark_price: mark==oracle price; last trade from book_reader (no HL-style mark formula)
- crates/torus-state/src/cf.rs:41-45,61-64,74 — only perps CFs (orders/positions/balances/order_books/markets/oracle/staking); no spot, token, or vault CF; grep for 'vault' across crates/*/src returned nothing

**Risk:** HL-native contracts (vaults, margin-aware lending, liquidation bots) read accountMarginSummary/withdrawable/bbo/markPx from L1Read; without them EVM dapps cannot be ported, and markPx currently aliases oracle px so any ported pricing logic diverges. spot/token/vault precompiles are blocked by missing state, not by precompile plumbing.

**Fix:** Keep the 4 addresses (don't renumber; HL uses 0x800-0x80e but Torus id space is already in contracts/tests) and add selectors to existing readers in crates/torus-core/src/precompiles.rs, each a new `else if sel == selector_for(...)` branch plus a `read_*` fn using abi::encode_*: (1) 0x0800 `getBbo(bytes32)` -> (uint128 bid, uint128 ask): call book_reader::detect_layout + read_book_depth, take bids[0]/asks[0]; ~25 LOC. (2) 0x0802 `getMarkPrice(bytes32)` -> uint128: reuse read_last_trade_price + oracle fp (same as RPC get_mark_price); `getL1BlockNumber()` -> uint64 from the `current_block` already passed into oracle_reader; ~20 LOC. (3) 0x0801 `getAccountMarginSummary(address)` -> (int128 accountValue, uint128 marginUsed, uint128 ntlPos, int128 rawUsd): build oracle_prices via read_all_oracle_prices path, call margin::cross_margin_equity and total_maintenance_margin through a PositionManager over the StateBackend; `getWithdrawable(address)` = max(0, equity - initial margin - order_margin); ~60 LOC. (4) 0x0800 `getPerpAssetInfo(bytes32)` -> (maxLeverage, tickSize, lotSize, active) from CF_NATIVE_MARKETS value (read_markets already decodes the active byte at :549-560; extend to decode the market borsh struct); ~30 LOC. (5) 0x0803 `getDelegations(address)` -> (address[] validators, uint128[] amounts) by extending the existing CF_STAKING_DELEGATIONS prefix scan in read_staking_info to emit arrays via abi::encode_arrays_response; `getDelegatorSummary` = existing getStakingInfo renamed/aliased; ~30 LOC. Gas: give margin summary/delegations GAS_PRECOMPILE_COMPLEX-ish by switching precompile_gas to per-selector (decode selector before cost in precompile_provider.rs:run). Tests: add to the existing precompiles.rs test module one ABI round-trip per new selector against an in-memory StateDb with a seeded position/book/oracle. Defer spotBalance/spotInfo/tokenInfo/userVaultEquity until spot tokens and vaults exist in torus-state.

**Unsure:** Did not read crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs PositionManager constructor to confirm it can wrap &impl StateBackend (NativeStateOverlay) without cloning; did not read CF_NATIVE_MARKETS value layout for perpAssetInfo fields; did not verify whether torus-economics has any spot-token or vault module under a different name than 'vault'. consensus_breaking=true because new selectors change EVM execution results for calls that previously reverted with UnknownSelector; needs a fork/height gate.

</details>

### astra-audit-status

**opus** — partial, impact high, effort L, lockstep yes · LOC: 800-1500 across all 26; top 6 priorities ~400

None of the 26 candidate findings in docs/audits/astra-round2-2026-09-24.md is fixed on current main. Since the audit was preserved in commit 6087761, main has 87 commits. Every non-perf commit among them is s73–s80 work on hotstuff rejoin, trade streams, the RPC decimal format, or telemetry, and none mentions an Astra item. I checked 15 of the findings in the code and all 15 are still present unchanged. ### parity-roadmap-order

**opus** — design, impact high, effort XL, lockstep yes · LOC: ~1500-3000 LOC across P1-P5 plus tests; the roadmap doc edit itself is ~60 lines

The roadmap at docs/Torus-hyperBFT-roadmap.md covers only performance and liveness, in Tiers 0 to 4. It has no product-parity track, even though several trading features are missing or not wired up. `LiquidationEngine` exists in `torus-core/src/liquidation.rs`, but `NativeExecutor::run_liquidation_checks` (native_executor.rs:5923) has no callers anywhere in the crates, so nothing drives liquidations. No fee schedule symbols exist (fee_bps, taker_fee, maker_fee and FeeSchedule all return nothing). Funding exists only as a `max_funding_rate_bps` market parameter in torus-types. `reduce_only` is stored and serialized in order_book.rs, but I found no function that enforces it. Proposal: add a "Tier P (product parity)" that starts once Tier 1 is done, runs alongside Tiers 2 and 3, and must land before T4.2 and T4.3. Nearly all of it is LOCKSTEP because it changes execution output and the state root. Inside the tier the order is: P1 wire the liquidation driver, then P2 enforce reduce-only, then P3 fees routed to the insurance fund, then P4 funding, then P5 finish margin modes.

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- docs/Torus-hyperBFT-roadmap.md:1 — the title says 'Performance & Correctness Roadmap'; no tier covers trading features
- docs/Torus-hyperBFT-roadmap.md:20 — defines the LOCAL / LOCKSTEP / CONSENSUS-SAFETY labels this proposal reuses
- docs/Torus-hyperBFT-roadmap.md:89-94 — T1.4 is already a lockstep fleet deploy, so it is a natural window to bundle the first product upgrade

- docs/Torus-hyperBFT-roadmap.md:193 — T4.3 caches margin and settlement (LOCAL); if it lands before fees and funding change settlement, the caching has to be redone
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5922-5960 — run_liquidation_checks(ctx, traders, oracle_prices) loops over margin_configs and calls LiquidationEngine::check_liquidations
- grep for run_liquidation_checks across crates/ finds only its definition at native_executor.rs:5923; it is never called (unwired)
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:72,115,150,193,432,442 — check_liquidations / check_cross_liquidation / check_isolated_liquidation / execute_liquidation / get_insurance_fund / set_insurance_fund exist
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:232,381 — check_isolated_maintenance and isolated_margin_check exist (partial margin-mode support)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:46,448,484,535,1314,2278,2354 — reduce_only is a field, is copied from params and stop orders, and is serialized; no enforcement function was found
- grep for fee_bps\|taker_fee\|maker_fee\|FeeSchedule in torus-core, torus-bridge, torus-economics and torus-consensus returns nothing
- crates/torus-types/src/lib.rs:828,906,1161 — max_funding_rate_bps is only a market parameter; 'funding' appears in no other non-test file except eip712.rs

**Risk:** The chain has no liquidation driver, no fees and no funding. It can reach 200k orders/s and still not be a Hyperliquid-equivalent perp venue, and underwater positions are never closed, which is an insolvency risk. If T4.2 (state-root schema) or T4.3 (margin/settlement caches) ships before fees and funding, both get redone and need an extra lockstep migration. All P-items change deterministic execution output. If any validator runs them before the others, the chain forks on state root, so they must ride a coordinated upgrade.

**Fix:** Add a section "Tier P — Product parity" to docs/Torus-hyperBFT-roadmap.md and to its dependency graph (line 209). Edges: T1.x --> P; P --> T4.2; P --> T4.3. P runs alongside T2 and T3.

P1 [LOCKSTEP], liquidation driver. Call NativeExecutor::run_liquidation_checks once per block from the end-of-block hook in the native_executor block path (the call site in crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs still needs locating). Derive `traders` deterministically from state, i.e. accounts with open positions in ctx.positions. Never take them from node-local input, or validators diverge. Feed prices from the committed oracle_aggregate result. Tests: replay determinism across 2 nodes; an underwater account gets liquidated within 1 block; the insurance fund is credited (extends liquidation.rs:520).

P2 [LOCKSTEP], reduce-only enforcement. Clamp or reject at order placement and stop trigger (order_book.rs:448/484/535/1314) against the current position in position.rs. Liquidation close orders depend on this.

P3 [LOCKSTEP], fee schedule. Add maker/taker bps to MarketMarginConfig or the market params in torus-types:1161, charge fees in settlement, and route a share to the insurance fund (set_insurance_fund, liquidation.rs:442). This changes the state root and the EIP-712 market-param encoding (torus-types eip712.rs).

P4 [LOCKSTEP], funding. Keep a per-market cumulative funding index and settle it lazily per position on touch, so no O(positions) sweep runs per block. Clamp at max_funding_rate_bps and use the mark price from oracle.rs.

P5 [LOCKSTEP], margin-mode parity. Cross/isolated switching and leverage update actions, building on margin.rs:232/381.

LOCAL items in the track: RPC/WS exposure of fees, funding and liquidations (torus-rpc); indexer and history; the per-block liquidation scan budget (only if made deterministic, otherwise LOCKSTEP).

Release bundling: ship P1+P2 with the T1.4 lockstep deploy, and P3+P4 with T3.2. Freeze the state schema before T4.2, and design the T4.3 caches over the post-P settlement path. Rerun the T0.3 harness after P3 and P4 so the S395 margin/settlement baseline includes the fee and funding cost.

**Unsure:** Hit the time box. I did not find the app.rs end-of-block hook where P1 should call run_liquidation_checks. I did not check whether reduce_only is enforced indirectly in native_executor or margin.rs; I found no explicit check, which is weaker than a confirmed gap. Fees may exist under other names, such as in torus-economics under 'commission' or 'rebate'. I did not check whether a funding-settlement action exists under another name (precompiles.rs QueuedActionKind at :1102 not read). The `idx` index returned nothing for every query; it may be stale or not built for this project.

</details>

**fable** — design, impact high, effort XL, lockstep yes · LOC: roadmap edit ~80 lines; code: P1 ~150, P2 ~120, P3 ~300 (action + eip712 + proposer), P4 ~60 wiring, P5 ~250 + tests ~500

The roadmap (docs/Torus-hyperBFT-roadmap.md) has no product track at all; its Tier 4 assumes the margin/settlement semantics are final and only caches them (T4.3). In code, the trading-feature gaps are worse than "missing polish": `check_margin_at_match` has no non-test caller, `run_liquidation_checks` has no caller anywhere, `ctx.total_native_fees` is declared/initialised but never incremented (so `distribute_fees` at app.rs:1939 distributes native fees of zero), `reduce_only` is only stored/serialised, never enforced in matching, and there is no funding engine (only a `max_funding_rate_bps` config field in eip712). Proposed design: add a "Tier P — Product parity" slotted after Tier 1 (liveness) and in parallel with Tier 2, with a hard rule that P lands BEFORE T2.5 (raise block cap) and BEFORE T4.3 (margin/settlement cache), because every P item changes the state transition that T4.3 caches and T2.5 amplifies. Order inside P: P1 reduce-only + margin-at-match (pure core, no new block inputs) -> P2 per-fill maker/taker fees feeding `total_native_fees` -> P3 oracle-price-in-block (new action/format; prerequisite) -> P4 wire `run_liquidation_checks` into the app.rs post-engine tail -> P5 funding accrual (needs P3 + an epoch/tail hook, `process_epoch_boundary` already exists).

<details><summary>Evidence, risk, fix</summary>

**Evidence:**
- docs/Torus-hyperBFT-roadmap.md:20 — defines the labels: [LOCAL]=cannot cause divergence, [LOCKSTEP]=all validators upgrade together, [CONSENSUS-SAFETY]; any state-transition change is therefore LOCKSTEP by the doc's own definition
- docs/Torus-hyperBFT-roadmap.md:193-197 — T4.3 'Margin & settlement caching [LOCAL]' caches apply_fill/balance path; must come after semantics are final
- docs/Torus-hyperBFT-roadmap.md:144 — T2.5 raise NATIVE_TOTAL_BLOCK_CAP gated on T3.1; P should precede it
- docs/Torus-hyperBFT-roadmap.md:209-235 — dependency graph has no product node; T1 --> T4_1 & T4_3 & T4_4
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5922-5937 — run_liquidation_checks(ctx, traders, oracle_prices) exists; grep over crates found no caller outside its definition
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:1374,1853,5995 — total_native_fees declared, init 0, read in distribute_fees; no += anywhere in the file
- crates/torus-bridge/src/native_executor.rs:5991-5995 — distribute_fees(ctx, total_evm_fees) sums native+evm fees
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs:1936-1940 — post-engine tail: drain_core_writer, process_governance, distribute_fees, process_epoch_boundary (the natural slot for liquidation + funding drivers)
- crates/torus-core/src/margin.rs:151 check_margin_at_match, :202 total_maintenance_margin — check_margin_at_match called only from crates/torus-core/tests/margin_tests.rs:252
- crates/torus-core/src/liquidation.rs:124 — LiquidationEngine uses total_maintenance_margin (engine exists, driver unwired)
- crates/torus-core/src/order_book.rs:46,106,448,484,535,1314,2278,2354 — reduce_only is a field, copied and (de)serialised, with no matching-time branch
- crates/torus-types/src/eip712.rs:620 — max_funding_rate_bps is hashed into a market-params action; no fn *funding* exists in any crate src
- crates/torus-consensus/src/app.rs — grep 'oracle_price' returns nothing: no oracle price feed reaches the executor from the block path

**Risk:** Without a product track, the perf tiers optimise and then cache (T4.3) a state transition that must change again; each later semantic change (fees, margin-at-match, liquidations, funding) is a LOCKSTEP state-root-affecting relaunch, so doing them after T4.3/T4.2 means re-validating the caches and the incremental-root oracle twice. For HL parity, a chain with zero native fees, no enforced reduce-only, no margin check at match and no liquidation/funding driver is not a perps exchange regardless of orders/s; and raising the block cap (T2.5) first only increases exposure of under-margined flow.

**Fix:** Add 'Tier P — Product parity' to docs/Torus-hyperBFT-roadmap.md between Tier 1 and Tier 2, with graph edges T1 --> P1..P5, P1&P2 --> T4_3, P3 --> P4 & P5, P --> T2_5. Labels: P1 reduce-only + margin-at-match [LOCKSTEP, no format change]: in order_book.rs submit path (around :448-535) reject/shrink reduce_only orders that would open or flip a position; call MarginEngine::check_margin_at_match from the executor's apply/match path (native_executor.rs near :5750 where initial_margin is built). P2 fees [LOCKSTEP]: per-fill maker/taker bps from MarketMarginConfig/market params, debit in apply_fill, `ctx.total_native_fees += fee` so the existing distribute_fees (:5991) becomes non-zero; RPC exposure of fee schedule is [LOCAL] (torus-rpc). P3 oracle price in block [LOCKSTEP + action-format change]: new native action (eip712.rs hash) carrying per-market oracle/mark prices, proposer-injected; bundle this relaunch with the T4.2 flat->bucketed migration or the T1.4/T3.2 lockstep deploy windows so there is one coordinated relaunch, not three. P4 liquidation driver [LOCKSTEP]: call NativeExecutor::run_liquidation_checks in the app.rs:1936-1940 tail before distribute_fees, traders = addresses touched this block (ctx positions dirty set) + a bounded scan cursor for the rest. P5 funding [LOCKSTEP]: new torus-core funding.rs (rate = clamp(premium, max_funding_rate_bps), accrue on an 8h/epoch boundary via process_epoch_boundary). LOCAL pieces: RPC/history endpoints, metrics, and T4.3 cache once P1/P2 are final. Tests: torus-core unit tests per engine (reduce-only reject, margin reject at match, fee debit = fill*bps, liquidation triggers when equity < maintenance, funding sign/clamp), and a four_node_consensus determinism run with the state-root oracle on for each P item since they are all state-root affecting.

**Unsure:** Did not read the executor's existing margin-lock path (native_executor.rs ~:5750 initial_margin) so some initial-margin check may exist under another name; the 'margin ~727ms' in T4.3 suggests something runs there. Did not confirm whether per-fill fees exist under a different name in a settlement module (grep for 'fee' in torus-core/src/*.rs and native_executor.rs found only distribute_fees). Did not verify how oracle prices are supposed to arrive today (grep in app.rs found none; proposer.rs not read). Time-boxed to 6 tool calls.

</details>
